Of 1,104 screened patients, 453 met inclusion criteria after excluding those with repeated testing or missing data; following exclusion of 118 patients without gastroscopy or adequate biopsy sampling, 335 patients who underwent standardized topographical gastric biopsy mapping constituted the definitive analysis cohort. Associations between APA status/titer dilutions and histopathological findings were assessed using chi-squared tests and multivariate logistic regression.

RESULTS: GIM was present in 24.5% (n = 82) of the cohort. APA positivity was significantly associated with GIM (40.5% vs. 15.4% in APA-negative patients, p <0.001), with a titer-dependent dose-response relationship peaking at 50.0% in the 1:320 and >1:320 dilution subgroups. In multivariate analysis, each incremental step-up in APA titer dilution (OR 1.522, 95% CI 1.304-1.776) and advancing age (OR 1.043, 95% CI 1.021-1.066) independently predicted GIM, while active H. pylori infection was an independent negative predictor (OR 0.348, 95% CI 0.184-0.660).

CONCLUSION: Quantitative APA titers, rather than binary positivity, demonstrate a clear dose-response relationship with histopathological GIM. Titers of 1:320 or greater identify a clinically actionable threshold that may guide prioritization of endoscopic evaluation with standardized topographical biopsy mapping.

articles.title: Screening strategies for the early detection of non-cardia gastric cancer in low- to moderate-prevalence regions: Asia-Pacific gastroesophageal cancer congress consensus 2026.
articles.journal: Gastric cancer : official journal of the International Gastric Cancer Association and the Japanese Gastric Cancer Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Gastric cancer (GC) remains a major global health burden, and early detection is essential for improving patient outcomes. Although GC screening has been widely implemented in East Asian countries with a high disease burden, the optimal screening strategy for low- to moderate-prevalence regions remains unclear. To address this gap, the Asia Pacific Gastroesophageal Cancer Congress (APGCC) convened an international consensus meeting to develop evidence-based recommendations for improving the detection of non-cardia gastric cancer (NCGC).

METHODS: The APGCC working group developed 11 clinical questions (CQs) addressing GC screening, with a particular focus on NCGC. For each CQ, assigned authors conducted literature reviews using PubMed and prepared evidence summaries and draft recommendations. Consensus was achieved through a two-round modified Delphi process involving 37 international voting members.

RESULTS: The consensus recommendations addressed population-based screening, screening modalities, identification of high-risk individuals, quality indicators for esophagogastroduodenoscopy (EGD), image-enhanced endoscopy, and artificial intelligence-assisted endoscopy. Population-based endoscopic screening is not recommended in low- to moderate-prevalence regions because of insufficient evidence. However, if screening is performed, EGD is preferred over upper gastrointestinal series for the detection of early NCGC in asymptomatic individuals. The recommendations also emphasize the importance of high-quality endoscopic examinations, risk-stratified screening using serum biomarkers, and the appropriate integration of advanced endoscopic technologies.

CONCLUSIONS: These APGCC consensus recommendations provide practical guidance for improving the early detection of NCGC in low- to moderate-prevalence regions. This consensus also highlights important evidence gaps and establishes a framework for future research and the development of region-specific GC screening strategies.

articles.title: Clinical outcomes of upper-arm port implantation under restrictive platelet transfusion in hematological diseases.
articles.abstract: The optimal periprocedural platelet transfusion strategy for implantable central venous port placement in patients with hematological diseases remains unclear. We retrospectively evaluated outcomes after upper-arm port implantation under a restrictive platelet transfusion strategy, with prophylactic platelet transfusion only given at counts < 20 × 109/L. This single-center study included 58 procedures in 57 patients between May 2022 and June 2026. The median preprocedural platelet count was 152.5 × 109/L (range, 4-412 × 109/L). Prophylactic platelet transfusion was not given in any of the 3 procedures at counts of 20 to < 50 × 109/L, but preprocedural transfusion was given in all 8 procedures at counts < 20 × 109/L. Intraoperative or postoperative transfusion was also given in 2 procedures during the initial study period. Technical success was achieved in all procedures. No bleeding or hematoma requiring additional intervention was documented, including among the 11 procedures at platelet counts < 50 × 109/L, and no port-related infection was documented. Port exposure occurred in 2 procedures, both requiring removal. These findings provide clinical data on upper-arm port implantation under a restrictive platelet transfusion strategy, including in patients with thrombocytopenia. Larger studies are needed to determine an appropriate platelet transfusion threshold.

articles.title: Outcomes of non-tuberculous mycobacterial infection of the bone, joint and soft tissue: a seven-year multicentre retrospective study.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Extrapulmonary nontuberculous mycobacterial (EPNTM) infections of bone, joint, and soft tissue are difficult to treat and lack species-specific outcome data. We sought to describe antimicrobial regimens and surgical management by Mycobacterium spp. and to identify predictors of a clinical cure within 12 months in this adult cohort with EPNTM.

METHODS: We conducted a multicentre retrospective cohort study across five tertiary hospitals in Australia and New Zealand 2014-2020. Adults with culture-confirmed EPNTM infection from sterile or intraoperative specimens were included. Primary outcome was clinical cure at 12 months. Secondary outcomes included relapse, drug toxicity and host factors.

RESULTS: Among 107 patients, six species groups were identified, most commonly M. abscessus complex (n = 26, 25%), Mycobacterium marinum (n = 25, 24%), and M. fortuitum complex (n = 24, 23%). Clinical cure within 12 months differed significantly by species, with high cure proportions for M. abscessus complex (n = 22, 92%) in surgically accessible infections and lower cure rates for M. chelonae (n = 6, 60%) and amalgamated slow growing mycobacteria (n = 4, 36%). Younger age (median 47 vs. 60 years, p = 0.006) and Mycobacterium spp. was associated with cure whereas antimicrobial class and surgical intervention were not. Of antibiotic classes used, only macrolide duration was associated with cure. Relapse was uncommon (8%) and occurred predominantly in immunosuppressed patients.

CONCLUSIONS: This first multicentre Australasian cohort demonstrates substantial species-specific variation in outcomes of EPNTM osteoarticular and soft-tissue infections. This study highlights the need for species-specific management pathways and prospective studies.

articles.title: From early recognition to precision medicine: advances in the diagnosis and management of adult sepsis and septic shock-a narrative review.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Emerging diagnostic, computational, and precision approaches are expanding the ability to detect, classify, and biologically characterise sepsis, but their translation into clinical benefit depends on whether added information changes management and, ultimately, improves patient-centred outcomes. This review evaluates selected advances in adult sepsis and septic shock through a framework of clinical actionability.

METHODS: A focused PubMed search was supplemented by major international guidelines, targeted searches, and reference-list screening through August 2026. Priority was given to randomised trials, systematic reviews and meta-analyses, multicentre studies, and prospective or external validation studies relevant to clinical implementation.

RESULTS: We developed a two-gap framework to distinguish gains in information from clinically meaningful translation. The information-to-action gap describes situations in which improved detection, prediction, biological classification, or physiological assessment does not alter management; the decision-to-outcome gap describes management changes without demonstrated patient-centred benefit. Digital alerts, rapid diagnostics, host-response assays, physiology-guided resuscitation, and phenotype- or biomarker-guided strategies show differing degrees of actionability. Across these domains, reproducibility, transportability, workflow integration, timing, temporal stability, and treatment-predictive validity remain key constraints.

CONCLUSION: Most of the emerging diagnostic, computational, and precision approaches reviewed here have not yet established a routine role in sepsis care. Established evidence-based management therefore remains the clinical foundation, while newer strategies should be evaluated prospectively for their ability to close the information-to-action and decision-to-outcome gaps.

articles.title: Clinical significance of human rhino-/enterovirus co-detection in pediatric Mycoplasma pneumoniae infections.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To determine whether upper respiratory tract co-detection of human rhino-/enterovirus is associated with a distinct clinical phenotype in children with Mycoplasma pneumoniae infection.

METHODS: We analyzed 236 children with M. pneumoniae infection detected by multiplex polymerase chain reaction (PCR) from 2022 to 2025 at the University Children's Hospital Zurich, comparing those without and with human rhino-/enterovirus co-detection, and performing a secondary analysis after excluding other co-detections.

RESULTS: No statistically significant differences were observed in demographic characteristics, clinical presentation, or inflammatory markers between groups.

CONCLUSION: Human rhino-/enterovirus co-detection may represent incidental viral detection rather than clinically relevant co-infection in children with M. pneumoniae infection, supporting cautious interpretation of multiplex PCR results.

articles.title: Effects of Exercise Training on the Metabolic Cost of Walking in Health and Disease: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The metabolic cost of walking (Cw) increases with heathy aging and in neurological conditions. No comprehensive assessment has been performed yet to determine whether chronic exercise training and rehabilitation could improve Cw.

OBJECTIVE: The purpose of this study was to determine whether the effects of chronic exercise interventions on Cw differ by type, dose, and intensity in healthy adults and individuals with neurological conditions (multiple sclerosis, Parkinson's disease, and stroke).

DESIGN: Systematic review and robust variance estimation meta-analysis with meta-regression following Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines.

DATA SOURCES: Systematic search of Medline, Web of Science, and CINAHL databases.

RESULTS: A total of 27 studies with 36 intervention arms and 54 outcomes in 1177 participants, of those 703 healthy adults and 474 patients with multiple sclerosis (1 study), Parkinson's disease (1 study), and stroke (9 studies) were included. Across all types of training (aerobic, resistance, other), chronic physical exercise training improved Cw (g = 0.40, p = 0.001). Improvements were significant in healthy individuals (g = 0.49, p = 0.001) but not in patients with stroke (g = 0.24, p = 0.065). Meta-regression confirmed that population moderated the effects of training on Cw (p = 0.043) after adjusting for exercise training characteristics. In the adjusted meta-regression, higher study-level mean body mass index (BMI) was associated with smaller intervention effects on Cw (β = - 0.20, p = 0.040). Training type, duration, intensity, frequency, and session duration did not significantly moderate the training effects on Cw, although the meta-regression may have been underpowered to detect such associations. Heterogeneity (I2 < 62.5%) and risk of bias were moderate.

CONCLUSIONS: This is the first meta-synthesis examining the effects of diverse forms of exercise training on Cw in different populations. Chronic physical exercise training improves Cw in healthy adults, with smaller effects observed in individuals with stroke. The findings support chronic physical exercise training as an effective strategy for improving walking economy.

articles.title: Clinical validation of an intra-abdominal pressure monitoring system by comparison with pneumoperitoneum pressure.
articles.journal: Journal of clinical monitoring and computing
articles.abstract: In critically ill patients, intra-abdominal hypertension (IAH) is associated with organ dysfunction and increased mortality. Acute kidney injury may occur early, since the kidney is particularly vulnerable to elevated intra-abdominal pressure (IAP). Accurate and timely measurement of IAP is essential for early detection of IAH and the initiation of appropriate therapeutic interventions. Therefore, the aim of this study was to assess the accuracy of an IAP monitoring system compared to a reference standard, the CO2 insufflator, during laparoscopy. The second aim was to assess the changes in renal biomarker levels during and after increases in IAP through pneumoperitoneum. A prospective cohort study in patients undergoing laparoscopy at the University Medical Center Groningen. IAP measurements were performed with a urinary catheter using an IAP monitoring system (Accuryn® Monitoring System, Accuryn Medical) and compared to the pressure set at the CO2-insufflator system. Bland-Altman analysis was performed with accounting for repeated measures. Urine samples were collected at several time-points and Kidney Injury Molecule 1 (KIM-1), Tissue Inhibitor of Metalloproteinase 2 (TIMP-2), urinary Neutrophil Gelatinase-Associated Lipocalin (NGAL), Liver-type Fatty Acid-Binding Protein (L-FABP), and albumin-creatinine ratio were measured. Between March 2025 and January 2026, 99 measurements were performed in 29 patients. One patient (3%) underwent hemicolectomy, and 28 patients underwent endometriosis surgery (97%). Analysis showed a bias of -1.4 mmHg (95% CI (-1.96 - (-0.82)) and limits of agreement of - 5.96 mmHg and 3.2 mmHg (95% CI -6.8-3.99) between the IAP monitoring system and the CO2-insufflators. The precision was 2.3 mmHg. The levels of renal biomarkers KIM-1, TIMP-2 and albumin/Cr ratio increased during laparoscopy compared to baseline, suggesting that relatively small IAP increases during laparoscopy have a subclinical effect on the kidney. The IAP monitoring system underestimated the IAP set by the CO2-insufflator by approximately 1 mmHg. The wide limits of agreement warrant cautious interpretation. Overall, the IAP monitoring system showed reasonable accuracy and precision. The increase of several renal biomarkers during laparoscopy compared to baseline may reflect a direct effect of elevated IAP on the kidney.

articles.title: A real-world multicenter study of statins in compensated advanced chronic liver disease on hepatic decompensation and mortality outcomes.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Statins exert pleiotropic effects, including antiinflammatory, endothelial, and antifibrotic actions, which may slow the progression of cirrhosis. However, their use in patients with compensated advanced chronic liver disease (cACLD) remains limited due to concerns regarding potential hepatotoxicity, and data specific to this population remains sparse.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective, multinational cohort study of adult cACLD (LSM >10 kPa) patients using data from the Cirrhosis Outcome and Research Endeavor (CORE) consortium, across 13 centers in 8 countries. Baseline statin use was the exposure of interest. Associations with first and second hepatic decompensation, composite liver-related events, and all-cause and cause-specific mortality were assessed using Fine-Gray competing-risks regression across two sequentially adjusted multivariable models and an inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) analysis.

RESULTS: Among 2267 patients, 786 (34.7%) were statin users. Statin use was independently associated with a lower risk of first decompensation (Model 1: sHR 0.64; Model 2: sHR 0.66; IPTW: sHR 0.56) and composite liver-related events (Model 1: sHR 0.61; Model 2: sHR 0.63; IPTW: sHR 0.50), with benefit most pronounced in the moderate-risk portal hypertension strata and MASLD subgroup. No association was observed with all-cause, liver-related, or cardiovascular mortality. Associations with second decompensation were inconsistent.

CONCLUSION: In this large multinational cohort of cACLD patients, statin use was associated with reduced risk of hepatic decompensation and liver-related events, but not all-cause mortality. These findings support a potential benefit for statins in this population.

articles.title: A comprehensive evaluation on the impact of MASLD on the prognosis of chronic hepatitis B-related hepatocellular carcinoma following hepatectomy: results from retrospective multicenter cohort study and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Prognosis after radical hepatectomy for chronic hepatitis B (CHB) related hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is poor. Comorbidity of CHB and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) has grown increasingly common, with MASLD further modifying the hepatic microenvironment beyond HBV-induced injury. However, its impact on postoperative prognosis remains unclear.

METHODS: Combining a retrospective study with meta-analysis, this study systematically compared prognostic differences and influencing factors in 424 hepatectomy patients (MASLD-CHB-HCC group vs. CHB-HCC group) from multiple centers. Additionally, a meta-analysis involving 6653 patients was performed to further verify the prognostic effect of MASLD.

RESULTS: In this retrospective cohort study, the MASLD-CHB-HCC group showed significantly superior overall survival (OS) (p = 0.041) and recurrence-free survival (RFS) (p = 0.028) compared with the CHB-HCC group, with statistically significant differences. However, after performing propensity score matching (PSM) screening, no statistical differences were observed in OS (p = 0.220) and RFS (p = 0.190) between the two groups. This result is consistent with our meta-analysis conclusion. Cox regression analysis demonstrated that higher body mass index (BMI) was an independent factor associated with favorable survival. In subgroup analyses stratified by different BMI cutoffs, among non-lean patients, the MASLD-CHB-HCC group achieved better OS (BMI ≥ 23 subgroup: p < 0.001; BMI ≥ 25 subgroup: p < 0.001) and RFS (BMI ≥ 23 subgroup: p < 0.001; BMI ≥ 25 subgroup: p < 0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: MASLD exerts differential impacts on survival prognosis in patients with CHB-HCC, with divergent effects observed between lean and non-lean subgroups stratified by BMI.

articles.title: Precision Immunosuppression in Heart Transplantation: Biomarker-Guided Therapy Comes of Age.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Heart transplantation is the definitive treatment for end-stage heart failure. While the number of heart transplant performed yearly in the United States has nearly doubled in the last decade, median survival has stagnated, largely due to the complications posed by lifelong immunosuppression. A shift towards precision medicine is needed to achieve the optimal balance between risk of allograft rejection and drug-related toxicities to improve post-transplant outcomes.

RECENT FINDINGS: Novel molecular based diagnostic tools and biomarkers are being investigated, and hold promise in evaluating graft health and assessing immune state. The use of circulating biomarkers and molecular diagnostics such as human and viral cell-free DNA, tissue-based gene expression profiling, and circulating microRNAs, will allow for more comprehensive assessment of post-transplant immune activity and rejection risk to personalize patient care.

articles.title: Epigenetically silencing gluconeogenic enzyme PCK1 by EZH2 promotes renal tubulointerstitial fibrosis.
articles.abstract: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is a leading cause of global morbidity. The kidney is a major gluconeogenic organ, and impaired renal gluconeogenesis contributes to CKD, yet the regulatory mechanisms remain poorly understood. Here we show that enhancer of zeste homolog 2 (EZH2), a histone H3K27 trimethyltransferase, epigenetically suppresses renal gluconeogenesis and drives tubulointerstitial fibrosis. Through integrative multi-omics profiling (RNA-seq, CUT&Tag, and single-nucleus RNA-seq), we show that EZH2 directly binds to and deposits H3K27 trimethylation at promoters of gluconeogenic genes in proximal tubular cells, with the most prominent repression observed at phosphoenolpyruvate carboxykinase (Pck1) gene. In fibrotic kidneys, Ezh2 is markedly upregulated in proximal tubules and inversely correlates with Pck1 expression across injury and maladaptive repair states. Genetic ablation or pharmacological inhibition of EZH2 restores PCK1 expression, enhances lactate-to-glucose conversion, and attenuates extracellular matrix deposition and fibrotic marker expression in both cultured tubular cells and mouse models of kidney fibrosis. Stable isotope 13C-lactate tracing shows that tubular Ezh2 deletion increases the labelling fractions of gluconeogenic intermediates while reducing the labelling fraction of acetyl-CoA, indicating preferential partitioning of lactate-derived carbon towards gluconeogenesis rather than oxidative entry into the tricarboxylic acid (TCA) cycle in vivo. Mechanistically, Pck1 gain- and loss-of-function experiments establish PCK1 as a non-redundant downstream effector of EZH2's pro-fibrotic action. Collectively, our findings uncover an EZH2-PCK1 epigenetic-metabolic axis that couples histone methylation to gluconeogenic reprogramming and fibrogenesis. This axis may offer a dual therapeutic opportunity for CKD by concurrently restoring metabolic homeostasis and limiting fibrotic progression.

articles.title: Molecular Epidemiology and Risk Factors of Theileria annulata Infection and Rhipicephalus and Hyalomma Tick Infestation in Three Districts of Northern Pakistan.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ticks and tick-borne diseases pose a major threat to livestock productivity in tropical and subtropical regions, by transmitting pathogens of veterinary and public health concern, including Theileria species. Despite the threats posed to the large ruminant industry, integrated studies on the causative agent of tropical theileriosis and its tick vectors from the same infected hosts, along with their associated risk factors, remain limited in northern Pakistan. This study investigated Theileria infection, its associated tick species, and host- and environmental-related risk factors in large ruminants from the region using an integrated approach.

METHODS: A total of 3151 ticks (female: 1630, 51.7%; male: 725, 23%; nymph: 458, 14.5%; larvae: 338, 10.7%) were collected from 900 animals (805 cattle, 89.45%; 95 buffaloes, 10.55%), along with 221 blood samples from symptomatic, tick infested animals (202 cattle, 91.4%; 19 buffaloes, 8.6%) between May 2024 and April 2025. Ticks were identified morphologically, while Theileria infection was assessed by microscopy and PCR targeting the 18S rRNA gene. Phylogenetic analysis was performed in MEGA X using the maximum-likelihood method. Host- and environmental-related risk factors were assessed for their association with tick infestation and Theileria infection.

RESULTS: Two tick genera were identified morphologically: Rhipicephalus (83.59%) and Hyalomma (16.41%). Within Rhipicephalus, Rhipicephalus microplus (70.29%) was the dominant species, followed by Rhipicephalus haemaphysaloides (7.61%) and Rhipicephalus sp. (5.68%). The genus Hyalomma comprised Hyalomma anatolicum (8.82%) and Hyalomma turanicum (7.58%). Tick infestation was significantly higher in cattle (46.33%) than in buffaloes (22.11%). In cattle, infestation rates were 46.49% in Upper Dir, 46.62% in Bajaur and 45.90% in Lower Dir, whereas in buffaloes, the corresponding rates were 24.14%, 23.53% and 18.75%, respectively. Microscopic examination detected Theileria infection in 18.09% (40/221) of blood samples from clinically affected, tick-infested animals (37/202 cattle, 18.31%; 3/19 buffaloes, 15.78%), whereas the detection rate by PCR was 45.24% (100/221) (92/202 cattle, 45.54%; 8/19 buffaloes, 42.11%). By BLAST analysis, the obtained sequence of 18S rRNA showed a maximum identity of 99.62% with a Theileria annulata sequence from Turkey, China and Pakistan, and phylogenetic tree grouped it with corresponding species from Asia and Europe. Risk factors analysis showed that host species was significantly associated with tick infestation, while age, season, and acaricide treatment were significantly associated with infestation in both cattle and buffaloes (p < 0.05). Age, season and acaricide use were significantly associated with Theileria infection in cattle, whereas in buffaloes, only acaricide use was significant. Gender, presence of rural poultry, grazing system and district showed no significant association (p > 0.05) with tick infestation or Theileria infection in either host.

CONCLUSIONS: This study provides an integrated assessment of the causative agent of tropical theileriosis and associated tick species from the same large ruminants, along with their associated risk factors, in the mountainous terrain of northern Pakistan. Given that tick vectors and tropical theileriosis can significantly affect livestock-dependent economies, this study may help guide better preventive measures in the region.

articles.title: Obesity-Related Asthma: Structure and Inflammation.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Asthma and obesity are affecting children and teenagers at higher rates than previous generations. Epidemiological data link obesity during childhood with the subsequent development of asthma. In this review we describe developmental and inflammatory factors that contribute to asthma severity in children with obesity.

RECENT FINDINGS: Asthma driven by obesity is likely due to both structural and inflammatory changes. Excess weight places mechanical stress on the airway thereby reducing lung volumes. In addition, obesity is linked to chronic inflammation. Adipose tissue releases pro-inflammatory cytokines (IL-6 and TNF-α) which drives the airway towards hyperresponsiveness. This "obesity-related asthma" phenotype does not respond well to corticosteroids making these patients difficult to treat. In children and teenagers, treatment options are limited to currently approved asthma medications; however, improvement in asthma control has been observed in adults utilizing metformin and GLP-1 agonists. Children with obesity are more likely to develop asthma. Their asthma symptoms tend to be more frequent and harder to control. With the rate of obesity on the rise, it is paramount to identify the mechanisms underlying systemic inflammation in those with elevated BMIs. This will allow us to find better treatment options for "obesity-related asthma."

articles.title: Identification and Characterization of Patient Populations at High Risk for Clostridioides difficile Infection (CDI): A Narrative Review.
articles.abstract: Clostridioides difficile infection (CDI) is a major cause of infections worldwide and can lead to life-threatening complications and a severe impact on patients' quality of life (QoL). CDI can affect anyone, but it is generally accepted that those at greatest risk include people receiving antibiotics, of older age, and with a compromised immune system. However, beyond these broad categories, specific populations at high risk for CDI are not clearly defined. We performed a literature search to identify and characterize patients at high risk for CDI. We found that those at high risk for CDI include patients undergoing hematopoietic stem cell transplant, solid organ transplant or chimeric antigen receptor T-cell therapy, or with chronic kidney disease/end-stage kidney disease, hematological malignancies or inflammatory bowel disease, or who are older and frail with comorbidities. In the identified patient populations, CDI was associated with significantly worse clinical outcomes, increased healthcare resource utilization and costs, and generally an increased risk of mortality compared with those without CDI. Patients at high risk for CDI have multiple risk factors for infection that further complicate management of their disease. Apart from older patients, there is a lack of information on the impact on QoL in high-risk populations. Prevention strategies for CDI in high-risk populations are lacking and are based on the general population. As such, there is a need to increase understanding of those at high risk for CDI and the significant impact infection has in these populations, and to identify preventive therapies to alleviate the burden on both patients and healthcare systems.

articles.title: Ramadan Fasting in Chronic Heart Failure: A Systematic Review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic heart failure (CHF) is a significant global health concern, affecting over 64 million individuals worldwide. During Ramadan, the ninth month of the Islamic calendar, Muslims abstain from food, drink, smoking, and sexual activity between dawn and sunset. This systematic review investigates the potential impact of Ramadan observance in patients with CHF.

METHODS: In accordance with JBI and PRISMA guidelines, a comprehensive literature search was performed across PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science to identify clinical studies examining the effects of Ramadan fasting in patients with CHF. Review articles, case reports, animal studies, editorials, conference abstracts, and commentaries were excluded. Risk of bias was evaluated using the JBI critical appraisal tools.

RESULTS: The search identified 137 articles, of which seven met the inclusion criteria. The included studies were mostly conducted in MENA region. Overall, Ramadan fasting was not associated with increased hospitalization rates, deterioration in clinical status, or higher mortality among patients with heart failure.

CONCLUSION: This study suggest that fasting may be relatively safe when undertaken with appropriate medical supervision and adherence to prescribed treatment. Nonetheless, larger prospective studies are warranted to further validate these observations.

articles.title: Correction to: Nicorandil Regulates Ferroptosis and Mitigates Septic Cardiomyopathy via TLR4/SLC7A11 Signaling Pathway.
Artificial Intelligence for Early Prediction of Intracranial Hypertension: From Single-Centre Development to Multicentre Validation.
authors: CENTER-TBI High-Resolution ICU (HR ICU) Sub-Study Participants and Investigators
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Raised intracranial pressure is one of the most severe secondary insults after traumatic brain injury. Recognising physiological patterns before they progress to dangerous intracranial pressure elevations could enable preventive rather than reactive interventions. In our previous Uppsala single-centre study, an XGBoost machine learning model showed high discriminative performance for prediction of imminent intracranial pressure insults. The model identifies short-term physiological trajectories associated with imminent threshold crossing rather than predicting independent future clinical events. Whether these results are generalisable across centres is unknown. The aim was therefore to evaluate whether the XGBoost model trained on an Uppsala dataset maintains similar performance when applied to a multicentre TBI cohort - The CENTER-TBI High-Resolution ICU cohort.

METHODS: The XGBoost model trained on the Uppsala high frequency traumatic brain injury cohort was externally validated using data from the multicentre CENTER-TBI cohort. Minute-level averages of intracranial pressure and invasive arterial blood pressure were used to predict the onset of an intracranial pressure insult within 30 min on the basis of a 4h historical window. A bidirectional validation design was applied and performance was assessed using multiple metrics.

RESULTS: The cohorts comprised 602 patients from Uppsala and 255 patients from the CENTER-TBI database. When trained on the Uppsala cohort and tested on CENTER-TBI, the model achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of 97.4%, sensitivity of 93.8%, and specificity of 98.6%. Training on CENTER-TBI and testing on the Uppsala dataset yielded an AUROC of 96.1%, sensitivity of 81.2%, and specificity of 98.7%. Balanced accuracy exceeded 88% in both validation directions.

CONCLUSIONS: The XGBoost model retained high performance under external multicentre validation, indicating that pre-insult physiological patterns preceding increased intracranial pressure are shared across cohorts. Differences in sensitivity between validation directions were observed and may reflect cohort characteristics or dataset size. These findings support the need for local evaluation before clinical implementation.

articles.title: Above-ground biomass estimation in tropical dry deciduous forests using multi-sensor data from ALOS-2 and sentinel-2 with advanced machine learning approaches.
articles.abstract: Accurate estimation of above-ground biomass (AGB) is essential for sustainable forest resource management and carbon stock assessment. This study focuses on the Pembi Forest, Telangana, India, where synthetic aperture radar (SAR) data from ALOS-2 PALSAR-2 L-band and multispectral data from Sentinel-2 were integrated with biophysical information to develop AGB prediction models. Predictor variables included SAR backscatter and polarization-derived features, Sentinel-2 spectral indices and band combinations, principal components, leaf area index (LAI), and global canopy height. Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LGBM), Support Vector Regression (SVR), Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGB), Artificial Neural Network (ANN), and a weighted voting ensemble were evaluated. The ensemble model achieved the highest predictive performance, with R2 = 0.67, RMSE = 24.35 t ha⁻1 and MAE = 14.97 t ha⁻1. Spatial AGB distribution maps showed prominent variation in the study area, providing valuable information for resource management and conservation planning. The findings highlight the potential of combining SAR and multispectral remote sensing data with machine learning techniques to improve accuracy of AGB estimation, surpassing the performance of conventional single-model methods and advancing the understanding of forest biomass dynamics.

articles.title: The impact of intraoperative hemoadsorption during cardiac surgery for infective endocarditis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Postoperative sepsis and/or systemic inflammatory response syndrome caused by infective endocarditis (IE) can lead to significant postoperative mortality. Intraoperative hemoadsorption therapy has shown promising results in the treatment of sepsis and dysregulated inflammatory response during cardiac surgery. The aim of this study was to evaluate the effects of intraoperative hemoadsorption in high-risk patients with IE undergoing cardiac surgery.

METHODS: A total of 176 high-risk patients with IE were enrolled from 10/2020 to 10/2024. Patients with intraoperative hemoadsorption (HA group, n = 93) were compared to patients without hemoadsorption (control, n = 83). The primary endpoint was a composite of 30-day mortality, incidence of vasoplegic syndrome within the first 24 h and 7 days postoperatively, and intensive care (ICU) stay, analyzed using an unmatched hierarchical win-ratio method.

RESULTS: There were no differences in baseline characteristics between the groups. The mean hemoadsorption time was 106 ± 61 min in the HA group. Vasoplegic syndrome was more frequent in the control group (49.4% vs. 24.7%, p < 0.001). Importantly, 30-day mortality was also significantly lower with intraoperative hemoadsorption (7.5% vs. 20.5%, p = 0.003). The mean ICU stay was shorter in the HA group (7.8 ± 4.6 vs. 11.5 ± 4.2 days, p < 0.001). The analysis met the primary endpoint in favor of patients receiving intraoperative hemoadsorption (win ratio 3.83; 95% CI 2.55, 5.74; p < 0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: In high-risk cardiac surgery patients with IE, the intraoperative use of hemoadsorption was associated with a significantly lower incidence of postoperative vasoplegic syndrome and lower overall 30-day mortality. These findings should be interpreted in the context of the study's methodological limitations and confirmed in future randomized controlled trials.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: This study was approved by the Institutional Review Board (IRB00012919) of the French Society of Thoracic and Cardiovascular Surgery (CERCSFCTCV20251021).

articles.title: Severe growth retardation in Dent disease: a case report of a novel OCRL variant.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Dent disease type 2 (DD-2) is a rare X-linked recessive renal tubulopathy caused by mutations in the OCRL gene. Clinically it is characterised by low molecular weight proteinuria (LMWP), hypercalciuria, and nephrocalcinosis. The phenotypic spectrum of DD-2 is expanding with the identification of new pathogenic variants.

CASE REPORT: A 12-year-old male presenting with marked short stature and poor weight gain was found to have LMWP, haematuria, hypercalciuria, and bilateral nephrocalcinosis on initial clinical evaluation. Renal function was normal. There was no relevant family history. Genetic analysis revealed a hemizygous missense variant (c.899 C > A; p.Ala300Asp) in the OCRL gene, which has not been previously reported in the literature. No abnormalities were found on ocular or neurological examination as the same gene also causes Lowe syndrome. Therefore DD-2 was considered in this patient. Hydrochlorothiazide treatment was initiated but discontinued due to hypokalaemia. Growth hormone therapy was started by the endocrinology clinic due to severe growth retardation.

CONCLUSION: Dent disease can present with a wide range of clinical findings. This case report describes a novel OCRL gene variant associated with DD-2. This newly identified variant contributes to the genotypic and phenotypic diversity of the disease, however, without functional validation, it is difficult to determine whether growth retardation is a significant complication in DD-2. Early diagnosis and a multidisciplinary approach are crucial for improving long-term outcomes.

articles.title: Fluent but not fail-safe: machine-translated radiology reports still need expert review.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Cross-border care, teleradiology, and international referral pathways increasingly require radiology report translation, but isolated mistranslations may alter clinical meaning. We evaluated German-to-English machine translation of radiology reports and correction-based localization of text requiring review.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this retrospective study, 310 de-identified German radiology reports from June and July 2025 were translated into English with DeepL. Eight radiologists assigned 5-point quality scores and corrected perceived errors. Thirty reports were reviewed by all eight readers, and 280 reports were assigned for single-reader evaluation, yielding 520 evaluations. Automated metrics and large language model judges were tested for report-level identification of translations requiring review; a correction-based segment-level edit-prediction model was evaluated on held-out shared reports.

RESULTS: Most translations were rated good or excellent (339/520, 65.2%), but clinically important mistranslations involved diagnosis, anatomy, and radiologic terminology. Agreement was low for ordinal quality scores (Krippendorff α = 0.078, p = 0.006) but high for expert corrections (pairwise "bilingual evaluation understudy"-BLEU = 83.0, p < 0.001). In the conservative primary screen of 30 shared reports, no automated method discriminated translations requiring review (area under receiver operating characteristic curve [AUC] = 0.51-0.65; p = 0.100-0.920). The final edit-prediction model achieved a concordance index of 0.697 and an AUC of 0.731 for segments edited by at least six of eight readers.

CONCLUSION: Machine-translated radiology reports were often acceptable on average, but translations containing errors requiring expert review persisted. Expert corrections were more reproducible than ordinal quality scores and supported localization of text requiring human review.

KEY POINTS: Question Cross-border radiology workflows increasingly require report translation, but fluent machine translations may still contain meaning-changing errors requiring expert review for safe care. Findings Most machine translations were rated good or excellent, yet clinically important mistranslations occurred, and automated report-level metrics did not reliably identify reports needing review. Relevance statement Machine translation may support cross-border radiology workflows, but clinically important mistranslations in otherwise fluent reports require human-in-the-loop oversight and tools that localize text requiring expert review.

articles.title: Contextualizing Trends in Television Viewing and Computer Use Among U.S. Children Aged 5-11 Years, 2001-2018.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Excessive screen time among children is linked to adverse physical, mental, and developmental outcomes. The putative drivers of increasing screen time among school-aged children in the United States remain unclear. Population-level changes may arise from intracohort change (IC)-change in average screen time across survey cycles-or cohort replacement (CR), as later-born cohorts with different levels of screen time replace earlier-born cohorts.

METHODS: We analyzed nine 2-year National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) cycles from 2001 to 2002 through 2017-2018, including 9,841 children aged 5-11 years old. Screen time was measured as the sum of proxy-reported estimates of daily hours of TV/video viewing and computer use. Using linear and algebraic decomposition techniques, we partitioned total change (TC) in screen time into IC and CR components. Models adjusted for demographic, wellness, family, and food security factors.

RESULTS: The weighted mean estimated daily screen time increased from 2.95 to 4.26 h (Δ = 1.31;44%). Boys consistently had higher proxy-reported mean screen time than girls. In the unadjusted model, IC contributed positively to the increase in screen time, whereas CR partially offset it. These opposing contributions persisted across all adjustment models.

DISCUSSION: Combined estimated daily screen time among U.S. children aged 5-11 years increased significantly between 2001 and 2018. Increases within birth cohorts were the main source of this rise, while cohort replacement partially offset it. Differences in screen time across birth cohorts were shaped by changing demographics and family environments.

articles.title: Nonlinear age-related differences in clinical profiles of obstructive sleep apnea: a cross-sectional study of 1,508 Chinese patients.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To characterize age-related clinical profiles and nonlinear age associations in treatment-naive Chinese patients with obstructive sleep apnea (OSA).

METHODS: This retrospective cross-sectional study included 1,508 patients aged 18-88 years at Peking Union Medical College Hospital (2022-2025). Clinical and polysomnographic characteristics were compared across five age groups. Restricted cubic splines assessed continuous-age associations, with separate overall and nonlinearity tests and sex-adjusted sensitivity analyses. Sex-adjusted logistic models evaluated prevalent severity, sleepiness, and cardiometabolic comorbidities; age-quartile comparisons were supplementary.

RESULTS: Among 1,840 participants undergoing PSG, OSA detection differed across ages, with a greater increase among women (age-by-sex interaction P = 0.031). Respiratory severity was broadly comparable across age groups. In unadjusted analyses, body mass index and Epworth Sleepiness Scale scores showed nonlinear age associations (both P < 0.001), as did lowest oxygen saturation (P = 0.018) and selected Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI) components. Global PSQI was associated with age overall, without clear nonlinearity (P = 0.099). Sex adjustment attenuated nonlinearity for oxygen saturation and sleep latency. Older age was associated with higher prevalence odds of hypertension, cardiovascular disease, and diabetes. Excessive daytime sleepiness showed a midlife elevation.

CONCLUSION: OSA clinical profiles differ across ages, with nonlinearity in selected measures. Older patients have greater comorbidity burden and poorer reported sleep quality despite comparable respiratory severity.

articles.title: Single-cell Transcriptomics in Autoimmune Diseases: Mechanistic Insights, Cross-disease Convergence, and Translational Challenges in Rheumatoid Arthritis, Systemic Lupus Erythematosus, Type 1 Diabetes, and Multiple Sclerosis.
articles.abstract: Autoimmune diseases are characterized by loss of immune tolerance and substantial heterogeneity across patients, tissues, and disease stages. Although bulk transcriptomic studies have identified important inflammatory pathways, they cannot directly resolve rare, transitional, and tissue-contextualized cell states that may be relevant to disease mechanisms and therapeutic response. Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) enables transcriptomic profiling at cellular resolution, while complementary multimodal, receptor-repertoire, epigenomic, and spatial approaches can link cellular states to protein phenotype, clonal architecture, regulatory programs, and tissue context. This review critically examines recent single-cell studies in rheumatoid arthritis, systemic lupus erythematosus and lupus nephritis, type 1 diabetes, and multiple sclerosis. Rather than providing a descriptive catalogue of published studies, we assess the strength of available evidence by distinguishing independently replicated findings from observations supported by limited studies, and cross-sectional associations from longitudinal, treatment-response, and functional evidence. Across the selected diseases, studies repeatedly report inflammatory programs involving interferon signaling, chemokine-mediated immune recruitment, and stromal-immune interactions; however, evidence for convergence at the cell-state and regulatory-network levels remains limited, and the extent to which shared signatures represent common pathogenic mechanisms rather than inflammatory context remains uncertain. We evaluate the translational potential of scRNA-seq for biomarker discovery, patient stratification, and treatment response prediction, while considering evidence from related tissue-based molecular stratification approaches, including the R4RA randomized trial in rheumatoid arthritis. R4RA provides prospective randomized evidence that synovial molecular features can enrich for differential therapeutic responses, but its use of bulk synovial transcriptomics and histopathology does not constitute prospective validation of single-cell-derived biomarkers. We further highlight cohort biases, reproducibility challenges, dissociation artifacts, computational ambiguity, and privacy concerns that constrain immediate clinical implementation. Together, these advances position single-cell profiling as a mechanistic discovery platform with substantial translational promise, contingent on standardization, validation across diverse cohorts, and integration with functional perturbation approaches.

articles.title: Comprehensive Assessment of Babesia gibsoni Infection in Dogs: Clinicopathological, Imaging, and Oxidative Stress Perspectives.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: The present study investigated clinico-pathological alterations associated with naturally occurring Babesia gibsoni infection in dogs from Mizoram, India.

METHODS: Diagnosis was established using rapid antibody detection, microscopic blood smear examination, and polymerase chain reaction (PCR). Blood samples were collected to study the haemogram, and serum samples were used for the evaluation of serum biochemical profile and oxidant-antioxidant indices. Abdominal ultrasonography was performed in the infected dogs.

RESULTS: Of 138 samples screened, 43 (31.15%), 70 (50.72%), and 85 (61.59%) were positive by rapid antibody test, blood smear examination, and PCR, respectively. The most consistent clinical signs included depression/lethargy, inappetence/anorexia, and pyrexia. Splenomegaly and splenic lesions were the most consistent ultrasonographic findings noticed. Major haemato-biochemical alterations comprised anaemia, leukocytosis with neutrophilia and eosinophilia, thrombocytopaenia, hypoproteinaemia, hypoalbuminaemia, hyperbilirubinaemia, azotaemia, and increased alanine aminotransferase (ALT), alkaline phosphatase (ALP), and C-reactive protein (CRP) levels. Dogs with B. gibsoni infection exhibited significantly (P < 0.001) higher lipid peroxide (LPO) levels and significantly (P < 0.001) lower total antioxidant capacity (T-AOC) and reduced glutathione (GSH). Red blood cell (RBC) count showed a negative correlation with LPO (r = - 0.741; P < 0.01) and a positive correlation with GSH (r = 0.714; P < 0.01) and T-AOC (r = 0.828; P < 0.01), indicating a role of oxidant-antioxidant imbalance in the severity of anaemia.

CONCLUSION: These findings underscore the multiorgan involvement of the disease and suggest a potential role of oxidative stress in the pathogenesis of B. gibsoni-induced anaemia in dogs.

articles.title: Melatonin Exerts Neuroprotective Effects in Escherichia coli/Lipopolysaccharide Induced Neuronal Injury via Regulating TFRC-Related Ferroptosis.
articles.abstract: Neonatal bacterial meningitis (NBM) is a severe neonatal infectious disease associated with a high incidence of neurological sequelae. Lipopolysaccharide (LPS) and inflammatory cytokines aggravate cerebral injury, whereas the mechanism of ferroptosis in the pathogenesis of NBM remains unclear. Melatonin (MT), an endogenous neurohormone, provides anti-ferroptotic neuroprotection in models of cerebral injury; however, its mechanism of action against NBM-related injury through ferroptosis has not been clarified. This study investigated the protective effects mediated by MT in vivo and in vitro. Rat models of LPS-induced inflammatory brain injury were established through intracerebroventricular (i.c.v.) injection, and Escherichia coli (E. coli)-infected cell models were developed to investigate the neuroprotective effects of MT against TFRC-related ferroptosis. CCK-8 assays, Western blotting, transmission electron microscopy (TEM), iron detection, and immunofluorescence, BODIPY staining were used to assess cell viability, inflammatory factors, mitochondrial ultrastructure, iron accumulation, and GPX4 expression. E. coli infection induced typical ferroptotic mitochondrial damage. MT alleviated neuroinflammation and reduced the expression of ferroptosis-related proteins both in vitro and in vivo. MT treatment increased mitochondrial GPX4 expression. The ferroptosis agonist RSL3 reversed the neuroprotective effects of MT. MT inhibited TFRC-related ferroptosis and alleviated neuronal damage. MT protects against E. coli/Lipopolysaccharide induced neuronal injury by regulating TFRC-related ferroptosis, indicating that MT may be a promising therapeutic agent for NBM.

articles.title: Development and independent regional validation of a dynamic ultrasound appendicitis score for suspected acute appendicitis: a prospective multicenter study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute appendicitis is the most common surgical emergency. Although CT is highly accurate, radiation exposure is a major concern in children, young adults, and pregnant women. Ultrasound is radiation-free but operator-dependent, and current scores rely on static weights without accounting for important patient-finding interactions.

OBJECTIVE: To develop and independently validate a Dynamic Ultrasound Appendicitis Score (Dynamic UAS) with interaction effects to improve risk stratification and potentially avoid unnecessary CT examinations.

METHODS: A prospective multicenter study collected development (n = 802) and independent regional external validation (n = 262) data. The Dynamic UAS was derived using multivariable logistic regression with interaction terms and internally validated using bootstrapping (1000 resamples).

RESULTS: A web-based calculator was developed. A sensitivity analysis addressed limitations of the reference standard, non-visualized appendix, and missing data. Appendicitis prevalence was 33.3% (development) and 32.8% (validation). The Dynamic UAS performed excellently in diagnosing acute appendicitis (AUC 0.96 and 0.94) and outperformed known scores (AUC 0.81 to 0.91). At the ≥ 6 level, sensitivity was 91.7%/90.7%, and specificity was 97.1%/96.0%. Calibration was good (slope 0.89, Brier 0.098). In non-visualized appendix cases, the AUC was 0.89 (95% CI: 0.84 to 0.93) in the external validation cohort and 0.90 (95% CI: 0.85 to 0.94) in the development cohort. The model is not very useful for distinguishing complicated from uncomplicated appendicitis (AUC 0.72).

CONCLUSIONS: The Dynamic UAS is a novel, independently validated tool that may reduce unnecessary CT use in radiation-sensitive populations and resource-limited settings. Future studies in different international settings are needed.

articles.title: Temporal trends in the clinical presentation, management, and outcomes of children with congenital cytomegalovirus infection.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Congenital cytomegalovirus (cCMV) is the most common congenital infection and a leading cause of sensorineural hearing loss as well as neurodevelopmental impairment. In recent years, awareness, screening, and management strategies for cCMV have evolved. This study aimed to assess temporal changes in the clinical presentation, treatment, and outcomes of children diagnosed with cCMV infection. We conducted a retrospective cohort analysis using data from the CCMVnet registry ( www.ccmvnet.org ), an international multicenter database collecting anonymized data on children with confirmed cCMV infection. A total of 1653 patients diagnosed between 2011 and 2024 were included and divided into two cohorts: 2011-2016 (n = 566) and 2017-2024 (n = 1087). The year 2017 was selected as a pragmatic cutoff, corresponding to the year of publication of the European expert consensus statement on congenital CMV. Children were identified through antenatal, clinical, hearing-related, and newborn screening pathways. Symptomatic cCMV at birth was defined by the presence of at least one predefined clinical, laboratory, hearing, or neuroimaging finding based on previously published criteria. A comparative analysis between two distinct time periods was conducted, encompassing neonatal clinical findings, neuroimaging results, treatment strategies, and long-term outcomes. Newborns classified as symptomatic at birth decreased in the more recent cohort, from 49.2% in P1 to 44.2% in P2 (p = 0.07). The use of intravenous ganciclovir decreased from 7.3% to 2.8% (p < 0.001), while the use of oral valganciclovir alone increased from 43.8% to 78.7% (p < 0.001). Differences in long-term outcomes were observed between the two periods, with motor impairment at 12 months decreasing from 16.5% to 6.2% (p < 0.001) and any long-term sequelae at 36 months decreasing from 40.0% to 31.0% (p = 0.05).

CONCLUSION: This study highlights temporal differences in the clinical spectrum, management, and outcomes of children with congenital CMV infection in Europe. The higher proportion of asymptomatic and mildly symptomatic children in the latter period may reflect changes in maternal and neonatal screening practices. The observed temporal differences provide insight into the evolving clinical landscape of cCMV diagnosis and management, while their underlying causes cannot be determined from the present data.

WHAT IS KNOWN: • Congenital cytomegalovirus (cCMV) infection is the leading infectious cause of sensorineural hearing loss and neurodevelopmental impairment in children. • Clinical management of cCMV has evolved substantially over the last decade, particularly following the publication of the European expert consensus statement in 2017 and alongside expanding screening strategies.

WHAT IS NEW: • In our cohort, children diagnosed with cCMV after 2017 presented with milder clinical manifestations and experienced fewer long-term sequelae than those diagnosed before 2017. • Temporal changes in diagnostic pathways, treatment practices, and clinical outcomes were observed between the two study periods.

articles.title: Leveraging High-Frequency Postoperative ICU Arterial Blood Pressure Data from Electronic Health Records for Research: A Brief Report.
articles.abstract: Postoperative blood pressure fluctuations after cardiac surgery are highly clinically relevant, yet analyzing high-frequency arterial pressure data remains challenging. In this study, we introduce a novel methodology for processing minute-by-minute postoperative intensive care unit (ICU) arterial pressure data. The pipeline implements a series of systematic data-cleaning steps to resolve artifacts and ensure physiological plausibility, and deploys a multi-stage imputation framework to address missing intervals. Our approach constructs longitudinal blood pressure profiles that quantify the time spent within predefined blood pressure ranges, minimizing assumptions and enhancing data utility for research. We detail a rigorous and reusable workflow for data extraction, cleaning, and imputation, which may address limitations of previous methods and offer a framework to build a robust exposure metric for future research utilizing postoperative arterial pressure data.

articles.title: A comprehensive review of European clinical practice guidelines on psychological and cognitive assessment and support for cancer patients and their families.
articles.journal: Supportive care in cancer : official journal of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Cancer remains a leading cause of mortality worldwide and, consequently, awareness of the psychological and cognitive challenges faced by patients and their families increases. To address these needs, psycho-oncological Clinical Practice Guidelines (CPGs) and recommendations have been progressively developed. This systematic review aimed to provide a comprehensive overview of existing European CPGs and recommendations regarding psychological and cognitive assessment and support for cancer patients and their families.

METHODS: A literature search was conducted on PsycINFO, Scopus, and Medline (PubMed interface), supplemented by a secondary search strategy. Only CPGs published in the last 15 years were considered. Data extraction focused on guideline characteristics, target population, symptoms addressed, assessment tools, recommended interventions, and quality appraisal.

RESULTS: After the screening phase, 38 publications were included. An increase in the publication of psycho-oncological guidelines emerges across European countries and the rise of a multidisciplinary approach. Most CPGs address adult cancer patients and prioritise distress, anxiety, and depression. Common screening tools are the Distress Thermometer and the Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale. Concerning interventions, psychosocial support and counselling are the most recommended forms of support, while digital and family-centred interventions are scarcely mentioned. Looking at the level of evidence and strength of recommendations, heterogeneity was observed across CPGs.

CONCLUSION: The rise of CPGs represents an effort to integrate psycho-oncological assistance into cancer care in Europe, but gaps in inclusivity, protocols, and implementation remain. Future guidelines should address underserved groups, enhance methodological quality of the CPGs, and include digital and family-centred interventions to improve equitable access and holistic care.

articles.title: Epidemiology, determinants, and microbiological profile of implant-associated infections following intramedullary nailing in a tertiary hospital in Ethiopia.
articles.journal: Archives of orthopaedic and trauma surgery
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Implant-associated infections after intramedullary nailing (IMN) are a major cause of morbidity in patients with long bone fractures. This study aimed to determine the magnitude, determinants, and microbiological profile of such infections in a tertiary hospital in Ethiopia.

METHODS: A hospital-based cross-sectional study was conducted among 260 patients who underwent IMN for lower extremity long bone fractures between January 2021 and December 2023. Clinical data, operative details, and microbiological results were collected, and logistic regression was applied to identify determinants of infection.

RESULTS: The overall infection rate was 8.46% (95% CI: 5.38-12.53; 22/260), comprising 4.62% deep and 3.85% superficial infections. We found that emergency surgery and hospital stay longer than 14 days were independently associated with an increased risk of infection. Among the limited number of culture-positive infections, Gram-negative bacteria predominated, with Escherichia coli as the most frequently identified pathogen.

CONCLUSION: The infection rate was higher than in many other settings, underscoring the need for improved perioperative infection prevention and reduced hospital stays. Findings highlight the importance of perioperative optimization and hospital infection control in LMICs.

articles.title: Strain-Based Assessment of Post-TAVR Left Bundle Branch Block in Bicuspid Aortic Valve Using Patient-Specific Computational Modeling.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Post-transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) left bundle branch block (LBBB) is the most common post-TAVR cardiac conduction abnormality (CCA), particularly in bicuspid aortic valve (BAV). Prior computational studies evaluated generalized CCA risk but did not quantify LBBB-specific mechanical injury or compare self-expanding (SE) and balloon-expandable (BE) devices in BAV. This proof-of-concept study established a patient-specific computational framework to (1) quantify mechanical stretch in the left bundle branch (LBB)-adjacent region, (2) identify a preliminary, cohort-specific strain-based separation value associated with post-TAVR LBBB, and (3) compare device-related LBBB risk trends between SE and BE devices.

METHODS: Cardiac CT scans from six type I BAV TAVR patients were analyzed (two with LBBB and four without CCA). Patient-specific finite element models incorporated anatomy and leaflet calcification. The LBB region was defined using membranous septum length and anatomical landmarks. Simulations reproduced implantation of deployed SE devices and virtual BE devices at standardized depth. Area-weighted logarithmic strain (LE), contact pressure, oversizing index, eccentricity index, and expansion metrics were computed.

RESULTS: LBB-adjacent LE showed clear separation (0.15-0.24 in LBBB vs. 0.03-0.11 without CCA), with 0.11 as a preliminary cohort-specific separation value. Mean LE was higher with SE than BE devices (0.11 vs. 0.08). Contact pressure showed no consistent association with outcome, suggesting that LE differences reflect multiple contributing factors.

CONCLUSION: In this six-patient cohort, LBB-adjacent strain clearly separated LBBB from No-LBBB cases, whereas contact pressure showed no consistent relationship with outcome. Larger cohorts and sensitivity analyses are needed to establish its clinical utility for BAV TAVR risk stratification or device selection.

articles.title: Point-of-care ultrasound in obstetrics and gynecology: latest advancements and evolution.
articles.abstract: Point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) in obstetrics and gynecology has evolved from a pragmatic bedside adjunct into a rapidly expanding clinical, educational and technological field. Since the publication of earlier narrative reviews, the discipline has been reshaped by handheld ultrasound systems, wireless probes, cloud-based image management, tele-ultrasound, artificial intelligence (AI) for image acquisition and interpretation, and the first specific practice guidance for POCUS in obstetrics and gynecology. This narrative review summarizes recent advances and proposes a clinically useful framework for the European ultrasound community. POCUS should be understood as a focused, problem-oriented and immediately actionable ultrasound examination performed and interpreted by the treating clinician. It is not a replacement for guideline-based screening, detailed fetal anatomy assessment, comprehensive transvaginal gynecologic imaging, Doppler surveillance or expert ultrasound. The strongest evidence supports POCUS for early pregnancy triage, confirmation of fetal viability and presentation, basic assessment of placental location and amniotic fluid, intrapartum evaluation of fetal head position and selected postpartum or gynecologic emergencies. In gynecology, POCUS can accelerate triage of acute pelvic pain, suspected ectopic pregnancy, intrauterine device position and adnexal pathology, but definitive risk stratification of complex masses remains a task for standardized specialist sonography. Technological progress has been substantial: handheld devices now provide diagnostically useful images for several focused tasks, AI-enabled blind-sweep protocols can estimate gestational age and fetal malpresentation in low-resource settings, and tele-ultrasound can extend expert support beyond tertiary centers. The next phase of OB/GYN POCUS will depend less on device availability than on implementation: indication-specific protocols, formal training, competency assessment, documentation, image archiving, infection control, data protection, quality assurance and clear escalation rules. POCUS in obstetrics and gynecology should therefore be framed as a governed clinical pathway rather than a device-driven shortcut.

articles.title: Retrograde access revascularization in chronic limb threatening ischaemia.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Chronic limb-threatening ischaemia (CLTI) is associated with high rates of major amputation, mortality and comorbidity that can make conventional femoral access challenging or contraindicated; in particular in patients with recent groin surgery, infection, previous aorto-bifemoral stent reconstruction, hostile groins, or unfavourable body habitus. Tibio-pedal arterial minimally invasive retrograde revascularisation (TAMI) provides an alternative access strategy.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective single-centre cohort study included 84 TAMI procedures in 81 limbs from 77 patients with CLTI (median age 72 years; 64% male; Rutherford IV 22%; Rutherford V-VI 78%). TAMI was performed because of recent groin surgery/infection in 35% of procedures and patient-related factors in 65%. The primary clinical endpoint was freedom from major adverse limb events (MALE), defined as major amputation or clinically driven target-vessel reintervention (CDTVR). Secondary endpoints included technical success, defined as restoration of continuous inline flow through at least one infrapopliteal artery to the foot with < 50% residual stenosis on completion angiography, and access vessel safety.

RESULTS: Retrograde access was obtained predominantly via the dorsalis pedis (71%) and distal posterior tibial arteries (16%). Technical success was achieved in 66/84 procedures (78%); in 10/84 (12%), TAMI access and lesion crossing were successful but the predefined angiographic endpoint was not met, while eight procedures (10%) were abandoned. Asymptomatic access vessel spasm was documented in 35/84 procedures (42%) that had resolved by 24 h. Among 68 patients (71 limbs) with longitudinal follow-up, median follow-up was 150 days (IQR 76-322). CDTVR occurred in 22/71 limbs (30%) and major amputation in 14/71 (20%); 25/68 patients (37%) died. Kaplan-Meier estimated freedom from MALE was 57.9% (95% CI 43.9-69.6%) at 6 months and 51.2% (95% CI 36.0-64.5%) at 12 months. In multivariable Cox regression analysis, none of the evaluated covariates was significantly associated with MALE.

CONCLUSION: In this selected, anatomically complex CLTI cohort, TAMI was a feasible alternative access strategy when conventional femoral access was challenging or not feasible, with a low observed rate of clinically significant pedal access complications.

articles.title: Postnatal evolution of electrocardiographic parameters in preterm infants: a prospective longitudinal cohort study.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Electrocardiography (ECG), an indispensable bedside tool in neonatal intensive care, complements echocardiography by providing assessment of cardiac rhythm and conduction, and when advanced imaging is unavailable, serves as a screening tool. Preterm birth alters cardiac and autonomic maturation. Applying term-based ECG norms may misclassify physiological findings in preterm. We aimed to characterise serial ECG maturation in preterms from birth to term-equivalent age and define gestational- and postnatal-age-specific patterns relevant to clinical interpretation. In this prospective cohort, infants between 28⁰/₇ and 36⁶/₇ weeks' gestation without congenital heart disease underwent serial 11-lead ECG recording within 24 h of birth, on day 7, day 28 and at term-equivalent age. Postnatal and gestation-based differences in ECG parameters were analysed and centile charts were generated. Among 249 infants (mean gestation-334/₇ weeks), 213 completed follow-up until term-equivalent age. ECG parameters demonstrated consistent maturation across time points. The mean QRS axis shifted leftward from 117° at birth to 82° at term-equivalent age (p < 0.001). PR-interval, QRS and P-wave duration remained stable across all time points. Mean QTc showed minimal overall change. Transient QTc prolongation occurred in 8.1% of infants and resolved by term-equivalent age. Right precordial R-wave amplitudes declined over time, whereas left precordial amplitudes increased. At term-equivalent age, very preterm infants exhibited a more leftward QRS axis compared with late preterm infants. Infants with bronchopulmonary dysplasia showed trends toward right ventricular dominance.

CONCLUSION: Preterm ECG findings are dynamic, gestation-dependent markers of cardiovascular transition. This study characterises longitudinal ECG maturation in preterms and provides reference values, supporting improved decision-making in preterm care.

WHAT IS KNOWN: • Electrocardiographic reference nomograms used in neonatal practice are primarily based on paediatric cohorts or cross-sectional studies of term infants. These references provide limited information on longitudinal electrophysiologic maturation in preterm neonates.

WHAT IS NEW: • In a cohort of 249 preterm infants, serial ECG measurements demonstrated changes in axes, QTc, and precordial voltages from birth to term-equivalent age. • These gestation and age-specific trajectories support cautious interpretation of preterm ECGs using term-derived standards.

articles.title: Robotic cholecystectomy using da Vinci SP, single-site, and multiport systems: a systematic review and comparative meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: Robotic platform names do not specify operative access or instrumentation. We compared da Vinci SP, Single-Site, and multiport cholecystectomy, prioritizing total operative time and planned-access completion failure. Five databases were searched in August 2026, with Scopus rerun on 6 October 2026. A registered review underwent outcome-specific, publication-based adjudication. Direct robot-to-robot mean differences were synthesized using restricted maximum likelihood (REML) and modified Hartung-Knapp confidence intervals (CIs). Single-incision laparoscopic cholecystectomy (SILC) comparisons were ancillary; historical indirect calculations were confined to a supplementary audit. Fourteen reports were included; nine supplied extractable direct data from analysis samples totaling 1,542 participants. For SP versus Single-Site, total operative time was very uncertain (4 studies; 580 participants; mean difference [MD] - 12.49 min; 95% CI - 36.50 to 11.53; I² = 91.0%), including one conditionally reconstructed mean. The full planned-access completion-failure composite was not estimable. Console time was secondary (4 studies; 580 participants; MD - 11.40 min; modified Hartung-Knapp 95% CI - 25.35 to 2.56; I² = 80.4%; approximate 95% prediction interval - 49.03 to 26.24). Its conventional REML-Wald CI excluded zero (- 19.43 to - 3.36), but the small-study-adjusted interval did not. Rare-event safety, long-term hernia, cost-effectiveness, and platform-specific workload evidence were insufficient. The evidence is very uncertain about differences in total operative and console time between da Vinci SP and Single-Site cholecystectomy. An overall operative-time advantage or comparative safety equivalence has not been established. The evidence does not isolate the causal effects of incision count and articulation.Review registration: PROSPERO CRD420261475321.

articles.title: Impact of Holika Dahan on ambient PM2.5 and associated health risks in an urban environment of Lucknow, India.
articles.abstract: Large-scale biomass-mix burning of Holika Dahan (HD) is celebrated before the Indian traditional festival Holi, which has adverse effects on air quality and health. This study aimed to assess chemical characteristics of airborne PM2.5, source contributions, emission dispersions, and related health risks during pre-HD, HD, and post-HD sequential nights for a residential area and a commercial area in Lucknow. Compared with pre-HD night, concentrations of ambient PM2.5 were higher during HD night by factors of 2.0 and 1.4 in the respective residential and commercial areas. Tracer signatures of PM2.5 emissions from HD biomass-mix combustion ranged from 1.2 to 2.7 times higher during HD night than during pre-HD night. Further, the peaks in the spectrum of ATR-FTIR functional group markers of PM2.5 samples indicate the impact of HD biomass-mix combustion on local air quality. In addition to peaks in marker species of HD emission, PCA and HCA statistics further confirmed that HD biomass-burning is the predominant source of PM2.5 at both study sites. The HYSPLIT simulated the HD emission transport paths towards primary eastward and south-eastward. The AERMOD dispersion hotspot isopleths indicated the extent of localised propagation of HD emissions up to 1.2 km and 1.5 km for residential and commercial areas, respectively. The hazard index (HI) values were found below the USEPA permissible limit, indicating negligible non-carcinogenic health risk despite the record of high HIs on HD night. Whereas the cancer risk (CR) exceeded USEPA safe limits due to HD impact at both the sites, however, peak CR was observed during HD night. The findings of the study highlighted short-term air quality degradation and potential long-term health concerns associated particularly with Holi festival-related HD combustion.

articles.title: Aldosterone-mineralocorticoid receptor signaling and residual cardiorenal risk in type 2 diabetes.
articles.abstract: Clinically important cardiorenal risk persists in type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) despite major advances in metabolic and organ-protective therapy. This narrative review evaluates aldosterone-mineralocorticoid receptor (MR) signaling as one potential contributor and separates mechanistic plausibility from clinical-outcome evidence. PubMed, Embase, Web of Science Core Collection, and ClinicalTrials.gov searches, together with supplementary searches using the Foreign Medical Literature Retrieval Service (FMRS; Metstr), were updated through 22 September 2026; titles/abstracts and relevant full texts were independently screened by two authors. Experimental and observational evidence links MR signaling with inflammation, oxidative stress, fibrosis, endothelial dysfunction, and cardiorenal remodeling, but circulating aldosterone, renin, and the aldosterone-to-renin ratio have no validated thresholds for identifying clinically relevant tissue MR activation or predicting treatment response in unselected T2DM. In T2DM with chronic kidney disease (CKD) receiving maximum tolerated renin-angiotensin system blockade, finerenone reduces prespecified kidney and cardiovascular composite outcomes. By contrast, CONFIDENCE and phase 2 BI 690,517 mainly provide urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio-based surrogate evidence, and FINEARTS-HF extends clinical-outcome evidence to heart failure with mildly reduced or preserved ejection fraction but was not restricted to diabetes. We therefore present four candidate domains for future MR-oriented phenotyping as a hypothesis-generating framework, not a diagnostic or treatment-selection algorithm. Overall, MR signaling is best regarded as a biologically plausible contributor within a multifactorial residual-risk model; prospective validation is required before biomarker-guided MR-targeted therapy can be recommended.

articles.title: GLP-1 receptor agonists and hair loss: adverse effect, epiphenomenon, or therapeutic paradox?
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Incretin-based therapies, including glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) and dual/triple agonists, have revolutionized the management of obesity and type 2 diabetes. However, hair loss has emerged as an adverse event in clinical practice. This review synthesizes the evidence on the prevalence, mechanistic pathways, and clinical course of hair loss associated with semaglutide, tirzepatide, and retatrutide.

METHODS: A narrative review was conducted using the PubMed/MEDLINE database. Data were integrated from clinical trials, real-world observational studies, and pharmacovigilance databases to evaluate the oncological and dermatological implications of these therapies.

RESULTS: There is a discrepancy in hair loss prevalence, ranging from 3 to 7% in controlled trials to over 70% in real-world cohorts. Telogen effluvium (TE) is the predominant phenotype, driven primarily by the magnitude and velocity of weight loss rather than drug toxicity. Newer agents like tirzepatide demonstrate stronger associations with hair shedding compared to older GLP-1 RAs. Pharmacovigilance data show inconsistent but significant signals for semaglutide and tirzepatide, with reporting odds ratios indicating a drug-associated risk. Conversely, paradoxical improvements in androgenetic alopecia and inflammatory scarring alopecias have been reported, likely mediated by metabolic normalization and anti-inflammatory effects. Female sex and significant weight reduction (> 10%) were the most robust predictors of hair loss.

CONCLUSION: Hair loss associated with incretin-based therapies is a biologically complex, threshold-dependent phenomenon reflecting systemic metabolic reprogramming.
