While predominantly transient and reversible, its psychological impact can compromise treatment adherence. Clinicians should provide proactive counseling, emphasizing the self-limiting nature of TE in this context while monitoring for diverse follicular responses.

articles.title: Risk of recurrent acute pancreatitis with GLP-1 receptor agonists after prior pancreatitis: a systematic review.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) are widely used for patients with type 2 diabetes (T2D) and obesity. However, their safety in patients with prior pancreatitis remains uncertain. This systematic review aims to evaluate the risk of recurrent acute pancreatitis (RAP) associated with GLP-1 RA therapy.

METHODS: We systematically searched for studies evaluating the safety of GLP-1 receptor agonists in adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) or obesity and a history of acute pancreatitis. The primary outcome was recurrent acute pancreatitis. We included studies of adults with prior acute pancreatitis treated with GLP-1 receptor agonists for type 2 diabetes, obesity, or related metabolic conditions. Studies without recurrent acute pancreatitis outcomes, pediatric populations, overlapping cohorts, insufficient data, or non-original publications were excluded.

RESULTS: We included four studies comprising 10,624 patients, of whom 5,427 (51.0%) received GLP-1 receptor agonists. Two studies provided comparative data (5,224 GLP-1 RA users; 5,197 controls). GLP-1 receptor agonist use was associated with lower odds of recurrent acute pancreatitis than placebo (OR 0.26, 95% CI 0.05-1.32) and lower risk than SGLT2 inhibitor use (OR 0.57, 95% CI 0.52-0.64). Two additional studies provided recurrence rates among GLP-1 RA users with prior pancreatitis, reporting rates of 9.9% (95% CI 5.8%-16.3%) and 11.9% (95% CI 5.1%-25.8%).

CONCLUSION: Across the four included studies, GLP-1 receptor agonist use was not associated with an increase in RAP among patients with a prior history of acute pancreatitis. However, comparative evidence was limited to two studies, warranting cautious interpretation of these findings.

articles.title: Gestational diabetes mellitus in Italian diabetes clinics: clinical characteristics, screening practices and management from the amd annals registry.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) is one of the most common complications of pregnancy and is associated with adverse maternal and neonatal outcomes. Nationwide real-world data describing characteristics , screening practices, clinical management, and quality of care of women with GDM attending diabetes clinics in Italy are limited.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective observational study using data from the AMD Annals Initiative, a well-established large quality-of-care monitoring program. Anonymized clinical data from women with GDM attending participating centers during 2025 were analyzed. Study measures included demographic characteristics, risk factors, oral glucose tolerance test (OGTT) timing and results, therapeutic management, intermediate outcomes, and available maternal and neonatal outcomes.The analysis was descriptive.

RESULTS: A total of 13,487 women with GDM were included. The mean age was 33.6±5.4 years, and 41.1% were aged ≥35 years. Pre-pregnancy overweight and obesity were reported in 28.1% and 24.9% of women, respectively. Overall, 20.3% of women met criteria for early OGTT screening based on established risk factors; however, only 15.2% of eligible women underwent testing within the recommended 16-18-week gestational window. Standard OGTT screening between 24 and 28 weeks was performed in 51.5% of cases. Women tested at 16-18 weeks showed higher fasting glucose levels but lower post-load glucose values than those screened at 24-28 weeks. Mean HbA1c at diagnosis was 5.2±0.7%, and only 0.9% of women had HbA1c ≥6.5%. Dietary treatment alone was used in 63.9% of women, while 33.1% required insulin therapy and 5.6% received metformin. Among women with available delivery data (n=2,288), mean gestational age at delivery was 38.8±1.4 weeks, with cesarean section and labor induction rates of 30.0% and 33.6%, respectively. Neonatal outcomes were recorded for 1,384 of these women, whereas postpartum glucose assessment was available for only 3.1% of the entire cohort.

CONCLUSIONS: This large real-world analysis provides a first nationwide snapshot of the characteristics and quality of care of GDM in Italy. Although management and perinatal outcomes appear broadly consistent with international standards, substantial gaps remain in adherence to recommended screening pathways, particularly the implementation of early OGTT testing in high-risk women. Improving the completeness and standardization of structured data collection, including maternal and neonatal outcomes, will further strengthen the ability of the AMD Annals to monitor and support continuous improvement in GDM care.

articles.title: Moderate therapeutic hypothermia with mechanical left ventricular unloading on non-infarct area in an acute myocardial infarction model.
articles.journal: Journal of artificial organs : the official journal of the Japanese Society for Artificial Organs
articles.abstract: Patients with cardiogenic shock due to acute myocardial infarction (AMI) treated with ECPELLA support have a poor prognosis. Impaired left ventricular (LV) wall motion is observed in both infarcted and non-infarcted areas. Therapeutic hypothermia and mechanical LV unloading have different myocardial protective effects. This study aimed to evaluate myocardial protective effects of moderate therapeutic hypothermia combined with mechanical LV unloading in non-infarcted areas using a porcine AMI model. The coronary artery was ligated, and an extracorporeal ventricular assist device was driven under mean left atrial pressure of 5 mmHg. Cooling was initiated via the thermostatic bath of ECMO 30 min after LAD ligation. Moderate therapeutic hypothermia (30-31 °C) was maintained for 2 h. The final evaluation was performed 30 min after rewarming. In the control group, LV fractional shortening (FS) and LV posterior wall motion score (WMS) were declined. In the hypothermia group, LVFS and LV posterior WMS were preserved. In the posterior wall of hypothermia group, mitochondria structure was maintained, reactive oxygen species production was reduced, and sarcoplasmic/endoplasmic reticulum Ca2+-ATPase expression was maintained more than in the control group. Moderate therapeutic hypothermia combined with mechanical LV unloading might provide more myocardial protection in non-infarcted areas compared to mechanical LV unloading alone in a porcine AMI model.

articles.title: The PVL threat: A multicenter, single-cohort retrospective study of Panton-Valentine leukocidin staphylococcal infections in critically ill children.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Staphylococcus aureus carrying the Panton-Valentine leukocidin (PVL) genes, in both methicillin-susceptible (MSSA) and methicillin-resistant (MRSA) strains, causes severe infection in previously healthy children. We described critically ill children with PVL-positive infection and explored predictors of prolonged intensive care. In this multicenter, single-cohort retrospective study, we included 44 consecutive children aged 0-16 years with PVL-producing S. aureus infection admitted to a neonatal or pediatric intensive care unit (PICU) at 13 Italian centers between 2022 and 2025. The primary outcome was PICU stay above the cohort median. We used Fisher exact tests and exploratory Firth penalized logistic regression, overall and within age strata, with sensitivity analyses. Median age was 22 months (interquartile range [IQR] 11-123); 5 children (11%) were neonates. MSSA caused 25 cases (57%) and MRSA 19 (43%). Necrotizing pneumonia predominated, with excavation in 34 children (77%). Empyema (52%), acute respiratory distress syndrome (41%), pneumothorax (36%) and septic shock (34%) were the leading complications; 41 children (93%) required respiratory support and 4 (9%) extracorporeal membrane oxygenation. Median PICU stay was 17 days (IQR 10-28); 2 children died (5%). Septic shock was associated with prolonged stay (odds ratio 7.2; 95% CI 1.5-49.3), also after adjustment in children ≥ 1 year (adjusted odds ratio 8.0; 95% CI 1.3-49.8), with consistent but imprecise sensitivity analyses.

CONCLUSION: PVL-producing S. aureus caused life-threatening infection at all pediatric ages. Methicillin resistance was not associated with prolonged stay, supporting PVL testing of S. aureus isolates from critically ill children. Predictors of prolonged stay are exploratory and need prospective confirmation.

WHAT IS KNOWN: • PVL-producing S. aureus causes necrotizing pneumonia and disseminated infection in previously healthy children. • Evidence rests largely on case reports and small series, and infants are underrepresented.

WHAT IS NEW: • In 44 critically ill children, including 5 neonates, MSSA and MRSA produced comparable critical illness. • In exploratory analyses, septic shock was associated with prolonged intensive care; mortality was 5%.

articles.title: Recurrent posterior stroke-like lesions heralding COQ8A-related coenzyme Q10 deficiency: a potentially treatable ataxia mistaken for stroke: a case report.
Perineural versus intravenous dexmedetomidine as an adjuvant for ilioinguinal/iliohypogastric nerve block in open inguinal hernia repair: a randomised controlled trial.
articles.journal: Hernia : the journal of hernias and abdominal wall surgery
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Dexmedetomidine is widely added to peripheral nerve blocks, but whether the perineural or intravenous route provides better analgesia-and at what haemodynamic cost-is unclear in inguinal hernia repair. We compared the two routes as adjuncts to an ilioinguinal/iliohypogastric (II/IH) nerve block.

METHODS: This single-centre, triple-blind randomised controlled trial enrolled 90 adults (ASA I-III) undergoing elective open inguinal hernia repair. All received an ultrasound-guided II/IH block (0.5% bupivacaine with epinephrine, 20 mL) and standardised tumescent local anaesthesia, and were randomised 1:1:1 to perineural dexmedetomidine 1 µg/kg (DexLA), intravenous dexmedetomidine 1 µg/kg over 10 min (DexIV), or placebo (Control). The primary outcome was movement-evoked visual analogue scale (VAS, 0-100) pain at 6 h, analysed by intention-to-treat.

RESULTS: Movement VAS at 6 h was lower with perineural dexmedetomidine (DexLA 10.3 ± 10.3) than DexIV (20.0 ± 17.4) or Control (22.0 ± 20.6; overall p = 0.018): DexLA versus Control - 11.7 (95% CI - 21.9 to - 1.4; p = 0.022), whereas DexIV did not differ from Control (p = 0.888). This reduction reached the established minimum clinically important difference of approximately 10 points, although pain was low overall. Time to first opioid was similar (p = 0.723). Bradycardia was more frequent with DexIV (20.0%) than DexLA (3.3%) or Control (6.7%; DexIV vs DexLA p = 0.040); hypotension occurred in 43.3%, 40.0% and 20.0% (p = 0.151).

CONCLUSION: Perineural-but not intravenous-dexmedetomidine produced a clinically relevant reduction in early movement-evoked pain, whereas intravenous dexmedetomidine added bradycardia without analgesic benefit. If dexmedetomidine is used in this setting, the perineural route is preferable.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: Thai Clinical Trials Registry TCTR20220208002; registered 7 February 2022.

articles.title: Longitudinal plasma phosphorylated neurofilament-heavy chain levels in oxaliplatin-induced peripheral neuropathy: a prospective multi-institutional exploratory study.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Reliable circulating biomarkers for chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy (CIPN) remain lacking. Phosphorylated neurofilament-heavy chain (pNF-H) is an axon-oriented biomarker of neuroaxonal injury, but its clinical relevance in oxaliplatin-induced peripheral neuropathy has not been established. We evaluated the feasibility and longitudinal behavior of plasma pNF-H in patients receiving oxaliplatin-based chemotherapy.

METHODS: This prospective multi-institutional exploratory study included patients with unresectable or recurrent colorectal cancer receiving CapeOX plus bevacizumab as part of the NYX study, a randomised trial of ninjin'yoeito (NYT; TJ-108, Tsumura & Co., Tokyo, Japan), a twelve-ingredient Kampo herbal extract, at 9.0 g/day for 24 weeks in the NYT arm. Plasma samples were collected at baseline, at clinically assessed CIPN onset (follow-up 1), and at the time of neuropathy resolution, at cycle 9, or at discontinuation, whichever came first (follow-up 2). Plasma pNF-H concentrations were measured by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay. CIPN was assessed using CTCAE version 5.0.

RESULTS: Thirty patients with evaluable plasma samples were included. Plasma pNF-H levels showed substantial inter-individual variability without a consistent temporal pattern. Compared with baseline and CIPN onset, plasma pNF-H levels at follow-up 2 were modestly but significantly increased. However, plasma pNF-H levels were not associated with the onset, severity, or persistence of clinically assessed CIPN.

CONCLUSIONS: Although longitudinal plasma pNF-H measurement was technically feasible, pNF-H did not function as a clinically meaningful biomarker for oxaliplatin-induced peripheral neuropathy. These findings may reflect a pathophysiological mismatch between dorsal root ganglion neuronal cell body injury and the axon-oriented biological specificity of pNF-H.

articles.title: Feasibility and acceptability of a telehealth-supported physical activity program for children with chronic kidney disease: a pilot mixed methods study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Children with chronic kidney disease (CKD) often experience high levels of physical inactivity, exacerbating their health challenges and diminishing their quality of life. Given the potential health risks and reported barriers to sustained engagement in physical activity interventions, our objective was to evaluate the feasibility and acceptability of an individualized telehealth-supported physical activity program for adolescents with CKD stages 2-5.

METHODS: This study was a 2-arm randomized waitlist control intervention to evaluate a 12-week telehealth physical activity program in children with CKD. Eligible participants, aged 11-18 years with CKD stages 2-5, were randomized via permuted block randomization, with CKD stage and sex as stratification factors, into a waitlist control (WLC) or physical activity intervention group. The treatment group received every 2-weeks video visits and personalized physical activity plans to increase or maintain ≥150 min of moderate to vigorous physical activity/week. All participants received a remotely tracked fitness wearable. Demographic and disease-based characteristics were collected at baseline to assess group differences. End-of-treatment surveys were conducted to assess acceptability, and inductive qualitative analysis was performed on two open-ended questions for both participant and guardian.

RESULTS: Of 400 patients screened for eligibility, 37 were randomized (19 to waitlist control, 18 to treatment) with a recruitment rate of 4/month and an attrition rate of 2.7%. No demographic or disease characteristic differences were observed between groups. High fitness wearable adherence was observed in 35 participants. Median telehealth visit compliance was 83%. Qualitative analysis identified 3 categories: accountability and motivation (>30% citations from participants and parents relating to instructor motivation and accountability), the interplay of physical or mental health and physical activity (44% participant physical health), and personalization of the program to limit barriers to implementation (52% participant activity type, 44% participant education).

CONCLUSION: Telehealth-supported physical activity intervention is feasible in children with CKD with low attrition rates and high compliance to visits. Participants and guardians identified personalization and engagement strategies as central to their experience of the program, suggesting these may be important to intervention success.

articles.title: [Early infantile nystagmus from the neuropediatric perspective].
articles.abstract: The differential diagnostic work-up of (early) infantile nystagmus depends largely on the presence of syndromic or neurological abnormalities, in addition to the child's age and ocular findings. In some cases, a careful medical history and physical examination alone are sufficient to establish a diagnosis. Electrophysiology, imaging, molecular genetics and metabolic diagnostics are further essential components of the neuropediatric part of the problem analysis. This paper aims to provide guidance on how to proceed in a way that is as efficient as possible and as gentle as possible on the child.

articles.title: Management and outcomes of moderate-to-severe pelvic ring fractures: a 10-year experience from an Australian Level 1 Trauma Centre.
articles.journal: European journal of trauma and emergency surgery : official publication of the European Trauma Society
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Moderate-to-severe pelvic ring fractures are associated with high morbidity and mortality despite advances in resuscitation, development in trauma systems and multispecialty haemorrhage control. This study aimed to describe the management strategies and clinical outcomes of moderate-to-severe pelvic ring fractures over a 10-year period at an Australian Level I Trauma Centre.

METHODS: A retrospective observational cohort study was performed of patients aged ≥ 16 years with moderate-to-severe pelvic ring fractures (Abbreviated Injury Scale (AIS) ≥ 3) treated between January 2015 and December 2024. Data were obtained from the institutional prospectively collected trauma registry.

RESULTS: A total of 313 patients met the inclusion criteria. The mean age was 47.0 years and 69.3% were male. Motor vehicle (35.1%) and motorcycle collisions (24.9%) accounted for 60.1% of injuries. Median ISS was 26 (IQR 19-34), with 70.6% sustaining pelvic AIS 4-5 injuries. 20.1% of patients underwent at least one haemorrhage-control intervention, including angioembolisation (14.4%), preperitoneal pelvic packing (5.8%) and external fixation (5.8%). Angioembolisation utilisation increased from 6.7% in 2015 to 40.0% in 2024. In-hospital mortality was 7.7%, with traumatic brain injury accounting for 62.5% of deaths and haemorrhagic shock for only one death.

CONCLUSION: Moderate-to-severe pelvic ring fractures remained characterised by high-energy mechanisms and severe multisystem injury over the study period, while management evolved with increasing utilisation of angioembolisation. In-hospital mortality was numerically lower compared with historical cohorts, with most deaths attributable to associated traumatic brain injury rather than pelvic haemorrhage.

articles.title: [Acute heart failure-management during the first 120 min : Approach for early stabilization and decongestion].
articles.abstract: Acute heart failure (AHF) is among the most common causes of emergency department, intermediate care, and intensive care unit admission and remains associated with substantial early mortality despite advances in contemporary therapy. The first 120 min of management are particularly critical, as this period determines not only respiratory and hemodynamic stabilization, but also trigger identification, decongestion strategy, and the foundation for subsequent prognostic improvement. This CME article provides a practical, phenotype-based approach to the early management of AHF. The proposed strategy is centered on the rapid classification of patients according to congestion ("wet" vs. "dry") and perfusion ("warm" vs. "cold") status. Stabilization and diagnostic work-up must occur simultaneously. Early assessment should focus on identifying acute coronary syndrome, clinically relevant arrhythmias, hypertensive crisis, pulmonary embolism, structural heart disease, and infectious triggers. In addition to clinical examination, electrocardiography, blood gas analysis, and biomarkers, point-of-care ultrasound with lung ultrasound and focused echocardiography play a pivotal role in the first-line evaluation. From a therapeutic perspective, early noninvasive ventilation in cardiogenic pulmonary edema, prompt vasodilation in hypertensive presentations, and effective decongestion with intravenous loop diuretics constitute the core interventions. In cases of insufficient response, escalation strategies such as sequential nephron blockade or selective use of vasoactive agents should be considered. Structured reassessment at short intervals is essential to detect persistent congestion, evolving hypoperfusion, inadequate therapeutic response, or overlooked differential diagnoses. The article emphasizes that successful acute management must already establish the transition toward guideline-directed long-term therapy during the first hours of hospitalization, including early initiation of evidence-based heart failure medication once hemodynamic stabilization has been achieved.

articles.title: The role of venoactive drugs in a modern treatment paradigm: evidence review.
articles.abstract: Chronic venous disease (CVD) causes substantial symptom burden and healthcare cost, driven not only by venous hypertension but by a persistent molecular cascade of endothelial activation, glycocalyx degradation, and inflammation within the vein wall. Venoactive drugs (VADs) - a heterogeneous class of flavonoid, synthetic, animal-derived, and plant-derived compounds - target this cascade and are recommended by international guidelines as adjuncts to compression therapy, endovenous intervention, and wound care in venous leg ulcer (VLU) management. This review synthesizes the pharmacological rationale and clinical evidence for VADs across these three adjunct settings. The evidence base is strongest for VAD use alongside compression, supported by multiple Cochrane-grade meta-analyses; MPFF and ruscus extracts have the most robust symptom evidence, while MPFF, pentoxifylline, and sulodexide have the strongest evidence for VLU healing. Evidence in the peri-interventional setting remains the weakest, limited to open-label studies of MPFF. Priorities for future research include stratified and biomarker-guided prescribing, combination pharmacotherapy, and larger, adequately powered VLU healing trials.

articles.title: Protocol-based medical management for inflammatory abdominal aortic aneurysms: a five-year single-center experience.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Inflammatory abdominal aortic aneurysm (IAAA), a distinct clinical entity characterized by dense periaortic fibrosis and elevated inflammatory markers, lacks a consensus-driven optimal management strategy. While medical therapy is often utilized, comparative data against surgical or endovascular interventions remain limited. We report our experience with a standardized medical protocol for the management of IAAAs.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of 27 consecutive patients diagnosed with IAAA between 2012 and 2019. Predefined diagnostic criteria for IAAA included an ESR>100 mm/h, aortic wall thickness >10 mm, and inflammatory symptoms. Risk of rupture was assessed using a PET-CT scan for patients with a maximal aortic diameter exceeding 5.5 cm. A standardized medical protocol was used for low rupture risk patients including IV methylprednisolone followed by oral prednisone taper. Methotrexate was introduced for steroid-refractory cases. Endovascular or open aortic repair was used for patients with high risk of rupture.

RESULTS: Patients had a mean age of 62.3 years, and 70.4% were male. The mean baseline aortic diameter was 48±5 mm (95% CI 46.0-50.0). Twenty-three patients (85.2%) were treated initially with corticosteroids. At the 3-month mark, 69.6% of medically treated patients achieved an acceptable response with steroids alone. Five steroid-refractory patients received methotrexate and demonstrated clinical improvement. ESR normalized in 95.7% of medically treated patients. During five-year follow-up, no medically managed patient required emergency surgical intervention. Eleven patients required temporary steroid reintroduction at 3 years, with sustained stability at 5 years. Three patients underwent EVAR with favorable outcomes. One patient underwent open repair, which was associated with significant perioperative morbidity and late mortality.

CONCLUSIONS: In selected patients with low risk of aortic rupture, protocol-based medical therapy for IAAA is safe and effective with minimal risk upon mid-term follow-up. PET-CT scan assessment for risk of immediate rupture is appropriate for patients with aortic diameter between 5.5 to 6.5 cm. Methotrexate introduction may be effective for steroid-refractory cases. Endovascular repair remains a suitable option when intervention is required. Larger prospective studies are needed to establish definitive management guidelines for IAAAs.

articles.title: Bailout stenting strategy in complex femoropopliteal lesions: mid-term outcomes with drug-eluting versus bare-metal stents.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The aim of this study was to compare mid-term outcomes of drug-eluting stents (DES) versus bare-metal stents (BMS) when used as a bailout strategy for complex femoropopliteal lesions in real-world practice.

METHODS: Single-center, retrospective cohort (January 2018 - February 2025) including patients requiring bailout stenting after suboptimal angioplasty. Primary endpoints included primary patency, freedom from clinically driven target lesion revascularization (cdTLR). Secondary endpoints were considered the limb loss, freedom from major adverse limb events (MALE) and all-cause mortality rate. Time-to-event outcomes were analyzed by Kaplan-Meier and log-rank testing up to 36 months; hazard ratios (HRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were estimated. A multivariable Cox model explored predictors of statistically significant outcomes.

RESULTS: A total of 141 patients were included (BMS 65; DES 76). Compared with DES, the BMS group had higher rates of diabetes (58.5% vs. 40.8, P=0.036), CKD (70.8% vs. 40.8, P<0.001), dialysis (12.3% vs. 1.3, P=0.008), CLTI (89.2% vs. 75.0, P=0.030), Rutherford 5-6 (69.2% vs. 52.6, P=0.045), and ASA ≥3 (100% vs. 89.5, P=0.007). Kaplan-Meier analyses showed no significant between-group differences for primary patency (log-rank χ2 0.0011, P=0.973; HR 0.99, 95% CI 0.43-2.27), freedom from cdTLR (χ2 1.6318, P=0.2015; HR 0.52, 0.19-1.41), limb loss (χ2 2.37, P=0.124; HR 4.03, 0.68-23.76), or freedom from MALE (χ2 0.68, P=0.409; HR 1.48, 0.58-3.79). The all-cause mortality rate in the unadjusted analysis resulted higher in the BMS group (log-rank χ2 13.09, P<0.0003); (HR 2.75; 95% CI 1.59-4.76). In multivariable analysis, mortality was independently associated with CKD (HR 3.43, P=0.001), dialysis (HR 2.70, P=0.012), tissue loss/Rutherford 5-6 (HR 2.54, P=0.006), and history for neoplasia (HR 1.96, P=0.028); stent type was not an independent predictor (BMS vs. DES HR 0.54, P=0.063).

CONCLUSIONS: In bailout setting for long, complex femoropopliteal disease, stent type did not influence the outcomes post revascularization at 36 months. The overall all-cause mortality rate was driven by baseline clinical status rather than the device.

articles.title: GLP-1 Receptor Agonists in Dentistry: Promise, Pitfalls, and Evidence Gaps.
articles.abstract: GLP-1RAs (glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists) have become one of the fastest-growing drug classes worldwide, with prescriptions for obesity treatment increasing by 587% from 2019 to 2024. While their metabolic and cardiovascular benefits are well established, the implications for oral health remain largely unexamined. Preclinical evidence consistently demonstrates anti-inflammatory and osteoprotective effects on periodontal and peri-implant tissues: GLP-1RAs promote osteogenic differentiation of periodontal ligament stem cells, reduce alveolar bone resorption in animal models of periodontitis, and enhance implant osseointegration in diabetic rats. However, these findings are based exclusively on in vitro and animal studies, with only a single retrospective cohort study providing limited clinical data. Conversely, several oral adverse effects have been reported based on pharmacovigilance analyses, including xerostomia, dysgeusia, and anosmia, particularly for semaglutide. Gastrointestinal side effects, particularly nausea (15% to 50%), vomiting (5% to 24%), and gastroesophageal reflux, pose a plausible but unquantified risk for tooth erosion and secondary caries. A bidirectional link between GLP-1 signaling and the oral microbiota, mediated by bacterial dipeptidyl peptidase (DPP)-4-like enzymes that degrade endogenous GLP-1, adds further complexity. Despite this breadth of potential interactions, no prospective study has used any dental outcome as an endpoint in patients receiving GLP-1RAs. This critical appraisal synthesizes the evidence across multiple dental disciplines, grades it in each domain, and identifies the gaps that demand urgent investigation.

articles.title: Customizing Treatment for Acute Kidney Injury in Distinct Populations.
articles.journal: Advances in kidney disease and health

articles.title: Exploring Self-Care Among Postpartum Women Recovering From Substance Use Disorders.
articles.abstract: Self-care is central to occupational therapy (OT), yet its role among postpartum women navigating substance use disorder (SUD) recovery remains under-researched. This mixed-methods study examined self-care performance among postpartum women and explored self-care experiences during SUD recovery. We analyzed Barkin Index for Maternal Functioning (BIMF) self-care items among postpartum women with and without SUD (N = 141). Descriptive statistics and regression analyses examined associations between participant characteristics, SUD diagnosis, and self-care. Interviews with women with SUD (n = 22) underwent deductive thematic analysis grounded in Orem's self-care theory. Overall, 34.0% of participants had a SUD; the mean self-care score was 13.56 (SD = 3.93). Self-care scores did not differ significantly by SUD diagnosis (p = .370), but children's daycare attendance was associated with lower self-care (p = .015). Qualitatively, women described self-care as an effort to maintain stability, well-being, and recovery. Patient-centered OT services are critical for supporting self-care among postpartum women navigating SUD recovery.

articles.title: American Society of Hematology 2026 Guidelines for the Management of Myelofibrosis in Adults.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Myelofibrosis (MF) is a myeloid bone marrow malignancy with a progressive clinical course marked by disease-related symptoms, splenomegaly, cytopenias, thrombosis/hemorrhage, and a risk for blast phase transformation. Treatment recommendations are based on the burden of symptoms, prognosis of the disease, and benefits/risks of each treatment modality.

METHODS: ASH formed a multidisciplinary guideline panel that included specialists in myelofibrosis and hematopoietic cell transplantation, as well 2 patient representatives and was balanced to minimize potential bias from conflicts of interest. The Mayo Clinic Evidence-based Practice Center supported the guideline development process, including updating or performing systematic evidence reviews (up to January 31, 2025). The panel prioritized clinical questions and outcomes according to their importance for patients and clinicians. The panel used the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) approach, including GRADE Evidence-to-Decision frameworks, to assess evidence and make recommendations, which were subject to public comment.

RESULTS: The panel agreed on 10 recommendations regarding prognostic testing, indications for interferon and JAK inhibitor therapy, management of MF-associated anemia, timing of transplantation, anti-platelet therapy, and iron chelation.

CONCLUSIONS: Key recommendations of these guidelines include suggestions for extended molecular genetic testing; use of JAK-inhibition in symptomatic, lower risk MF patients; therapeutic strategies for patients with MF-anemia and JAK-inhibitor induced anemia; and considerations regarding hematopoietic cell transplantation including timing of referral and optimization prior to the procedure. Key future research agendas were identified for all recommendations.

articles.title: [The blood biomarker breakthrough in Alzheimer's disease: what applications in 2026? Part I: Blood biomarkers transitioning to clinical practice].
articles.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is the leading cause of cognitive decline, and its diagnosis increasingly relies on a clinicobiological approach combining cognitive assessment with disease-specific biomarkers. Until recently, these biomarkers were mainly measured in cerebrospinal fluid (CSF), requiring lumbar puncture. Advances in ultrasensitive analytical technologies now enable their detection in blood, providing a less invasive, more accessible, and potentially earlier diagnostic alternative. This review summarizes the current state of blood-based biomarkers available for clinical use, focusing on markers of the amyloid pathway (Aβ1-42, Aβ1-40, and their ratio) and the Tau pathway (pTau181, pTau217, pTau231, and BD-Tau). Amyloid peptides reflect early amyloid pathology but show limited diagnostic performance when used alone. In contrast, phosphorylated Tau biomarkers, particularly pTau217 and the pTau217/Aβ1-42 ratio, demonstrate excellent diagnostic accuracy and strong correlations with established CSF and amyloid PET biomarkers. These blood biomarkers have recently been incorporated into national and international diagnostic recommendations and are progressively entering routine clinical practice. Their implementation represents a major advance in the diagnosis, patient stratification, and therapeutic monitoring of AD. Despite these promising developments, challenges remain regarding analytical standardization, interpretation thresholds, and ethical considerations related to very early diagnosis. Nevertheless, blood-based biomarkers are expected to play a central role in future Alzheimer's disease management and precision medicine strategies.

articles.title: Photophysical and quenching principles governing advanced materials for fluorescence-based biosensing: mechanisms and analytical performance.
articles.abstract: Optical fluorescence biosensing has emerged as one of the most powerful strategies for ultrasensitive molecular detection, driven by rapid advances in fluorophore engineering, nanomaterial design, and signal-transduction architectures. At the core of these technologies lie fundamental excited-state processes, including fluorescence emission, Förster resonance energy transfer (FRET), photoinduced electron transfer (PET), and intramolecular charge transfer (ICT), that govern the generation, modulation, and detection of optical signals. In this review, we present a photophysics-centered framework for understanding and designing fluorescence-based biosensing processes, systematically correlating excited-state dynamics with analytical sensing performance. We examine a broad range of fluorescent materials, including organic dyes, semiconductor and metal quantum dots, perovskite nanocrystals, transition-metal complexes, lanthanide emitters, and emerging carbon-based nanodots, highlighting how their emission characteristics, quantum yields, photostability, and surface chemistry influence sensing capabilities. Particular emphasis is placed on fluorescence quenching mechanisms and the role of advanced quenching platforms including graphene derivatives, metal oxides, metal-organic frameworks (MOFs), covalent organic frameworks (COFs), and hybrid nanostructures in tuning sensitivity, selectivity, and detection limits. Beyond material systems, we discuss recent progress in device integration and analytical methodologies, including microfluidic architectures, smartphone-enabled sensing platforms, nanophotonic metasurfaces, and artificial-intelligence-assisted spectral analysis, which are accelerating the translation of fluorescence biosensing toward portable and high-throughput applications. Despite these advances, challenges such as photobleaching, spectral interference, surface heterogeneity, and manufacturing reproducibility continue to affect analytical reliability. Emerging strategies based on defect-engineered two-dimensional materials, hybrid optical modalities, and machine-learning-driven signal interpretation are therefore highlighted as promising routes toward improved robustness and accuracy. By integrating photophysical principles, nanomaterial design, and analytical performance metrics into a unified perspective, this review provides a conceptual roadmap for the rational development of next-generation fluorescence-based biosensing technologies.

articles.title: Fenestrated Microneedle Biosensor for Continuous In Vivo Lactate Monitoring in Interstitial Fluid.
articles.abstract: Lactate is a key biomarker of tissue metabolism and oxygenation, yet clinical assessment still relies on intermittent blood tests that overlook rapid metabolic dynamics and disrupt clinical workflows. Continuous transdermal monitoring of lactate in interstitial fluid (ISF) offers a minimally invasive approach for real-time monitoring of metabolic status, particularly in conditions associated with metabolic syndrome such as obesity and diabetes. Here we report a proof-of-concept transdermal lactate biosensor based on a fenestrated microneedle array (F-MNA), consisting of a polymeric MNA enclosed within a fenestrated polymeric shell that protects the biosensing layer while retaining access to ISF. Under controlled anesthetized conditions, the biosensor differentiated ISF lactate profiles between healthy and diabetic-obese (db/db) mice, with the db/db group exhibiting higher baseline lactate concentrations. In fasted healthy mice subjected to subcutaneous glucose challenge, the biosensor captured transient increases in ISF lactate followed by partial recovery over the 2 h monitoring period. Biosensor-derived ISF lactate showed strong temporal association with paired blood lactate measurements while exhibiting a systematic positive ISF-to-blood concentration offset. These findings establish proof-of-concept continuous transdermal ISF lactate monitoring under controlled in vivo conditions.

articles.title: Isoflurane-Based Inhaled Sedation in Mechanically Ventilated Adults With Acute Hypoxemic Respiratory Failure: The SAVE-ICU Randomized Clinical Trial.
authors: SAVE-ICU Investigators and the Canadian Critical Care Trials Group
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Rigorous evidence for inhaled sedation using isoflurane in mechanically ventilated patients with acute hypoxemic respiratory failure (AHRF) is limited.

OBJECTIVE: To evaluate whether an inhaled sedation strategy lowers hospital mortality compared with usual care intravenous sedation strategy in mechanically ventilated adults with AHRF.

DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: Pragmatic, effectiveness, open-label, superiority, randomized clinical trial in 14 intensive care units (ICUs) in Canada. Adults (≥18 years) receiving sedation for less than 72 hours and receiving mechanical ventilation for AHRF from non-COVID respiratory failure (ratio of partial pressure of arterial oxygen [Pao2] to fraction of inspired oxygen [Fio2] <300 mm Hg) or COVID-19 were enrolled between September 2020 and March 2025 with follow-up through June 2025.

INTERVENTION: Patients were randomized to an inhaled sedation strategy using isoflurane with intravenous adjuncts as clinically needed or to a usual intravenous sedation care strategy. Sedatives were titrated to achieve the desired target sedation score guided by clinical teams and continued until extubation or death.

MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Primary outcome was all-cause hospital mortality. Secondary outcomes included ICU- and ventilator-free days at day 30; hospital-free days at day 60; use of refractory hypoxemia adjunctive therapies; delirium- and coma-free days at day 14; and quality-of-life and disability scores at 3 months.

RESULTS: Of 786 patients randomized, 780 were included in the primary analysis (mean age, 61.1 years; 34.0% female; 73.7% non-COVID AHRF, mean Pao2:Fio2 ratio, 152.6 mm Hg); 385 in the inhaled sedation and 395 in the intravenous sedation groups. In the inhaled sedation group, 49.9% to 55.4% of patients received concomitant intravenous sedation on any day during the first 14 days after randomization. At hospital discharge, 161 of 379 patients (42.5%) in the inhaled sedation group had died, compared with 171 of 390 patients (43.8%) in the intravenous sedation group (risk ratio, 0.98 [95% CI, 0.84 to 1.14]; P = .85). There was no effect modification in prespecified subgroup analyses for age, sex, and COVID-19 status. ICU-, ventilator-, and hospital-free days were similar between groups. The inhaled sedation group received more adjunctive therapies for hypoxemia (239 [63.9%] vs 214 [55.0%]; between-group difference, 8.89% [95% CI, 1.95% to 15.83%]) and had fewer delirium- and coma-free days (between-group difference, -0.95 [95% CI, -1.69 to -0.22]). There was no difference in quality-of-life and disability scores between groups.

CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In mechanically ventilated adults with AHRF, an inhaled sedation strategy using isoflurane with intravenous adjuncts as clinically needed did not reduce hospital mortality compared with an intravenous sedation strategy.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT04415060.

articles.title: Impact of Trimetazidine on Echocardiographic Indices and Clinical Outcomes in Ischemic Cardiomyopathy: An Updated Meta-Analysis of Clinical Trials.
articles.abstract: Ischemic cardiomyopathy (ICM) is a major cause of chronic heart failure with impaired left ventricular (LV) function. Trimetazidine, a metabolic modulator that shifts energy utilization from fatty acid oxidation to glucose oxidation, may improve cardiac function in ischemic myocardium. This meta-analysis aimed to evaluate trimetazidine's effect in patients with ICM compared to standard therapy alone. A systematic search was conducted across PubMed, ProQuest, SAGE, EBSCO Host, Wiley, Science Direct, and SpringerLink databases until November 2024. Clinical trials assessing trimetazidine versus standard therapy in ICM were included. Data were analyzed using a random-effects model to calculate mean differences (MD) and relative risk (RR), with heterogeneity evaluated using the I2 statistic. Ten studies met the inclusion criteria. Trimetazidine significantly improved left ventricular ejection fraction (MD 6.35%, 95% CI: 4.63-8.07; p<0.05), reduced LV end-systolic diameter (MD -4.51 mm, p<0.05), LV end-diastolic diameter (MD -3.13 mm, p<0.05), and LV end-systolic volume (MD -14.20 ml, p<0.05). Exercise capacity improved markedly with a mean increase of 83.64 meters in the 6-minute walking test (p<0.05). NYHA class also improved (MD -0.80, p<0.05). However, no significant differences were found in anginal episodes or nitrate consumption. Trimetazidine as an adjunct to standard therapy improves cardiac function and exercise capacity in ischemic cardiomyopathy patients. It may be considered in patients with persistent symptoms or exercise intolerance despite optimal medical therapy. Further large-scale trials are warranted to assess long-term outcomes such as mortality and hospitalization.

articles.title: Tools Measuring Health Literacy in Critically Ill Patients and Their Caregivers: A Scoping Review.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Health literacy, the ability to understand and use health information, is important for critically ill patients and their caregivers in the neonatal ICU (NICU), PICU, and adult ICU to make informed decisions and navigate complex care. This review aimed to identify and summarize tools used to assess health literacy in critically ill patients or their caregivers.

DATA SOURCES: We searched MEDLINE, Embase, CINAHL, and PsycINFO through July 24, 2025.

STUDY SELECTION: Included articles reported on tools to assess health literacy in critically ill patients or their caregivers. Two reviewers independently performed screening and data extraction.

DATA EXTRACTION: Two independent reviewers extracted data in Covidence. Data items included study characteristics (country in which the study was conducted, study funding, study setting) and health literacy tool characteristics (tool user, types of questions in the tool, method of tool administration, if the tool was created by the study team, and if a full version was available in the publication).

DATA SYNTHESIS: We included 92 articles describing 84 health literacy tools. Tools measured: 1) topic-specific clinical knowledge (e.g., organ donation, cardiopulmonary resuscitation; n = 24/84, 29%; NICU: n = 9; PICU: n = 1; ICU: n = 14); 2) ICU prognosis, diagnosis, and treatment (n = 23/84, 27%; NICU: 6; PICU: 3; ICU: n = 15); 3) neonatal and parenting (n = 13/84, 15%; all NICU); 4) general health literacy abilities (n = 11/84, 13%; NICU: n = 6; PICU: n = 2; ICU: n = 7); 5) information needs (n = 4/84, 5%; NICU: n = 1; PICU: n = 0; ICU: n = 3); 6) readiness for discharge (n = 3/84, 4%; all NICU); 7) decision-making (n = 3/84, 4%; all NICU); 8) health-related behaviors (n = 2/84, 2%; NICU: n = 1; ICU: n = 1); and 9) research participation (n = 1/84, 1%; NICU).

CONCLUSIONS: Although several health literacy tools exist, they often focus on individual knowledge of specific aspects of ICU care, with less attention to how understanding is produced within the clinical context through interactions among patients, caregivers, and healthcare providers. This may limit their ability to reflect how health literacy functions in critical illness. Assessment of health literacy requires pairing the appropriate tools with interaction-focused approaches to guide communication and support informed decision-making in ICU settings.

articles.title: Effect of Vasopressin Initiation Threshold on Septic Shock Mortality: Research Summary.
Inhaled Sedation in Acute Respiratory Failure: Air Cleared?
Vasopressin in Septic Shock-Is Early the Right Question?
Real-World Use of Ceftazidime-Avibactam for Carbapenem-Resistant Enterobacterales Infections in Children: A 7-Year Cohort From a Latin American Referral Center.
articles.journal: Journal of the Pediatric Infectious Diseases Society
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pediatric data on ceftazidime-avibactam (CAZ-AVI) for carbapenem-resistant Enterobacterales (CRE) infections remain limited, particularly in Latin America, where KPC-producing organisms are endemic. We describe the clinical characteristics, microbiological profile, and outcomes of children with CRE infections treated with CAZ-AVI at a tertiary referral center in Colombia.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of children younger than 18 years with clinically significant CRE infections treated with CAZ-AVI between January 2018 and June 2025. Clinical, microbiological, treatment, and outcome data were collected. The primary outcome was clinical response at the end of therapy.

RESULTS: Forty-three patients were included (median age, 11 years [IQR, 6-15]); 25 patients (58%) were immunocompromised, 29 (67%) required PICU admission, and 16 (37%) presented with septic shock. Klebsiella pneumoniae was the predominant pathogen (33 patients, 77%), and KPC was the most common carbapenemase detected (39 patients, 91%). Clinical improvement within 72 hours occurred in 40 patients (93%), with a median time to response of 2 days (IQR, 2-3). Overall, 40 patients (93%) achieved clinical cure. The estimated 30-day survival probability was 95.3% (95% CI, 88.8-100), recurrence occurred in 3 patients (7%), and no treatment-related adverse events were documented.

CONCLUSION: In this real-world pediatric cohort from a KPC-endemic setting, CAZ-AVI was associated with favorable clinical outcomes and good tolerability. These findings support its role as an important therapeutic option for pediatric CRE infections and underscore the importance of mechanism-guided antimicrobial management.

articles.title: Population pharmacokinetics of piperacillin based on multicenter data to support model-informed precision dosing in critically ill women.
articles.abstract: Sex-specific differences in pharmacokinetics are increasingly recognized as clinically relevant, yet most population pharmacokinetic models for antibiotics have been developed in predominantly male populations with limited transferability to female patients. This study aimed to develop and externally evaluate a population pharmacokinetic model of piperacillin specifically for critically ill women to support model-informed precision dosing (MIPD). A total of 923 samples from 165 critically ill women (from four previously published studies) receiving piperacillin/tazobactam were analyzed. The data set was randomly split into a training set (80%) and an independent external evaluation set (20%). Non-linear mixed-effects modeling was employed based on the training data using NONMEM, and covariates were identified using stepwise covariate modeling with cross-validation. Prediction accuracy and bias were quantified using the median prediction error (MDPE) and the median absolute prediction error (MDAPE) in an MIPD scenario. Model predictions for future concentrations were generated both a priori and through Bayesian forecasting based on one prior sample. A two-compartment model provided the best fit for the data. Clearance was significantly affected by renal function estimated by the Cockcroft-Gault equation, along with procalcitonin and serum albumin. The external evaluation demonstrated strong predictive performance with very low systematic bias. In the MIPD scenario, a priori predictions exhibited good predictive performance (MDPE < |5.2|%, MDAPE < 33.4%), which substantially improved with Bayesian forecasting (MDPE < |3.2|%, MDAPE < 19.1%). A female-specific population pharmacokinetic model of piperacillin was developed and externally validated, demonstrating robust predictive performance and clear benefits for Bayesian forecasting.

articles.title: New Insights Into U.S. Pediatric Critical Care Epidemiology.
Inhaled Sedation Strategy for Acute Hypoxemic Respiratory Failure: New Evidence for Debate.
The lung-gut axis and airway inflammation in COPD.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is a common lung disease characterized by multiple persistent respiratory symptoms and decreased lung function. Despite extensive research exploring the complex pathogenic mechanisms and signaling pathways underlying COPD, there are currently no effective disease-modifying drugs capable of halting or reversing progressive lung damage, standard interventions including bronchodilators, long-term oxygen therapy and pulmonary rehabilitation merely alleviate clinical symptoms while failing to arrest disease progression, accompanied by unavoidable adverse effects. Against this backdrop, microbiota-targeted interventions emerge as a promising alternative therapeutic strategy. This drives the urgent need to dissect unrecognized pathogenic pathways and develop novel prevention and treatment strategies.

METHODS: This narrative review summarizes recent data on gut microbiota dysregulation and gut-lung crosstalk in COPD, highlighting immune-mediated gut-lung crosstalk mechanisms, including the shared mucosal immune system and metabolite-induced modulation of pulmonary structure and function.

RESULTS: In addition to immune inflammation and hypoxia, COPD patients usually have gastrointestinal complications and gut microbiota (GM) dysregulation. Role of GM in regulating the functional development of the host immune system, and the "gut-lung axis" established by GM and the lung also plays a crucial role in regulating lung inflammation and airway function. This may be attributed to the shared mucosal immune system between the gut and lungs, as well as the ability of metabolites to influence lung structure and function. However, the specific pathway of this gut-lung communication in COPD is still unclear.

CONCLUSIONS: This article reviews the changes of GM related to COPD, and focuses on the mechanism of GM and its metabolites in the occurrence and development of COPD from the immune pathway, so as to find new intervention targets, and highlight the emerging potential of GM interventions (diet, probiotics and prebiotics) for future clinical research and treatment of COPD.

articles.title: Association of Oliguria With Acute Kidney Injury, Chronic Kidney Disease, and Mortality: Determining the Optimal Threshold in Critically Ill Patients.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Oliguria is a key prognostic indicator of acute kidney injury (AKI), yet the consensus definition (< 0.5 mL/kg/hr) is increasingly questioned. We aimed to determine thresholds of lowest mean diuresis (LMD) associated with AKI, chronic kidney disease (CKD), and mortality.

DESIGN: Retrospective observational study.

SETTING: Uppsala University Hospital ICU, Sweden.

PATIENTS: A total of 4999 adults (≥ 18 yr) without preexisting CKD admitted to the ICU between 2017 and 2024.

INTERVENTIONS: None.

MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: LMD was calculated over 3, 6, 12, and 24 hours (LMD3h-LMD24h). Generalized additive models were used, adjusting for Simplified Acute Physiology Score 3 estimated mortality ratio and gender. Outcomes were AKI within 7 days of LMD (Kidney Disease Improving Global Outcomes creatinine criteria), incident CKD after ICU discharge, and 90-day mortality. All LMD time frames were significantly associated with AKI, CKD, and death (p < 0.0001). Thresholds for AKI were 0.43, 0.41, 0.42, and 0.53 mL/kg/hr; for CKD, 0.21, 0.21, 0.31, and 0.43 mL/kg/hr; and for mortality 0.16, 0.18, 0.24, and 0.39 across LMD3h-LMD24h.

CONCLUSIONS: The risk of mortality or persistent kidney injury, reflected by incident CKD, increases at a lower urine output threshold than the current AKI definition. These findings support the idea of filtration deficit, urine output, and tissue injury as different dimensions of AKI and should influence future AKI definitions.

articles.title: Effect of Vasopressin Initiation Threshold on Septic Shock Mortality: The VASSPR Cluster Crossover Randomized Strategy Trial.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: The optimal vasopressor dose at which to initiate a second vasopressor in patients with septic shock is uncertain.

OBJECTIVE: To compare the effects of hospital-level strategies initiating vasopressin infusion at a lower threshold vs a higher threshold on outcomes in patients with septic shock.

DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: Cluster-randomized, cluster-crossover, pragmatic clinical strategy trial including adult patients receiving vasopressors for septic shock at 13 hospitals in Idaho and Utah from February 1, 2024, to July 31, 2025. The last day of follow-up for the primary outcome was February 17, 2026.

INTERVENTION: Hospital-level implementation of septic shock management strategies recommending fixed-dose vasopressin initiation when the total dose of other vasopressors reached 0.1 µg/kg/min of norepinephrine or equivalent (lower-threshold strategy) or when the total dose of other vasopressors reached 0.4 µg/kg/min of norepinephrine or equivalent (higher-threshold strategy). Hospitals were randomized for the first month to an initial strategy (6 hospitals to the lower threshold vs 7 hospitals to the higher threshold) and then crossed over to the alternate strategy monthly thereafter.

MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome of 28-day mortality and the key secondary outcome of kidney replacement therapy-free days through day 28 were analyzed using multivariable generalized linear mixed-effects models, accounting for trial site and baseline patient characteristics.

RESULTS: There were 3959 unique patients with septic shock (median age, 68 [IQR, 57 to 77] years; 1903 [48%] were female). Of the patients more likely to experience differential management under the tested hospital-level vasopressin dose strategies (maximum vasopressor dose ≥0.07 µg/kg/min of norepinephrine or equivalent), 1034 of 1521 (68.0%) cared for under the lower-threshold strategy received vasopressin compared with 651 of 1526 (42.7%) cared for under the higher-threshold strategy. In the hospital-level strategy recommending a lower-dose threshold for vasopressin initiation, the maximum vasopressor dose received prior to vasopressin initiation was a median of 0.14 (IQR, 0.10 to 0.22) µg/kg/min of norepinephrine or equivalent vs 0.34 (IQR, 0.16 to 0.42) µg/kg/min of norepinephrine or equivalent in the hospital-level strategy recommending a higher-dose threshold for vasopressin initiation. Mortality at 28 days occurred in 628 of 1975 patients (31.8%) treated with the hospital-level strategy recommending initiation of vasopressin at a lower-dose threshold of other vasopressors vs 655 of 1984 patients (33.0%) treated with the higher-threshold strategy (adjusted marginal odds ratio, 0.98 [95% CI, 0.87 to 1.06], P = .62; adjusted risk difference, -0.4 [95% CI, -2.7 to 1.3] percentage points). Patients in both strategies for vasopressin initiation had a median of 29 (IQR, -1 to 29) kidney replacement therapy-free days (adjusted marginal odds ratio, 1.01 [95% CI, 0.91 to 1.14]).

CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this large, pragmatic clinical trial comparing the effectiveness of 2 hospital-level strategies for second-line vasopressor management in septic shock, a strategy recommending initiation of vasopressin at a lower dose of other vasopressors did not reduce 28-day mortality compared with a strategy recommending vasopressin initiation at a higher dose of other vasopressors.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT06217562.

articles.title: Long-Lasting Mental Disorders in Caregivers of ICU Sepsis Survivors and Their Association With Patients' Post-Intensive Care Syndrome: A Prospective Multicenter Cohort Study.
authors: Investigating Long-term Outcomes of ICU patients with Sepsis or Septic shock (ILOSS) Study Group
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To investigate the prevalence of long-term mental disorders in caregivers of ICU sepsis survivors and examine associations with post-intensive care syndrome (PICS) in patients.

DESIGN: Prospective observational study.

SETTING: Twenty-one mixed ICUs.

PATIENTS: Caregivers (the next of kin) of the patients diagnosed with sepsis between November 2020 and April 2022.

INTERVENTIONS: None.

MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: Caregivers and patients were assessed at 3, 6, and 12 months after hospital discharge by telephone and mail. The primary outcome was caregiver mental disorders (mental post-intensive care syndrome-family [PICS-F]). Mixed-effects logistic regression analyses were performed to evaluate the association between caregiver PICS-F and patient PICS. Ninety-four caregiver-patient dyads were analyzed. Caregivers were a median of 67 years old (55-79 yr old), 31 (33.0%) were male, and 41 (43.6%) were spouses. Patients were a median of 74 years old (69-82 yr old), and 54 (57.4%) were male. The prevalence of mental PICS-F did not decrease from 3 to 12 months (43% vs. 42%, respectively), whereas the presence of PICS symptoms in patients decreased from 82% to 62%. In mixed-effects logistic regression, the presence of PICS symptoms in patients was significantly associated with PICS-F (adjusted odds ratio, 3.00; 95% CI, 1.54-5.88; p < 0.01). Among the individual patient PICS domains, only mental PICS was significantly associated with PICS-F (3.71; 2.03-6.77; p < 0.01), whereas physical and cognitive impairments in patients were not.

CONCLUSIONS: The prevalence of mental PICS-F in caregivers of ICU sepsis survivors was frequent and long-lasting over the first year after hospital discharge. Since it was most strongly associated with patients' mental disorders rather than physical or cognitive impairments, the mental PICS domain in patients may be an important indicator of PICS-F and should be considered in future studies.

articles.title: Intraoperative Dobutamine Plus Norepinephrine to Prevent Postoperative Acute Kidney Injury in Septic Shock: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
authors: Chinese Perioperative Septic Shock Investigators for the Chinese Peri-Operative Organ Protection Group
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: International guidelines recommend dobutamine for management of septic shock and cardiac dysfunction with persistent hypoperfusion in adults based on very low-certainty evidence. Randomized trials are lacking on the effect of intraoperative dobutamine combined with norepinephrine vs norepinephrine on postoperative outcomes in patients with septic shock undergoing surgical source control.

OBJECTIVE: To determine whether intraoperative dobutamine combined with norepinephrine reduces acute kidney injury (AKI) within 7 postoperative days in patients with septic shock undergoing surgical source control.

DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This randomized, open-label clinical trial in 39 tertiary hospitals in China enrolled adults with septic shock who were undergoing surgical source control between June 2024 and August 2025. Follow-up ended on November 15, 2025.

INTERVENTION: Intraoperative, intravenous infusion of dobutamine (up to 5 µg/kg/min) combined with norepinephrine vs norepinephrine alone.

MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was new-onset AKI or worsening of preoperative AKI within 7 days after surgery, defined using Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO) criteria. The 11 secondary outcomes included Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA) score on postoperative day 1 and urine output 1 hour post intervention.

RESULTS: Among 584 patients (median [IQR] age, 67.5 [55.0-76.0] years; 192 [32.9%] females), new-onset or worsening AKI within 7 postoperative days occurred in 22.8% (66/290) randomized to receive dobutamine plus norepinephrine vs 34.7% (102/294) randomized to receive norepinephrine alone (adjusted risk ratio [ARR], 0.64 [95% CI, 0.49-0.83]). No significant differences were observed in 9 of the 11 secondary outcomes. SOFA scores on postoperative day 1 (adjusted difference, -0.53 [95% CI, -0.98 to -0.07]) were lower and urine output 1 hour post intervention (adjusted difference, 0.55 [95% CI, 0.03 to 1.07] mL/kg/h) was higher in the dobutamine plus norepinephrine group. Stage 2 and 3 AKI were lower in the dobutamine plus norepinephrine group compared with the norepinephrine alone group (stage 2: 4.8% vs 9.9%; ARR, 0.48 [95% CI, 0.26-0.88]; stage 3: 7.9% vs 13.6%; ARR, 0.56 [95% CI, 0.35-0.91]). Tachycardia (heart rate >100/min) occurred more frequently in patients receiving dobutamine and norepinephrine than norepinephrine alone.

CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Among adult patients with septic shock undergoing surgical source control, intraoperative dobutamine combined with norepinephrine reduced the incidence of new-onset or worsening AKI within 7 postoperative days compared with norepinephrine.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT06462313.

articles.title: Isoflurane-Based Inhaled Sedation in Mechanically Ventilated Adults With Acute Hypoxemic Respiratory Failure: Research Summary.
Intraoperative Dobutamine Plus Norepinephrine to Prevent Postoperative Acute Kidney Injury in Septic Shock: Research Summary.
Repositioning Vericiguat after VICTOR: Towards a Risk- and Timing-Based Framework in Contemporary HFrEF.
articles.abstract: Vericiguat, an oral soluble guanylate cyclase stimulator, provides a mechanistically distinct approach to reducing residual risk in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF). The VICTORIA trial demonstrated a reduction in cardiovascular death or heart failure hospitalisation among patients with recent worsening heart failure, whereas vericiguat did not significantly reduce the primary endpoint in the subsequent VICTOR trial in a more stable HFrEF population. Nevertheless, the prespecified pooled analysis of VICTORIA and VICTOR showed a significant reduction in cardiovascular death or first heart failure hospitalisation across the combined HFrEF population, without significant heterogeneity between the trials. Together, these findings shift the focus from efficacy alone to clinical prioritisation according to baseline risk and timing, while recognising that validated treatment-selection criteria and an optimal timing strategy remain undefined. Contemporary observational studies have identified associations between blood pressure, disease severity, prior heart failure hospitalisation, and clinical or biomarker outcomes during vericiguat treatment; however, these characteristics have not been validated as predictors of vericiguat-specific treatment benefit. This review integrates evidence from VICTORIA, VICTOR, pooled analyses, and contemporary real-world studies and proposes a hypothesis-generating, risk- and timing-based framework for vericiguat use. Clinically meaningful worsening heart failure may represent a period of increased absolute risk in which consideration of vericiguat may be particularly relevant after clinical stabilisation, but neither an optimal therapeutic window nor a validated responder phenotype has been established. Prospective studies specifically evaluating treatment-by-risk and treatment-by-timing interactions are required to validate this framework.

articles.title: Unraveling the spatial heterogeneity of urban traffic crashes: A GeoXGBoost and point-mapping SHAP framework.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: In urban traffic risk research, traditional models struggle to simultaneously capture the complex nonlinearity and spatial heterogeneity of risk-driving factors, while often lacking fine-grained spatial interpretability. To address these limitations, this study develops a comprehensive traffic risk analysis framework that integrates high predictive accuracy with micro-scale causal attribution.

METHODS: Using the central urban area of Liyang as an empirical case, an overlapping grid sampling strategy is employed to overcome the constraints of sample sparsity. A GeoXGBoost-based prediction framework is constructed to internalize spatial heterogeneity within the boosting algorithm, supplemented by a local spatial SHAP interpretation framework using a point-mapping strategy to enable precise risk attribution from global statistics to micro-spatial units.

RESULTS: The GeoXGBoost model achieves a superior goodness-of-fit (OOB-predicted R2) of 0.896, significantly outperforming five benchmark models and effectively eliminating the spatial autocorrelation of prediction residuals. Core risk factors, including shopping services, transport facility services, and population density, exhibit pronounced spatial non-stationarity and location-specific functional differentiation, with their driving effects highly dependent on the local road network context.

CONCLUSIONS: A deep interactive coupling mechanism of "place-exposure-function" is identified. Standalone static facilities and population scale constitute only potential hazards; however, when superimposed with high-load dynamic traffic flows or highly mixed functions, they trigger an abrupt, nonlinear surge in local crash probabilities. This framework provides a scientific basis for fine-grained, location-specific spatial interventions in urban traffic safety governance.

articles.title: Confined-Space Self-Assembly of Nano-HNS Into Hierarchical Micro-Nano Structured Microspheres for Selective Stimuli Sensitization and Passivation.
articles.abstract: To address the balance between reactivity and safety in nano-HNS, this study presents a green composite molding strategy that facilitates the self-assembly of nano-HNS into micro-nano-structured microspheres within confined spaces. This approach utilizes confined spaces to precisely control the morphology and size of the resultant microspheres. The effects of process parameters on the morphology and size of microspheres were systematically investigated, and the underlying formation mechanisms were elucidated. Comprehensive characterizations encompassing morphology, crystal structure, mechanical sensitivity, thermal behavior, and impact properties were conducted. The results demonstrate that the synthesized HNS microspheres possess high sphericity, an average particle size of 224.2 µm, and exhibit favorable fluidity and bulk density. This approach effectively reduces the mechanical sensitivity of the material while preserving the crystal structure and thermal stability of HNS-IV (impact sensitivity: 12 J vs. 20 J; friction sensitivity: 216 N vs. 240 N). Furthermore, it enhances the initial sensitivity to short duration shock, as evidenced by reductions in the 50% and 99.9% initiation voltages by 18 and 48 V, respectively. This approach facilitates the synergistic stimulation of selective sensitization and passivation. This methodology is straightforward and applicable, providing a versatile and eco-friendly approach for the multi-structural modification of nano-HNS.

articles.title: Histones and nucleoid-associated proteins in Methanosarcina acetivorans mediate recovery from stress and stasis.
articles.abstract: Many archaea encode histones in tandem with nucleoid-associated proteins (NAPs), but the functional overlap between these two classes of non-specific DNA-binding proteins (DBPs) is not well studied. Most in vivo studies of DBPs have been conducted with archaea that only encode histones or NAPs. Here, we characterize the endogenous function of the two families of DBPs in a methanogen, Methanosarcina acetivorans, that encodes a histone and two copies of an archaea-specific NAP called methanogen chromatin Protein 1 (MC1). In M. acetivorans, we found that each DBP is individually dispensable, but at least one copy of mc1 appears to be essential. By and large, the single- and double-DBP knockouts phenocopy the wild-type strain under optimal laboratory growth conditions. Remarkably, mutants lacking the histone, one copy of MC1, or both recover faster than wild-type after being subjected to UV shock or long periods of growth stasis. Overexpression of the DBPs leads to a delay in growth recovery after extended periods in stationary phase, which is abrogated by introducing point mutations in DNA-binding residues. Together, our data suggest that histones and MC1 proteins have partially overlapping roles in M. acetivorans, one of which might be genome maintenance when growth has stalled or stopped.IMPORTANCEThough it is known that many archaea encode histones in tandem with archaea-specific nucleoid-associated proteins (NAPs), the interplay between these two classes of DNA-binding proteins (DBPs) in vivo is not known. Most studies on archaeal DBPs have focused either on archaea known to form histone-based chromatin or on strains that lack histones and compact their genomes exclusively with archaea-specific NAPs. Our study, therefore, fills an important gap in the literature by characterizing DBPs in a model methanogen, Methanosarcina acetivorans, which encodes both histones and archaea-specific NAPs. While no DBP is essential, at least one copy of MC1 appears to be needed, likely for genome compaction. In addition, mutants lacking DBPs had a growth advantage after being subjected to stressors or long periods of growth stasis, indicating that DBPs likely function in genome maintenance when growth has stalled or stopped.

articles.title: Redistributing Insulin Pumps for Patients Facing Access Barriers.
articles.journal: Journal of diabetes science and technology
articles.abstract: Insulin pumps are durable, high-cost medical devices that support continuous subcutaneous insulin infusion and automated insulin delivery. Despite their utility, access to insulin pumps in the United States remains uneven across socioeconomic strata, insurance types, and racial and ethnic groups, and is far more limited internationally. Meanwhile, functional pumps accumulate through predictable lifecycle events such as device upgrades, therapy discontinuation, and patient mortality, without a defined pathway for reuse. This commentary contends that coordinated redistribution of functional pumps is an actionable, near-term equity intervention and sustainability strategy, already occurring through nonprofit programs. We outline sources of surplus, the populations most affected by inadequate access, how redistribution can be operationalized safely, and the stakeholder roles and governance needed to implement a pump redistribution pathway.

articles.title: Effectiveness of Continuous Glucose Monitoring in Non-Intensively Managed Type 2 Diabetes: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
articles.journal: Journal of diabetes science and technology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The effectiveness of continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) in adults with type 2 diabetes (T2D) not receiving intensive insulin therapy remains incompletely established, particularly regarding glycemic metrics beyond glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c).

METHODS: We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) evaluating real-time CGM (rtCGM) or intermittently scanned CGM (isCGM) in adults with T2D managed with non-intensive insulin regimens or non-insulin therapies. Databases were searched from inception to February 2026. Primary outcomes included HbA1c, mean glucose concentration, time in range (%TIR), time above range (%TAR), time below range (%TBR), body mass index (BMI), and patient-reported outcomes. Random-effects meta-analyses were performed using Stata 17. Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane Risk-of-Bias tool, version 2, and certainty of evidence was evaluated using Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE).

RESULTS: Twenty-five RCTs were included. Continuous glucose monitoring significantly reduced HbA1c (mean difference [MD] -0.34, 95% confidence interval [CI], -0.46 to -0.23), mean glucose concentration (MD -13.97 mg/dL, 95% CI, -23.13 to -4.81), and %TAR (MD -6.75%, 95% CI, -10.81 to -2.70), while significantly increasing %TIR (MD +7.85%, 95% CI, 4.32-11.38). No significant effects were observed for BMI (MD -0.16 kg/m2, 95% CI, -0.45 to 0.12) or %TBR (MD -0.11%, 95% CI, -0.31 to 0.08). Benefits were generally more pronounced in non-insulin-treated populations. Patient-reported outcomes were heterogeneous but suggested improved treatment satisfaction and glucose-monitoring experience with CGM. Certainty of evidence was moderate across outcomes.

CONCLUSIONS: Continuous glucose monitoring probably improves glycemic control in adults with T2D not receiving intensive insulin therapy, particularly by reducing hyperglycemia and improving TIR, with limited effects on hypoglycemia or body weight.

articles.title: From Clinician-Based Risk Score to Diabetes Complications: Validating the Glycemia Risk Index with the Virtual Diabetes Control and Complications Trial Continuous Glucose Monitoring Data.
articles.journal: Journal of diabetes science and technology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The glycemia risk index (GRI) is a validated continuous glucose monitoring (CGM)-derived metric of overall glycemic risk. Hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c) has been the gold-standard metric of glycemic control since the Diabetes Control and Complications Trial (DCCT). This study evaluates the relationship of GRI with long-term diabetes complications and compares its performance with HbA1c within the Virtual DCCT.

METHODS: The Virtual DCCT reconstructed CGM traces from HbA1c values and quarterly 7-point capillary glucose profiles collected during the original DCCT. Glycemia risk index values were computed from 14 days of CGM data. Rates of retinopathy progression were calculated across deciles of GRI and HbA1c. Poisson regressions quantified the relationship between each metric and complication risk. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves evaluated the ability of GRI and HbA1c to discriminate between the DCCT intensive and conventional treatment groups.

RESULTS: Increased GRI was associated with higher rates of retinopathy progression (β=0.03, P < .001, D2=0.97). Comparable results were observed using HbA1c for retinopathy progression (β=0.47, P<.001, D2=0.93). The glycemia risk index also demonstrated separation between the intensive and conventional treatment groups, with an ROC area of 0.91 (95% CI, 0.90-0.93) compared to 0.88 (95% CI, 0.86-0.90) for HbA1c.

CONCLUSIONS: Glycemia risk index demonstrated a significant association with retinopathy progression within the Virtual DCCT framework. The relationship observed between GRI and retinopathy was comparable to that obtained using HbA1c. These findings extend the validation of GRI beyond clinician-based assessment and support its potential utility as a CGM-derived metric for glycemic risk assessment and diabetes complications.

articles.title: Invasive non-typhoidal Salmonella disease in the vaccine-development era: diagnostic blind spots, antimicrobial resistance, genomic transmission, and prevention.
articles.abstract: SUMMARYInvasive non-typhoidal Salmonella (iNTS) disease is a severe bloodstream and focal invasive infection caused by non-typhoidal serovars of Salmonella enterica, especially S. Typhimurium and S. Enteritidis. Its clinical importance is disproportionate to its routine visibility because disease often presents as undifferentiated fever, sepsis, meningitis, severe anaemia-associated deterioration, recurrent bacteraemia, or focal infection, while definitive recognition depends on blood or other sterile-site microbiology. Global estimates indicate substantial mortality, but the true incidence remains uncertain because blood-culture access, prior antimicrobial exposure, specimen volume, and surveillance intensity vary widely. The vaccine-development era has intensified the need for a unified clinical microbiology framework. Prevention of invasive disease requires host-risk recognition, laboratory-confirmed endpoints, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, lineage-aware genomic surveillance, reservoir assessment, and post-introduction systems able to detect residual disease, breakthrough infection, non-target serovars, lineage shifts, and resistant invasive clones. This narrative review synthesizes the clinical, immunological, genomic, diagnostic, antimicrobial resistance, and vaccine era evidence relevant to iNTS control. Emphasis is placed on immune evasion, macrophage survival, T-cell dysfunction, immunosuppressed hosts, diagnostic blind spots, treatment under uncertainty, and the integration of laboratory systems with surveillance and prevention policy.

articles.title: Cross-sectional Comparison of the PREVENT and Pooled Cohort Equations for 10-Year Atherosclerotic Cardiovascular Risk Estimates in a U.S. Cohort of Black and Latina Transgender Women with HIV.
articles.journal: Journal of acquired immune deficiency syndromes (1999)
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Transgender women with HIV face higher rates of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) than the general population. However, ASCVD risk estimators use binary sex variables that may misclassify their risk.
