articles.abstract: Degenerative diseases progress through gradual cell-intrinsic damage that is difficult to resolve with bulk transcriptomics or discrete cell-state analysis. We introduce a generalizable single-cell and spatial transcriptomics framework that quantifies continuous damage trajectories in vivo using cell-type-specific scores. Applied to chronic kidney disease and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease, the podocyte damage score (PDS) and hepatocyte damage score (HDS) place individual podocytes and hepatocytes on a health-to-damage axis. Across mouse and human single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq), single-nucleus RNA-seq (snRNA-seq), spatial transcriptomics, proteomics, histology, and clinical datasets, PDS and HDS robustly detect disease-associated damage, align disease models as well as unperturbed cells, and reveal conserved pathways. The PDS links podocyte injury and FSGS progression to circadian gene-expression disruption. The HDS identifies a damage threshold in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD)/NASH beyond which hepatocytes adopt senescent, metabolically dysfunctional states. These damage scores enable scalable mapping of degenerative disease progression and stage-specific therapeutic targets.

articles.title: PFO-Mediated Paradoxical Coronary Embolism Causing Myocardial Infarction: Concordant Imaging Findings.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Paradoxical coronary embolism is a rare cause of myocardial infarction in which establishing causality may be challenging without an identifiable venous thromboembolic source.

CASE SUMMARY: A 36-year-old man presented with chest pain and elevated troponin. Coronary angiography demonstrated distal thrombotic occlusion of the right posterolateral ventricular branch within an otherwise smooth coronary tree without significant atherosclerosis. Cardiac magnetic resonance showed subendocardial-to-transmural infarction with edema confined to the corresponding vascular territory. Transthoracic and transesophageal echocardiography demonstrated a patent foramen ovale (PFO) with right-to-left shunting, and no alternative embolic source was identified. Findings supported probable PFO-mediated paradoxical coronary embolism, and percutaneous closure was performed.

DISCUSSION: Concordant angiographic and cardiac magnetic resonance findings, together with echocardiographic demonstration of right-to-left shunting, supported probable paradoxical coronary embolism and guided conservative acute management followed by PFO closure.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: Plaque-free distal coronary thrombus should prompt consideration of embolism. Multimodality imaging can support mechanism-informed diagnosis and secondary prevention.

articles.title: Direct Visualization of Acute Left Atrial Pressure Elevation During Atrioventricular Nodal Re-Entrant Tachycardia.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Supraventricular tachycardia (SVT) can acutely elevate left atrial pressure (LAP), yet real-time hemodynamic data during spontaneous episodes are rarely captured. We present a case of real-time capture of LAP during SVT episodes using the implantable V-LAP system (Vectorious Medical Technologies), a new LAP monitoring sensor implanted in the interatrial septum of patients with heart failure.

CASE SUMMARY: A 55-year-old female patients with heart failure and an implanted implantable left atrial pressure (V-LAP) sensor presented with symptomatic SVT, which terminated with intravenous adenosine. The V-LAP sensor revealed that LAP rose acutely from 4.4 mm Hg to 16.4 mm Hg during SVT, returning to 3.2 mm Hg after its termination. An electrophysiology study confirmed typical atrioventricular nodal reentrant tachycardia, and successful ablation was performed.

DISCUSSION: This case provides the first direct visualization of elevated LAP during an atrioventricular nodal reentrant tachycardia episode and suggests that typical atrioventricular nodal reentrant tachycardia ablation was feasible, without device interference, in this patient with a V-LAP sensor. This case highlights the value of integrated electrical and hemodynamic monitoring in managing patients with cardiomyopathy and arrhythmia.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: The V-LAP sensor supports the hemodynamic contribution to symptom generation by correlating real-time LAP elevation with arrhythmia. Additionally, standard atrioventricular nodal reentrant tachycardia ablation was feasible in this patient with an interatrial septal sensor, without device interference.

articles.title: Right Superior Vena Cava Drainage Into the Left Atrium in Association With Vein of Galen Malformation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Anomalous drainage of the right superior vena cava to the left atrium is a rare form of congenital heart disease. This typically results in mild cyanosis when present as an isolated defect.

CASE SUMMARY: An asymptomatic term female demonstrated an SpO2 level of 88% despite supplemental oxygen. Transthoracic echocardiography with agitated saline contrast injection revealed drainage of upper-extremity venous blood to the left atrium. Advanced imaging confirmed the diagnosis and revealed partial anomalous pulmonary venous return. Hemodynamic instability noted following elective repair prompted additional investigation and demonstrated a congenital arteriovenous malformation in the brain (vein of Galen malformation).

DISCUSSION: This case highlights a rare association of a vein of Galen malformation with abnormal drainage of the right superior vena cava. It underscores the importance of maintaining a high index of suspicion for noncardiac anomalies when taking care of a patient with congenital heart disease.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: Multimodality imaging is essential to detecting associated intracardiac and often extracardiac anomalies.

articles.title: Delayed Aortic Embolization of a Left Atrial Appendage Occlusion Device: Implications for Risk-Stratified Postprocedural Management.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Left atrial appendage occlusion (LAAO) is an established alternative to long-term anticoagulation for stroke prevention in select patients with atrial fibrillation. Device embolization is rare, most commonly occurring intraprocedurally or within 24 hours.

CASE SUMMARY: A 67-year-old man with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation underwent successful implantation of a Watchman FLX device. Eighteen days later, while shoveling snow, he developed sudden-onset chest and back pain followed by bilateral lower extremity paralysis. Computed tomography revealed complete mid-abdominal aortic occlusion from embolization of the LAAO device. Despite emergent endovascular retrieval and restoration of aortic flow, the patient developed fatal distributive shock from severe ischemia-reperfusion injury.

DISCUSSION: This case illustrates a rare but clinically significant presentation of delayed device embolization. This patient possessed multiple National Cardiovascular Data Registry-identified risk factors for postdischarge device embolization, indicating that current risk stratification protocols may not be adequate for patients with device embolization risk factors.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: Risk-stratified protocols with extended activity restrictions and earlier postprocedure surveillance imaging warrant investigation in patients with National Cardiovascular Data Registry-identified risk factors for postdischarge LAAO device embolization.

articles.title: Guiding Pacemaker Implantation With Multimodality Imaging in an Adult With Ventricular Septal Defect.
articles.abstract:
CASE SUMMARY: A 57-year-old man with a history of congenital ventricular septal defect and bicuspid aortic valve with surgical repair of aortic coarctation presented with dyspnea and found to be in complete heart block with junctional escape rhythm necessitating pacemaker implantation.

DISCUSSION: Pacemaker implantation in adult congenital heart disease and atrioventricular block requires preprocedural planning. Multimodality imaging is important in patients with complex septal anatomy, as it can reduce procedural difficulty and improve procedural safety by identifying optimal lead positioning strategies.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: Multimodality imaging can facilitate safer and more precise pacemaker implantation in adult patients with congenital heart disease with abnormal septal anatomy.

articles.title: Purulent Pneumococcal Pericarditis Presenting as Normotensive Cardiac Tamponade in Austrian Syndrome.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Austrian syndrome is a rare manifestation of invasive Streptococcus pneumoniae infection. Purulent pneumococcal pericarditis causing cardiac tamponade is an exceptionally uncommon but life-threatening complication.

CASE SUMMARY: A 63-year-old unhoused woman presented with altered mental status and respiratory failure. Despite preserved blood pressure, electrocardiography demonstrated electrical alternans, and point-of-care echocardiography revealed cardiac tamponade. Pericardiocentesis yielded purulent fluid growing S pneumoniae. Systemic emboli and echocardiographic findings were consistent with Austrian syndrome complicated by purulent pericarditis and cardiac tamponade. Despite medical and surgical management, the patient developed refractory shock and died.

DISCUSSION: Purulent pneumococcal pericarditis may present with tamponade despite normotension or hypertension. Early recognition and prompt drainage are critical.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: Cardiac tamponade may occur despite preserved blood pressure. Electrical alternans and point-of-care echocardiography are key diagnostic clues. Purulent pericarditis often requires surgical drainage and carries high mortality.

articles.title: Tetralogy of Fallot With Pulmonary Atresia/MAPCAs Complicated by Bronchial Ischemia and Pneumonectomy.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Bronchial ischemia after unifocalization in patients with tetralogy of Fallot with pulmonary atresia and major aortopulmonary collateral arteries (ToF/PA/MAPCAs) is a rare and serious postoperative complication. Progression to carinal dehiscence requiring pneumonectomy, and subsequent survival with a single lung, has not been previously reported.

CASE SUMMARY: We describe a 4-month-old girl with 22q11.2 deletion and ToF/PA/MAPCAs who developed bronchial ischemia with carinal dehiscence after unifocalization surgery, ultimately requiring left pneumonectomy and slide tracheoplasty. Despite this, she underwent successful biventricular repair at 1 year of age and was discharged 17 months after her initial procedure.

CONCLUSIONS: This case demonstrates that single-lung physiology can sustain adequate oxygenation and ventilation after biventricular repair in patients with ToF/PA/MAPCAs, while highlighting the critical importance of recognizing bronchial ischemia as a postoperative complication of unifocalization.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: Bronchial ischemia should be recognized as a rare but critical postoperative complication of unifocalization surgery in patients with ToF/PA/MAPCAs with potential to progress to carinal dehiscence requiring pneumonectomy. The key considerations for managing single-lung physiology include permissive hypercapnia and protective lung strategies in the postoperative period and close surveillance assessing the need for pulmonary vasodilators due to the risk of pulmonary hypertension. Biventricular repair remains a feasible option in selected patients with ToF/PA/MAPCAs after pneumonectomy.

articles.title: Desminopathy: A Rare Cause of Cardiac Arrhythmia.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Desminopathy is a disorder of the desmin intermediate filament network, caused by a defect in the desmin gene (DES), which can lead to cardiomyopathy and skeletal myopathy. However, cardiac arrhythmia is a rare presentation of desminopathy.

CASE SUMMARY: A previously well 29-year-old woman presented with ventricular fibrillation and complete heart block, with subsequently slow decline in skeletal muscle function. Following extensive work-up, she was found to have a novel mutation of the desmin gene (DES c.640-1G>C).

DISCUSSION: We have identified a new DES variant possibly causing ventricular fibrillation, complete heart block, and skeletal myopathy. There is currently no cure, and management focusses on optimizing medical management and quality of life.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: It is important to determine the cause for unusual arrhythmic presentations, and we hope to increase awareness of genetic causes for cardiac arrhythmias. Multidisciplinary teamwork is important in managing these cases and optimizing patient care.

articles.title: Post-TAVR Bundle Branch Re-entrant Ventricular Tachycardia Managed Without ICD: A Rare Turn of Rhythm.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Conduction disturbances are common after transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR), usually manifesting as atrioventricular block. Rarely, injury to the His-Purkinje system may create substrate for bundle branch re-entrant ventricular tachycardia (BBR-VT).

CASE SUMMARY: A 78-year-old man developed new conduction abnormalities after TAVR and was discharged on ambulatory monitoring. Loop recorder interrogation revealed recurrent symptomatic wide-complex tachycardia. Repeat electrophysiology study demonstrated inducible sustained monomorphic ventricular tachycardia with His-V-His activation confirming BBR-VT. Two reciprocal re-entrant circuits were inducible: one with antegrade conduction over the right bundle branch (left bundle branch block-pattern QRS) and the other in the reverse direction (right bundle branch block-pattern QRS). Right bundle branch ablation terminated the arrhythmia and induced persistent right bundle branch block. Given paroxysmal complete atrioventricular block, a dual-chamber pacemaker was implanted. With preserved ventricular function and no additional substrate, implantable cardioverter-defibrillator insertion was deferred.

DISCUSSION: BBR-VT is a rare but serious complication of post-TAVR conduction injury. Early recognition allows curative ablation and tailored device therapy.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: Post-TAVR conduction delay can facilitate BBR-VT. Successful ablation with pacing may avoid implantable cardioverter insertion implantation in selected patients.

articles.title: Intracardiac Thrombi Mimicking Cardiac Metastases in a Patient With Lung Adenocarcinoma.
articles.abstract:
CASE SUMMARY: A 50-year-old man with venous thromboembolism and newly diagnosed lung adenocarcinoma developed 2 right-sided intracardiac masses that persisted despite therapeutic anticoagulation. Findings on cardiac magnetic resonance raised concern for cardiac metastases. Histopathologic examination of the excised atrial mass demonstrated organizing thrombus, and the remaining ventricular lesion resolved after 1 month of therapeutic enoxaparin.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: Cancer-associated intracardiac thrombi may mimic metastatic disease on cardiac magnetic resonance because their fibrin-rich and inflammatory composition can produce overlapping imaging features. When imaging and clinical findings are discordant, histopathologic confirmation may be required for definitive diagnosis and management.

articles.title: Reversible Right-to-Left Shunt After Mitral TEER Resolved by Tricuspid TEER.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Iatrogenic atrial septal defects are common after transseptal interventions and are usually clinically insignificant; however, under specific hemodynamic conditions, they may result in clinically relevant right-to-left shunting and hypoxemia.

CASE SUMMARY: A 67-year-old woman with severe mitral and torrential tricuspid regurgitation underwent a combined transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (TEER) strategy. Shortly after successful mitral TEER, the patient developed acute hypoxemia (oxygen saturation decreased from 96% to 82%) during preparation for tricuspid intervention. Transesophageal echocardiography revealed a 0.7-cm iatrogenic atrial septal defect with predominant right-to-left shunting. Instead of defect closure, tricuspid TEER was performed, resulting in rapid improvement in oxygen saturation (to 95%) and reversal of shunt direction.

DISCUSSION: Right-to-left shunting after mitral TEER may be driven by right-sided pressure overload and altered flow dynamics rather than the septal defect itself.

CONCLUSIONS: Treating tricuspid regurgitation can restore interatrial pressure balance, reverse shunt direction, and potentially obviate the need for atrial septal defect closure.

articles.title: Severe Functional Tricuspid Regurgitation Masked by Annular Deformation in Primary Cardiac Lymphoma.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Primary cardiac lymphoma can regress rapidly with chemotherapy; however, release of tumor-related annular compression may paradoxically alter valvular geometry and unmask regurgitation.

CASE SUMMARY: A 79-year-old woman with clinically diagnosed primary cardiac diffuse large B-cell lymphoma involving the right heart developed severe tricuspid regurgitation 4 months after chemotherapy despite marked tumor regression. Serial echocardiography demonstrated relief of extrinsic tricuspid annular compression, subsequent annular enlargement and flattening, and leaflet malcoaptation without progressive intrinsic leaflet or subvalvular abnormalities. Symptoms improved with intensified diuretic therapy.

DISCUSSION: This case suggests that tumor regression likely contributed to compression release-related annular remodeling, thereby unmasking severe functional tricuspid regurgitation. In cardiac tumors adjacent to valvular structures, serial imaging should evaluate annular geometry as well as tumor burden.

TAKE HOME MESSAGES: Rapid regression of a cardiac tumor adjacent to a valve may paradoxically unmask or worsen valvular regurgitation by altering annular geometry. Serial echocardiography should assess annular configuration and leaflet coaptation, not only tumor burden, in patients with cardiac tumors involving valvular structures.

articles.title: Left Atrial Appendage Occlusion for Persistent Thrombus Preventing Rhythm Control.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Atrial fibrillation is the most common sustained arrhythmia and a major risk factor for cardioembolic stroke. Left atrial appendage occlusion (LAAO) is an established alternative to long-term anticoagulation in selected patients; however, active left atrial appendage (LAA) thrombus is generally considered a contraindication.

CASE SUMMARY: A 69-year-old man with hypertension, hyperlipidemia, newly diagnosed nonvalvular atrial fibrillation, and severe left ventricular systolic dysfunction (ejection fraction 20% to 25%) underwent transesophageal echocardiography (TEE) before cardioversion. A large apical LAA thrombus was identified, preventing cardioversion. Despite 9 months of anticoagulation, with apixaban for 2 months followed by warfarin for 7 months, serial TEEs demonstrated persistent thrombus despite supratherapeutic international normalized ratio values as high as 6.9. Following multidisciplinary evaluation, TEE-guided 27-mm Watchman FLX device was successfully performed without complication allowing direct-current cardioversion to normal sinus rhythm with return to normal ejection fraction.

DISCUSSION: This case highlights the potential role of LAAO in patients when persistent thrombus prevents definitive rhythm control.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: Persistent LAA thrombus may remain despite prolonged anticoagulation and can prevent definitive rhythm-control therapy in patients with atrial fibrillation. To recognize persistent LAA thrombus as a barrier to rhythm-control therapy and review the role of LAAO in carefully selected patients with thrombus refractory to anticoagulation.

articles.title: Compound MYH7 Mutations: Risk Stratification Challenges in an Affected Family.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) is a genetically heterogeneous disease associated with sudden cardiac death (SCD). Risk stratification is challenging in genotype-positive individuals with borderline phenotypic expression.

CASE SUMMARY: A 54-year-old man was referred for SCD risk stratification in familial HCM. His daughter had obstructive HCM, underwent septal myomectomy, and received an implantable cardioverter-defibrillator after a cardiac arrest. The patient was asymptomatic with mild septal hypertrophy and nonsustained ventricular tachycardia. Genetic testing revealed 2 pathogenic MYH7 variants in his daughter (Ala655Thr and Gly571Arg); the patient carried only Ala655Thr, whereas his wife carried Gly571Arg. Repeat cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) under anesthesia revealed late gadolinium enhancement burden of 23%, prompting implantable cardioverter-defibrillator insertion.

DISCUSSION: This case underscores the value of cardiac MRI and genetic testing in individualizing SCD risk assessment when conventional HCM markers are insufficient.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: Genotype-phenotype discordance in familial HCM underscores the need for family-based genetic evaluation and individualized risk stratification. Cardiac MRI is invaluable for SCD risk assessment in ambiguous cases.

articles.title: Presumed Fatal Bronchospasm From Adenosine Administered for Assessment of Fractional Flow Reserve.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Adenosine is a commonly used vasodilating agent to induce hyperemia in fractional flow reserve. Most side effects are transient and self-limiting because of its short half-life.

CASE SUMMARY: A 79-year-old man with known airway disease underwent coronary angiography for unstable angina. A moderate-to-severe lesion was found in the proximal left anterior descending artery. Pressure wire assessment was undertaken and intravenous adenosine was administered. This resulted in severe bronchospasm progressing to respiratory arrest. Despite resuscitation attempts, the patient did not survive.

DISCUSSION: Although bronchospasm is a recognized adverse reaction to adenosine, to our knowledge there have been no prior reports of presumed fatal adenosine-associated bronchospasm during fractional flow reserve testing.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: Although extremely rare, adenosine carries a risk of fatal bronchospasm, and alternative hyperemic agents or nonhyperemic physiological indices should be used preferentially in patients with known obstructive airway disease. Aminophylline should be immediately available in all clinical settings where adenosine is administered frequently.

articles.title: Directional Coronary Atherectomy as a Diagnostic Adjunct in Suspected IgG4-Related Coronary Artery Disease.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Immunoglobulin (Ig) G4-related disease can involve the cardiovascular system, and isolated vessel involvement is diagnostically challenging.

CASE SUMMARY: A 79-year-old Japanese man with a history of percutaneous coronary intervention presented with exertional angina. Imaging demonstrated in-stent occlusion of the left anterior descending artery, severe distal left circumflex artery stenosis, and marked adventitial thickening of the coronary arteries and aorta. Serum IgG4 levels were markedly elevated. Directional coronary atherectomy (DCA) enabled retrieval of intimal tissue. Although the pathological findings did not fulfill formal classification criteria, tissue sampling provided supportive histopathological evidence for IgG4-related disease. Prednisolone therapy resulted in regression of adventitial thickening and reduction of nonrevascularized coronary lesions.

DISCUSSION: DCA may serve as both a therapeutic strategy and an adjunctive diagnostic approach.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: DCA may provide supportive histopathological information when conventional biopsy is not feasible, and steroid therapy can be effective for cases of vascular involvement in IgG4-related disease.

articles.title: Primary Cardiac Leiomyosarcoma in a Young Patient: A Therapeutic Challenge.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Primary cardiac leiomyosarcoma is an extremely rare and aggressive sarcoma. Its diagnosis is challenging, and its treatment is not yet standardized, resulting in a poor prognosis.

CASE SUMMARY: A 29-year-old man presented with a 1-month history of respiratory symptoms, initially treated with antiflu medication and antibiotics, showing no clinical improvement. During cardiology consultation, a cardiac mass was identified on echocardiography and subsequently characterized by cardiac magnetic resonance and positron emission tomography. Histopathological and immunohistochemical studies confirmed the diagnosis. The patient remains alive at 20 months while receiving systemic treatment.

DISCUSSION: The diagnosis of primary cardiac leiomyosarcoma is challenging due to its rarity and aggressive behavior; it requires multimodal imaging and immunohistochemical confirmation. Its treatment remains nonstandardized, with limited evidence supporting the benefit of combining surgery, chemotherapy, and/or radiotherapy. This case highlights the importance of timely diagnosis and documents longer survival than typically reported.

articles.title: Balancing Ischemia and Hemorrhage After Tenecteplase in Wake-Up Stroke.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Contemporary stroke management assumes discrete clinical scenarios with clear separation between ischemic and hemorrhagic risks. When these processes coexist, guideline recommendations may be insufficient or conflicting.

CASE SUMMARY: A 74-year-old woman with a wake-up stroke received computed tomography perfusion-guided thrombolysis. She developed hemorrhagic transformation, followed by intermediate-risk pulmonary embolism (PE) requiring anticoagulation. Despite treatment, recurrent intracranial large-vessel occlusion occurred; mechanical thrombectomy achieved complete reperfusion. Transesophageal echocardiography revealed a thrombus traversing a patent foramen ovale, confirming paradoxical embolism. WHY BEYOND THE GUIDELINES?: Management required balancing competing thrombotic and hemorrhagic risks: anticoagulation for PE after hemorrhagic transformation and thrombectomy in a recently thrombolyzed brain.

DISCUSSION: Overlapping thrombotic and hemorrhagic conditions require individualized decision-making guided by continuous risk reassessment and multidisciplinary collaboration.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: Concurrent stroke, PE, and hemorrhagic transformation create conflicting recommendations requiring dynamic decision-making. A thrombus crossing a patent foramen ovale confirms paradoxical embolism and justifies aggressive intervention.

articles.title: Stent-Free Sirolimus DCB for Left Main STEMI: Acute and Long-Term OCT Follow-Up.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Left main (LM) ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) is typically managed with urgent stent implantation according to current guidelines. Yet intravascular imaging has shown that plaque erosion may permit alternative strategies.

CASE SUMMARY: A 43-year-old man with anterior STEMI and hypotension underwent angiography, revealing distal LM thrombus extending into the left anterior descending/left circumflex arteries. Postaspiration optical coherence tomography (OCT) confirmed plaque erosion without rupture. Following lesion preparation, a drug-coated balloon-only strategy was applied to all 3 vessels. Follow-ups at 20 days and 15 months confirmed vessel patency, satisfactory healing, and no recoil or neoatherosclerosis.

DISCUSSION: Current guidelines lack support for stent-free LM STEMI intervention. However, OCT-guided management allows for individualized treatment in young patients by characterizing lesion biology. Long-term follow-up demonstrates successful vessel healing, suggesting that avoiding permanent metallic scaffolds in selected cases may mitigate lifelong stenting risks.

TAKE-HOME-MESSAGE: OCT can identify plaque erosion and guide stent-free percutaneous coronary intervention in select left main STEMI cases, offering durable healing and flexibility in antithrombotic therapy.

articles.title: Dyspnea as an Anginal Equivalent: Multimodality Diagnosis of Dynamic, Severe Ischemic Mitral Regurgitation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Dynamic ischemic mitral regurgitation (IMR), provoked by ischemia or exercise, may escape detection at rest and is associated with adverse outcomes.

CASE SUMMARY: A 65-year-old man with ischemic cardiomyopathy (left ventricular ejection fraction, 20%) and recurrent left circumflex in-stent restenosis refractory to multiple interventions presented with progressive dyspnea and chest pain. Resting filling pressures were mildly abnormal, though symptoms remained out of proportion to findings. During balloon angioplasty of the left circumflex, transient ischemia provoked large V waves on the pulmonary catheter wedge pressure tracing; simultaneous echocardiography confirmed severe MR that resolved on deflation of the intracoronary balloon. Stress echocardiography corroborated exercise-induced severe MR. Despite revascularization and medical therapy optimization, symptoms persisted, and mitral transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (M-TEER) was performed with successful resolution of symptoms.

DISCUSSION: Dynamic IMR may be underdiagnosed when diagnostic studies are performed at rest. This case demonstrates concordant invasive and noninvasive provocative strategies for diagnosis, with M-TEER for refractory symptoms.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: Dynamic IMR requires a high index of suspicion and provocative multimodality testing. M-TEER may benefit patients with severe IMR refractory to revascularization and optimized medical therapy.

articles.title: Microaxial Flow Pump Thrombosis Presenting as Predominant Direct Hyperbilirubinemia.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Clinically significant hemolysis and device thrombosis are uncommon with the Impella 5.5, and presentation with predominant direct hyperbilirubinemia has not been described.

CASE SUMMARY: A 57-year-old man with refractory cardiogenic shock underwent Impella 5.5 placement as a bridge to transplant. He developed severe direct-predominant hyperbilirubinemia (total bilirubin 18.4 mg/dL; direct 11.7 mg/dL) with rising lactate dehydrogenase (1,395 U/L) and undetectable haptoglobin, despite normal purge pressures and no device alarms. Duplex ultrasonography excluded biliary obstruction. Device exchange revealed a large, organized thrombus in the motor/outflow housing, after which hemolysis was resolved, and biochemical improvement followed, allowing successful bridging to heart transplantation.

DISCUSSION: Occult Impella thrombosis may present as direct-predominant hyperbilirubinemia, an atypical pattern that can mimic hepatobiliary disease and confound the diagnostic evaluation.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: Direct hyperbilirubinemia during Impella support should prompt evaluation for subclinical device thrombosis. Timely device exchange can reverse hemolysis and preserve transplant candidacy.

articles.title: Intravascular Ultrasound-Guided Balloon Spacer Technique for Unstable Device Passage During LAD PCI.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coronary dissection during percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) may create a dissection-related cavity that destabilizes device passage. When rewiring alone does not ensure stable true-lumen device delivery, a balloon spacer technique may serve as a bailout option.

CASE SUMMARY: A man in his 50s underwent staged PCI for severe mid-left anterior descending artery stenosis. After cutting-balloon dilation, intravascular ultrasound (IVUS) suggested a dissection-related cavity. IVUS-guided rewiring placed a second guidewire in the true lumen, but repeat balloon passage followed the cavity. IVUS-based assessment guided selection of a 1.5 × 10 mm semicompliant balloon for focal occlusion, after which stents were successfully delivered.

DISCUSSION: This case highlights the gap between true-lumen rewiring and stable device passage during PCI-related dissection.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: True-lumen rewiring does not necessarily ensure stable device passage. IVUS may help guide balloon spacer bailout when device passage remains unstable after rewiring.

articles.title: Recurrent Nonischemic Left Ventricular Aneurysms: A Cardiac MRI-Driven Diagnosis in a DES Variant Carrier.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) is the gold-standard technique for characterizing nonischemic structural cardiomyopathies, offering tissue characterization and precise localization of myocardial injury.

CASE SUMMARY: A 24-year-old man presented with recurrent chest discomfort and tachyarrhythmias. Initial CMR revealed an apical left ventricular aneurysm with imaging features consistent with a true aneurysm and normal coronary arteries, successfully treated surgically. Five years later, recurrent ventricular tachycardia prompted re-evaluation; CMR identified a new inferolateral basal aneurysm in a region previously normal on postoperative imaging. Coronary computed tomography angiography again showed normal epicardial coronary arteries. Surgical patch repair and implantable cardioverter-defibrillator placement were performed. Genetic testing revealed a pathogenic desmin (DES) c.785A>T (p.Glu262Val) variant and additional variant of unknown significance in VCL and CDH2.

DISCUSSION: The identification of a pathogenic DES variant suggests a potential underlying susceptibility to structural remodeling, although causality cannot be confirmed.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: CMR was crucial in identifying sequential, anatomically distinct left ventricular aneurysms. The combination of recurrent nonischemic aneurysms and a pathogenic DES variant suggests a possible cytoskeletal genetic cardiomyopathy with arrhythmic risk.

articles.title: Critical Aortic Stenosis With Rapid Multiorgan Decompensation Reversed by Emergency TAVR.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Critical aortic stenosis can deteriorate abruptly from compensated disease to low-output shock and multiorgan dysfunction. We describe rapid multiorgan decompensation from severe bicuspid aortic stenosis with recovery following emergency transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR).

CASE SUMMARY: A previously active 69-year-old man with severe bicuspid aortic stenosis re-presented to the emergency department with pulmonary edema and rapidly progressive breathlessness. Although systolic blood pressure was preserved, he had severe hypoperfusion with lactate 8.6 mmol/L, alanine aminotransferase 5,379 IU/L, international normalized ratio 2.8, creatinine 189 μmol/L, and bilirubin 48 μmol/L. Repeat echocardiography demonstrated new biventricular dysfunction, functional mitral regurgitation, and a high probability of pulmonary hypertension. He underwent emergency transfemoral TAVR, which reduced the gradient from 129 to <10 mm Hg. The biochemical abnormalities improved within 48 hours, and he was discharged well 8 days later.

DISCUSSION: This case illustrates rapid, reversible multiorgan decompensation caused by critical aortic stenosis.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: Deteriorating critical aortic stenosis should prompt urgent reassessment and expedited intervention. Emergency TAVR can restore forward flow and facilitate rapid physiologic recovery.

articles.title: Transient Coronary Thrombosis Mimicking Myopericarditis Revealing JAK2-Positive Essential Thrombocythemia.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute coronary thrombosis without atherosclerosis may mimic myopericarditis, particularly in young patients.

CASE SUMMARY: A 20-year-old woman presented with pleuritic chest pain following a viral illness. Serial electrocardiography showed dynamic ST-segment elevation in leads V3 to V6, and high-sensitivity troponin T increased from 18.6 to 1,151 ng/L. Echocardiography demonstrated regional wall motion abnormalities in the left anterior descending territory. Coronary angiography revealed a proximal left anterior descending intraluminal thrombus causing severe narrowing without underlying atherosclerosis. Conservative management with anticoagulation and dual antiplatelet therapy was initiated. Repeat angiography after 3 days showed complete thrombus resolution with no residual stenosis. Further evaluation revealed marked thrombocytosis and a JAK2 V617F mutation, confirming essential thrombocythemia.

DISCUSSION: This case highlights a mechanism-based approach to myopericarditis-like presentations. JAK2-positive essential thrombocythemia represents a plausible prothrombotic contributor after the exclusion of common causes of coronary artery disease in very young patients.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: Dynamic regional electrocardiogram changes, rapid troponin elevation, and regional wall motion abnormalities should prompt coronary evaluation despite pleuritic symptoms.

articles.title: Kounis Syndrome Triggered by Hymenoptera Stings and Exacerbated by Streptokinase.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Kounis syndrome (KS) is an allergy-mediated acute coronary syndrome that is frequently under-recognized and potentially life threatening.

CASE SUMMARY: A 52-year-old man developed an inferior ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction following a bee swarm attack. Standard thrombolysis with streptokinase triggered severe hemodynamic collapse and systemic hemorrhage. Upon recognizing KS, management was shifted to steroids and antihistamines, leading to complete recovery. Recurrence was documented 8 years later following an ant bite.

DISCUSSION: This case illustrates how standard acute coronary syndromes treatments, such as antigenic thrombolytics, can inadvertently exacerbate the allergic cascade in KS. It highlights the need to maintain a high index of suspicion when cardiac symptoms follow an allergic trigger.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: Avoid antigenic thrombolytics when KS is suspected to prevent iatrogenic clinical deterioration. Primary percutaneous coronary intervention and early allergy management are the preferred clinical strategies.

articles.title: Gallic acid carbon dot-supported heparin-like polymer as an optimized membrane-anchored anticoagulant for functionalization of hemodialysis membranes.
articles.abstract: Conventional hemodialysis membranes exhibit suboptimal blood compatibility, predisposing patients to thrombotic events and oxidative stress-associated complications that accelerate disease progression. To address this challenge, we developed a gallic acid carbon dots (GA-CDs)-functionalized polyethersulfone (PES) membrane via polydopamine-assisted co-deposition of nitrogen-doped GA-CDs and a heparin-mimetic polymer. The resulting membrane features stable surface immobilization of GA-CDs, conferring durable hemocompatibility and intrinsic dual functionality: (i) sustained ROS-scavenging-driven antioxidant activity for long-term oxidative stress mitigation; and (ii) enhancement of anticoagulant performance through suppression of oxidative stress-mediated tissue factor (TF) activation, thereby synergistically preventing thrombosis. Mechanistically, GA-CDs activated the nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 (Nrf2) signaling cascade to upregulate endogenous antioxidant enzymes, efficient reactive oxygen species (ROS) clearance, and protection against oxidative cellular damage. Concurrently, by scavenging ROS, GA-CDs suppressed oxidative stress-induced tissue factor activation, establishing a functional link between redox homeostasis and coagulation regulation. In vitro evaluation demonstrated outstanding dual functionality: potent free radical scavenging capacity (83% DPPH and 97% ABTS⁺ scavenging), significantly prolonged activated partial thromboplastin time (APTT 420 s, 8.4-fold increase vs. control), excellent cytocompatibility, and markedly improved hemocompatibility. Collectively, these findings highlight the translational promise of this rationally designed dual-action hemodialysis membrane, where localized durable ROS scavenging and surface-confined anticoagulation operate in concert to mitigate key pathophysiological drivers of dialysis-associated complications.

articles.title: Evaluation of Chromium Picolinate Supplementation and Insulin Requirements in Critically Ill Adults With Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus.
articles.journal: The Journal of pharmacy technology : jPT : official publication of the Association of Pharmacy Technicians
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chromium picolinate has been studied as an adjunct to improve glycemic indices in ambulatory type 2 diabetes mellitus, but its role in critically ill patients is unknown.

OBJECTIVE: To evaluate whether chromium picolinate supplementation was associated with reduced insulin requirements without worsening glycemic control in critically ill adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus.

METHODS: We conducted a single-center retrospective pre-post cohort study of adult intensive care unit patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus or hemoglobin A1c ≥6.5% who received insulin and at least 4 consecutive chromium picolinate doses between July 2022 and January 2023. Patients served as their own controls during 24-hour pre- and post-chromium periods. The primary outcome was change in total daily insulin dose. Secondary outcomes included proportion of measured glucose values within 140 to 180 mg/dL, acute kidney injury, hypoglycemia, and exploratory Sequential Organ Failure Assessment-2 change.

RESULTS: Among 91 screened patients, 45 met the inclusion criteria. Median total daily insulin dose decreased from 76.3 U/d (interquartile range [IQR], 40.1-96.9) before chromium to 40.0 U/d (IQR, 20.5-65.6) after chromium; the Hodges-Lehmann paired difference was -23.0 U/d (95% CI, -33.25 to -14.25; P < .0001). Proportion of measured glucose values within target did not differ significantly. No post-intervention hypoglycemia was observed, and 2 patients met the study-defined acute kidney injury criterion. Interpretation is limited by the retrospective design and absence of a concurrent control group.

CONCLUSIONS: Chromium picolinate supplementation was associated with lower insulin requirements without worsening glycemic control. These hypothesis-generating findings require confirmation in prospective controlled studies.

articles.title: Fractional exhaled nitric oxide in non-cystic fibrosis bronchiectasis: an exploratory prospective observational study.
articles.journal: Monaldi archives for chest disease = Archivio Monaldi per le malattie del torace
articles.abstract: Fractional exhaled nitric oxide (FeNO) is a non-invasive biomarker of type 2 airway inflammation, but its role in non-cystic fibrosis bronchiectasis remains uncertain. This study explored the associations of FeNO with peripheral blood eosinophils, pulmonary function, high-resolution computed tomography (HRCT)-defined morphology, and short-term post-treatment change in adults with non-cystic fibrosis bronchiectasis. We conducted an exploratory prospective observational study including 152 adults with clinically and HRCT-confirmed non-cystic fibrosis bronchiectasis admitted to a national tertiary pulmonary center. FeNO was measured using a standardized single-flow technique. Pulmonary function testing, blood eosinophil assessment, and HRCT evaluation were performed. Descriptive statistics, between-group comparisons, correlation analyses, and exploratory multivariable linear regression were used. A subgroup underwent repeat FeNO assessment after antibiotic treatment. Mean FeNO was 12.1±7.9 ppb. FeNO correlated positively with blood eosinophil percentage (r=0.41, p<0.001) and MEF50% predicted (r=0.48, p<0.001) and inversely with total lung capacity % predicted (r=-0.39, p<0.001). FeNO distributions differed across ventilatory patterns (overall Kruskal-Wallis p=0.030) and HRCT morphology groups (overall Kruskal-Wallis p=0.040); the exploratory cylindrical versus cystic/saccular comparison yielded p=0.023 (unadjusted). In exploratory multivariable regression, blood eosinophil percentage remained associated with FeNO (β=1.12, 95% confidence interval: 0.29-1.95; p=0.009). Among 55 reassessed patients, FeNO decreased from 12.1±6.8 to 7.0±3.1 ppb after antibiotic treatment (p=0.010). FeNO was generally low in adults with non-cystic fibrosis bronchiectasis but showed exploratory associations with eosinophilic inflammation, selected pulmonary function parameters, HRCT morphology, and short-term post-treatment change. Larger longitudinal studies with standardized severity classification, microbiological characterization, and predefined outcomes are needed before FeNO can be recommended for routine clinical use.

articles.title: The determinants of incorrect inhaler use in patients with obstructive airway disease.
articles.journal: Monaldi archives for chest disease = Archivio Monaldi per le malattie del torace
articles.abstract: Inhaler therapy is the standard treatment for obstructive airway disease. Even in today's world, it is very challenging to utilize this therapy optimally. Errors in inhaler technique are very common. Identifying the errors is the first step towards correction to improve the disease. This is a cross-sectional observational study conducted at AIMS, Mohali, where 212 patients on inhaler therapy were enrolled who were diagnosed with asthma or chronic obstructive pulmonary disease or post-tuberculosis lung disease. The inhaler technique was assessed by a 5-point inhaler technique checklist by the clinician during the OPD visit. A multivariate binomial regression analysis was performed to calculate the crude and adjusted odds ratio of at least 1 error in inhalation technique and other covariates, including age, gender, education, profession, device, duration, and diagnosis. Among 212 enrolled patients, 135 adults (18-60 yrs) and 77 elderly (>60 years) were analyzed. Elderly [p<0.001; adjusted odds ratio (AOR) 8.12], unemployed (p=0.016), more than 5 years of inhaler use (p=0.005; AOR 9.54) and metered dose inhaler (p<0.001; AOR 5.86) had more chances of committing at least 1 error in inhaler technique. Identifying and correcting the errors in inhalational technique is the easiest and cost effective method to decrease the exacerbations and improve disease control in patients suffering from OAD by further decreasing the healthcare burden.

articles.title: African recommendations for diagnosis and management of systemic juvenile idiopathic arthritis (sJIA) - a PAFLAR initiative.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To develop evidence-based recommendations for diagnosis and treatment of children and adolescents with systemic juvenile idiopathic arthritis (sJIA), taking into consideration the socioeconomic status and availability of medications in African countries.

METHODS: A steering group composed of five PAFLAR members formulated questions in PICO format (Patient/Population, Intervention, Comparison, Outcome), conducted a systematic literature review, and identified experts in pediatric rheumatology throughout Africa. The Delphi method was used to reach consensus among the experts on the recommendations for diagnosis and treatment of sJIA patients.

RESULTS: The online Delphi questionnaire was sent to the 22 experts selected by the steering committee, who were asked to vote for each statement and to provide their suggestions for modifications or rewording. A 100% response rate was obtained. A minimum agreement of 70% among the voting panel was required. A total of 15 recommendations were formulated, 4 regarding diagnosis and 11 regarding treatment. The percentage of agreement with the recommendations ranged from 72.7% to 95%.

CONCLUSION: We present the first African recommendations for diagnosis and management of sJIA. The feedback about the application of these recommendations in pediatric rheumatology centers will serve as the basis for future revisions in the light of African-specific experiences and insights.

articles.title: Factors associated with 1-year health-related quality of life after neck-specific exercise in chronic whiplash-associated disorders: an exploratory secondary analysis of a randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Factors associated with changes in health-related quality of life (HRQoL) outcomes in neck disorders have not been investigated after internet-based support for exercise. The purpose of the study was to investigate baseline and short-term outcome factors associated with changes in HRQoL (EQ-5D-3L and EQ-VAS) at 3 and 15 months, respectively, after a neck-specific exercise programme (NSE) for individuals with chronic whiplash-associated disorders grades 2 and 3.

METHODS: This was a secondary analysis of a prospective randomized controlled multi-centre trial with concealed allocation. Participants (n = 140) were randomized to NSE at a physiotherapy clinic or internet-based NSE with four physiotherapy visits (NSEIT). Assessor-blinded investigators obtained measurements at baseline and at 3- and 15-month follow-up. Orthogonal partial least square (OPLS) and OPLS discriminant statistical analyses (OPLS-DA) were used.

RESULTS: There were no significant differences between the exercise programmes. Improvement in psychosocial measures, pain, disability and several objective measures were associated with improvements in HRQoL in OPLS models (R2 = 0.20 to 0.27, Q2 = 0.06 to 0.12, p < 0.05 to < 0.001). Higher baseline score on adverse psychosocial measures and disability, together with lower dizziness, self-efficacy, and neck-muscle endurance in extension, were associated with clinically relevant improvement in EQ-5D-3L at 15-month follow-up (R2 = 0.26, Q2 = 0.13, p < 0.01). The other models were non-significant.

CONCLUSIONS: Several factors, including adverse psychosocial measures, may be clinically relevant for HRQoL after neck-specific exercise interventions. Given the models' weak predictive ability, the findings should be regarded as exploratory and hypothesis-generating.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: The study was registered before data collection started, ClinicalTrials.gov Protocol ID: NCT03022812, initial release 12/20/2016. The study was approved by the regional ethical review board in Linköping, Sweden (Dnr 2016/135-31; 2016/526-32; 2017/45-32).

articles.title: Efonidipine inhibiting CYP4A attenuates palmitate-induced hepatocyte lipotoxicity.
articles.abstract: Efonidipine, a dual L-/T-type calcium channel blocker (CCB), is a clinically established antihypertensive agent with cardiovascular and renoprotective effects. However, whether efonidipine affects CYP4A, a previously established mediator of hepatic lipotoxicity, remains unknown. In the present study, palmitate (PA)-induced steatotic HepG2 and SNU-449 hepatocytes were used to evaluate the hepatoprotective effects of efonidipine and its underlying mechanism. Efonidipine inhibited CYP4A enzyme activity, revealing a previously unrecognized CYP4A inhibitor. It also reduced CYP4A protein expression in PA-treated hepatocytes. This was accompanied by reduced intracellular lipid accumulation and lipogenesis, suppressed oxidative and ER stress, and improved insulin signaling and glucose uptake. These effects were consistently observed in both hepatocyte cell lines. Taken together, these findings suggest that efonidipine may represent a potential repurposing strategy for hepatic lipotoxicity through CYP4A inhibition.

articles.title: Comparative transcriptomics identifies conserved gene signatures defining megakaryocyte development states across species.
articles.abstract: Megakaryocytes and platelets are essential for hemostasis, immune regulation and hematopoietic niche maintenance, while also promoting thrombosis. Comprehensive characterization of late-stage megakaryocyte maturation in mammals using single-cell RNA-sequencing (scRNA-Seq) remains challenging due to the large size of megakaryocytes and the low RNA content of platelets. Although zebrafish thrombocytes are functionally analogous and retain high transcriptional activity at maturity, their transcriptional similarities to mammals have not been systematically defined. To address this, we generated a single-cell transcriptomic atlas spanning the full developmental trajectory of zebrafish thrombocytes, demonstrating that lineage progression is continuous and functionally coordinated. Cross-species comparison with human and mouse datasets defined conserved differentiation stages and gene modules of the megakaryocyte-platelet lineage, indicating evolutionary conservation of lineage development at single-cell resolution. Moreover, we identified a gene set (M3pan-PLT) that marks a platelet-like transcriptional state in zebrafish thrombocytes, supporting their transcriptomic analogy to mammalian platelets. Finally, bulk transcriptomic analyses using these conserved gene signatures demonstrated their ability to capture physiological megakaryocyte states, as well as disease-associated transcriptional alterations in acute megakaryoblastic leukemia. Together, our study defines a conserved and continuous developmental framework of megakaryocytes at single-cell resolution and establishes zebrafish thrombocytes as a transcriptionally conserved model for dissecting late-stage megakaryocyte-platelet biology.

articles.title: Impact of symmetrical and asymmetrical foot pronation and arch deformities on three-dimensional pelvic kinematics during standing and walking: A systematic review and Meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Foot pronation and structural arch deformities may influence pelvic motion, but effects vary across conditions and tasks. This review examined whether three-dimensional pelvic responses differ by foot-condition symmetry and between standing and dynamic weight-bearing.

METHODS: Following PRISMA 2020, observational and non-randomized experimental studies of habitual foot arch dysfunction or experimentally induced calcaneal eversion/inversion were reviewed. Primary outcomes were sagittal pelvic tilt, frontal pelvic tilt or drop, and transverse pelvic rotation. Comparable standing pelvic angles were analyzed using exploratory random-effects mean differences (MDs, degrees); repeated-measures contrasts used reported paired-change statistics. Other outcomes were summarized narratively. Risk of bias was assessed with JBI tools and certainty with GRADE.

FINDINGS: Sixteen publications representing 15 independent study samples were included. Two bilateral 10° wedge studies showed increases in anterior pelvic tilt, but exploratory pooling was imprecise (MD 0.97°, 95% CI [-0.05, 1.99]; I2 = 81.8%). Habitual bilateral flatfoot was not pooled because compatible summary data were unavailable. Three studies reported positive lateral pelvic tilt differences for unilateral foot conditions; their exploratory pooled estimate was highly heterogeneous (MD 2.18°, 95% CI [-0.36, 4.71]; I2 = 96.5%). High-arched/inversion and dynamic transverse-plane outcomes were summarized narratively. Certainty was very low for pooled outcomes.

INTERPRETATION: Foot-condition type and assessment task appear relevant to pelvic alignment, but the small evidence base and substantial heterogeneity limit pooled conclusions. These results are preliminary biomechanical observations rather than evidence of causation or treatment effectiveness. PROSPERO registration number: CRD420261329855.

articles.title: Letter to the editor: endovascular therapy for mild-to-moderate stroke due to basilar artery occlusion: interpreting the certainty of excellent functional recovery.
SGLT1/2 inhibitor sotagliflozin, but not SGLT2-selective inhibitor empagliflozin, attenuates platelet activation and thrombosis.
articles.abstract: As rates of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) have risen, comorbidities of T2DM and cardiovascular disease (CVD) have similarly increased. The adoption of sodium-glucose cotransporter (SGLT) 2 inhibitors as a treatment for T2DM has provided an effective means of decreasing renal glucose reabsorption. In recent clinical trials, sotagliflozin, the first FDA-approved inhibitor of both isoforms of SGLT (SGLT1 and SGLT2), demonstrated a reduction in myocardial infarction and stroke in patients with T2DM at high cardiovascular risk. The cardiovascular protective effect of sotagliflozin compared to the SGLT2-selective inhibitor, empagliflozin, was investigated by evaluating effects on platelet activation and thrombus formation. Employing ex vivo models using blood from healthy donors or T2DM patients, and in vivo mouse models, we demonstrate an inhibitory effect on platelet activity and thrombus formation with sotagliflozin, while empagliflozin has minor to no effects. Further, no impact on hemostasis was observed with sotagliflozin. Finally, a platelet-specific deletion of SGLT1 via Slc5a1fl/fl Gp1ba-Cre⁺ mice resulted in reduced platelet integrin activation and thrombus formation. This study provides insight into a potential explanation for the cardiovascular protection conferred by sotagliflozin observed in patients with T2DM at risk of an ischemic event and reveals an added benefit to SGLT2-selective inhibitors.

articles.title: Phenotype-based risk stratification for deep vein thrombosis in Behçet's disease: a global 10-year longitudinal study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Vascular involvement, particularly deep vein thrombosis (DVT), is a major cause of morbidity and mortality in Behçet's disease (BD). This study aimed to identify independent risk factors for DVT and establish a robust framework for phenotype-based risk stratification.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the TriNetX global health research network and identified 19,739 patients with BD. Three independent propensity score-matched cohorts were established to evaluate the impact of intestinal involvement, thrombophlebitis, and antiphospholipid syndrome (APS). A multivariable Cox proportional hazards model was used to identify independent predictors of DVT over a 10-year follow-up. To ensure the robustness of our findings and minimise peri-diagnostic detection bias, a 90-day landmark analysis was performed as a sensitivity analysis.

RESULTS: Multivariable analysis identified APS (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR] 6.28, 95% confidence interval [CI] 4.56-8.64) and a history of thrombophlebitis (aHR 5.92, 95% CI 4.72-7.41) as the strongest independent predictors of DVT. In the 90-day landmark analysis, these associations remained significant, with persistent risk observed for APS (aHR 5.10) and thrombophlebitis (aHR 2.50), confirming their long-term predictive value. Additional independent predictors included intestinal involvement (defined as non-infective inflammatory colitis; aHR 1.51), obesity (aHR 1.98), glucocorticoid use (aHR 1.78), and male sex (aHR 1.77).

CONCLUSIONS: APS and thrombophlebitis, markers of heightened inflammatory and thrombotic activity at diagnosis, also appear to be persistent indicators of elevated DVT risk in BD. These findings support phenotype-based risk stratification and highlight the need for intensive monitoring and individualised preventive strategies to improve long-term outcomes.

articles.title: Modeling patient variants of Cnot1 and Cdc42bpb results in distinct forms of congenital diaphragmatic hernia in mice.
articles.abstract: Congenital diaphragmatic hernia (CDH) is a severe congenital anomaly characterized by impairment of both diaphragm and lung development in utero. CDH presents as a spectrum of forms and severities, with diaphragm defects arising in the dorsal/posterior region typically correlating with more severe pulmonary disease and higher risk of mortality than those appearing in ventral/anterior regions. The genetic etiology underlying CDH is complex, with many implicated genes showing variable expressivity and incomplete penetrance in both human patients and mouse models. Here we present in vivo validation of two genes previously unassociated with CDH: the CDC42-interacting kinase CDC42BPB; and CNOT1, a scaffolding protein of the CCR4-NOT protein complex, critical for mRNA regulation through modifications such as deadenylation. Each gene was found to have a damaging, de novo missense variant in a recent large-scale CDH patient sequencing screen. Loss of Cdc42bpb leads to ventral diaphragmatic hernias, heart septal defects, and minor lung epithelial differentiation defects in mouse embryos. Installation of the orthologous patient-specific missense variant through CRISPR/Cas9 editing leads to less severe ventral diaphragm defects. Mouse embryos with either one or two copies of the orthologous Cnot1 variant, c.1867C > T (p.R623W), develop dorsal diaphragmatic hernias with low (<50%) penetrance, and mutants showed alterations in mRNA isoform expression consistent with the molecular role of Cnot1 in RNA splicing. These results underscore the power of in vivo functional modeling to validate genes and patient-specific variants uncovered by patient sequencing, reveal two previously unrecognized genetic causes of CDH, and highlight the heterogeneity of different patient anatomic presentations.

articles.title: Bayesian Predictive Inference for Future Order Statistics from the Two-Parameter Lomax Distribution under Type-II Censoring.
articles.abstract: This study develops Bayesian predictive procedures for future order statistics from the two-parameter Lomax distribution under Type-II censored sampling schemes. The proposed framework combines predictive likelihood inference with Bayesian prediction based on independent gamma priors and Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) simulation using the Metropolis-Hastings algorithm. Bayesian point predictors are derived under the squared error, LINEX, and general entropy loss functions, and predictive intervals are constructed from posterior predictive samples. A detailed Monte Carlo simulation study compares the proposed methods with the classical predictive maximum-likelihood approach across varying sample sizes and censoring levels. For the small-sample scenario (n = 20, r = 14), the Bayesian-LINEX predictor reduced the mean squared prediction error (MSPE) from 0.1542-0.1182, decreased the average predictive interval width (APIW) from 2.4512-2.1985, and increased the coverage probability (CP) from 0.938-0.952 compared with the predictive maximum likelihood method. Overall, the Bayesian methods consistently outperformed the classical approach across all simulation settings, with the Bayesian-LINEX predictor achieving the best predictive performance. These findings demonstrate that the proposed Bayesian framework provides a more accurate and consistent approach for predicting future order statistics from the Lomax distribution while accounting for parameter uncertainty.

articles.title: Impact of a Dynamic Visualized Pain Assessment Tool on Pediatric Pain Management: A Stepped-Wedge Cluster Randomized Trial.
articles.abstract: Effective pediatric pain management relies on accurate assessment; however, current behavioral scales are limited by observer subjectivity and fail to capture dynamic fluctuations. The primary goal of this protocol is to detail the implementation and evaluation of a dynamic visualized pain assessment tool, providing a standardized methodology to transition nursing practice from experience-based estimation to data-driven precision. Using a stepped-wedge cluster randomized trial design across five clinical wards, the study enrolled 15 infants and analyzed 45 video segments across three clinical contexts: baseline, acute procedural pain, and postoperative recovery. The system captured high-definition facial video synchronized with bedside physiological monitoring to generate real-time pain trajectory curves and trend-based alerts. Generalized linear mixed models showed that the tool reduced nursing response latency from 15.4 to 6.7 min (P < 0.001) and increased assessment consistency (intraclass correlation coefficient [ICC]: 0.71-0.93). Concurrently, pediatric satisfaction scores rose, and parental anxiety levels decreased. These findings suggest that dynamic visualization may improve clinical efficiency and patient outcomes through timely, objective decision support.

articles.title: Early Discharge Strategy Including Subcutaneous Furosemide in Hospitalized Heart Failure.
articles.journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients hospitalized for heart failure often require prolonged intravenous diuretic therapy, contributing to costs and risks associated with inpatient care.

OBJECTIVES: We evaluated whether an early discharge strategy using subcutaneous furosemide delivered via a wearable minipump could increase days alive and out of hospital (DAOH).

METHODS: In this multicenter, open-label, randomized, active-controlled trial in the United Kingdom, 172 patients hospitalized for heart failure requiring ongoing parenteral diuretics were randomly assigned to an early discharge strategy or usual care. Patients in the early discharge group received pH-neutral subcutaneous furosemide via a wearable, patient-operated minipump; postdischarge care included a review every 3 days while receiving subcutaneous furosemide. Both groups had a 2-week clinic review. The primary outcome was DAOH at 30 days after randomization.

RESULTS: A total of 92 patients were assigned to early discharge and 80 to usual care. The early discharge strategy resulted in 4.0 more DAOH at 30 days (95% CI: 2.1-5.8 days; P < 0.001). Index hospitalization was shorter by a mean of 5.5 days (95% CI: 7.4-3.6 days; P < 0.001). The benefit in DAOH was sustained at 60 days (difference 4.2 days; 95% CI: 0.9-7.6 days), despite more heart failure readmissions in the early discharge group (13 [14%] patients vs 5 [6%] patients; OR: 2.45; 95% CI: 0.81-7.43). Serious adverse events occurred in 25% and 23% of patients, respectively. Device-related problems occurred with 3% of minipump placements, but none were serious.

CONCLUSIONS: An early discharge strategy using a subcutaneous furosemide minipump increased DAOH compared with usual care. (Use of a Novel SUBCUTaneous Preparation of Furosemide to Facilitate Early Supported Discharge of Patients With Heart Failure [SUBCUT-HF II]; NCT05419115).

articles.title: Epidemiological Characteristics of Venous Thromboembolism and Associated Indicators for Catheter-Related Thrombosis Subtypes.
articles.abstract: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) is a severe and life-threatening complication in hospitalized patients, and central venous catheter (CVC) insertion significantly increases the risk of catheter-related thrombosis (CRT). Epidemiological profiles of hospitalized patients with confirmed VTE are characterized; indicators correlated with CRT subtype are identified; the discriminative performance of circulating biomarkers is evaluated; and VTE recurrence metrics are contrasted between cohorts with and without CVC placement. A single-center retrospective case-case comparative analysis is conducted on 862 patients with imaging-confirmed VTE. Analytical methodologies incorporate univariate and multivariate logistic regression, Kaplan-Meier survival analysis, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve testing. The in-hospital VTE incidence was 2.1%, concentrated in elderly, malignancy, and postoperative patients. CRT incidence was 10.2%, highest with peripherally inserted central catheter (PICC). Five clinical indicators correlated with CRT subtype were identified: prolonged catheter indwelling, catheter malposition, elevated D-dimer levels, malignant tumor history, and prior VTE events. The combination of D-dimer and catheter indwelling time exhibited robust discriminative power (AUC = 0.82) for differentiating CRT from non-CRT VTE among patients with confirmed VTE. The 6-month VTE recurrence rate was 28.4% in the CVC group and 9.7% in the non-CVC group. These observational findings yield only tentative clinical hypotheses aimed at distinguishing thrombotic subtypes among VTE patients. Further multicenter prospective research is necessary to validate these indicators and develop mature, standardized prevention protocols for broad clinical application.

articles.title: Effects of 30- and 90-Minute Afternoon Nap Opportunities on Field-Test Performance in Female Collegiate Basketball Players.
articles.abstract: Afternoon napping is used as a recovery strategy in sport, but a scheduled nap opportunity is not equivalent to objectively verified sleep. This study compared no-nap seated wakefulness (N0), a 30-minute scheduled nap opportunity (N30), and a 90-minute scheduled nap opportunity (N90) in 18 female collegiate basketball players using a randomized, fully counterbalanced, three-period within-participant crossover design. Conditions were separated by at least 72 h and ended at 14:30, followed by a common 60 min wakefulness buffer, a standardized 15 min warm-up, and a fixed basketball field-test battery. Linear mixed-effects models included condition, period, and sequence as fixed effects, with participant as a random intercept; the nine omnibus condition tests were controlled for using the Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate procedure. Four of nine outcomes remained significant after false-discovery-rate correction: the modified-505 first 10 m split, combined modified-505 completion time, three-quarter-court sprint time, and 30-15 Intermittent Fitness Test final velocity. N90 differed from both N0 and N30 for these outcomes, whereas N30 did not differ from N0. The other five outcomes did not meet the false-discovery-rate threshold. Sensitivity analyses, including reanalysis of the pre-correction modified-505 data, preserved the same four-outcome pattern. Because sleep onset and duration were not objectively measured, the findings estimate the effects of assigned recovery-opportunity conditions rather than a physiological sleep-duration dose-response.

articles.title: Machine Learning, Radiomics, and Clinical Models Predicting Checkpoint Inhibitor Pneumonitis in Lung Cancer: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: Checkpoint inhibitor pneumonitis (CIP) is a potentially fatal immune-related adverse event of immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) therapy in lung cancer, and many machine-learning (ML), computed tomography (CT) radiomics, deep-learning, and clinical models have been proposed to predict it. This systematic review searched PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, CINAHL, and SinoMed, supplemented by citation searching and other sources, with independent dual-reviewer screening throughout and a reproducible PubMed verification search updated to August 16, 2026. Twelve peer-reviewed lung-cancer CIP-occurrence models (4,875 patients, 1,057 events) formed the main analysis; validation C-statistics were pooled on the logit scale with restricted maximum likelihood and Hartung-Knapp intervals, stratified by validation design. The pooled validation C-statistic was 0.82 (95% confidence interval 0.75-0.88) with high heterogeneity (I2 = 90.7%) and a wide 95% prediction interval of 0.51-0.95, which is the decision-relevant quantity. By validation design, internal cross-validation pooled to 0.83, internal split-sample to 0.76, and only two studies reported external validation (0.84 and 0.92, described narratively). Imaging-based models (k = 8) showed numerically higher discrimination than clinical models (k = 4; 0.85 versus 0.78, moderator p = 0.46) without a statistically significant difference, and this comparison is confounded by design covariates. Estimates were stable on leave-one-out, alternative-model, cohort-overlap, and standard-error-source sensitivity analyses (range 0.80-0.84). Under the standard Prediction model Risk Of Bias ASsessment Tool, applied independently by two reviewers with consensus resolution, two studies were at high, nine at unclear, and one at low overall risk of bias; certainty of evidence was low (very low under a stricter appraisal scenario, which left the pooled estimate essentially unchanged). Current models separate risk groups on average but remain unready for clinical use; adequately powered, externally validated, and calibration-reported models are needed.

articles.title: Premenstrual Syndrome and Premenstrual Dysphoric Disorder: A Systematic Review of Academic Performance and Well-Being in University Students.
articles.abstract: Premenstrual syndrome (PMS) and premenstrual dysphoric disorder (PMDD) are common among women of reproductive age and are associated with academic performance and general well-being at the university level. This review aimed to synthesize evidence on the prevalence of PMS and PMDD and their associations with academic, psychological, and well-being outcomes among female medical and health sciences students. Searches were conducted using PubMed, MEDLINE via Ovid, Web of Science, Wiley Online Library, and EBSCOhost, through which Academic Search Complete, MEDLINE, and PsycINFO were searched for studies published between January 2014 and December 2024. Of 317 identified records, 11 studies met the inclusion criteria; all were observational and cross-sectional. Prevalence estimates varied widely, with PMS ranging from 37.0% to 86.2% and probable PMDD from 13.8% to 66.9%. All PMDD estimates were based on questionnaire screening rather than prospective diagnostic confirmation and therefore represent screening-positive cases rather than confirmed diagnoses. Premenstrual symptoms were associated with impaired concentration, absenteeism, reduced class participation, lower perceived academic performance, and poorer psychological well-being. Associated factors included severe dysmenorrhea, family history, academic stress, irregular or shorter menstrual cycles, and low physical activity. The cross-sectional designs, heterogeneous diagnostic criteria, and varying outcome measures limit causal inference and generalizability. PMS and probable PMDD are associated with poorer academic performance and well-being among female medical and health sciences students. Universities should consider proportionate supportive responses, including menstrual health education, access to health services and counseling, and appropriate academic or social support. Future research should employ standardized diagnostic and outcome measures and prospective study designs.

articles.title: PTCD and Peroral Electronic Cholangioscopy with Holmium Laser Lithotripsy for CBD Stones in a Super-Elderly Patient Post-Billroth II Gastrojejunostomy.
articles.abstract: The management of impacted common bile duct stones in patients with prior Billroth II gastrectomy poses unique challenges. Altered gastrointestinal anatomy renders duodenoscope passage and biliary cannulation during conventional ERCP exceedingly difficult, resulting in a low success rate. Super‑elderly (over 90 years old) patients often have multiple comorbidities such as cardiovascular diseases and require rapid relief of biliary obstruction and infection control to create a subsequent therapeutic window. Meanwhile, traditional open biliary surgery and general anesthesia carry prohibitive risk, along with prolonged preoperative preparation and extensive trauma. Although percutaneous transhepatic choledochoscopic lithotripsy (PTCSL) is unaffected by gastrointestinal reconstruction, it often depends on a large mature biliary sinus tract, necessitating a multi‑stage procedure, entails a risk of hemorrhage, and has difficulty in managing stones, especially papillary impacted stones. To overcome these difficulties, an innovative stepwise strategy was devised comprising "urgent PTCD for rapid decompression followed by multimodal lithotripsy under direct visualization with a peroral electronic cholangioscope." A 92‑year‑old male had a history of multiple surgeries, including Billroth II gastrectomy, cholecystectomy, and colon resection, along with coronary heart disease and atrial fibrillation. Emergency PTCD was performed first, promptly controlling infection and relieving jaundice. After preoperative preparation, the tract was dilated to 10 Fr, and a peroral electronic cholangioscope was introduced through the sheath. Under direct visualization, the common bile duct stones were efficiently fragmented using a holmium laser, initially in a fragmentation mode and then in a dusting mode. Post‑procedural cholangiography confirmed complete stone clearance. The PTCD tube was subsequently removed uneventfully, and the patient recovered well without complications. This strategy successfully circumvents the anatomical alterations, integrates biliary drainage, direct intra‑ductal visualization, and lithotripsy, providing a minimally invasive treatment strategy for patients with bile duct stones after gastrointestinal reconstruction, especially for super‑elderly and other high‑risk individuals.

articles.title: Gliflozin-Derived SGLT2 Inhibitors: Recent Advances and Future Perspectives in the Management of Type 2 Diabetes.
articles.abstract: Gliflozin derivatives, a class of Sodium-Glucose Cotransporter (SGLT) inhibitors, have emerged as effective antidiabetic agents offering notable cardiovascular and renal protection. This class of compounds inhibits glucose reabsorption in the kidneys, thereby improving overall glycaemic control. This review provides a comprehensive overview of gliflozin derivatives, emphasizing their chemical characterization, safety, therapeutic efficacy, pharmacokinetic analysis, and potential future applications, focusing on clinical trials and new developments released between 2010 and 2026. Gliflozin derivatives slow the progression of chronic kidney disease and reduce the risk of heart failure. Some preliminary experimental evidence has reported the antibacterial activity of canagliflozin against MRSA. The Gliflozin derivatives dapagliflozin (IC50 =1.1nM), ertugliflozin (IC50 =0.9nM), sotagliflozin (IC50 =1.8nM), and bexagliflozin (IC50 =2.3nM), which has core motif, 1-chloro-2-(4-alkoxy benzyl) benzene as an aglycon unit and a glycon unit bind with SGLT2 receptor and lowered the HbA1c by 1.2%, 1.7%, 0.41% and 0.80%, respectively. Its selectivity, pharmacokinetics, and toxicity profiles are also optimal. Recent studies have demonstrated their involvement in conditions other than diabetes, including obesity, non-alcoholic fatty liver disease, Cardioprotective, Nephroprotective, Anti-inflammatory, and antihypertensive effects. Gliflozin derivatives represent a paradigm shift in the management of diabetes and have broad therapeutic potential. Future studies should emphasize creative structural changes to increase safety and efficacy.

articles.title: Synthesis of ultra-large Ti3C2T x MXene nanoflakes: enabling high-performance flexible transparent conductive coatings.
articles.abstract: Flexible transparent conductive electrodes (FTCEs) are critical components in next-generation wearable electronics and display technologies. However, achieving low sheet resistance without compromising optical transparency remains a significant challenge due to percolation limitations in thin conductive films. MXenes, a rapidly expanding class of two-dimensional (2D) transition metal carbides and nitrides, offer remarkable potential as transparent conducting electrodes (TCEs) owing to their exceptional electrical conductivity, mechanical flexibility, and intrinsically hydrophilic nature. In this work, a modified orbital shaker-assisted Minimally Intensive Layer Delamination (Orbital-MILD) etching method is introduced, yielding ultra-large Ti3C2T x MXene nanoflakes with an average lateral size of ∼30 µm (optical-microscopy statistics over 168 individual flakes) and individual flakes reaching up to 48 µm - among the largest reported to date for solution-processed MXenes. The gentle orbital mixing action prevents flake fragmentation during both the etching and delamination stages, preserving the large lateral dimensions of the parent MAX phase particles.
