Of the analysed variables, prior ear surgery (adjusted (a)OR 1.43, p = 0.005), age younger than 8 years (aOR 1.73, p = 0.015), a postoperative infection within 6 weeks after surgery (aOR 1.92, p < 0.001) and the surgical aim of achieving a dry/infection free ear (aOR 1.53, p = 0.045) were predictors for unsuccessful healing. For simultaneous ossiculoplasty at surgery, there was a significantly higher chance of having a healed tympanic membrane (aOR 1.49, p = 0.016). For other variables such as gender, operated side, season, graft material, perioperative antibiotics and infection free status at surgery, there was no significant effect on tympanic membrane healing.

CONCLUSION: The present evaluation of the surgical results in SwedEar constitutes one of the largest studies on myringoplasty outcome. The results showed that the age of the patient, surgical aim, prior ear surgery and postoperative infection constituted risk factors for unsuccessful healing after myringoplasty. Surprisingly, ears requiring a concomitant ossiculoplasty had a higher healing rate.

articles.title: Oral Fluid Inflammatory Biomarker Profile in Long COVID: Evaluation of Oral Active and Total MMP-8, MMP-9, and TIMP-1 in Relation to BMI and Disease Status.
articles.journal: International journal of infectious diseases : IJID : official publication of the International Society for Infectious Diseases
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Long COVID (LC) is characterized by persistent systemic symptoms, but its oral inflammatory profile remains unclear. This study evaluated oral inflammatory biomarkers, particularly matrix metalloproteinase (MMP) -8, -9 and their regulators in oral rinse samples from LC patients.

METHODS: This cross-sectional study analyzed oral rinse samples from 115 LC patients and 103 comparable controls. Periodontal inflammation was screened using a chair-side active MMP-8 (aMMP-8) point-of-care test (POCT). Biomarkers (aMMP-8, total MMP-8, MMP-9, TIMP-1, and MPO) were quantified and validated by Western blotting and gelatin zymography. Associations with LC and clinical variables were assessed using bivariate analysis and multivariable regression.

RESULTS: LC patients had significantly higher total MMP-8, MMP-9, TIMP-1, and MMP-9/TIMP-1 ratio (all p<0.05 in both analyses). IFMA-measured active MMP-8 became independently associated with LC after multivariable adjustment. Chair-side aMMP-8 POCT showed a non-significant trend toward higher positivity in LC (16.5% vs. 8.7%). BMI was positively associated with aMMP-8, tMMP-8 and tMMP-8/TIMP-1 molar ratio. Antidepressant use was associated with tMMP-8/TIMP-1 molar ratio. Western blotting confirmed active MMP-8 species and gingipain.

CONCLUSION: These findings suggest an altered oral inflammatory biomarker profile in LC. The potential role of chair-side aMMP-8 POCT for screening oral inflammation in this population merits further investigation.

articles.title: Prevalence and Factors Associated with Cognitive Impairment Among Sepsis Survivors: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.journal: International journal of infectious diseases : IJID : official publication of the International Society for Infectious Diseases
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sepsis survivors frequently experience cognitive impairment, which negatively affects long-term quality of life and functional recovery. However, the prevalence and associated factors remain insufficiently characterized.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to evaluate the prevalence of cognitive impairment among sepsis survivors across different follow-up periods and identify associated factors using systematic review and meta-analysis.

METHODS: PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, CNKI, SinoMed, Wanfang Data, and VIP Database were searched from inception to March 19, 2026. Cohort and cross-sectional studies were included. Random-effects models were used to estimate pooled prevalence and odds ratios, and the certainty of evidence was evaluated using the GRADE approach.

RESULTS: Eighteen studies involving 218,152 sepsis survivors were included. Cognitive impairment remains common among sepsis survivors, with prevalence estimates varying across follow-up time points. Older age, prolonged delirium duration, hyperglycemia, and hypoxemia were positively associated with cognitive impairment (ORs ranging from 1.12 to 2.84). The certainty of evidence ranged from very low to low.

CONCLUSIONS: The pooled prevalence of cognitive impairment among sepsis survivors differed across follow-up time points. However, because estimates at different time points were largely based on different studies and populations, these findings should be interpreted as study-level time-stratified differences rather than evidence of within-individual cognitive recovery or decline. Older age, prolonged delirium duration, hyperglycemia, and hypoxemia were associated with cognitive impairment among sepsis survivors. Given the low to very low certainty of the available evidence, the observed associations should be interpreted cautiously. Further well-designed prospective studies are needed to confirm these findings.

articles.title: treatable trait in COPD: is LVDD the potential next?
Diffusion MRI Assessment of White Matter Microstructure and Free-Water Fraction in Drug-Naïve Children with SeLECTS.
articles.abstract: Self-limited epilepsy with centrotemporal spikes (SeLECTS) is a common childhood-onset focal epilepsy syndrome. Although seizures are typically self-limited, some children may show neurodevelopmental or cognitive vulnerability. Diffusion MRI may provide insight into white matter alterations in SeLECTS. Objective To evaluate white matter diffusion differences in newly diagnosed, drug-naïve children with SeLECTS using tract-based spatial statistics (TBSS) and white matter free-water fraction (FW-WM), and to explore within-patient associations with selected seizure-related and cognitive variables. Methods Fifty-three newly diagnosed, drug-naïve children with SeLECTS and 53 healthy controls with a similar age and sex distribution were prospectively enrolled in this cross-sectional case-control study. Diffusion MRI was acquired at 3.0T, and white matter diffusion differences were assessed using TBSS and FW-WM analyses. Voxelwise between-group differences in fractional anisotropy (FA) were tested with age and sex as covariates and corrected using threshold-free cluster enhancement-based family-wise error correction. FW-WM was compared between groups using age- and sex-adjusted general linear models, with additional adjustment for years of education in a sensitivity analysis. Exploratory within-patient associations between imaging measures and selected clinical or cognitive variables were assessed using partial Spearman correlations with false-discovery-rate correction. Results Children with SeLECTS showed lower FA than healthy controls in multiple TBSS-defined white matter regions after correction for multiple comparisons, mainly involving commissural, projection, and association pathways. No between-group differences in mean, axial, or radial diffusivity survived correction for multiple comparisons. FW-WM was higher in the SeLECTS group after adjustment for age and sex (adjusted mean difference = 0.0085; 95% CI, 0.0023 to 0.0147; P = 0.008), with similar results after additional adjustment for education. In exploratory cluster-level analyses, mean FA in a left-sided cluster involving the posterior internal capsule, posterior thalamic radiation, and sagittal stratum was inversely associated with disease duration after FDR correction (r = -0.413; P = 0.003; q = 0.010). No imaging-cognition or within-patient FW-WM-FA association survived FDR correction. Conclusions Newly diagnosed, drug-naïve children with SeLECTS showed white matter diffusion differences, including lower FA in distributed TBSS-defined regions and higher FW-WM. These findings support diffusion MRI-based characterization of white matter alterations at diagnosis, before antiseizure treatment. Longitudinal studies are needed to clarify their clinical and developmental relevance.

articles.title: Dupuytren's disease: From the first signs to the most advanced stages.
articles.abstract: Dupuytren's disease is a benign fibroproliferative condition of the palmar fascia, characterized by onset of nodules that develop into cords causing irreducible digital contracture. Prevalence increases with age. It mainly affects males of Northern European origin. Etiopathogenesis is multifactorial, combining genetic predisposition and environmental factors such as alcohol consumption, smoking, microtrauma and diabetes. Management is based on precise clinical assessment, with Tubiana classification and diathesis screening, to adapt therapeutic strategy. In the early stages, monitoring may be combined with medical treatment (radiotherapy, collagenase, corticosteroids, anti-TNF) aimed at slowing progression. In case of functional impairment or significant retraction, several surgical options are available: percutaneous fasciotomy, limited or segmental fasciectomy, dermofasciectomy with skin grafting, or even phalangectomy in severe recurrent cases. This narrative review provides an up-to-date summary of epidemiological, pathophysiological and therapeutic data, emphasizing the importance of a decision-tree that takes account of the progression, diathesis and severity of the contracture.

articles.title: Divergent bacterial signatures in dental clinic bioaerosols: a real-field investigation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Dental procedures generate bioaerosols containing oral microorganisms, posing a potential cross-infection risk. Effective infection control requires real-world data on aerosol behaviour in clinical settings.

OBJECTIVE: To characterize particulate matter and bacterial profiles during active ultrasonic periodontal scaling under routine clinical conditions.

METHODS: Sampling occurred under background and ultrasonic scaling conditions. Airborne particles were monitored in real-time using an optical particle sizer. Bioaerosols were collected using an Andersen six-stage sampler (culturable) and a filter-based high-flow pump (non-culturable). Surface samples were obtained from personal protective equipment (PPE) and environmental surfaces. Bacterial communities were analyzed via 16S rRNA sequencing.

FINDINGS: A notable decoupling was observed between physical and biological aerosol profiles: although ultrasonic instrumentation produced a substantial surge in sub-micron particles, culturable microbial recovery was predominantly concentrated within the respirable 1.1-3.3 μm fractions. High-throughput sequencing revealed clear spatial differentiation in bacterial communities. Microbial contamination was heavily confined to the clinician's PPE within the immediate splash zone. Airborne bacteria differed significantly from those on PPE (ANOSIM R = 0.633, p = 0.001), whereas clinical air and peripheral non-touch surfaces shared an indistinguishable ambient microbiome (R = 0.095, p = 0.249), with oral pathogens rarely detected in either compartment.

CONCLUSION: Under the specific conditions evaluated, total particle counts do not reflect culturable bacterial load, which is concentrated in the 1.1-3.3 μm respirable fraction. Bacterial contamination remains predominantly localized to the operative field and PPE, with minimal dispersion to ambient air. Accordingly, physical particle metrics should not be used as direct indicators of bacterial hazard, and clinician protection relies primarily on strict PPE compliance.

articles.title: Impact of Earthquake-Related Mass Casualty Burden on Hospital Microbial Ecology and Surgical Site Infections After Elective Orthopaedic Surgery: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: The aim of this study was to compare surgical site infections (SSIs) developing after primary elective orthopaedic procedures before and after the February 6, 2023 earthquakes and to investigate the incidence, causative pathogen distribution, and antimicrobial resistance patterns.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort study included patients undergoing primary total or partial hip arthroplasty, total knee arthroplasty, or open reduction and internal fixation. The Patients were divided into pre-earthquake (June 1, 2018-February 5, 2023) and post-earthquake (June 1, 2023-November 1, 2025) periods. The SSI cases were defined according to periprosthetic joint infection (ICM 2025) and fracture-related infection (FRI 2018) criteria. Microbiological profiles, resistance patterns, and clinical outcomes were compared between groups.

RESULTS: A total of 99 and 118 SSI cases were identified in the pre- and post-earthquake cohorts, respectively. Overall SSI rates were similar between groups (0.98% vs. 1.19%; p=0.143). However, post-earthquake infections were associated with significantly longer hospital stays (28 vs. 22 days; p=0.025) and increased debridement procedures (2.0 vs. 1.0; p=0.006). Polymicrobial infections increased significantly (12.1% vs. 23.7%; p=0.028). A marked microbiological shift was observed, with Gram-negative organisms becoming predominant (67.7% vs. 47.6%; p=0.004), while Gram-positive organisms decreased. Staphylococcus aureus isolation significantly declined (35.4% vs. 17.2%; p=0.008). Meticillin resistance among Gram-positive isolates increased (34.9% vs. 60.0%; p=0.022), whereas no significant change in Gram-negative carbapenem resistance was observed.

CONCLUSION: Our study results showed that the rates of polymicrobial infections and meticillin resistance among Gram-positive isolates increased significantly. This microbiological shift was also associated with clinically relevant outcomes, including prolonged hospital stay and an increased number of debridement procedures. Taken together, in centers exposed to a high burden of mass casualty patients, the infection dynamics of routine elective surgical cases may continue to evolve even months after the disaster. Reassessment of existing empirical treatment protocols is warranted in such settings.

articles.title: Am I receiving good care? A qualitative study exploring the moral experiences of MDRO carriers in Dutch hospitals and nursing homes.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Carriership of multi-drug resistant organisms (MDROs) and associated infection prevention and control (IPC) measures can negatively affect hospital patients and nursing home residents. Little is known about how carriers appraise these experiences in light of what matters to them - i.e. the moral dimension. This study explores the moral experiences of carriers receiving care in hospitals and nursing homes.

METHODS: We conducted a qualitative analysis of moral experiences present in semi-structured interviews with 20 MDRO carriers.

RESULTS: Carriers reported that some values were upheld, whereas others were undermined during care. We identified four themes. First, carriers felt responsible for protecting loved ones or the public by preventing transmission, yet perceived inconsistencies in IPC protocols generated doubt, frustration and feelings of injustice. Second, carriers described being visited less frequently or treated differently by healthcare providers (HCPs). Some felt guilty towards HCPs and other patients that their care required additional staff time. Third, carriers experienced burdens in receiving care like not seeing HCPs' faces, loss of freedom or feeling dirty, but also moments of compassion from empathic HCPs. Fourth, concerns about carriership extended beyond hospital care, with uncertainties about implications in daily life.

DISCUSSION: Identifying which values carriers perceive as upheld or undermined can guide more proportionate and equitable IPC policies and improve quality of care. HCPs should support carriers in navigating the many questions and uncertainties they face during care and in their daily lives. Future research should normatively evaluate IPC policies and explore how to address undermined values in care.

articles.title: Ferroptosis in endodontic pathobiology: Emerging evidence, mechanistic rationale, and translational uncertainties.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Ferroptosis is an iron-dependent form of regulated cell death characterized by lipid peroxidation and impaired antioxidant defense. Its defining biochemical features, including iron-redox imbalance and lipid peroxide accumulation, overlap with biological conditions present in infected, hypoxic, and cytokine-rich endodontic tissues. This narrative review examined the potential role of ferroptosis in endodontic pathobiology, with emphasis on separating direct endodontic evidence from indirect or extrapolated oral evidence.

METHODS: Electronic searches were performed in PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science using terms related to ferroptosis, endodontics, pulpitis, apical periodontitis, dental pulp, root canal infection, Enterococcus faecalis, periodontal ligament, ferritinophagy, iron metabolism, lipid peroxidation, and major ferroptosis-related regulators. Ferroptosis-associated papers were classified according to proximity to endodontic disease and strength of evidence.

RESULTS: Current evidence suggests that ferroptosis-associated pathways may participate in pulpitis and apical periodontitis. Direct evidence is strongest for active pulpitis and apical periodontitis, where ferroptosis-related changes have been reported in human tissues, animal models, and endodontic-relevant cell systems, including dental pulp fibroblasts, dental pulp cells, dental pulp stem cells, endothelial cells, and macrophages. Extrapolated evidence from periodontitis, periodontal ligament cells, oral bone models, and dental stem-cell studies provides biological context but does not establish causation in endodontic disease. Evidence for complete pulp necrosis, inflammatory root resorption, post-treatment healing, and regenerative endodontics is indirect, limited, or absent.

CONCLUSIONS: Ferroptosis-associated pathways represent a credible but still emerging area of endodontic pathobiology. Current evidence suggests a possible contributory role in pulpal and periapical inflammation, but causal relevance, disease-stage specificity, and clinical significance remain unresolved. Future studies should use polymicrobial or infected-dentin models, human tissue validation, standardized ferroptosis criteria, and longitudinal intervention designs before ferroptosis-related mechanisms can be translated into endodontic diagnosis, treatment, or regenerative strategies.

articles.title: Cellular toxicity and apoptosis-related responses to individual and combined exposure to microplastics and perfluorooctane sulfonic acid (PFOS) in Hediste diversicolor coelomocytes.
articles.abstract: Microplastics (MPs) are emerging contaminants of increasing concern in marine ecosystems due to their widespread occurrence and ability to adsorb and transport hazardous chemicals such as perfluorooctane sulfonic acid (PFOS). PFOS is a persistent per- and polyfluoroalkyl substance (PFAS) with high environmental stability, bioaccumulative potential, and well-documented toxicity to aquatic organisms. However, the combined effects of MPs and PFOS on marine invertebrates remain poorly understood. This study evaluated the individual and combined effects of environmentally relevant concentrations of MPs (50 mg kg-1 sediment) and PFOS (0.1, 0.5, and 1 μg kg-1 sediment) on the coelomic fluid of the benthic polychaete Hediste diversicolor after 7 days of sediment exposure. The MPs consisted of particles <30 μm composed of PVC, PET, PS, HDPE, LDPE, and PE with heterogeneous morphologies. PFOS accumulated in the coelomic fluid in a dose-dependent manner, with higher concentrations observed under co-exposure, suggesting that the presence of MPs may influence PFOS bioavailability and uptake. This increased accumulation was accompanied by pronounced cytotoxic and genotoxic effects, including lysosomal membrane destabilization, increased micronucleus frequency, and DNA fragmentation. Co-exposure also upregulated the pro-apoptotic genes p53, Bax, and Casp-3, while downregulating the anti-apoptotic gene Bcl-2, indicating activation of apoptotic pathways. Overall, the effects of combined exposure varied according to the endpoint and PFOS concentration, with co-exposure producing greater responses for some endpoints but not consistently across all treatments. These findings highlight the increased hazard posed by the co-occurrence of MPs and PFOS and emphasize the need to consider contaminant mixtures in marine environmental risk assessment.

articles.title: Transgenerational Effects of Paternal in Utero Arsenic Exposure on MASLD-like Phenotypes.
articles.abstract: Previous study indicated that early-life arsenic (As) exposure caused adulthood metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD)-like phenotypes. This study aimed to investigate the impacts of paternal in utero As exposure on MASLD-like phenotypes in offspring. Pregnant dams received NaAsO2 (15 mg/L) through drinking water. In utero As-exposed male pups were designated as F0 mice and mated with untreated females to produce F1 offspring. F1 males were subsequently mated with untreated females to generate F2 offspring, both without further As exposure. MASLD-like phenotypes were evaluated in F1 and F2 offspring. On PNW28, As-exposed F1 offspring exhibited hepatic steatosis, glucose intolerance, insulin resistance, and obesity, accompanied by altered metabolic hormones, such as GLP-1, GIP, insulin, and ADPN. The core MASLD-like phenotypes, including hepatic steatosis, glucose intolerance and insulin resistance, exhibited transgenerational transmission from F1 to F2 generations. In F2 offspring, these metabolic abnormalities were detected at PNW45 but not at PNW28, predominantly in male offspring. In contrast, As-induced obesity and metabolic hormone alterations exhibited transgenerational attenuation. F2 offspring retained only adipocyte hypertrophy, with no significant changes in white or brown adipose tissue weight. Furthermore, hormonal alterations in F2 mice were limited to reduced GLP-1 and elevated ADPN levels, while other altered hormones normalized. This study is the first to confirm that paternal in utero As exposure causes MASLD-like phenotypes in F1 offspring and transgenerational transmission to F2 generation.

articles.title: Early-life animal exposure was not associated with risk of inflammatory bowel disease: a nationwide birth cohort study.
articles.journal: Clinical gastroenterology and hepatology : the official clinical practice journal of the American Gastroenterological Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: The incidence of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) continues to rise globally. Early-life environmental exposures may influence immune development, but evidence regarding animal exposure remains inconsistent. We examined whether early-life exposure to pets or farm animals was associated with offspring risk of IBD in a prospective birth cohort.

METHODS: In this nationwide cohort study based on the Danish National Birth Cohort, prenatal offspring exposure to pets or farm animals, based on maternal reports, was used as the primary indicator of early-life animal exposure. Early-childhood exposure from birth to 18 months was examined in exposure-window analyses. Incident IBD, Crohn's disease (CD), and ulcerative colitis (UC) were identified through national registries. Associations were estimated using Cox proportional hazards models.

RESULTS: Among 90,306 offspring, 46% were prenatally exposed to pets and 7% to farm animals. During median follow-up of 24 years, 615 offspring developed IBD. Pet exposure was not associated with IBD risk (aHR 1.05, 95% CI 0.89-1.24), nor was farm animal exposure (aHR 1.00, 95% CI 0.73-1.37). Findings were consistent across specific animal categories and in analyses of CD and UC separately. In exposure-window analyses restricted to 63,958 offspring with maternal reports of both pre- and postnatal exposure, no associations were observed among offspring exposed only during pregnancy (aHR 1.10, 95% CI 0.75-1.63) or only during early childhood (aHR 0.73, 95% CI 0.46-1.15).

CONCLUSIONS: Early-life exposure to pets or farm animals was not associated with offspring risk of IBD. These findings suggest that early-life animal exposure may not be a major determinant of disease development.

articles.title: Fibromyalgia Subgroups Identified Using Model-Based Clustering: Results from UK Biobank.
articles.abstract: Fibromyalgia (FM) is a heterogeneous chronic condition with wide variability in symptom burden, psychosocial distress, and functional impact. This study aimed to identify latent FM subgroups reflecting multidimensional patient profiles using comprehensive biopsychosocial variables and model-based clustering methods within UK Biobank. Individuals meeting the 2016 American College of Rheumatology FM criteria (n = 4,172) were analysed using Gaussian mixture clustering. Twenty-eight variables across sociodemographic, clinical symptoms, and psychological/behavioural domains were included. Cluster stability was evaluated using bootstrap resampling and adjusted Rand indices (ARI). Variable importance was assessed using Random Forest analysis. Three distinct subgroups were identified: the Resilient Majority (62.3%) with low symptoms and psychological resilience; the Severe Phenotype (20.1%) with pronounced pain, fatigue, and psychological distress; and the Socially Vulnerable Minority (17.6%) characterized by ethnic diversity, rural residence, and social isolation. Sociodemographic and psychological/behavioural variables (e.g. frequency of feeling down, home area population density, ethnicity, frequency of home visits, and smoking status) demonstrated greater discriminative contribution than clinical symptom variables. All clusters demonstrated high stability (ARI > 0.93). These findings identify subgroups within FM defined not only by symptom severity but also by structural vulnerabilities and psychosocial factors. Recognizing such heterogeneity has implications for developing stratified, equitable management approaches that integrate psychosocial dimensions alongside clinical symptoms. PERSPECTIVE: Three fibromyalgia subgroups were identified: a resilient majority, a severe phenotype with socioeconomic disadvantage, and a socially vulnerable minority characterized by ethnic diversity and rural isolation patterns. Psychosocial factors outperformed clinical symptoms in discriminating subgroups, underscoring the need for stratified and patient-centred management addressing the biopsychosocial complexity of fibromyalgia.

articles.title: WSSV355 enhances IDH1 enzymatic activity and promotes efficient WSSV replication.
articles.abstract: White spot syndrome virus (WSSV) drives extensive metabolic reprogramming to support viral replication, including activation of reductive carboxylation, a pathway in which host isocitrate dehydrogenase 1 (IDH1) has a central role. However, the mechanisms by which viral factors regulate IDH1 and associated metabolic networks remain unclear. Here, we identified WSSV355 as a key viral regulator that contributed to IDH1 binding and activation during infection. Using yeast two-hybrid screening, WSSV355 was identified as an LvIDH1-interacting protein and further validated by co-immunoprecipitation and co-localization analyses. Functional assays demonstrated that WSSV355 enhanced IDH1 enzymatic activity, whereas truncation mapping revealed that distinct regions of WSSV355 contributed to IDH1 binding and activation. In vivo silencing of WSSV355 suppressed viral gene expression, and decreased viral genome copy number, establishing its role in promoting efficient WSSV replication. Affinity purification-mass spectrometry (AP-MS) further revealed that WSSV355 identified a set/network of WSSV355-associated proteins enriched in cytoskeletal, RNA-processing, and metabolic pathways. Integration with infection-responsive proteomic datasets identified candidate modules linking the WSSV355-associated protein network to host infection responses, suggesting broader potential involvement of WSSV355 in host cellular processes during infection. Collectively, these findings identify WSSV355 as an LvIDH1-interacting viral protein that enhances IDH1 enzymatic activity and is required for efficient WSSV replication. To our knowledge, WSSV355 is the first reported virus-encoded protein shown to enhance IDH1 enzymatic activity, providing new insights into how aquatic viruses exploit host metabolic machinery to promote infection.

articles.title: Schisandra chinensis in sepsis intervention through multi-target mechanisms and organ protection.
articles.abstract: Sepsis is a life-threatening syndrome characterized by overwhelming inflammation, oxidative stress, immune imbalance, endothelial dysfunction, and progressive multiple organ injury. Schisandra chinensis (S. chinensis) and its bioactive constituents possess anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, immunomodulatory, and organ-protective properties, but their sepsis-related evidence has not been comprehensively summarized. This narrative review critically summarizes the current evidence on S. chinensis and its bioactive constituents in sepsis, with emphasis on inflammatory regulation, immune homeostasis, oxidative stress, endothelial dysfunction, regulated cell death, and sepsis-associated organ injury. PubMed/MEDLINE, Web of Science, Scopus, Google Scholar, China National Knowledge Infrastructure, and Wanfang Data were searched without restriction on publication year, and the reference lists of relevant publications were also screened. Eligible studies were narratively synthesized according to intervention type, experimental model, biological effects, signaling pathways, and organ outcomes, with evidence from isolated or chemically characterized constituents distinguished from that derived from multicomponent preparations. Current evidence, derived predominantly from in vitro and LPS- or CLP-induced animal studies, indicates that S. chinensis constituents may attenuate inflammatory responses, oxidative stress, ferroptosis, endothelial barrier disruption, and sepsis-associated lung and myocardial injury through the TLR4/MyD88/NF-κB, JAK2/STAT3, NLRP3, Nrf2/GPX4, RhoA/ROCK1/MLC and MAPK pathways. However, clinical evidence remains limited and is mainly based on multicomponent traditional Chinese medicine preparations, preventing determination of the independent contribution of S. chinensis. Overall, S. chinensis is a promising but investigational adjunctive candidate for sepsis. Future studies should prioritize chemically standardized preparations, pharmacokinetic and safety characterization, causal validation of reproducible mechanisms, and biomarker-based identification of responsive sepsis phenotypes before early-phase and randomized clinical trials.

articles.title: Dietary Patterns and Chronic Disease Risk: A Proteomic Framework to Strengthen Causal Inference.
articles.abstract: The strength of evidence in nutrition research is hampered by the difficulty of maintaining long-term dietary compliance in randomized trials. Despite providing valuable evidence, short-term feeding trials typically rely on a limited set of surrogate outcomes, and observational studies are susceptible to measurement error and residual confounding. We propose a complementary research framework that integrates randomized feeding trials with Mendelian randomization (MR) using proteomic markers to strengthen causal inference in nutrition research. In this approach, feeding trials are used to identify proteins that respond to dietary patterns, and MR analyses are subsequently used to assess whether these diet-responsive proteins are relevant to the development of chronic diseases. In addition to instrumenting individual proteins, we propose using genetic scores to instrument proteomic signatures of dietary patterns in MR analyses. We argue that proteins are particularly informative biomarkers because they reflect multiple biological pathways involved in disease pathophysiology and can often be instrumented with cis-protein quantitative trait loci (pQTLs), which reduces concerns about horizontal pleiotropy compared with other MR approaches. To illustrate the feasibility of several steps in the proposed approach, we highlight studies of the Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension (DASH) diet. This research shows that randomized feeding trials can identify reproducible proteomic changes and that several of these associations can be confirmed in population-based cohort studies. We further note that selected diet-related proteins have been associated with the risk of type 2 diabetes in prospective studies and, in some cases, supported by MR and colocalization analyses. We also discuss potential limitations, including incomplete proteomic coverage, measurement error, epitope effects, and challenges in satisfying MR assumptions. In sum, we argue that a cross-design, proteomic-based research strategy can contribute to the triangulation of evidence in nutrition research, generating more specific and robust dietary recommendations for chronic disease prevention.

articles.title: Prognostic associations of left atrial strain with major adverse cardiovascular events and atrial fibrillation: Data from the Akershus cardiac examination (ACE) 1950 study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Left atrial (LA) reservoir (LASr), conduit (LAScd) and contractile (LASct) strain are known to reflect atrial remodeling and is prognostic in atrial fibrillation (AF) and heart failure. Evidence is scarce on prediction of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) in general populations. LA mechanical dispersion (LA MD) and stiffness index (LASI) are less studied strain-derived indices of AF and cardiovascular risk.

METHODS: The Akershus Cardiac Examination 1950 Study included 3706 participants from the general population who underwent baseline echocardiography in 2012-2015. MACE (cardiovascular death, non-fatal stroke, non-fatal myocardial infarction or coronary intervention) and incident AF were recorded through 2022. Prognostic value of LA strain was assessed by Cox regression.

RESULTS: In 3229 participants with baseline LA strain analysis, MACE was recorded in 242 (7.5%) and incident AF in 157 (5.0%) over a median 8.3 years (IQR 7.9-8.9) of follow-up. LASr, LAScd and LASI were associated with MACE in univariable analyses, and LASI remained independently associated with MACE after multivariable adjustment (HR per 1SD increment 1.12, 95% CI 1.04-1.21). LASr (HR per 1SD decrement 1.21, 95% CI 1.01-1.45), LASct (HR per 1SD decrement 1.26, 95% CI 1.04-1.52) and LA MD (HR per 1SD increment 1.23, 95% CI 1.03-1.48) were independently associated with incident AF after multivariable adjustment. Accounting for competing risk of all-cause death, LA MD remained independently associated with incident AF, whereas LASr and LASct did not.

CONCLUSION: In a general population, LASI was independently associated with MACE, whereas LASr, LASct and LA MD were associated with incident AF.

articles.title: In vivo antiviral efficacy and safety of 5-hydroxymethyltubercidin against DENV2 and SARS-CoV-2.
articles.abstract: Several newly emerging and re-emerging viral infections significantly affect human health and the global economy each year. As many of these viruses lack treatment options other than symptomatic management, the development of effective preventive and therapeutic measures is urgently needed. We previously identified 5-hydroxymethyltubercidin (HMTU) as a broad-spectrum antiviral ribonucleoside analog and demonstrated its in vitro potent antiviral activity against positive-sense single-stranded RNA viruses, including dengue virus (DENV) and severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2). In this study, we evaluated the in vivo efficacy, pharmacokinetics, and safety of HMTU. Pharmacokinetic analysis revealed that effective concentrations of HMTU were maintained in the plasma and lung tissues of mice following intravenous and intramuscular administration. In a DENV2 infection model using AG129 mice, prophylactic administration of HMTU provided 100% protection against lethal infection. Similarly, in a SARS-CoV-2 infection model using BALB/c mice, HMTU significantly reduced viral titers in the lungs and improved the survival rates versus those in vehicle-treated mice. Furthermore, mutagenicity assessments using the Ames and HPRT tests demonstrated that HMTU did not exhibit mutagenic activity under the tested conditions. Our findings highlight HMTU as a broad-spectrum antiviral candidate potentially offering a promising therapeutic approach for dengue, COVID-19, and other infectious diseases caused by emerging orthoflaviviruses and coronaviruses.

articles.title: Characterizing One-Year Mortality in Early Survivors of Open Thoracoabdominal Aortic Repair.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although operative mortality after open thoracoabdominal aortic aneurysm (TAAA) repair is well characterized, only limited data describe 1-year survival among patients who survive the index hospitalization. This study sought to further characterize 1-year mortality among operative survivors of open TAAA repair.

METHODS: From January 1986 through July 2025, 3838 open TAAA repairs were performed within our single practice. After operative deaths and patients lacking 1-year follow-up were excluded, 3378 early survivors comprised the study cohort. Demographic, operative, and postoperative data were compared between patients who survived ≥1 year after repair and those who did not. Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify independent predictors of 1-year mortality.

RESULTS: Among early survivors, 328 (9.7%) died within 1 year. One-year mortality was associated with older age, prior percutaneous coronary intervention, prior stroke, and chronic kidney disease. Postoperative complications-namely paraplegia (odds ratio [OR] 1.96, P=.03), dialysis dependence (OR 2.00, P=.001), arrhythmia (OR 1.48, P=.01), tracheostomy (OR 2.17, P<.001), and 1-year repair failure (OR 5.13, P<.001)-independently predicted death, whereas elective repair (OR 0.57, P<.001) and discharge home (OR 0.38, P<.001) predicted 1-year survival. Model discrimination was good (C-statistic=0.77 [0.74-0.81]). Kaplan-Meier analysis showed markedly greater 1-year survival in patients initially discharged home (94%) versus elsewhere (73%; P<.001).

CONCLUSIONS: Among operative survivors of open TAAA repair, 1-year mortality remains considerable and is primarily determined by persistent postoperative complications and repair durability rather than intraoperative variables. Vigilant surveillance, structured rehabilitation, and multidisciplinary follow-up may be needed to ensure success beyond the perioperative period.

articles.title: ED-71 ameliorates oxeiptosis-associated signaling in BMSCs under diabetic osteoporosis by alleviating PKM2-associated metabolic dysregulation and mitochondrial dysfunction.
articles.abstract: Diabetic osteoporosis (DOP) poses a significant clinical challenge, characterized by elevated fracture risk linked to bone quality deterioration. The pathogenesis involves reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation and metabolic dysfunction in bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs). This study investigates the role of oxeiptosis, a novel ROS-triggered, caspase-independent cell death pathway, in DOP and explores the therapeutic potential of Eldecalcitol (ED-71). In a type 2 diabetes mouse model, ED-71 treatment significantly ameliorated bone loss and suppressed the upregulation of oxeiptosis-associated molecular changes in BMSCs. In vitro, high glucose (HG) conditions induced oxeiptosis-associated signaling, mitochondrial dysfunction, a glycolytic shift, and impaired osteogenic differentiation in BMSCs. ED-71 intervention partially counteract these effects. Mechanistic studies predicted a potential molecular interaction between ED-71 and PKM2, a key regulator of glycolysis, which reduced its abundance and reversed metabolic imbalance. These effects were accompanied by improved mitochondrial function and enhanced Nrf2/GPX4-mediated antioxidant defense, ultimately suppressing the KEAP1/PGAM5/AIFM1 oxeiptosis-associated signaling. Pharmacological activation of PKM2 by TEPP-46 partially reversed ED-71's protective effects, supporting a functional involvement of PKM2 in the observed mechanism, although genetic validation is required to establish causality. In conclusion, ED-71 may alleviate mouse DOP by reducing PKM2 expression to correct metabolic reprogramming and mitochondrial dysfunction, thereby suppressing oxeiptosis and restoring HG-treated BMSCs' osteogenic potential, offering a novel mechanistic foundation for its therapeutic application.

articles.title: The role of vitamin D in pulmonary arterial hypertension: From vascular biology to patient outcomes.
articles.abstract: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) is a progressive pulmonary vascular disease characterized by endothelial dysfunction, excessive vasoconstriction, vascular remodeling, and right ventricular failure. In recent years, vitamin D (VitD) has emerged as a potential modulator of several biological pathways implicated in PAH pathobiology. Beyond its classical role in calcium and phosphate homeostasis, VitD exerts pleiotropic effects through activation of the VitD receptor, which is expressed in pulmonary artery endothelial cells and smooth muscle cells. Experimental evidence indicates that VitD signaling is associated with the regulation of key mechanisms involved in PAH, including endothelial nitric oxide production, prostacyclin and endothelin pathways, Endothelial-to-Mesenchymal Transition, smooth muscle cell proliferation, inflammation, oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, and extracellular matrix remodeling. Studies conducted in experimental pulmonary hypertension models, including models with PAH-like vascular remodeling, have reported associations between VitD restoration and improved pulmonary hemodynamics, right ventricular function, endothelial function, and pulmonary vascular remodeling. However, these models do not fully recapitulate human Group 1 PAH and therefore their findings should be interpreted cautiously. Clinical studies have demonstrated a high prevalence of VitD deficiency among patients with PAH, although several studies have included heterogeneous pH populations, and lower circulating 25-hydroxyvitamin D levels have been associated with worse functional class, reduced exercise capacity, more severe hemodynamic impairment, right ventricular dysfunction, and poorer survival. However, clinical evidence regarding the benefits of VitD supplementation remains limited and is mainly derived from small observational studies and uncontrolled interventions. This narrative review summarizes the current experimental and clinical evidence linking VitD to PAH pathobiology and patient outcomes, highlighting potential mechanistic pathways and discussing the opportunities and challenges for future therapeutic strategies. Although available data support a biologically plausible association between VitD/VitD receptor signaling and pulmonary vascular homeostasis, adequately powered randomized controlled trials are required to determine whether correction of VitD deficiency is associated with improved clinical outcomes in PAH.

articles.title: Spatial transcriptomics reveals renal ER stress in alcohol-associated kidney injury.
articles.abstract: Alcohol misuse damages numerous organs, including the liver, heart, brain, and pancreas. The kidney remains a severely understudied target of alcohol-induced injury despite renal injury being commonly observed in end-stage alcohol-associated liver disease (ALD) patients. A 6-week murine ethanol (1-6% v/v) model for early-stage ALD combined with carbon tetrachloride (CCl4) treatment was utilized to reveal mechanisms of renal injury. This paradigm yields elevated kidney damage markers when compared to ethanol consumption alone, including elevated urinary KIM-1 in 3 weeks. Hypothesis generating tissue spatial analysis was used to explore ethanol-related transcriptomic alterations across kidney morphology. Using a publicly available scRNA-seq dataset, the predominant cell-type specific differences were identified and allowed for the generation of spatially resolved gene clusters. Ethanol + CCl4 increased kidney injury marker gene expression in proximal tubule cells, signifying extensive damage. Overall, a decrease in expression of ethanol metabolizing genes was localized to the renal cortex. Genes associated with the unfolded protein response (UPR) were induced across the kidney and were morphologically associated throughout the nephron. Key mRNAs (Hspa5, Hsp90b1, Ndrg1) and ribosomal transcripts were altered due to ethanol metabolism across proximal tubules. Furthermore, epigenetic alterations in regulatory marks of lysine acetylation or trimethylation are associated with the combination treatment. Collectively, the application of tissue spatial transcriptomics to a well-defined model of alcohol toxicity reveals dynamic morphologic changes in gene expression across renal cell types due to ethanol. Our results indicate ER stress and the UPR are significantly impacted by ethanol metabolism throughout proximal tubules, associating with ethanol-induced renal dysfunction.

articles.title: From Empiricism to Precision: Century of Paradigm Shifts in Medical Dermatology.
articles.abstract: Over the past century, advances in scientific understanding and therapeutic development have fundamentally reshaped dermatology. Diseases once managed with empiric, toxic, or largely ineffective treatments can now be approached with therapies that target specific pathways, achieve sustained disease control, and, in some cases, alter prognosis. Herein, we reviewed landmark therapeutic advances across infectious, inflammatory, autoimmune, vascular, and oncologic dermatology, focusing on interventions that changed the standard of care or substantially improved patient outcomes. Transformative advances include penicillin for syphilis, isotretinoin for severe acne, biologics for psoriasis, corticosteroids and rituximab for pemphigus vulgaris, targeted biologic and Janus kinase inhibitors for inflammatory and autoimmune diseases, beta-blockers for infantile hemangiomas, immunotherapy and targeted therapy for cutaneous malignancies, and Hedgehog pathway inhibitors for advanced basal cell carcinoma. Collectively, these breakthroughs expanded what treatment could achieve, from curing previously chronic infection and controlling severe inflammatory disease to restoring hair or pigmentation and prolonging survival in advanced malignancy. Progress arose through both sustained research into disease biology and unexpected clinical observations that opened new therapeutic possibilities. These landmark therapeutic breakthroughs trace dermatology's evolution from empiric treatment toward increasingly precise, mechanism-based care. This history illustrates how scientific discovery and clinical observation can redefine the management and prognosis of dermatologic disease.

articles.title: CaMKIIδ/ZO-2-mediated phosphorylation of AQP9 at Ser292 drives hepatic steatosis and oxidative stress in MASLD.
articles.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is a prevalent chronic liver disorder with limited treatment options. Aquaporin 9 (AQP9) is the main glycerol channel in hepatocytes, but its regulatory mechanisms in MASLD remain unclear. Here, we identified Ser292 as a key phosphorylation site on AQP9. We demonstrate that CaMKIIδ, scaffolded by ZO-2, phosphorylates AQP9 at Ser292. This modification increases the plasma-membrane localization of AQP9 and thereby enhances glycerol uptake, leading to increased hepatic lipid accumulation and, notably, exacerbates oxidative stress. Both pharmacological inhibition of CaMKIIδ and genetic disruption of this pathway (via TJP2 knockdown or an AQP9-S292A mutant) effectively reduced lipid deposition and oxidative damage in vitro and in mouse models of MASLD. Our findings reveal the CaMKIIδ/ZO-2/AQP9-Ser292 axis as a critical driver that integrates metabolic and oxidative stress pathways in MASLD. Targeting this axis, particularly via hepatocyte-specific CaMKIIδ inhibition, represents a promising therapeutic strategy to simultaneously ameliorate steatosis and oxidative injury.

articles.title: MenSC-EV-derived HSPA5 activates the AKT/mTOR axis to suppress ferroptosis in Type 1 diabetes mellitus-associated ovarian dysfunction.
articles.abstract: Type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM) is associated with ovarian dysfunction, including menstrual irregularities, impaired ovarian reserve, and premature reproductive aging, yet effective therapeutic strategies to safeguard ovarian function against metabolic stress remain limited. Mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) have emerged as pivotal regulators of tissue homeostasis, with their paracrine effects largely mediated by extracellular vesicles (EVs). Here, we demonstrate that menstrual blood-derived endometrial stem cell-EVs (MenSC-EVs) alleviate streptozotocin (STZ)-induced ovarian dysfunction and inhibit granulosa cells (GCs) ferroptosis by delivering HSPA5. Mechanistically, EV-associated HSPA5 restored AKT/mTOR signaling and was accompanied by reduced BECN1 phosphorylation, thereby preserving the SLC7A11/GPX4-associated antioxidant pathway. We further show that BECN1 directly interacts with SLC7A11, linking BECN1 signaling to regulation of the system Xc-/GPX4 antioxidant axis. MenSC-EVs preserved this antioxidant pathway and reduced lipid peroxidation in injured GCs. Collectively, these findings identify an HSPA5-dependent anti-ferroptotic mechanism through which MenSC-EVs ameliorate T1DM-associated ovarian dysfunction, supporting their potential as an ovarian-protective strategy under diabetic conditions.

articles.title: The Liver-Heart Axis: Linking Liver Stiffness to Early Cardiac Dysfunction in MASLD.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is increasingly recognized as a systemic disorder with cardiovascular consequences. Conventional measures such as left ventricular ejection fraction fail to identify early myocardial impairment. The present prospective study was undertaken to evaluate subclinical myocardial dysfunction in MASLD using global longitudinal strain (GLS), assess its correlation with liver stiffness measurement (LSM), and identify its independent predictors.

METHODS: This prospective cross-sectional study included 128 patients with MASLD. GLS was assessed by speckle-tracking echocardiography, and liver stiffness was measured using vibration-controlled transient elastography (FibroScan). A GLS value ≥ 18% was considered abnormal (indicative of subclinical left ventricular dysfunction). Correlation and regression analyses were performed to identify predictors of subclinical myocardial dysfunction.

RESULTS: Subclinical myocardial dysfunction (GLS ≥ 18%) was detected in 74.2% of MASLD patients despite preserved ejection fraction. Liver stiffness correlated strongly with impaired GLS (r = 0.722, p < 0.001). Patients with abnormal GLS had significantly higher liver stiffness (8.98 ± 1.24 kPa vs. 6.95 ± 0.85 kPa, p < 0.001). Fibrosis stage showed a graded association with worsening GLS. On regression analysis, liver stiffness and body mass index (BMI) emerged as independent predictors of subclinical myocardial dysfunction, while steatosis (CAP) did not correlate with GLS.

CONCLUSIONS: MASLD patients demonstrate a high prevalence of early cardiac dysfunction that is strongly associated with liver stiffness. Myocardial strain imaging combined with liver stiffness measurement offers a valuable approach for early cardio-hepatic risk stratification and integrated care of MASLD patients.

IMPACT AND IMPLICATIONS: MASLD confers a "silent" cardiac burden, with nearly three-quarters of patients showing subclinical left ventricular dysfunction despite normal ejection fraction. Our study identifies liver stiffness as the key correlate of this cardiac impairment, whereas steatosis alone was not correlated with myocardial dysfunction. These findings suggest that integrating myocardial strain imaging and liver stiffness assessment can enable earlier identification of at-risk MASLD patients, underscoring the need for multidisciplinary management bridging hepatology and cardiology.

CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: CTRI/2024/02/062960 (Clinical Trials Registry - India).

articles.title: Evaluation of six generative large language models answering pre-analytical questions in medical microbiology.
articles.journal: Clinical microbiology and infection : the official publication of the European Society of Clinical Microbiology and Infectious Diseases
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Large language models (LLMs) have the potential to be integrated into diagnostics workflows, yet their reliability in pre-analytical diagnostic stewardship remains uncertain. We aimed to evaluate the performance of six LLMs answering common pre-analytical questions in the domain of medical microbiology. Next, we propose a blueprint to evaluate LLMs in medical microbiology.

METHODS: We compared general-purpose models from OpenAI (GPT-3.5, GPT-4) and Meta AI (Llama2-7B, Llama2-13B), alongside two domain-enhanced versions (customised GPT-4 agent and Llama2-7B Medical) in a hybrid evaluation framework. First, we quantified the response length (word count), then assessed the similarity between LLM-generated responses and expert-reviewed reference answers (BLEU/ROUGE scores, BERTScore). Finally, thirty-three medical professionals rated the accuracy and completeness of the LLM-generated responses on a 1-7-point scale.

RESULTS: Responses of OpenAI models showed greater similarity to the reference set and significantly outperformed Meta AI-based models in accuracy and completeness. The customized generative pre-trained transformer (GPT) matched performance of OpenAI's general-purpose models, while generating significantly shorter responses (p<0.001). Quality ratings varied markedly between professionals, as medical microbiologists and experienced infectious disease specialists assigned significantly lower scores compared to infectious disease trainees and medical students (p<0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: We observed considerable variation in LLM performance and highlight differences in perceived response quality across professional groups, emphasizing the need for critical appraisal when consulting LLMs for pre-analytical guidance.

articles.title: Yearly relative variations of bacteraemia and pneumonia incidence acquired in intensive care units at Lyon University Hospitals (2004-2024): a scatterplot visualization.
articles.journal: Clinical microbiology and infection : the official publication of the European Society of Clinical Microbiology and Infectious Diseases

articles.title: How do I manage candiduria: practical algorithms and remaining conundrums in 2026.
articles.journal: Clinical microbiology and infection : the official publication of the European Society of Clinical Microbiology and Infectious Diseases
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Candiduria is frequently encountered in hospitalized patients and encompasses a wide spectrum of clinical scenarios, ranging from asymptomatic colonization or sample contamination to genuine urinary tract infections and, in rarer cases, invasive candidiasis. Despite its high prevalence, especially in urological and intensive care settings, its clinical relevance is often uncertain, leading to diagnostic uncertainty and inconsistent management, even among infectious disease specialists.

OBJECTIVES: This review aims to provide a structured approach to the evaluation and management of candiduria, illustrated by a clinical vignette. The objective is to support evidence-informed decision-making by highlighting key diagnostic and therapeutic decisions.

SOURCES: In the absence of randomized controlled trials addressing symptomatic candiduria management, we conducted a narrative review of the literature, focusing on observational studies and expert guidance from the 2016 IDSA and 2025 international ECMM guidelines.

CONTENT: Based on the case of a patient with a double-J ureteral stent presenting with acute febrile illness, this review explores diagnostic and therapeutic challenges associated with candiduria. It addresses epidemiology, risk factors, and the distinction between colonization and infection. Antifungal treatment options are discussed considering their pharmacological properties, particularly their diffusion in kidneys and excretion in urine and potential toxicities. We further address the rare but severe complication of fungus balls.

IMPLICATIONS: By converting current evidence into practical clinical algorithms, this review aims to enhance diagnostic accuracy, support antifungal stewardship, and highlight gaps in knowledge. It underscores the need for further research to improve evidence-based management strategies for candiduria.

articles.title: TNF Receptor-2 Drives Tumoural Coagulation Factor Synthesis and Enhances Thrombosis in Clear Cell Renal Cell Carcinoma.
articles.abstract: Clear-cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC), the most prevalent form of kidney cancer, is associated with an increased risk of local and systemic thromboembolism and a worse prognosis. The mechanisms that drive the coagulation program in tumours are not known. Combining RNAscope with immunofluorescence, local transcription of the key coagulation factors X and V, as well as prothrombin and fibrinogen chains (α, β, γ), across tumour cells, vascular endothelial cells and T cells is significantly enhanced in ccRCC tumours compared to adjacent normal kidney tissue. Elevated intratumoural protein expression of factors X and V is accompanied by local thrombin generation, fibrin deposition, and the presence of intravascular microthrombi, which themselves harbour coagulation transcripts. Mechanistic analysis using ccRCC organ cultures reveal that selective engagement of tumour necrosis factor receptor-2 (TNFR2) by a R2TNF mutein is sufficient to significantly enhance the transcription and protein expression of the same coagulation program in tumour cells, endothelial cells, and T cells compared to adjacent normal kidney cultures, whereas TNFR2 knockdown attenuates this response. In addition, TNFR2 appears to link inflammatory signalling with activation of the local coagulation system through the PI3K/Akt/MEK/NFκB signalling axes. These data provide evidence that locally produced coagulation factors driven by TNFR2 signalling may contribute to intratumoural pro-thrombotic outcomes in ccRCC, highlighting a novel pathway with potential therapeutic relevance.

articles.title: Thyrotropin-releasing hormone increases dorsal premammillary nucleus neuron activity and darting behavior.
articles.abstract: Thyrotropin-releasing hormone (TRH) is classically recognized for its role in regulating the hypothalamic-pituitary-thyroid (HPT) axis; however, it also functions as a central neuromodulator influencing arousal, locomotion, and autonomic processes. Despite these established roles, the circuit-level mechanisms through which TRH modulates behavior remain poorly defined. The dorsal premammillary nucleus (PMd) is a hypothalamic structure implicated in high-imminence defensive states, yet whether TRH directly engages PMd circuits is unknown. Here, we assessed the role of TRH as a modulator of PMd neuronal activity and behavioral output using in situ hybridization, electrophysiology, calcium imaging, and behavioral assays in male and female mice. TRHR mRNA was co-localized with a subset of PMd CCK-positive neurons. TRH increased firing rate in a subset of PMd neurons in brain slices, revealing functional activation of a subset of the population. This finding was corroborated by calcium imaging that showed increased activity following TRH exposure. In vivo, intrahypothalamic administration of TRH produced darting and behavioral effects. Together, these findings identify a subpopulation of PMd neurons that serve as a functional hypothalamic target of TRH signaling associated with rapid locomotor behavioral output.

articles.title: Multisite veno venous extracorporeal support in children below 5 kg, experience from a referral center.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Refractory respiratory failure is one of the leading indications for extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) in neonates and children. Despite strong arguments supporting the use of veno-venous ECMO (VV ECMO), the international ELSO registry still reports a higher rate of veno-arterial ECMO (VA ECMO) in such situations. We report our experience with multisite V-V ECMO in children weighing less than 5 kg.

METHODS: We conducted a single-center retrospective study from January 2017 to December 2025. All patients weighing less than 5 kg who underwent multisite VV ECMO were included in the analysis.

RESULTS: During the study period, 52 patients weighing less than 5 kg underwent VV ECMO. Among these, 43 (83 %) received multisite VV ECMO. The median weight was 3.5 kg (2.9 - 4.3) and 12 patients (28 %) weighed less than 3 kg. Seventeen (39 %) patients were initially supported with VA ECMO and subsequently converted to VV ECMO. Percutaneous cannulation was performed using 21 femoral cannulas (48 %) and 17 jugular cannulas (39%). All vascular complications occurred during percutaneous femoral cannulation. Median blood flows on days 1, 3 and 7 were 106 ml/kg/min (92 - 117), 105 ml/kg/min (94 - 116) and 101 ml/kg/min (93 - 118), respectively. The median duration of ECMO support was 12 days (6 - 17). Twenty-six (60%) patients were successfully weaned from ECMO, and 25 were alive 6 months after ECMO support.

CONCLUSION: Multisite VV ECMO is an effective cannulation strategy in children weighing less than 5 kg with refractory respiratory failure.

articles.title: A 0/2-Hour Algorithm Using a Novel Point-of-Care High-Sensitivity Cardiac Troponin I Assay for Suspected Myocardial Infarction.
articles.abstract: This letter describes the derivation and internal validation of an assay-specific hs-cTnI-SPINCHIP 0/2h-algorithm for rapid triage of patients with suspected myocardial infarction (MI) in the emergency department (ED). The algorithm provided very high safety for rule-out, high accuracy for rule-in, and enabled definitive triage within 2 hours in approximately 80% of patients. These findings support the clinical potential of the novel point-of-care hs-cTnI-SPINCHIP assay for accelerated ED decision-making.

articles.title: Lifetime management of valvular heart disease in younger and low risk patients.
articles.abstract: Valvular heart disease in younger and low-risk patients presents unique therapeutic challenges because treatment decisions must account not only for immediate procedural success but also for the durability of the index intervention, the feasibility of future reinterventions, and the preservation of subsequent treatment options. Consequently, lifetime management has emerged as a longitudinal treatment paradigm in which every intervention influences the sequence, complexity, and outcomes of future procedures. Over the past decade, transcatheter valve therapies have expanded rapidly from a treatment reserved for elderly and high-surgical-risk patients to an increasingly adopted option in younger and lower-risk populations. Although contemporary evidence has demonstrated excellent procedural safety and mid-term outcomes, important uncertainties remain regarding long-term durability and the optimal management of structural valve deterioration and repeat interventions. These considerations highlight the importance of approaching each intervention not as an isolated procedure, but as a step within a predefined lifetime therapeutic strategy. In this context, structured Heart Team discussion and shared decision-making are fundamental to develop an individualized treatment plan that optimizes outcomes while preserving future surgical and transcatheter options across decades of patient care. This review aims to provide a practical framework for the lifetime management of aortic, mitral, and tricuspid valve disease in younger and low-risk patients.

articles.title: Epicardial adipose tissue phenotyping by cardiac CT in heart failure.
Bacterial and viral infections promote proliferation and local aggregation of IgM+ B cells in fish spleen.
articles.abstract: Humoral immunity is a central component of host defense in teleost fish, yet the dynamics of IgM+ B cells during infection remain poorly understood. In this study, we generated and characterized a monoclonal antibody (mAb) against native IgM protein purified from grass carp (Ctenopharyngodon idella) sera. This mAb specifically recognized the recombinant grass carp IgM heavy chain expressed in the HEK293 cells and showed cross-reactivity with IgM molecules from multiple cyprinid species, including rare minnow, zebrafish, black carp, and common carp, but not with IgM from largemouth bass. Flow cytometric analysis showed that IgM+ B cells were abundant in the spleen and head kidney of grass carp, accounting for 35.40 ± 3.15% and 27.63 ± 3.97% of total leukocytes, respectively. Using this antibody, we further investigated IgM+ B-cell responses in grass carp and rare minnow after infection with Aeromonas hydrophila or grass carp reovirus genotype II. Both bacterial and viral infections significantly enhanced the proliferation and local aggregation of splenic IgM+ B cells. Moreover, EdU+ proliferating cells were preferentially enriched within localized IgM+ B-cell clusters in the spleens of infected fish. Taken together, our work provides a useful antibody tool for studying B-cell responses and reveals that bacterial and viral infections induce proliferation and localized aggregation of splenic IgM+ B cells in teleost fish, highlighting infection-induced remodeling of splenic IgM+ B-cell responses.

articles.title: Immune homeostasis as the missing link between systemic fungicide exposure and pathogen susceptibility in aquatic animals.
articles.abstract: Systemic fungicides are widely used in modern agriculture and are increasingly detected in aquatic environments, raising concerns about their potential effects on non-target aquatic organisms. Unlike conventional toxicological studies that primarily focus on acute toxicity, oxidative stress, or organ damage, emerging evidence suggests that sublethal fungicide exposure may also disturb immune regulation and compromise host defense. This review systematically summarizes the environmental occurrence and biological effects of major systemic fungicides, including triazoles, strobilurins, benzimidazoles, and other systemic fungicides, in aquatic animals. Available evidence indicates that fungicide exposure can induce developmental and organ-specific toxicity, disrupt barrier integrity, alter immune-related responses, and interfere with cellular processes involved in immune regulation, including oxidative balance, mitochondrial function, endocrine signaling, and energy metabolism. Importantly, these effects differ in their relevance to host immunity: general physiological toxicity and changes in individual immune biomarkers should not be considered equivalent to functional immune impairment. Recent studies provide direct evidence that azoxystrobin and trifloxystrobin can impair antiviral defense and increase susceptibility to rhabdovirus infection in fish, whereas comparable pathogen-challenge evidence for other fungicides, pathogens, and aquatic animal taxa remains limited. Based on these findings, we propose immune homeostasis as a conceptual link between systemic fungicide exposure and altered host defense, and highlight the need to integrate environmentally realistic exposure, functional immune endpoints, mechanistic validation, and pathogen-challenge models into aquatic immunotoxicology. This immune homeostasis-centered perspective may improve the assessment of disease-related risks associated with chronic fungicide exposure and provide a basis for understanding how environmental chemical stress contributes to disease susceptibility in aquatic animals.

articles.title: Prenatal exposure to maternal SARS-CoV-2 infection leads to altered neuro-immune biomarker profiles at birth.
articles.abstract: Maternal infection during pregnancy can induce immune-mediated biological adaptations that influence fetal neurodevelopment. Although vertical transmission of SARS-CoV-2 is uncommon, the impact of maternal infection on fetal neuroimmune signaling remains poorly characterized. We investigated whether prenatal exposure to maternal SARS-CoV-2 infection is associated with alterations in circulating neuroimmune biomarkers detectable at birth. In this case-control study, 28 women with SARS-CoV-2 infection during pregnancy and 61 uninfected controls were enrolled. Maternal and cord blood samples were collected at delivery. Following an initial inflammatory screening, neuro-specific biomarkers (NfL, Tau, P-Tau217, GFAP, S100β, α-Synuclein) and PTX3 were measured. Correlation network analyses, PTX3 promoter methylation assessment, and haplotype stratification analyses were also performed. Systemic inflammatory mediators did not differ significantly between groups. In contrast, neonates exposed to maternal SARS-CoV-2 infection exhibited significantly lower cord blood concentrations of GFAP, NfL, and P-Tau217 and increased α-Synuclein levels compared with controls. Tau showed a decreasing trend, whereas S100β and PTX3 remained unchanged. Network analyses revealed reduced cytokine connectivity but enhanced interactions among neuro-specific biomarkers. Although PTX3 promoter methylation was unchanged, the PTX3 h2/h2 haplotype appeared to modulate biomarker interaction patterns. To our knowledge, this is the first study to characterize a circulating neuro-specific biomarker signature in neonates prenatally exposed to maternal SARS-CoV-2 infection. This supports the utility of neuroimmune biomarker networks as translational tools to investigate the biological consequences of maternal immune activation during pregnancy.

articles.title: Mechanisms overcoming the resistance of human TRPV2 to chemical activation.
articles.abstract: Transient receptor potential vanilloid 2 (TRPV2) is a thermosensitive cation channel widely expressed across diverse cell types. There, it contributes to numerous physiological processes and plays a role in the pathophysiology of inflammation, immunity, various cancers and neuronal development. The inherent resistance of human TRPV2 (hTRPV2) to stimuli that readily activate its rodent orthologs currently limits progress in translational and clinical research on this channel. Here, we present engineered variants of hTRPV2 that were designed to enhance channel activation induced by 2-aminoethoxydiphenylborate (2-APB), cannabidiol, and the TRPV2 agonist AV2-1, thereby identifying sites that allow for the most effective channel regulation. Through a series of rational mutations and chimeric constructs, combined with electrophysiology and molecular modeling, we identified two key allosteric sites in hTRPV2 that determine the resistance of the channel to activating stimuli. We discovered that two intracellular membrane-proximal salt bridges prevent effective activation of hTRPV2: (i) one formed between residues of the putative 2-APB-binding site and the bottom of S6 helix (R533-E647), and (ii) another formed between residues from the TRP helix and the proximal N-terminus (D655-R369). We also propose possible mechanisms by which the non-conserved pore turret contributes to channel activation. Our results may facilitate the rational drug design towards potent and selective hTRPV2 ligands and help to elucidate the functions of this channel in organs or cell types of interest.

articles.title: HtpG-High-Expressing Escherichia coli Promotes Fibrosis in Chronic Pancreatitis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND & AIMS: Chronic pancreatitis (CP) is a progressive fibroinflammatory disease with rising global incidence and no curative therapy. Gut dysbiosis has been associated with CP, but its causal contribution to disease pathogenesis remains unclear. We intended to identify specific pathogenic microbial species that promote CP and to delineate the underlying pathogenic mechanisms.

METHODS: Multi-omics analyses were used to identify key microbial signatures in CP patients and mice. Novel pathogenic Escherichia coli strains were isolated and bioengineered for functional studies. In vitro and in vivo assays, along with macrophage-specific knockout mice, adenoviral tools, and pharmacological inhibitors, were employed to dissect host-microbe mechanistic pathways. Therapeutic intervention included administering a screened next-generation probiotic.

RESULTS: Metagenomic sequencing identified HtpG-high-expressing E. coli (HHEC) enrichment as a dominant microbial signature in CP patients. Prevention of HHEC adherence and colonization alleviated CP, whereas recolonization with a new patient-derived HHEC strain PS718 exacerbated it. Mechanistically, E. coli-derived HtpG upregulated protein arginine methyltransferase 5 (PRMT5) in pancreatic macrophages. Pharmacological inhibition of PRMT5 or macrophage-specific deletion of PRMT5 mitigated pancreatic fibrosis and CP progression. PRMT5 methylated Krüppel-like factor 4 (KLF4) at residues R387/R389, stabilizing it, which promoted M2 polarization and pancreatic fibrosis. Therapeutic intervention with Akkermansia muciniphila, which is reduced in CP, suppressed HHEC colonization and ameliorated CP.

CONCLUSION: These findings provide novel evidence for a pathogenic HHEC-HtpG-macrophage axis in CP, highlighting the potential of microbiota-targeted therapies for the condition.

articles.title: Prevalence and predictors of the honeymoon phase in type 1 diabetes: A longitudinal study from a tertiary care center of north India.
articles.abstract:
AIM: Honeymoon phase (HP) of type 1 diabetes (T1D) represents a transient period of partial remission with preserved β-cell function. This study assessed the prevalence, duration, and early predictors of HP in newly diagnosed Asian-Indian T1D subjects.

METHODS: In this longitudinal cohort study, 76 individuals aged 12-25 years were recruited within two months of T1D diagnosis. HbA1c, insulin dose-adjusted A1c (IDAA1c), fasting and mixed-meal stimulated C-peptide were assessed every three months till 18 months.

RESULTS: 42% (25) of subjects entered HP defined as IDAA1c ≤ 9, with median onset of 6 months and median duration of 9 months. Most baseline parameters were comparable, although baseline total daily insulin dose/kg body weight (TDD) and IDAA1c were significantly lower in HP group. Subjects entering HP demonstrated significantly lower TDD, superior glycemic control and preserved C-peptide levels. At 3 months, stimulated C-peptide > 2.10 ng/mL showed strongest predictive performance for HP occurrence, AUC 0.89, followed by HbA1c < 9.75%, AUC 0.83, TDD < 0.58 IU/kg/day, AUC 0.79 and Fasting C-peptide > 1.10 ng/mL, AUC 0.77.

CONCLUSIONS: 3-month C-peptide, HbA1c, and TDD may serve as early predictors to identify patients likely to enter HP and may support selection of candidates for β-cell preserving interventions.

articles.title: Baseline blood-based DNA methylation in impaired fasting glucose and impaired glucose tolerance: epigenome-wide differences and associations with subsequent progression to type 2 diabetes mellitus.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Impaired fasting glucose (IFG) and impaired glucose tolerance (IGT) differ in type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) progression risk, but whether they have distinct blood DNA methylation (DNAm) patterns and CpG features associated with progression remains unclear.

METHODS: DNAm was profiled in peripheral blood leukocytes from 78 CATAMERI participants (26 IFG, 27 IGT, and 25 NGT). IFG and IGT participants were stratified by prediabetes persistence or T2DM progression. DNAm differences were assessed using a unified epigenome-wide model. Features were selected by 20 x 5-fold repeated resampling and evaluated for metabolic correlations, progression, and discrimination.

RESULTS: DNAm analysis identified 8,082 differentially methylated CpGs in IFG versus NGT, 1,992 in IGT versus NGT, and 9,488 in IFG versus IGT. Resampling retained three CpGs per phenotype showing ordered baseline DNAm patterns according to glycaemic outcome; cg23913182 was retained in both phenotypes. Lower baseline DNAm at these CpGs was associated with subsequent T2DM progression. cg23913182 showed lower odds of progression per 1 percentage-point DNAm increase (OR1%=0.291 in IFG; OR1%=0.171 in IGT) and moderate discriminatory performance (AUC = 0.757 and 0.791, respectively).

CONCLUSIONS: IFG and IGT show distinct blood-based DNAm patterns, highlighting epigenetic heterogeneity. CpG features associated with subsequent T2DM progression warrant validation in independent cohorts.

articles.title: Role of shrimp tegumental glands in the dynamics of infection with the white spot syndrome virus.
articles.abstract: The cuticle and peritrophic membrane are important physical barriers against pathogens in shrimp. However, exposed structures, such as tegumental glands (TGs), can act as entry points for the white spot syndrome virus (WSSV). Previous studies have detected viral signals in TGs, although it remains unclear whether the virus is retained in the mucus or infects glandular cells. In this study, in situ hybridization for viral RNA in TG cells indicated the presence of viral transcripts, suggesting that TGs could function as sites of viral infection and subsequent tissue dissemination. Furthermore, β-glucans showed a local protective effect, indicating potential activation of immune mechanisms.

articles.title: First-in-Human Safety and Pharmacokinetic Evaluation of Seralutinib, an Investigational Inhaled Tyrosine-protein Kinase Inhibitor for Pulmonary Hypertension.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: First-in-human studies were conducted to evaluate the safety, tolerability, and pharmacokinetics (PK) of single and multiple doses of inhaled seralutinib in healthy participants.

METHODS: Two phase I, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled studies were conducted. In Study 1, participants received single ascending doses of seralutinib (3.75-48 mg) or placebo (Part 1) and multiple ascending doses of seralutinib (18 mg BID, 24 mg TID, and 48 mg TID) or placebo for 7 days (Part 2). In Study 2, participants received a single dose of seralutinib 90 mg or placebo (Part 1) and multiple doses of seralutinib (90 mg BID) or placebo for 7 days (Part 2). Sentinel dosing strategy was utilized for all cohorts. Safety was assessed. Seralutinib PK was characterized.

RESULTS: 82 healthy participants completed the studies (20 received placebo; 37, single doses of seralutinib; 25, multiple doses of seralutinib BID or TID for 7 days). No serious adverse events (AEs) or AEs leading to withdrawal were reported. Most AEs were mild in severity. Following single and multiple dose inhalations, seralutinib was quickly absorbed (median tmax 5 minutes) into, and rapidly cleared from the systemic circulation.
