METHODS: In this retrospective and prospective multicenter study, 854 echocardiographic scans were analyzed. Conventional and novel radiomic features were extracted from parasternal short-axis views at basal, mid, and apical LV levels, with incorporated age and sex from echocardiogram metadata. A machine learning pipeline was developed using a balanced training set (150 ATTR-CM, 150 nonamyloid HF). Performance was evaluated on an independent internal validation set (50 ATTR-CM, 399 nonamyloid HF) and an external validation set (10 ATTR-CM, 10 immunoglobulin light-chain-amyloid, 10 hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, 75 nonamyloid HF).

RESULTS: In internal validation, the model achieved 86% sensitivity (95% CI: 73.8%-93%), 92% specificity (95% CI: 88.9%-94.3%), 57.3% positive predictive value (95% CI: 46.1%-67.9%), 98.1% negative predictive value (NPV) (95% CI: 96.2%-99.1%), and receiver operating characteristic-area under the curve 0.938 (95% CI: 0.891-0.985). Performance was consistent in the external validation (100% sensitivity, 78.9% specificity, 33.3% positive predictive value, 100% NPV, and receiver operating characteristic-area under the curve of 0.917). The model correctly classified 77.3% of nonamyloid HF, 70% of AL-amyloid cases, and 100% of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy cases as non-ATTR in subgroup analysis.

CONCLUSIONS: We developed an echocardiographic radiomics-based tool to identify ATTR-CM with excellent discrimination and very high NPV in a cohort that approximates clinical experience. These preliminary findings require validation in larger, more diverse cohorts.

articles.title: Risk factors and preventive strategies for pressure injury and medical device-related pressure injury in ICU patients receiving invasive mechanical ventilation: A scoping review.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Adult ICU patients receiving invasive mechanical ventilation (IMV) are at risk of pressure injury (PI) and medical device-related pressure injury (MDRPI) due to immobility, impaired perfusion, and device contact. This scoping review synthesized evidence on PI and MDRPI risk factors and preventive strategies.

METHODS: This scoping review followed the Arksey and O'Malley framework and PRISMA-ScR guidelines. Five databases (PubMed, CINAHL, Scopus, MEDLINE, ScienceDirect) were searched from inception to April 2026. Studies of adult ICU patients receiving IMV reporting PI, MDRPI, risk factors, or preventive strategies were eligible.

RESULTS: Forty-two studies from 14 countries (2009-2026) were included. PI incidence ranged from 10.3 to 36.3% (up to 88.7% when prone-positioned); MDRPI (oral mucosal injury) ranged from 25.9 to 43.1% (80.1% with a broader erythema criterion). Cutaneous PI mainly affected the sacrum, heels, occiput, face, and thorax (generally Stage 1-2); oral mucosal MDRPI, assessed using heterogeneous severity criteria, was typically mild-to-moderate. Onset was commonly reported on days 3-9. PI risk factors included immobility, impaired perfusion, vasopressor therapy, and poor nutrition; MDRPI risk factors involved prolonged intubation and device exposure. Preventive strategies included device repositioning, securement adjustment, device-contact protection, and oral care.

CONCLUSIONS: Prolonged mechanical loading and reduced tissue tolerance are intensified by immobility, sedation, hemodynamic instability, impaired perfusion, vasopressor use, and device exposure. Early-stage cutaneous PI and mild-to-moderate mucosal MDRPI were more commonly reported than severe cutaneous and mucosal injuries; given the descriptive, non-comparative evidence, this cannot be attributed to preventive effectiveness. Early monitoring may be important for detecting early-stage injury and identifying progression toward more severe injury.

IMPLICATIONS FOR CLINICAL PRACTICE: Prevention should combine pressure redistribution with tolerance-based repositioning, skin monitoring, device securement, device-contact protection, and oral mucosal care. An exploratory, hypothesis-generating observation is that the first 10 days of ICU stay may be a high-risk period, requiring prospective validation.

articles.title: Predicting acute kidney injury in type B aortic dissection: development and validation of a clinical nomogram.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Acute Kidney Injury (AKI) is a frequent and serious complication in patients with Type B Aortic Dissection (TBAD). Existing prediction models are mainly derived from type A or mixed cohorts and do not account for the distinct pathophysiology of TBAD. This study aimed to develop and validate a nomogram for individualized AKI risk prediction in TBAD patients.

METHODS: Data were obtained from the eICU Collaborative Research Database (eICU-CRD) and the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV (MIMIC-IV). The eICU-CRD cohort was used for model development and internal validation, while MIMIC-IV served for external validation. A three-step variable selection strategy combining Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator (LASSO), univariate, and multivariate logistic regression analyses was applied. Model performance was evaluated using the Area Under the receiver operating characteristic Curve (AUC), calibration curves, and Decision Curve Analysis (DCA).

RESULTS: Six independent predictors were identified: ICU length of stay, minimum glucose, minimum sodium, maximum bicarbonate, minimum creatinine, and minimum diastolic blood pressure. The nomogram showed excellent discrimination, with AUCs of 0.926 (95% CI: 0.893-0.956), 0.922 (95% CI: 0.869-0.967), and 0.921 (95% CI: 0.895-0.944) in the training, internal validation, and external validation cohorts, respectively. Calibration analysis demonstrated good agreement, and DCA indicated clinical utility within a threshold probability range of 0-70%.

CONCLUSIONS: This study developed a practical nomogram based on six readily available variables for dynamic in-hospital prediction of AKI in TBAD patients. The model may assist early risk stratification, although further prospective validation is warranted.

articles.title: Navigating Infection Control and Dialysis Delivery in Nursing Homes: Organizational Perspectives From 2020 to 2025.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Medical Directors Association
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Nursing home (NH) residents with end-stage kidney disease requiring thrice-weekly hemodialysis faced challenges during the COVID-19 pandemic, as infection control imperatives conflicted with access to life-sustaining care. This study examines how NHs and dialysis organizations navigated dialysis care for NH residents from 2020 to 2025, exploring how pandemic-era adaptations continue to shape care delivery.

DESIGN: Descriptive qualitative study that synthesized interview data from the qualitative arms of three mixed-methods studies conducted between 2020 and 2025.

SETTING AND PARTICIPANTS: Participants included NH administrators, clinical staff, and residents, as well as Medicare Advantage plan executives, kidney care management company leadership, and dialysis organization administrative leadership and staff across diverse US health care markets.

METHODS: Semistructured interviews were conducted. Interview transcript coding used a modified grounded theory approach. Theme and subtheme development used thematic and content analysis.

RESULTS: Three hundred nine interviews were conducted with representatives from 66 NHs, 8 Medicare Advantage plans, 5 kidney care management companies, and 6 dialysis organizations. Three themes were identified, reflecting varied perspectives on the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on dialysis care for NH residents. First, during the pandemic, NHs and dialysis centers prioritized infection mitigation through spatial distancing, cohorting, extended quarantine protocols, and reduced admissions of residents requiring dialysis. Second, NH residents experienced significant barriers to dialysis access, including transportation and schedule disruptions. Third, the pandemic continues to affect dialysis care for this population: although infection control practices have become routine, transportation challenges remain unresolved, and many NHs have reduced admissions of dialysis-dependent residents, threatening access for this vulnerable population.

CONCLUSIONS AND IMPLICATIONS: Although the COVID-19 pandemic prompted more rigorous infection control practices at NHs and dialysis centers, it also intensified longstanding vulnerabilities in cross-sector health care coordination for NH residents requiring dialysis. Insights from this study's findings could inform efforts to design more resilient, better coordinated models of care.

articles.title: Chaperoning post-thaw cryo-competence: HSP90 abundance as a molecular signature of sperm quality, oxidative status, cellular integrity, and fertility potential in Indonesian dairy bulls.
articles.abstract: Improving reproductive efficiency in dairy cattle is critical for sustainable artificial insemination (AI)-based breeding systems in Indonesia. Variability in semen freezability and the limited predictive value of conventional sperm assessments remain challenges for fertility evaluation. This study investigated Heat Shock Protein 90 (HSP90) as a molecular marker associated with sperm cryotolerance and fertility in Indonesian Holstein-Friesian bulls. Cryopreserved semen from 20 bulls was classified into good freezability (GF) and poor freezability (PF) groups based on post-thaw sperm plasma membrane integrity, determined using SYBR-14/propidium iodide (PI) double staining and flow cytometry. Sperm quality, oxidative stress markers (malondialdehyde, MDA; aspartate aminotransferase, AST), HSP90 mRNA and protein abundance, and field fertility (first-service conception rate) were evaluated. GF bulls exhibited higher HSP90 mRNA (0.068 ± 0.003 vs. 0.018 ± 0.003) and protein abundance (0.72 ± 0.02 vs. 0.41 ± 0.02 ng/mL), together with improved motility, kinematic parameters, acrosome integrity, and mitochondrial membrane potential and fewer sperm abnormalities than PF bulls (P < 0.05). PF bulls showed higher MDA and AST levels (P < 0.05). HSP90 expression was strongly correlated with fertility rate (r = 0.964 for mRNA; r = 0.945 for protein) and sperm functional parameters (r ≈ 0.95-0.99), while negative correlations were observed with MDA, AST, and sperm defects (r ≈ -0.92 to -0.98). Multivariable regression models were highly significant (P < 0.001), with post-thaw sperm quality and fertility-related parameters collectively explaining 98.4% and 99.2% of the variation in HSP90 mRNA and protein expression, respectively. Overall, HSP90 abundance was strongly associated with post-thaw sperm quality, biochemical indicators of cellular damage, and field fertility, supporting its potential as a candidate molecular biomarker for evaluating post-thaw sperm quality and reproductive performance in Indonesian dairy bulls. Further validation using paired pre-freezing and post-thaw assessments is needed to determine whether HSP90 abundance is associated with the preservation of sperm quality during cryopreservation.

articles.title: 12-week yoga intervention effect on metabolome in Polyendocrine Metabolic Ovarian Syndrome (PMOS): An LC-MS-based study.
articles.journal: Journal of Ayurveda and integrative medicine
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS) is a complex, heterogeneous disorder affecting endocrine, reproductive, and metabolic health. It is fundamentally a systemic metabolic defect that, if not addressed in time, can compromise the function of multiple systems, resulting in conditions such as impaired glucose tolerance, insulin resistance, cardiovascular disease, dyslipidemia, fatty liver disease, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. It is a lifestyle disorder with long-term health implications, requiring a holistic approach for management.

METHODS: This prospective quasi-experimental study involved 60 women (30 diagnosed with PMOS, 30 age and BMI-matched controls). Women with PMOS underwent a 12-week Yoga practice that included physical postures (Asanas), regulated breathing practice (Pranayama), and meditation (Dhyana) under the guidance of a trained therapist. Clinical characteristics and laboratory biochemical data were recorded, followed by an untargeted metabolomics analysis using high-resolution Orbitrap Fusion Tribrid Mass Spectrometer technology to study plasma metabolome changes.

RESULTS: Following Yoga intervention, women with PMOS showed significant improvements in hormonal, anthropometric parameters, and lipid profile. The metabolomics analysis showed that post-Yoga intervention, several key metabolites were significantly downregulated, including glucose, fructose, d-ribose, 3-hydroxybutanoate, taurine, and methylmalonate. However, metabolites like succinate and ascorbate were upregulated. Besides, AUC suggests significant metabolic shifts following Yoga intervention.

CONCLUSION: Yoga offers a holistic, integrated mind-body approach to managing the endocrine, metabolic, and reproductive dysfunction in PMOS and lowers the risk of developing long-term comorbidities.

articles.title: LAP inhibits the clearance of Staphylococcus aureus by neutrophils and suppressed excessive inflammatory responses in mice.
articles.abstract: Staphylococcus aureus (S. aureus) is a major cause of acute pneumonia, which leads to various complications, including lung abscess, respiratory distress syndrome, and myocarditis. With the rapid development of drug resistance, it is urgent to find new strategies for the treatment of S. aureus infectious diseases. The LC3-associated phagocytosis (LAP) has been reported to play a defensive role in various bacterial infections. However, certain pathogens have evolved strategies to resist LAP and even utilize the LAP effect exerted by the host for bacterial reproduction. In this article, we demonstrated that during the acute pulmonary infection caused by S. aureus, the LAP function is detrimental to the host's ability to eliminate the bacteria. LAP hinders the bactericidal effect of neutrophils by inhibiting the production of ROS, the secretion of NO, and the degranulation of cells. However, LAP helps to control the excessive inflammation in the host. The LAP effects of neutrophils and macrophages inhibit the inflammatory response through the MAPK and NF-κB pathways. These data suggest that targeting LAP may become a promising new treatment for S. aureus infections.

articles.title: Medication adherence and health-related quality of life among patients with heart failure: a cross-sectional study.
articles.journal: Heart & lung : the journal of critical care
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Heart failure (HF) continues to be a significant public health concern. Adherence to guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) is essential for improving clinical outcomes and quality of life (QoL) in these patients.

OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to evaluate how well patients with chronic HF adhere to GDMT and to assess their health-related QoL.

METHODS: This cross-sectional study was conducted using data collected between March and May 2025. Eligible participants were adult outpatients with a confirmed diagnosis of HF who were able to complete the study questionnaires. Medication adherence was assessed using the 8-item Morisky Medication Adherence Scale (MMAS-8), while health-related QoL was evaluated with the Minnesota Living with Heart Failure Questionnaire. Data were analyzed using SPSS version 25, with statistical significance set at p < 0.05.

RESULTS: Among 300 HF patients (64.7% male; median age of 63), sixty-nine percent had reduced ejection fraction (median EF 30%), with 62.4% classified as NYHA III or IV. Medication adherence was low in 25%, moderate in 44.6%, and high in 30.3%. Patients with more severe HF symptoms (higher NYHA class) reported significantly lower QoL, while higher adherence correlated significantly with better QoL. Older patients had a lower risk of low adherence, while intracardiac devices were linked to a higher risk.

CONCLUSION: Despite GDMT's critical role in HF management, a notable proportion of patients demonstrated low adherence, which was associated with diminished QoL. Special attention and targeted interventions for high-risk groups, particularly patients with intracardiac devices, are imperative for enhancing outcomes.

articles.title: Curcumin-loaded silk fibroin nanoparticle-stabilized pickering emulsions for co-delivery of resveratrol: Synergistic efficacy in strawberry preservation.
articles.abstract: Strawberries are nutrient-dense and economically vital fruits with extremely high perishability. They frequently suffer from postharvest losses and safety hazards due to their thin epidermis, active metabolism, and susceptibility to microbial infection. Conventional preservation strategies including refrigeration, chemical fungicides and polymer coatings suffer from chilling injury, health risks and high costs. Herein, we developed a novel Pickering emulsion stabilized by curcumin-loaded silk fibroin nanoparticles (Cur-SF NPs) for the co-delivery of resveratrol (Res) to synergistically enhance strawberry preservation. Formulated via a facile eco-friendly route, Cur-SF NPs serve as bifunctional stabilizers to enhance emulsion stability as well as solubility and stability of Res. Physicochemical characterization, antioxidant assays, and microbial tests verified the emulsion's favorable properties, revealing enhanced antioxidant activity and broad-spectrum antibacterial efficacy against Aspergillus niger and Escherichia coli. Integrated into chitosan edible coating, the emulsion effectively reduced strawberry weight loss, maintained firmness and inhibited spoilage. This green, sustainable strategy presents a highly viable approach for the postharvest preservation of soft fruits.

articles.title: UBA6 confers neuroprotection against sepsis-associated encephalopathy through facilitating LCN2 ubiquitin-dependent degradation.
articles.abstract: Sepsis-associated encephalopathy (SAE) is a common secondary complication of sepsis, accompanied by neuroinflammation and neuronal apoptosis. As an E1 ubiquitin-activating enzyme, ubiquitin-like modifier-activating enzyme 6 (UBA6) deficiency aggravates inflammation. Herein, we first confirmed that UBA6 is decreased in brain tissues of cecal ligation and puncture (CLP)-induced SAE mice. Lentivirus was bilaterally injected into the hippocampus to establish in vivo UBA6 overexpression. Lentivirus-mediated overexpression of UBA6 effectively inhibited microglial activation, downregulated the levels of pro-inflammatory mediators, and reduced inflammatory cytokine release. Furthermore, UBA6 upregulation mitigated neuronal apoptosis and improved spatial learning and memory functions in SAE model mice. For in vitro validation, BV-2 microglial cells were stimulated with 100 ng/mL LPS for 24 h. Consistent with in vivo observations, exogenous UBA6 decreased the proportion of CD86-positive pro-inflammatory microglia. After culturing HT-22 neuronal cells with BV-2 cell conditioned medium, UBA6 overexpression elevated neuronal viability and restrained caspase-3-mediated neuronal apoptosis. Quantitative proteomics was applied to screen and identify lipocalin 2 (LCN2) as a downstream interacting partner of UBA6. Mechanistically, UBA6 binds LCN2 at residue 147 to accelerate K48 ubiquitination and degradation of LCN2, which attenuates neuronal apoptosis induced by LCN2 paracrine. Rescue assays revealed that ectopic LCN2 expression reversed the protective effects of UBA6 against neuroinflammation and neuronal apoptosis. In summary, UBA6 ameliorates SAE-induced cerebral damage, neuroinflammation and cognitive dysfunction via accelerating LCN2 ubiquitination and degradation. These findings advance the mechanistic understanding of SAE progression and establish UBA6/LCN2 as a prospective therapeutic target for SAE intervention.

articles.title: The PGC-1α-ferroptosis axis mediates empagliflozin-induced epithelial barrier protection in sepsis-associated acute lung injury.
articles.abstract: Sepsis-associated acute lung injury is characterized by epithelial barrier failure, excessive oxidative stress, and inflammatory tissue damage. Ferroptosis has emerged as an important mechanism linking lipid peroxidation to epithelial dysfunction, but the regulatory mechanisms governing ferroptosis resistance in sepsis-associated lung injury remain unclear. Using an LPS-induced acute lung injury model and LPS-challenged A549 cells, we investigated whether empagliflozin protects epithelial barrier integrity by modulating PGC-1α-associated ferroptosis resistance. Endotoxin challenge suppressed PGC-1α expression, disrupted PI3K/AKT signaling, weakened the SLC7A11-GPX4 anti-ferroptotic defense axis, and promoted ROS accumulation, lipid peroxidation, tight junction loss, impaired epithelial repair, and lung pathological injury. Empagliflozin reversed these pathological alterations, preserving ZO-1, Occludin, and Claudin-1 expression while reducing ferroptosis-associated oxidative damage. Mechanistically, PGC-1α emerged as a central node linking metabolic stress adaptation, PI3K/AKT signaling, ferroptosis resistance, and epithelial barrier maintenance. Pharmacological inhibition or siRNA-mediated knockdown of PGC-1α weakened the protective effects of empagliflozin, indicating that PGC-1α is functionally required for empagliflozin-mediated epithelial protection. These findings identify a PGC-1α-associated ferroptosis-epithelial barrier mechanism through which empagliflozin protects against LPS-induced lung injury and provide mechanistic insight relevant to sepsis-associated acute lung injury.

articles.title: Variation in procedure selection for end stage ankle arthritis management in England.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: End-stage ankle arthritis is a debilitating condition presenting with pain and functional limitations. Surgical management typically involves ankle arthrodesis (AA) or total ankle replacement (TAR). This study aimed to investigate demographic, socioeconomic, and clinical factors associated with receiving TAR versus AA in England.

METHODS: A retrospective cohort analysis was conducted using Hospital Episode Statistics (HES) data for all elective AAs and TARs performed in England between April 2013 and March 2025. Patients aged 17 years and over were included. Multivariable logistic regression was used to assess associations between procedure type and patient-level factors.

RESULTS: A total of 26,331 procedures were identified, comprising 8836 (33.6%) TARs and 17,495 (66.4%) AAs. Older age and female sex were independently associated with increased odds of TAR (age ≥80 years relative to 17-29 years: odds ratio (OR) 12.89, 95% confidence interval (CI) 9.86-17.29; female sex: OR = 1.46, 95% CI 1.36-1.56). Relative to no frailty, mild and moderate frailty increased the likelihood of TAR, whereas severe frailty reduced it (OR 0.51, 95% CI 0.37-0.71). Patients from less deprived areas were more likely to receive TAR (IMD 5th quintile relative to 1st quintile OR 1.40, 95% CI 1.25-1.58). Compared with White patients, those of Asian ethnicity were less likely to undergo TAR.

CONCLUSION: Older age, female sex, lower deprivation, and mild-to-moderate frailty are associated with higher odds of TAR, while Asian ethnicity, higher deprivation and severe frailty are associated with reduced likelihood. These findings likely highlight patterns in clinical decision making, but may also suggest possible variation in access to ankle arthroplasty.

articles.title: Incision and Drainage of Acute Paronychia in the Emergency Department.
articles.abstract: Paronychia is a common emergency department presentation, representing up to 35% of hand infections. Standard of care involves incision and drainage, with systemic antibiotic therapy dependent upon the severity of the presentation. The treating emergency nurse practitioner (ENP) should consider factors that may impact wound healing, medications, comorbidities, and perform a thorough history and physical examination to properly address this common infection. This article describes a case of a 43-year-old female with about four weeks of gradually developing paronychia that presented to a community emergency department (ED) for treatment. This article will review the patient's case, including history and management to increase the skills of Emergency Advanced Practice Registered Nurses.

articles.title: Variability and Misalignment in Pre-Clinical Veterinary Microbiology Education: Implications for Competency-Based Training.
articles.abstract: Microbiology is fundamental to veterinary medicine, providing the scientific basis for infectious disease diagnosis, antimicrobial stewardship, vaccination, bio-security, zoonotic disease management, and public health. Despite its importance, little information exists regarding how pre-clinical veterinary microbiology is taught or how curricular content aligns with competency-based veterinary education (CBVE). A survey conducted in collaboration with the American Association of Veterinary Medical Colleges (AAVMC) examined curricular structure, faculty composition, instructional methods, and conceptual priorities among accredited veterinary colleges in North America and Europe. Responses from 24 institutions and reviews of 24 course syllabi revealed substantial variability in disciplinary organization, instructional approaches, faculty expertise, and assessment practices. Most programs delivered microbiology through discipline-specific courses and relied primarily on lecture-based instruction. Learning objectives were common, but explicit competency statements and mapping to CBVE competencies were rare. These findings suggest a disconnect between traditional microbiology curricula and emerging competency-based educational frameworks. Development of discipline-specific competencies, systematic curriculum mapping, and greater integration of foundational sciences with clinical training may improve alignment between microbiology education and professional outcomes.

articles.title: Diabetes and work participation at older ages: evidence from the HEAF cohort.
articles.journal: Journal of occupational and environmental medicine
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To examine associations between diabetes and work participation in adults aged 50-64 years, by treatment regimen.

METHODS: Diabetes of all types was ascertained through Clinical Practice Research Datalink linkage in the Health and Employment After Fifty cohort and categorised by treatment (no glucose-lowering medication, oral medication, insulin). Health-related job loss (HRJL) and prolonged sickness absence over nine years were examined among 4,813 employed adults using mixed-effects logistic regression.

RESULTS: Compared with no diabetes, diabetes treated with oral glucose-lowering medication (OR 1.89, 95%CI 1.26-2.82) and insulin (OR 3.07, 95%CI 1.83-5.15) was associated with HRJL. No treatment category was associated with prolonged sickness absence.

CONCLUSIONS: Diabetes at older ages is associated with HRJL, most strongly among those on insulin. Treatment regimen likely marks disease severity and self-management burden rather than itself increasing risk.

articles.title: Treatment variability among people assigned male at birth with repeat positive Mycoplasma genitalium tests: a case series.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mycoplasma genitalium (MG) can cause nongonococcal urethritis (NGU) and symptomatic proctitis. Rising antimicrobial resistance and lack of clinically available molecular resistance assays make MG treatment challenging. This study adds systematic data on the effectiveness of alternative MG regimens.

METHODS: Adult natal male patients who attended a public Sexual Health Clinic (SHC) and had ≥2 positive MG nucleic acid amplification tests within any 6-month period from January 2023-September 2025 were included. We classified cases as persistent infection or reinfection using clinical, demographic and self-reported behavioral data. For each patient, we summarized total number of visits, number, duration and components of each antibiotic regimen, and outcomes by MG clinical syndrome and infection status (persistence vs reinfection).

RESULTS: Among 3,009 SHC patients, 400 (13%) had incident MG and 19 (4.8%) met inclusion criteria for repeat MG infection across 61 clinic visits. Nongonococcal urethritis (n=14/19 patients, 74%) and proctitis (n=2/19 patients, 10%) were the most prevalent syndromes. Suspected reinfection was common (40%). All 19 patients achieved cure, including 10 (53%) with microbiologic and 9 (47%) with presumed clinical cure, after treatment for a mean of 18-49 days with between 1-9 antibiotic regimens. Eight (53%) patients were cured with doxycycline plus moxifloxacin, two (100%) with doxycycline plus pristinamycin, three (75%) with minocycline alone, and three (75%) with prolonged minocycline plus tinidazole treatment.

CONCLUSIONS: Despite frequent reinfection, most repeat positive tests represented persistent MG infections. All cases achieved cure after initial treatment failure, but many required multiple regimens over several weeks.

articles.title: Failure to Prevent Heart Failure is not a Failure -A Heart Failure Prevention Service facilitates early heart failure diagnosis.
Promoting High-Quality, Accessible Cancer Care for People With Disabilities.
articles.abstract: People with disabilities (PWD) face numerous challenges throughout the continuum of cancer care. Many of these are due to personal and structural biases that have historically made it more difficult for PWD to access oncologic care and which can be dehumanizing. We provide a narrative review of these challenges, starting with a review of disability statistics and methodologic considerations when reviewing the epidemiology of disability. We then discuss historic legal frameworks designed to support PWD, and barriers to oncology care faced by PWD, organized around the following primary topics: (1) biases faced by PWD from health care professionals, (2) screening, (3) diagnosis, (4) treatment, (5) survivorship, and (6) historical exclusion from oncology research. We conclude by identifying key areas that must be addressed to provide high-quality oncologic care for PWD. A variety of suggestions for addressing these issues are presented, including additional education of oncology providers, rethinking performance status, engaging stakeholders in the disability community, improving enrollment in clinical trials for PWD, and collecting consistent disability-related data.

articles.title: The Effect of Stimulus Polarity on Auditory Brainstem Responses Elicited by Level-Specific CE-Chirp in Young Adults With Normal Hearing.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: This study investigated the effect of stimulus polarity on the auditory brainstem response (ABR) elicited by level-specific Claus Elberling Chirp (LS CE-Chirp) stimuli in young adults with normal hearing.

METHOD: Thirty-one healthy participants (23 females, eight males; Mage = 20.6 ± 1.4 years; range: 18-25 years) underwent LS CE-Chirp ABR recordings at 70 dB nHL using three polarities: rarefaction, condensation, and alternating. Right and left ear values were averaged per participant. Absolute latencies of Waves I, III, and V; interpeak latencies (IPLs) I-III, III-V, and I-V; and wave amplitudes were compared across polarities using the Friedman test, with Wilcoxon signed-ranks test post hoc comparisons and Bonferroni correction applied where warranted.

RESULTS: No statistically significant differences were observed among the three polarity conditions for any of the nine ABR parameters (all ps > .05). The largest Friedman statistics were obtained for Wave I latency (χ2 = 5.193, p = .075) and IPL III-V (χ2 = 5.600, p = .061), neither of which reached significance. Mean values were numerically similar across all polarity conditions.

CONCLUSIONS: Stimulus polarity does not exert a statistically significant or clinically meaningful influence on LS CE-Chirp ABR measures in young normal-hearing adults. The traveling-wave delay compensation inherent to the LS CE-Chirp stimulus appears to attenuate polarity-related phase sensitivity, suggesting that all three polarities are clinically equivalent under the conditions examined (70 dB nHL, young adults with normal hearing). Caution is warranted before extending this conclusion to other intensity levels or clinical populations.

CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Clinicians recording LS CE-Chirp ABR at suprathreshold levels may select any of the three standard polarities without compromising the validity or accuracy of measurements under the specific conditions described in this study. Consistent application of a single polarity within a laboratory setting is recommended to maintain comparability with internally established normative data.

articles.title: Anticipated Barriers and Facilitators to the Implementation of an AI Tool Advising on the Placement of Mitigation Strategies to Improve Air Quality in the Hospital Setting: Qualitative Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: AI is increasingly prevalent within health care; however, its implementation within the hospital setting may come with its own limitations, given the high-pressure and sensitive environment. Barriers and facilitators to the implementation of AI within hospitals have been largely explored quantitatively, and there is a scarcity of qualitative research on the implementation of AI tools to improve air quality.

OBJECTIVE: This study aims to qualitatively explore, through a normalization process theory (NPT) lens, the anticipated barriers and facilitators to the successful implementation of an AI tool to guide the placement of mitigation strategies to reduce airborne transmission of infections within the hospital setting. Specifically, we sought to (1) understand the day-to-day work of key hospital staff involved in reducing airborne transmission of infections, (2) identify potential barriers to the implementation of an AI tool to guide the placement of mitigation strategies in the hospital setting, and (3) recognize necessary conditions for the successful implementation of the AI tool within the hospital setting.

METHODS: We conducted ethnographic observations (n=4) and semistructured interviews (n=18) with hospital staff following preliminary one-on-one meetings and group discussions involving patients, members of the public, national leaders in ventilation working within academic and industry environments, and hospital staff (n=70). Data were collected between October 2025 and May 2026 in the United Kingdom. Interview transcripts, field notes, and summaries from preliminary wider engagement work activities were analyzed in NVivo (Lumivero; version 12) following codebook thematic analysis to facilitate confirmatory triangulation. Findings were organized according to the core constructs of NPT.

RESULTS: Hospital staff understanding of the AI tool and their preparedness to invest time in its implementation varied across those consulted. The anticipated work required by hospital staff to successfully implement the AI tool and its recommended mitigation strategies was identified as a significant challenge for its scalability. Differences in the ways of working among trusts and the competition for limited resources (collective action), and issues associated with hospitals' physical estate (coherence) were seen as particularly problematic. The need for local champions (cognitive participation) was raised as a facilitator, as well as expert validation and the assessment of the AI tool's effectiveness (reflexive monitoring).

CONCLUSIONS: This preimplementation study suggests that the successful implementation of an AI tool to improve air quality in the hospital setting depends not only on the effectiveness demonstrated by the AI tool but also on the way trial outcomes are conveyed to hospital staff. Hospital staff anticipate an initial resistance to the AI tool's implementation. Further, the impact of the AI tool and suggested mitigation strategies in workflows, costs, and staff and patient outcomes may be decisive.

articles.title: Tablet-Based Neurocognitive Tests for Ugandan Adolescents Living With HIV: Cross-Sectional Validation Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Adolescents living with perinatally acquired HIV (PHIV) remain at risk of neurocognitive difficulties, yet access to valid neurocognitive tests is limited in sub-Saharan Africa (SSA), where most of this population resides. Tests that can be administered by nonspecialist personnel are culturally and linguistically appropriate for SSA's diverse populations and are brief enough for routine use are needed to expand access, but few such tools exist.

OBJECTIVE: We adapted NeuroScreen, a brief tablet-based neurocognitive test battery, into Luganda and evaluated its validity and acceptability for use among Ugandan adolescents with PHIV.

METHODS: In this cross-sectional validation study, 100 Ugandan adolescents aged 11 to 20 years (50 with PHIV; 50 HIV-negative controls) completed the Luganda- or English-language NeuroScreen battery and a commonly used traditional test battery. Participants were recruited from an existing longitudinal cardiovascular cohort at the Joint Clinical Research Centre in Kampala, Uganda. We examined convergent validity with correlations between the 2 batteries' individual and global z-scores, known-groups validity with unadjusted and age-adjusted group comparisons, criterion validity by examining classification agreement between the 2 batteries quantified with Cohen κ, and acceptability through self-reported technology use and ease of use.

RESULTS: NeuroScreen and the traditional battery global z-scores were strongly correlated (r=0.75; P<.001). Correlations between tests assessing similar domains were generally small to moderate, and were strongest for processing speed, attention, and working memory. Adolescents with PHIV scored significantly lower than controls on global scores for both NeuroScreen (P=.008) and the traditional battery (P=.003), even after adjusting for age. Agreement between batteries in classifying participants ≤1 SD (κ=0.56) and ≤2 SD (κ=0.66) below the global z-score mean was moderate, with both batteries classifying more adolescents with PHIV than controls below these thresholds. Although fewer than half of participants (42/97, 43%) had previously used a tablet, most rated NeuroScreen as easy to use, and prior tablet experience was not independently associated with NeuroScreen performance after age adjustment.

CONCLUSIONS: The Luganda-adapted NeuroScreen demonstrated convergent, known-groups, and criterion validity in Ugandan adolescents with PHIV. By delivering automated administration, automated scoring, and standardized multimedia instructions in the local language on a portable tablet, NeuroScreen addresses several persistent barriers to neurocognitive assessment in low-resource settings, including shortages of specialist personnel, the time burden of traditional batteries, and the scarcity of culturally and linguistically appropriate tools. The NeuroScreen battery was found to be highly acceptable among adolescents with little or no prior tablet experience. These findings add to a growing body of evidence supporting tablet-based assessment as a practical and scalable mobile health approach to expanding access to neurocognitive testing. Future research should evaluate test-retest reliability, sensitivity to change over time, normative benchmarks, and implementation within real-world clinical workflows.

articles.title: Body Composition Assessment and Correlation to Metabolic Profile in Survivors of Childhood Brain Tumors.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Survivors of childhood brain tumors (CBT) are at increased risk for metabolic syndrome, contributing to long-term cardiometabolic morbidity. BMI may underestimate risk by failing to capture altered body composition in this population. More precise tools such as air displacement plethysmography (ADP) may improve early risk detection. This study aimed to identify ADP-derived markers of adiposity and characterize early metabolic abnormalities at the end of cancer therapy.

METHODS: This was a prospective, single-visit study enrolling pediatric survivors of high-grade CBT aged 2 to 21 years, off therapy for <5 years. Data included anthropometric measurements, metabolic markers (glucose, insulin, lipids, adiponectin, leptin, IL-6), and body composition (fat mass, fat-free mass, percent fat, measured by ADP). Descriptive statistics were used to summarize demographics and clinical characteristics, and categorical variables were presented as counts and percentages. Pearson correlation coefficients were calculated for log adiponectin versus percent body fat and BMI z-score.

RESULTS: Thirty survivors of CBT (n=30; age: 6 to 23 y) were evaluated a median of 0.3 years after treatment. Over half were normal weight (53%), and 47% were overweight or obese; 20% had hypertension and 23% had elevated waist circumference. Body composition (n=29) showed high adiposity, with a mean fat mass of 33% and 59% having elevated fat percentage. Metabolic assessment demonstrated early cardiometabolic dysfunction: insulin resistance and significant insulin resistance by HOMA-IR were seen in 50% and 33%, respectively, and lipid abnormalities and the metabolic syndrome were seen in 27% and 15%, respectively. Higher adiposity was associated with worse metabolic health, with greater fat mass percentage in insulin-resistant patients (P<0.01) and higher BMI z-score (P=0.02). Adiponectin was inversely correlated with fat mass% (r=-0.72), but not with BMI z-score.

CONCLUSION: Childhood brain tumor survivors demonstrated a high prevalence of metabolic abnormalities and excess adiposity shortly after therapy completion. BMI underestimated abnormal adiposity compared with ADP-derived body composition assessment, supporting the need for comprehensive metabolic screening and early intervention during survivorship.

articles.title: Incidence and Predictors of Symptomatic Thrombosis During Asparaginase-containing Therapy in Children With Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia: A Meta-analysis and Narrative Synthesis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Symptomatic thrombosis is a clinically important complication of asparaginase-containing therapy in children with acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL), but reported incidence and predictors vary across studies. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis to estimate its incidence and synthesize reported predictors.

METHODS: PubMed, Embase, Web of Science Core Collection, Scopus, and the Cochrane Library were searched from inception through April 15, 2026. Eligible studies enrolled patients aged ≤21 years with ALL receiving asparaginase-containing therapy and reported extractable incidence or predictor data for overall symptomatic thrombosis or symptomatic venous thromboembolism. Proportions were pooled after logit transformation using a random-effects model. Predictor data were synthesized narratively when quantitative pooling was inappropriate.

RESULTS: Twenty-three studies met the eligibility criteria; 15 studies involving 17,809 children and 655 events contributed to the incidence meta-analysis. The pooled incidence of symptomatic thrombosis was 5.6% (95% CI: 3.5%-9.0%), with substantial heterogeneity (I²=96.9%). Study-specific estimates ranged from ∼1% to 22.7%. Older age was the most consistently reported predictor; associations with inherited thrombophilia, non-O blood group, high-risk treatment status, and T-ALL phenotype were inconsistent across cohorts.

CONCLUSIONS: Symptomatic thrombosis affects ∼6% of children with ALL receiving asparaginase-containing therapy, although incidence varies considerably across studies. Older age was the most reproducible risk factor, whereas evidence for other predictors remains heterogeneous.

articles.title: Modified Free Functional Muscle Transfer for Thenar Reconstruction After High Pressure Injection Injuries: A Timing-Based Algorithm for the Plastic Surgeon.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: High-pressure injection injuries of the hand can cause deep tissue destruction despite a small entry wound. When the thenar region is involved, radical debridement may leave a combined defect involving skin, dead space, and intrinsic muscle loss. Conventional treatment usually focuses on infection control and soft-tissue coverage, whereas the restoration of active thumb abduction and opposition is less commonly addressed.

METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed 10 patients with thenar high-pressure injection injuries treated between March 2023 and April 2025. After staged debridement and infection control, reconstruction was performed using a composite free muscle-skin flap based on 1 or more muscle segments harvested from the superficial portion of the vastus lateralis. The surgical design emphasized preoperative ultrasonographic estimation of the thenar muscle defect, chimeric flap harvest, dead space filling, tension-adjusted muscle fixation, and neurovascular anastomosis. Postoperative outcomes were evaluated by flap survival, wound healing, sensory recovery, muscle strength, thumb abduction, musculoskeletal ultrasonography, and donor-site morbidity.

RESULTS: All flaps survived completely, and all wounds healed primarily. Follow-up ranged from 4 to 12 months, with a mean of 8 months. The reconstructed thenar region had a satisfactory contour and soft texture, and no secondary debulking was required. Protective sensation recovered in all patients, with static 2-point discrimination ranging from 7 to 10 mm. Thumb muscle strength recovered to M5 in 6 patients and M4 in 3 patients. According to thumb abduction and opposition assessment, 5 patients had excellent results, 4 had good results, and 1 had a fair result. Postoperative ultrasonography demonstrated contraction of the transferred muscle. No obvious donor-site complication or knee dysfunction was observed.

CONCLUSIONS: A modified free functional muscle transfer using the superficial portion of the vastus lateralis can provide simultaneous wound coverage, dead space obliteration, and dynamic thenar reconstruction after severe high-pressure injection injuries. This technique is not intended to replace established methods in all cases, but it may be useful when the thenar defect is contaminated, irregular, and associated with extensive intrinsic muscle loss.

articles.title: Microtia Reconstruction in Children Based on the Nagata Method: Modifications of Ear Framework Fabrication and Outcomes.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Microtia reconstruction using the Nagata technique is seldom offered to younger patients under 10 years, as there may not be enough cartilage for reconstruction. In this study, we present our 13-year experience of microtia reconstruction by using the modified Nagata method in patients aged ≤10 years.

METHODS: Technical modifications included a refinement to the first-stage framework fabrication, whereby the base frame was sufficiently broadened to accommodate the helical crus. Besides shaping the helix, the eighth costal cartilage was split into another 2 pieces, followed by a novel use of the inferior portion to create the antihelix-antitragus complex, and the thick C-shaped portion was used for a second-stage projection strut with the residual cartilage pieces. An alternative surgical technique using expanded polytetrafluoroethylene (e-PTFE) was introduced to the patients without cartilage leftovers during ear elevation.

RESULTS: Between 2012 and 2025, 255 ears were reconstructed in 242 patients aged 7 to 10 years using this technique. During more than 1 year of follow-up, 222 patients (91.7%) had satisfactory outcomes. Surgery-related complications (hematoma, infection, and skin necrosis) occurred in 9 ears (3.53%). Framework resorption by habitual compression with the affected ear was 2.75%.

CONCLUSIONS: Microtia reconstruction using the Nagata method in patients aged ≤10 years can be safe and successful. It should be considered as an option for growing microtia patients with relatively early reconstruction.

articles.title: Howell-Jolly Body-Like Inclusions in Neutrophils and Monocytes of a Preterm Neonate During Sepsis.
Genetics of Hearing Loss.
articles.abstract: Since 1995, advancements in human genetics have elucidated many of the causes of hearing loss. Currently, over 150 genes are identified as responsible for nonsyndromic sensorineural hearing loss, and more than 200 are linked to syndromic forms (for review, see Hereditary Hearing Loss Homepage, https://hereditaryhearingloss.org). Genetic epidemiology is better understood for congenital hearing loss than for progressive adult-onset forms. It is estimated that three-quarters of early-onset hearing loss has a genetic origin, the remaining causes being acquired (prenatal cytomegalovirus infection, meningitis, sound trauma, temporal bone injuries). This article is an update of the main etiologies in genetic hearing loss.

articles.title: Natural killer cell receptor signaling and activation depend on cell cycle stages.
articles.abstract: Natural Killer (NK) cells are lymphocytes of the innate immunity and provide key protection against infection and cancer. NK cells express a wide array of inhibitory and activating receptors on the cell surface including the activating receptor NKG2D. Receptor signaling in NK cells leads to rapid post-translational modification (e.g., phosphorylation) of sub-cellular signaling proteins within minutes of receptor stimulation that ultimately give rise to diverse effector functions including cell proliferation. Recent single-cell mass cytometry (i.e., CyTOF) experiments in macrophages showed variations of abundances of phosphorylated signaling proteins across cell cycle stages indicating a dependence of cell signaling kinetics on an order of magnitude slower kinetics (~ several hours) of cell cycle transitions. We investigated cell cycle dependence of NKG2D signaling kinetics in NK cells using longitudinal CyTOF measurements up to 256 minutes post stimulation performed on IL-2-treated NKG2D-stimulated primary human CD56dim NK cells. The CyTOF experiments revealed cell stage specific kinetics of signaling proteins such as pVav1, pErk, and pS6, with the degranulation marker CD107a showing its largest upregulation specifically in the G2 + M stage. We developed stochastic minimal computational models coupling signaling and cell cycle processes to investigate the effect of cell cycle transitions on NK cell receptor induced signaling kinetics. These models suggest that the observed cell stage specific NK cell receptor signaling kinetics arise due to active modulation of the receptor signaling kinetics by cell cycle progression. The framework can be extended to study the interplay between receptor signaling and cell cycle progression in other cell types.

articles.title: Forecasting of infectious disease epidemics in sexual networks using attenuated renewal processes.
articles.abstract: Forecasting emerging infectious disease outbreaks is particularly challenging for sexual networks of men who have sex with men (MSM), where transmission can be shaped by heterogeneous and overdispersed contact structures, mixing assortativity, and both one-time and recurrent partnerships. Using stochastic epidemic simulations on synthetic MSM networks and empirical mpox case data from major cities, we systematically evaluated five classes of short-term forecasting models, from random walk approaches to semi-mechanistic attenuated renewal processes. Model performance was assessed using the continuous ranked probability score (CRPS). Across both simulated and empirical epidemics in heterogeneous networks, renewal models attenuated by a reverse-sigmoid curve, to account for early depletion of highly-connected nodes, consistently outperformed alternatives, achieving more balanced and reliable forecasts. Our findings suggest a practical approach for robust forecasting in highly overdispersed networks, where distinguishing network effects from other factors remains challenging and usually requires additional data.

articles.title: Intracellular SCARB2 mimicry overcomes decoy failure to broadly inhibit enteroviruses.
articles.abstract: Enterovirus A71 (EV-A71) and coxsackievirus A16 (CV-A16) are leading causes of severe hand, foot, and mouth disease (HFMD) with high childhood mortality and no specific antiviral therapy. SCARB2 is the essential uncoating receptor, yet extracellular SCARB2-Fc decoys fail to block infection, representing a decade-old paradox in enterovirus therapeutics. Here, we overcome this limitation by engineering RMP(R8), a cell-penetrating SCARB2 mimetic peptide comprising the minimal VP2-binding domain (W146-K166) fused to an octa-arginine transporter. RMP(R8) shows potent antiviral activity (EC50 = 0.156 μg/mL), outstanding safety (selectivity index > 2003), and excellent aqueous solubility, a critical asset for clinical translation. It broadly inhibits genetically divergent EV-A71 isolates and CV-A16 in intestinal and neural cells by blocking viral entry. In a lethal neonatal mouse model, RMP(R8) increases survival against EV-A71 and CV-A16 challenge in vivo. Intracellular receptor mimicry thus establishes a generalizable strategy for viruses refractory to extracellular intervention. RMP(R8) is a promising clinical candidate to address the unmet need for targeted anti-enterovirus treatment, and our findings redefine how to drug virus-receptor interactions that act inside cells.

articles.title: Correction to: Standard-dose direct oral anticoagulants for Asian patients with atrial fibrillation: the definitive case from COMBINE AF.
Efficacy and Safety of Sublingual versus Subcutaneous Immunotherapy for Patients with Allergic Rhinitis with Asthma: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
articles.journal: International archives of allergy and immunology
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Allergic rhinitis (AR) and asthma are common chronic respiratory disorders that frequently coexist. Allergen immunotherapy (AIT) is a disease-modifying treatment; however, the comparative efficacy and safety of subcutaneous immunotherapy (SCIT) and sublingual immunotherapy (SLIT) remain uncertain in patients with concomitant AR and asthma.

METHODS: PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, Embase, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials were searched from inception to March 2026. Studies directly comparing SCIT and SLIT in patients with AR and concomitant asthma were eligible. Outcomes included symptom scores, medication use, reported asthma exacerbations or worsening events, visual analog scale (VAS) scores, immunological markers, and adverse events.

RESULTS: Nine studies were included in the systematic review, seven of which contributed to the meta-analysis. SLIT was associated with fewer reported asthma exacerbations or worsening events than SCIT (odds ratio [OR], 0.28; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.09-0.89; moderate-certainty evidence). SCIT was associated with greater improvement in VAS scores (mean difference [MD], 1.80; 95% CI, 0.82-2.78; low-certainty evidence). No statistically significant differences were observed in the total rhinitis symptom score (TRSS; MD, 0.44; 95% CI, -0.14 to 1.02; very-low-certainty evidence), total medication score (TMS; MD, -0.48; 95% CI, -1.12 to 0.16; low-certainty evidence), or total asthma symptom score (TASS; MD, -0.24; 95% CI, -1.03 to 0.55; very-low-certainty evidence). No statistically significant differences were found in systemic reactions (OR, 0.28; 95% CI, 0.05-1.43), skin reactions (OR, 0.72; 95% CI, 0.41-1.28), nausea or vomiting (OR, 1.25; 95% CI, 0.23-6.94), or withdrawal rates (OR, 0.72; 95% CI, 0.21-2.51).

CONCLUSION: Limited comparative evidence suggests that SLIT may be associated with fewer reported asthma-worsening events than SCIT, whereas SCIT may be associated with greater improvement in VAS scores. However, these findings were based on a small number of clinically heterogeneous studies using nonstandardized outcome definitions. No clear differences were observed in rhinitis symptoms, medication use, asthma symptom scores, or most safety outcomes. Further high-quality head-to-head randomized controlled trials are needed.

articles.title: Changes in clinical management related to continuous versus routine EEG in critically ill adults: analysis of a randomized trial.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Continuous electroencephalogram (cEEG) is increasingly utilized in the intensive care unit for consciousness-impaired patients with various conditions. It is, however, costly in terms of technical and human resources, and its impact on prognosis compared with routine EEG (rEEG) remains debated. We aimed to characterize the effect of cEEG vs rEEG on clinical management modifications, and to determine if these correlated with a better outcome.

METHODS: This is an ancillary analysis using data of CERTA (NCT03129438), a randomized trial comparing cEEG versus repeated rEEG in critically ill adults with altered consciousness. Clinical management modifications due to the EEG intervention, pre-defined as performed within 60 hours of EEG start, were prospectively recorded (anti-seizure medication -ASM, sedation, new radiological examination, new surgical intervention, withdrawal of life sustaining therapy). Correlation with the EEG type were analyzed by 2x2 tables; Mantel-Haenszel tests explored the impact on mortality and functional outcome at 6 months.

RESULTS: The trial included 364 patients completing follow-up (182 each in the cEEG and rEEG groups). While 58.2% of cEEG and 45.6% of rEEG patients had any management change (p= 0.018), ASM were modified in 22.0% (cEEG) and 12.1% (rEEG) (p = 0.012)); other clinical interventions were comparable across EEG groups. Adjusting for ASM modifications, mortality (p=0.845) and functional outcome (p=0.619) remained similar between the EEG groups.

CONCLUSION: In critically ill adults, cEEG is associated with more clinical management modifications compared to repeated rEEG, particularly regarding ASM, but this does not seem to translate into improved patients' outcomes.

articles.title: Inborn Errors of Immunity in Neonatal and Pediatric Intensive Care Units: Clinical Spectrum and Diagnostic Outcomes.
articles.journal: International archives of allergy and immunology
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Inborn errors of immunity (IEI) may manifest with infections, immune dysregulation, syndromic features, and multisystem involvement. Critically ill neonates and children admitted to intensive care units (ICUs) with severe or atypical presentations may harbor underlying IEI, posing significant diagnostic challenges. This study aimed to evaluate the clinical characteristics, consultation indications, immunological findings, warning signs, and diagnostic outcomes of patients assessed for suspected IEI in neonatal and pediatric intensive care units.

METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed patients from the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) and pediatric intensive care unit (PICU) of our hospital who were referred to the Department of Pediatric Immunology and Allergy because of clinical and/or laboratory suspicion of IEI between January 2017 and September 2025. Consultation indications, final diagnoses, IEI categories, and traditional Jeffrey Modell Foundation (JMF) and additional warning signs were evaluated. The diagnostic performance of individual warning signs for confirmed IEI was assessed, and the incremental contribution of additional warning signs beyond the traditional JMF criteria was examined at the patient level.

RESULTS: A total of 172 patients were referred from the NICU and PICU, corresponding to 0.8% and 2.6% of all admissions, respectively; 40 (23.3%) were diagnosed with IEI. Syndromic features with systemic involvement were the most frequent indication for consultation in the NICU, whereas severe infection/sepsis predominated in the PICU. Combined immunodeficiencies with syndromic features were most frequent in the NICU, while predominantly antibody deficiencies were most common in the PICU. Deep-seated infection/septicemia, chronic diarrhea/enteropathy, and syndromic features were significantly associated with confirmed IEI, with ORs of 2.21 (95% CI, 1.08-4.53), 2.57 (95% CI, 1.08-6.07), and 2.41 (95% CI, 1.06-5.48), respectively. Overall, 38/40 (95.0%) patients with IEI fulfilled at least one traditional JMF warning sign. Both JMF-negative patients with IEI had at least one additional warning sign; therefore, considering traditional and additional warning signs together retrospectively identified all 40 patients with IEI in this referral cohort. Mortality among patients with IEI was 32.5%.

CONCLUSION: IEI was diagnosed in 23.3% of critically ill patients referred for immunological evaluation because of suspected IEI. Deep-seated infection/septicemia, chronic diarrhea/enteropathy, and syndromic features were significantly associated with confirmed IEI. Traditional JMF warning signs identified most patients with IEI; however, additional warning signs captured two IEI patients who did not fulfill any traditional JMF criteria. These findings support considering additional non-infectious and syndromic manifestations alongside traditional warning signs when evaluating critically ill children for IEI.

articles.title: Life-Threatening Ventricular Tachycardia and Transient Brugada-Like Electrocardiographic Abnormalities Caused by Severe Hyperkalemia Due to Urinary Retention in a 55-Year-Old Man.
articles.journal: The American journal of case reports
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND Hyperkalemia is a potentially fatal electrolyte disturbance that typically manifests as progressive conduction abnormalities, bradyarrhythmias, and sine-wave electrocardiographic changes. In rare cases, however, severe hyperkalemia also presents with malignant ventricular tachyarrhythmias and transient electrocardiographic abnormalities involving the right precordial leads, potentially leading to diagnostic confusion with primary arrhythmic disorders. CASE REPORT A 55-year-old man with no known cardiovascular disease presented with palpitations, dyspnea, and diaphoresis. Electrocardiography demonstrated sustained wide-QRS ventricular tachycardia accompanied by hemodynamic instability. Following electrical cardioversion, recurrent ventricular tachyarrhythmias occurred, requiring repeated defibrillation, cardiopulmonary resuscitation, intravenous amiodarone, and mechanical ventilation. Laboratory testing revealed severe hyperkalemia (7.6 mmol/L), profound metabolic acidosis (pH 7.059, HCO₃⁻ 13.8 mmol/L), and advanced renal dysfunction. Serum potassium was confirmed on repeat testing. Subsequent electrocardiography demonstrated marked QRS widening, terminal conduction delay, and transient right precordial ST-segment abnormalities involving leads V1-V2. Intravenous calcium gluconate and sodium bicarbonate rapidly improved the electrocardiographic abnormalities. Continuous hemodiafiltration and bladder catheterization were performed after postrenal acute kidney injury caused by urinary retention was identified. Correction of hyperkalemia together with treatment of metabolic acidosis resulted in complete resolution of the ventricular arrhythmias and electrocardiographic abnormalities without recurrence. No evidence of structural heart disease or persistent myocardial ischemia was identified during subsequent evaluation. CONCLUSIONS This case illustrates that severe hyperkalemia secondary to reversible postrenal acute kidney injury can simultaneously present with malignant ventricular tachyarrhythmia and transient electrocardiographic abnormalities. Recognition of this reversible metabolic condition is essential to avoid diagnostic error and facilitate prompt life-saving treatment.

articles.title: Bridging the Gap: Thrombolysis Access and Treatment Times Before and After Telestroke Implementation in Matão, Brazil.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Intravenous thrombolysis (IVT) rates for acute ischemic stroke (AIS) remain suboptimal in Brazil, largely due to limited access to specialized stroke teams. Telestroke (TS) has emerged as a potential strategy to overcome geographic and structural barriers to timely stroke care, particularly in countries with continental dimensions such as Brazil. However, robust evidence regarding the effectiveness and safety of telestroke in the country remains scarce. The primary aim was to compare access to IVT before and after the implementation of a mobile TS program in the municipality of Matão, São Paulo. Secondary objectives included comparing treatment metrics, safety outcomes-specifically, intracranial hemorrhage and mortality-and functional independence at 90 days.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective analysis of a prospectively collected stroke registry, using an uncontrolled before-and-after (pre/post-implementation) design at Carlos Fernando Malzoni Hospital (Matão-SP), including patients with confirmed AIS between September 1, 2016, and August 31, 2022. Patients were divided into two groups: pre-TS (36 months before implementation) and post-TS (36 months after implementation). The TS platform used was the JOIN® app (Allm Inc., Tokyo, Japan).

RESULTS: Of 379 patients diagnosed with AIS during the 72-month period, the mean age was 69.8 ± 13.6 years, and 59.1% were male. The most common risk factors were hypertension (76.8%), diabetes mellitus (38.5%), and smoking (26.1%). Although 65.4% of patients arrived within 4.5 hours from symptom onset, only 58 (15.3%) received IVT. Nevertheless, the number and proportion of patients receiving IVT increased from 11 (6.7%) in the pre-TS period to 47 (22.0%) in the post-TS period (p < 0.001). Among thrombolysed patients, median door-to-needle time was significantly reduced from 145.0 minutes (IQR 119.0-265.0) pre-TS to 92.0 minutes (IQR 66.0-129.0) post-TS (p = 0.004). There were no significant differences in symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage (p = 1.000), 90-day mortality (p = 0.729), or 90-day functional outcomes (p = 0.742). In multivariable analysis, post-TS period (OR 5.65; 95% CI 2.68-11.93; p < 0.001) and higher NIHSS score at admission (OR 1.05; 95% CI 1.02-1.08; p = 0.002) were independently associated with IVT.

CONCLUSION: In this single-center before-and-after study, implementation of a mobile telestroke program was associated with higher rates of intravenous thrombolysis and shorter treatment times. No statistically significant differences were observed in symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage, 90-day mortality, or functional outcomes. These findings support further evaluation of mobile telestroke strategies in low- and middle-income settings.

articles.title: Clinical Outcomes of Anomalous Aortic Origin of Right Coronary Artery from the Left Coronary Sinus.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Anomalous Aortic Origin of Right Coronary Artery (AAORCA) is a rare congenital anomaly that may be associated with adverse cardiac events, including sudden cardiac death. Surgical correction is commonly recommended in patients with AAORCA. Coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) is a prevalent diagnostic modality, which increases AAORCA detection. However, the clinical significance of incidentally detected AAORCA remains unclear.

METHODS: This non-randomized retrospective analysis included 10,134 patients who underwent CCTA between January 2014 and December 2022, either for suspected coronary artery disease (CAD) or a medical check-up. Three groups were created: patients with normal coronary anatomy (normal), with AAORCA (anomaly), and CAD without AAORCA (CAD). CAD was defined as a percentage diameter stenosis of ≥50% in one or more segments. Cardiac mortality was this study's primary endpoint.

RESULTS: Normal, anomaly, and CAD group comprised 7592 (74.9%), 66 (0.7%), and 2476 (24.4%) patients, respectively. During a median follow-up of 33.7 months (IQR: 13.2-53.4), Kaplan-Meier analysis revealed no significant difference in the cardiac death occurrence between the normal (15 events, 0.2%) and anomaly groups (0 events, 0%) (log-rank p=0.685). Cox proportional hazards model revealed no difference in mortality in the anomaly group compared with normal group.

CONCLUSIONS: In our cohort, incidentally detected AAORCA in adults did not demonstrate a clearly elevated cardiac death risk relative to CAD during mid-term follow-up. However, given the small number of events, these findings should be interpreted as descriptive rather than confirmatory evidence of a benign natural course, particularly in populations at higher risk of exertional sudden cardiac death.

articles.title: Specialist Palliative Care Nurses' Perspectives on Spirituality and Spiritual Care at End of Life - A Quantitative Study.
articles.journal: The American journal of hospice & palliative care
articles.abstract: BackgroundSpirituality is an important component of holistic palliative care, but challenges remain regarding its understanding and delivery. Limited quantitative evidence exists regarding specialist palliative care nurses' perspectives in specialist palliative care settings in the Republic of Ireland (ROI).ObjectivesTo explore specialist palliative care nurses' perspectives of spirituality and spiritual care at end of life and examine associated factors.DesignA descriptive correlational, cross-sectional survey design was used.Setting/SubjectsSpecialist palliative care nurses (SPCNs) from inpatient and community services were recruited using non-probability convenience sampling. Data from 123 completed responses were analysed.MeasurementsThe Spirituality and Spiritual Care Rating Scale (SSCRS) was used. Data were analysed using descriptive statistics and multiple regression analysis.ResultsParticipants demonstrated high endorsement of spirituality and spiritual care (median = 4.2, IQR = 0.61). No significant differences were identified between nurses working in inpatient or community settings (P = 1.00). Spiritual needs were most commonly recognised through direct interaction, observation, and listening rather than formal assessment tools. In addition, guidance to spiritual care came from personal and spiritual experience of SPCNs.ConclusionsSpecialist palliative care nurses strongly endorsed spirituality and spiritual care as important aspects of end-of-life practice. Findings suggest that explicit undergraduate education, together with personal and spiritual experience, may strengthen nurses' understanding of spiritual care and should remain a priority within specialist palliative care education.

articles.title: Opsonic Peptide MOP3 Attenuates Ischemic Acute Kidney Injury.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Renal ischemia/reperfusion (I/R) induced acute kidney injury (AKI) is a common and serious condition characterized by renal dysfunction, inflammation, tubular injury, and cell death. Extracellular cold-inducible RNA-binding protein (eCIRP) is a damage-associated molecular pattern that contributes to inflammation and tissue injury. MFG-E8-derived oligopeptide 3 (MOP3) is an opsonic peptide that binds eCIRP and promotes its phagocytic clearance. Here, we investigated the therapeutic effects of MOP3 in a murine model of renal I/R-induced AKI.

METHODS: Mice were subjected to 30 minutes of bilateral renal ischemia and treated with MOP3 or vehicle at the onset of reperfusion. Blood and kidney tissues were collected 20 h later. Renal inflammation, kidney function, tubular injury markers, histological damage, and cell death were assessed by RT-qPCR, biochemical assays, Western blotting, hematoxylin and eosin staining, and TUNEL staining.

RESULTS: MOP3 treatment reduced circulating eCIRP by 40% and renal IL-6, IL-1β, MIP-2, and KC mRNA expression by 43%, 84%, 73%, and 69%, respectively, compared with vehicle treatment. Serum urea nitrogen, creatinine, and NGAL levels were reduced by 56%, 63%, and 44%, respectively, after MOP3 treatment. MOP3 also decreased renal KIM-1 and NGAL mRNA expression by 88% and 44% and reduced their protein levels by 29% and 45%, respectively. Furthermore, MOP3 attenuated renal tubular injury and decreased TUNEL-positive cells.

CONCLUSIONS: These findings demonstrate that MOP3 attenuates inflammation, renal dysfunction, tubular injury, and cell death following renal I/R, suggesting that MOP3 may represent a promising therapeutic strategy for ischemic AKI.

articles.title: Premature menopause and risk of type 2 diabetes among postmenopausal women: findings from the Women's Health Initiative.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The association between premature menopause (age below 40 y) and subsequent risk of type 2 diabetes (T2D) is not fully understood. Sex hormone fluctuation due to ovarian function, hormone therapy (HT), and menopause-related changes in body composition may likely modify or mediate this relationship, which is the focus of this study.

METHODS: We included 136,759 postmenopausal women aged 50-70 years from the Women's Health Initiative. Menopausal age and type (natural vs. surgery-associated) were determined using self-reported reproductive history, surgeries, menopausal symptoms, and postmenopausal HT use. T2D incidence was determined through self-reported initiation of diabetes treatment. Multivariable Cox models assessed the association between premature menopause and T2D, adjusting for demographic, lifestyle, reproductive, and health-related factors. Interaction terms were used to evaluate effect modification by HT use. Mediation analysis quantified the contribution of body mass index (BMI) to this association.

RESULTS: Premature menopause (n=13,230; 9.7%) was associated with a higher risk of T2D compared with menopause at ages 50-54 (hazard ratio [HR]: 1.10; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.05-1.16). Among women with natural menopause, HT use modified the relationship between premature menopause and T2D (Pinteraction=0.047). Elevated risks were observed among women who never used HT (HR: 1.24; 95% CI: 1.08-1.42) or used estrogen plus progestogen (HR: 1.35; 95% CI: 1.09-1.68), but not among estrogen-only users. BMI mediated (indirect effect: 27.9%; 95% CI: 19.0%-45.8%) of the association.

CONCLUSIONS: Premature menopause was modestly associated with an increased T2D risk; this association varied by HT use and was partially mediated by BMI.

articles.title: Validation of the Klinrisk CKD Progression Model in the Dapagliflozin and Prevention of Adverse Outcomes in CKD (DAPA-CKD) Population.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Early identification and treatment of high-risk CKD can lower the risk of kidney failure and cardiovascular events. A laboratory-based machine-learning model (Klinrisk) was developed to predict the risk of CKD progression in adults with, or at risk for, CKD. It has shown good accuracy in the general population and in clinical trial populations with diabetic kidney disease, but its performance in non-diabetic CKD is unclear. We evaluated Klinrisk in a clinical trial of the sodium glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitor dapagliflozin in patients with CKD, with and without type 2 diabetes.

METHODS: We externally validated Klinrisk in the DAPA-CKD trial population for prediction of CKD progression (first occurrence of sustained ≥40% eGFR decline or kidney failure) up to 3 years. Performance was assessed with the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), Brier scores and calibration plots, and compared with Kidney Disease Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO) heat-map categories based on eGFR and urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio. Consistency of the dapagliflozin effect on CKD progression across Klinrisk risk categories was also examined.

RESULTS: The analysis included 4,304 DAPA-CKD participants, of whom 578 experienced CKD progression events over a median follow-up of 2.4 years. Klinrisk achieved an AUC of 0.79 (95% CI 0.77-0.81) and a Brier score of 0.10 (95% CI 0.09-0.11). It outperformed KDIGO heat-map categories in subgroups of patients with and without type 2 diabetes, and in those with IgA nephropathy. Dapagliflozin reduced CKD progression compared with placebo, irrespective of baseline risk.

CONCLUSIONS: In DAPA-CKD, Klinrisk accurately predicted CKD progression and outperformed KDIGO-based risk stratification in patients with and without type 2 diabetes. Eight of the 22 model inputs were unavailable and supplied from the development model rather than measured. Dapagliflozin reduced CKD progression across the full spectrum of predicted risk compared with placebo.

articles.title: Real-World Use and Outcomes of Post-Discharge Venous Thromboembolism Prophylaxis After Thoracic Cancer Operation.
articles.journal: Journal of the American College of Surgeons
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Post-discharge venous thromboembolism prophylaxis is conditionally recommended after thoracic cancer operation, but real-world use and associated outcomes across procedures and operative approaches remain poorly characterized.

STUDY DESIGN: We conducted a retrospective Epic Cosmos cohort study of adults undergoing lung or esophageal cancer resection from 2016-2025. Post-discharge prophylaxis was defined as prophylactic-dose anticoagulation prescribed within 7 days of discharge. Thirty-day outcomes were compared using 1:3 propensity-score matching stratified by procedure and operative approach.

RESULTS: Among 157,619 patients (14,277 esophagectomy; 143,342 lung resection), 11.15% and 1.48%, respectively, received post-discharge prophylaxis. After open esophagectomy, prophylaxis was associated with lower DVT (1.23% vs 2.63%; p=0.039), PE (0.46% vs 1.44%; p=0.047), and mortality (1.70% vs 5.20%; p<0.001), without significantly increased bleeding. Findings were similar after minimally invasive esophagectomy: DVT 0.32% vs 1.46% (p=0.003), PE 0.21% vs 0.89% (p=0.034), and mortality 1.28% vs 3.20% (p=0.003). After open lung resection, prophylaxis was associated with lower PE and mortality but higher bleeding and healthcare use. After minimally invasive lung resection, thromboembolic outcomes did not significantly differ, while bleeding and healthcare use were higher. Enoxaparin accounted for 79.35% of prophylaxis prescriptions; thromboembolic outcomes did not significantly differ between apixaban and enoxaparin.

CONCLUSIONS: Associations between post-discharge thromboprophylaxis and outcomes differed across thoracic procedures and operative approaches. Favorable associations after esophagectomy contrasted with less consistent lung resection findings, supporting prospective studies to define procedure- and risk-specific prophylaxis strategies.

articles.title: Wastage of injectable anticancer drugs in a public hospital chemotherapy compounding unit: A prospective descriptive study.
articles.journal: Journal of oncology pharmacy practice : official publication of the International Society of Oncology Pharmacy Practitioners
articles.abstract: IntroductionEvidence on cancer drug wastage comes largely from high-income countries and generally excludes the pediatric setting. This study quantified consumption, leftover reuse and wastage in a chemotherapy compounding unit of the Brazilian public health system.MethodsProspective, observational, descriptive study covering every compounding episode performed between October and December 2024 in a public hospital serving adult oncology and adult and pediatric onco-hematology.
