Of 32 formulary injectable cytotoxic drugs, the 29 with activity were analyzed by quantity and cost. The daily balance was classified as reusable leftover or wastage by a 24-h stability threshold. Relative wastage (quantity discarded divided by quantity compounded) was calculated per drug.Results1298 patients were treated in 2030 compounding episodes. Compounded doses totaled 612,192 mg or IU (BRL 657,724.73), of which 5.5% by quantity came from reused leftovers. Wastage reached 53,996.45 mg or IU (BRL 30,391.78; USD 5206.84), equivalent to 8.8% of the compounded quantity, 4.6% of its value and 13.9 mg or IU per patient treated per month. Fluorouracil led both compounded quantity (29.5%) and wastage (27.1%), yet relative wastage was highest in low-volume drugs with short stability: fludarabine (158.9%), etoposide (134.0%) and azacitidine (95.5%). Pegaspargase, used predominantly in children, combined 57.5% relative wastage with the largest discard cost (BRL 15,402.00). Pertuzumab, the costliest drug compounded, generated none.ConclusionsWastage concentrated in drugs with short stability and vial sizes poorly matched to prescribed doses, whereas the greatest financial impact fell on high unit-cost biologics. Relative wastage reveals intervention targets that absolute volume does not.

articles.title: The Easiest Decision in the Room: Continuous Renal Replacement Therapy in Cirrhosis.
Environmental Justice Index and 30-Day Wound Morbidity After Ventral Hernia Repair.
articles.journal: Journal of the American College of Surgeons
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Place-based vulnerability may contribute to wound morbidity after ventral hernia repair (VHR), but the relevance of multidomain Environmental Justice Index (EJI) rankings is uncertain. We evaluated associations between overall and module-specific EJI rankings and 30-day wound outcomes.

STUDY DESIGN: This retrospective cohort study included 35,626 patients undergoing clean VHR with hernia width ≤18 cm in the Abdominal Core Health Quality Collaborative. Parastomal hernias and repairs involving anterior component separation were excluded. Overall EJI and social, environmental, health, and climate module rankings were modeled per 0.1-point increase. Multivariable logistic regression with institution-clustered robust standard errors evaluated surgical site infection (SSI), surgical site occurrence (SSO), and SSO requiring procedural intervention (SSOPI), adjusting for patient, hernia, and operative characteristics.

RESULTS: SSI, SSO, and SSOPI occurred in 1.9%, 8.1%, and 1.8%, respectively. Overall EJI was associated with SSOPI (OR 1.05, 95% CI 1.01-1.09), but not SSI or SSO. Social vulnerability was associated with SSO (OR 1.06, 95% CI 1.02-1.10) and SSOPI (OR 1.09, 95% CI 1.05-1.14). Health vulnerability was associated with SSI (OR 1.03, 95% CI 1.00-1.07), whereas climate burden was inversely associated with SSI (OR 0.95, 95% CI 0.91-0.99). Highest-versus-lowest EJI stratum absolute risk differences were not statistically significant.

CONCLUSIONS: Social vulnerability demonstrated the most consistent association with wound morbidity after VHR. EJI may provide complementary contextual information for perioperative assessment, but modest absolute differences do not support its use as a standalone clinical decision tool.

articles.title: GC-MS-guided phytochemical profiling of Morus alba leaves identifies 5-O-methylnaringenin as a promising antidiabetic agent.
articles.journal: European journal of mass spectrometry (Chichester, England)
articles.abstract: Objective: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is a rapidly increasing metabolic disorder linked with cardiovascular, renal, and neurological complications. This study investigated the phytochemical composition, antioxidant, antimicrobial, and antidiabetic potential of methanolic leaf extract of Morus alba using in vitro and in silico approaches. Methods: Gas chromatography-mass spectrometry analysis of the methanolic extract identified 16 bioactive compounds, including 5-O-methylnaringenin 2TMS derivative and Benzenepropanoic acid derivatives. Antidiabetic activity was evaluated through α-amylase and α-glucosidase inhibition assays, while antioxidant activity was assessed using the DPPH assay. Antimicrobial activity was tested against Bacillus subtilis and Staphylococcus aureus. Molecular docking, molecular dynamics (MD) simulation, SwissADME, and ProTox-II analyses were also performed. All in vitro experiments were conducted in triplicate (n = 3), and data were analyzed using one-way analysis of variance followed by Tukey's multiple-comparison test, with p < .05 considered statistically significant. Results: The extract showed concentration-dependent inhibition of α-amylase (IC50 = 184.6 µg/mL) and α-glucosidase (IC50 = 112.3 µg/mL), with stronger inhibition of α-glucosidase. DPPH analysis confirmed antioxidant activity (IC50 = 230 µg/mL). Antimicrobial assays demonstrated inhibitory effects against both tested bacterial strains. Molecular docking identified 5-O-methylnaringenin as the most active compound with stable binding interactions at the α-glucosidase active site, supported by 100 ns MD simulation. SwissADME predicted favorable gastrointestinal absorption, blood-brain barrier permeability, and compliance with Lipinski's rules, while ProTox-II suggested no organ-specific toxicity. Conclusion: The findings indicate that M. alba leaves possess promising antidiabetic, antioxidant, and antimicrobial properties. Among the identified compounds, 5-O-methylnaringenin demonstrated strong therapeutic potential with favorable pharmacokinetic and safety characteristics, supporting further in vivo studies for T2DM management.

articles.title: Evaluation of Pediatric Cardiologists' Knowledge Levels Regarding Pulmonary Hypertension: Commonly Misunderstood Concepts.
articles.journal: Turk Kardiyoloji Dernegi arsivi : Turk Kardiyoloji Derneginin yayin organidir
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to identify common misconceptions regarding pulmonary hypertension (PH) among pediatric cardiologists.

METHOD: Before an online educational session on common misconceptions in PH, a 10-question test was administered to pediatric cardiologists across Türkiye via the Jotform platform. The questionnaire was developed following a pilot study in which an initial 20-question survey was administered to five experienced pediatric cardiologists. Based on their feedback, the 10 questions that best captured clinically relevant misconceptions were retained for the final instrument. The questions were prepared by an expert pediatric cardiologist and reviewed by two additional specialists. The test comprised multiple-choice, fill-in-the-blank, and true/false items covering the diagnostic criteria, treatment approaches, and pharmacological management of PH. Correct answer rates were calculated as percentages.

RESULTS: Sixty-six pediatric cardiologists participated, with an overall correct response rate of 43.6%. The most common misconceptions involved bosentan storage after reconstitution and the use of a three-stratum risk assessment model in pediatric PH. Nearly half of the participants incorrectly identified first-line therapy in vasoreactivity-positive IPAH/HPAH patients.

CONCLUSION: This study demonstrates that important concepts in pediatric PH management are not consistently understood among pediatric cardiologists. The identified knowledge gaps, particularly in pharmacology and risk assessment, highlight the need for targeted educational initiatives and regular updates on current guideline recommendations to promote more consistent clinical practice.

articles.title: Association of an Exploratory Iron Index Score With Observed NT-proBNP Trajectory in SGLT2-Treated Heart Failure and Clinical Outcomes in a Broader Cohort.
articles.journal: Turk Kardiyoloji Dernegi arsivi : Turk Kardiyoloji Derneginin yayin organidir
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Iron-related risk in heart failure is multidimensional, yet routine assessment still relies primarily on single laboratory-based definitions. This study evaluated whether an exploratory composite Iron Index Score was associated with the observed routine-care NT-proBNP trajectory after SGLT2 inhibitor therapy and with adverse clinical outcomes in a broader score-complete cohort.

METHODS: This retrospective real-world cohort study used a nested analytic design. The primary biomarker analysis included a final SGLT2-treated cohort with paired baseline and follow-up NT-proBNP measurements and complete score components (n=238). The supportive clinical analysis included a broader score-complete cohort regardless of SGLT2 use (n=472). The cohort predominantly comprised patients with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction. The Iron Index Score assigned 1 point each for transferrin saturation <20%, hemoglobin <12 g/dL, ferritin <100 ng/mL, albumin <3.5 g/dL, and red cell distribution width >14.5%. The primary outcome was the change in log-transformed NT-proBNP from baseline to the lowest recorded on-treatment value. Secondary analyses examined NT-proBNP response, heart failure hospitalization, and exploratory all-cause mortality.

RESULTS: In the final SGLT2-treated biomarker cohort, the adjusted ordinal score showed a directionally less favorable delta log NT-proBNP estimate but did not reach conventional statistical significance (beta 0.15, 95% CI -0.00 to 0.30; P=0.054). The high-risk group showed a stronger exploratory adverse signal compared with the low-risk group (beta 1.00, 95% CI 0.40 to 1.59; P<0.001). NT-proBNP responder status was not independently associated with score burden. In the broader score-complete cohort, higher score burden was associated with heart failure hospitalization in the unadjusted analysis, but this association was attenuated after adjustment (hazard ratio 1.04, 95% CI 0.85 to 1.27; P=0.690). All-cause mortality analyses were interpreted as exploratory because only 21 deaths occurred.

CONCLUSION: A higher exploratory Iron Index Score showed a hypothesis-generating signal toward a less favorable observed NT-proBNP trajectory in a predominantly HFrEF SGLT2-treated cohort. Broader cohort analyses showed supportive but less stable clinical outcome signals.

articles.title: Technical considerations in endovascular thrombectomy for distal vessel occlusions.
articles.journal: Interventional neuroradiology : journal of peritherapeutic neuroradiology, surgical procedures and related neurosciences
articles.abstract: The role of endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) in acute ischemic stroke due to distal vessel occlusions (DVOs) remains to be clarified. Anatomical complexities in the distal vasculature, such as tortuosity and vessel fragility, render technique selection particularly paramount during EVT. Herein, we present two illustrative cases of anatomically similar DVOs treated with two different techniques at a single institution to frame a discussion of important procedural considerations during EVT for DVO.

articles.title: Association of Noise Exposure, Perceived Noise Impact, and BMI on Nonalcoholic Fatty Liver Disease Among Chinese Seafarers: Nationwide Population-Based Survey.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Nonalcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) is a global public health challenge, yet its relationship between occupational noise exposure and perceived noise impact remains unclear.

OBJECTIVE: We characterized maritime noise exposure patterns and examined the associations of noise exposure, perceived noise impact, and BMI with NAFLD among seafarers.

METHODS: A population-based survey was conducted from March to May 2024 through the China Shipowners' Association. Participants completed a structured online questionnaire. Noise exposure was assessed via self-report, and NAFLD presence was determined by self-reported physician diagnoses based on the 2018 updated NAFLD guidelines.

RESULTS: A total of 8143 male seafarers was included, with an overall NAFLD prevalence of 18.5% (n=1503). The prevalence was significantly higher among seafarers with a BMI of 24.0 kg/m² or above (25.9%, n=1261), chronic noise exposure (19.4%, n=1293), and higher perceived noise impact (slightly: 16.9%, n=589; moderate: 19.1%, n=359; significant: 22.5%, n=511). Among seafarers with a BMI of 24.0 kg/m² or above, chronic noise exposure and higher perceived noise impact were significantly associated with an elevated risk of NAFLD. After full adjustment, the combined association of chronic noise exposure and higher perceived noise impact remained significantly associated with increased NAFLD risk, with consistent patterns observed across both workplace and rest area settings. A significant interaction was also observed between rest-area noise exposure and perceived noise impact in this BMI subgroup.

CONCLUSIONS: Noise exposure, perceived noise impact, and BMI were significantly associated with NAFLD among seafarers. These findings highlight the importance of optimizing occupational health benefits, especially among those with metabolic disorders.

articles.title: Reduced total arterial compliance in frail older adults is associated with orthostatic blood pressure variability but not baroreflex sensitivity.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Total arterial compliance (TAC) reflects arterial elasticity and may be associated with baroreflex sensitivity (BRS) and beat-by-beat blood pressure variability (BPV) during postural transitions. Frailty is also associated with impaired autonomic cardiovascular regulation, which may further compromise blood pressure control during orthostatic stress. However, these relationships have not been investigated in frail older adults. We hypothesized that frail participants would exhibit lower TAC than non-frail participants and that reduced TAC would be associated with impaired autonomic regulation.

METHODS: Community-dwelling older adults aged 60-79 years were classified as non-frail (n=28) or frail (n=22) using the Frailty Index. Participants completed sitting-to-standing and lying-to-standing transitions with continuous cardiovascular monitoring. TAC was estimated as the stroke volume-to-pulse pressure ratio, BRS using the sequence method, and BPV using frequency-domain analysis. General linear models compared TAC between groups. Correlation and regression analyses examined associations between TAC, BRS, and BPV, adjusting for frailty status and medication use.

RESULTS: Frail participants exhibited lower TAC than non-frail participants during both conditions (all p < 0.05). TAC was not associated with BRS during either orthostatic transition (both p > 0.05). In contrast, lower TAC was associated with greater systolic BPV during sitting-to-standing (SBPV-VLF: β = -0.46, p = 0.006) and lying-to-standing (SBPV-VLF: β = -0.60, p < 0.001; SBPV-LF: β = -0.56, p < 0.001; SBPV-HF: β = -0.32, p = 0.04).

CONCLUSIONS: These findings suggest that impaired arterial compliance contributes to orthostatic autonomic dysfunction in frail older adults primarily through reduced vascular buffering rather than impaired cardiovagal baroreflex function.

articles.title: Simplified bacterial identification and antimicrobial resistance detection in bacteraemia by on-chip multiplexed LAMP from blood cultures.
articles.abstract: Bacteraemia is a severe infection associated with high risks of complications and mortality. Diagnosis relies mainly on blood cultures, followed by culture-based methods, which remain the gold-standard but are time-consuming. Isothermal bacterial DNA amplification provides a rapid, reliable and cost-effective alternative for identifying and characterising bacteria directly from positive blood cultures, enabling a timelier diagnosis, particularly in resources-limited settings. However, routine implementation has been hindered by sample processing requirements and its limited multiplexing capacity. Here, we developed an on-chip loop-mediated isothermal amplification (LAMP) workflow, ALADIM (accessible and integrated LAMP analysis for multiplex detection of infectious agents in microfluidics), that integrates bacterial extraction and multiplex LAMP, followed by instrument-free amplicons detection using lateral flow immunoassay (LFIA), all within two hours (vs. 24-48 hours for the gold-standard). To demonstrate the capabilities of our device, we targeted the most common bacteria found in bacteraemia, E. coli, the co-amplification of two highly prevalent antimicrobial resistance genes, blaCTX-M-15 and blaOXA-48, and the detection of a positive control. Multiplex LAMP followed by LFIA detection was first evaluated using 14 strains cultured in LB. On-chip results were comparable to those obtained with our reference method (tube-based LAMP in a thermocycler followed by LFIA detection), showing 100% sensitivity, >84% specificity for the detection of malF and blaOXA-48, and 68% sensitivity, 83% specificity for blaCTX-M-15. As a proof of concept for the applicability of the complete ALADIM workflow, we analysed positive overnight blood cultures spiked with 15 strains resulting in 61 independent experiments (DNA extraction/amplification/LFA readout). In this complex matrix, ALADIM specificity remained above 77% for all targets, while sensitivity exceeded 94% for malF and blaOXA-48 but decreased to 56% for blaCTX-M-15. A similar decrease in overall sensitivity was observed for the in-tube method (>68%), highlighting the challenges associated with direct whole-blood analysis. This feasibility study shows the integration of multiplex DNA amplification, microfluidic processing, and LFIA detection in a single platform. Future work will focus on improving sample preparation, assay performance in complex matrices, and expanding multiplexing capabilities of ALADIM towards additional targets, to deliver a clinically reliable point-of-care testing device for low- and middle-income countries.

articles.title: Plasma testosterone heterogeneity reveals genetic and demographic determinants of donor health and red blood cell quality.
articles.abstract: Testosterone is a key determinant of red blood cell (RBC) biology and susceptibility to hemolysis; however, its contribution to donor-dependent variation in RBC quality and transfusion effectiveness remains unclear. Using data from 2,357 male participants in the NHLBI REDS-III RBC-Omics study, we quantified plasma total testosterone, free testosterone (bioavailable form), and androstenedione and evaluated their associations with donor characteristics, RBC hemolysis, and recipient post-transfusion hemoglobin increments, a clinical measure of RBC transfusion effectiveness. Subphysiological testosterone concentrations were common (~35%) and independently associated with increased storage and osmotic hemolysis. Frequent blood donations were independently associated with lower circulating free testosterone concentrations, even after adjustment for demographic and hematologic factors. Genome-wide association analyses identified loci associated with circulating testosterone, including regions near SHBG, TNFSF12, and the long noncoding RNA BALR6. Several testosterone variants were associated with RBC transfusion effectiveness. Specifically, variants associated with lower testosterone (e.g., TNFSF12) corresponded to higher post-transfusion hemoglobin increments (+9%), whereas BALR6 variants associated with higher testosterone were linked to reduced hemoglobin increments (-40%). In contrast, androstenedione-associated variants were not related to hemolysis or transfusion outcomes. Together, these findings demonstrate that genetic and physiologic variation in testosterone contributes to inter-individual variability in RBC quality and transfusion effectiveness.

articles.title: Interference-free detection of glucose in human urine based on a core-shell structured SERS nanoprobe.
articles.abstract: Non-invasive glucose monitoring plays a key role in the diagnosis and management of diabetes and related diseases. However, the application of conventional SERS glucose sensors in complex biofluids is often limited by spectral overlap between Raman signals from the reporter molecules and those of endogenous biomolecules. To overcome this issue, we developed a SERS nanoprobe capable of interference-free glucose detection. The probe comprises a gold-core silver-shell nanostructure (Au@Ag NPs), with 4-mercaptobenzonitrile (MBN) as the Raman reporter embedded between the core and the shell, and glucose oxidase (GOx) immobilized on the outer silver surface via electrostatic adsorption. Glucose is oxidized under GOx catalysis to generate H2O2, which etches the silver shell and consequently attenuates the SERS signal intensity. Accordingly, the intensity of the characteristic peak at 2226 cm-1 decreases as the glucose concentration increases from 0 to 2 mM, enabling quantitative detection. The excellent interference-free capability of the nanoprobe originates from two structural and molecular designs. First, MBN produces exclusive Raman signals within the biological Raman-silent window (1800-2800 cm-1), completely eliminating spectral overlap with endogenous biomolecules. Second, the core-shell structure physically isolates the internal Raman reporter from external biological matrices, effectively maintaining signal stability and accuracy. These design features endow the probe with outstanding selectivity for glucose over its structural analogues (e.g., fructose and lactose). The probe was further applied to glucose detection in human urine samples, supporting its potential utility in clinical urinalysis.

articles.title: Elevated lithium levels in drinking water are associated with higher prevalence of Wolff-Parkinson-White diagnoses.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Supraventricular tachycardia (SVT) and Wolff-Parkinson-White (WPW) are potentially highly symptomatic and, rarely, lethal arrhythmias associated with atrioventricular accessory pathways. While the etiology of accessory pathways remains largely unknown, they are frequently observed with Ebstein's Anomaly, a congenital heart disease associated with maternal medicinal lithium use. Therefore, we evaluated whether in utero exposure to lithium from environmental sources is associated with the prevalence of accessory pathways.

METHODS: We conducted a county-level ecological comparison of lithium levels in drinking water versus prevalence of WPW diagnoses among patients < 18-years-old in California using multivariable logistic regression. Children were analyzed given their high likelihood to reside in the same county during fetal development. WPW cases were identified using diagnostic codes. Positive and negative controls, including falsification endpoints, were analyzed.

RESULTS: Among 2,329,090 patients (mean age 8.2 ± 5.9 years, 47.8% female), 686 (0.03%) were diagnosed with WPW. Areas where lithium levels ≥ 75th percentile were associated with 71% greater odds of WPW (OR 1.71, 95% CI 1.44 to 2.03). Areas above the lithium health-based screening limit had 29% greater odds of WPW (OR 1.29, 95% CI 1.05 to 1.58). Similar results existed in a New York statewide cohort. In validation analyses, areas where lithium levels ≥ 75th percentile were associated with a higher prevalence of SVT, syncope, palpitations, and catheter ablation procedures.

CONCLUSIONS: Higher lithium levels in drinking water were associated with a greater prevalence of childhood-diagnosed WPW, implicating a potentially modifiable risk factor for the development of accessory pathways.

articles.title: Detection of serotonin and serotonin-related genes reveals unique roles in human intestinal epithelial development.
articles.abstract: Although 95% of serotonin in the human body is produced in the gastrointestinal tract, most prior research work has focused on the brain. Despite its abundance in the gut, serotonin's role in early intestinal development remains poorly understood. Here we show that serotonin is detected in both the small intestine and large intestine as early as 14 to 15 weeks gestational age. Using single-cell transcriptomics with histological validation, we generated a spatiotemporal atlas of serotonin and serotonin-related genes in the human gut from first trimester to late adulthood. The serotonin synthesis gene, TPH1, was exclusively expressed in enteroendocrine cells at all time points analyzed, with the highest expression in the second trimester. The serotonin reuptake gene, SLC6A4, was largely restricted to mature absorptive enterocytes and increased postnatally. Serotonin receptors also displayed distinct cellular and developmental expression patterns. HTR1E was confined to the first trimester during highly proliferative stage. HTR4 was enriched for in crypt regions, suggesting a role in proliferation for serotonin. Finally, HTR3E was associated with tuft cells throughout development. Together, these findings reveal the dynamic, cell-type-specific regulation of serotonin in the developing human gut, suggesting its importance in early intestinal development, and provide a framework to study its roles in intestinal development and diseases.

articles.title: Dark Urine After Nonfatal Drowning: Rhabdomyolysis-Associated Acute Kidney Injury and Freshwater Aspiration Pneumonia.
articles.abstract: Nonfatal drowning is managed primarily as a respiratory emergency, but clinically important kidney injury may be overlooked, particularly with delayed presentation. A previously healthy 53-y-old man fell into a freshwater pond that may have been contaminated by wastewater, struggled for ∼30 to 60 min, aspirated water, and presented 2 to 3 d later with fever, dyspnea, oliguria, and dark brown urine. Respiratory testing identified Aeromonas hydrophila complex and Escherichia coli, supporting drowning-associated pneumonia after freshwater aspiration. Serum creatinine was 986 μmol·L-1 (11.2 mg·dL-1), creatine kinase 79,765 U·L-1, and serum myoglobin 8630 ng·mL-1; urine was heme positive with few red blood cells. The patient had Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes stage 3 acute kidney injury requiring continuous renal replacement therapy followed by intermittent hemodialysis. Dialysis ended on Day 25, and kidney function normalized by Day 94. Delayed presentation, prolonged struggle, hypoxemia, oliguria, and dark urine should prompt targeted renal assessment after drowning. When drowning-associated pneumonia is evident clinically, respiratory sampling should guide antimicrobial treatment; renal replacement therapy should be used for standard severe acute kidney injury indications rather than myoglobin removal alone.

articles.title: Shark Bites in Florida Are Underreported: A Multi-Dataset Analysis.
articles.abstract: IntroductionThere is uncertainty about the number of shark bites on humans in Florida (FL).MethodsThe International Shark Attack File (ISAF) and Global Shark Attack File (GSAF) databases (2016-2024) were compared with the non-inpatient FL Ambulatory and Emergency Department Patient Data database (AHCA) (2018-2023) and the National Emergency Medical Services (EMS) Information System (NEMSIS) (2016-2024).ResultsBetween 2016-2024 there were 244 FL shark encounters reported in ISAF (mean 27.1 per year), 214 in GSAF (mean 23.8 per year), and 293 in a merged ISAF and GSAF (mean 32.6 per year). Between 2020-2023, there were 373 FL shark encounters reported in AHCA (mean 62.2 per year) compared with 114 encounters reported in NEMSIS (mean 22.8 per year) for 2020-2024. The rate ratio for AHCA FL shark encounters compared to the merged ISAF and GSAF was 1.91 (95% CI 1.64-2.23); p < .001. The percentage of shark encounters in Volusia County, FL, compared with all of FL shark encounters showed no significant differences between the ISAF and GSAF (40.2% and 33.6%, respectively) (p = .16) and between the AHCA and NEMSIS (7.2% and 7.5%, respectively) (p = 1.0). However, when comparing either ISAF or GSAF with either AHCA or NEMSIS, there were significant differences (p < .001 for all).DiscussionThe AHCA dataset identified about twice as many shark bites as either the ISAF or GSAF. Many FL shark encounters did not require EMS or admission to the hospital. The discrepancy in the number of shark encounters attributed to Volusia County, FL, varied based on the dataset being examined.

articles.title: Severe infections as collateral damage of decorative tattoos - A literature survey.
articles.abstract: Tattooing is an ancient decorative cosmetic procedure with increasing popularity, but regulations concerning professional including hygienic practice are limited. Although mild inflammatory responses due to infections, for instance, are known complications, severe sequelae are beyond consideration. Here we summarize 40 cases of invasive and systemic infections as collateral damages of decorative tattooing. Reports from 14 countries revealed that most patients were male, with a median age of 28.5 years including a 6-week-old infant. Cases were categorized into deep abscesses and cellulitis, infective endocarditis, necrotizing soft-tissue infection, toxic shock syndrome, sepsis, and others. Overall, Gram-positive bacteria including Staphylococcus aureus and streptococci dominated as infectious agents. Thirty out of 40 patients were considered immunocompetent, 23 required surgical interventions alongside antimicrobial therapy, and five cases were fatal. Severe complications occurred due to soft-tissue destruction near the tattoo, hematogenous seeding to distant sites such as the heart valves, and toxin-mediated systemic responses; unregulated inadequate hygienic practices were risk factors for such collateral damages. In conclusion, severe tattoo-associated infections are rare events but can be fatal even in immunocompetent individuals. In cases of otherwise unexplained soft-tissue, systemic, or cardiac valve infections a tattooing history should be considered even if the tattoo site looks uninflamed.

articles.title: Assessing musculoskeletal discomfort among head porters in open-air markets in Ibadan, Nigeria.
articles.abstract: BackgroundManual load-carrying remains common in developing countries and poses significant occupational health risks. However, integrated three-dimensional (frequency, severity, and interference)-based ergonomic assessment of the head porterage job is limited.ObjectiveThis study assesses the distribution of Musculoskeletal Discomfort (MSD) among head porters in selected open-air markets in Ibadan, Nigeria.MethodsA descriptive cross-sectional survey was done among 100 head-porters in Bodija, Oja-Oba, and Challenge markets using stratified and purposive sampling. Data were collected via an adapted Cornell Musculoskeletal Discomfort Questionnaire (CMDQ) and analysed by descriptive statistics. CMDQ scores for frequency, severity, and work interference were multiplied to obtain composite CMDQ index for each body region, while percentage CMDQ index (%CMDQ) was calculated to rank affected body regions. Data were analysed using chi-square tests and Spearman's rank correlation at a significance level of 0.05.ResultsMost participants were females (78.0%), aged 30-55 years (71.0%), and worked more than six hours per day (79.0%). MSD was widely reported across multiple body regions, with the lower back being the most affected, followed by the left thigh, right thigh, neck, and knees, with %CMDQ of 8.8, 7.8, 7.7, 7.6, and 7.2%, respectively. MSD frequently interfered with work performance and reduced job satisfaction. A weak, but statistically significant, positive correlation (r = 0.31, p < 0.05) was found between MSD severity and daily working hours.ConclusionsThe multidimensional approach provides a comparative empirical framework for prioritising MSD severity across body regions. The high ergonomic risk observed highlights urgent need for targeted interventions in the informal market environments.

articles.title: Risk Visualization With Petal-X and Continuous Glucose Monitoring to Support Person-Centered Care and Lifestyle Change in Cardiovascular Prevention: Qualitative Descriptive Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiovascular diseases (CVDs) remain a leading cause of morbidity and mortality. In primary prevention, effective communication of individual risk and support for behavior change are crucial. Interactive risk visualizations can enhance understanding and engagement, while continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) offers immediate feedback on the physiological effects of daily choices.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to explore how patients at increased CVD risk and family medicine nurses perceive CVD risk visualization (Petal-X) and the integration of real-time glucose monitoring, with a focus on perceived person-centered care (PCC), motivation, and lifestyle change. This manuscript reports the qualitative phase of a larger sequential mixed methods study; the quantitative randomized controlled trial is reported separately.

METHODS: Using total population (census) sampling within a closed, predefined trial cohort, we invited every eligible patient who had completed the intervention arm of a parallel randomized controlled trial and every eligible registered nurse providing preventive consultations at the same single community health center in central Slovenia who had been familiarized with the intervention and with the Petal-X dashboard; 6 patients at increased CVD risk who had used the Petal-X dashboard in combination with CGM, and 6 nurses familiar with the intervention, took part, and interviews were conducted between September and December 2024. Data were collected through individual, face-to-face semistructured interviews that explored perceptions of the visualization, real-time glucose monitoring, and lifestyle change. Interviews were audio-recorded, transcribed verbatim, and analyzed by inductive qualitative content analysis within a qualitative descriptive design; coding continued until code saturation and data adequacy were judged to have been reached.

RESULTS: The analysis produced 11 subcategories, which were grouped into 4 categories, with an overarching theme running across them: visualization and digital tools as support for PCC to enhance motivation and lifestyle change in individuals at risk of CVD. Patients and nurses reported that personalized visual displays improved understanding of risk factors, facilitated dialogue and shared decision-making, and increased patients' sense of involvement, responsibility, and control, although the 2 groups differed in emphasis: patients foregrounded personal meaning and self-regulation, whereas nurses foregrounded communication and fit with the consultation workflow. CGM was perceived as particularly motivating by linking behavior (food, activity, and stress) to real-time glucose changes, encouraging dietary and activity adjustments that some participants maintained after the intervention. Key barriers included variable digital literacy (especially among older users), fear or mistrust of technology, the attentional burden of continuous monitoring, potential information overload, workflow integration needs, and affordability or accessibility of CGM.

CONCLUSIONS: Interactive CVD risk visualization Petal-X, especially when complemented by CGM, was perceived as a meaningful support for PCC and a driver of motivation and lifestyle change in primary prevention. Implementation should address training, usability, integration into routine workflows, and equity of access.

articles.title: Noun vs. Verb processing in aphasia: new data from matched comprehension and production tasks.
articles.journal: Journal of clinical and experimental neuropsychology
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Existing studies in aphasia show conflicting results regarding the presence and the nature of differences between nouns and verbs across comprehension and production modalities. While studies generally report greater difficulty with verb production, the results are more mixed for comprehension tasks. In this study, for the first time, we directly compare noun and verb processing using fully balanced, parallel tasks for both comprehension and production in a large sample of Russian-speaking individuals with aphasia.

METHOD: We analyzed data from 156 individuals with post-stroke aphasia. Participants completed four tasks from the detailed language assessment tool in Russian (Russian Aphasia Test): noun comprehension, verb comprehension, object naming, and action naming. Tasks were carefully matched for key psycholinguistic variables, allowing for direct comparison of performance.

RESULTS: Participants performed significantly better on comprehension tasks than on production tasks. Crucially, across both modalities, nouns had higher accuracy than verbs. Error analysis revealed differing patterns: semantic paraphasias were more common in action naming, while phonological paraphasias predominated in object naming.

CONCLUSIONS: The results indicate that word production is more impaired than comprehension in individuals with aphasia, reflecting the greater demands of lexical retrieval relative to semantic recognition. Verbs were consistently more difficult than nouns across modalities, supporting a modality-general noun-verb dissociation. The greater difficulty associated with verbs likely stems from their increased grammatical and semantic complexity, as also evidenced by the higher rate of semantic errors in verb production. In all, these findings have significant implications for models of lexical processing and clinical assessments.

articles.title: Exercise improves heart failure by regulating cardiomyocyte autophagy via the ILF3/lncRNA NEAT1 axis.
articles.abstract: Heart failure (HF) is a common cardiovascular disease. It has been reported that the lncRNA NEAT1 is involved in the progression of HF and that exercise can regulate the expression of NEAT1 in muscle tissue. This study aimed to investigate whether exercise can influence HF progression by regulating NEAT1 expression and to elucidate its molecular mechanisms. Two independent rat HF models were established separately by intraperitoneal injection of isoproterenol hydrochloride (ISO) or by abdominal aortic constriction (AAC), whereas an in vitro HF model was induced by angiotensin II (Ang-II) in rat H9c2 cardiomyocytes. After 4 weeks of exercise training, serum NT-pro BNP levels were measured in the rats, and cardiac injury was assessed via HE staining and Masson staining. The expression of key genes and proteins was detected using RT‒qPCR, Western blotting, and immunofluorescence, and apoptosis was evaluated via TUNEL staining. RNA immunoprecipitation experiments were performed to validate the interaction between NEAT1 and ILF3. NEAT1 expression is upregulated in HF, and its knockdown can inhibit cellular damage in in vitro and in vivo HF models and improve cardiac function in rats. Additionally, exercise training reduces the expression of NEAT1 in the cardiac tissues of HF rats, and overexpression of NEAT1 weakens the inhibitory effect of exercise training on the progression of HF in rats, indicating that exercise training improves HF progression by suppressing NEAT1 expression. Mechanistic studies revealed that upregulated ILF3 in HF binds to NEAT1 to stabilize its expression, thereby activating the PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling pathway, which subsequently inhibits autophagy, ultimately leading to HF. Exercise training can downregulate NEAT1 expression, thereby suppressing abnormal activation of the PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling pathway and further relieving HF progression through the activation of autophagy. Additionally, NEAT1 expression is regulated by ILF3.

articles.title: CYP2U1: a cardiac metabolic switch alleviating obesity cardiomyopathy via lipid metabolic reprogramming.
articles.abstract: Cytochrome P450 2U1 (CYP2U1) modulates lipid metabolism, yet its role in obesity-induced cardiomyopathy remains unknown. Here, we demonstrate that cardiac-specific overexpression of CYP2U1 safeguards against high-fat diet (HFD)-induced myocardial dysfunction. Mice received tail-vein injection of adeno-associated virus serotype 9 (AAV9) carrying CYP2U1 under the cardiac troponin T promoter (AAV9-cTnT-CYP2U1) and were maintained on a 16-week HFD. Cardiac-specific CYP2U1 overexpression was associated with better preservation of systolic function and with reduced myocardial hypertrophy, interstitial fibrosis, and cardiac inflammation. By combining transcriptomics, untargeted metabolomics, and oxylipidomics, we identified two protective mechanisms. Transcriptomic analysis indicated that CYP2U1 attenuated multiple inflammatory cascades, including nuclear factor-κB (NF-κB) p65 phosphorylation and nuclear translocation, with a corresponding reduction in interleukin-6 (IL-6) transcription; CCAAT/enhancer-binding protein β (C/EBPβ) may contribute to this regulation. Metabolomic analysis suggested that CYP2U1 remodels polyunsaturated fatty acid metabolism, consistent with a "metabolic switch" that shifts the balance away from pro-inflammatory arachidonic acid-derived hydroxyeicosatetraenoic acids (HETEs) toward the docosahexaenoic acid (DHA) pathway, with increased levels of the protective lipid mediators 19,20-epoxydocosapentaenoic acid (19,20-EDP) and protectin DX (PDX). In vitro, CYP2U1 overexpression in palmitic acid-challenged H9C2 cells reproduced these anti-inflammatory and metabolic features. CYP2U1 therefore limits obesity-driven cardiac inflammation by coupling suppression of the NF-κB/C/EBPβ-IL-6 axis with a shift in lipid mediators toward DHA-derived specialized pro-resolving mediators. Whether targeted activation of CYP2U1 can be translated into a therapeutic strategy for obesity-associated cardiomyopathy warrants further investigation.

articles.title: Piperine enhances hyperthermia-induced apoptosis in AGS gastric cancer cells by increasing reactive oxygen species and attenuating heat-shock protein induction.
articles.abstract: Thermotherapy can potentiate anticancer activity, yet heat-induced stress adaptation-largely involving the HSF1-HSP axis-may limit its efficacy. Here, we investigated whether piperine acts as a thermosensitizer in AGS gastric cancer cells and explored associations with oxidative stress, apoptosis, and the heat-shock response. AGS cells were treated with piperine and subjected to mild hyperthermia (43 °C), followed by evaluation of viability, migration, colony formation, apoptosis, and cell-cycle distribution. Piperine enhanced hyperthermia-induced growth suppression, reduced scratch closure, and increased apoptotic cell death, accompanied by an increase in the sub-G1 populations. The combination elevated intracellular ROS, promoted caspase activation, and was associated with attenuation of pro-survival signaling. Piperine attenuated hyperthermia-induced HSP expression, most prominently HSP27 and HSP90, without reducing HSF1 or its activating phosphorylation. To extend these observations, we validated the cytotoxic and apoptotic phenotype in a second gastric cancer cell line, NCI-N87: piperine plus hyperthermia increased cleaved caspase-3, and NAC pretreatment partially attenuated this increase, supporting a contribution of oxidative stress to the apoptotic response, whereas the heat-shock protein response in NCI-N87 cells was not uniformly reproduced, indicating a cell-line-dependent pattern. Collectively, piperine enhanced hyperthermia-associated cytotoxicity and apoptosis in both gastric cancer cell models, whereas attenuation of HSP expression was more evident in AGS cells and was not uniformly reproduced in NCI-N87 cells, supporting further study as an adjunct strategy for hyperthermia-based anticancer approaches.

articles.title: Loss of UBE3C-mediated PIM2 ubiquitination drives Helicobacter pylori-induced gastritis via JAK2/STAT3 activation.
articles.abstract: Helicobacter pylori (H. pylori) infection is a major cause of chronic gastritis, yet its molecular mechanisms remain incompletely understood. In this study, we found that the proviral integration site for Moloney murine leukemia virus kinase 2 (PIM2) was significantly upregulated in H. pylori-infected gastric tissues and cells. Functionally, PIM2 knockdown not only attenuated inflammatory responses both in vivo and in vitro but also significantly reduced gastric H. pylori colonization in mice. Mechanistically, H. pylori infection downregulated the expression of the E3 ubiquitin ligase UBE3C, leading to decreased ubiquitination of PIM2 at K165 and enhanced PIM2 protein stability. Accumulated PIM2 subsequently activated the JAK2/STAT3 pathway, driving inflammatory responses. Combined treatment with the JAK1/2 inhibitor Ruxolitinib further potentiated the anti-inflammatory effects of PIM2 knockdown in H. pylori-infected GES-1 cells and mouse gastric tissues. This study revealed a novel mechanism by which H. pylori promoted gastritis through downregulation of UBE3C, impairment of PIM2 ubiquitination, and activation of the JAK2/STAT3 pathway. The dual benefits of PIM2 knockdown, suppressing inflammation while promoting bacterial clearance, positioned PIM2 as a potential therapeutic target for H. pylori-associated gastritis.

articles.title: A Spatial Machine Learning Approach for Analyzing Population-Level Factors Associated with Emergency Department Visits with Diabetes Diagnoses.
articles.journal: Journal of urban health : bulletin of the New York Academy of Medicine
articles.abstract: Emergency department (ED) visits for diabetes arise from complications related to both acute and chronic symptoms including, but not limited to, cardiovascular diseases, renal failure, neurological issues, and retinopathy. Research has shown that such complications disproportionately affect racial and ethnic minority populations. This is likely due to the complex pathogenesis of diabetes, which includes both individual-level factors such as race and family history and population-level drivers such as neighborhood walkability and access to healthy food outlets, which may be heavily influenced by residential segregation. We use spatial machine learning and statistical methods to estimate population-level factors associated with ED visits with diabetes diagnoses at the ZCTA level in Maryland as stratified by race and local measures of residential segregation. Using XGBoost and SHAP, we identified population-level factors associated with diabetes-coded ED visits and used logistic regression to estimate odds ratios. Our findings show that ED visits were associated with factors including housing vacancy, heavy traffic, greenspace, and health behaviors like physical leisure time and smoking across all subgroups. Further, we found that the factors associated with diabetes-coded ED visits differ across racial groups and across communities with different patterns of residential segregation. Heavy traffic, a proxy for traffic-related air pollution and barriers to walkability, was consistently linked to higher odds of diabetes-coded ED visits, especially among Black patients.

articles.title: Follow-up Outcomes of 100 Children with Frequently Relapsing and Steroid Dependent Nephrotic Syndrome Treated with Oral Cyclophosphamide: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: The primary objective was to estimate the proportion of children with frequently relapsing nephrotic syndrome (FRNS) and steroid-dependent nephrotic syndrome (SDNS) responding to oral cyclophosphamide, while secondary objectives were to document adverse effects, evaluate relapse-free survival following therapy, and assess outcomes at the last follow-up.

METHODS: In this retrospective cohort study, 100 children aged 1-18 years with FRNS or SDNS who received oral cyclophosphamide (cumulative dose ≤168 mg/kg) between 2010 and 2023 at a pediatric nephrology clinic were included. Demographic characteristics, previous treatments, adverse effects, and relapse patterns were retrieved from medical records. Response was defined as being relapse-free and off steroids for ≥6 months after completion of cyclophosphamide therapy, while sustained remission was defined as absence of relapse for ≥2 years.

RESULTS: The median (q1, q3) age at onset of nephrotic syndrome was 4 (2.5, 6) years, and oral cyclophosphamide was initiated at 8 (7, 10) years. The response rate to oral cyclophosphamide was 67%, with a median (q1, q3) relapse-free interval of 9.1 (3.9, 24.7) months. Adverse effects occurred in 28%, most commonly nail discoloration (28 cases), followed by transient leukopenia (4 cases). During follow-up, 56% required an alternative steroid-sparing agent. At a median (q1, q3) follow-up of 72.5 (25.5, 107.25) months, 28% achieved sustained remission, while 69% had infrequent relapses.

CONCLUSION: Oral cyclophosphamide is effective in children with FRNS and SDNS, inducing sustained remission in a significant proportion and suggesting a prolonged therapeutic effect. However, many children require additional immunosuppressive therapy during follow-up.

articles.title: Postoperative FIB-4 Trajectories by Biopsy-Confirmed Fibrosis Stage After Sleeve Gastrectomy: An Exploratory Biopsy-Based Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Whether advanced histological liver fibrosis limits postoperative improvement in fibrosis-related biomarkers after laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy (LSG) remains unclear. We evaluated the fibrosis-related biomarker dynamics using biopsy-confirmed staging.

METHODS: This retrospective study included 74 patients who had undergone LSG with intraoperative liver biopsy. Fibrosis was staged using the Brunt classification and patients were stratified into the F0-2 (n = 64) and F3-4 (n = 10) groups. Changes in the Fibrosis-4 (FIB-4) index from baseline to 1 year postoperatively were assessed. The proportion of patients with FIB-4 ≥ 1.3 was analyzed. An exploratory analysis of covariance was performed among 41 patients with baseline diabetes to identify predictors of 1-year FIB-4.

RESULTS: The baseline FIB-4 was significantly higher in the F3-4 than in the F0-2 group (median 1.593 vs. 0.847, p = 0.026). At 1 year, the FIB-4 values did not differ significantly between the two groups (0.853 vs. 0.857, p = 0.433). The proportion of patients with FIB-4 ≥ 1.3 decreased from 60 to 20% in the F3-4 group and from 12.5 to 7.8% in the F0-2 group. Postoperative %total weight loss (%TWL), diabetes remission, HbA1c, aspartate aminotransferase (AST), and alanine aminotransferase (ALT) levels did not differ between groups. In an exploratory multivariable analysis of 41 patients with baseline diabetes, baseline FIB-4 was significantly associated with 1-year FIB-4 (unstandardized β = 0.472, p < 0.001), whereas fibrosis stage was not statistically significant.

CONCLUSIONS: These findings suggest that favorable changes in fibrosis-related biomarkers may occur after LSG even among patients with histologically advanced fibrosis. However, these observations should be considered exploratory and require confirmation in larger cohorts.

KEY POINTS: • How severe liver fibrosis affects fibrosis-related risk after LSG remained unclear. • We evaluated the fibrosis-related biomarker dynamics using biopsy-confirmed staging. • The FIB-4 index decreased after LSG in patients with advanced fibrosis, and no significant difference in FIB-4 was detected between the fibrosis groups at 1 year. • The favorable changes in fibrosis-related risk markers may occur after LSG even among patients with histologically advanced fibrosis.

articles.title: Vidas en Contexto: Unpacking Social Determinants of Health and Related Health Outcomes among Puerto Ricans through a Person-Centered Approach.
articles.journal: Journal of racial and ethnic health disparities
articles.abstract: This study used a person-centered approach to uncover patterns of Social Determinants of Health (SDOH) among adults aged 18 and older residing in Puerto Rico. This research addresses a knowledge/population gap relating to the co-occurrence of SDOH among Puerto Ricans who may experience unique patterns of unmet social needs associated with the island's colonial status. Data were drawn from the 2023 Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System survey, which included respondents residing in Puerto Rico (n = 4,594), of whom the largest age group was aged 65 and older (26.9%). Latent class analyses uncovered SDOH clusters, while descriptive statistics identified various health outcome correlates. Model selection was based on relative fit indices, log likelihood test, entropy, and interpretability. SDOH was best represented by four latent classes: Low Material and Psychosocial Needs (n = 2,872), High Material Scarcity (n = 801), High Psychosocial Needs (n = 677), and High Material and Psychosocial Needs (n = 244). Demographic characteristics and health risk profiles also varied significantly across the four classes, with most social need classes exhibiting a higher risk for negative health outcomes in comparison to the Low Material and Psychosocial Needs class. Our findings provide insights into patterns of SDOH classes in this population that vary across classes and correspond with different burdens of chronic physical and behavioral health conditions. This work informs efforts targeting distinct patterns of social needs within Puerto Rico's colonial context that may enable precise allocation of resources, tailored screening, and structural intervention to alleviate health disparities.

articles.title: Dexamethasone-mediated modulation of the renin-angiotensin system: current insights.
articles.abstract: Dexamethasone (DEX) exerts pleiotropic effects that extend beyond classical glucocorticoid receptor signaling and include interactions with the renin-angiotensin system (RAS). Growing evidence indicates that DEX regulates both systemic and tissue-specific RAS activity through genomic and non-genomic mechanisms, affecting the expression and activity of key components, including angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE), angiotensin-converting enzyme 2 (ACE2), and angiotensin receptors AT1 and AT2. This mini-review summarizes current evidence on DEX-induced RAS modulation and its physiological and pathological implications. Depending on dose, duration, and biological context, DEX may exert both beneficial and adverse effects. Short-term exposure can suppress renin activity and aldosterone secretion and may provide protective effects in selected acute pathological conditions. In contrast, prolonged or high-dose treatment may promote hypertension, electrolyte imbalance, cardiac remodeling, and tissue dysfunction through dysregulation of RAS signaling. DEX also alters local RAS activity in bone, contributing to osteoporosis and osteonecrosis by enhancing osteoclast activity and impairing osteoblast function. In the kidney and lung, DEX-mediated RAS modulation affects fluid homeostasis, inflammatory responses, and susceptibility to tissue injury. Prenatal exposure to DEX may further induce long-term RAS programming, increasing the risk of cardiovascular, renal, and skeletal disorders in adulthood. Collectively, DEX-RAS interactions represent an important but often overlooked aspect of glucocorticoid pharmacology and may contribute to both the therapeutic and adverse effects of DEX.

articles.title: Modality mismatch or clinical blind spot? Methodological considerations in benchmarking large language models against human raters of PET/CT radiation-safety videos.
Fibro-Inflammatory Signaling, Fibrosis, and Microvascular Ischemia as Convergent Translational Substrates of Sudden Cardiac Death in Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy: A Systematic Review.
articles.abstract: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) remains an important cause of sudden cardiac death (SCD), but the biological determinants of ventricular arrhythmic vulnerability remain incompletely defined. This systematic translational review examined whether fibro-inflammatory signaling, fibrotic remodeling, and microvascular ischemia represent convergent components of the arrhythmogenic substrate in HCM. MEDLINE/PubMed, Embase, Web of Science Core Collection, and Cochrane Library were searched from inception to January 2026. Of 167 records, 37 full-text reports were assessed and 11 studies included. Fibrosis emerged as the most clinically mature substrate marker, while microvascular ischemia appeared to amplify electrical instability, particularly in remodeled myocardium. Molecular and tissue studies suggested upstream fibro-inflammatory programs involving activated fibroblasts, extracellular matrix dysregulation, SMAD/TGF-beta signaling, CRLF1/LIFR-JAK-STAT signaling, and altered multicellular communication. Overall, the evidence supports an integrated mechanism-to-substrate model, but prospective outcome-validated studies are needed before these biological layers can refine SCD risk stratification beyond established clinical and imaging markers in contemporary HCM practice.

articles.title: Metallothionein-Related Findings in Autism Spectrum Disorder: A Systematic Review and Targeted Quantitative Synthesis of Human Studies.
articles.abstract: Metallothioneins (MTs) are cysteine-rich proteins that regulate zinc (Zn) and copper (Cu) homeostasis, bind toxic metals, and contribute to redox control. Disturbed trace-element status, oxidative stress, gastrointestinal disease, and immune alterations have been reported in autism spectrum disorder (ASD), raising the question of whether MT biology is altered in this condition. Systematic searches of PubMed, Embase, Web of Science Core Collection, Scopus, Cochrane CENTRAL, and APA PsycINFO were updated on 5 September 2026. Studies directly measuring circulating MT protein, MT isoform mRNA, or anti-MT immunoglobulin G (IgG) antibodies in individuals with ASD, their first-degree relatives, or both were eligible. The review followed PRISMA 2020. Nine reports met the eligibility criteria, comprising eight primary reports and one secondary analysis. Study-level standardized mean differences, risk ratios, and odds ratios were calculated when sufficient published data were available. No pooled meta-analysis was performed because sufficiently comparable datasets were unavailable; otherwise, findings were synthesized narratively. Serum MT protein did not differ significantly between ASD and controls in one study, whereas one small, selected gastrointestinal cohort reported more participants above a study-defined high-MT threshold. In an uncontrolled Zn supplementation study, serum MT-1A increased together with higher serum Zn and lower Cu, but the absence of a concurrent control group precluded causal attribution. Five primary reports assessed MT gene expression, with higher, lower, null, and internally inconsistent findings across different MT isoforms and blood-derived samples; no reproducible ASD-associated transcriptional pattern was identified. Anti-MT antibody findings were also inconsistent across familial, gastrointestinal, and ASD-control comparisons. Across eight primary human reports, MT-related findings in ASD were inconsistent across cohorts, biological matrices, and clinical contexts. Current evidence does not establish a consistent ASD-associated alteration of the MT system, an ASD-specific anti-MT antibody response, or a validated MT biomarker. It also does not determine whether gastrointestinal phenotype, trace-element status, redox biology, immune-related factors, or other variables explain the observed between-study differences. Larger, independently replicated studies using standardized MT measurements and well-characterized populations are required.

articles.title: Pharmacological and Non-Pharmacological approaches to manage Tension-Type Headache: a Systematic Review.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Tension-Type Headaches (TTH), particularly in its chronic form, constitutes a persistent pain syndrome that can substantially impair physical, cognitive, emotional, and social functioning. Although this is the most common type of headache, there is a lack of clear consensus on the optimal long-term treatment strategy.

OBJECTIVES: A systematic review was conducted to evaluate the evidence for the effectiveness of pharmacological and non-pharmacological treatments in patients diagnosed with episodic or chronic TTH, focusing on improvements in headache pain and related clinical outcomes.

METHODS: A search across five electronic databases (PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, Cochrane CENTRAL, and PsycNET) was conducted to identify randomized clinical trials (RCTs). The review was registered in PROSPERO, followed PRISMA guidelines and used the Cochrane Risk of bias 2 tool. Due to significant clinical and methodological heterogeneity, a narrative synthesis was performed following the Synthesis Without Meta-analysis (SWiM) framework, and the certainty of evidence was appraised using the GRADE approach.

RESULTS AND CONCLUSIONS: Ninety-three RCTs were included, most of which had a moderate to low risk of bias. Based on the findings of this systematic review, the evidence suggests that pharmacological, manual, and behavioral therapies each have specific indications. These approaches can be combined in an individualized manner according to each patient's needs, with the aim of maximizing long-term symptom reduction, minimizing side effects, and ultimately improving quality of life in individuals with TTH.

articles.title: The use of capillary refill time In adult critically ill patients: a narrative review on potentials, pitfalls, and perspectives.
articles.journal: Journal of clinical monitoring and computing
articles.abstract: The evolution of Capillary refill time (CRT) use in clinical medicine is interesting, transforming a simple bedside observation into a reliable tool for assessing tissue perfusion in critically ill patients. When Henry Beecher and colleagues first systematized CRT measurement in 1947, they recognized its potential as a rapid method to evaluate circulatory status in trauma casualties, establishing a foundational framework that would influence intensive care practice for decades to come. However, clinicians soon discovered that relying on visual inspection alone introduced troubling variability between observers and even within the same observer's assessments, with expertise and training significantly influencing measurement accuracy. This recognition of CRT's limitations sparked a concerted effort to transform the measurement from a purely subjective exercise into a standardized, objective clinical tool. Researchers systematically refined protocols by establishing consistent pressure application techniques, standardized measurement sites, and defined normal thresholds (approximately 3 s for healthy adults). These methodological advances set the stage for rigorous clinical validation. Subsequent research revealed that CRT correlated powerfully with microvascular blood flow and independently predicted mortality and organ dysfunction in septic patients. Meta-analyses encompassing over 60,000 patients confirmed that abnormal CRT carried substantially elevated mortality risk, particularly when measured using standardized techniques. More recently, the ANDROMEDA-SHOCK trials demonstrated that CRT could serve not merely as a prognostic marker but as an actionable resuscitation target. CRT is nowadays considered an adjunct bedside marker to guide fluid and vasopressor resuscitation in adults with sepsis and septic shock, supporting individualized hemodynamic strategies while reducing over-resuscitation risks.

articles.title: Venetoclax combined with olverembatinib and prednisone as a frontline therapeutic strategy for Philadelphia chromosome-positive mixed-phenotype acute leukemia.
articles.abstract: Mixed-phenotype acute leukemia (MPAL) is a rare hematological malignancy with poor prognosis, for which there are currently no standardized therapeutic guidelines. Preclinical and clinical studies have shown that venetoclax and BCR::ABL1 tyrosine kinase inhibitors have synergistic effects on Philadelphia chromosome-positive (Ph +) leukemias. We retrospectively analyzed five patients with de novo Ph + MPAL who received venetoclax, olverembatinib, and prednisone (VOP) therapy. All patients achieved complete remission after the initial induction therapy and tested negative for measurable residual disease. During consolidation therapy, two patients developed severe myelosuppression and died of respiratory failure due to pulmonary infections. The remaining three patients underwent allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation and maintained durable complete molecular remission. These findings suggest that the VOP regimen may be effective in patients with Ph + MPAL. However, they also underscore the need to optimize venetoclax dosing during consolidation to reduce the risk of life-threatening myelosuppression and infectious complications.

articles.title: Opioid-free versus opioid-based anesthesia for robot-assisted radical prostatectomy: a single-center randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract: Multimodal, opioid-sparing analgesia is standard in urological surgery, and there is additional interest in eliminating intraoperative opioids in prostate cancer surgery. Randomized evidence for opioid-free anesthesia (OFA) in robot-assisted radical prostatectomy (RARP) is lacking. In this single-center randomized controlled trial, adult men undergoing RARP were allocated 1:1 to OFA (dexmedetomidine plus ketamine, no intraoperative opioids) or a remifentanil-based technique. Both groups received identical multimodal premedication, a bilateral quadratus lumborum block, sevoflurane maintenance and identical oxycodone patient-controlled analgesia (PCA). The primary outcome was cumulative PCA oxycodone consumption over the first 24 postoperative hours. Prespecified secondary outcomes were pain (NRS), postoperative nausea and vomiting (PONV), the demanded-to-delivered PCA bolus ratio, and perioperative changes in serum creatinine and white-cell count. A total of 149 patients were analyzed (OFA n=75, opioid-based n=74). Cumulative 24-h oxycodone consumption was lower with OFA (median 12.0 mg [interquartile range, IQR 6.0-22.0] vs 19.0 mg [10.5-34.0]; p=0.001), with a Hodges-Lehmann location-shift estimate of -6.0 mg (95% confidence interval, CI -10.0 to -2.0). Pain scores did not differ at any time point, and PONV was infrequent, with no significant between-group difference. Intraoperative hemodynamic adverse events (bradycardia, hypotension), perioperative white-cell count and serum creatinine did not differ between groups. In RARP delivered on a standardized multimodal and regional analgesic background, OFA reduced postoperative opioid consumption compared with a remifentanil-based technique, without a detectable difference in pain scores and with a similar safety profile.Trial registration ClinicalTrials.gov NCT06380244, registered 23 April 2024.

articles.title: Defining progression in erosive tooth wear: an interpretive challenge.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To critically evaluate current approaches to longitudinal erosive tooth wear (ETW) monitoring and examine whether quantitative intraoral scanner (IOS)-based measurements and conventional clinical indices can be meaningfully compared in defining progression.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: A systematic review identified longitudinal studies evaluating ETW using IOS-based quantitative approaches alongside conventional clinical assessment methods. MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched from database inception to January 2026, with grey literature sources also searched. The electronic database searches were updated in August 2026 using the original search strategies. Reference-list screening and forward citation tracking were undertaken alongside both the initial search and the updated search.

RESULTS: Five longitudinal studies met the eligibility criteria. IOS-based approaches consistently detected measurable surface change over time, including during relatively short follow-up intervals in which conventional clinical indices frequently demonstrated no categorical progression. Substantial heterogeneity existed in progression thresholds, outcome measures, superimposition methodologies, and reporting strategies. Agreement between IOS-derived measurements and conventional index scores was variable and generally weak to moderate. IOS quantifies continuous dimensional change, whereas clinical indices categorise severity using ordinal scales. No validated framework was identified linking quantified dimensional surface loss to clinically meaningful ETW progression.

CONCLUSIONS: Quantitative IOS measurements and conventional clinical indices assess different dimensions of tooth wear and cannot currently be interpreted as directly interchangeable measures of progression. Validated frameworks linking quantitative surface loss to biological and clinical relevance are required.

CLINICAL RELEVANCE: IOS enables high-resolution longitudinal quantification of tooth surface change, but the clinical significance of detected change remains uncertain. Establishing clinically meaningful progression thresholds is essential for integrating quantitative digital monitoring into routine care.

articles.title: Transcranial doppler ultrasonography in normal pressure hydrocephalus: a systematic review and exploratory meta-analysis of diagnostic, prognostic, and monitoring roles.
articles.abstract: Transcranial Doppler (TCD) ultrasonography provides noninvasive measurements of cerebral hemodynamics, but its clinical role in normal pressure hydrocephalus (NPH) remains uncertain. We reviewed its diagnostic, prognostic, and monitoring applications. Five databases were searched through June 10, 2025 for quantitative TCD studies in adults with suspected or confirmed NPH. Study-level eligibility and denominators were reconciled against full reports. Design-specific critical appraisal distinguished physiological association, treatment response, and diagnostic discrimination. Exploratory meta-analyses assessed paired three-month post-shunt changes using restricted maximum likelihood and modified Hartung-Knapp confidence intervals (CIs) for all outcomes. Sixteen direct TCD reports were retained. Potentially overlapping cohorts precluded a reliable total of unique patients. Two shunt studies contributed 21 paired participants. Pooled changes were - 0.14 for pulsatility index (PI; 95% CI - 0.49 to 0.21), - 2.29 cm/s for mean flow velocity (95% CI - 40.37 to 35.79), and 0.75 for Hedges-corrected standardized reactivity change (95% CI - 2.39 to 3.88). The conventional PI interval excluded zero ( - 0.20 to - 0.09), illustrating sensitivity to inference. Physiological associations, small response subgroups, and apparent waveform discrimination did not establish independent clinical utility. TCD can characterize cerebral hemodynamics in NPH, but current evidence does not establish diagnostic thresholds, independent prediction of shunt response, or validated surveillance criteria. Post-shunt physiological changes remain exploratory and do not demonstrate clinical benefit.

articles.title: Right Ventricular Function Assessed by Speckle Tracking Echocardiography in Patients Undergoing Transcatheter Pulmonary Valve Replacement.
articles.abstract: The effect of pulmonary valve replacement (PVR) on right ventricular (RV) function remains unclear. Cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) is the gold standard for RV assessment but has practical limitations. Speckle tracking echocardiography (STE) may offer an alternative for evaluating RV systolic function. This study used STE to assess changes in RV systolic strain and right atrial (RA) strain following PVR. STE parameters including RV free-wall longitudinal strain (RVFWSL), RV four-chamber strain (RV4CSL), regional basal, mid-ventricular, apical RV strain, RA reservoir and contraction strain were assessed in 50 patients who underwent TPVR at pre-, post-operative day 1 and at six-month follow-up. RV systolic strain significantly improved after TPVR. RVFWSL increased from - 20.3 ± 5.1% at baseline to - 23.3 ± 5.2% (P < 0.001), and RV4CSL improved from - 18.5 ± 4.1% to - 21.3 ± 4.1% (P < 0.001). Regional RV strain also significantly improved at the basal, mid-cavity and apical levels (- 18.1 ± 4.3% to - 21.4 ± 5.5%, P < 0.001). RA reservoir and contraction strain, did not change significantly. Patients with RV end-systolic volume index < 80 mL/m2 demonstrated greater improvement in RV4CSL than those with larger RV systolic volumes. Transcatheter PVR is associated with significant improvement in RV systolic strain at six months, with no significant change observed on postoperative day 1. This delayed recovery highlights the importance of longitudinal assessment, for which STE may serve as a feasible complementary tool to CMR in guiding follow-up imaging.

articles.title: Tailoring discharge planning after pediatric febrile urinary tract infection: a cohort study.
authors: CAKUT-UTI study group of the Italian Society of Pediatric Nephrology
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Febrile urinary tract infections (fUTIs) are a common cause of hospitalization in children and may recur in predisposed patients. Although current recommendations define indications for imaging and specialist referral, limited guidance is available to help hospital pediatricians identify, during hospitalization, children with clinical features associated with recurrent fUTI and tailor discharge planning accordingly. We conducted a retrospective, nationwide Italian cohort study including children aged 2 months to 3 years who were hospitalized for fUTI. Routinely collected clinical, laboratory, microbiological and imaging data were analyzed. Patients were stratified by sex and by the presence or absence of previously diagnosed congenital anomalies of the kidney and urinary tract (CAKUT). Adjusted multivariable logistic regression analyses were performed to identify factors associated with recurrent fUTIs. A total of 570 children were included, with a median age of 0.55 years. In the overall cohort, recurrent fUTIs were independently associated with older age, previously diagnosed CAKUT, acute kidney injury (AKI), and hydronephrosis with anterior-posterior diameter of the pelvis 5-15 mm. Among males with previously diagnosed CAKUT, recurrent fUTIs were independently associated with phimosis. Among males without previously diagnosed CAKUT, they were independently associated with AKI and non-E. coli infection. Among females, AKI was independently associated with recurrent fUTIs regardless of CAKUT status.

CONCLUSIONS: In children hospitalized for fUTIs, readily available clinical, laboratory, microbiological, and imaging findings are associated with recurrent fUTIs. Considering these elements during hospitalization may help hospital pediatricians identify children who may benefit from targeted interventions and tailored discharge planning.

WHAT IS KNOWN: • Current Italian recommendations provide guidance on imaging and specialist referral after pediatric febrile urinary tract infection (fUTI) but offer limited guidance for discharge planning. • Several clinical factors are associated with recurrent fUTI.

WHAT IS NEW: • In boys, recurrent fUTIs were independently associated with phimosis in those with known CAKUT and with AKI and non-E. coli infection in those without known CAKUT, whereas in girls AKI was the only independent factor regardless of CAKUT status. • These findings were translated into a practical framework to support tailored discharge planning for hospital pediatricians.

articles.title: Ultrasound-guided central venous access in the NICU: indications, insertion and management.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Ultrasound-guided cannulation of deep veins has advanced in little more than a decade from the operating room to the neonatal bedside and from a rescue maneuver to a planned procedure. Centrally inserted central catheters (CICCs) and femorally inserted central catheters (FICCs) are quite different from epicutaneo-cava catheters: they are 3-4 Fr power-injectable polyurethane catheters that are easy to tunnel, secured by subcutaneous anchorage, and suitable for blood transfusion, high-flow infusions, repeated blood sampling, and hemodynamic monitoring. This narrative review examines the indications, materials, insertion bundles for CICCs and FICCs in newborns, as well as their management, complications, and the training gap that now limits their diffusion more than any technical obstacle. In published studies, procedural success is 97-100%, immediate complications are absent or rare (when an insertion bundle is used), and the bloodstream infection rate is severalfold lower in infants below 1,500 g and below 1,000 g compared with the epicutaneo-cava catheter. Since the evidence comes mainly from a few high-volume centers with high procedural expertise, the priority for future research is to define strategies - structured programs, simulation, proctoring - to build and maintain the same level of competence in lower-volume units.

CONCLUSION: Though the supporting evidence is observational, Ultrasound-guided CICCs (or FICCs, if in selected cases) appear to be the most appropriate central venous access for the critically ill newborn.

WHAT IS KNOWN: • Ultrasound-guided CICCs and FICCs can be placed at the bedside in neonates, including extremely low birth weight infants, and outperform epicutaneo-cava catheters in safety, flow, dwell time, and range of use. • The adoption of insertion bundles reduces immediate and late complications of central venous catheterization in neonates and children.

WHAT IS NEW: • Multicenter and comparative neonatal data show reproducible procedural success across centers and several-fold lower bloodstream infection rates in the smallest infants, compared with epicutaneo-cava catheters. • The limiting factor is no longer technical feasibility but structured training; tunneling remains the most frequently omitted step in the insertion bundle and the least easily replaced.
