Of all first-line drugs evaluated, isoniazid showed the lowest concordance (94.4%) between phenotypic and genotypic methods. The isolates in this study harbor some mutations that are not currently documented in the WHO mutation catalog, indicating that these variants may be rare. The findings suggest that the prevalence of M. bovis infection in Canada is low with cases unlikely to be acquired through human-to-human transmission.IMPORTANCEIncidence of human infections due to Mycobacterium bovis in Canada is largely unknown as these data are not collected or annually published. This research is a first effort to identify historical M. bovis isolates that were available for culture, had drug susceptibility testing data, and were analyzed through whole-genome sequencing. The annual reporting of these data in Canada holds value.

articles.title: ZBP1 specifically binds pre-formed Z-RNA, limiting its potential pool of nucleic acid ligands compared to ADAR1.
articles.abstract: ZBP1 senses foreign nucleic acids in the unusual, left-handed Z-conformation via binding through its Zα1 and Zα2 domains and initiates cell death pathways that enable viral clearance. dsDNA and dsRNA can adopt Z-conformations; however, both typically require chemical modifications or protein binding to induce Z-form conversion and stabilization. ZBP1 has been previously shown to bind and convert B-DNA to the Z-conformation and was assumed to be able to convert A-RNA as well, despite the lack of experimental validation. Here, we use NMR and other biophysical and biochemical experiments to characterize the Z-DNA and Z-RNA binding properties of ZBP1's Zα1 and Zα2 domains. While ZBP1's Zα domains are able to convert and stabilize unmodified dsDNA in the Z-conformation, they are incapable of flipping unmodified (CpG)n repeat dsRNA. ZBP1's Zα domains require dsRNAs with Z-promoting chemical modifications to be able to bind and stabilize the Z-conformation. These results contrast with ADAR1's Zα domain, which can bind and flip both dsDNA and dsRNA into the Z-conformation, potentially indicating finely tuned competition between ADAR1 and ZBP1 for pro-survival and pro-death outcomes, respectively. This work highlights the functional variability of Zα domains and narrows down potential physiological substrates of ZBP1 in infection and disease.

articles.title: Association between the inferior vena cava collapsibility index and Fontan pressure in patients with Fontan physiology: a two-centre prospective pilot study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Patients with functional single ventricle anatomy undergo staged surgical palliation in early childhood culminating in the Fontan procedure whereby the inferior vena cava is connected to the pulmonary artery. Fontan circulation inherently requires elevated central venous pressure to maintain adequate pulmonary blood flow; however, excessive elevation is associated with morbidity and mortality. In adults, a key component of echocardiographic evaluation is the use of a "sniff test" as a surrogate of downstream right atrial pressure. This technique has not yet been validated as a measure of pressure assessment in patients with Fontan circulation.

METHODS: This was a two-center prospective study of patients with functional single ventricle physiology who had undergone the Fontan procedure and were undergoing previously scheduled transthoracic echocardiogram and cardiac catheterization as part of their standard clinical care. We correlated collapsibility index on echocardiogram with directly obtained Fontan pressure measurements from cardiac catheterization performed the same day.

RESULTS: 15 patients were enrolled and analyzed for the study. Collapsibility index demonstrated an inverse correlation with Fontan pressure, (Pearson r = -0.72, R2 = 0.51, p = 0.003). Collapsibility index was significantly higher for patients with non-elevated Fontan pressure (45% vs 30%, p = 0.0005). Using a collapsibility index threshold of 35.0% demonstrated a 100% positive predictive value for detecting elevated Fontan pressure (greater than 14 mmHg).

CONCLUSIONS: There was a significant inverse relationship between the collapsibility index and Fontan pressure. These findings may suggest a possible association between collapsibility index and Fontan pressure, warranting further investigation in larger studies.

articles.title: MRSA nasal PCR as a prevalence-dependent stewardship tool in hospitalized children: a structured review.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Empiric anti-methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) therapy is common in hospitalized children with severe pneumonia or suspected sepsis. MRSA nasal polymerase chain reaction (PCR) is increasingly used to support de-escalation, but its central metric, the negative predictive value (NPV), is often quoted without the prevalence on which it depends.

AREAS COVERED: PubMed, EMBASE, and the Cochrane Library were searched from January 2018 to April 2026. Twenty-seven sources were synthesized; the pediatric diagnostic-accuracy and stewardship studies and the in-window meta-analyses were appraised with QUADAS-2, EPOC, or AMSTAR-2. We examine why NPV is high in children, the prevalence above which a negative swab no longer rules out infection, performance by syndrome, and the pediatric implementation and cost literature, and propose a prevalence-conditioned framework for prospective evaluation.

EXPERT OPINION: The pediatric evidence is observational, and no study was designed to test whether PCR-guided de-escalation is safe. A negative swab is a defensible rule-out aid in severe or complicated pneumonia and selected low-prevalence intensive care sepsis, but not in skin, soft-tissue, or osteoarticular infection. Because NPV depends on prevalence, programs should measure the proportion of children with the target syndrome who have culture-confirmed MRSA infection locally before applying a published NPV.

articles.title: Shifts in Dermatology Outpatient Diagnostic Patterns Following a Major Earthquake: A Comparative Pre- and Post-Disaster Study.
articles.journal: Disaster medicine and public health preparedness
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare dermatologic outpatient diagnostic frequencies before and after the February 6, 2023 Hatay earthquake and to evaluate the implications of these temporal changes for disaster-responsive dermatologic care.

METHODS: This retrospective study compared tertiary-center dermatology outpatient diagnosis records from the pre-earthquake (February 6, 2021-February 3, 2023) and post-earthquake (May 11, 2023-February 6, 2025) periods. Diagnoses were classified into 18 categories and 69 ICD-10-coded subdiagnoses. Logistic regression adjusted for age, sex, and calendar month using patient-clustered robust standard errors; aORs with 95% CIs and FDR-adjusted q values were reported.

RESULTS: Among 41,012 diagnosis records, 19,646 were from the pre-earthquake period and 21,366 from the post-earthquake period. After adjustment, infestations/insect bites were more frequently represented in the post-earthquake diagnostic mix (aOR 2.55, q < 0.001). Dermatitis (aOR 1.17, q < 0.001), bacterial diseases (aOR 1.58, q < 0.001), environmentally induced diseases (aOR 1.51, q = 0.003), and sexually transmitted diseases (aOR 1.50, q < 0.001) were also more frequently represented. Acneiform disorders were less frequently represented (aOR 0.61, q < 0.001). Despite a crude increase, fungal infections did not differ significantly in the adjusted analysis (aOR 1.04, q = 0.149).

CONCLUSIONS: Post-earthquake records showed more infestations and selected infectious and environmentally related diagnoses, but lower representation of some chronic disorders. These clinic-based associations support dermatologic surveillance, infection control, and continuity of care in disaster planning without implying population-level prevalence changes or causal earthquake effects.

articles.title: Guideline directed medical therapy and decongestion in patients with acute heart failure.
Consistency of the effect of digoxin across clinical subgroups in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction: insights from the DIG trial.
The Polypill: The Unmet Need and Great Hope for Heart Failure Patients.
Identifying Potential Drug Targets for Treating ADHD From a Genetic Perspective: A Mendelian Randomization Study.
articles.journal: Twin research and human genetics : the official journal of the International Society for Twin Studies
articles.abstract: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) is a chronic neurodevelopmental disorder. Current pharmacological treatments have limitations, highlighting the need for new therapeutic targets. Using two-sample Mendelian randomization with cis-expression quantitative trait loci from the eQTLGen Consortium (31,684 individuals), we performed genomewide analysis against ADHD genomewide association study summary statistics from European ancestry (20,183 cases; 35,191 controls) and FinnGen R10 (2,788 cases; 405,153 controls). Genetic instruments were selected at p < 5 × 10-8 with F-statistic > 10 and linkage disequilibrium clumping (r2 < .001). Mendelian randomization estimates were derived using inverse-variance weighted, weighted-median, and Mendelian randomization-Egger methods, with leave-one-out sensitivity analysis. Colocalization was performed to distinguish causality from linkage disequilibrium. From 5430 genes with valid instruments, we identified 10 ADHD-associated genes (inverse-variance weighted p < .01, consistent direction across methods): four risk-increasing genes (RRAGD, DTX2, HMOX1, AGAP3) and six protective genes (NUCKS1, CPSF1, MAU2, CLDN5, CYP4F12, ATP6V1E2). MAU2 demonstrated strong colocalization support (posterior probability for hypothesis 4 > .6). Pathway enrichment highlighted mechanistic target of rapamycin signaling as a priority mechanism. Computational in silico drug prioritization nominated candidate compounds (e.g., selenium, ketoconazole) predicted to modulate these targets. This study identifies genetically supported therapeutic targets for ADHD. MAU2 emerged as the most promising causal locus. Rapamycin signaling represents a key mechanistic pathway. Several repositioned candidates (e.g., selenium, ketoconazole) warrant further experimental evaluation as potential leads. These findings provide a hypothesis-generating foundation for drug target prioritization, and require functional confirmation in CNS models and clinical validation before therapeutic relevance can be established.

articles.title: The Effectiveness of a Theory-Based Integrated Intervention on Medication Adherence Among Community-Dwelling Individuals With Schizophrenia: A Quasi-Experimental Study.
articles.journal: Journal of psychiatric and mental health nursing
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Medication nonadherence remains a major recovery barrier for community-dwelling individuals with schizophrenia.

AIM: To evaluate a theory-based integrated medication-adherence intervention.

METHOD: This quasi-experimental study included 75 participants (39 experimental and 36 control). Medication adherence (Medication Adherence Rating Scale, MARS), psychiatric symptoms (Brief Psychiatric Rating Scale, BPRS), medication adherence motivation (University of Rhode Island Change Assessment, URICA) and medication attitudes (Drug Attitude Inventory-10, DAI-10) were assessed at baseline, 12 and 24 weeks. Repeated-measures ANOVA examined Group × Time interactions, change-from-baseline interaction contrasts and timepoint-specific between-group differences; rehospitalisation was assessed from medical records.

RESULTS: Group × Time interactions were significant for MARS (p = 0.035, ηp 2 = 0.047), BPRS (p = 0.042, ηp 2 = 0.045), URICA (p = 0.003, ηp 2 = 0.087) and DAI-10 (p = 0.004, ηp 2 = 0.082). Between-group differences in change from baseline to Week 24 were significant for all outcomes, whereas from baseline to Week 12, a significant difference in change was observed only for DAI-10. At Week 24, between-group differences favoured the experimental group for MARS (1.186, 95% CI [0.261, 2.111]), URICA (1.507 [0.625, 2.389]) and DAI-10 (3.923 [1.743, 6.103]); the BPRS CI included zero. No rehospitalisations occurred.

DISCUSSION: The intervention was associated with favourable medication-related outcomes; adherence effects were modest, symptom findings less conclusive and the non-randomised design limits causal inference.

articles.title: Analysis of nontuberculous mycobacteria infection risks from CDC's water-related healthcare outbreak consultations, 2018-2024.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Nontuberculous mycobacteria (NTM) are commonly found in healthcare facility water systems and can lead to serious and difficult-to-treat infections. We analyzed Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) consultations of water-related healthcare-associated infections (HAI) investigations involving NTM.

DESIGN: Retrospective observational study.

METHODS: We searched CDC consultation records from January 1, 2018, through December 31, 2024, using water-related terms and organisms, excluding Legionella, to identify and review investigations involving potential or confirmed transmission of water-related organisms; we reviewed investigations that involved NTM.

RESULTS: Among 1,458 consultations, we identified 639 (43.8%) water-related investigations involving 4,685 patients and 60 different organisms. Investigations involving NTM accounted for 10.3% (n = 66) with 15 NTM species identified. Among NTM-related investigations, almost half involved M. abscessus (n = 31, 47.0%) and two-thirds (n = 44, 66.7%) involved extrapulmonary infections only. More than half of identified NTM investigations (n = 37, 56.1%) occurred in hospitals and over one-third (n = 23, 34.8%) in outpatient settings. Exposures to surgery (n = 27, 40.9%) and medical products (e.g., medical devices, medications, and biological products) (n = 35, 53.0%) were common.

CONCLUSIONS: Over this seven-year period, approximately one-tenth of CDC healthcare water-related consultations involved NTM. The majority involved extrapulmonary infections, with surgery and exposure to contaminated medical products representing the most common exposures of concern. These findings highlight the potential for NTM infections when water-related healthcare exposures occur. Healthcare facilities are encouraged to identify the potential for exposure to nonsterile water during surgery, during the use of medical devices, and during the preparation and administration of medications to reduce the risk from NTM.

articles.title: Healthcare-associated infections in Singapore's long-term acute care hospitals: results from the first national point prevalence survey.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: While healthcare-associated infection (HAI) surveillance in Singapore's acute care hospitals is well established, comparable data from long-term acute care hospitals (LTACHs), known as community hospitals, are limited. We conducted the first national point prevalence survey (PPS) to determine HAI prevalence in Singapore LTACHs.

METHODS: A standardized protocol adapted from the Singapore acute care hospital HAI PPS protocol, which was adapted from the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control protocol for acute care hospitals, was implemented across 9 LTACHs. Adult inpatients present in participating wards at 8 a.m. on the survey day were included. Data on patient characteristics, invasive devices, and active infections were collected from electronic medical records. Factors associated with HAIs were determined using multivariate logistic regression.

RESULTS: Among 1,546 patients, 86 had 94 HAIs, corresponding to a prevalence of 5.6% (95% confidence interval [CI]: 4.5-6.8). The most common infection types were unspecified sepsis (36.2%), urinary tract infection (UTI) (24.5%), and surgical site infection (18.1%). Microbiological confirmation was available for 25.5% of HAIs, with Enterobacterales (54.8%) most frequently identified. Presence of central vascular catheter (odds ratio [OR]: 3.88; 95% CI: 1.66-9.08) and peripheral vascular catheter (OR: 10.48; 95% CI: 6.45-17.03) were associated with HAIs, while larger hospital size (≥250 beds) was associated with reduced odds (OR: 0.62; 95% CI: 0.39-0.99).

CONCLUSION: This inaugural PPS establishes the baseline for HAIs in Singapore's LTACHs. Findings suggest broad infection prevention initiatives may provide the greatest benefit sector-wide, while the high UTI burden highlights an opportunity for targeted prevention strategies.

articles.title: Multidisciplinary Approach to Antiplatelet Management in Coronary Syndromes: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association.
authors: American Heart Association Clinical Pharmacology Committee of the Council of Clinical Cardiology; Council on Cardiovascular and Stroke Nursing; Council on Cardiovascular Surgery and Anesthesia; and Council on Genomic and Precision Medicine
articles.abstract: Antiplatelet therapy is a cornerstone of care for patients with acute coronary syndrome and chronic coronary disease, yet its optimal use requires careful balancing of thrombotic risk reduction with bleeding complications. Since the mid-2000s, advances in stent technology, antiplatelet pharmacotherapy, procedural technique, and risk stratification tools have led to increasingly individualized approaches to antiplatelet management. Current guidelines and evidence emphasize tailoring agent selection, intensity, and duration of therapy according to patient-, procedure-, and disease-specific factors rather than a uniform strategy. However, the growing complexity of evidence, frequent care transitions, social determinants of health, and variability in patient characteristics have increased the risk of inappropriate prescribing, nonadherence, and adverse outcomes. This scientific statement reviews contemporary evidence informing antiplatelet strategies and highlights the critical role of the multidisciplinary cardiovascular team (interventional cardiology, general cardiology, pharmacists, advanced practice nurses) and the importance of their collective expertise in ensuring antithrombotic stewardship in patients with acute coronary syndrome and chronic coronary disease.

articles.title: Dual Control of Low-Density Lipoprotein Cholesterol Levels by ANGPTL3 and ANGPTL8.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Inactivation of ANGPTL3 (angiopoietin-like protein 3; A3) is a proven therapeutic strategy for lowering plasma lipid levels independently of the low-density lipoprotein receptor, yet the optimal approach to inactivate A3 remains unclear. A3 is proteolytically cleaved and circulates as full-length, N-terminal, and C-terminal fragments. The specific contribution of each form of A3, and of its paralog, ANGPTL8 (angiopoietin-like protein 8; A8), in modulating circulating levels of ApoB (apolipoprotein B)-containing lipoproteins remain poorly defined. Clarifying these relationships will inform next-generation A3-directed therapies.

METHODS: We performed liver perfusion studies to directly compare the number and composition of very-low-density lipoprotein particles secreted from mice with and without A3. To amplify effects on cholesterol metabolism, we generated Ldlr-/- mice expressing wild-type A3, full-length A3, or N-terminal A3 fragments, with or without coexpression of A8, and analyzed plasma lipids, circulating A3 and A8 complexes, and intravascular lipase activities. Complementary in vitro assays and structural modeling were used to assess relative endothelial lipase inhibition by A3 alone or in complex with A8.

RESULTS: Liver perfusion studies revealed that A3 inactivation does not alter the rates of hepatic secretion of very-low-density lipoprotein in wild-type or Ldlr-/- mice. Inactivation of A8 alone lowered plasma low-density lipoprotein cholesterol levels by ≈20%, an effect dependent upon the expression of both endothelial lipase and A3. Maximal inhibition of lipoprotein lipase required coexpression of A8 plus both full-length A3 and N-terminal A3 fragments, indicating that A3 cleavage, in addition to A8 expression, is essential for maximal lipoprotein lipase inhibition. In contrast, A8 expression, but not A3 cleavage, was required for optimal endothelial lipase inhibition.

CONCLUSIONS: A8 acts in concert with A3 to differentially modulate lipoprotein lipase- and endothelial lipase-mediated lipolysis, which antagonizes hepatic clearance of newly secreted atherogenic ApoB-containing lipoproteins. This mechanistic framework refines our understanding of A3-targeted lipid lowering and highlights the therapeutic potential of dual A3- plus A8-directed strategies to treat dyslipidemia and prevent atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease.

articles.title: Thrombolysis in the Delayed Treatment Window for Acute Ischemic Stroke: Updated Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Intravenous thrombolysis is a standard treatment for acute ischemic stroke but has traditionally been limited to 4.5 hours after symptom onset. This time-based restriction may exclude patients with salvageable brain tissue, especially those with wake-up or unknown-onset strokes. Multimodal imaging allows for the identification of viable penumbra beyond traditional treatment windows. This study compiles randomized evidence evaluating intravenous thrombolysis in imaging-selected patients treated after 4.5 hours.

METHODS: We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis in accordance with Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses guidelines. PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane Central were searched through February 2026 for randomized trials comparing intravenous thrombolysis (alteplase or tenecteplase) with best medical therapy in patients presenting beyond 4.5 hours or with wake-up/unknown-onset stroke selected by imaging. The primary outcome was excellent functional outcome at 90 days (modified Rankin Scale score 0-1). Secondary outcomes included functional independence (modified Rankin Scale score 0-2), symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage, and 90-day mortality.

RESULTS: Fourteen trials involving 4192 participants were analyzed. Intravenous thrombolysis improved excellent functional outcomes (modified Rankin Scale score 0-1; risk ratio, 1.22 [95% CI, 1.16-1.29]) and functional independence (modified Rankin Scale score 0-2; risk ratio, 1.12 [95% CI, 1.06-1.18]). Both alteplase and tenecteplase contributed to these benefits. Thrombolysis increased the risk of symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage (risk ratio, 2.58 [95% CI, 1.58-4.22]) but did not significantly affect 90-day mortality (risk ratio, 1.15 [95% CI, 0.97-1.35]).

CONCLUSIONS: In patients selected using advanced imaging, intravenous thrombolysis performed after 4.5 hours improves functional outcomes without increasing mortality, supporting a tissue-based rather than strictly time-based approach to treating acute ischemic stroke.

articles.title: Bleeding With Asundexian Versus Placebo in Patients With Noncardioembolic Ischemic Stroke or High-Risk TIA: OCEANIC-STROKE Randomized Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: OCEANIC-STROKE (XXX) showed that asundexian added to antiplatelet therapy reduced ischemic stroke without significantly increasing bleeding in patients with noncardioembolic ischemic stroke or high-risk transient ischemic attack. We characterized bleeding categories, sites, and key subgroups.

METHODS: In the safety population, 12 254 participants received at least 1 dose of asundexian (n=6124) or placebo (n=6130). Bleeding was categorized by International Society on Thrombosis and Haemostasis criteria as major, clinically relevant nonmajor (CRNM), or minor. While-on-treatment analyses included events through 2 days after the last dose, with death and permanent discontinuation as competing risks.

RESULTS: Major bleeding occurred in 117 (1.9%) participants with asundexian and 107 (1.7%) with placebo (cause-specific hazard ratio [csHR], 1.10 [95% CI, 0.85-1.44]; P=0.46). Major or CRNM bleeding occurred in 339 (5.5%) and 307 (5.0%), respectively (csHR, 1.12 [95% CI, 0.96-1.30]; P=0.16), and any bleeding in 763 (12.5%) and 752 (12.3%) (csHR, 1.02 [95% CI, 0.93-1.13]; P=0.65). Treatment effects for major and major or CRNM bleeding were consistent across prespecified subgroups, including planned dual antiplatelet therapy. Symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage occurred in 41 (0.7%) and 36 (0.6%) participants. Any gastrointestinal bleeding occurred in 186 (3.0%) and 147 (2.4%) (csHR, 1.28 [95% CI, 1.03-1.59]), and lower gastrointestinal bleeding in 102 (1.7%) and 59 (1.0%) (csHR, 1.75 [95% CI, 1.27-2.41]), primarily rectal bleeding. Any procedure-related bleeding and any mucosal bleeding did not differ significantly.

CONCLUSIONS: Asundexian added to antiplatelet therapy reduced ischemic stroke without significantly increasing major, major or CRNM, or any bleeding. Lower gastrointestinal bleeding was more frequent with asundexian, whereas treatment effects on major and major or CRNM bleeding were consistent across prespecified subgroups.

articles.title: Impact of 18FDG-Avidity and Immunosuppression on Idiopathic and Genetic Cardiomyopathies.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Myocardial 18fluorodeoxyglucose (18FDG)-avidity is frequently seen in patients with genetic cardiomyopathy, as well as a growing "idiopathic 18FDG-avidity" group of genotype-negative patients who do not clearly have cardiac sarcoidosis. The prognostic implications of 18FDG-avidity in patients with and without genetic cardiomyopathy, and the effects of immunosuppression in the latter, remain uncertain.

METHODS: This multicenter, retrospective study included all patients who were referred for both 18FDG-PET and cardiomyopathy genetic testing. Patients with acute myocarditis, biopsy-proven sarcoidosis, or extracardiac 18FDG-avidity were excluded. We investigated heart failure (HF) composite (left ventricular assist device, heart transplant, HF hospitalization, or death) and arrhythmia composite (sustained ventricular arrhythmias [ventricular tachycardia/VF], atrioventricular block, or death) outcomes using survival analysis, including Cox proportional hazards modeling and inverse probability of treatment weighting.

RESULTS: Among 372 patients, 142 (38%) were 18FDG-avid. The prevalence of genetic cardiomyopathy among 18FDG-avid patients (12%) was similar to that of 18FDG-negative patients (18%; P=0.11). Unadjusted, 18FDG-avidity was associated with an increased risk of HF composite (hazard ratio, 1.69 [95% CI, 1.04-2.75]; P=0.034) and arrhythmia composite (hazard ratio, 1.63 [95% CI, 1.1-2.4]; P=0.014) outcomes compared with 18FDG-negative patients. However, these associations were not statistically significant after multivariable adjustment, nor were there significant differences in 18FDG-associated risks in patients with genetic cardiomyopathy versus genotype-negative patients. After inverse probability of treatment weighting, immunosuppression of 18FDG-avid patients (n=49) was not associated with a reduction in HF or arrhythmia composite outcomes compared with those who were not immunosuppressed (n=93).

CONCLUSIONS: Myocardial-only 18FDG-avidity is not significantly associated with HF or arrhythmia risk in patients who do not clearly have cardiac sarcoidosis (including those with genetic cardiomyopathy). Immunosuppression therapy does not seem to modify the disease course, suggesting that not all myocardial 18FDG uptake reflects clinically significant inflammation.

articles.title: Culture-Proven Endophthalmitis Associated With Penetrating Keratoplasty: Clinical Features, Microbiologic Aspects, and Outcomes.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: The objective of this study was to report the clinical features, microbiologic profile, treatments, and outcomes of culture-proven endophthalmitis following penetrating keratoplasty (PKP) in a contemporary cohort.

METHODS: A retrospective chart review of all patients with culture-proven endophthalmitis following PKP between January 2017 and July 2025 was conducted. Patients with endophthalmitis from endothelial keratoplasty, trauma, or other surgery were excluded.

RESULTS: Ten eyes of 10 patients met inclusion criteria. The mean age was 74 ± 3 years, and 70% were female. Indications for PKP were diverse, including 5 optical grafts for Fuchs dystrophy, keratoconus, and corneal edema and 4 therapeutic grafts. Initial visual acuity was hand motion on average. Hypopyon was present in 60%, vitritis in 80%, and suture abscesses in 30%. Initial management was intravitreal aspiration, with intravitreal injection of antimicrobials in 90% and primary pars plana vitrectomy in 10% of eyes. A pars plana vitrectomy for endophthalmitis was performed 1 to 5 days later in an additional 5 of 10 eyes (50%): 3 of 5 for debulking of the vitreous and 2 of 5 because of retinal detachments. Vitreous cultures were positive in all cases, with Candida in 40% isolates, Streptococcus sp. in 20%, Staphylococcus aureus in 10%, Staphylococcus epidermidis in 10%, Enterococcus in 10%, and Pseudomonas in 10%. Despite prompt treatment, visual acuity at the last follow-up was poor at <5/200; however, no eyes were eviscerated or enucleated.

CONCLUSIONS: Endophthalmitis after PKP is an uncommon but devastating complication. In this series, fungal pathogens accounted for a substantial proportion of cases. Management was individualized, but outcomes were generally poor.

articles.title: Chromogenic and FRET peptide substrates, quantum-dot peptide conjugates and electrochemical peptide interfaces: A 25-year journey from combinatorial chemistry to clinical readouts-A viewpoint.
articles.abstract: This Viewpoint synthesises 25 years of work from a single laboratory on activity-based protease sensing and offers a critical appraisal of where each of the three resulting platforms stands today. The activity of proteolytic enzymes-rather than their abundance-determines the outcome of inflammation, tumour progression, viral entry and barrier dysfunction. Measuring it in clinical samples is demanding: closely related proteases share substrate preferences, and biological matrices are crowded with endogenous inhibitors and competing hydrolases. Over the past 25 years, our group at the University of Gdansk has developed a chemical toolkit along three complementary axes, assembled here, as a probe ladder running from solution chemistry to solid-state interface. First, internally quenched chromogenic and Förster resonance energy transfer (FRET) peptide substrates, designed by iterative deconvolution of combinatorial libraries spanning non-primed and primed subsites, provide selective readouts for serine, cysteine, metallo- and viral proteases. Second, peptide-quantum dot conjugates built on non-toxic ZnO nanocrystals improved detection limits 20-30-fold over the parent solution substrate in two published demonstrators. Third, peptide-modified gold electrodes translate protease cleavage and molecular recognition into a label-free electrochemical signal-exemplified by an electrode that reads 20S proteasome activity and by an antimicrobial-peptide interface for bacterial endotoxin. We applied the resulting probes in exploratory studies of bladder cancer, type-2 diabetes and diabetic nephropathy, and positioned them within the broader landscape of activity-based protease sensing-the activity-based probes of the Bogyo and Cravatt laboratories, the PS-SCL and HyCoSuL combinatorial approaches, and the Weissleder near-infrared imaging program.

articles.title: Definition and Prognosis of Mitral Regurgitation in Transthyretin Amyloid Cardiomyopathy: A Multicenter International Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy, mitral regurgitation (MR) severity may be underestimated by conventional (semi-)quantitative echocardiographic criteria due to restrictive low-flow hemodynamics. We sought to define and validate disease-specific MR risk thresholds and compare their prognostic performance with guideline definitions.

METHODS: In a multicenter cohort study (8 centers, 4 countries), 1101 patients with newly diagnosed transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy (derivation, n=722; validation, n=379) underwent standardized echocardiography with blinded core laboratory analysis, including MR measures (vena contracta width, effective regurgitant orifice area, regurgitant volume, and regurgitant fraction). All-cause mortality and time to first heart failure hospitalization (HFH) served as end points. Prognostic thresholds were derived from spline analysis, validated externally, and compared with American Heart Association/American College of Cardiology, European Society of Cardiology/European Association for Cardiothoracic Surgery, and American Society of Echocardiography definitions.

RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 24.9 months (interquartile range, 12.0-42.0), 314 patients (28.5%) died and 244 (22.2%) experienced HFH. All MR metrics independently predicted mortality and HFH (all P<0.05). Spline-derived thresholds identified intermediate risk at vena contracta width ≥3.0 mm, effective regurgitant orifice area ≥0.10 cm2, regurgitant volume ≥15 mL, and regurgitant fraction ≥20% and high risk at effective regurgitant orifice area >0.25 cm2, regurgitant volume >38 mL, and regurgitant fraction >35%. Compared with guideline grading (≈12%-13%), the composite MR grading scheme classified a significantly higher proportion (21%) as severe MR and provided superior discrimination for clinical outcomes at 12 and 24 months in both the derivation and validation cohort. After multivariable adjustment, only the composite MR grading scheme remained strongly predictive for both mortality (hazard ratio, 1.20 [1.07-1.36]) and HFH (hazard ratio, 1.21 [1.05-1.38]).

CONCLUSIONS: Quantitative MR thresholds in transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy are substantially lower than current guideline cutoffs. A validated, risk-based composite MR grading scheme improves prediction of both mortality and HFH, better reflecting the restrictive low-flow pathophysiology of transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy and supporting disease-specific MR grading.

articles.title: National Survival Estimates After Surgical Repair of Congenital Heart Disease.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Survival estimates after congenital heart surgery (CHS) in the United States are essential for planning healthcare services for this growing, resource-intensive patient population. However, the absolute number of individuals living after interventions for congenital heart disease is unknown because nationally representative survival estimates are unavailable. Understanding postoperative survival from a representative national sample is a critical first step toward estimating the size and future healthcare needs of this population. This study aimed to develop nationally representative long-term survival estimates after CHS in the United States, focusing on benchmark procedures defined by the Society of Thoracic Surgeons.

METHODS: We used 3 US data sets of children aged 0 to 20 years at the time of their benchmark CHS from 1998 to 2002 and surviving to hospital discharge. The Pediatric Cardiac Care Consortium (PCCC), a multi-institutional clinical registry, was matched to the National Death Index to determine mortality through December 2019. The Kids' Inpatient Database 2000, a nationally representative administrative claims data set, was used to derive age- and sex-specific weights. Kaplan-Meier curves were estimated from the PCCC-National Death Index cohort for benchmark operations, and Kids' Inpatient Database 2000 weights were applied. Unweighted PCCC survival estimates were also compared with those of Boston Children's Hospital, a large tertiary care center.

RESULTS: Nationally representative survival curves were generated for 7 benchmark CHS from 7973 cases; 3802 (48%) were female, and 4505 (57%) were infants at the time of CHS. These weighted national survival curves closely mirrored the unweighted curves derived from PCCC-National Death Index. Unweighted survival estimates from PCCC also closely approximated those from BCH, with only modest differences observed for selected lesions.

CONCLUSIONS: The weighted PCCC-National Death Index methodology provides the first nationally representative estimates of long-term survival after benchmark congenital heart disease in the United States. These estimates provide an important resource for healthcare planning and research for the growing population of individuals with congenital heart disease.

articles.title: Aldosterone-Producing Lesions Harboring ATP1A1 and ATP2B3 Mutations: An International Multicenter Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Somatic aldosterone-driver mutations are identified in >90% of patients with primary aldosteronism undergoing adrenalectomy, and they display distinct demographic clustering. ATP1A1 and ATP2B3 mutations, encoding the Na+/K+ ATPase α1 subunit and the Ca2+ ATPase 3, respectively, are relatively rare and are often grouped as ATPase mutations. Differences in their clinical and biochemical phenotypes remain understudied.

METHODS: This international collaboration of 16 centers included patients with primary aldosteronism harboring pathogenic variants in ATP1A1 and ATP2B3. Clinical data were collected from medical records. Where available, we compared histopathologic features and steroid profiles (from peripheral and adrenal vein samples) by liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry.

RESULTS: We included 300 patients (mean age, 57±11 years; 85% men) with aldosterone-producing lesions harboring ATP1A1 (204) and ATP2B3 (96) mutations. Age and sex distributions were similar. ATP2B3 mutations were associated with lower serum potassium, higher lateralization indices, and stronger contralateral suppression. Postoperative biochemical cure was achieved in 96% of patients with ATP2B3 mutations versus 83% of those with ATP1A1 mutations (P=0.02). Multiple CYP11B2-positive lesions were observed in 47% of ATP1A1 versus 27% of ATP2B3 cases (P=0.03). Baseline peripheral steroid profiling was available in 126 patients (84 with ATP1A1 and 42 with ATP2B3) and showed higher aldosterone concentrations in the ATP2B3 group (median [interquartile range], 31 ng/dL [20-43] versus 23 ng/dL [11-38]; P=0.03).

CONCLUSIONS: ATPase mutations are most common in middle-aged men with lateralized primary aldosteronism. Compared with ATP1A1, ATP2B3 mutations are associated with a more severe primary aldosteronism phenotype, stronger lateralization, and higher rates of single aldosterone-producing lesions and postoperative biochemical cure.

articles.title: Can a Non-VCTE HCC Prediction Model Be Validated Exclusively in VCTE-Assessed Patients?
The Effects of GLP-1RA-Based and SGLT2 Inhibitor Therapy on Perirenal Adipose Tissue in CKD Patients.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Perirenal adipose tissue (PRAT) surrounds the kidney and may contribute to chronic kidney disease (CKD) progression. SGLT2 inhibitors have been associated with reductions in this depot, but PRAT has not been quantified under GLP-1RA-based therapy in CKD. We assessed ultrasound-measured PRAT thickness under both treatments and whether changes tracked weight loss.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Adults with CKD Stages 1-4 in the prospective ADIPO-CKD inception cohort underwent ultrasound at baseline and at the 8-month visit. PRAT thickness was the mean of right and left measurements; epicardial adipose tissue and body composition were also assessed. Patients received neither drug class (reference), SGLT2i or GLP-1RA-based therapy. Follow-up PRAT was analysed by covariance analysis adjusted for baseline.

RESULTS: Of 277 patients, 80 had paired studies (32 reference, 24 SGLT2i, 24 GLP-1RA-based; body weight 46-122 kg). PRAT was unchanged in the reference group (+0.035 cm, p = 0.376) and decreased with SGLT2i (-0.273 cm, -20.4%, p = 0.0006) and GLP-1RA-based therapy (-0.463 cm, -36.2%, p < 0.0001). Adjusted differences versus reference were -0.227 cm (95% CI -0.417 to -0.036) and -0.433 cm (-0.622 to -0.244); under multiple imputations, -0.218 cm (-0.482 to +0.046) and -0.421 cm (-0.693 to -0.149). GLP-1RA-based therapy reduced body weight, fat mass and visceral fat area; SGLT2i only body weight, modestly. PRAT change correlated with none.

CONCLUSIONS: In CKD, both drug classes were associated with lower follow-up PRAT, not explained by measured body-composition change. Under multiple imputations, both estimates were essentially unchanged, though the SGLT2i interval included no difference. PRAT may represent a candidate depot-specific target.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT07309094 (ADIPO-CKD).

articles.title: Revisiting What HIV in the Brain Can Teach Us About SARS-CoV-2 Neurological Complications.
articles.abstract: In 2021, a Perspective article suggested that principles of HIV neuropathogenesis could provide a conceptual framework for understanding the neurological complications of severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) infection when mechanistic evidence was limited. Five years later, extensive clinical, neuropathological, and experimental studies allow reassessment of that framework. Current evidence has shifted emphasis away from direct viral infection of the central nervous system toward host-mediated mechanisms involving persistent immune activation, endothelial dysfunction, glial activation, thromboinflammation, and disruption of the neuroimmune axis. At the same time, persistent viral antigens and adaptive immune responses, including autoantibodies in subsets of patients, have expanded our understanding of the biological heterogeneity underlying post-acute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 infection with neurological manifestations. This Perspective revisits the original framework in light of these advances and examines how concepts derived from HIV neuropathogenesis continue to inform our understanding of persistent neurological dysfunction following SARS-CoV-2 infection.

articles.title: SGLT2 Inhibitors Reduce Heart Failure Hospitalization, Cardiovascular Death and Kidney Outcomes in Type 2 Diabetes: A Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiovascular disease and chronic kidney disease are the principal drivers of morbidity and mortality in type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). Sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) have demonstrated cardiorenal benefits in landmark trials, yet cross-trial inconsistencies in cardiovascular mortality, renal endpoints and drug-specific effects leave the class-level estimates incompletely synthesized.

METHODS: PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus and CENTRAL were searched from inception through 15 May 2026. Large placebo-controlled RCTs (≥ 1000 participants) and prespecified subgroup analyses in adults with T2DM were eligible. The primary outcome was the composite of first hospitalization for heart failure (HHF) or cardiovascular death (CV death). Secondary outcomes were 3-point major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), CV DEATH, myocardial infarction (MI), stroke, first HHF and composite kidney outcomes. Hazard ratios (HRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were estimated using random-effects inverse-variance models.

RESULTS: Fourteen studies (76 969 patients; 41 761 SGLT2i, 35 208 placebo) were included. SGLT2i reduced the primary composite by 23% (HR: 0.77, 95% CI: 0.73-0.81, p < 0.0001; I2 = 0%), with no effect modification by baseline HF (p-interaction = 0.82) or established ASCVD (p-interaction = 0.46). MACE was reduced by 14% (HR: 0.86, 95% CI: 0.81-0.92), driven by significant reductions in CV DEATH (HR: 0.86, 95% CI: 0.79-0.93) and MI (HR: 0.88, 95% CI: 0.81-0.96), with no significant effect on stroke (HR: 0.93, 95% CI: 0.81-1.08). First, HHF was reduced by 29% (HR: 0.71, 95% CI: 0.66-0.77) and composite kidney outcomes by 31% (HR: 0.69, 95% CI: 0.60-0.79).

CONCLUSIONS: SGLT2i confer consistent and clinically meaningful cardiorenal protection in T2DM across the full spectrum of cardiovascular and renal risk. The ertugliflozin estimate and the moderate heterogeneity in kidney outcomes should be interpreted in the context of trial-level clinical differences and nonstandardized kidney endpoint definitions. These findings support proactive, guideline-concordant initiation of evidence-based SGLT2i agents by endocrinologists, cardiologists and primary care providers as foundational therapy in T2DM.

articles.title: Efficacy of minocycline-containing bismuth quadruple therapy for Helicobacter pylori infection: a single-center retrospective study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Increasing antibiotic resistance has undermined Helicobacter pylori eradication. Despite a low resistance to minocycline, clinical evidence for minocycline-containing bismuth quadruple therapy (MCQT) limited. This retrospective study aimed to evaluate the clinical efficacy of MCQT.

RESEARCH DESIGN AND METHODS: Patients who had Helicobacter pylori infection by 13C-urea breath testing at our department from October 2024 to July 2025 were screened. They were classified into MCQT (minocycline-amoxicillin-acid-inhibitors-bismuth [MAAB], minocycline-clarithromycin-acid-inhibitors-bismuth [MCAB], and minocycline-levofloxacin-acid-inhibitors-bismuth [MLAB]) and non-MCQT (amoxicillin-clarithromycin-acid-inhibitors-bismuth [ACAB] and amoxicillin-levofloxacin-acid-inhibitors-bismuth [ALAB]). Four comparisons (MAAB vs. ACAB, MCAB vs. ACAB, MLAB vs. ALAB, and MAAB vs. ALAB) were separately performed in treatment‑naïve and treatment‑experienced patients. Logistic regression analyses were used to identify the influence factors.

RESULTS: Overall, 687 treatment-naïve and 92 treatment-experienced Helicobacter pylori patients were included. MAAB demonstrated significantly higher eradication rates than ACAB in both groups (P = 0.020, P = 0.016), with no significant differences in other comparisons. Multivariate logistic regression analysis indicated that female was independently associated with a higher eradication rate in treatment-naïve patients in three comparisons (MAAB vs. ACAB, P = 0.021; MCAB vs. ACAB, P = 0.009; MAAB vs. ALAB, P = 0.043).

CONCLUSIONS: MCQT achieve favorable Helicobacter pylori eradication rates in both treatment-naïve and treatment-experienced patients, and MAAB demonstrates a significantly higher eradication rate than ACAB.

articles.title: Relationship between extent of jeopardized myocardium derived from myocardial viability study to post-myocardial infarction outcome.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to assess the relationship between the extent of jeopardized myocardium, quantified using cardiac viability imaging, and clinical outcomes in patients after myocardial infarction. By utilizing rest myocardial perfusion imaging (MPI) and cardiac 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose PET/computed tomography (18F-FDG PET/CT) analyzed with Emory Cardiac Toolbox software (ECTb), the study aimed to determine how quantitative viability parameters correlate with left ventricular functional recovery and post-myocardial infarction outcomes, and to assess their utility in guiding clinical decision-making.

METHODS: This prospective study included 85 patients who underwent 2-day rest MPI followed by cardiac FDG-PET/CT imaging. Quantitative parameters, including the percentage of jeopardized myocardium, comprising viable, scarred, and total jeopardized myocardial segments, along with left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) were obtained using the ECTb platform (version 4.2). The relationship between these quantitative PET parameters and functional myocardial recovery, defined as improvement in ≥5% LVEF as assessed by two-dimensional echocardiography, was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic curve analysis. Follow-up was conducted over a period of 3 months, 6 months, and 1 year to assess the association between baseline quantitative imaging parameters and the occurrence of adverse cardiac events.

RESULTS: The analysis demonstrated that the extent of viable myocardium was a strong predictor of functional recovery (area under the curve, 0.762; P < 0.001), with a cutoff of approximately 17% yielding 76.7% sensitivity, 68.8% specificity, and 71.8% accuracy. Major adverse cardiac events (MACE) occurred in 16% of patients. There was no significant association with imaging parameters, except a nonsignificant trend for scar burden in medically managed patients. Patients undergoing surgical intervention had a significantly greater extent of jeopardized myocardium, underscoring the role of viability imaging in therapeutic decision-making.

CONCLUSION: The extent of viable myocardium identified through imaging was strongly correlated with functional recovery, as reflected by improvements in cardiac function on follow-up echocardiography. Although no significant relationship with MACE was seen in the overall cohort, the higher burden of jeopardized myocardium in surgically treated patients underscores the value of viability imaging in guiding revascularization decisions, supporting FDG-PET/CT as a useful tool for post-myocardial infarction risk stratification and management.

articles.title: Soluble Indicators of Endothelial Injury and Activation Emerge During Acute HIV Infection and Persist Despite Rapid Antiretroviral Therapy Initiation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Vascular activation occurs during human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection and is a risk factor for cardiovascular disease (CVD). This study investigates whether vascular endothelial and hemostatic perturbations emerge during acute HIV infection (AHI) and persist despite immediate antiretroviral therapy (ART) initiation.

METHODS: Thirteen plasma biomarkers indicative of endothelial and hemostatic perturbations were measured in 83 RV254 AHI cohort participants during pre-ART AHI and at week 288 post-ART, compared with cross-sectional measures from 32 people without HIV (PWoH). Hierarchical clustering was applied to week 288 biomarker profiles of RV254 participants and PWoH to identify distinct biomarker phenotypes.

RESULTS: During pre-ART AHI, RV254 participants exhibited higher intercellular adhesion molecule-1 (ICAM-1), vascular cell adhesion molecule-1 (VCAM-1), tissue factor, neopterin, and myeloperoxidase than PWoH (P < .05), independent of age, sex, and body mass index (BMI). These markers correlated with plasma HIV RNA or the CD4/CD8 ratio (P < .05). At week 288, significant reductions in ICAM-1, VCAM-1, vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF)-C, VEGF-D, neopterin, and myeloperoxidase and a significant increase in tissue plasminogen activator were observed in RV254 (P < .05). However, VCAM-1 and thrombomodulin remained higher, and VEGF-A remained lower in RV254 participants compared to PWoH (P < .05). Hierarchical clustering identified 2 distinct clusters. Despite comparable 10-year CVD risk, 1 cluster exhibited concomitant elevation of ICAM-1, ICAM-2, VCAM-1, and E-selectin. Notably, 45% of RV254 participants vs 13% of PWoH were classified into this phenotype.

CONCLUSIONS: Endothelial and hemostatic perturbations emerge during AHI and correlate with HIV-related parameters. Despite suppressive ART, RV254 participants remained approximately 3.5 times more likely than PWoH to exhibit an endothelial activation biomarker phenotype.

articles.title: Continuity of care interventions for people with stroke and their caregivers: a scoping review of randomized controlled trials.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: People with stroke (PwS) and their family caregivers characterize transitions across care environments as challenging. Enhancing the family-centered nature of continuity of care interventions could improve experiences and outcomes. This scoping review aimed to synthesize the literature on continuity of care interventions for PwS and/or their caregivers.

METHODS: The Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) methodology for scoping reviews was followed. Five databases were searched, and only randomized controlled trials were included. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics and deductive content analysis.

RESULTS: We included 65 interventions identified from 80 included studies. Most intervention studies included only PwS. Most interventions addressed the transition from acute inpatient management to home care services. On average, two of three continuity of care dimensions were addressed, and two of four family-centred care components were addressed across interventions.

CONCLUSIONS: This scoping review emphasizes the need for continuity of care intervention studies to include both PwS and their caregivers. Future research should investigate interventions that promote a family-centered care approach. The review also highlights that current interventions do not address all transitions across the stroke care continuum. Finally, future interventions should explore which aspects of continuity of care may need to be prioritized at specific transition points.

articles.title: The impact and value of [18F]-FDG PET-CT on management of patients with cervical cancer with service evaluation audited against national evidence-based PET-CT guidelines.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: First, to assess the diagnostic value of fluorine-18-fluorodeoxyglucose PET-computed tomography ([18F]-FDG PET-CT) compared with conventional MRI and/or CT. Second, to audit the clinical indications for referring patients with cervical cancer for [18F]-FDG PET-CT against the 2022 guidelines published by the Royal College of Radiologists and the Royal College of Physicians. Finally, to evaluate the impact of [18F]-FDG PET-CT on management plans.

METHODS: A retrospective cohort study of 49 patients with histologically proven cervical cancer across the Sussex Cancer Network underwent 59 [18F]-FDG PET-CT between 1 November 2020 and 31 October 2022. Scans were compared with the most recent CT and MRI scan conducted within 4 months of the [18F]-FDG PET-CT. Scan indications were categorized as either 'in accordance' or 'outside' the guidelines. Those in accordance fell into one of four groups: staging, response assessment, suspected recurrence, or staging when considering exenterative surgery. A questionnaire investigating the impact of the [18F]-FDG PET-CT on the management plan of each patient was answered by one clinical oncology consultant.

RESULTS: [18F]-FDG PET-CT identified new metastatic sites in 16/59 (27.1%) scans. The remaining scans were concordant with the CT and MRI. The majority, 57/59 (96.6%), of the scans were performed in accordance with the guidelines. The management plan was changed by 5/59 scans (8.4%), confirmed by 48/59 (81.4%) and was not impacted with 6/59 (10.2%) scans.

CONCLUSION: [18F]-FDG PET-CT is superior to conventional imaging and enhances the management plan. Future cohort studies with larger patient numbers involving multicentric studies are needed to fully assess its impact on cervical cancer management and prognosis.

articles.title: Proteasuria: extending an existing term into a framework for concentration-based and catalytic protease diagnostics in urine, with emphasis on activity-based methods.
articles.journal: Critical reviews in clinical laboratory sciences
articles.abstract: Proteases are central to cancer pathobiology and attractive targets for noninvasive diagnosis. Diagnostic use of urinary proteases has developed along two methodologically distinct streams: measurement of protein abundance by immunoassay and increasingly by mass spectrometry, and direct measurement of enzymatic activity using peptide substrates. However, no common terminology unifies these approaches. This narrative review synthesizes evidence published between 2016 and 2026, concentrating on urine and, for the transferability of the methodology, on fecal water and serum. Saliva and seminal fluid are surveyed only to show that protease biomarkers there are measured by abundance alone. It adopts, from its existing use in nephrology, the term proteasuria as a unifying construct for the urinary protease diagnostic field, proposing a wider scope than the pathophysiological sense in which it was introduced. Two operational subtypes are defined: concentration-based and catalytic proteasuria. The distinction rests on the parameter measured rather than on the detection chemistry. Within the catalytic subtype single-enzyme detection using a selective substrate is distinguished from disease profiling using a multi-substrate panel. Evidence was identified by a PubMed search supplemented by citation and semantic search and screened by a single reviewer without protocol registration or formal risk-of-bias assessment. Concentration-based proteasuria is the clinically established stream, yet no urinary analyte has displaced cystoscopy, and approved assays remain insufficient as stand-alone rule-out or triage tests. The catalytic stream rests mainly on small single-center case-control studies reporting activity qualitatively; only one reports formal diagnostic performance, with a single elastase-specific substrate in 12 cases and 24 controls, and no head-to-head comparison with concentration-based assays has been published. Analytical validity is partial: substrate selectivity is established by combinatorial screening and confirmed with inhibitor and orthogonal controls, but precision, limits of quantification in urine and inter-laboratory reproducibility are not systematically reported, and no reference material or external quality-assessment scheme exists for this assay class. A largely independent exogenous stream of synthetic urinary biomarkers and activity-based nanosensors reports high accuracy, but all published diagnostic-accuracy data derive from animal models. On a translational-readiness scale the urinary catalytic stream is proof-of-concept, research-grade work, and any realistic target is therefore not cystoscopy but the margin at which established assays fail, principally low-grade noninvasive disease. The same reasoning identifies the detection of advanced adenoma, for which the fecal immunochemical test performs poorly, as the concrete benchmark for extending the framework to fecal protease profiling in colorectal cancer.

articles.title: Non-coding RNAs as potential clinical biomarkers of heart failure: analytical validation, laboratory methodology, and clinical implementation pathways.
articles.journal: Critical reviews in clinical laboratory sciences
articles.abstract: Heart failure (HF) is a heterogeneous clinical syndrome that has pathophysiologic manifestations of hemodynamic abnormalities, downstream neurohumoral activation and inflammation, myocardial fibrosis, metabolic dysfunction, and cardiomyocyte injury. Relevant to the issue of B-type natriuretic peptide (BNP) and N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) as clinically established biomarkers, their interpretation may be influenced by confounding factors such as obesity, renal dysfunction, atrial fibrillation, and HF phenotype. Recent data highlight a broad spectrum of non-coding RNA (ncRNA) types, including microRNAs (miRNAs), long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs), and circular RNAs (circRNAs), which can be detected in circulating samples and participate in regulatory networks associated with myocardial remodeling, supporting their investigation as potential complementary biomarkers. A structured literature search of PubMed/MEDLINE, Web of Science Core Collection, and Scopus from database inception to August 6, 2026, was conducted according to predefined eligibility, study-selection, and evidence-appraisal criteria. Here, HF-associated ncRNAs are assessed from perspectives including biological relevance, pre-analytical variables, detection platforms, quality control (QC), analytical and clinical validation, clinical-use scenarios, and implementation pathways. The available evidence so far rather supports a role in which ncRNAs serve as adjunctive rather than stand-alone biomarkers. The field is highlighted by the fact that presently no ncRNA-based assay is ready for routine clinical use in HF. Harmonized pre-analytical and analytical workflows, independent multicenter validation, predefined clinical-use scenarios, as well as demonstration of incremental clinical value and cost-effectiveness beyond established biomarkers, imaging, and clinical variables will be needed for future progress.

articles.title: Endovascular versus open repair for aortoiliac occlusive disease - nationwide in-hospital outcomes by sex.
articles.abstract: Background: Evidence comparing endovascular therapy and open surgery for aorto-iliac occlusive disease remains limited, particularly for early complications, resource use, and sex-specific outcomes. Patients and methods: We conducted a retrospective nationwide cohort study using the 2023 German inpatient dataset. Adult hospitalisations with major endovascular or open aorto-iliac reconstructive procedures and arterial occlusive disease were included. Hospitalisations with aneurysm, dissection, or combined procedure codes were excluded. Outcomes included in-hospital mortality, myocardial infarction, ischaemic stroke, major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events (MACCE), complications, length of stay, and reimbursement. Adjusted estimates were obtained employing a doubly robust estimator using machine learning algorithms and were stratified by sex. Results: Among 2,710 hospitalisations, 1,923 (71.0%) underwent open surgery and 787 (29.0%) endovascular therapy; 41.3% involved women. Endovascular therapy was associated with lower adjusted risks of in-hospital mortality (RR .44, 95% CI .31-.64), MACCE (RR .47, 95% CI .34-.64), acute kidney injury (RR .38, 95% CI .29-.50), major bleeding (RR .36, 95% CI .25-.51), prolonged ventilation (RR .28, 95% CI .18-.43), and SAEs (RR .46, 95% CI .33-.65). Length of stay was shorter after endovascular therapy (-8.57 days, 95% CI -9.63 to -7.52), while reimbursement did not differ significantly. Sex-stratified estimates were more pronounced in men but exploratory without interaction testing. Conclusions: Endovascular therapy was associated with lower in-hospital morbidity and mortality and shorter hospital stay than open surgery, with similar reimbursement. Case-based data lacked longitudinal follow-up and detailed clinical, anatomical and treatment-selection information, limiting causal and patient-level interpretation.

articles.title: Calprotectin as a Prognostic Marker for Sepsis Independent of Renal Dysfunction.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The role of calprotectin in sepsis pathophysiology is becoming increasingly recognized; however, optimal biomarkers for sepsis prognosis are lacking. We compared the prognostic accuracy of calprotectin with that of established biomarkers.

METHODS: In this single-center prospective cohort study, patients who met the Sepsis-3 criteria were recruited between December 2022 and January 2024. Blood samples were collected at sepsis recognition (day 0) in the emergency department and on days 3 and 7 during the intensive care unit admission.

RESULTS: Ninety patients with community-onset sepsis were included (median age, 79 yrs [69-85]; 51 women [56.7%]), and 17 patients (18.9%) died during hospitalization. Pneumonia was the most common etiology in both survivors and non-survivors. Calprotectin showed good prognostic performance across all time points, without significant temporal differences (area under the curve [AUC], day 0, 0.785 [95% confidence interval, 0.681-0.890]; day 3, 0.800 [0.680-0.921]; day 7, 0.813 [0.696-0.930]; all P <0.001). After estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) adjustment, the predictive performance of calprotectin was preserved, whereas presepsin and procalcitonin showed significant renal function dependency. Calprotectin did not significantly correlate with eGFR and showed good prognostic performance regardless of renal dysfunction status. Incremental value analyses revealed that serial calprotectin measurements provided no significant improvement over baseline assessment. In pneumonia-induced sepsis, calprotectin consistently showed the highest AUC, regardless of renal adjustment.

CONCLUSIONS: Calprotectin demonstrated reliable prognostic performance for hospital mortality in community-onset sepsis independently of renal dysfunction, warranting validation in larger cohorts. A single measurement at initial presentation could provide clinically useful early prognostic information.

articles.title: Food ration affects mRNA processing, translation, proteostasis, and cytoskeletal responses during heat shock in Mytilus californianus.
articles.abstract: Despite a likely role in setting stress tolerance limits, food ration has received limited attention as an ecological factor affecting the cellular stress response (CSR). To study the interactive effects of food and temperature on the proteomic heat shock response, we acclimated intertidal mussels (Mytilus californianus) to four combinations of nearshore (low) and aquaculture (high) phytoplankton levels, combined with low (20 °C) and high (30 °C) aerial temperatures during daytime low tides. Mussels were then exposed to an acute (6 h), aerial heat stress (33 °C) and allowed to recover for 1 h and 25 h in pre-exposure conditions. Proteomic changes in the gill before and after heat shock were measured using label-free liquid-chromatography-mass spectrometry. Compared to other acclimation treatments, low-food-low-temperature (LTLF) mussels modified more splicing factors, heterogeneous nuclear ribonucleoproteins, ribosomal proteins, and translation initiation and elongation factors, suggesting systemic changes to RNA processing, selection, and translation. LTLF mussels also increased chaperones of the actin- and microtubule-associated cytoskeleton and proteins that mature along the endoplasmic reticulum to Golgi secretory pathway. Simultaneously, actin stress fiber formation at focal adhesions and the extracellular matrix, along with anchoring of microtubule-associated cilia, indicate a possible system-wide mechanical breakdown of the cytoskeleton. Signaling proteins causing cytoskeletal changes varied mainly in LTLF mussels and suggest a food-dependent role for prostaglandin synthesis. Overall, the acclimation-dependent proteomic changes show how thermal conditioning and food ration together will shape the CSR of mussels during heat waves.

articles.title: Underserved communities at risk of heart failure: effectiveness of community-based recruitment strategies and burden of unrecognised cardiovascular disease.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients from socioeconomically deprived and ethnically diverse backgrounds are under-represented in cardiovascular research. EARLY-HF is a community-based pilot study designed to predict incident HF in primary care. We aimed to assess effectiveness of recruitment strategies for engaging underserved populations and quantify the burden of unrecognised CVD.

METHODS: Prospective cohort study enrolling 550 adults aged ≥50 years with two or more cardiometabolic risk factors and no prior diagnosis of HF. Participants were recruited via: (i) targeted identification using electronic health records in eight primary care centres; (ii) digital advertising and targeted social media campaign; (iii) ten community outreach events; (iv) direct referral from family or friends. The baseline study visit included ECG, blood sampling, and imaging.

RESULTS: 185 (34%) participants were from the most deprived Index of Multiple Deprivation (IMD) quintile and 97 (18%) were of non-White ethnicity. Primary care and digital advertising were the most effective recruitment strategies, enrolling 444 (81%) and 68 (12%) participants respectively, while maintaining diverse representation. The social media campaign generated 15,207 advertisement clicks and 1,012 expressions of interest at a cost of £5.93 per sign-up. Community outreach events enrolled 5 (1%) participants and were resource intensive. A substantial burden of previously unrecognised CVD was identified: 125 (23%) participants had clinically actionable cardiac abnormalities, including 46 (9%) with previously unrecognised myocardial infarction, 331 (60%) had uncontrolled blood pressure (≥140/90 mmHg), and 162 (30%) had elevated N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP ≥125 pg/ml).

CONCLUSIONS: Primary care-embedded and digital recruitment strategies can effectively engage underserved communities at risk of HF, at scale and at low cost. This population has a very high burden of unrecognised CVD.

articles.title: Genetic landscape of paediatric channelopathies and cardiomyopathies in Hong Kong.
articles.journal: Hong Kong medical journal = Xianggang yi xue za zhi
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Cardiac channelopathies and cardiomyopathies are important causes of sudden cardiac death. The genetic background of these conditions in Asian paediatric populations has rarely been reported. This study aimed to report the genetic underpinnings of these conditions in patients treated at a single tertiary paediatric cardiac centre in Hong Kong.

METHODS: All patients diagnosed with cardiac channelopathy or cardiomyopathy who underwent genetic testing in our cardiology centre between 2007 and 2022 were included in this cohort study. Phenotype classification, genetic testing methodologies, and results were reviewed. Genetic yields were assessed.

RESULTS: In total, 165 probands were identified. Ninety-four probands carried at least one pathogenic or likely pathogenic (P/LP) variant (57.0%), whereas 27 probands (16.4%) had only variants of uncertain significance (VUS). Pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants were identified in 58 patients with channelopathy (63.7%) and 36 patients with cardiomyopathy (48.6%), including 22 novel variants (16 P/LP variants and 6 VUS). The yield of P/LP variants was highest in catecholaminergic polymorphic ventricular tachycardia (81.8%). The clinical features of selected probands with significant mortality or morbidity were described in relation to variant details. The yield of subsequent cascade genetic screening among first-degree relatives was 27.3%.

CONCLUSION: This study describes the genetic landscape of paediatric cardiac channelopathies and cardiomyopathies at a single tertiary paediatric cardiology centre in Hong Kong. The findings facilitated genotype-guided management and enabled identification of at-risk family members for the prevention of sudden cardiac death.

articles.title: ESR and CRP Testing in an Urban Emergency Department: Should We Still Be Doing This?
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Pediatricians in the Emergency Department frequently evaluate febrile children. To help identify the cause of fever and assess the severity of the underlying condition, practitioners often utilize erythrocyte sedimentation rate and C-reactive protein testing. While these markers of inflammation are deeply embedded in the practice of pediatrics, they were each developed more than 90 years ago, and their utility to current clinical practice is not well characterized.

METHODS: We conducted a 1-year retrospective study of children who underwent CRP and ESR testing at an urban Children's Hospital. We recorded and analyzed indications for testing, concordance between testing methods and metrics, including admission status and test performance, as reflected by sensitivity, specificity, and likelihood ratios.

RESULTS: ESR and CRP tests were frequently ordered in patients with clinically evident diagnoses. There were no cases of occult bacteremia, and patients with bacteremia typically had presentations indicative of bacterial infection. CRP was superior to ESR as a predictor of bacterial infection; however, the positive likelihood ratio was only 2.1. Combined testing was ordered for 39.4% of all CRP tests, and there was a high concordance (69.9%) between CRP and ESR testing. Combined testing offered limited incremental value for the detection of bacterial infections.

CONCLUSIONS: CRP and ESR testing are currently overused in our Pediatric Emergency Department, providing limited diagnostic value while adding unnecessary hospital cost. Combined CRP and ESR testing provides limited incremental value. Stewardship of these testing modalities and an active reconsideration of how these tests are employed should be considered.

articles.title: Who We Recruit, Who We Miss: EARLY-HF and the Equity Gap in Heart Failure Research.
Estimate Optimal Dynamic Treatment Regimes with Partial Compatibility: An Application to data from a TREAT Asia HIV Observational Database (TAHOD) site in Pune, India.
articles.abstract: Dynamic treatment regimes (DTRs) formalize sequences of treatment decision rules that adapt to a patient's evolving clinical status. In observational studies, estimation of the value of a DTR (i.e., the expected population-outcome of a treatment strategy) using inverse probability weighting (IPW) and augmented IPW can be unstable when strict regime compatibility yields few valid participant trajectories, leading to highly variable weights and noisy estimates. In this paper, we introduce two adaptive weighting frameworks: generalized compatibility weighting (GCW) and bootstrap compatibility windowing (BCW), that allow near-compatible trajectories to contribute information in limited samples, with diminishing information-borrowing in larger samples. We illustrate how these estimators reduce noise in estimation and stabilize empirical optimal treatment threshold identification. Using data from adults living with HIV in one site of the TREAT Asia HIV Observational Database in India observed from 2013-2024, we evaluate clinically interpretable threshold-based decision rules based on baseline CD4 count and weight. In this application, GCW and BCW produced more stable estimated regime values than standard IPW-based approaches, with reduced variability across candidate thresholds and more reliable identification of empirically optimal treatment rules. These methods provide practical tools for improving treatment rule evaluation in observational studies.

articles.title: A Law of Iterated Expectation Primer for Causal Inference.
articles.abstract: The g-formula is a foundational tool for identifying causal effects in observational data. This tool is based on the law of iterated expectation, a key mathematical identity in statistics. However, the notation with which the law of iterated expectation and the g-formula is expressed can be opaque to those with little background in statistics. We provide a primer introducing the law of iterated expectation, the integration notation used to express it, and its role for causal effect identification via the g-formula. Combined with the assumptions of causal consistency, positivity, and conditional exchangeability, the law of iterated expectation yields a causal standardization formula (the g-formula) in two nonparametrically equivalent forms: a non-iterative conditional expectation (NICE) form involving a single weighted average of conditional outcome means, and an iterative conditional expectation (ICE) form involving nested expectations. We illustrate both forms using three progressively complex numerical examples: a time-fixed example with a single binary confounder, a time-fixed example with discrete and continuous confounders, and a time-varying example with two timepoints. We provide clarity on what the law of iterated expectation is, how it is related to the g-formula, and how to gain intuition of its mathematical formulations in actual data examples that can be generalized to a range of settings.

articles.title: Genotype and arrhythmic risk in dilated cardiomyopathy.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) presents with variable risk of life-threatening arrhythmias. Genetic diagnosis guides sudden death prevention strategies, but risk magnitude for arrhythmogenic genes remains unknown. This study leveraged the international Sarcomeric Human Cardiomyopathy Registry (SHaRe) to address this gap and improve risk stratification.

METHODS: Effects of pathogenic/likely pathogenic (P/LP) variants in genes associated with DCM and ventricular arrhythmia on clinical events were analysed in DCM-SHaRe patients. Patients were stratified by presence of a P/LP variant in a high-arrhythmogenic risk gene (LMNA, DSP, FLNC, RBM20, PLN, SCN5A, DES, TMEM43), a low-arrhythmogenic risk gene (TTN, TNNT2, MYH7, others), or gene-elusive. Outcomes included age-, sex-, and baseline left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF)-adjusted risk of major ventricular arrhythmia (MVA), atrial fibrillation (AF), heart failure (HF), death, and their composite.

RESULTS: Among 2660 genotyped adults with DCM (mean diagnosis age 47 ± 15 years, 39.8% female), 434 (16%) had P/LP variants in high-arrhythmogenic genes, 451 (17%) in low-arrhythmogenic genes, and 1775 (67%) were gene-elusive. Compared with gene-elusive patients, patients with high-arrhythmogenic P/LP variants showed increased MVA [hazard ratio (HR) 3.25, 95% confidence interval (CI) 2.63-4.01], AF (HR 2.42, 95% CI 1.96-2.98), HF (HR 2.46, 95% CI 1.89-3.19), and composite (HR 1.97, 95% CI 1.69-2.29) risk, which remained significant after adjusting for age, sex, and LVEF. Patients with high-arrhythmogenic P/LP variants and LVEF ≥ 50% maintained increased MVA (HR 2.36, 95% CI 1.59-3.51) and composite (HR 1.63, 95% CI 1.25-2.12) risk.

CONCLUSIONS: Genetic testing enables powerful risk stratification for arrhythmias and HF in DCM independent of age, sex, or LVEF.

articles.title: Improving hand hygiene compliance in Greek hospitals: results of a Nationwide Quality Improvement Program (GRIPP-SNF).
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Hand hygiene (HH) is the most effective way to prevent healthcare-associated infections (HAIs) and the spread of antimicrobial-resistant pathogens. HH compliance is particularly relevant in Greece, which has among the highest rates of HAIs and antimicrobial resistance in the European Union. The aim of our study was to assess current HH practices in Greece and to improve compliance.

DESIGN: Prospective observational quasi-experimental (before-after) study.

SETTING: Eight public adult tertiary hospitals.

PARTICIPANTS: "Physicians, Nurses, and Ancillary Healthcare Workers."

METHODS: Three time periods were defined: the baseline period (December 2021-June 2022), intervention period (July 2022-January 2023), and postintervention period (February 2023-May 2024). An improvement bundle was implemented. A minimum of 30 observations per department per month of HH opportunities were required. Trained observers conducted observations using a standardized data collection tool. Interrupted time-series analysis was performed.

RESULTS: 38,069 HH opportunities were observed. Overall compliance was 48.5%. Glove use without proper HH was observed in 72.9% of opportunities. Alcohol-based hand rub was used for HH by 57.8% of HCW who conducted HH. Compliance improved from 37.3% in the baseline period to 53.3% after the intervention (16% increase, P < .001). Improved compliance was observed in 9/13 (69%) intensive care units. Of 10 participating medical and surgical wards, improved compliance was observed in 9 (90%) units, and improvement ranged from 7.2% to 28.3.

CONCLUSIONS: Overall, we found low compliance rates and gaps in HH practices in Greek hospitals. A quality improvement intervention improved overall HH compliance. This is the largest study of HH compliance in Greek hospitals to date.
