articles.title: Recurrent healthcare-associated pediatric HIV outbreaks in Pakistan: a call to reinforce infection prevention and control.
Cost-effectiveness of screening for carbapenemase-producing Enterobacterales in a university-affiliated tertiary care hospital in Hong Kong: a real-world analysis of data from 2015 to 2024.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Carbapenemase-producing Enterobacterales (CPE) are a major healthcare-associated threat due to multidrug resistance, gastrointestinal colonization, and hospital transmission. We evaluated the cost-effectiveness of CPE screening using real-world data from 2015 to 2024.

METHODS: We conducted a healthcare provider-perspective economic evaluation at Queen Mary Hospital, using electronic health records and hospital data. Screening episodes, clinical outcomes, lengths of stay, and costs (laboratory testing, staffing, personal protective equipment, and disinfection) were analyzed. We calculated the number needed to screen (NNS), incremental cost-effectiveness ratio (ICER) for infection prevention, and cost per quality-adjusted life-year (QALY) gained.

RESULTS: Among 375,213 hospitalization episodes in which CPE testing was performed (447,745 tests), 10,046 (2.7%) were positive; 390 (3.9%) were clinical infections and 9,656 (96.1%) colonizations. After patient-level deduplication (149,965 individuals), 3,628 (2.4%) were CPE-positive, with 153 clinical infections. Mean cost per CPE infection was US＄35,290 and per colonization US＄7,721. Annual screening program cost was US＄1,487,969. An estimated 63.6 infections were averted and 47.8 QALYs gained annually (NNS = 590). Compared with no screening, it was cost-saving (annual saving US＄757,604). Sensitivity analyses showed NNS most sensitive to screening effectiveness (-40.9% to +59.2%); screening remained dominant except at lower limit of effectiveness (ICER = US＄1,958; cost/QALY = US＄2,048). Worst-case scenario ICER was US＄31,019 (cost/QALY = US＄29,831). All values were below the World Health Organization cost-effectiveness threshold of US＄54,301 (Hong Kong gross domestic product/capita).

CONCLUSION: CPE screening was cost-saving and highly cost-effective, remaining robust across sensitivity analyses. These findings support sustained screening in high-volume tertiary settings.

articles.title: Predictors of immediate mother-newborn skin-to-skin contact and missed contact in health facilities in Malawi: a multilevel analysis of the Malawi Demographic and Health Survey-2024.
articles.abstract:
AIM: This study aimed to examine the prevalence and predictors of immediate mother-newborn skin-to-skin contact (SSC) in Malawi and factors associated with missed SSC despite being delivered in health facilities.

BACKGROUND: SSC immediately after birth is an evidence-based essential newborn care intervention associated with improved thermoregulation, early breastfeeding initiation, maternal-infant bonding, and neonatal survival. Although facility delivery is expected to promote SSC, a substantial proportion of newborns in low- and middle-income countries still do not receive this recommended practice.

METHODS: We analysed data from the Malawi Demographic and Health Survey 2024. After restricting to the most recent live birth per woman and applying a complete-case approach across the outcome and all explanatory variables, the final analytic sample comprised 6,065 mother-newborn pairs (weighted sample: 6,142). The outcome was maternal report of immediate SSC after birth. Weighted descriptive statistics, chi-square tests, and multilevel logistic regression were used to identify factors associated with SSC. Adjusted odds ratios (aORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) are reported.

FINDINGS: Overall, 77.3% of newborns experienced SSC. In the fully adjusted model, caesarean delivery (aOR = 0.13, 95% CI: 0.10-0.17) and multiple births (aOR = 0.47, 95% CI: 0.26-0.86) were associated with lower adjusted odds of receiving SSC. Institutional delivery (aOR = 5.20, 95% CI: 1.86-14.56) and antenatal care attendance were associated with higher adjusted odds of receiving SSC. Among institutional deliveries, caesarean delivery and multiple births (aOR = 0.44, 95% CI: 0.24-0.80) remained associated with lower odds of receiving SSC. Cluster-level variation was substantial (ICC = 0.172-0.173).

articles.title: Refining Home-Based Squat Training: The Role of Hip Adduction in Improving Neuromuscular Control for Clinically Diagnosed Patellofemoral Pain Syndrome.
articles.journal: Medical science monitor : international medical journal of experimental and clinical research
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND Patellofemoral pain syndrome (PFPS) often stems from neuromuscular imbalances, particularly vastus medialis obliques (VMO) dysfunction impairing patellar tracking. Research is shifting toward integrated rehabilitation strategies, such as combining hip adduction with squats to enhance VMO recruitment. MATERIAL AND METHODS Thirty participants with PFPS were randomized to traditional squatting (SQU, n=15) or squatting with hip adduction (SQU-HA, n=15) for an 8-week home-based program with identical stretching. SQU-HA squeezed a Swiss ball during squats. Fifteen healthy individuals served as a reference group (RG). Outcome measures assessed before and after intervention included Q-angle, patellar tilt, clinical scales (visual analog scale [VAS], patellofemoral pain severity scale [PSS]), and electromyographic parameters (VMO, vastus lateralis [VL], adductor [ADD] amplitudes, onset times, VMO/VL ratio, and VMO-VL onset difference). RESULTS Both PFPS groups showed significant improvements in VAS and PSS after intervention, with greater VAS improvement in the SQU-HA group (P<0.01). Within-group analysis showed reduced patellar tilt in the SQU-HA group (P=0.003); between-group comparison did not reach statistical significance (P=0.217). Muscle activation onset sequences shifted from an abnormal pattern, in which VL activation preceded VMO and ADD activation, to a more typical pattern, in which VMO activation preceded VL and ADD activation. This shift was particularly evident in the SQU-HA group, whose activation pattern resembled that of the RG after intervention. Only VMO-VL onset difference, VMO/VL ratio, and Q-angle were correlated with clinical outcomes (P<0.05). CONCLUSIONS An 8-week SQU-HA program demonstrates promising short-term improvements in VMO-related neuromuscular measures and pain reduction for patients with PFPS. This accessible motor re-education strategy serves as a practical, home-based approach to patellofemoral rehabilitation.

articles.title: Successful Kidney Transplantation Under Combined Spinal-Epidural Anesthesia in a Patient With a History of Left Pneumonectomy Due to Bronchiectasis.
articles.journal: The American journal of case reports
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND Kidney transplantation offers clear survival and quality-of-life advantages over dialysis, but severe pulmonary disease can complicate perioperative planning. In patients with substantially reduced respiratory reserve after pneumonectomy, general anesthesia may be considered high risk, creating uncertainty about transplant feasibility. CASE REPORT A 33-year-old man with end-stage kidney disease secondary to biopsy-proven AA amyloidosis was evaluated for preemptive living-donor kidney transplantation. He had undergone left pneumonectomy in 2015 because of bronchiectasis. Pulmonary function testing showed a mixed restrictive-obstructive pattern, with a forced vital capacity of 1.6 L (33% predicted), a forced expiratory volume in 1 second of 1.05 L (30% predicted), and a forced expiratory volume in 1 second/forced vital capacity ratio of 65%, indicating severe pulmonary impairment. Thoracic computed tomography demonstrated leftward mediastinal shift and diffuse bronchiectatic changes in the remaining right lung. Given the anticipated risk associated with general anesthesia, combined spinal-epidural anesthesia was selected. The transplant was successfully performed using a kidney from the patient's human leukocyte antigen (HLA)-identical sister. No intraoperative respiratory or hemodynamic instability occurred. Renal function rapidly improved after surgery: serum creatinine decreased from 6.6 mg/dL preoperatively to 0.63 mg/dL on postoperative day 3. Heavy proteinuria also greatly improved during follow-up. CONCLUSIONS This case demonstrates that kidney transplantation can be successfully performed under combined spinal-epidural anesthesia in carefully selected patients with severely limited pulmonary reserve after pneumonectomy. It also highlights the importance of individualized anesthetic planning and close multidisciplinary coordination for complex transplant candidates with major pulmonary comorbidities.

articles.title: Forty-Eight Hour Lactate Normalization Predicts Favorable Neurologic Recovery and Survival in Venoarterial ECMO for Cardiogenic Shock.
articles.journal: ASAIO journal (American Society for Artificial Internal Organs : 1992)
articles.abstract: Extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) for cardiogenic shock (CS) is associated with high mortality and poor neurological outcomes. Dynamic assessment of metabolic recovery, reflected by lactate normalization, may offer additional prognostic value compared with static severity indices. We retrospectively analyzed 662 consecutive patients from the multicenter RESCUE II registry who remained on venoarterial ECMO for at least 48 hours. Patients were stratified by 48 hour lactate level: 48 hour lactate normalization group (< 2.0 mmol/L, n = 371) and persistent lactate elevation group (≥ 2.0 mmol/L, n = 291). The primary outcome was favorable neurologic discharge (FND), defined as discharge with a Cerebral Performance Category score of 1 or 2. The persistent lactate elevation group had a higher SOFA score (9.8 ± 3.2 vs. 8.5 ± 3.4, p < 0.001) and initial serum lactate (7.9 ± 4.8 mmol/L vs. 6.0 ± 4.3 mmol/L, p < 0.001). Lactate normalization was associated with a higher rate of FND (71.4% vs. 41.9%, p < 0.001), remained an independent predictor of FND (odds ratio [OR]: 3.12, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 2.21-4.41, p < 0.001), and was associated with lower risks of all-cause death (hazard ratio [HR]: 0.49, 95% CI: 0.38-0.64, p < 0.001) at 12 months. In conclusion, lactate normalization within 48 hours of ECMO initiation is associated with favorable neurologic status and 12 month survival.

articles.title: Strengthening the Occupational Safety and Health Workforce: A Mixed Methods Evaluation of a NIOSH-Funded Education and Research Center.
articles.journal: Journal of public health management and practice : JPHMP
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Workplace injuries and fatalities remain persistent public health and occupational concerns in the United States. At the same time, emerging hazards, including automation, psychosocial stressors, climate-related exposures, and an aging workforce, are reshaping occupational risk profiles. These challenges underscore the need for a well-prepared occupational safety and health (OSH) workforce. National Institute for Occupational Safety and Health (NIOSH)-funded Education and Research Centers (ERCs) play a central role in workforce development through graduate education, research training, continuing education, and outreach.

METHODS: This Practice Report describes the Deep South Center for Occupational Safety and Health (DSC), a NIOSH-funded ERC serving parts of the southeastern United States. Between October 2025 and January 2026, a cross-sectional stakeholder survey was administered to DSC program alumni, employers, continuing education (CE) participants, and industry leaders. Data were collected anonymously using Qualtrics XM and included quantitative and open-ended items. Quantitative data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, and qualitative responses were examined using deductive thematic analysis.

RESULTS: A total of 297 stakeholders responded. Respondents represented diverse OSH sectors, with the largest representation from manufacturing, health care, and the private sector. Most DSC alumni reported maintaining employment or securing positions within 12 months of graduation and reported high levels of workforce preparedness. Employers similarly rated graduates as well prepared and reported positive contributions to organizational safety practices. CE participants rated courses highly for quality, relevance, and practical applicability. Respondents consistently emphasized the importance of applied learning, experiential training opportunities, and alignment between academic preparation and workforce needs.

CONCLUSION: Findings highlight the DSC's role in strengthening the regional OSH workforce through integrated graduate education and CE programming. Stakeholders emphasized continued emphasis on experiential learning, flexible delivery modalities, and enhanced research-to-practice translation. Ongoing refinement of programming in response to workforce feedback may further improve preparedness, accessibility, and occupational safety outcomes.

articles.title: A University and Community Partnership to Address Diaper Insecurity Among Infants in Suburban Communities Through Home Visiting Services.
articles.journal: Journal of public health management and practice : JPHMP
articles.abstract:
CONTEXT: Despite overall affluence in a suburban county, diaper insecurity affects many families in low-income communities where poverty rates are 3 times the county average. Existing federal assistance programs do not cover diapers, and transportation barriers in this car-dependent suburb limit access to traditional diaper bank models.

OBJECTIVE: To describe and evaluate a university-community-federally qualified health center (FQHC) partnership model for addressing diaper insecurity among Medicaid-eligible families with infants and toddlers through community health worker (CHW) home visiting services.

DESIGN: Mixed-methods program evaluation using descriptive statistics and thematic analysis of open-ended survey responses.

SETTING: Nassau County, New York.

PARTICIPANTS: Medicaid-eligible families with infants and toddlers enrolled in the Perinatal and Infant Community Health Collaborative (PICHC) program who received 3 or more diaper deliveries (n = 88).

INTERVENTION: A community diaper bank established through a university-FQHC partnership distributed diapers to families via CHW home delivery, eliminating transportation barriers and leveraging existing CHW-client relationships.

MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Diaper distribution volume, participant demographics, financial trade-offs made to afford diapers, psychosocial well-being, and child health outcomes.

RESULTS: From May 2023 to April 2025, the bank distributed 31 457 diapers to 218 family units. Among survey respondents, 45.5% reported that they had previously chosen between diapers and food; 85.2% reported reduced stress; 81.8% reported fewer diaper rashes; and 86.4% felt their community cared about their family.

CONCLUSIONS: Integrating diaper distribution into existing CHW home-visiting infrastructure is a feasible, low-barrier model for addressing material hardship in suburban communities experiencing hidden poverty. Survey participants reported reductions in financial trade-offs and parental stress, and an increased sense of community support; however, the post-only survey design precludes causal inference about program impact.

articles.title: Sexual Health Service Use Among High School Students Accessing School-Based Versus Non-School-Based Sites in a Health Center System.
articles.journal: Journal of public health management and practice : JPHMP
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To preliminarily compare health care utilization, sexual behaviors, and sexual health outcomes among high school students accessing school-based health centers (SBHCs) vs. non-SBHCs and develop an initial hypothesis on the potential impact of SBHCs.

DESIGN: Retrospective chart review.

SETTING: Three SBHC locations and 5 non-SBHCs locations within an adolescent and young adult health center system in Houston, Texas.

PARTICIPANTS: Random sample of 189 high school students receiving care between August 2022 and May 2023 at a SBHC (n = 129) or non-SBHCs (n = 60).

MAIN OUTCOME MEASURE: Demographic characteristics, health center utilization patterns, sexual behaviors, and sexual health outcomes, including sexually transmitted infection (STI) testing and results.

RESULTS: Students accessing SBHCs were more likely to be male (35.9% vs. 21.7%, P = .03) and Spanish-speaking (24.8% vs. 8.3%, P = .01) compared with students accessing non-SBHCs. Students accessing SBHCs also tended to be uninsured at higher rates (70.3% vs. 54.7%, P = .06), although the difference was not statistically significant. SBHC users were less likely to report having a primary care provider (22.5% vs. 41.7%, P = .01) or being sexually active (30.2% vs. 60.0%, P < .001). No significant differences were observed in STI testing rates or STI outcomes between groups.

CONCLUSIONS: These preliminary data show that SBHCs serve adolescents with greater structural barriers to health care, including lack of insurance and limited access to primary care. SBHCs can be accessible points of care within schools that address disparities in health care access. Continued investment and expansion of SBHCs may have positive implications strengthen public health systems by improving access to preventive and sexual health services for underserved youth. Further research is needed to explore correlations between student utilization of health care to SBHC access.

articles.title: Evaluation of a Quality Improvement Project for Pediatric Blood Pressure Screening in Community Clinics Guided by Reach, Effectiveness, Adoption, Implementation, and Maintenance (RE-AIM) Framework.
articles.journal: Journal of public health management and practice : JPHMP
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Pediatric hypertension (HTN) requires accurate, timely diagnosis, and management to prevent long-term adverse cardiac events. Our health system's adherence to the American Academy of Pediatrics best practice guidelines (AAP 2017) was noted to be suboptimal, including gaps in blood pressure (BP) screening, repeat BP measurements after an elevated BP, and documentation. A quality improvement (QI) project was conducted to improve adherence to the guideline among children aged 3-18 years at systemwide pediatric primary care clinics from June 2024 through December 2024.

DESIGN: The QI project was evaluated using the Reach, Effectiveness, Adoption, Implementation, and Maintenance (RE-AIM) framework. Education on accurate BP measurement and AAP guidelines were delivered in primary care clinics within one Southeast health system. Data were extracted from electronic health records 4 times: preintervention, midpoint, postintervention, and 6-month follow-up.

RESULTS: Reach: Participating clinics cared for 9781 children, representing 25.27% of the system's population. Effectiveness: Repeat BP measurement after an elevated BP significantly improved from 5.58% preintervention to 11.22% at follow-up, peaking at 17.29% postintervention (P < 0.01). Overall BP screening rates remained stable over time but significantly improved in clinics providing care for both adults and children. The proportion of elevated BP among boys significantly decreased from preintervention to postintervention, whereas no significant changes were observed among girls. Adoption: Approximately three-quarters (73.33%) of invited clinics participated in the QI project. Implementation: Staff education on accurate BP measurements was the most used implementation strategy across participating clinics (100%). Maintenance: BP screening rates remained stable, and repeated BP measurements were partially sustained at 6-month follow-up.

CONCLUSIONS: This QI project improved adherence to AAP guidelines by increasing accurate BP measurement, primarily through staff education. Further research should explore strategies to improve long-term adherence to pediatric HTN guidelines and address BP measurement challenges in children under the age of 5.

articles.title: Nurse Practitioner-Led Integration of Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonists in Patients With Obesity-Related Heart Failure With Preserved Ejection Fraction: A Prospective Clinical Effectiveness Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Obesity-related heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) is characterized by systemic inflammation and reduced functional capacity. Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) improve symptoms and weight in randomized trials, but uptake in routine cardiovascular practice is inconsistent.

OBJECTIVE: The purpose of this study was to evaluate a structured nurse practitioner-led program for GLP-1 RA initiation in obesity-related HFpEF.

METHODS: Prospective 12-month, single-center pre-post effectiveness study at a U.S. urban academic outpatient cardiology clinic. Adults with left ventricular ejection fraction ≥45%, body mass index ≥30 kg/m2, New York Heart Association class II-III symptoms, and at least 1 cardiometabolic comorbidity were enrolled. The intervention included registry-based identification, baseline assessment, patient education, protocolized titration, and longitudinal follow-up. Each participant's 12-month preenrollment period served as a comparator. The primary outcome was GLP-1 RA initiation and 12-month persistence.

RESULTS: Of 156 enrolled, 128 (82.1%) completed follow-up. Mean age 67.4 ± 11.2 years; 61.7% female; 43.8% Black. GLP-1 RA use rose from 7.8% to 92.2% (87.5% at target dose). Mean weight decreased 6.2 ± 3.8 kg, Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire Clinical Summary Score improved 16.6 ± 11.3 points, and 6-minute walk distance rose 48.3 ± 36.2 m (all P < .001). Systolic blood pressure, hemoglobin A1c (diabetic subgroup), high-sensitivity C-reactive protein, and N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide all decreased significantly. Heart failure hospitalization fell from 18.2% to 4.7% (P = .002). Gastrointestinal symptoms were most common; 4.7% discontinued for intolerance.

CONCLUSIONS: A structured nurse practitioner-led cardiometabolic program was associated with high GLP-1 RA initiation and persistence and with clinically meaningful improvements in symptoms, function, and hospitalization in obesity-related HFpEF.

articles.title: Evaluation of DeepSeek with a RAG-based knowledge base in preoperative assessment for arthroplasty to improve the decision-making accuracy of junior physicians.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients undergoing elective joint replacement are mostly elderly individuals with multiple chronic diseases. These patients have a higher risk, so preoperative assessment for joint replacement is vital for surgical safety but remains challenging for junior physicians. This study aimed to evaluate the decision-making performance of different versions of DeepSeek (Chat and R1) and their knowledge base (KB)-enhanced schemes in perioperative risk assessment and their impact on junior physicians' decision-making quality.

METHODS: A total of 292 anonymized medical records from joint replacement patients were retrospectively analyzed. A professional knowledge base was constructed using 21 perioperative management guidelines and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) technology. The performance of four models (DeepSeek-Chat, DeepSeek-Chat + KB, DeepSeek-R1, and DeepSeek-R1 + KB) was compared in ASA scoring, RCRI scoring, surgical tolerance judgment, and risk prediction. These indicators are related to specific decisions in joint replacement surgery, including preoperative optimization before elective TKA/THA, mitigation of infection risk, planning of VTE prophylaxis, and indication for postponing elective arthroplasty, etc. Senior physicians evaluated model performance using a Likert scale. A 5 × 5 balanced Latin square crossover design was used to assess the impact of model assistance on junior physicians' clinical decision-making.

RESULTS: No significant difference was found in ASA scoring accuracy (p > 0.05). For RCRI scoring and risk stratification, DeepSeek-R1 models (79.1%-79.7%) outperformed Chat models (56.5%-66.0%, p < 0.05). In surgical tolerance assessment, DeepSeek-R1 + KB showed relatively better performance, with significantly better predictive precision (p = 0.0284) and a lower missed diagnosis rate (p = 0.005) compared to the Chat models. The R1 series also showed higher predictive efficiency (87.2%-86.4% vs. 63.6%-61.8%, p < 0.05). The R1 models showed better performance than Chat models in medical comprehension, retrieval accuracy, and reasoning logic. After adjusting for physician variability and patient case mix, the DeepSeek-R1 + KB showed a statistically significant improvement over independent decision-making (OR = 1.58, p = 0.004), as well as the DeepSeek-R1 and Chat series.

CONCLUSION: The DeepSeek-R1 model, with chain-of-thought reasoning, shows a marginal advantage over the Chat version in preoperative assessment for joint replacement. As a cost-effective clinical auxiliary tool, its integration with a professional knowledge base scheme can optimize the decision-making quality of junior physicians, particularly in terms of providing helpful and comprehensive decision support and providing novel insights for individualized assessment in the context of precision medicine.

articles.title: First report of proven Fusarium brachygibbosum sinusitis in a paediatric patient with acute myeloblastic leukaemia.
articles.journal: European journal of clinical microbiology & infectious diseases : official publication of the European Society of Clinical Microbiology
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Fusarium brachygibbosum is an environmental mould belonging to the Fusarium sambucinum species complex (FSAMSC) and is only exceptionally reported as a human pathogen. Invasive fusariosis is a recognized complication in patients with hematological malignancies; however, proven infection caused by F. brachygibbosum has not previously been described. We report the first case of proven breakthrough sinusitis in a pediatric female with refractory acute myeloblastic leukaemia (AML) receiving posaconazole prophylaxis.

METHODS: We describe the clinical presentation, microbiological diagnosis, antifungal susceptibility profile, treatment, and outcome of a 13-year-old neutropenic female with refractory AML who developed invasive fungal sinusitis. Species identification was established by Sanger sequencing of the elongation factor 1-alpha, and antifungal susceptibility testing was performed according to the EUCAST reference method.

RESULTS: Computed tomography revealed extensive paranasal sinus involvement, and direct microscopy of sinus tissue demonstrated hyaline septate hyphae. Culture yielded a mould initially misidentified by MALDI-TOF MS as F. chlamydosporium. Molecular sequencing confirmed F. brachygibbosum. The isolate exhibited elevated Minimal inhibitory concentrations (MICs) to amphotericin B, azoles, echinocandins, and olorofim, while fosmanogepix showed a lower in vitro MIC. Extensive surgical debridement combined with liposomal amphotericin B, voriconazole, and subsequently olorofim was performed. Despite local control of the sinonasal infection and no microbiological or histopathological evidence of dissemination, the patient died 23 days after diagnosis. The death occurred in the context of progressive refractory AML, invasive fungal disease, pulmonary abnormalities, and subsequent neutropenic complications.

CONCLUSION: This report represents the first proven pediatric case of invasive sinusitis caused by F. brachygibbosum (FSAMSC) isolate with higher MICs to classical antifungals. The case highlights the diagnostic limitations of MALDI-TOF MS for rare Fusarium species, the value of molecular identification and antifungal susceptibility testing, and the emergence of environmental moulds breakthrough fungal infections. It also underscores the urgent need for effective novel antifungal agents against resistant Fusarium species.

articles.title: Cyclophilin D deficiency exacerbates diet-induced obesity and selectively enhances skeletal muscle mitochondrial respiration in male mice.
articles.journal: Pflugers Archiv : European journal of physiology
articles.abstract: Mitochondrial dysfunction is a hallmark of obesity-associated metabolic disease, with the mitochondrial permeability transition pore serving as a key regulator of cellular energy homeostasis. Cyclophilin D, encoded by Ppif, is the principal regulatory component of this pore and has been implicated in insulin secretion, adipocyte survival, and whole-body energy balance. However, whether Ppif loss produces a consistent metabolic phenotype when challenged with high fat diet (HFD) exposure, and whether systemic metabolic alterations reflect tissue-specific changes in mitochondrial oxidative capacity, remains unresolved. Here, we characterized male, 21-weeks-old mice with germline Ppif deletion longitudinally over 34 weeks under standard (SD) and HFD using body composition analysis, indirect calorimetry, glucose and insulin tolerance testing and tissue-resolved, Seahorse-based mitochondrial respirometry. Under SD, knockout mice displayed elevated fat mass without differences in food intake or energy expenditure. High-fat feeding progressively amplified this adiposity, with knockout mice developing significantly greater body weight and fat mass than wild-type littermates by weeks 28 and 36. Glucose tolerance and insulin sensitivity remained comparable between genotypes under either diet. ANCOVA revealed significant effects of lean mass (p < 0.001) and genotype (p = 0.017) on energy expenditure, as well as a significant lean mass × genotype interaction (p = 0.025). Consistent with a distinct contribution of lean mass to EE in KO vs. WT mice, we found increased ADP-stimulated mitochondrial respiration in quadriceps of knockout mice under both diets, without corresponding differences in brown adipose tissue or liver, or changes in mitochondrial content across tissues. These findings establish cyclophilin D as a diet- and tissue-specific regulator of energy homeostasis, informing therapeutic strategies targeting the permeability transition pore or cyclophilin D interactome in metabolic disease.

articles.title: Acute Ischaemic Stroke: Therapeutic Targets and Key Modulators of the Fibrinolytic System and Clot Formation.
articles.abstract: The processes of clot formation and clot dissolution with fibrinolysis underpin the pathophysiological mechanisms of acute ischaemic stroke (AIS) and its treatment. Detailed understanding of the modulation of this system is required to develop effective and safe stroke therapeutics. Clot formation occurs with the interaction of the coagulation cascade, along with platelets and fibrin meshwork. Conversely, fibrinolysis involves the serine protease plasmin, its zymogen, plasminogen and its enzymatic conversion by tissue plasminogen activator. The regulators and inhibitors that modulate the interactions in clot formation and fibrinolysis can be potential targets for new and emerging stroke therapies. The aim of this narrative review is to help inform stroke clinicians and researchers about the role of the fibrinolytic system and its inhibitors in AIS and the potential for new therapeutic targets. We outline the processes involved in clot formation and dissolution, the role of endogenous inhibitors of the fibrinolytic system, followed by potential therapeutic targets including tissue plasminogen activators as well as novel therapies and adjuncts. Better understanding of these processes will provide insight into the variable response to current stroke fibrinolytics amongst AIS patients and help to develop new and improved AIS therapeutics in future.

articles.title: Long-Term Quantitative MRI and Quality-of-Life After Endovascular Therapy in Acute Ischemic Stroke - A MR CLEAN-NO IV Substudy.
articles.abstract: This study aims to explore the long-term evolution of endovascular treatment after acute ischemic stroke (AIS) using quantitative MRI, and its relationship with quality of life (QoL). In this long-term substudy of patients from the MR CLEAN-NO IV trial, patients were included who received 24-hour post-stroke MRI and were functionally independent 90 days after stroke onset. Patients underwent a quantitative MRI exam three years after stroke onset to measure focal volume loss, myelin damage, iron deposition, and atrophy within and around the ischemic lesion seen on 24-hour-MRI, in addition to a QoL assessment. Bayesian statistical analyses were used to assess MRI measures lateralized to the ipsilateral hemisphere and to evaluate the relationship of these measures with baseline and treatment characteristics along with QoL. The Bayes Factor (BF) reflected moderate, strong or very strong evidence (BF = 3.0;20;1.5⋅102 respectively). In the 24 included patients, prominent focal volume loss, iron deposition, ventricular enlargement and myelin damage (BF:2.0⋅102) were observed peripheral to the initial 24-hour DWI lesion at long-term FU MRI. In the basal ganglia nuclei, very strong evidence of focal volume loss (BF > 8.1⋅102) and moderate to very strong evidence of iron deposition (BF: 5.0 to 2.7⋅102) were observed at long-term assessment. Higher systolic blood pressure was associated with reduced long-term ventricular atrophy (BF:5.8). Long-term differences in ipsilateral versus contralateral hippocampal volume difference (BF:8.0) and iron deposition (BF:4.1) were moderately associated with QoL. Long-term subtle yet widespread demyelination and iron deposition were observed, and these changes correlated with long-term recovery.

articles.title: Mapping the knowledge landscape and identifying frontiers of mitochondrial dysfunction in sepsis-associated acute kidney injury: a four-decade bibliometric and visualized analysis.
articles.abstract: Mitochondrial dysfunction has been recognized as a central pathogenic event and is under active investigation as a candidate therapeutic target in sepsis-associated acute kidney injury (SA-AKI). This study aims to employ multi-tool bibliometric analysis to systematically map the four-decade intellectual landscape of this field, thereby identifying emerging research hotspots and outlining priority-setting directions for future pharmacological investigation. Because publication and citation metrics quantify scholarly attention rather than therapeutic efficacy, the pathways highlighted here reflect research trends and priority-setting signals, not established therapeutic targets. A comprehensive literature retrieval was conducted across PubMed, Web of Science, and Scopus up to March 18, 2026. Following rigorous data cleaning, 837 publications were analyzed using CiteSpace, VOSviewer, and the bibliometrix R package to visually evaluate publication trends, knowledge networks, and evolving research hotspots. Cumulative publication output exhibits sustained exponential growth (R2 = 0.997), accelerating significantly post-2010. China and the USA dominate global productivity, though institutional collaboration networks reveal pronounced regional clustering. Notably, publication hubs have transitioned significantly from traditional critical care journals to molecular and pharmacological journals, consistent with a shifting emphasis of scholarly attention toward molecular and pharmacological research themes. Keyword and citation burst analyses suggest that the research frontier has evolved from broad physiological observations to specific subcellular executioners. Mitochondria-mediated programmed cell death (apoptosis, pyroptosis, and ferroptosis) and oxidative stress have become the most prominent bibliometric hotspots and candidate pharmacological targets. The field of SA-AKI research has shown a pronounced, publication-driven shift from clinical phenotyping to the target-driven molecular deconstruction of mitochondrial damage; we emphasize that this result reflects research priorities, not proven therapeutic efficacy of these targets. To overcome current translational bottlenecks and off-target effects of existing agents, future drug development should transition from isolated in vitro models toward clinical multi-omics validation. Developing innovative targeted delivery systems (such as engineered nanomaterials and exosomes) and multi-target synergistic therapies will need rigorous empirical testing to determine whether they can precisely mitigate the complex SA-AKI "mitochondrial storm".

articles.title: Medical cannabis for the treatment of insomnia.
articles.journal: The Cochrane database of systematic reviews
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE: Insomnia is highly prevalent and associated with substantial individual and societal burden, while existing pharmacological treatments are limited by adverse effects and concerns about long-term use. The role of medical cannabis in the treatment of insomnia remains unclear because of limited and heterogeneous evidence. Despite increasing clinical use, current guidelines do not provide clear recommendations due to uncertainty regarding its efficacy and safety. A clear synthesis of available evidence is needed to inform patients, clinicians, and policymakers about the potential benefits and harms of medical cannabis for insomnia.

OBJECTIVES: To assess the benefits and harms of medical cannabis in adults with insomnia.

SEARCH METHODS: We used CENTRAL, MEDLINE, Embase, Global Index Medicus, and two trial registers, together with reference checking, citation searching, and contacting study authors, to identify studies for inclusion in the review. The latest search date was 5 April 2025.

ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA: We included parallel randomized controlled trials (RCTs), cross-over RCTs, and cluster RCTs in adult participants with any type of insomnia comparing medical cannabis with placebo, benzodiazepine receptor agonists, benzodiazepines, melatonin receptor agonists, antidepressants, and antipsychotics. We excluded studies that were quasi-RCTs and studies using experimental and unregistered drugs, cannabis receptor antagonists and negative allosteric modulators like rimonabant, as well as modulators that enhance endocannabinoid system activity, such as fatty acid amide hydrolase inhibitors, and synthetic cannabis, like levonantradol.

OUTCOMES: Our critical outcomes were quality of sleep/satisfaction with sleep, total sleep time and adverse events. Our important outcomes included sleep onset latency, wake after sleep onset, daytime functioning, withdrawal symptoms, and quality of life.

RISK OF BIAS: We used the Cochrane RoB 2 tool for parallel RCTs and the Cochrane RoB 2 tool for cross-over RCTs.

SYNTHESIS METHODS: We synthesized results for each outcome using meta-analysis where possible, using a random-effects model. Where this was not possible due to the nature of the data, we synthesized results narratively. We used GRADE to assess the certainty of evidence for our critical outcomes, daytime functioning and quality of life for the comparison of medical cannabis versus placebo.

INCLUDED STUDIES: We included nine studies with 537 participants aged 18 to 76 years. Most studies included predominantly female populations (72.66%), focused mainly on participants with primary insomnia, although one study focused on insomnia associated with comorbidities. Three studies included patients with acute insomnia, and six included patients with chronic insomnia. One study compared medical cannabis with antidepressants (amitriptyline), while the other eight studies compared medical cannabis with a placebo. Two studies used licensed medications (one plant-based cannabinoid, one synthetic cannabinoid), and the other seven studies used magistral preparations.

SYNTHESIS OF RESULTS: Medical cannabis versus placebo The synthesized evidence from our comparison indicates that, compared with placebo, medical cannabis may have little to no clinically meaningful effect on the quality of sleep/satisfaction with sleep (SMD -0.49, 95%CI -1.06 to 0.08, I2 = 91%; 7 studies, 374 participants, very low-certainty evidence), total sleep time (MD 7.68 minutes, 95% CI -23.04 to 38.39; I2 = 80%; 6 studies, 194 participants; very low-certainty evidence), and daytime functioning (SMD -0.34, 95% CI -0.83 to 0.16; I2 = 65%, 5 studies, 144 participants; very low-certainty evidence), and may improve quality of life (SMD 0.84, 95% CI -0.61 to 2.29; I2 = 78%; 3 studies, 95 participants; very low-certainty evidence), but the evidence is very uncertain. Additionally, medical cannabis may result in a slight increase in adverse events (OR 11.25, 95% CI 4.46 to 28.35; I2 = 0%; 3 studies, 98 participants; low-certainty evidence; participants with adverse events in the intervention period: 37; in the placebo period: 0; in both periods: 14; in neither period: 47). The main reasons for downgrading the certainty of the evidence were high risk of bias, serious inconsistency, and imprecision.

AUTHORS' CONCLUSIONS: Medical cannabis may have little to no clinically meaningful effect on quality of sleep/satisfaction with sleep, total sleep time, or daytime functioning. It may lead to an improvement in quality of life, although the evidence is very uncertain. Medical cannabis may result in a slight increase in adverse events, but the certainty of this evidence is low. Future research must address the substantial uncertainty in the current evidence by conducting adequately powered, well-designed randomized trials with longer follow-up, standardized outcomes, and detailed reporting of efficacy and safety, including long-term harms. In addition, studies should explicitly incorporate equity considerations by enrolling more diverse populations and reporting disaggregated data by sex, age, and other relevant characteristics to improve the applicability and fairness of the evidence base.

FUNDING: This Cochrane review had no dedicated funding.

REGISTRATION: Protocol: https://doi.org/10.1002/14651858.CD016216.

articles.title: Substantial improvement in short-term survivorship in patients receiving robotic arm-assisted medial unicompartmental knee arthroplasty : a retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Robotic arm-assisted unicompartmental knee arthroplasty (R-UKA) has been shown to improve alignment and accuracy of component placement compared with conventional unicompartmental knee arthroplasty (C-UKA). Despite this, there is conflicting evidence for whether this has an impact on revision rates.

METHODS: We performed a retrospective analysis of a prospective database, comparing patients who underwent R-UKA using the Stryker Restoris MCK implant with those who underwent C-UKA using the cemented Oxford Partial Knee implant, between January 2002 and December 2024 at The Prince Charles Hospital (Brisbane, Australia), with a minimum six-month follow-up. Patient selection for UKA mirrored the recommendations by Kozinn and Scott. The primary outcome of interest was to compare the all-cause revision rate between these two groups. Secondary outcomes of interest were to compare hospital length of stay (HLOS), surgical duration, the odds of superficial surgical site infection, and the odds of periprosthetic joint infection (PJI) between the same groups. The analysis of individual outcomes were adjusted for age, sex, BMI, American Society of Anesthesiologists grade, Charlson Comorbidity Index, and primary surgeon grade.

RESULTS: The hazard of all-cause revision significantly decreased by 78% in the R-UKA group as compared with the C-UKA group (p = 0.046). HLOS was also significantly shorter by 2.2 days (95% CI 1.0 to 3.3) in the R-UKA group (p < 0.001). There was no significant difference in the surgical duration (p = 0.733), odds of superficial surgical site infection (p = 0.845), nor in the odds of PJI (p = 0.415) between the two groups.

CONCLUSION: The substantial improvement in revision outcomes suggests that R-UKA is the option of choice for managing symptomatic unicompartmental knee arthritis in carefully selected patients with isolated medial compartmental osteoarthritis, especially in the hands of low-volume surgeons. Decreased HLOS should be interpreted with caution, given the non-contemporaneous nature of the two cohorts.

articles.title: How Would You Screen This 26-Year-Old Woman for Cervical Cancer? Grand Rounds Discussion From Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center.
articles.abstract: Cervical cancer is the third most common gynecologic cancer, with more than 13 000 new cases diagnosed in 2025. The incidence of and mortality from cervical cancer vary across racial and ethnic groups and in persons living in medically underserved or geographically isolated areas, with half of all cervical cancers occurring in women who are underscreened or have never been screened. Persistent infection with high-risk types of human papillomavirus (HPV) is the most important risk factor for cervical cancer and is associated with nearly all cases. Although genital tract HPV infection is common, most HPV infections are transient, and cervical cancer occurs in only a small portion of patients with HPV. For decades, cervical cancer screening relied on annual cytologic assessment. A growing understanding of the role of HPV infection in the natural progression of cervical cancer has led to updated screening recommendations from the American Cancer Society and the Women's Preventive Services Initiative, as well as a draft update from the U.S. Preventive Services Task Force. These recommendations include primary HPV testing as a preferred screening strategy and include an option for self-collected specimens for HPV testing. Here, 2 experts in this field, a primary care physician and an obstetrics and gynecology physician, debate how to apply these guidelines when screening a patient for cervical cancer. They discuss a range of screening options and consider the challenges of applying these guidelines across different age groups and in patients at increased risk.

articles.title: Delirium.
articles.abstract: Delirium is a common, acute confusional state that is associated with adverse patient, caregiver, and health system outcomes. All patients are at risk for delirium, although those with advanced age or acute infection and those taking sedatives and anticholinergics are at greater risk. The pathophysiology of delirium is complex and includes neuronal injury, inflammation, metabolic imbalance, and blood-brain barrier disruption. It is important to note that delirium is preventable; recognizing people at risk and identifying and addressing predisposing and precipitating factors is paramount. No single intervention or medication has been shown to be effective in treating delirium; therefore, standard-of-care treatments rely on multifaceted strategies to address contributing factors.

articles.title: Molecular Imaging of Thrombotic Sources of Ischemic Stroke.
The Amyloid Atrium: A Distinct Phenotype Demanding a Distinct Paradigm.
Approach to Heart Failure With Mildly Reduced Left Ventricular Ejection Fraction.
Cardiovascular Complications of Chronic Liver Disease.
articles.abstract: Chronic liver disease is an increasingly prevalent and heterogeneous syndrome with important consequences for cardiovascular function. As the global burdens of chronic liver disease and cirrhosis continue to rise, cardiovascular disease has emerged as a major driver of overall morbidity and mortality in affected patients. Despite the growing recognition of the intersectionality between hepatology and cardiology care clinically, cardiovascular disease risk among patients with liver disease is underrecognized. This state-of-the-art review summarizes the current understanding of the bidirectional interactions between the liver and the cardiovascular system. Shared mechanisms-including inflammation, endothelial injury, and neurohormonal overactivation-that contribute to the development of adverse myocardial remodeling, atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, heart failure, arrhythmias, pulmonary vascular syndromes, and cirrhosis-associated cardiovascular syndromes are reviewed. A specific focus is placed on metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease, the most common form of chronic liver disease, while highlighting the distinct cardiovascular manifestations associated with other types of chronic liver disease. These include alcohol-associated liver disease and infiltrative diseases that affect the liver and heart with cardiovascular implications across the spectrum from early stages of liver disease through cirrhosis. We discuss practical approaches to detecting liver disease, including the assessment of liver fibrosis noninvasively in individuals at risk. We discuss the approach to assessing cardiovascular risk through cardiac imaging, biomarkers, and cardiac functional testing once chronic liver disease is detected. Management considerations for commonly encountered cardiovascular conditions and a critical appraisal of the evolving evidence supporting cardiometabolic therapies in patients with chronic liver disease are discussed to underscore potential cardiovascular and liver benefits. Critical evidence gaps and future research priorities are identified, including the development and evaluation of liver-informed cardiovascular risk models, incorporation of cardiovascular end points into liver disease trials, and implementation of integrated cardiohepatometabolic care pathways. Improved recognition of chronic liver disease and related cardiovascular disease risk represents a major opportunity to facilitate earlier disease detection, enhance risk stratification, and improve outcomes across the spectrum of chronic liver disease.

articles.title: Comparison of Outcomes between Teacher-Led Large Group Teaching and Scenario-based Team Learning in Physiology among Phase I MBBS.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In Indian medical colleges, physiology is taught largely using a conventional lecture-based format with its focus on factual information and memorization instead of understanding and application, leading to passive learning. Team-based learning (TBL) is a highly structured form of active-learning strategy designed to integrate engagement, accountability, and application of knowledge to promote learning in large classes. Despite being well-established globally, evidence from Indian medical colleges remains sparse.

AIM: The aim of our study is to compare the students' academic performance and perception between teacher-led large-group teaching (TLGT) and scenario-based team learning (SBTL) in selected topics of Physiology among Phase-I MBBS students with regards to conceptual clarity, knowledge retention, teamwork, motivation, communication and readiness for examination.

METHODOLOGY: A mixed-methods approach was adapted, where 167 Phase-I MBBS students participated in both lecture-based classes and team-based learning sessions. Learning outcomes were measured by pretest and posttest scores, a 20-item questionnaire (represented with a Likert scale of 1 = strongly disagree, 5 = strongly agree) and focus-group discussions (FGDs) of students and faculty. Quantitative data were analyzed with descriptive statistics and paired t-tests, and qualitative data were interpreted by Braun and Clarke's six-phase thematic analysis framework.

RESULTS: Substantial improvements were seen in academic performance (knowledge acquisition) on postintervention analysis (pretest = 9.8 ± 2.4; posttest = 15.6 ± 3.1; P < 0.001; Cohen's d = 1.02), suggesting a highly significant increase in the mean academic scores for SBTL as against lectures. Quantitative analysis of the Likert scale perception study showed that there was a general preference for SBTL (mean = 3.96) over lecture sessions (mean = 3.83) by students. The perception scores of students showed a strongly agree opinion for TBL improving understanding of subject concepts (4.35 ± 0.71), retention (4.22 ± 0.76), teamwork (4.31 ± 0.72), communication (4.18 ± 0.79), and motivation (4.27 ± 0.78). Thematic analysis revealed the major advantages of SBTL as active engagement/involvement, working as a team, correlating clinically, and retention is better, whereas challenges include time constraint, unequal participation and the need for training facilitators to implement TBL better. Student and faculty FGDs reinforced these findings: students reported enhanced participation, peer learning, and motivation, while faculty emphasized improved engagement but raised concerns about preparation time and curricular scheduling. The overall results comply with the international literature and systematic reviews supporting the role of team-based learning as a pedagogical tool to promote self-directed learning, collaboration and use of physiological knowledge in clinical reasoning.

CONCLUSIONS: Scenario-based team learning (SBTL) is a good evidence-based pedagogy for physiology teaching in CBME. A blended model of small, short, concept-oriented lectures followed by structured SBTL sessions are ideal for effective knowledge practice integration. Required faculty preparations, student preparedness and well-designed facilitator guides are essential prerequisites for successful implementation of SBTL.

articles.title: From Rare to Rising: A Story of Enterobacter-associated Pneumonia Evolving in the Community.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Pneumonia is a common cause of mortality and morbidity worldwide and is the fifth leading cause of death. It is generally caused by Streptococcus pneumoniae, Klebsiella pneumoniae, Haemophilus influenzae, and some atypical microorganisms. Interestingly, a member of ESKAPE pathogens, mainly Enterobacter cloacae complex, is increasingly showing its presence in the samples of lower respiratory tract specimens. Emergence of multidrug resistance (MDR) in these bacteria, including resistance to last-resort carbapenems, has led to an increased interest in this organism causing pneumonia.

AIMS AND OBJECTIVES: (1) Prevalence of E. cloacae complex among community-acquired pneumonia (CAP) patients and (2) antibiotic resistance pattern of these pathogens.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Respiratory samples from adult patients were processed according to standard microbiological techniques, including direct smear examination, incubation in blood, MacConkey and chocolate agar plates, and Gram staining. Identification of E. cloacae complex and antibiotic susceptibility testing, along with resistance patterns, was performed by automated ID/AST instrument.

RESULTS: About 15.7% of E. cloacae complex-associated CAP patients were found over a 1-year study period. Antimicrobial susceptibility tests indicated a MDR profile in 58.3% of isolates. Resistance was mostly to carbapenems (72.73%), followed by aztreonam (69.7%), piperacillin-tazobactam (68%), and fluoroquinolones (63.6%).

CONCLUSION: E. cloacae complex is an emerging and clinically significant pathogen causing CAP. Its MDR profile contributes to an increased tendency to intensive care unit admission and the development of sepsis. Hence, detecting this pathogen in lower respiratory tract specimens should be treated as a high alert and should prompt treatment at the earliest.

articles.title: Validation of Baveno VII Criteria using Liver and Splenic Elastography for Predicting Esophageal Varices Severity in Chronic Liver Disease: A Multiparametric, Observational Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Baveno VII criteria prioritize Liver Stiffness Measurement (LSM) for portal hypertension risk stratification, primarily using transient elastography. We aimed to evaluate two-dimensional-shear wave elastography (2D-SWE) cutoffs, assess the etiology-dependent utility of spleen stiffness (SSM), and introduce a novel Combined Hepato-splenic Stiffness Index (CHSSI).

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This ambispective, observational study enrolled 100 chronic liver disease patients. Participants underwent 2D-SWE for LSM and SSM, alongside endoscopy as the reference standard. A novel multiparametric index, CHSSI, was formulated. Diagnostic accuracy for Varices Needing Treatment (VNT; Grade >= II) was assessed using area under the receiver operating characteristic (AUROC).

RESULTS: The cohort was predominantly Alcohol-related Liver Disease (ALD, 49%) and Viral Hepatitis (30%). LSM independently predicted VNT (P < 0.001), with an optimal 2D-SWE cutoff of 19.2 kPa (sensitivity 90% and specificity 82%). SSM utility diverged by etiology: it correlated significantly with variceal grade in ALD (r = 0.549, P < 0.001) but poorly in viral cirrhosis (r = 0.174, P = 0.358). The novel CHSSI demonstrated excellent diagnostic performance (AUROC 0.892) for predicting VNT.

CONCLUSIONS: Liver stiffness remains the most robust single-parameter surrogate for esophageal varices. However, in heterogeneous cohorts where splenic stiffness alone yields inconsistent results, novel composite indices such as CHSSI and Liver Size-stiffness Index offer superior discriminative ability. These findings support a refined noninvasive risk stratification strategy, potentially reducing unnecessary screening endoscopies.

articles.title: Current Practices of Laryngoscope Blade Cleaning, Sterilization, and Disinfection Postintubation: A Survey of Indian Healthcare Facilities.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Reusable laryngoscope blades are exposed to oropharyngeal secretions, blood, and mucosal surfaces during airway procedures. Incomplete reprocessing can make them a preventable source of cross-contamination. This survey assessed current practices related to cleaning, disinfection, sterilization, storage, and monitoring of laryngoscope blades in Indian healthcare facilities.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This cross-sectional survey was conducted in January 2026 among 97 healthcare professionals involved in airway management or laryngoscope handling. Data were collected using a structured 20-item questionnaire through online forms and direct interviews. Responses were analyzed using descriptive statistics. Associations between selected practice-related variables were assessed using the Chi-square test, with P < 0.05 considered statistically significant.

RESULTS: Reusable laryngoscopes were reported by 96 respondents (99.0%). A written disinfection protocol was available in 59 facilities (60.8%). High-level disinfection was reported by 23 respondents (23.7%), whereas 20 (20.6%) were unaware of the disinfection level followed at their workplace. Swab and culture-based sterility assurance was practiced by 29 respondents (29.9%), whereas 41 (42.3%) reported no sterility testing. Inadequate postreprocessing storage was reported by 72 respondents (74.3%), and regular audit was absent in 68 facilities (70.1%). Written protocol availability was significantly associated with high-level disinfection practice (P = 0.002). Guideline familiarity was associated with sterility testing (P < 0.001), and professional role was associated with inspection frequency (P = 0.031).

CONCLUSION: Significant gaps were observed in laryngoscope blade reprocessing, particularly in high-level disinfection, sterility verification, storage, and audit systems. Written protocols, repeated hands-on training, objective monitoring, and structured preuse inspection can improve compliance and patient safety.

articles.title: VPS34 regulation in pulmonary arterial vascular smooth muscle cells in pulmonary hypertension.
articles.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) is characterized by the hyperproliferative phenotype of pulmonary arterial smooth muscle cells (PAVSMCs) and extensive extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling. Vacuolar protein sorting 34 (VPS34), a Class III Phosphatidylinositol-3 Kinase (PI3K), regulates cell proliferation, but its specific function in pulmonary vascular remodeling remains poorly understood. We aim to determine the role of VPS34 activation and regulation in PAVSMC proliferation, matrix deposition, and the progression of PAH. First, we found a marked decrease in the inhibitory phosphorylation of VPS34 at Ser164 (P-S164-VPS34), indicative of constitutive VPS34 activation, in remodeled pulmonary arteries (PAs) from human PAH patients and male mice exposed to Sugen/Hypoxia (SuHx). In human PAH PAVSMCs, siRNA-mediated knockdown of VPS34 or pharmacological inhibition via the selective inhibitor SAR405 significantly blunted cell proliferation and reduced the production of fibronectin, a major component of the remodeled ECM. Mechanistically, we found that Akt activation in PAH PAVSMCs promotes VPS34 activation; Protein Phosphatase 1 Catalytic Subunit Alpha is a potential effector in VPS34 activation; and active VPS34 led to the activation of the mTOR/S6 signaling pathway with tuberous sclerosis complex 2 downregulation. Finally, in vivo treatment with SAR405 attenuated right ventricular systolic pressure, right ventricular hypertrophy, and pulmonary vascular remodeling in SuHx mice, while concurrently decreasing vascular fibronectin deposition. Our study demonstrates that VPS34 activation, driven by an Akt-mediated loss of the inhibitory P-S164, is crucial in PAVSMC proliferation and fibrotic vascular remodeling in PAH. Targeting the VPS34 axis represents a promising anti-remodeling therapeutic strategy for the treatment of PAH.

CLINICAL RELEVANCE: What is new?: This study identifies VPS34 activation via loss of the inhibitory Ser164 Phosphorylation as a previously unrecognized mechanism promoting pulmonary arterial smooth muscle cell (PAVSMC) hyperproliferation, pulmonary vascular remodeling, and pulmonary hypertension.VPS34 activation increases PAVSMC-derived fibronectin production, highlighting the potential role of VPS34 in regulating extracellular matrix remodeling.Pharmacological inhibition of VPS34 by SAR405 decreased PAH PAVSMC proliferation and pulmonary vascular remodeling.What are the clinical implications?: There is no FDA-approved VPS34 inhibitor, but chemicals or macromolecules targeting VPS34 activation, at least in PAVSMC, could be beneficial against pulmonary vascular remodeling and pulmonary hypertension progression.Further understanding the regulation of extracellular matrix remodeling by VPS34 can also spark new therapies for pulmonary vascular diseases.

articles.title: Left ventricular ejection fraction recovery under contemporary quadruple guideline-directed therapy and the need for ICD/CRT-D implantation in HFrEF: a retrospective single-center cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Guidelines advise deferring primary-prevention implantable cardioverter-defibrillator (ICD) or cardiac resynchronization therapy-defibrillator (CRT-D) implantation until left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) is reassessed after at least three months of medical therapy in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF). Real-world data under contemporary quadruple therapy are limited.

RESEARCH DESIGN AND METHODS: Retrospective single-center cohort of 65 HFrEF patients (Coburg Hospital, Germany; October 2023-December 2024), prescribed beta-blocker, angiotensin receptor-neprilysin inhibitor, mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist and SGLT2 inhibitor (all four in 92%; doses not recorded). LVEF was measured by echocardiography (TTE) and cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) at baseline and ~3 months; reader blinding was not documented. Device implantation followed guideline criteria. Patients with severe arrhythmic events were excluded.

RESULTS: Twenty-nine patients (44.6%) received a device. LVEF rose on TTE (28.0→36.0%) and CMR (26.3→38.5%) (both p < 0.001), mainly without device implantation (TTE +13.0 vs + 1.5 points). Larger baseline left ventricular end-diastolic diameter was associated with smaller recovery (β = -0.41, p = 0.006) and device implantation (odds ratio 1.11/mm, 95% CI 1.01-1.22). Adverse events were not recorded.

CONCLUSIONS: LVEF recovery was common, and associations are consistent with disease severity. Findings are hypothesis-generating; absent dose, arrhythmic-outcome and wearable-defibrillator data and the selected cohort limit generalizability.

articles.title: [Efficacy of bidirectional switching therapy between adrenal ablation and adrenalectomy in patients with primary aldosteronism].
articles.abstract: To investigate the efficacy in patients with primary aldosteronism (PA) who converted from adrenal ablation to surgical intervention or from surgical intervention to adrenal ablation. A retrospective analysis was performed on the clinical data of patients with PA who sequentially underwent transcatheter adrenal ablation and surgical intervention (regardless of treatment sequence) admitted to Daping Hospital, Army Medical University between June 2018 and June 2025. Patients were divided into the post-ablation surgery group and post-surgery ablation group according to the treatment sequence. Clinical data, PA classification, and primary causes for second intervention were collected. Biochemical and clinical outcomes after second treatment were evaluated in accordance with the PA surgical outcome criteria. A total of 10 patients were enrolled, including 8 males and 2 females, with the age of (42.6±14.0) years. There were 7 cases in the ablation-then-surgery group and 3 cases in the surgery-then-ablation group. Adrenal CT scans revealed nodular lesions (adenomas) in all 10 PA patients. The indications for the second intervention in both groups were persistent hypertension, failure to achieve the target plasma aldosterone-to-renin ratio, with or without hypokalemia, following the initial treatment. In the ablation-then-surgery group, 6 patients had left-sided lesions and 5 were male, with a median interval between the two procedures of 1.5 (1.0, 2.0) years. All patients in the surgery-then-ablation group were male, and the interval between the two procedures ranged from 2 to 12 years. Patients were followed-up 1 year after second intervention. The post-ablation surgery group exhibited complete biochemical success in 4 cases and partial biochemical success in 3 cases; complete clinical success was noted in 1 case and partial clinical success in 6 cases. In the post-surgery ablation group, complete biochemical success was seen in 3 cases, complete clinical success in 1 case, and partial clinical resolution in 2 cases. Male patients predominated among PA patients undergoing re-intervention, and favorable biochemical and clinical responses could be achieved by second intervention.

articles.title: [Correlation between peripheral blood inflammatory markers and Wagner grade as well as IWGDF/IDSA infection grade in patients with diabetic foot infection].
articles.abstract: Objective: To investigate the correlation between peripheral blood inflammatory markers and Wagner grade as well as Interhational Working Group on the Diabetic Foot (IWGDF)/Infections Diseases Society of America (IDSA) infection grade in patients with diabetic foot infection (DFI). Methods: A retrospective analysis was performed on the clinical data of 396 patients with type 2 DFI who were hospitalized at the Ninth Medical Center of PLA General Hospital from January 1, 2021 to December 31, 2023. Patients were classified into grade 2, grade 3 and grade 4 according to Wagner classification, and divided into mild, moderate and severe groups according to IWGDF/IDSA infection classification. The levels of peripheral blood inflammatory markers were compared among patients with different grades. Spearman rank correlation analysis was used to explore the association between inflammatory markers and the two grading systems. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve was used to evaluate the diagnostic efficacy of each inflammatory marker for Wagner grade 4 and severe IWGDF/IDSA infection. Results: Among the 396 DFI patients, 281 were males and 115 were females, with the age of (64.7±11.3) years. According to Wagner classification, there were 58 cases of grade 2, 196 cases of grade 3, 130 cases of grade 4, and 12 cases with missing grading. According to IWGDF/IDSA infection classification, there were 62 mild cases, 218 moderate cases and 116 severe cases. There were statistically significant differences in platelet count (PLT), platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (PLR), neutrophil percentage, neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), monocyte-to-lymphocyte ratio (MLR), high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hs-CRP), fibrinogen degradation products (FDP), fibrinogen (FIB), C-reactive protein (CRP) and erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) among DFI patients with different Wagner grades (all P<0.05). The levels of white blood cell count (WBC), PLT, PLR, neutrophil percentage, NLR, MLR, hs-CRP, FDP, FIB, CRP and ESR were significantly different among patients with different IWGDF/IDSA infection grades (all P<0.05). Spearman rank correlation analysis showed that both grading systems were positively correlated with PLT, PLR, neutrophil percentage, NLR, MLR, hs-CRP, FIB, CRP and ESR, and negatively correlated with FDP (all P<0.05). ROC curve analysis showed that WBC, PLR, NLR, hs-CRP, CRP and ESR had diagnostic value for both severe IWGDF/IDSA infection and Wagner grade 4 (all P<0.001), with under the curve (AUC) ranging from 0.663 to 0.783. The AUC of all indicators for the diagnosis of severe IWGDF/IDSA infection was higher than that for Wagner grade 4 (all P<0.05). Conclusions: The levels of peripheral blood inflammatory markers in DFI patients are closely correlated with the severity of Wagner grade and IWGDF/IDSA infection grade. WBC, PLR, NLR, hs-CRP, CRP and ESR exhibit better diagnostic performance for severe IWGDF/IDSA infection than for Wagner grade 4.

articles.title: [Risk factors for pulmonary hemorrhage and severe infection in leptospirosis patients and construction of a prediction model].
articles.abstract: Objective: To investigate the risk factors for pulmonary hemorrhage and severe infection in adult leptospirosis patients and to construct a prediction model. Method: A retrospective analysis was conducted on patients with leptospirosis admitted to the First Affiliated Hospital of Wenzhou Medical University from August 2017 to September 2025. Patients were divided into a non-pulmonary hemorrhage group (n=95) and a pulmonary hemorrhage group (n=63) based on the presence or absence of pulmonary hemorrhage. Multivariate logistic regression model was used to analyze the risk factors for pulmonary hemorrhage and severe infection. A prediction model was constructed and a nomogram was developed. Bootstrap method was used for internal validation of the model, and the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), Hosmer-Lemeshow test, calibration curve and decision curve analysis were used to evaluate the model performance. Results: A total of 158 patients (141 males) were enrolled, with the age [M (Q1,Q3)] of 66 (57, 72) years. Among them, 95 (60.1%) were classified as the pulmonary hemorrhage type and 63 (39.9%) were non-pulmonary hemorrhage type. Compared with the non-pulmonary hemorrhage group, the pulmonary hemorrhage group had lower hemoglobin [(96.7±16.2) vs (119.1±18.9) g/L], lower platelet count [32.0 (13.5, 70.5)×10⁹/L vs 95.0 (55.0, 141.0)×10⁹/L], lower albumin level [26.4(24.3,28.4) vs. 29.9(26.9,32.5) g/L] and higher serum creatinine [230.0 (141.5, 342.0) vs 133.0 (87.0, 262.0) μmol/L], with all differences being statistically significant (all P<0.05). Logistic regression model analysis identified a symptom onset-to-admission time exceeding 3 days (OR=2.53, 95%CI: 1.03-6.26, P=0.042), thrombocytopenia (OR=1.80, 95%CI: 1.15-2.81, P=0.010), and hypoproteinemia (OR=3.95, 95%CI: 1.25-12.48, P=0.019) as independent risk factors for pulmonary hemorrhage. On this basis, a diagnostic prediction model incorporating these risk factors together with the degree of anemia was established, with an AUC of 0.886 (95%CI: 0.835-0.937). At the maximum Youden index, the sensitivity and specificity were 80.9% and 82.1%, respectively. The Hosmer-Lemeshow test indicated that all the aforementioned models demonstrated satisfactory calibration (χ2=9.104, P=0.334). The calibration curve indicated good calibration. Decision curve analysis demonstrated a stable net benefit across the clinical decision threshold range of 0.05-0.85. Conclusions: A symptom onset-to-admission time exceeding 3 days, thrombocytopenia, and hypoproteinemia are independent risk factors for pulmonary hemorrhage in adult leptospirosis patients. The prediction model based on these risk factors may facilitate identification of patients at high risk of pulmonary hemorrhage.

articles.title: [Mid-pregnancy atherogenic index of plasma associated with early postpartum abnormal glucose metabolism in women with previous gestational diabetes].
articles.abstract: Objective: To investigate the relationship between the atherogenic index of plasma (AIP) during mid-pregnancy and abnormal glucose metabolism (AGM) in early postpartum period among women with previous gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM). Methods: In this retrospective cohort study, women with previous GDM who attended the Department of Endocrinology and Metabolism, Shanghai General Hospital, Shanghai Jiao Tong University School of Medicine, between December 2014 and June 2021 were recruited. Based on the outcomes of the 75 g oral glucose tolerance test (OGTT) performed at 4 to 12 weeks postpartum, the patients were classified into normal glucose tolerance (NGT) group and AGM group. Demographic characteristics, glycemic and lipid profiles, and AIP levels at mid-pregnancy and postpartum were compared between the two groups. Logistic regression analysis was used to identify the risk factors for postpartum AGM, and restricted cubic spline (RCS) analysis was performed to assess the dose-response relationship between mid-pregnancy AIP and postpartum AGM. Results: Finally, 921 women completed follow-up at 4 to 12 weeks postpartum, among whom 626 (68.0%) exhibited NGT and 295 (32.0%) were diagnosed with AGM.Compared with the NGT group, the AGM group had significantly higher AIP levels during both mid-pregnancy and postpartum peroid (P<0.05). Logistic regression identified age, insulin therapy during pregnancy, mid-pregnancy fasting plasma glucose (FPG), and AIP were independent risk factors for postpartum AGM; each 1 unit increase in AIP was associated with a 237.6% increased risk of postpartum AGM (OR=3.376, 95%CI: 1.431 to 7.964, P<0.01). After full adjustment for age, pre-pregnancy body mass index (pre-BMI), gestational weight gain rate, diabetic family history, insulin therapy during pregnancy, FPG, low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C), and total cholesterol (TC), each 1-standard-deviation (SD) increase in the Z-score-standardized AIP was associated with a 25.3% increased risk of postpartum AGM (OR=1.253, 95%CI: 1.069 to 1.470, P<0.01). RCS analysis demonstrated a linear positive association between mid-pregnancy AIP and the risk of postpartum AGM (P for overall=0.020; P for nonlinearity=0.697). When mid-pregnancy AIP>0.093, the risk of postpartum AGM showed an increasing trend. Subgroup analyses stratified by age (<35 vs ≥35 years), pre-BMI (<24 vs ≥24 kg/m2), and insulin therapy during pregnancy (yes vs no) revealed that there was no interaction between mid-pregnancy AIP levels and the risk of AGM across any of the subgroups (all P for interaction>0.05). Conclusion: Mid-pregnancy AIP level was independently and positively correlated with the risk of early postpartum AGM in women with GDM.

articles.title: [Expert consensus on the clinical application of continuous glucose monitoring in critically ill patients (2026 edition)].
authors: Branch of Critical Care Medicine, China Association for Disaster & Emergency Rescue Medicine
articles.abstract: Glycemic fluctuations are highly prevalent among critically ill patients. Glycemic abnormalities constitute an independent risk factor for adverse outcomes, and their effective identification and management are essential to improving clinical prognosis in this population. Continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) technology, which continuously and in real time captures interstitial fluid glucose concentrations, provides multidimensional glycemic metrics and offers a novel technical approach to overcoming the inherent limitations of conventional intermittent glucose monitoring, thereby enabling refined glycemic management in critically ill patients. However, systematic guidance for its standardized application in the intensive care units (ICU) setting remains lacking. To address this gap, the Branch of Critical Care Medicine, China Association for Disaster and Emergency Rescue Medicine, convened a multidisciplinary panel of experts in critical care medicine, endocrinology, and nursing. Drawing on international evidence-based literature and clinical practice issues specific to China, the panel jointly developed the present consensus, with the aim of providing guidance for the standardized and individualized application of CGM in adult ICU patients. This consensus puts forward 27 recommendations addressing 12 questions regarding the use of CGM in critically ill patients. The content covers the definition, classification and hazards of glycemic abnormalities in critically ill patients, common blood glucose monitoring methods and their clinical implications, eligible populations for CGM, data interpretation, quality control and routine care of CGM, as well as accessibility and economic costs.

articles.title: [Chinese guideline for the laboratory diagnosis of venous thromboembolism (2026 edition)].
authors: Expert Committee of the National Capacity Building Project for Pulmonary Embolism and Deep Venous Thrombosis Prevention and Treatment
National Health Commission Capacity Building and Continuing Education Center
articles.abstract: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) is a multifactorial disease induced by the interplay between environmental exposures and genetic predisposition. It features intricate pathological mechanisms and an insidious clinical course, with severe cases potentially resulting in disability or death. In recent years, laboratory assays for VTE have become increasingly diverse,nevertheless, prominent challenges persist, including ambiguous indications for clinical application, inconsistent interpretation criteria, and insufficient evidence-based support. To further promote the standardization of laboratory diagnosis for VTE in China, enhance the safety and efficacy of clinical applications, and ensure the rational utilization of diagnostic resources, initiated by Expert Committee of the National Capacity Building Project for Pulmonary Embolism and Deep Venous Thrombosis Prevention and Treatment, National Health Commission Capacity Building and Continuing Education Center and National Center for Clinical Laboratories, the Chinese guideline for the laboratory diagnosis of venous thromboembolism (2026 edition) was developed in accordance with the methodologies and procedures in the Guiding Principles for the Formulation and Revision of Clinical Practice Guidelines in China (2022 Edition), the Appraisal of Guidelines for Research and Evaluation Ⅱ (AGREEⅡ), and the Reporting Items for Practice Guidelines in Healthcare (RIGHT). This guideline addresses 12 clinical questions and includes 33 recommendations, covering exclusion diagnosis, etiological analysis, risk assessment and anticoagulation monitoring of VTE.
