LAY SUMMARY: This study explores how visceral adipose tissue (VAT), a type of body fat located around internal organs, elevates the risk of recurrent cardiovascular events in patients with premature coronary artery disease (pCAD), even with optimal medical treatment.Key finding 1: Patients with elevated VAT levels faced a significantly higher risk of recurrent major cardiovascular events.Key finding 2: These results indicate that reducing VAT through lifestyle modifications or targeted interventions could decrease cardiovascular risks in patients with pCAD.

articles.title: Comprehensive analysis of peptide pharmaceutical: Development of three orthogonal chromatographic methods and characterization of bivalirudin degradation products by high-resolution mass spectrometry.
articles.journal: Journal of pharmaceutical and biomedical analysis
articles.abstract: Bivalirudin is a synthetic oligopeptide used as an anticoagulant for the treatment of acute coronary syndromes and for the prevention of thrombosis in patients undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention. As peptides are complex molecules that may exhibit inherently complex impurity profiles, three orthogonal ultra-performance liquid chromatographic methods were developed in this work, in accordance with Analytical Quality-by-Design principles, to ensure the safety and efficacy of the bivalirudin drug product. Starting from a structure-driven theoretical assessment of bivalirudin, which anticipates the formation of peptide fragments, deamidation and oxidation products, as well as covalent oligomers under stress conditions, method development was directed into three orthogonal chromatographic modes-size-exclusion (SEC), reversed-phase (RP) and hydrophilic interaction liquid chromatography (HILIC) - enabling a comprehensive evaluation of its degradation pathways. For the first time, bivalirudin oligomers (dimers and trimers) were detected and characterized using size-exclusion chromatography. The combination of HILIC and RP chromatography methods ensured separation of 10 non-oligomeric bivalirudin impurities. The developed methods employed MS-compatible mobile phases to facilitate structural elucidation of bivalirudin degradation products by high-resolution mass spectrometry. Stress conditions included acid and base hydrolysis, oxidation with H₂O₂, thermal decomposition, and light exposure, as regulated by ICH guidelines. Extensive risk assessment was conducted using Ishikawa diagrams and heat maps. Method development was carried out using Design of Experiments methodology, supported by Fusion AE software. The developed ultra-performance liquid chromatography (UPLC) methods were validated, confirming their suitability for analyzing bivalirudin and its related impurities.

articles.title: SilMA-stabilized micro-wavy PLCL vascular grafts for native-like nonlinear mechanics and vascular remodeling.
articles.abstract: Cardiovascular diseases remain a major cause of mortality, yet small-diameter vascular grafts (SDVGs) are still limited by thrombosis and pathological luminal remodeling caused in part by mechanical mismatch. Here, we developed electrospun poly(L-lactide-co-ε-caprolactone) (PLCL) grafts with a mechanically programmed micro-wavy architecture and artery-like nonlinear elasticity. A conformal methacrylated silk fibroin (SilMA) layer was photopolymerized onto the PLCL fibers to stabilize the programmed structure and improve the blood-contacting interface. The resulting graft preserved a porous architecture, achieved a compliance of 15.0 ± 1.8% per 100 mmHg, and maintained nonlinear mechanics during degradation. Fluid-structure interaction analysis showed improved diameter matching and local hemodynamic distributions closer to those of native arteries under pulsatile loading. SilMA modification also improved hemocompatibility by reducing clot formation and platelet adhesion. At 30 days, the final graft formulation remained patent and showed continuous endothelial coverage, organized α-SMA⁺ tissue formation, and a mild inflammatory response. These results demonstrate that interfacial photostabilization can integrate mechanical matching with organized vascular remodeling in biodegradable SDVGs.

articles.title: Doxepin Attenuates Cognitive and Anxiety-like Behavioral Deficits Induced by Acute Kidney Injury in Rats.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Acute kidney injury (AKI) is a systemic disorder with consequences extending beyond the kidney, including central nervous system dysfunction. Clinical and experimental evidence indicates that AKI is associated with cognitive impairment and neuropsychiatric disturbances. However, effective strategies to prevent or attenuate AKI-associated brain dysfunction are lacking. Doxepin, a tricyclic antidepressant, exhibits neuroprotective properties that may counteract key mechanisms implicated in AKI-induced neural injury.

METHODS: In this study, acute renal failure (ARF) was used as an experimental model of AKI. ARF was induced in male Wistar rats through glycerol injection. Animals were allocated into four experimental groups: Control, doxepin (DOX), ARF, or ARF-DOX. Doxepin was given orally at a dose of 5 mg/kg once daily over a 12-day period. Renal function was assessed using serum and urinary urea measurements. Anxiety-related behavior was assessed using the open field test and the elevated plus maze, whereas spatial learning and memory were evaluated with the radial arm water maze.

RESULTS: Glycerol-induced ARF resulted in significant alterations in urinary parameters, including reduced urinary urea concentration and increased urine output and flow rate, while serum urea levels did not differ significantly among groups. ARF did not impair spatial learning acquisition but significantly disrupted short- and long-term memory retention. In addition, ARF induced specific anxiety-like behavioral alterations, including increased freezing behavior, reduced rearing activity, and decreased open-arm entries in anxiogenic environments. Doxepin treatment significantly attenuated memory impairments and partially normalized anxiety-related behaviors, without improving biochemical markers of renal dysfunction.

DISCUSSION: These findings demonstrate that AKI induces selective cognitive and anxiety-like behavioral deficits and support the existence of a kidney-brain axis. Doxepin attenuated AKI-associated neurobehavioral impairments.

CONCLUSION: This study supports the potential repurposing of doxepin, an established clinically used and brain-penetrant drug, as a therapeutic strategy for attenuating AKI-associated neurobehavioral dysfunction.

articles.title: Knowledge and self-reported infection prevention and control practices among community health extension workers in primary healthcare facilities in Southeast Nigeria.
articles.abstract:
AIM/OBJECTIVES: To assess the knowledge and practice of infection prevention and control (IPC) among community health extension workers (CHEWs) in primary healthcare facilities in Southeast Nigeria and examine the relationship between IPC knowledge and preventive practices.

METHODS AND RESULTS: A cross-sectional study was conducted among 328 CHEWs in Ebonyi State, Southeast Nigeria, using a multistage sampling technique. Data were collected using a structured pre-tested questionnaire and analysed with IBM SPSS version 20. Descriptive statistics and chi-square tests were performed at p ≤ 0.05. Most respondents were female (53.7%) and had received previous IPC training (91.8%). Overall, 97.3% demonstrated good IPC knowledge. High compliance with IPC practices was reported, including hand hygiene (88.1%), consistent use of personal protective equipment (90.9%), safe injection practices (98.2%), and proper sharps disposal (95.4%). Significant associations were observed between IPC knowledge and all assessed preventive practices (p < 0.001).

DISCUSSION: The findings suggest high levels of IPC knowledge and self-reported compliance among CHEWs in primary healthcare settings. Regular training, workplace monitoring, and availability of IPC policies may have contributed to these outcomes. However, gaps in hand hygiene consistency and IPC supply availability indicate the need for sustained institutional support.

SIGNIFICANCE AND IMPACT: Strengthening continuous IPC training, supportive supervision, and access to essential IPC resources may improve frontline preparedness and reduce the risk of healthcare-associated infections in resource-limited primary healthcare settings.

articles.title: Acute spinal cord injury.
articles.journal: Journal of the Intensive Care Society
articles.abstract: Spinal cord injury results in transient or permanent disruption to the central nervous system with far reaching multi-system consequences, alongside having profound and devastating effects on the individual, their family and wider society. This review provides an overview on the epidemiology, pathophysiology and clinical presentation of spinal cord injury. The clinical syndromes of spinal cord injury are also discussed in detail. The medical and surgical management strategies of spinal cord injury in the acute phase is considered, alongside highlighting the importance of early referral to dedicated spinal rehabilitation services. The natural history and prognosis of traumatic spinal cord injury are also discussed.

articles.title: Surgical cancellation and changes in postoperative level of care among high and moderate risk surgical patients in the UK.
authors: Pan-London Perioperative Audit and Research Network Committee, The REPACC Study Investigators
articles.journal: Journal of the Intensive Care Society
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The clinical and administrative pressures leading to cancellation of surgery are well established. However, it is not known whether the same factors lead to a change in patients' planned postoperative destination and level of care.

METHODS: We conducted a secondary analysis of the REPACC dataset; a nationwide, retrospective, observational study examining the provision of enhanced and critical care services in the UK. The reasons for cancellation and changes to the level of care received postoperatively were ascertained from free-text data.

RESULTS: Our analysis included 5990 patients from 65 sites across the UK, of which 539 (9.6%) had their surgery cancelled. The most common reason for surgical cancellation was a lack of resources (51.0%), primarily bed shortages (37.1%). Among the 5451 patients who proceeded with surgery, 81.3% received the anticipated level of care postoperatively, 3.9% required escalation and 14.8% were de-escalated to a lower level of care. Changes to the anticipated level of care occurred most often among patients initially triaged to enhanced care. Clinical reasons were the major cause of escalation (53.3%) and de-escalation (61.2%) postoperatively with bed shortages accounting for a minority. Patients were commonly de-escalated following a postoperative assessment (21.8%).

CONCLUSION: Cancellation of surgery in the UK is primarily a consequence of resource scarcity, whereas clinical reasons account for the majority of those re-allocated to different levels of care postoperatively. Future work should explore the clinical and health economic impacts of this dynamic bed management with particular focus on the role of enhanced care as an interface between critical care and the ward.

articles.title: Prevalence and characteristics of disabilities in physicians in Canada: an analysis of Canadian Census data.
articles.journal: CMAJ : Canadian Medical Association journal = journal de l'Association medicale canadienne
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite the importance of equity and accessibility with respect to the medical workforce in Canada, limited data exist on physicians with disabilities. We aimed to estimate the prevalence and types of disabilities among physicians and compare them with other occupations.

METHODS: We performed a population-based cross-sectional study using weighted data from the 2021 mandatory Canadian long-form Census, obtained from Statistics Canada. Participants included those working in Canada, categorized into physicians, non-health care professionals (lawyers, engineers, professors), nurses, and the remaining working population. We calculated the prevalence of self-reported disabilities overall and by type (mental health, visual, hearing, mobility or physical, cognitive or learning) among physicians. We compared variation in disability by age, sex, and specialty. We compared physicians to other occupations using age-sex standardization and calculated adjusted odds ratios (OR).

RESULTS: Of 16 468 900 individuals, 89 760 (0.6%) were physicians (mean age [standard deviation] 48.1 yr [13.0], 54.5% male). The prevalence of respondents reporting a disability always or often was 5.0%, including mental health (2.0%), visual (1.8%), hearing (0.7%), mobility or physical (0.6%), and cognitive or learning (0.3%) disabilities. Overall, the prevalence of disability increased with age, primarily owing to increasing hearing and mobility or physical disabilities, whereas mental health disabilities were more common at younger ages. Male physicians (4.5%) reported lower (adjusted OR 0.75, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.71 to 0.80) prevalence of disability than female physicians (6.0%). The age-sex standardized prevalence of disabilities in physicians (5.3%) was lower than in non-health care professionals (7.8%; adjusted OR 1.48, 95% CI 1.44 to 1.53), nurses (9.2%; adjusted OR 1.74, 95% CI 1.69 to 1.79), and the remaining working population (10.8%; adjusted OR 2.21, 95% CI 2.15 to 2.27). When we broadened disability to include impairments reported sometimes, the overall prevalence of disability among physicians increased to 17.0%.

INTERPRETATION: One in 20 practising Canadian physicians reports always or often experiencing a disability, which was less than other occupations. These Census-based estimates provide a national benchmark to inform efforts to improve accessibility and sustainability in the physician workforce.

articles.title: Lack of fear acquisition to film clip unconditional stimuli despite contingency awareness: Implications for electrodermal fear conditioning.
articles.abstract: Fear conditioning is most commonly assessed by measuring electrodermal activity to a conditioned stimulus (CS) in anticipation of an electric shock or another unconditioned stimulus (US). Replacing the electric shock with aversive film clips is an innovation that potentially has higher ecological validity for posttraumatic stress disorder. The present report examined boundary conditions of this paradigm across two between subjects experiments, with a particular focus on the effectiveness of film clip versus electric shock USs in promoting physiological fear conditioning. In Experiment 1, we tested whether fear acquisition was influenced by the inclusion of a shock US (n = 30), prior exposure to a longer trauma film (n = 29), or the use of face (n = 33) versus shape (n = 33) conditioned stimuli (CSs). Fear acquisition was enhanced by the inclusion of a shock US and to a lesser extent by prior trauma film exposure; however, conditioning in groups using film clip USs alone was characterised by lack of conditioned electrodermal responding. Experiment 2 investigated whether this absence of conditioned responding reflected reduced contingency awareness by measuring online US expectancy across film-based (four US film clip group with n = 55 and one US film clip group with n = 44) and shock-based (n = 30) US conditions, as well as salivary stress responses following acquisition. Despite equivalent US expectancy, CS pleasantness, and subjective US ratings across groups, conditioned electrodermal responses during acquisition were observed only in the shock US condition. Differences between groups may be explained by differences in salivary cortisol reactivity, with higher cortisol responses following acquisition in the shock group. Together, these findings indicate that shock USs increase physiological arousal, which appears to be essential for electrodermal reactivity, irrespective of conditioned learning processes. This finding has potentially important implications for the interpretation of electrodermal measurement in fear conditioning paradigms.

articles.title: Long-term metabolic regulation in the era of GLP-1 receptor agonists: An integrative review of Ayurvedic and biomedical perspectives.
articles.journal: Journal of Ayurveda and integrative medicine
articles.abstract: Obesity and type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) are chronic, relapsing, and multifactorial disorders arising from long-term dysregulation of metabolic, neuroendocrine, behavioral, and environmental systems. Glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonists represent a major advance in contemporary metabolic pharmacotherapy. Among them, semaglutide has demonstrated robust efficacy in improving glycemic control, inducing clinically meaningful weight loss, and reducing cardiovascular and renal risk in high-risk populations through well-established molecular and physiological mechanisms. Despite these benefits, challenges related to long-term metabolic sustainability persist, including weight regain after discontinuation, loss of lean mass defined as the reduction in skeletal muscle and non-adipose body tissue and the need for prolonged or lifelong therapy. These observations highlight the adaptive nature of human energy homeostasis and underscore the importance of approaches that support durable metabolic regulation beyond appetite suppression alone. This discussion uses semaglutide as a case example to explore how integrative frameworks, particularly Ayurveda, may complement pharmacotherapy by offering systems-level perspectives on digestion, regulation, tissue integrity, and behavioral rhythms. Ayurvedic concepts are employed as interpretive analogues rather than mechanistic explanations, with the aim of contextualizing why short-term metabolic improvements may not always translate into long-term resilience. Rather than positioning traditional knowledge systems in opposition to evidence-based medicine, this paper argues for a complementary model in which pharmacotherapy stabilizes acute metabolic risk while integrative lifestyle-oriented strategies support sustained metabolic health.

articles.title: ATF4 alleviates doxorubicin-induced cardiomyopathy by promoting H2S production and antioxidant defense.
articles.abstract: Doxorubicin (DOX) remains a cornerstone in cancer treatment. However, its clinical utilization is significantly hampered by dose-dependent cardiotoxicity. The generation of reactive oxygen species (ROS) constitutes the central component of the pathogenesis of DOX-induced cardiotoxicity. Activating transcription factor 4 (ATF4) has been demonstrated to exert a cardioprotective effect and augment cardiac antioxidative capacity in settings of heart failure. To explore the role of ATF4 in DOX-induced cardiomyopathy, cardiac-specific ATF4 conditional heterozygous mice and AAV9 mediated ATF4 overexpression mouse models were utilized. Cardiac function was assessed by echocardiography. The upstream regulator and downstream mediator of ATF4 were evaluated using RNA-seq analysis and further verified using ChIP assay and luciferase reporter assay. ATF4+/- mice exhibited a higher degree of susceptibility to DOX-induced cardiotoxicity in comparison with ATF4flox/flox mice. In contrast, cardiac-specific overexpression of ATF4 by AAV9 confers robust cardioprotection against DOX-induced cardiomyopathy. Mechanistically, we identified the upstream regulator of ATF4 as KLF16. Further, the decrease of ATF4 led to a reduction in cystathionine γ-lyase (CSE) transcription and hydrogen sulfide (H2S) production in the context of DOX-induced cardiotoxicity. ChIP and luciferase reporter assays revealed that ATF4 functioned as the transcription factor of the CSE gene. In contrast, the ectopic expression of ATF4 mitigated oxidative stress and apoptosis in DOX-induced cardiotoxicity, both in vivo and in vitro. The study identified a novel function of ATF4 in opposing oxidative stress in DOX cardiotoxicity through the promotion of CSE transcription. Targeting ATF4 may offer therapeutic benefits for DOX-induced cardiomyopathy.

articles.title: The AMPK/mTOR axis is linked to placental ferroptosis in human gestational diabetes mellitus.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ferroptosis has been closely implicated in placenta-related complications. Nevertheless, its specific role in the placenta of gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) remains poorly understood. We hypothesized that ferroptosis contributes to impaired placental cell function in GDM and that the adenosine 5'-monophosphate (AMP)-activated protein kinase (AMPK)/mammalian target of rapamycin (mTOR) axis acts as an potential regulator of ferroptosis.

METHODS: Term placental tissues from pregnant women with GDM and healthy controls were analyzed, and the human chorionic trophoblast line (HTR8/SVneo) was used in the in vitro experiments.

RESULTS: Altered levels of ferroptosis markers-transferrin receptor 1 (TfR1), acyl-CoA synthetase long-chain family member 4 (ACSL4), glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4), ferrous iron and malondialdehyde (MDA), and potential ferroptosis mediators-reactive oxygen species (ROS), AMPK, and mTOR were observed in GDM placentas compared to control. AMPK inhibitor, AMPK activator, and mTOR inhibitor were applied to modulate the AMPK/mTOR signaling axis in in vitro experiments. Our in vitro data revealed that modulation of AMPK or mTOR activation directly affects the induction of ferroptosis as well as trophoblast cell proliferation and migration.

CONCLUSIONS: Our study suggests that AMPK/mTOR axis is closely associated with placental ferroptosis which may represent a promising therapeutic target for mitigating GDM-related placental complications following further validation in animal models.

articles.title: External Validation of the Risk Assessment of Morbidity in Pediatric Surgery Score.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The Risk Assessment of Morbidity in Pediatric Surgery (RAMPS) score was developed by a tertiary care children's center to predict risk of noncardiac pediatric surgical morbidity using intrinsic surgical risk (ISR) and individual comorbidity. The score demonstrated good internal validity, discrimination, and generalizability. This study seeks to externally validate the score in a similar patient population at a different tertiary care children's hospital.

METHODS: Following institutional review board (IRB) approval, data for all noncardiac, nontrauma, and nontransplant pediatric surgeries performed at the external children's hospital in 2019 were collected via review of medical records. The RAMPS score for each patient was calculated. A composite morbidity score defined as transfer to intensive care unit (ICU), cardiac arrest, unplanned endotracheal intubation, or unplanned initiation of positive pressure ventilation (PPV) in the 72 hours following surgery was calculated. Discrimination was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic curve analysis, and calibration between predicted and observed risk of morbidity was assessed.

RESULTS: Of 13,718 patients included, 409 (2.98%) experienced the composite morbidity outcome. The most common morbidity was postoperative PPV-361 (2.63%). Only 1.5% (n = 205) of the cohort was critically ill, though 14.1% (n = 1934) had at least three chronic conditions and 19.5% (n = 2668) of patients had a procedure in ISR quartiles 3 or 4. Each component of the RAMPS score was significantly associated with the outcome. The RAMPS score had very good discrimination (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve [AUC] = 0.829; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.809-0.849) and good calibration between observed and predicted probabilities (Brier score = 0.03).

CONCLUSIONS: The RAMPS score performed well in this external validation with overall less patient complexity and less morbidity than in the original cohort included for development and internal validation. The score moderately overestimated risk in the most complex patients, which does not diminish its utility in guiding resource allocation to manage or prevent perioperative adverse events. In summary, the RAMPs score is a simple, highly discriminant, well-calibrated, and externally validated tool clinicians and health systems can use to predict morbidity among pediatric surgery patients.

articles.title: Sensitization and Impaired Habituation of Somatosensory Evoked Potentials in Central Post-stroke Pain.
articles.journal: Annals of Indian Academy of Neurology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Central post-stroke pain (CPSP) is associated with hyperpathia and allodynia, and neurophysiological biomarkers may help to clarify these mechanisms. We report sensitization and impaired habituation of median somatosensory evoked potentials (MSEPs) in CPSP and examine their association with quantitative sensory testing (QST) and clinico-radiological features.

METHODS: Thirty-four CPSP patients and 18 matched healthy controls were prospectively included. Clinical evaluation, QST, Visual Analog Scale (VAS), Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI), and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-based stroke location were recorded. Five consecutive MSEP blocks were obtained bilaterally. N19 latency and amplitude from block 1, as well as habituation across blocks 1 to c5, were analyzed. Impaired habituation was defined as failure of amplitude reduction in blocks 2-5 compared with block 1.

RESULTS: CPSP patients showed significantly prolonged N19 latency (21.7 ± 2.25 ms vs 18.8 ± 1.26 ms) and reduced amplitude (3.1 ± 1.57 μV vs 6.2 ± 2.58 μV) compared with controls. N19 amplitude was also reduced on the unaffected side. Tactile threshold correlated with higher pain intensity ( P = 0.04), inversely with allodynia ( P = 0.01), and with extra-thalamic lesions ( P = 0.01). Impaired habituation occurred in 64.7% of CPSP patients and was significantly associated with hyperalgesia ( P = 0.008).

CONCLUSIONS: CPSP is marked by altered somatosensory processing, reduced cortical excitability, and impaired habituation, reflecting maladaptive thalamocortical plasticity.

articles.title: An extended knowledge intervention addressing vaccine hesitancy in the field: Results from two representative surveys.
articles.journal: Health psychology : official journal of the Division of Health Psychology, American Psychological Association
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Older adults may fail to demand influenza and pneumococcal vaccinations due to limited knowledge of its role in preventing initial influenza infections, secondary complications such as pneumonia, and serious late consequences such as sepsis. We evaluated the extended health knowledge approach during the field intervention "Vaccination60+" to determine whether providing this additional information could improve vaccination among older adults.

METHOD: The intervention was implemented in a model region in Germany during two influenza seasons. Two quota-sampled telephone surveys targeting adults 60+ were conducted to evaluate the extended health knowledge approach in an intervention (N = 700 each). Quasi-experimental groups were defined based on whether participants recalled the intervention (intervention-exposed vs. nonexposed). Knowledge (influenza, pneumococci, and sepsis), the 5 °C antecedents of vaccination, and vaccination intention and behavior were assessed.

RESULTS: Intervention exposure was associated with higher knowledge about influenza (η² = .009), pneumococci (η2 = .012), and sepsis (η² = .004). It was also associated with higher risk-benefit calculation regarding influenza vaccination (η² = .003) and increased confidence in the safety of pneumococcal vaccination (η² = .020). Vaccination intentions for both diseases did not differ according to exposure. Vaccination behavior increased over time, (influenza: OR = 1.88; pneumococci: OR = 2.08), potentially due to external factors that are discussed.

CONCLUSIONS: Providing information can support health decisions and relate to higher risk awareness but may not alter actual behavior. Further recommendations regarding vaccination interventions (e.g., provider endorsement, tailoring to prior knowledge) that could decrease hesitancy are discussed. (PsycInfo Database Record (c) 2026 APA, all rights reserved).

articles.title: The Application of Laser Technology in Cholesteatoma Surgery: Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
articles.journal: The journal of international advanced otology
articles.abstract: To evaluate the effectiveness of laser-assisted cholesteatoma surgery compared with conventional techniques, with a focus on residual disease, postoperative complications, and hearing preservation. A systematic review and meta-analysis were conducted following PRISMA guidelines. Databases were searched for studies comparing laser and non-laser cholesteatoma surgery. Eligible studies were screened, and risk ratios (RR) with 95% CI were calculated using a random-effects model. Three studies including 271 participants reported residual disease outcomes. The pooled risk ratio was RR = 0.53; 95% CI, 0.12-2.39; P = .406, indicating no statistically significant difference between laser and non-laser groups. Moderate heterogeneity was observed (I2 = 63.5%). Only 1 study reported postoperative complications, with RR = 1.04; 95% CI, 0.18-5.97. A subgroup analysis from 1 study compared laser myringotomy with endaural laser-assisted single-stage inside-out cholesteatoma, showing RR = 0.57; 95% CI, 0.15-2.19. Laser-assisted cholesteatoma surgery demonstrates comparable rates of residual disease and complications to conventional surgery. While lasers may offer technical advantages, current evidence is limited and underpowered. Larger, high-quality trials are needed to clarify their role in cholesteatoma management.

articles.title: Ten-Year Experience with Combined Hyperbaric Oxygen and Steroid Therapy for Idiopathic Sudden Sensorineural Hearing Loss: A Retrospective Cohort of 332 Patients.
articles.journal: The journal of international advanced otology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: To evaluate the clinical efficacy and safety of hyperbaric oxygen therapy (HBOT) combined with systemic corticosteroids in patients with idiopathic sudden sensorineural hearing loss (ISSNHL), with particular focus on treatment timing, predictors of hearing recovery, and the impact of comorbidities.

METHODS: This retrospective observational cohort study was conducted at a tertiary referral center (AOU "San Giovanni di Dio e Ruggi d'Aragona," Salerno, Italy). A total of 332 adult patients with ISSNHL treated between 2014 and 2024 were included. All patients received combined therapy with systemic corticosteroids (oral prednisone 1 mg/kg/day, tapered over 10-15 days) and HBOT (2.4 atmospheres absolute, 90 minutes per session; median of 10 sessions). Audiometric outcomes were assessed using pure-tone average (PTA). Treatment response was defined as a ≥30% improvement in PTA compared with baseline. Multivariate logistic regression was performed to identify independent predictors of hearing improvement. Safety outcomes were also recorded.

RESULTS: Mean baseline PTA was 61.3 ± 21.5 dB HL, improving to 44.6 ± 22.7 dB HL after treatment, with a mean hearing gain of 16.7 ± 14.2 dB HL (P < .001). Overall, 151 patients (43.5%) met the response criteria. Responders presented with significantly higher baseline PTA compared with nonresponders (67.6 vs. 56.8 dB HL, P < .001) and more frequently reported tinnitus (64.2% vs. 51.5%, P = .014). Median time to treatment initiation was 15 days (interquartile range: 7-30). Multivariate analysis identified shorter time to treatment (odds ratio [OR]: 0.95, 95% CI: 0.92-0.98), presence of tinnitus (OR: 1.79, 95% CI: 1.15-2.80), and higher baseline PTA (OR: 1.03, 95% CI: 1.01-1.05) as independent predictors of hearing improvement. Common comorbidities, including hypertension, diabetes, and cardiovascular disease, were not significantly associated with treatment response. No serious adverse events related to HBOT were observed.

CONCLUSION: Hyperbaric oxygen therapy combined with systemic corticosteroids was associated with improved audiometric outcomes in patients with ISSNHL, particularly when initiated early. Shorter time to treatment, greater baseline hearing loss, and the presence of tinnitus emerged as independent predictors of hearing recovery. Overall, these findings suggest an association between early HBOT use and improved audiometric outcomes and support its consideration as an adjunctive component of multimodal treatment strategies for ISSNHL.

articles.title: The diagnostic blind spot of spirometric staging in biomass-related non-smoking chronic obstructive pulmonary disease: a cross-sectional study of spirometry-diffusion discordance in a rural South Indian population.
articles.journal: Monaldi archives for chest disease = Archivio Monaldi per le malattie del torace
articles.abstract: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is heterogeneous, yet severity is conventionally graded by spirometry [forced expiratory volume in 1 second (FEV1)] on the assumption that airflow limitation reflects parenchymal damage. Biomass-related non-smoking COPD (NS-COPD) is common in low- and middle-income countries. In this hospital-based cross-sectional study, we compared the physiological phenotypes of smoking COPD (S-COPD) and biomass-related NS-COPD and tested the concordance between Global Initiative for Chronic Obstructive Lung Disease (GOLD) spirometric severity and diffusion-based gas-exchange impairment. A total of 91 stable COPD patients (S-COPD, n=54; NS-COPD, n=37) underwent post-bronchodilator spirometry, single-breath diffusing capacity of the lung for carbon monoxide (DLCO) with transfer coefficient (KCO), residual volume to total lung capacity ratio, and the 6-minute walk test; cohorts were stratified by exposure (>10 pack-years vs. >60 hour-years of biomass) and compared using the Student t-test and Fisher's exact test. Compared with smokers, non-smokers had higher DLCO (71.4±12.4 vs. 57.7±17.5% predicted; p<0.001) and KCO (0.95±0.19 vs. 0.71±0.22 mmol/min/kPa/L; p<0.001). All non-smokers with severe (GOLD 3) airflow limitation (8/8, 100%) retained normal or only mildly impaired diffusion [7/8 (87.5%) strictly normal], whereas 14/28 (50.0%) GOLD 3 smokers had impaired gas exchange [4/28 (14.3%) severe]. Non-smokers more often retained a normal DLCO [31/37 (83.8%) vs. 26/54 (48.1%); odds ratio 5.6, 95% confidence interval 2.0-15.5; p<0.001]. This difference persisted after multivariable adjustment for age, sex and body mass index (odds ratio 30.0, 95% confidence interval 2.5-358.5; p=0.007) and after further adjustment for FEV1 percent predicted (odds ratio 21.1, 95% confidence interval 1.6-282.7; p=0.021), indicating that the dissociation was not explained by these covariates or by the degree of airflow limitation itself. GOLD staging tended to overestimate parenchymal severity in biomass-related NS-COPD, in which airflow obstruction was largely uncoupled from gas-exchange loss, whereas in smokers the two were more tightly coupled. These cross-sectional, single-center findings, limited by a sex imbalance and the absence of imaging confirmation, support routine DLCO/KCO measurement to phenotype these patients and, where imaging is scarce, as a low-cost structural surrogate.

articles.title: Variable expiratory airflow, and not airway obstruction, is the defining physiological feature of asthma.
articles.journal: Monaldi archives for chest disease = Archivio Monaldi per le malattie del torace
articles.abstract: Asthma is usually diagnosed by history and presence of airway obstruction with a significant bronchodilator response on spirometry. However, airway obstruction may not always be present, or a bronchodilator response may not be significant. Contrary to wide perception, airway obstruction is not the defining functional feature of asthma. Definitions of asthma have never included the term 'airways obstruction'. According to the Global Initiative for Asthma, the diagnosis of asthma requires a history of typical variable symptoms and confirmation by variable expiratory airflow. It has emphasized that variable expiratory airflow is the key physiological feature of asthma. Airway obstruction is a manifestation of this variability and represents one end of the spectrum of this variation. When airways obstruction is observed, a positive bronchodilator response is the most convenient method to confirm the diagnosis. However, when airway obstruction or bronchodilator responsiveness is not demonstrable, there are other options to demonstrate variability in not demonstrable, there are other options to demonstrate variability of expiratory airflows and confirm the diagnosis.

articles.title: A novel, free regional conference model to increase interest and engagement of medical trainees in pediatrics and pediatric gastroenterology research.
articles.abstract: Declining interest in pediatrics, contraction of the pediatric gastroenterology fellowship applicant pool, and the long-standing erosion of the physician-scientist workforce threaten the future of pediatric academic medicine. Cost and logistical barriers to traditional academic conferences disproportionately affect trainees from underrepresented or resource-limited backgrounds and may compound these pipeline pressures. We developed Eats, Streets, and Beets (ESB), a free, trainee-centered regional pediatric nutrition conference held in Brooklyn, NY, combining faculty-led symposia, guaranteed podium presentations for every accepted abstract, and a community block party. A post-conference survey (n = 12; response rate 63.2%) demonstrated high overall satisfaction (mean 8.25/10) and self-reported increases in interest in research, pediatrics, and pediatric gastroenterology and nutrition. Trainee-only programming, podium-only presentations, and community engagement were most strongly associated with increased interest. This low-cost, replicable model may help reinvigorate trainee engagement across the pediatric and pediatric gastroenterology pipelines.

articles.title: Tirzepatide use in adolescents with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD): A case series.
articles.abstract: Pediatric obesity and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) prevalence has risen markedly over the past decade. Due to transition delays and workforce shortages, pediatric specialists often manage patients into young adulthood, and thus familiarity with adult pharmacotherapies for MASLD is essential. Currently, Semaglutide, a glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonist, is approved for adults with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) and F2-F3 fibrosis; however, dual and triple agonists are being evaluated. Tirzepatide, a dual agonist that targets gastric inhibitory peptide (GIP) and the GLP-1 receptor, has demonstrated superior weight reduction to Semaglutide (-20.2% vs. -13.7%) with a more favorable gastrointestinal adverse effect profile. Adult literature has demonstrated its effectiveness in MASH resolution, and pediatric data suggest it is safe in younger populations. Currently, there are no pediatric/adolescent studies exploring the use of Tirzepatide in MASLD. We present our experience using Tirzepatide in two adolescent patients with obesity and MASLD.

articles.title: Assessing the current landscape of North American pediatric nutrition support teams: A survey study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Nutrition support teams (NSTs) were developed to standardize nutrition evaluation practices and coordinate transdisciplinary expertise for appropriate administration of inpatient nutritional care. Minimal data are available regarding the current practices, structure, and perceived utility of pediatric NSTs in diverse hospital systems.

METHODS: This was a cross-sectional survey study disseminated electronically to three electronic listservs associated with the North American Society for Pediatric Gastroenterology, Hepatology, and Nutrition (NASPGHAN).

RESULTS: Forty-seven unique responses were obtained. Sixty-two percent reported a current NST at their institution. Of those with an NST, 97% reported reviewing parenteral nutrition (PN) orders, 90% recommended nutritional assessment modalities, 86% determined PN appropriateness, and 72% reviewed enteral nutrition orders. More than 50% of respondents strongly agreed that an NST improved patient safety, improved patient nutritional status, improved quality of care, decreased rates of malnutrition, and promoted interdisciplinary care. Among those without an NST, 33% of respondents reported that they were previously unsuccessful at developing an NST at their site. Perceived barriers to NST implementation in more than 50% of respondents were lack of protected time, budget or funding issues, lack of available staff, and lack of interdisciplinary support.

DISCUSSION: This study demonstrates heterogeneity of pediatric NSTs in North America with regard to frequency of services, while showing general consistency in the scope of services provided. It highlights the overall perceived benefit of NSTs. Financial compensation continues to be a barrier to access to NSTs with a notable percentage of NSTs reportedly not billing for services.

articles.title: Acetone sensing with a single-atom transition metal (Fe, Co, Ni, Mn, Pd, and Zn)-doped InP3 monolayer: a theoretical study.
articles.abstract: Acetone (C3H6O) in the exhaled breath of diabetic patients serves as an important biomarker for the noninvasive diagnosis of diabetes mellitus. In this work, based on density functional theory (DFT), we theoretically examined six single-atom transition metal (Fe, Co, Ni, Mn, Pd, and Zn)-doped InP3 monolayers (denoted as M-InP3) as C3H6O gas sensors to screen suitable electrochemical materials for non-invasive diabetes detection. The adsorption and cycling performances of M-InP3 (M = Fe, Co, Ni, Mn, Pd, and Zn) toward the C3H6O molecule were investigated, and the calculation results indicate that single-atom transition metal (Fe, Co, Ni, Mn, Pd, and Zn) doping greatly enhances the C3H6O adsorption capacity of the InP3 monolayer. The Zn-InP3 monolayer exhibits a suitable gas response (-100%) and a short recovery time (0.1 s) at 298 K, making it potentially applicable as a room-temperature reusable acetone sensor. Fe-InP3 and Pd-InP3 deliver high gas responses (-96% and -86%, respectively) to C3H6O, positioning them as promising candidates for acetone. Pd-InP3 achieves rapid recycling within 81 s at 373 K. The long desorption times and low response values of C3H6O make the Mn-InP3, Co-InP3 and Ni-InP3 surfaces unsuitable for C3H6O detection. This work presents a theoretical study of the adsorption and recyclability of C3H6O on six single-atom transition metal (Fe, Co, Ni, Mn, Pd, and Zn)-doped InP3 monolayers, potentially offering a new class of sensing materials for acetone sensors in the non-invasive diagnosis of diabetes mellitus.

articles.title: Sustainable synthesis of a Zr-based UiO-66 MOF from PET waste for UV-assisted degradation of organic contaminants.
articles.abstract: The coexistence of polyethylene terephthalate (PET) waste and persistent organic pollutants in aquatic environments requires comprehensive circular-economy strategies to valorize PET waste into functional materials for water treatment. In this study, post-consumer PET was converted to terephthalic acid (TPA) via a neutral hydrothermal depolymerization process and was used as an organic linker for the synthesis of a Zr-based UiO-66. The recovered linker and synthesized UiO-66 were characterized by FTIR, PXRD, TEM/SAED, nitrogen adsorption-desorption, UV-vis spectroscopy, electrochemical impedance spectroscopy, and Mott-Schottky analysis. PXRD confirmed UiO-66 crystallinity, while TEM revealed nano-sized polyhedral particles with an average size of approximately 120 nm. The material exhibited a BET surface area of 822.2 m2 g-1, total pore volume of 0.379 cm3 g-1, and average pore diameter of 2.93 nm. Optical and electrochemical analyses showed a band gap of about 3.51 eV, n-type semiconducting behavior, and a flat-band potential of -0.68 V vs. Ag/AgCl. The photocatalytic activity of PET-derived UiO-66 was evaluated using methylene blue (MB) under UV light irradiation. Under optimized conditions, the catalyst achieved about 97.3% degradation with an apparent pseudo-first-order rate constant of 0.024 min-1, which was about 12 times higher than that of direct photolysis. Radical scavengers' experiments showed that hydroxyl radicals (˙OH) acted as major reactive species, followed by superoxide radicals (˙O2 -) and photogenerated holes (h+). The catalyst showed good recyclability with about 86% activity retained after five cycles. These results offer an environmentally sustainable approach to recycle PET waste into a useful photocatalyst for water treatment.

articles.title: Clinical and Electrophysiological Characteristics of Peripheral Neuropathy in Immune-Related Adverse Event of Immune Checkpoint Inhibitors: A Retrospective Study and Literature Review.
articles.journal: Journal of clinical neurophysiology : official publication of the American Electroencephalographic Society
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To summarize clinical and laboratory characteristics of peripheral neurological immune-related adverse event (irAEs-PN) patients, to improve understanding and provide reference for early diagnosis of irAEs-PN caused by immune checkpoint inhibitors.

METHODS: We screened 61 patients with irAEs in our center from September 2020 to June 2025. In addition, studies with detailed clinical data related to irAEs-PN were collected in PubMed database from January 2015 to June 2025. A total of 50 patients with irAEs-PN were included, including 8 cases from our center and 42 cases reported in literature. The patients' demographic information, clinical characteristics, electrophysiological examination, therapy and outcomes were retrospectively analyzed and summarized.

RESULTS: Among the eight patients in our center, the first symptom was paresthesia, occurring in two cases, and limb weakness, occurring in six cases. Electrophysiology identified two axonal neuropathies, three demyelinating, and three mixed axonal and demyelinating neuropathies. Among the 42 patients reported in literature, the first symptom was paresthesia, occurring in 39 cases, and limb weakness, occurring in 41 cases. Electromyography identified 13 axonal neuropathies, 25 demyelinating neuropathies, and 4 mixed axonal and demyelinating neuropathies.

CONCLUSIONS: In most patients, irAEs-PN is characterized by demyelinating sensorimotor involvement of both the upper and lower limbs. In individuals receiving immune checkpoint inhibitors, prompt electromyography after the onset of neuropathic symptoms can aid in detecting neurological involvement and facilitate earlier treatment.

articles.title: Superior Efficacy of Besifovir in Reducing Hepatocellular Carcinoma Risk Compared to Tenofovir in Chronic Hepatitis B Patients: A Nationwide Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Besifovir dipivoxil maleate (BSV) is a novel therapeutic option for the treatment of chronic hepatitis B (CHB). However, its long-term effectiveness in reducing the risk of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains unclear.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the Korean Health Insurance Review and Assessment Service database from 2018 to 2022. A total of 32,383 patients with CHB were included (BSV, n = 2,358; tenofovir disoproxil fumarate [TDF], n = 30,025). Propensity score matching was conducted at a 1:3 ratio to minimize selection bias. The primary outcome was the incidence of HCC, with cirrhosis development as the secondary endpoint.

RESULTS: In the overall population, 57 cases of HCC were reported in the BSV group (2,358 individuals, 5,918 person-years), while 1,268 cases of HCC were reported in the TDF group (30,025 individuals, 83,587 person-years). After propensity score matching, the incidence of HCC was significantly lower in the BSV group (9.63 per 1,000 person-years; 95% confidence interval [CI], 7.43-12.49) than in the TDF group (15.36 per 1,000 person-years; 95% CI, 13.72-17.18), with an incidence rate ratio of 1.59 (P = 0.001). This protective effect remained consistent in both cirrhotic (hazard ratio [HR], 1.609; P = 0.028) and non-cirrhotic subgroups (HR, 1.831; P = 0.002).

CONCLUSION: BSV treatment demonstrated superior efficacy in reducing the risk of HCC compared to TDF, regardless of baseline cirrhosis status. These findings suggest that BSV may provide enhanced protection against HCC in patients with CHB.

articles.title: Publishing Quality Statistics Videos on YouTube: Analysis of Sources and Publishing Formats.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study aims to assess the content quality, presentation characteristics, and viewer engagement of YouTube videos on statistics, and to compare video quality categories based on fundamental video parameters, interaction metrics, presentation formats, and content sources.

METHODS: YouTube videos were searched for on November 17, 2025, using the search terms "statistical analysis," "data analysis," "statistics," and "statistical methods." The top 50 most relevant videos for each search term were assessed; after applying exclusion criteria, 114 videos were reviewed. The Global Quality Scale was used to measure video quality, and reliability was determined using a modified DISCERN tool. Videos were divided into low-, intermediate-, and high-quality categories. Engagement metrics and presentation methods were compared among quality groups.

RESULTS: Eighty-seven (76.3%) of the videos were categorized as high quality. Statistically significant differences were observed among video quality groups in daily views, likes, and comments (P < 0.001 for all comparisons); these differences were attributed to the disparity between the low- and high-quality groups. Videos produced by academic institutions, nonprofit associations, and professional experts had higher percentages classified in the high-quality category (n = 1; 100%, n = 5; 83.3%, and n = 32; 80%, respectively). Presentation formats differed significantly across quality categories, with greater diversity observed in high-quality videos. Within this group, slide-based presentations accounted for 33.3%, animated content for 32.2%, and demonstration-based (software-centric) videos for 18.4% (P = 0.020).

CONCLUSION: A substantial proportion of YouTube videos on statistics were rated high quality, and significant differences were observed in engagement metrics across quality groups. The quality distribution varied by video source and presentation format. These findings emphasize the need for educators and content developers to integrate accurate statistical content with engaging presentation formats to improve the educational value of YouTube videos.

articles.title: Screening for Left Ventricular Dysfunction in Sepsis Using a Smartphone ECG Analysis Application: A Multicenter Validation Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sepsis-induced left ventricular (LV) dysfunction complicates fluid resuscitation, increasing the risk of pulmonary edema and worsening outcomes. Echocardiographic assessment is often delayed, and natriuretic peptides such as N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) have limited diagnostic accuracy in this setting. We evaluated a smartphone-based electrocardiogram (ECG) analysis application for screening LV dysfunction in patients with sepsis.

METHODS: In this multicenter retrospective observational study, we included 425 adult sepsis patients from three university hospitals who underwent both a 12-lead ECG and transthoracic echocardiography within 72 hours of emergency department admission. ECG images displayed on a monitor were photographed and analyzed using an artificial intelligence (AI)-based smartphone application (ECG Buddy™), which generated a quantitative digital biomarker for LV dysfunction (quantitative electrocardiogram scores for LV dysfunction [QCG-LVDys]). LV dysfunction was defined as a left ventricular ejection fraction ≤ 40%. The diagnostic performance of QCG-LVDys for detecting LV dysfunction was evaluated using area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (ROC-AUC). A predefined comparison with NT-proBNP was performed in the single center where NT-proBNP was routinely measured.

RESULTS: In the overall multicenter cohort, QCG-LVDys showed high diagnostic performance for LV dysfunction, with an ROC-AUC of 0.901. Using an optimized threshold (37.35), QCG-LVDys achieved a sensitivity of 89.6%, specificity of 75.1%, and negative predictive value (NPV) of 97.5%. In the NT-proBNP subset, QCG-LVDys outperformed NT-proBNP (ROC-AUC 0.911 vs. 0.637, P < 0.001). Higher QCG-LVDys values were associated with increased lactate levels (P = 0.002) and 28-day in-hospital mortality (P < 0.001).

CONCLUSION: AI-driven ECG analysis via a smartphone app provided a rapid, accessible, and accurate screening tool for LV dysfunction in sepsis and outperformed NT-proBNP. Its high NPV suggests potential utility for early risk stratification and for informing cautious hemodynamic management, although prospective studies are needed to define its role in sepsis treatment protocols.

articles.title: Mesenchymal stem cells in diabetic kidney disease: Potential regulatory mechanisms and related signaling pathways of mesenchymal stem cells.
articles.abstract: Diabetic kidney disease (DKD) is a severe complication of diabetes and the leading cause of end-stage renal disease (ESRD). However, DKD treatment remains challenging owing to its complex etiology and unclear pathogenesis. Recent reports of the anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, antifibrotic, and regenerative properties of mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) indicate that they may serve as potential novel treatments for kidney disease-particularly DKD. However, current MSC-based therapies for DKD are at the initial clinical stage of research with the precise underlying mechanisms requiring further investigation. Current studies have predominantly concentrated on the renal protective effects mediated by classical signaling pathways such as Wnt/β-catenin, phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase/protein kinase B/mammalian target of rapamycin (PI3K/Akt/mTOR), vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF), transforming growth factor-β1 (TGF-β1)/Smad, and nuclear factor-erythroid 2-related factor 2 (Nrf2), whereas other potentially relevant pathways remain insufficiently investigated. This review comprehensively discusses the key MSC-regulated signaling pathways and their therapeutic potential to provide a theoretical foundation for DKD-related drug development and its clinical translation.

articles.title: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease increases the risk of cardiovascular disease occurrence in nonsmokers: A nationwide cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is among the leading causes of mortality worldwide, and patients experience a high prevalence of concomitant cardiovascular diseases (CVDs). In this study, we aimed to determine whether never smokers with COPD exhibit an increased risk of CVD compared with those without COPD and whether this risk parallels that observed in smokers with COPD.

METHODS: We conducted a prospective cohort study using data from the China Kadoorie Biobank (CKB). Spirometry was performed on all the participants, and COPD was defined as the ratio of forced expiratory volume in 1 second to forced vital capacity (FEV1/FVC) <0.7. Eligible participants in our study were free of diagnosed CVDs, including ischemic heart disease, heart failure, hypertension, or atrial fibrillation at baseline. The clinical outcomes were the incidences of these 4 CVDs and their overall incidence during follow-up. Cox proportional hazard models were used to estimate the associations of COPD and smoking status with incident CVD outcomes.

RESULTS: Among all eligible participants (n = 366,161, 20,887 with COPD), 40,861 incident cases of CVD events were observed during a median follow-up time of 10 years. Compared with never smokers without COPD, those with COPD exhibited a significantly higher risk of overall CVD, with hazard ratios (HRs) of 1.23 (95% CI: 1.09-1.39) for men and 1.24 (95% CI: 1.17-1.31) for women. Among male COPD participants, the incidence rates of overall CVD, ischemic heart disease, and hypertension, but not that of heart failure, were similar between never smokers and smokers. In contrast, female COPD participants who never smoked exhibited lower risks across all cardiovascular endpoints compared with their smoking counterparts. These results remained unchanged after propensity score matching.

CONCLUSION: In never smokers, COPD per se serves as an independent risk factor for CVD. Among men with COPD, smoking exposure confers no added hazard, whereas women with COPD who smoke remain at higher risk for CVD than their never-smoking counterparts.

articles.title: Long-term trends in pediatric intussusception in Hokkaido, Japan, 2007-2024 across the rotavirus vaccination era.
articles.journal: Journal of pediatric gastroenterology and nutrition
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Pediatric intussusception is the most common cause of acute intestinal obstruction in young children. We investigated long-term epidemiological trends in pediatric intussusception before and after rotavirus vaccine introduction and during the COVID-19 pandemic in Hokkaido, Japan.

METHODS: A retrospective multicenter surveillance study was conducted at 17 hospitals in Hokkaido between 2007 and 2024. Clinical characteristics, management, outcomes, and viral antigen test results were collected. Only cases fulfilling Brighton Level 1 diagnostic certainty were included. Annual incidence rates were calculated using regional population statistics.

RESULTS: A total of 513 children met the inclusion criteria, with 93.0% aged 0-4 years. Non-surgical reduction was successful in 94.0% of cases, and no deaths or long-term sequelae were observed. Among infants aged <1 year, incidence decreased from 99.4 per 100,000 person-years during the pre-vaccination period (2007-2011) to 69.9 during the voluntary vaccination period (2012-2019), and was 79.7 during the universal vaccination/COVID-19 period (2020-2024). Corresponding incidence rates among children aged 0-4 years were 55.4, 36.7, and 38.1 per 100,000 person-years, respectively.

CONCLUSION: Among children aged 0-4 years, intussusception incidence was lower during the period following rotavirus vaccine introduction than during the pre-vaccine period and remained broadly stable during the universal vaccination and COVID-19 period. The observed changes cannot be attributed to rotavirus vaccination alone because of concurrent changes in infectious disease circulation and other population-level factors. Continued surveillance is warranted to further clarify the epidemiology of pediatric intussusception.

articles.title: Outcomes and Predictors of Inpatient Mortality for Infective Endocarditis in Patients with Malignancy: Contemporary Nationwide Study from the United States.
articles.abstract: Infective endocarditis (IE) in patients with malignancy represents a high-risk clinical cohort, yet nationwide data on outcomes and predictors of mortality remain limited. Using the United States National Inpatient Sample (2016-2022), we identified hospitalizations involving IE and a malignancy diagnosis. Inpatient mortality, complications, and temporal trends were analyzed overall and across malignancy subtypes, causative organisms, and prosthetic valve status. Survey-weighted multivariable logistic regression was performed across the full IE cohort. Of 635 715 IE hospitalizations, 44 060 (6.9%) involved a malignancy diagnosis. Inpatient mortality was higher in this group than among IE hospitalizations without malignancy (13.5% vs 9.8%; P < .001), and malignancy remained associated with mortality after adjustment (adjusted odds ratio 1.29; 95% CI 1.19-1.39; P < .001). The proportion of IE hospitalizations involving malignancy increased from 6.7% in 2016 to 7.7% in 2022. Fungal infection, shock, acute kidney injury, and stroke were associated with mortality. Prosthetic-valve IE had lower mortality than non-prosthetic-valve IE (7.7% vs 13.9%; P < .001). These findings identify a high-risk, heterogeneous phenotype and support earlier diagnostic evaluation and coordinated oncology, cardiology, and infectious diseases management.

articles.title: Apolipoprotein A (ApoA) in Cardiovascular Disorders: Connections and Insights.
articles.abstract: Apolipoprotein A (ApoA) family members-ApoA-I, ApoA-II, ApoA-IV, and ApoA-V-play important roles in the vasculature that extend beyond lipid transport to regulate lipid-immune crosstalk, vascular homeostasis, and triglyceride metabolism. ApoA-I mediates reverse cholesterol transport, yet its cardioprotective capacity depends on functional integrity rather than HDL-cholesterol levels alone. ApoA-II, ApoA-IV, and ApoA-V exhibit context-dependent roles ranging from enhancing cholesterol efflux and triglyceride clearance to modulating inflammation, oxidative stress, endothelial activation, and thrombosis. Post-translational modifications such as oxidation, glycation, and citrullination within inflammatory milieus can convert protective ApoA proteins into dysfunctional or proinflammatory mediators. Genetic variations within APOA gene clusters have clarified the causal contribution of triglyceride-rich lipoproteins to atherosclerotic risk, shifting emphasis from HDL quantity toward lipoprotein quality and remnant cholesterol burden. In this comprehensive review, we synthesize structural, genetic, mechanistic, and clinical evidence to evaluate the position of the 4 ApoA proteins as context-dependent modulators of cardiovascular disease. We highlight the dualistic nature of their actions and examine failed clinical trials of ApoA-I infusions and mimetic peptides. We conclude by discussing how shifting focus from HDL quantity toward lipoprotein quality and preservation of ApoA functional integrity may inform more precise approaches to residual cardiovascular risk and triglyceride-driven atherogenesis.

articles.title: Anal Incontinence in Primiparous Women With Second- to Fourth-Degree Perineal Tears One Year After Vaginal Delivery: Development and Validation of a Multivariable Prediction Model.
articles.journal: BJOG : an international journal of obstetrics and gynaecology
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To develop and validate a prediction model estimating the individual risk of anal incontinence 1 year postpartum following second-, third- and fourth-degree perineal tears.

DESIGN: Development of a prognostic prediction model.

SETTING: Data were retrieved from three Swedish health and quality registers.

POPULATION: 8909 primiparous women with second-, third- and fourth-degree perineal tears who delivered vaginally at ≥ 34 weeks' gestation between 2014 and 2019.

METHODS: Seventeen predictors were identified as candidate variables. A prediction model was built using logistic regression to predict anal incontinence at 1 year postpartum. Additional models were built for gas and faecal incontinence. Model performance was assessed using the Efron-Gong optimism bootstrap. Temporal validation was conducted in a separate cohort of women who delivered between 2020 and 2022.

MAIN OUTCOME MEASURE: Anal incontinence (gas and/or faecal incontinence) at 1 year postpartum.

RESULTS: Seven variables remained in the final model for anal incontinence. A high Wexner score was the strongest predictor of anal incontinence at 1 year postpartum. The models accurately predicted anal incontinence (AUC 0.78, 95% CI: 0.76-0.80), faecal incontinence (AUC 0.80, 95% CI: 0.77-0.83), and gas incontinence (AUC 0.78, 95% CI: 0.76-0.80). Calibration curves demonstrated that all models were accurate, particularly for women with third-degree tears. Temporal validation confirmed the high accuracy (AUC 0.78; 95% CI: 0.75-0.81).

CONCLUSIONS: The article presents an accurate prediction model for anal incontinence at 1 year after vaginal delivery among women with second-, third- and fourth-degree perineal tears, based on perineal laceration register data collected at 8 weeks postpartum.

articles.title: Metal-Polyphenol Network-Based Biomaterials for Infected Bone Defects: Microenvironment Regulation and Stage-Oriented Regenerative Strategies.
articles.abstract: Infected bone defects are not simply bone defects complicated by bacterial infection; they are dynamic pathological niches in which biofilms, intracellular bacterial persistence, oxidative stress, dysregulated immunity, vascular failure, and pathological bone remodeling are mutually reinforcing. This coupling explains why bacterial killing alone rarely restores functional bone. Metal-polyphenol networks (MPNs), assembled through reversible coordination between metal ions and polyphenols, can translate these pathological stimuli into programmable therapy. Their tunable composition, interfacial adhesion, and pH/redox-responsive disassembly support a therapeutic transition from early infection control to redox-inflammatory regulation and vascularized bone regeneration. This review presents a disease-oriented framework connecting MPN chemistry and architecture with the evolving microenvironment of infected bone defects. Recent strategies for targeting planktonic and biofilm-associated bacteria, balancing reactive oxygen species generation and scavenging, reshaping osteoimmune signaling, protecting mitochondrial function, coupling angiogenesis with osteogenesis, and rebalancing bone remodeling are critically examined. Emphasis is placed on stage-oriented design, therapeutic trade-offs, and translational gaps. Priorities include eliminating hidden bacterial reservoirs, controlling ion dosing and long-term safety, evaluating functional vascularization and mechanical integration, and standardizing disease models. MPNs are thereby positioned as programmable platforms that coordinate infection resolution with durable bone regeneration.

articles.title: Resveratrol reduces inflammatory responses in peripheral blood mononuclear cells from patients with severe asthma.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Severe asthma is a chronic inflammatory airway disease frequently associated with neutrophilic inflammation, corticosteroid resistance, and persistent activation of pro-inflammatory signaling pathways, including nuclear factor kappa B (NF-κB) and mitogen-activated protein kinases (MAPKs).

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to investigate the effects of resveratrol on inflammatory responses in peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) obtained from healthy subjects and patients with severe asthma.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: PBMCs were stimulated with lipopolysaccharide (LPS; 1 µg/mL) for 24 h in the presence or absence of resveratrol (10-4-10-8 M). Cell viability was assessed using the MTT assay, cytokine levels (IL-6, IL-8, and IL-10) were measured by ELISA, and intracellular signaling pathways (NF-κB, ERK1/2, and p38 MAPK) were evaluated by flow cytometry.

RESULTS: Resveratrol did not affect cell viability and significantly reduced IL-6 and IL-8 production in a dose-dependent manner in LPS-stimulated PBMCs, without altering IL-10 levels. Additionally, resveratrol attenuated the phosphorylation of NF-κB, ERK1/2, and p38 MAPK in both monocytes and lymphocytes from healthy individuals and patients with severe asthma.

DISCUSSION AND CONCLUSION: Resveratrol exerts significant anti-inflammatory effects in human PBMCs by modulating cytokine production and key intracellular signaling pathways associated with severe asthma, suggesting its potential as a complementary therapeutic strategy.

articles.title: Early Ulnar Artery Occlusion and Recanalization After Coronary Angiography via Distal Ulnar Access: A Doppler-Followed Case Series.
articles.abstract: This single-center retrospective case series assessed early ulnar artery patency by Doppler ultrasonography (DUS) after coronary angiography via distal ulnar access (DUA), described flow evolution in patients with follow-up, and reported access-related complications. Thirty-eight consecutive patients with a day-3 DUS after coronary angiography via DUA between September 2023 and March 2024 were included. All procedures were performed by 1 operator using a short 6F sheath and 5000 IU intra-arterial heparin. Flow was categorized as thrombosis/no flow, monophasic, or triphasic; the primary endpoint was day-3 non-triphasic flow, and month-1 and month-3 DUS were selective. Mean age was 58.8 ± 10.1 years and 47.4% were male; 21.1% underwent same-session percutaneous coronary intervention. On day 3, thrombosis/no flow occurred in 18.4% (7/38), monophasic flow in 5.3% (2/38), and triphasic flow in 76.3% (29/38); non-triphasic flow was 23.7% (9/38). Month-1 DUS (n = 35) showed no thrombosis/no flow and 94.3% triphasic flow; month-3 DUS (n = 4) was triphasic in all. No clinically relevant hematoma, neuropathy, hand ischemia, or functional impairment was documented. After coronary angiography via DUA, day-3 non-triphasic flow occurred in 23.7%; selective follow-up suggested recanalization without major clinical complications, but limits generalizability.

articles.title: Maternal PFOS Exposure Impairs β‑Cell Insulin Secretion and Glucose Tolerance in Rats.
articles.journal: Toxicological sciences : an official journal of the Society of Toxicology
articles.abstract: Perfluorooctanesulfonic acid (PFOS) is epidemiologically linked to gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM), but the mechanisms remain undefined. We hypothesized that PFOS exposure impairs pancreatic β-cell function through mitochondrial dysfunction and deficits in ATP/cAMP signaling. Pregnant and non-pregnant rats received PFOS (50 μg/mL in drinking water) for 17 days (gestation day [GD] 4-20 in pregnant dams). PFOS-exposed pregnant dams exhibited fasting hypoinsulinemia (65% decrease) with normal fasting glucose. Glucose tolerance was impaired (31% increase in glucose AUC), with blunted insulin secretion (52% decrease in insulin AUC). In contrast, non-pregnant PFOS-exposed rats showed no changes in fasting glucose or insulin but developed glucose intolerance (25% increase in glucose AUC) with only modest early insulin suppression, revealing greater vulnerability in pregnancy. Pancreatic islet morphology and insulin content remained unchanged in PFOS-exposed dams. Isolated islets from PFOS-exposed dams and INS-1 β-cells treated with PFOS (10-100 μM) showed reduced glucose-stimulated insulin secretion despite normal Ins1 and Ins2 expression and insulin content. In INS-1 cells, PFOS selectively reduced Complex II subunits, depleted ATP (32-39%) and cAMP (57-74%), and impaired insulin secretion under low and high glucose. Co-treatment with the mitochondria-targeted antioxidant MitoQ (0.1μM) fully restored ATP, cAMP, and insulin secretion to control levels. These findings demonstrate that PFOS exposure causes gestational glucose intolerance and β-cell secretory failure, accompanied by reduced mitochondrial Complex II subunit abundance and ATP/cAMP depletion. The complete rescue by MitoQ highlights oxidative mitochondrial dysfunction as a mechanistic contributor linking PFOS exposure and GDM risk.

articles.title: Explainable Machine Learning Model for Personalized Assessment of the Need for Intensive Care in Patients with Myasthenia Gravis Based on Phenotype and Inflammatory Markers.
articles.journal: QJM : monthly journal of the Association of Physicians
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Early identification of myasthenia gravis (MG) severe exacerbations that require intensive care unit (ICU) admission remains challenging due disease highly heterogeneous. Existing models seldom incorporate phenotype stratification, limiting interpretability and clinical utility.

AIM: This study aimed to develop an explainable machine learning (ML) model to assess phenotype-specific risk factors and predict ICU admission for patients with MG.

DESIGN AND METHODS: This retrospective study included 319 hospitalized patients with MG. We utilized clinical variables and systemic inflammation markers for ML modeling. Subgroups were prespecified by thymoma status and age at onset. Primary outcome was need for intensive care during the hospitalization. Model performance was assessed. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) was employed for interpretation of global and individual features.

RESULTS: Of 319 admissions, 33 (10.3%) required ICU care. Four ML models were trained with nested 3-fold validation. eXtreme Gradient Boosting performed best (AUC: 0.94). SHAP ranked MGFA clinical classification, infection during admission, body mass index, and inflammatory indices as principal predictors. Subgroup analyses revealed phenotype-specific patterns, including opposite SHAP directions for inflammatory markers between thymoma and non-thymoma groups and distinct rankings between different age of onset groups. SHAP-based personalized explanations revealed patient-specific variations in risk ranking and directionality of predictive features. A web-based calculator was developed to support real-time clinical implementation of the model, potentially allowing for risk stratification.

CONCLUSIONS: An explainable machine learning framework that integrates clinical features with systemic inflammation indices reliably predicts ICU admission in MG and reveals phenotype-specific risk patterns, enabling personalized risk stratification in MG management.

articles.title: Efficacy of Ccombody as an Immunoprophylaxis Strategy: Impact on Immune Gene Expression of Pacific White Shrimp (Penaeus vannamei) Against Acute Hepatopancreatic Necrosis Disease (AHPND).
articles.abstract: Acute hepatopancreatic necrosis disease (AHPND) is caused by a plasmid bearing strain of Vibrio parahaemolyticus (VpAHPND), which produces PirA and PirB toxins that specifically target and damage hepatopancreatic and epithelial cells of the shrimp gastrointestinal tract. The impact of AHPND, together with concerns regarding antibiotic resistance, has necessitated investigations into alternative forms of disease prevention. This study evaluated the protective efficacy of Ccombody, a recombinant variable lymphocyte receptor B (VLRB)-based antibody targeting the PirA toxin, on immune-related gene expression and survival in Pacific white shrimp (Penaeus vannamei) challenged with VpAHPND. Shrimp were allocated into six experimental groups, each in triplicate. Two groups served as controls fed a basal commercial diet: an unchallenged negative control and a VpAHPND-challenged positive control. An additional reference group was fed a commercial diet supplemented with IgY at 500 mg/100 g feed. The remaining three treatment groups were fed diets supplemented with the Ccombody at 1, 10 or 100 mg/100 g feed for 7 days. At 7 days post-feeding (7 d.p.f.), prophenoloxidase-2 (proPO-2), anti-lipopolysaccharide factors-1 (ALF-1) and penaeidin-4 (PEN4) expression levels showed no significant differences among treatments. At 24 h post-infection (24 h.p.i.), proPO-2 expression of Ccombody groups differed significantly from both the positive and negative control groups (p < 0.05), while no significant differences were observed among Ccombody-treated groups. ALF-1 expression remained unchanged across treatments. In contrast, the Ccombody 1 and 10 mg/100 g feed groups showed significantly enhanced PEN4 expression compared to the positive control group (p < 0.05). Notably, PEN4 expression significantly increased in Ccombody 1 mg/100 g feed group at 24 h.p.i. relative to 7 d.p.f. (p < 0.05), whereas a decline was observed in the positive control and Ig-Guard A groups. Principal component analysis (PCA) also showed the same scattering trend towards gene expression analysis at both 7 d.p.f. and 24 h.p.i. Dietary supplementation with Ccombody 1, 10 and 100 mg/100 g feed effectively reduced the mortality rate following challenge with V. parahaemolyticus causing AHPND. All supplemented groups showed highly significant reduction in mortality compared to the positive control group (p < 0.001). Among them, the 10 and 100 mg/100 g feed groups exhibited the lowest mortality rates (3.70% ± 1.28% and 3.70% ± 3.39%, respectively). When considered alongside the immune-related gene expression, these findings suggest that Ccombody has strong potential as an alternative immunoprophylaxis strategy for the prevention of VpAHPND.

articles.title: Evaluation of radiation dose reduction effect of a foldable attached lead curtain in portable X-ray examinations in the neonatal intensive care unit: A Monte Carlo simulation study.
articles.journal: Journal of X-ray science and technology
articles.abstract: Mobile X-ray examinations in neonatal intensive care units (NICUs) are essential for the critically ill neonates. However, scattered radiation generated during imaging can lead to unnecessary radiation exposure for adjacent neonates and healthcare workers. Conventional mobile shielding devices are often challenging to implement effectively in NICU environments due to limited space and workflow constraints. Consequently, this study developed a foldable lead curtain that can be attached to a mobile X-ray unit and evaluated experimental measurements and Monte Carlo simulations. The lead curtain features a foldable acrylic panel structure that contains 0.15 mmPb shielding material and is designed for attachment to a mobile X-ray unit. Shielding efficiency experiments showed that the lead curtain reduced scattered radiation by 91.1% at a distance of 50 cm when positioned directly in the scatter path. At distances of 100 cm and 150 cm, the shielded readings fell below the detection limit of the ionization chamber dosimeter. Notably, significant dose reductions were observed even under the relatively low shielding condition of 0.15 mmPb. These findings suggest that the proposed attachable foldable lead curtain may serve as a practical auxiliary radiation protection device for reducing scattered radiation exposure to adjacent neonates, which often face substantial spatial limitations.

articles.title: Financial burden, non-medical drivers of health, and early caregiving role formation after stroke: a scoping review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Family caregivers are essential to stroke recovery, yet existing assessments may not adequately capture structural factors influencing caregiving capacity. Financial toxicity, non-medical drivers of health (NMDOH), and caregiver role formation during early post-stroke recovery remain poorly characterized. This scoping review evaluated how current caregiver assessments address these domains.

METHODS: A scoping review using the Arksey and O'Malley and Levac frameworks was reported according to PRISMA-ScR guidelines. Four databases were searched for studies published within the past 10 years examining informal caregiving during hospitalization, inpatient rehabilitation, or early transition home after stroke. Data were extracted on caregiver assessments, financial toxicity, NMDOH, and caregiver role formation.
