RESULTS: Sixteen studies were included. Assessments commonly capture caregiver burden, psychosocial distress, preparedness, social support, and caregiving tasks. Financial toxicity was absent in seven studies; most others assessed only subjective financial strain or a single objective indicator, such as income loss. Only one study assessed financial toxicity multidimensionally, incorporating income loss, direct costs, and debt. Employment and healthcare access were the most frequently assessed NMDOH domains (11 studies each), while housing and transportation were less frequently addressed; food security was absent. All studies addressed aspects of caregiver role formation, most commonly preparedness, but only one examined its relationship with financial toxicity.

CONCLUSIONS: Caregiver assessments inconsistently capture financial toxicity and NMDOH. Future instruments should integrate multidimensional financial toxicity and NMDOH measures with caregiver role formation to better identify vulnerability and support equitable, sustainable stroke recovery.

articles.title: Heat-Shock and Cold-Shock Proteins in Energy-Based Aesthetic Medicine.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Energy-based aesthetic devices alter tissue temperature across defined spatial and temporal distributions, producing biological effects commonly described as collagen contraction, neocollagenesis, elastogenesis, adipocyte injury, or tissue tightening. These clinical labels encompass distinct processes including protein damage, cellular stress adaptation, inflammation, cell death, extracellular matrix turnover, and long-term remodeling. Heat-shock proteins (HSPs) and mammalian cold-shock proteins provide a mechanistic framework for interpreting these responses.

OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the roles of heat- and cold-responsive proteins in energy-based aesthetic medicine and propose a temperature-time-depth framework linking device-specific tissue exposure to molecular, histological, and clinical responses.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: A structured narrative review was conducted using targeted PubMed searches and examination of reference lists from pivotal mechanistic and human-tissue studies. Literature through August 2026 was considered. Priority was given to studies reporting tissue-temperature measurements, human skin biopsies, spatial histology, protein or RNA measurements, controls, serial assessments, and late clinical or structural outcomes.

RESULTS: Heat activates heat-shock factor 1 and induces HSP70, HSP27, HSP90, and other chaperones. HSP47 (SERPINH1) is particularly relevant to dermal remodeling because it is an endoplasmic reticulum collagen chaperone required for procollagen folding, trafficking, and secretion. Human studies of fractional laser and radiofrequency, together with emerging microfocused ultrasound histology, support a sequence in which early stress and inflammatory responses precede HSP47-positive fibroblast recruitment and matrix remodeling. However, HSP induction alone does not establish durable clinical tightening, and excessive thermal exposure may cause necrosis, fibrosis, scarring, dyschromia, or injury to nerves and fat. Mammalian cold adaptation involves cold-inducible RNA-binding protein (CIRBP/CIRP) and RNA-binding motif protein 3 (RBM3), best characterized during sustained mild hypothermia near 32°C-34°C. These proteins regulate RNA stability, translation, metabolism, and cell survival. Their adaptive intracellular functions must be distinguished from profound cold injury and extracellular CIRP-mediated inflammation. Direct evidence linking aesthetic cooling to CIRBP- or RBM3-mediated dermal neocollagenesis remains insufficient.

CONCLUSIONS: Mechanistic interpretation should be based on measured biological dose, tissue compartment, and response timing rather than console temperature, surface temperature, or device category alone. Heat-shock mechanisms are supported for several thermal modalities, whereas cold-shock-mediated aesthetic neocollagenesis remains a translational hypothesis requiring direct molecular, histological, and clinical validation.

articles.title: Modifiable Determinants of Exclusive Breastfeeding at NICU Discharge among Infants Born before 32 Weeks' Gestation: A Cross-Sectional Study in Malaysia.
articles.journal: Breastfeeding medicine : the official journal of the Academy of Breastfeeding Medicine
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mothers of preterm infants often face unique challenges in the Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (NICU), which may adversely affect breastfeeding outcomes.

AIM: To determine the rate of exclusive breastfeeding (EBF) at NICU discharge among infants born <32 weeks' gestation and to identify associated maternal and clinical factors.

METHOD: A cross-sectional study was conducted between 2021 and 2023 in two tertiary NICUs in Malaysia. A total of 180 mothers of preterm infants were enrolled. Prior to discharge, participants completed self-administered questionnaires assessing their breastfeeding experiences, including the NICU Mother's Breastfeeding Survey and the Breastfeeding Self-Efficacy Scale-Short Form (BSES-SF). Data on skin-to-skin contact, antenatal breastfeeding education, and prior breastfeeding experience were also collected.

RESULTS: EBF at discharge was achieved by 52% of the cohort. Factors significantly associated with EBF included prior breastfeeding experience (adjusted odds ratio [aOR]: 1.95; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.08-3.53; p = 0.03), antenatal breastfeeding education (aOR: 3.43; 95% CI: 1.36-8.64; p < 0.05), skin-to-skin contact in the NICU (aOR: 2.56; 95% CI: 1.20-5.47; p = 0.02), and higher BSES-SF scores (aOR: 2.19; 95% CI: 1.11-4.32; p = 0.02). Perceived breastfeeding barriers were significantly associated with lower odds of EBF (aOR: 0.11; 95% CI: 0.05-0.24; p = 0.001).

CONCLUSION: EBF at NICU discharge among preterm infants <32 weeks is influenced by modifiable maternal factors. Enhancing breastfeeding education, fostering self-efficacy, and encouraging early skin-to-skin contact may improve breastfeeding outcomes in this population.

articles.title: Trailhead to Triage: A Backcountry Ski Workshop for Sharpening Clinical Decision Making in Emergency Medicine Residents.
articles.abstract: IntroductionDecision making in emergency medicine is influenced by cognitive bias, time pressure, uncertainty, and incomplete or unreliable feedback. Outdoor experiential learning may provide an environment in which these decision-making processes can be experienced and discussed in a practical context.ObjectiveThis study evaluated a novel outdoor experiential learning workshop designed to assess changes in emergency medicine residents' self-reported awareness and understanding of decision-making science.MethodsWe conducted a prospective single-cohort study of emergency medicine residents participating in an outdoor experiential learning workshop. Residents completed a 15-min asynchronous video lecture during the 2 wk preceding the field day, followed by guided backcountry activities incorporating structured discussions of decision-making science and clinical parallels. Participants completed surveys before and after the workshop and a 3-mo follow-up survey. Descriptive statistics and independent-samples t tests were used to evaluate changes in self-reported decision-making awareness and understanding.ResultsThirty residents completed the pre-intervention survey, 21 (70%) completed the post-intervention survey, and 22 (73%) completed the 3-mo follow-up. All measures demonstrated overall improvements from before to after the survey. The largest improvement was in understanding the importance of feedback in decision making (3.53±1.17 vs 4.38±0.74; P=0.001). This improvement maintained statistical significance at the longitudinal follow-up (3.53±1.17 vs 4.09±1.11; P=0.043), reflecting continued appreciation for the value of feedback in decision making.ConclusionsParticipants reported increased awareness and understanding of decision-making science following the workshop, with several measures remaining elevated at the 3-mo follow-up. Participants also reported high levels of enjoyment and perceived educational value.

articles.title: Effects of a telerehabilitation 'booster' on maintaining communication gains after completion of an Intensive Comprehensive Aphasia Program (ICAP).
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Although a growing literature supports the positive effects immediately following participation in an Intensive Comprehensive Aphasia Program, there is little research assessing treatment maintenance following program completion. The Teleconnect Aphasia Group project was initiated to assess treatment maintenance and provide a 'boost' of continued intervention via telerehabilitation after completion of an Intensive Comprehensive Aphasia Program.

METHOD: A longitudinal cohort design was employed, with replication across two groups of three participants each. Six participants with stroke-associated aphasia were recruited following participation in an Intensive Comprehensive Aphasia Program, then completed one weekly 60 minute aphasia group therapy session and up to 60 minutes per week of individual coaching over four weeks (M = 1.88 hours/week).

RESULT: Pre-Teleconnect Aphasia Group, only one of six participants showed clear maintenance. After completing Teleconnect Aphasia Group, most participants demonstrated either language maintenance (n = 1) or trend reversal (n = 4). Notably, all participants demonstrated gains in functional, participation-focused communication, as assessed by personalised Goal Attainment Scales. Furthermore, all participants endorsed the benefit of continuing language/communication therapy through telerehabilitation groups, especially when supplemented with individual sessions.

CONCLUSION: Findings from this study support the provision of meaningful, impactful telerehabilitation group services to promote maintenance and generalisation of communication gains following participation in an Intensive Comprehensive Aphasia Program.

articles.title: Linking obesity and type 2 diabetes: Mechanistic insights and personalized nutritional strategies.
articles.abstract: BackgroundGlobally, the incidence of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and obesity is increasing at an alarming rate, with the World Health Organization reporting a sharp rise in both conditions over the past two decades. The emerging concept of "diabesity" underscores the close interconnection between excessive weight gain and the development of T2DM, together posing a major global public health challenge. Obesity directly and indirectly contributes to chronic diseases such as diabetes, atherosclerosis, hypertension, and certain cancers. Obese individuals show altered levels of inflammatory cytokines such as interleukin-6, tumor necrosis factor-α, and C-reactive protein, and this inflammation from visceral adiposity promotes insulin resistance, a key mechanism in T2DM development.AimThis narrative review aims to: (1) explore the pathophysiological mechanisms linking obesity to T2DM, with an emphasis on adipose tissue dysfunction, chronic low-grade inflammation, and insulin resistance; and (2) critically evaluate the potential of personalized nutrition-tailored dietary and lifestyle interventions based on an individual's metabolic, genetic, and lifestyle profile as a preventive strategy against diabesity.MethodsTo provide a comprehensive grasp of the subject, pertinent research on obesity, T2DM mechanisms, and personalized dietary approaches was found, examined, and summarized.SummaryVisceral adiposity and other obesity-related metabolic abnormalities play an important role in insulin resistance, a significant underlying mechanism in the aetiology of type 2 diabetes. By transcending the "one-size-fits-all" paradigm, personalized nutrition facilitates more precise and sustainable prevention and management of diabesity. "Personalized nutrition may transform diabetes management and prevention when incorporated into public health frameworks.

articles.title: Community Paramedics Address Health Inequities Within EMS Through Mobile Integrated Healthcare (MIH) Program Referrals from a "Medical Home".
articles.abstract: To advance local health equity, a large urban fire department's Mobile Integrated Healthcare (MIH) Unit worked with a Chicago-based health care organization to refer patients in "medical homes" to a MIH program. Medical home coordinators referred individuals to Community Paramedics (CPs) in the MIH Unit for program enrollment with a 4-visit model in 4 clinical pathways (hypertension, diabetes, asthma/Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease [COPD], and heart failure). A total of 911 utilization of ambulance transportation, emergency department (ED) visits, and inpatient hospitalizations before and after intervention were measured to gauge program impact. A postgraduation survey was distributed to participants. From November 2022 to March 2025, 68 referred individuals completed the program and graduated with a total of 321 in-person visits by CPs. Data were gathered for 6 months before program enrollment and 6 months post-intervention. The most common clinical pathway for graduated patients was hypertension (75%), diabetes (57%), asthma/COPD (47%), and heart failure (41%). Among graduated patients, there was a 43% decrease in 911 ambulance transports, a 46% decrease in ED utilization, and a 42% decrease in hospital admissions. The postgraduation survey was completed by 53% of program graduates; 81% reported symptom improvement, 58% indicated an improved relationship with their primary care clinic, and 74% agreed that CPs improved their overall health care experience. Creating a partnership between a patient's primary care medical home and a large urban fire department's MIH program is a successful strategy for decreasing 911 ambulance transports, ED utilization, and inpatient hospital admissions for individuals at risk for poor health outcomes.

articles.title: Barriers and motivators for sustainable eating in the Czech Republic: A cross-sectional pilot survey.
articles.abstract: BackgroundSustainable healthy diets benefit human and planetary health, but evidence on self-reported awareness and dietary practices remains limited in Central and Eastern Europe.AimTo explore self-reported awareness and adherence, perceived barriers, and motivators related to sustainable eating among adults in the Czech Republic.MethodsA cross-sectional online survey (n = 192) was conducted from March to July 2025 using non-probability purposive and snowball sampling. The questionnaire addressed awareness, dietary behaviours, information sources, barriers, and facilitators. Data were analysed using descriptive statistics and exploratory chi-square, Mann-Whitney U, and Kruskal-Wallis tests. Open-ended responses were reviewed descriptively; no formal qualitative analysis was conducted.SummarySeventy-one per cent reported familiarity with sustainable healthy diets, while median self-rated adherence was 5/10. The most frequently recognised principles were food waste reduction (74%) and consumption of local and seasonal products (72%). Major barriers were food cost (67%), lack of motivation (52%), and insufficient information (34%); key motivators were affordability (63%) and simple recipes (53%). Only 16% perceived school-based nutrition education as sufficient, 5% regularly used nutrition-related mobile applications, and 40% would attend a free course. This pilot study suggests a possible discrepancy between self-reported awareness and adherence among Czech respondents. Affordability, practical information, and nutrition education warrant further investigation. Given the exploratory design and non-representative sample, findings should be interpreted cautiously and used primarily to inform future research and evaluation of context-sensitive public health approaches.

articles.title: Investigation of Seroprevalence and the Risk Factors of Ehrlichia and Anaplasma Species Along the Texas-Mexico Border.
articles.journal: Vector borne and zoonotic diseases (Larchmont, N.Y.)
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ehrlichiosis and anaplasmosis are emerging tick-borne bacterial zoonotic diseases resulting from infections with Ehrlichia and Anaplasma species, respectively, within the family Anaplasmataceae. These tick-borne pathogens represent a growing public health problem in the United States.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: To assess their seroprevalence and risk factors for infection along the Texas-Mexico border, we conducted a cross-sectional seroprevalence study using plasma samples obtained from 616 adults residing in Starr County, Texas. Plasma samples were screened for IgG reactivity to Ehrlichia and Anaplasma antigens using a dual-spot indirect immunofluorescent assay. Ticks were also collected from this region and tested for Anaplasmataceae DNA.

RESULTS: Seroprevalence was higher for cases of Anaplasma spp. (10.4%) than Ehrlichia spp. (4.8%) and Anaplasmataceae unspecified (6.9%). Age and gender were both significantly associated with seropositivity. PCR testing of the collected ticks revealed a 12.4% (12/97) positivity for Ehrlichia canis, all detected in Rhipicephalus sanguineus (Brown dog) ticks, but none were positive for Anaplasma species.

CONCLUSION: These findings suggested that Ehrlichia and Anaplasma species are endemic in the region and highlighted the need for ongoing surveillance and public health interventions.

articles.title: Early Changes in Post-Stroke Quality of Life and Associated Factors: A Prospective Study.
articles.abstract: BackgroundStroke affects physical, psychological, and social functioning. Early changes in health-related quality of life (HRQoL) remain incompletely characterized.ObjectivesTo assess early HRQoL changes after stroke and identify associated factors.MethodsWe assessed 111 patients with first-ever stroke at baseline, 1 month, and 3 months. Functional status, cognition, depressive symptoms, and HRQoL were evaluated using the Barthel Index, Functional Ambulation Scale, Mini-Mental State Examination, Beck Depression Inventory, Form-36 (SF-36) and the Stroke Impact Scale 3.0 (SIS 3.0). Paired tests, correlations with false discovery rate correction, and multivariable linear regression were used.ResultsNinety-seven patients completed follow-up. Physical and psychosocial HRQoL showed divergent recovery trajectories. SF-36 physical component scores progressively improved across both intervals (baseline to 1 month, p  =  0.006; 1 to 3 months, p = 0.033), whereas mental component scores improved only during the first month (p = 0.021) and showed no further significant improvement thereafter (p = 0.342). Similarly, SIS 3.0 emotion scores showed no significant change between 1 and 3 months (p = 0.831) and no significant net change over 3 months (q = 0.103), unlike the other domains, which continued to improve. In multivariable regression, functional ambulation at 3 months was independently associated with physical HRQoL change (β = 0.483, p < 0.001; adjusted R2 = 0.450), whereas depressive symptom severity was independently associated with mental HRQoL change (β = -0.692, p < 0.001; adjusted R2 = 0.667).ConclusionPhysical and psychosocial HRQoL did not recover in parallel during the first 3 months after stroke. Ambulation and depressive symptoms warrant separate attention during early rehabilitation planning.

articles.title: The Role of Decompressive Craniectomy for Severe Refractory Head Injury.
articles.abstract: Decompressive craniectomy is a potential therapeutic option for patients with severe traumatic brain injury and refractory intracranial hypertension, although its indications and clinical benefits remain controversial. A total of 4060 articles were identified, with 94.6% published after 2010. Several major randomized clinical trials have shaped current understanding of decompressive craniectomy, including the RESCUE-ASDH for primary intracranial hypertension, and the DECRA and RESCUEicp for secondary intracranial hypertension. RESCUE-ASDH and DECRA showed no overall benefit and suggested potential harm associated with decompressive craniectomy. RESCUEicp trial showed reduced mortality and sustained long-term improvement in a subset of patients, although many survivors remained in a dependent state. Critical appraisal of the inclusion and exclusion criteria of these trials, together with supporting evidence from animal studies, suggest that decompressive craniectomy should not be treated as primary intervention for traumatic brain injury. Instead, it may be more appropriately used as an adjunct procedure to prevent worsening cerebral edema following other neurosurgical interventions - such as evaluation of contusions or hematomas - when the operative hemisphere is tight and swollen. Decompressive craniectomy performed solely to control refractory intracranial hypertension in traumatic brain injury is unlikely to provide meaningful patient-centered benefit. Its role as an adjunct procedure after evacuation of contusions or hematomas remains uncertain, particularly in patients with a low predicted risk of unfavorable outcome. Decision regarding decompressive craniectomy should incorporate shared decision making and reflect careful consideration of the functional outcomes acceptable to patients and their families.

articles.title: Physical Activity and Sedentary Time in Chronic Stroke: An Agreement Study Between the IPAQ-SF and ActiGraph Measures.
articles.abstract: BackgroundThe International Physical Activity Questionnaire - Short Form (IPAQ-SF) and ActiGraph accelerometers are widely used and internationally recommended to assess physical activity (PA) and sedentary time (ST). However, their agreement in individuals with chronic stroke remains unclear.ObjectivesTo quantify the magnitude of agreement between IPAQ-SF and ActiGraph-derived weekly moderate-to-vigorous PA (MVPA), total PA, and ST in chronic stroke survivors.MethodsFifty community-dwelling adults with chronic stroke who walked independently were enrolled in this cross-sectional study. Participants wore an accelerometer (ActiGraph GT3X+) on the non-paretic side of the waist for seven consecutive days. The IPAQ-SF was completed via interview on the following day.ResultsIPAQ-SF and ActiGraph-derived estimates showed substantial individual-level discrepancies, with wide limits of agreement (LoA) across outcomes. For MVPA, the mean ratio was 1.02 (95%CI: 0.49 to 2.11; ratio LoA: 0.01 to 154.62). For total PA, the median ratio was 0.08 (95% CI: 0.06 to 0.14; non-parametric ratio LoA: 0.00 to 1.33). For ST, the mean ratio was 0.85 (95%CI: 0.78 to 0.92; ratio LoA: 0.47 to 1.53).ConclusionFindings indicate poor individual-level agreement between the IPAQ-SF and ActiGraph-derived estimates, with wide LoA and evidence of heteroscedasticity. At the group level, the IPAQ-SF underestimated total PA and ST, whereas MVPA showed no evidence of fixed bias. Although the IPAQ-SF may provide a broad descriptive assessment of PA and ST at the group level, it should not be used interchangeably with ActiGraph for individual-level estimation in individuals with chronic stroke.

articles.title: Headache disorders among Indigenous communities: A scoping review undertaken with knowledge keeper guidance.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: We performed a scoping review of literature on headache etiology, classification, prevalence, and treatment in Indigenous communities in Canada, the United States, Australia, and New Zealand.

BACKGROUND: In the United States, analysis of national prevalence indicates that Indigenous Americans lead all other racial/ethnic groups in headache prevalence. Risk factors associated with headache burden, including diabetes, head injury, psychological trauma, environmental exposures, and lack of access to appropriate diagnosis and treatment, have been documented in Indigenous communities across the geographies studied.

METHODS: A systematic search of literature in PubMed, Cumulative Index to Nursing and Allied Health Literature, Scopus, and Informit Indigenous Collection was conducted through January 2026 using descriptors of headache, migraine, and Indigenous populations across Canada, the United States, Australia, and New Zealand. Of the 616 citations identified, 30 publications from 1981 to 2024 were included in the present review and analyzed under the following areas of inquiry: (1) headache classification, (2) headache etiology, (3) headache prevalence, (4) headache treatment, and (5) barriers to headache care.

RESULTS: Analysis of national data in the United States indicates a higher prevalence of headache in Indigenous communities in comparison to all other communities. In Canada, evidence from smaller studies suggests a similar pattern. Prevalence data for Indigenous communities in Australia and New Zealand remains limited. Ethnographic data and expert informant data from Indigenous communities demonstrate conceptualization and treatment of headaches within biopsychosocial models that relate individuals to the life of their community and land. There were no data from medical headache treatment trials or intervention studies specific to or inclusive of Indigenous patients with headache. Barriers to headache care for Indigenous peoples were identified prior to diagnosis, at the point of assessment, and in treatment. Addressing these barriers demands system level changes as well as development of individual relations of respect and care for Indigenous patients.

CONCLUSIONS: Included studies from Canada, the United States, Australia, and New Zealand reported a high prevalence of headache in some Indigenous communities and suggest that this burden may result from or be associated with a combination of intergenerational trauma, adverse childhood experiences, lower socioeconomic status, head injury, environmental contaminants, and systemic racism resulting in barriers to diagnosis and care. Despite this apparent burden, the literature reveals a paucity of quality, headache-specific research conducted with Indigenous peoples across all four regions of study. To close gaps in headache diagnosis, treatment, and prevention, research and program development must be led by, or conducted in meaningful collaboration with, Indigenous communities in a manner that recognizes and uplifts Indigenous knowledge systems, healing, and conceptualizations of headache.

articles.title: Temporal dynamics of the cerebrospinal fluid proteome in tick-borne encephalitis and enteroviral meningitis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Tick-borne encephalitis (TBE) is a severe viral infection of the central nervous system (CNS), causing acute meningoencephalitis and often long-term neurocognitive sequelae. The lack of specific treatment for TBE highlights the need to improve understanding of disease mechanisms and identify novel biomarkers. Enteroviral meningitis is typically a milder infection of the CNS and rarely causes encephalitis.

OBJECTIVES: In this hypothesis-generating study, we aimed to characterise temporal changes in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) proteome in TBE and identify candidate biomarkers associated with pathophysiological mechanisms, disease severity, and neurocognitive outcome.

METHODS: Patients with TBE, enteroviral meningitis, or aseptic meningoencephalitis of unknown origin were retrospectively included from a previously established cohort. CSF proteomes were analysed by label-free mass spectrometry, followed by differential protein expression analysis and functional annotation. Temporal proteome dynamics and protein associations with disease severity and neurocognitive outcome were assessed. Data are available via ProteomeXchange with identifier PXD077931.

RESULTS: Proteomic analyses revealed alterations in proteins related to synaptic function, inflammatory pathways, the complement system, and the 14-3-3 protein family. Adrenomedullin was markedly increased in the late phase of TBE compared with enteroviral meningitis.

CONCLUSION: Temporal changes in the CSF proteome in TBE indicate a strong inflammatory response occurring in concert with lower levels of proteins related to synaptic function during the acute phase. These findings provide insights into the host response and pathogenesis of TBE and identify proteins of potential interest for future validation.

articles.title: Fine mapping of cucumber downy mildew resistance loci identifies candidate genes linked to ethylene-associated stomatal defence.
articles.journal: Journal of the science of food and agriculture
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Downy mildew, caused by Pseudoperonospora cubensis, is one of the most destructive diseases affecting cucumber and remains difficult to manage sustainably through fungicide-dependent control strategies. Although several resistance loci have been reported, many previously mapped regions remain too broad for efficient marker-assisted selection or reliable candidate-gene prioritisation. This study aimed to refine three TH118FLM-derived downy mildew resistance loci and to identify biologically plausible candidate genes associated with resistance by integrating advanced recombinant populations, QTL-seq, parent-bulk concordance analysis, and candidate-gene evaluation.

RESULTS: Two recombinant inbred line populations, dm2.1-F7 and dm2.2-F7, and one near-isogenic/backcross-derived population, dm5.1-BC4F2, were developed from a cross between TH118FLM and WMEJ. Phenotypic distributions in all three populations showed a higher frequency of susceptible disease-index classes, supporting the involvement of multiple resistance-associated quantitative loci rather than a single dominant resistance factor. QTL-seq reduced the dm2.1, dm2.2, and dm5.1 regions to 333, 296, and 694 kb, respectively. Subsequent parent-bulk concordance analysis of SNPs and INDELs further refined these loci to 61.7, 84.7, and 80.0 kb, containing seven, ten, and five annotated genes, respectively. By integrating positional, sequence, transcriptional, and predicted structural evidence, CsACO, CsCA, and CsSTPK were prioritised as the candidate genes for dm2.1, dm2.2, and dm5.1, respectively. Expression and physiological analyses further showed that these candidates responded to pathogen infection and ethephon treatment, while the resistant background exhibited reduced stomatal aperture and altered stomatal conductance following ethephon application, supporting a testable ethylene-associated stomatal-defence hypothesis.

CONCLUSION: This study refined three cucumber downy mildew resistance loci into compact, marker-ready intervals and identified CsACO, CsCA, and CsSTPK as biologically credible candidate genes. The findings provide practical genomic resources for marker-assisted cucumber resistance breeding and a testable biological framework, suggesting that TH118FLM-derived resistance may involve ethylene-associated stomatal defence. © 2026 The Author(s). Journal of the Science of Food and Agriculture published by John Wiley & Sons Ltd on behalf of Society of Chemical Industry.

articles.title: How well do junior neurology residents recognize multiple sclerosis? Analysis of the "Close the Loop" resident clinical acumen project.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate diagnostic accuracy and patterns of errors among junior neurology residents evaluating acute presentations of multiple sclerosis and other demyelinating diseases.

METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed a morning-report case log of overnight neurology consultations presented by postgraduate year-2 residents at a New York academic center over 6 years. Cases with an initial resident impression of multiple sclerosis/demyelinating disease or a final diagnosis of multiple sclerosis/demyelinating disease were analyzed using a predefined localization-etiology schema.

RESULTS: Among 1301 cases with uncertain initial diagnoses, 66 (5.1%) had an initial resident impression of multiple sclerosis/demyelinating disease and 57 (4.4%) had a final multiple sclerosis/demyelinating disease diagnosis. Overall diagnostic accuracy for multiple sclerosis/demyelinating disease presentations was 66.7%. Of initial multiple sclerosis/demyelinating disease impressions, 33.3% were incorrect (over-called); most errors occurred at the level of neurologic versus non-neurologic (40.9%) and central nervous system etiologies (40.9%). Among confirmed multiple sclerosis/demyelinating disease cases, 22.8% were under-called, predominantly due to errors in central nervous system etiology (69.2%).

CONCLUSIONS: Acute multiple sclerosis/demyelinating disease presentations pose educational challenges for neurology residents, with errors primarily arising from misclassification of central nervous system etiologies. Diagnostic accuracy was influenced by prior disease history and patient age, highlighting cognitive biases such as framing and anchoring. Structured feedback models like "close the loop" may help improve multiple sclerosis diagnostic acumen in residency training and clinical practice.

articles.title: Letter: "Natural History of Mild Non-Proliferative Diabetic Retinopathy in Adults with Type 1 Diabetes Under Contemporary Diabetes Care".
AI-Enhanced Wearable Glucose Sensors: From Intelligent Sensing to Closed-Loop Management of Diabetes.
articles.abstract: Wearable glucose sensors enable continuous monitoring of glycemic dynamics, yet their clinical utility is constrained by signal instability, physiological delay, and limited predictive capability. Artificial intelligence (AI) has been increasingly integrated to address these limitations. This review summarizes recent advances in AI-enhanced wearable glucose sensors, with a focus on the evolution of sensing technologies and the role of AI across three main aspects: calibration, glucose prediction, and wearable closed-loop control. In calibration, AI-based approaches for improving short-term signal reliability and compensating long-term drift are reviewed. In prediction, methods ranging from continuous glucose monitoring (CGM)-based forecasting to multimodal sensor fusion and noninvasive sensing are summarized, including both continuous glucose estimation and event-oriented detection of hypo- and hyperglycemia. The integration of sensing, prediction, and insulin delivery in wearable closed-loop artificial pancreas is also discussed. Finally, the remaining challenges and future directions are discussed, highlighting the potential of AI-enhanced wearable glucose sensors to support more reliable and integrated diabetes management.

articles.title: The efficacy of interventions to prevent type 2 diabetes among women with recent gestational diabetes mellitus-First update of a living systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.journal: Diabetic medicine : a journal of the British Diabetic Association
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The increased risk of developing type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) in the decade following childbirth among women with gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) warrants early intervention. A prespecified update of a systematic review and meta-analyses published in 2024 was performed, examining the efficacy of interventions to prevent T2DM among women within 5 years of a GDM-affected pregnancy.

METHODS: An updated search on PubMed, EMBASE and Web of Science (PROSPERO: CRD4202127989) was conducted on 14 November 2024. The primary outcome was T2DM diagnosis or measures of dysglycaemia with at least 12 months follow-up in women within 5 years of a GDM-complicated pregnancy. A Bayesian approach was adopted with results reported as effect sizes with 95% credible intervals (95% Crl), and posterior probabilities of intervention effectiveness.

RESULTS: Nine new publications were identified in this updated search, resulting in a total of 26 publications from 25 studies (n = 7379) included. Of those, four studies involved a pharmacological intervention and 21 evaluated lifestyle interventions. There was a 15% (95% CrI: 0.69-1.04) and 32% (95% CrI: 0.40-1.07) reduction in risk and hazard ratio for T2DM, respectively, with high posterior probabilities (95.0% and 96.0%, respectively). Reductions were observed for other secondary metabolic outcomes (fasting plasma glucose, body mass index, HOMA-IR and total cholesterol).

CONCLUSION: Compared to the original review, this update indicates greater certainty of the efficacy of preventive interventions for T2DM in women delivered during the first 5 years after a GDM-affected pregnancy. Evidence on the efficacy and safety of pharmacotherapy interventions is still limited.

articles.title: Dual-Pathogen Defense: Engineering an ExPEC Ghost to Display Protective Epitopes of Streptococcus suis.
articles.abstract: Streptococcus suis and extraintestinal pathogenic Escherichia coli (ExPEC) cause severe swine infections and major economic losses worldwide. Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) and polymicrobial interactions complicate disease control. Existing vaccine strategies are insufficient to provide broad cross-serotype protection against S. suis strains while simultaneously combating ExPEC infections. We developed a bivalent vaccine platform that integrates bacterial ghost (BG) technology with surface antigen display. By utilizing the porcine ExPEC strain PU-1 as a carrier, which could cause acute sepsis in mouse infection model. Using an Lpp'-OmpA surface display system, we constructed recombinant BGs derived from E. coli that express a multi-epitope antigen against S. suis (MEAS 1), while retaining native E. coli antigenic components as the immunogen against ExPEC. Administration of this vaccine induced robust cellular and humoral immune responses specific to both S. suis and E. coli. The vaccine demonstrated dual protection: 70%-90% survival against S. suis (serotypes 2/9) and 70% against ExPEC challenge in mouse model. Porcine trials demonstrated a significant reduction in bacteremia and provided effective protection against pathogenic challenges. This platform offers a potential solution for preventing infections caused by S. suis and ExPEC.

articles.title: Venlafaxine modulates white matter integrity in dorsal and ventral language pathways after subcortical stroke: a longitudinal TBSS study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Subcortical aphasia results from disrupted cortico-subcortical language networks after left-hemispheric infarction. Venlafaxine, an SNRI, may accelerate language recovery, but its effects on white matter plasticity remain unclear. We used diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) and tract-based spatial statistics (TBSS) to assess early venlafaxine effects on dorsal and ventral language pathways in subacute stroke.

METHODS: Thirty-two patients with first-ever left subcortical infarction and mild-to-moderate aphasia were randomized to venlafaxine (n=16; 75 mg/day, day 7-week 4) or control (n=16). DTI was acquired at 30±7 and 90±7 days post-stroke. TBSS compared fractional anisotropy (FA) in language-related tracts using permutation testing with TFCE (corrected p<0.05).    .

RESULTS: At Visit 2, venlafaxine recipients had higher FA in right superior longitudinal fasciculus/arcuate fasciculus (SLF/AF), bilateral inferior fronto-occipital fasciculi (IFOF), and left inferior longitudinal fasciculus (ILF), but lower FA in left SLF and uncinate fasciculus (UF). At Visit 3, FA increases extended to SLF/AF and UF, yielding bilateral dorsal and ventral enhancement; only right ILF FA decreased. FA changes positively correlated with aphasia quotient, spontaneous language fluency, and picture-naming improvements.  .

CONCLUSION: Early venlafaxine induces biphasic white matter remodeling: initial contralesional and bilateral ventral enhancement, followed by bilateral integration, suggesting optimized language network reorganization.

articles.title: Pediatric Inpatient Continuous Glucose Monitoring: Development and Implementation of a Hospital Policy for Accuracy-Validated Insulin Dosing.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: We assessed the safety, clinical accuracy, glycemic outcomes, user outcomes, and implementation of a pediatric hospital-wide continuous glucose monitor (CGM) policy.

RESEARCH DESIGN AND METHODS: We used the Model for Improvement to develop a pediatric hospital policy supporting CGM-based insulin dosing with accuracy validation using capillary finger-stick blood glucose (FSBG) and then retrospectively evaluated the program's clinical effectiveness and implementation outcomes with the Simplified Implementation Logic Model to connect contextual determinants, support strategies, and outcomes.

RESULTS: From September 2024 to October 2025, 60 people with diabetes used the CGM policy in 93 hospital encounters, including 46.7% (28/60) people with type 1 diabetes and 38.7% (36/93) encounters with automated insulin delivery use. The most used CGMs were Dexcom G7 (49.5%) and Abbott Libre 3 or 3 Plus (31.2%). Accuracy validation using the %20/20 criteria was successful in 81.5% of attempts, and the mean absolute relative difference was 12.6%, with 1207 paired CGM and reference FSBG values. Nurses responded appropriately after 97.8% (218/223) of failed CGM validation attempts. CGM time in range (70-180 mg/dL) was 54.8%, and time in level 2 hypoglycemia (<54 mg/dL) was 0.8% for the 58 out of 93 encounters with complete CGM data downloads. Nurses preferred using CGM with policy support instead of FSBG for insulin dosing (adjusted P = 0.046). Factors contributing to nursing preference included ease of use, system integration, and the ability to learn the system quickly.

CONCLUSIONS: We translated an inpatient CGM policy from an adult to pediatric hospital setting, supporting high levels of protocol adherence, clinical accuracy, safety, and improved experiences for clinicians. Program evaluation informs connections between contextual determinants, support strategies, and outcomes of implementing a hospital CGM program. These data offer a roadmap for implementing pediatric hospital CGM at other centers.

articles.title: Micromitophagy in plant spermatogenesis.
articles.abstract: Mitochondria of embryos in most plants and animals are inherited from the egg cell rather than the sperm cell, a phenomenon known as mitochondrial maternal inheritance. Nevertheless, how plants regulate paternal mitochondrial elimination (PME) has long remained a mystery. We discovered micromitophagy in higher plants and revealed that micromitophagy could serve as a specific mechanism underlying PME, which is triggered by fate determination of male germline (MG) cells. This process underpins maternal mitochondrial inheritance and normal early embryogenesis. Mechanistically, we demonstrate that the vacuole-localized ATG5 (autophagy-related protein 5) undergoes neofunctionalization and interacts with the mitochondrion-localized HSP90.2 (heat shock protein 90.2) to mediate paternal micromitophagy. Collectively, through interdisciplinary research on spermatogenesis, micromitophagy and mitochondrial inheritance, our work fills a long-standing gap in plant PME, and offers new insights into the functional divergence of autophagy-related genes and the adaptive evolution of autophagy.Abbreviations: PME, paternal mitochondrial elimination; 3-MA, 3-Methyladenine; ATG5, autophagy-related protein 5; HSP90.2, heat shock protein 90.2; MG, male germline; TEM, transmission electron microscopy; MVB, Multivesicular body.

articles.title: Acute Onset Orolingual Choreoathetosis and Auditory Hallucinations in a Healthy Young Adult Following High Melatonin Dose.
articles.abstract: Melatonin is considered a safe OTC sleep aid with rarely reported adverse effects despite limited data. We present a case of acute orolingual choreoathetosis and auditory hallucinations following 132 mg ingestion of melatonin in an otherwise healthy, 22-year-old active-duty male in IBOLC training. The patient developed abrupt, predominantly orolingual choreoathetosis and mild auditory hallucinations, 1 hour after waking. Three days earlier, he began taking 24 mg of melatonin nightly for insomnia and ingested 132 mg the night before presentation. He denied alcohol, illicit drug, or other medication use. On ED arrival, he was hemodynamically stable with continuous orolingual choreoathetosis. Initial labs demonstrated mild acute kidney injury and transaminitis. Head CT was unremarkable. MRI head showed a nonspecific left frontal white matter hyperintensity. Lumbar puncture revealed normal protein and WBC, negative culture, and negative oligoclonal bands, though CSF processing difficulties prevented autoimmune panel completion. Neurologic symptoms resolved by the next morning without recurrence, and a subsequent EEG was unremarkable. This case documents a temporal association between high-dose melatonin exposure and acute neurologic symptoms but does not establish melatonin as the cause. The clinical presentation also occurred in the setting of substantial confounders, including sleep deprivation and heat exposure. This observation supports further investigation of uncommon neurologic presentations occurring after high-dose melatonin intake.

articles.title: The Microbiome-Gut-Lung axis in Respiratory Diseases: From Biological Mechanisms to Clinical Translation.
articles.abstract: Respiratory diseases exhibit substantial heterogeneity in clinical phenotypes and underlying pathobiology that cannot be fully captured by conventional lung-centred frameworks. Accumulating evidence implicates a role for the microbiome-gut-lung axis in respiratory disease pathogenesis. Within this bidirectional axis, gut-derived microbial metabolites and structural components can modulate pulmonary immunity, whereas respiratory infection and exposures can reciprocally influence the gut microbiota. Dysregulation of the microbiome-gut-lung axis may influence respiratory disease susceptibility, progression, and clinical presentation. In this Review, we outline core mechanisms of gut-lung crosstalk, including metabolite-driven immunomodulation, pattern recognition receptor signalling and reciprocal immune-ecological remodelling. We synthesize phenotype-specific evidence linking the axis to major chronic inflammatory airway diseases (asthma, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, cystic fibrosis and bronchiectasis) and acute respiratory disorders (pneumonia and sepsis-associated acute respiratory distress syndrome), emphasizing mechanistic and clinical evidence. We discuss the translational promise of gut-lung signatures as biomarkers and treatable traits and review current therapies with microbiome effects and emerging microbiome-targeted interventions. Finally, we address key challenges and propose future research priorities to advance clinical management leveraging the gut-lung axis.

articles.title: The Era of Precision Medicine: Exacerbation Phenotyping to Determine the Role of Inhaled Corticosteroids in COPD?
Glucose control and clinical outcomes in surgical patients: A narrative review.
articles.journal: Nutrition in clinical practice : official publication of the American Society for Parenteral and Enteral Nutrition
articles.abstract: Perioperative hyperglycemia occurs in up to 40% of noncardiac and 80% of cardiac surgery patients, frequently independent of a diabetes diagnosis; it is driven by the neuroendocrine stress response, inflammatory cytokine release, and postoperative insulin resistance. Elevated glucose promotes protein glycosylation, which impairs wound healing and immune function, and it has been consistently associated with surgical site infection, anastomotic leak, prolonged length of stay, and increased mortality across surgical subspecialties. This narrative review examines biochemical aspects of glycogen metabolism and stress-induced insulin resistance, synthesizes evidence linking hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c) thresholds to surgical outcomes, and summarizes contemporary guidelines from the American Diabetes Association, Endocrine Society, European Society of Cardiology, Society of Critical Care Medicine, and Surviving Sepsis Campaign. Current consensus favors moderate, protocolized glucose targets (generally 100-180 mg/dL) while avoiding iatrogenic hypoglycemia. Preoperative optimization toward an HbA1c near 7%, judicious carbohydrate loading, and avoidance of glycemic extremes offer meaningful, modifiable strategies to improve outcomes in surgical and critically ill surgical patients.

articles.title: Etiology, interventions, and predictors of mortality in a tertiary malnutrition clinic: A retrospective cohort study.
articles.journal: Nutrition in clinical practice : official publication of the American Society for Parenteral and Enteral Nutrition
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Malnutrition worsens outcomes in chronic diseases, and delayed detection increases morbidity and mortality. This study described the characteristics of malnutrition in a tertiary referral clinic, summarized nutrition interventions, and identified predictors of mortality.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 431 adults referred to a tertiary malnutrition clinic between 2017 and 2023. Global Leadership Initiative on Malnutrition (GLIM) criteria were applied retrospectively to routinely documented clinical data to classify malnutrition severity. Logistic regression identified factors associated with severe malnutrition, and Cox proportional hazards models evaluated predictors of mortality.

RESULTS: Among 431 patients, 66.8% had severe malnutrition by GLIM criteria. Mean body mass index (BMI) was 20.9 ± 5.9 kg/m2, with weight loss of 19.0 ± 11.9% from usual weight. Leading etiologies were reduced oral intake (77.7%) and malabsorption (45.2%), including short bowel syndrome. After assessment, 37.6% received dietary counseling, 29.9% were recommended oral supplements, 13.9% initiated enteral feeding, and 18.6% received PN (11.6% newly initiated). Median clinical follow-up was 19 months; mortality ascertainment documented 105 deaths (24.4%). Low hemoglobin was associated with severe malnutrition (adjusted odds ratio, 2.49; 95% CI, 1.56-3.97). In the Cox model stratified by sex, higher Charlson Comorbidity Index (CCI) score (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR] per point, 1.20; 95% CI, 1.12-1.27), severe GLIM malnutrition (aHR, 1.76; 95% CI, 1.09-2.86), and low hemoglobin (aHR, 3.02; 95% CI, 1.99-4.56) were associated with mortality.

CONCLUSION: Severe malnutrition was common in this tertiary referral population. Greater comorbidity burden, severe GLIM malnutrition, and low hemoglobin were associated with higher mortality, supporting risk stratification and close clinical monitoring.

articles.title: Association Between Baseline Cognitive Impairment and Atrial Fibrillation Recurrence After Catheter Ablation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cognitive impairment is common among patients with atrial fibrillation (AF), yet its prognostic significance in the context of catheter ablation remains unclear.

AIMS: We aimed to investigate whether baseline cognitive impairment, assessed by the Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA), was associated with post-ablation AF recurrence.

METHODS: Based on the China-AF Registry, we identified 2692 patients with nonvalvular AF who underwent index catheter ablation and had baseline MoCA assessments from 2022 to 2024. Patients were stratified into mild cognitive impairment (MCI, MoCA ≤ 26) and normal cognition (MoCA > 26) groups. The primary outcome was AF recurrence beyond the blanking period. The secondary outcome was a composite of all-cause death, ischemic stroke, and major bleeding. To adjust for confounding factors, we applied inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) methodology. Weighted Cox proportional hazards models were used to estimate adjusted hazard ratios (aHRs).

RESULTS: After IPTW adjustment, all baseline covariates were well balanced (all standardized mean differences < 0.03). Over a median follow-up of 218 days (IQR, 192-376), the MCI group had a significantly higher risk of AF recurrence (aHR 1.48; 95% CI, 1.27-1.73; p  <  0.001). The composite secondary endpoint did not demonstrate a statistically significant between-group difference (aHR, 1.05; 95% CI, 0.25-4.52; p = 0.945). The association between baseline MCI and AF recurrence was consistent across all prespecified subgroups (all p for interaction > 0.05).

CONCLUSION: In this large prospective registry study, an independent association was observed between baseline cognitive impairment and an elevated risk of post-ablation AF recurrence. Cognitive assessment may be useful for risk stratification but requires external validation.

CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: Clinicaltrials.gov Identifier: NCT06987825.

articles.title: Timing of Catheter Ablation After Heart Failure Diagnosis for Atrial Fibrillation: A Propensity-Score-Matched Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Catheter ablation improves outcomes in patients with atrial fibrillation (AF) and heart failure (HF). However, most of the evidence on the importance of ablation timing has been anchored to AF rather than HF onset, leaving the optimal interval between HF diagnosis and ablation incompletely defined.

OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the association between the timing of catheter ablation following the first diagnosis of HF and subsequent clinical outcomes in patients with established AF.

METHODS: We performed a retrospective propensity-score-matched cohort study using the TriNetX Research Network. Adults (≥18 years) with AF who subsequently developed HF and underwent catheter ablation were included. The primary analysis compared ablation from day 1 through 3 months after HF diagnosis with ablation at least 91 days after HF diagnosis. Propensity-score matching yielded 2,570 patients in each group. Outcomes were assessed for 2 years after ablation and included all-cause mortality, electrical cardioversion, emergency department or inpatient encounters, and HF exacerbation. A 1-year timing threshold and analyses stratified by recorded left ventricular ejection fraction were examined as sensitivity analyses.

RESULTS: Mean follow-up was 549.3±253.2 days after early ablation and 534.1±255.3 days after later ablation. Mortality was similar between groups (11.0% vs 10.0%; hazard ratio [HR] 1.078, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.910-1.276; p = 0.384), as were emergency department or inpatient encounters (66.2% vs 65.6%; HR 1.006, 95% CI 0.940-1.076; p = 0.865). Early ablation was associated with fewer cardioversions (15.0% vs 18.6%; HR 0.788, 95% CI 0.689-0.901; p < 0.001) and fewer HF exacerbation events (39.5% vs 46.0%; HR 0.824, 95% CI 0.758-0.896; p < 0.001). The 1-year timing analysis showed a similar pattern for cardioversion and the HF exacerbation.

CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with AF and HF who ultimately underwent ablation, ablation within 3 months of HF diagnosis was associated with fewer subsequent cardioversions and HF exacerbations than ablation performed from day 91 onward. However, there was no significant difference in mortality between the two cohorts. These findings identify the first months after HF diagnosis as a clinically relevant period for reassessing rhythm-control strategy and warrant prospective evaluation of ablation timing after HF recognition.

articles.title: Early Invasive Fungal Infections in Liver Transplant Recipients Receiving Risk-Stratified Echinocandin Prophylaxis: A Descriptive Single-Center Cohort Study.
articles.journal: Transplant infectious disease : an official journal of the Transplantation Society
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Invasive fungal infection (IFI) remains a cause of morbidity and mortality after liver transplantation; guidelines recommend targeted antifungal prophylaxis in recipients with specific risk factors.

METHODS: We retrospectively studied adult liver transplant recipients (LTR) at a single center, 2017-2023. High-risk recipients received a planned 14-day course of echinocandin prophylaxis, caspofungin in 97.6%. The primary endpoint was IFI within 30 days of transplantation, a window spanning the planned prophylaxis and the 2 weeks after it. Secondary endpoints were fungal etiology and factors associated with IFI. We also examined the temporal distribution of early aspergillosis across the whole institutional registry to 2025.

RESULTS: Of 286 recipients, 85 (29.72%) were high risk. IFI was more frequent in high-risk than non-high-risk LTR (8/85, 9.41% vs. 4/201, 1.99%; p = 0.0077); most were breakthrough (7/8) mold infections. In exploratory analyses, IFI was associated with high-risk status (unadjusted odds ratio: 5.12, 95% CI: 1.50-17.49), MELD > 30 (4.67, 1.25-17.41) and diabetes (4.64, 1.37-15.79); with 12 events, these estimates are imprecise, and no multivariable model was fitted. Among 452 transplants performed in 2017-2025, seven developed early aspergillosis across four calendar years, with no significant variation in annual incidence (p = 0.146), never more than two cases in any 90-day window (Monte Carlo p = 0.82) and none among the 117 transplants of the following 28 months.

CONCLUSION: Early IFI under risk-stratified echinocandin prophylaxis concentrated in the sickest recipients and was dominated by mold disease. No clear temporal pattern suggestive of a sustained common-source outbreak was identified, although environmental transmission cannot be excluded.

articles.title: Electronic Intensive Care Unit Diaries: A Scoping Review of Applications, Implementation, and Evaluation.
articles.abstract:
AIM(S): To map evidence on the applications, implementation, and evaluation of electronic intensive care unit diaries in critical care.

DESIGN: Scoping review.

METHODS: Joanna Briggs Institute methodology guided eligibility, independent screening and data extraction, and descriptive and frameworkguided narrative synthesis. Methodological quality was not appraised because the review aimed to map evidence.

DATA SOURCES: Twelve databases and two registries were searched from inception to 17 September 2026.

RESULTS: Fifteen sources of evidence published between 2012 and 2026 represented eight distinct programmes; sources were from the Netherlands, China, the United States, Italy and the United Kingdom. Five broad platform or delivery modes were identified: web-based platforms, mobile or tablet applications, an online document platform, an electronic clinical record-integrated diary module and digital scrapbooking. Framework-guided synthesis identified multilevel implementation determinants, while reported strategies varied by implementation stage. Evaluations covered platform- and user-related, implementation and patient- and family-related outcomes, but evidence on sustained implementation and benefits was limited.

CONCLUSION: Electronic intensive care unit diaries are implemented through diverse digital platforms and participation models, but implementation and evaluation remain heterogeneous, and evidence on sustained use and benefits is limited.

IMPLICATIONS FOR THE PROFESSION AND/OR PATIENT CARE: Nurses and organisations should clarify writing roles and content boundaries, integrate diary work into workflows, provide training and support, protect privacy and monitor sustained use.

IMPACT: The review identifies nursing-relevant requirements for workflow integration, role clarity, training, organisational support and privacy. Findings can inform nurses, nurse leaders, critical care teams and healthcare organisations implementing digital diary programmes.

REPORTING METHOD: Reporting followed the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses Extension for Scoping Reviews.

articles.title: A Novel Indicator of Cytomegalovirus Infection After Allogeneic Hematopoietic Cell Transplantation: Current CMV Reactivation.
articles.journal: Transplant infectious disease : an official journal of the Transplantation Society
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cytomegalovirus reactivation (CMVR) after allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation (allo-HCT) is a reversible event, and conventional indicators such as the simple cumulative incidence cannot reflect transitional CMVR states. We propose a novel indicator, current CMVR (cCMVR), which visualizes both the occurrence and remission of CMVR over time.

METHODS: To evaluate the utility of cCMVR, we analyzed 389 CMV seropositive patients who had received their first allo-HCT. cCMVR was defined as the probability of the state where anti-CMV drugs were administered for CMVR or CMV disease without relapse or death at any time.

RESULTS: We compared two groups with or without letermovir prophylaxis (LTV and no-LTV groups). The 1-, 2-, 3-, and 6-month cCMVR values were 0.0%, 0.0%, 2.9%, and 2.9% in the LTV group, and 7.1%, 31.9%, 11.0%, and 0.8% in the no-LTV group. In the LTV group, cCMVR never exceeded 10%, while in the no-LTV group, cCMVR peaked at approximately 2 months after allo-HCT, and fewer than 5% of patients developed CMVR after 4 months post-HCT. Next, in the no-LTV group, we assessed cCMVR stratified according to the presence of risk factors for the simple cumulative incidence of CMVR, and this revealed that patients grafted from HLA-mismatched related donors and those who received alemtuzumab for GVHD prophylaxis appeared to experience repeated episodes of CMVR, whereas the early difference in cCMVR according to pretransplant CMV-IgG titer diminished over time.

CONCLUSION: cCMVR could be a valuable indicator for visualizing recurrent CMV infection and illustrating differences in the time course of CMVR.

articles.title: Early experience of a dedicated heart-brain integrated ward at Peking Union Medical College Hospital: a retrospective descriptive study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Heart-brain comorbidities present unique diagnostic and therapeutic challenges because neurological and cardiac conditions often share pathophysiological mechanisms yet create conflicting treatment demands. Multidisciplinary wards integrating neurosurgery, cardiac surgery, cardiology, and neurology have been proposed, but real-world experience remains limited. We report the initial experience of a dedicated heart-brain integrated ward at a Chinese tertiary referral center.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective descriptive study of all consecutive patients admitted to the Heart-Brain Integrated Ward at Peking Union Medical College Hospital between July 1 and August 21, 2026. Clinical data were entered prospectively into the electronic medical record during routine care and analyzed retrospectively. Variables included demographics, neurological and cardiac diagnoses, a six-category comorbidity classification, MDT decisions, treatment strategies, and discharge outcomes. Treatment categories were predefined as: (i) diagnostic procedures, (ii) therapeutic single-system interventions, (iii) staged dual-system treatment within the same admission, and (iv) synchronous dual-system treatment in a single session.

RESULTS: Fifty-six patients (42 males, 75.0%; mean age 62.4 ± 12.2 years, range 19-80) were enrolled. The most common category was I.1 (shared atherosclerotic vascular disease; 29/56, 51.8%), predominantly ischemic cerebrovascular disease with coronary artery disease (18/56, 32.1%). Category IV (psychocardiological disorders) accounted for 12 patients (21.4%), and Category V (therapeutically interactive) for 3 (5.4%). All patients underwent at least one MDT discussion (100%), and 55 (98.2%) required a second. Of 56 patients, 41 (73.2%) underwent surgical or endovascular intervention and 15 (26.8%) received medical management or remained under evaluation. Among treated patients, 4 (7.1%) received synchronous dual-system procedures, 13 (23.2%) completed staged procedures within the same admission, and 24 (42.9%) underwent single-system intervention. Fourteen patients (25.0%) required intervention for both organ systems. No in-hospital mortality or major procedure-related complications were observed among 38 discharged patients (67.9%); 18 patients (32.1%) remained hospitalized at data cutoff.

CONCLUSIONS: Establishing a dedicated heart-brain integrated ward at a tertiary referral center appears operationally feasible and enables structured MDT-based care for complex neuro-cardiac patients. The early disease spectrum is dominated by atherosclerotic pan-vascular disease. Synchronous dual-system procedures were performed in a small selected subset without observed major early events among discharged patients, but this cannot establish safety or generalizability. Larger prospective studies with controlled comparisons and longer follow-up are needed.

articles.title: Robotic-assisted versus conventional coronary artery bypass grafting: a systematic review, meta-analysis, and trial sequential analysis of 39,918 patients.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Robotic-assisted coronary artery bypass grafting (RA-CABG) is an evolving minimally invasive alternative to conventional CABG (C-CABG), but comparative evidence remains fragmented. We conducted a comprehensive systematic review, meta-analysis, and trial sequential analysis to compare outcomes between RA-CABG and C-CABG.

METHODS: Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, we searched PubMed, Embase, Cochrane CENTRAL, and Web of Science through January 2026. Studies comparing RA-CABG to C-CABG reporting at least one outcome of interest were eligible. Random-effects meta-analyses using DerSimonian-Laird estimators were performed. Risk of bias was assessed using ROBINS-I. Trial sequential analysis evaluated the conclusiveness of cumulative evidence.

RESULTS: Nine studies comprising 39,918 patients (13,638 RA-CABG; 26,280 C-CABG) were included. All included studies were observational in design, and long-term outcome data were sparse. RA-CABG was associated with significantly lower mortality (OR 0.55, 95% CI 0.43-0.69; P < 0.001; I²=0%), atrial fibrillation (OR 0.53; P < 0.001), respiratory failure (OR 0.31; P < 0.001), blood transfusion (OR 0.28; P < 0.001), hospital length of stay (MD - 1.95 days; P < 0.001), and ICU stay (MD - 22.7 h; P < 0.001). Stroke showed a non-significant trend favoring RA-CABG (OR 0.76; P = 0.071). Trial sequential analysis confirmed conclusive evidence for mortality, atrial fibrillation, respiratory failure, and blood transfusion. Results were robust across sensitivity analyses.

CONCLUSIONS: In this meta-analysis of observational studies, RA-CABG was associated with significantly improved short-term outcomes compared to C-CABG across multiple endpoints, with conclusive statistical evidence for four of seven binary outcomes. However, all included studies were observational, and these associations should be interpreted with caution given potential residual confounding and case-selection bias. Multicenter randomized trials with long-term follow-up are needed to confirm these findings.

articles.title: Preoperative levels of biomarkers of coagulation to predict massive bleeding after surgical repair for acute type A aortic dissection: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute type A aortic dissection is a highly emergent condition with a high mortality rate. The condition poses an imminent risk of serious complications such as coagulopathy with massive bleeding. This increases the risk of mortality even after surgical repair. Procoagulant drugs are routinely administered but some patients still suffer postoperative massive bleeding that can be fatal. The study aimed to investigate whether massive bleeding after surgical treatment for type A aortic dissection can be predicted preoperatively through routine coagulation tests such as APTT, PT (INR), fibrinogen, D-dimer, and platelets.

METHODS: The study was a retrospective, single-center, cohort study performed at a tertiary cardiac surgery unit. A total of 474 patients who underwent surgery for type A aortic dissection at our department between January 2005 and May 2023 were included in the study. Of these, 87 patients had massive postoperative bleeding after surgery for type A aortic dissection and were compared to 387 patients who did not have massive postoperative bleeding. Uni- and multivariable analyses were performed using logistic regression. The multivariable model included predictors of massive bleeding. Bleeding-related routine lab variables were then forced into the model.

RESULTS: Patients with massive bleeding (18%) had higher preoperative activated partial thromboplastin time (APTT) (33 s vs 29 s, p<0.01), and creatinine (97 µmol/L vs 87 µmol/L, p<0.01), as well as lower preoperative platelet counts (172 × 109/L vs 187 × 109/L, p=0.03) compared to patients without massive bleeding. Patients with massive bleeding also had longer duration of cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) (221 min vs 170 min, p<0.01) and suffered more postoperative complications. Multivariable logistic regression identified preoperative APTT per mmol increment (OR 1.04 (95% CI 1.01-1.07, p=0.01), preoperative APTT > 34.5 s (OR 2.95 (95% CI 1.60-5.47), p<0.01), preoperative creatinine > 82.5 µmol/L (OR 2.16 (95% CI 1.15-4.06), p=0.02), hypertension (OR 1.83 (95% CI 1.01-3.32), p<0.05) and CPB time per 10 min increment (OR 1.09 (95% CI 1.05-1.13, p<0.01)) as independent predictors of massive bleeding.

CONCLUSION: Preoperative APTT exceeding 34.5 s was independently associated with massive bleeding after type A aortic dissection repair and may, pending prospective validation, help identify patients who could potentially benefit from earlier hemostatic intervention.

articles.title: Improvement in peripheral airway function after a 12-week exercise intervention in COPD.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Exercise is a cornerstone of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) management and improves quality of life, exercise capacity, exacerbation frequency and survival. However, the physiological mechanisms underlying these effects remain unclear. Small airway dysfunction and airway remodeling may not be adequately captured by spirometry, whereas impulse oscillometry (IOS) may be more sensitive to changes in respiratory mechanics. We hypothesized that an exercise intervention designed to engage the peripheral lung may promote adaptive, and potentially, reparative processes in COPD. The aim of the study was to evaluate changes in lung function after a 12-week exercise intervention, focusing on small airway-related measures assessed by IOS. Secondary aims were to assess changes in exercise capacity and patient-reported outcomes.

METHODS: In this prospective multicenter single-arm non-randomized intervention study, participants with COPD (n = 62) completed a 12-week supervised, individually tailored moderate-intensity aerobic- and muscle-strengthening exercise program (3 sessions/week). Lung function (spirometry, body plethysmography, diffusing capacity and IOS), exercise capacity (6-minut walk test, 1-minute sit-to-stand) and symptom burden (CAT, CCQ, mMRC) were assessed before and after the intervention.

RESULTS: Significant improvements were observed in IOS measures including R5 (median paired difference (Δ) = - 0.75 z-score, p = 0.001), R5-R20 (Δ=-0.18 z-score, p = 0.007), Fres (Δ=-0.33 Hz, p = 0.022) and AX (Δ=-0.05 kPa·s⁻¹, p = 0.042). No significant changes were observed in spirometry or lung volumes, except for a small increase in FVC (Δ = 0.12 z-score, p = 0.027). Exercise capacity improved (Δ6MWT = + 15 m, p = 0.002; Δ1STS = + 3 repetitions, p < 0.0001), while symptom burden decreased (ΔCAT = - 1.0, p = 0.014; ΔCCQ = - 0.1, p = 0.011).

CONCLUSIONS: IOS measures improved after the exercise intervention, suggesting physiological adaptations beyond skeletal muscle conditioning that resulted in improved airway mechanics and ventilation distribution in the peripheral lung, while other lung function measures remained largely unchanged.

CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov ID NCT06335992 (Registration date 2024-03-28).

articles.title: Changes in pediatric oncology nurses' knowledge and observed mucormycosis-prevention practices following an educational programme: a one-group pretest-posttest study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mucormycosis is a life-threatening fungal infection increasingly affecting immunocompromised individuals, including children receiving chemotherapy. Its rising prevalence and severe outcomes highlight the importance of prevention. Nurses play a pivotal role, requiring improved knowledge and strict adherence to infection control practices.

AIM: This study aimed to evaluate the changes in pediatric oncology nurses' knowledge and observed mucormycosis-prevention practices following an educational programme.

METHODS: A quasi-experimental design with pre- and posttest assessments were used. The study was conducted at the Children's Cancer Hospital Egypt (CCHE) 57,357 and included 81 nurses. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire to assess characteristics and knowledge, along with an observational checklist designed to evaluate nurses' practices. The educational intervention consisted of three sessions covering mucormycosis risk factors, pathophysiology, and infection control measures.

RESULTS: The mean knowledge score increased from 5.82 ± 0.91 to 12.1 ± 0.76 (p < 0.001), and the mean practice score increased from 3.86 ± 1.13 to 7.58 ± 1.02 (p < 0.001). A positive correlation was found between knowledge and practice scores in both preintervention (r = 0.348, p = 0.001) and postintervention (r = 0.382, p < 0.001). Knowledge and observed practice scores increased significantly following the educational sessions.

CONCLUSION: Structured educational sessions were associated with significant short-term improvements in nurses' knowledge and observed mucormycosis-prevention practices. As patient outcomes and mucormycosis incidence were not measured, these findings should not be interpreted as evidence of reduced infection rates. Continuous professional development and targeted training are important for strengthening infection prevention knowledge and practices among pediatric oncology nurses.

CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: Not applicable.

articles.title: Beyond BCLC and AFP: A Circulating IL-6/IL-8 Inflammatory Signature Refines Survival Prediction in Hepatocellular Carcinoma.
articles.abstract: Prognostic assessment in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) primarily relies on clinical staging integrating tumour burden, liver function, and performance status; circulating cytokines may capture complementary tumour-host biology. To assess whether cytokines measured at diagnosis were associated with overall survival (OS) and improved prognostic stratification beyond AFP and BCLC, we retrospectively analysed 656 consecutive adults with HCC (median age 67 [IQR 59-75] years; 516 men, 78.7%). Viral liver disease predominated (n = 432, 65.9%). BCLC stage was 0/A/B/C in 101 (15.4%)/301 (45.9%)/151 (23.0%)/103 (15.7%); BCLC D was excluded. Serum GM-CSF, IFN-γ, IL-2, IL-4, IL-6, IL-8, IL-10, and TNF-α were measured at diagnosis using Bio-Plex 200 bead-based multiplex immunoassay (Luminex xMAP technology). The primary endpoint was OS. Overall, IL-6 and IL-8 levels increased across BCLC stages and were the only cytokines significantly associated with OS (IL-6: HR = 1.12, p < 0.001; IL-8: HR = 1.14, p < 0.001). Using previously published cut-offs, IL-6 > 4.28 pg/mL (aHR = 2.01, p < 0.001) and IL-8 > 17.60 pg/mL (aHR = 1.35, p = 0.033) were significantly associated with OS independently from age, sex, AFP > 400 ng/mL, BCLC stage, and HCC treatment. The combination of IL-6/IL-8 was able to stratify patients into low-risk (neither cytokine elevated; n = 358), intermediate-risk (one elevated; n = 155), and high-risk (both elevated; n = 143) groups, with median OS of 53.0, 28.7, and 20.5 months, respectively (log-rank p < 0.001). The C-index was 0.619 for IL-6/IL-8, 0.588 for AFP, 0.674 for BCLC, and 0.717 for the combined BCLC + AFP + IL-6/IL-8 model, which significantly improved model fit over BCLC + AFP alone (p < 0.001). Time-dependent AUCs for the combined model were 0.787, 0.755, 0.763, and 0.768 at 12, 24, 36, and 60 months, respectively. In conclusion, circulating IL-6 and IL-8 measured at HCC diagnosis define a simple inflammatory prognostic model independently associated with OS. When combined with BCLC and AFP, the IL-6/IL-8 score improves baseline prognostic discrimination and shows acceptable internal calibration.

articles.title: Design and in silico evaluation of PV-GNProtecta: an mRNA multi-epitope vaccine candidate against Puumala virus using immunoinformatics and structural analysis.
articles.abstract: Puumala virus (PUUV), the principal causative agent of nephropathia epidemica (NE), poses a significant public health threat due to its zoonotic transmission, renal complications, and the lack of an approved vaccine. In this study, an immunoinformatics-driven mRNA multi-epitope vaccine, PV-GNProtecta, was designed using conserved regions of the viral glycoprotein (G) and nucleoprotein (N). Highly antigenic, non-allergenic, and non-toxic T-cell and B-cell epitopes were identified and assembled with appropriate adjuvants to enhance immunogenicity. Population coverage analysis suggested broad HLA responsiveness across diverse populations. The vaccine construct exhibited favorable physicochemical properties, including stability, solubility, and antigenicity. Structural validation predicted high model quality, with 95.5% of residues located in favored Ramachandran regions and an ERRAT score of 91.4. Molecular docking and MM-GBSA analyses predicted favorable computational interactions between PV-GNProtecta and TLR4, while a 100 ns molecular dynamics simulation provided computational insights into the dynamic behavior of the vaccine-TLR4 complex. Codon optimization suggested compatibility of the designed sequence with an Escherichia coli-based expression framework. Immune simulation predicted potential humoral and cellular immune response patterns, including changes in IgG, IFN-γ, and IL-2 levels. The designed mRNA sequence exhibited favorable predicted secondary structural characteristics; however, further experimental evaluation is required to assess translational efficiency and stability. Although this study is limited to computational analyses and requires experimental validation, the findings suggest that PV-GNProtecta may represent a potential candidate for further investigation against PUUV infection.

articles.title: A big problem for little people: the impact of proposed Medicaid reimbursement cuts and the fragility of pediatric rheumatology care.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: There is a significant shortage of pediatric rheumatologists in the United States with only about 420 practicing providers and more than 300,000 children with rheumatologic conditions. This shortage is compounded by regional maldistribution with large geographic areas lacking pediatric rheumatology providers and by the increasing prevalence of autoimmune diseases.

MAIN TEXT: Medicaid was established in 1965 to provide coverage for low-income families, children, senior citizens and people with disabilities. About 50% of children in the US are insured through Medicaid or The Children's Health Insurance Program (CHIP), programs that significantly increased access to health care for children. Pediatric subspecialists, including rheumatologists, see patients predominately covered through public insurance. However, the lower reimbursement rates have led to lower salaries for pediatric rheumatologists compared to peers with the same level of training. Medicaid cuts will potentially worsen this shortage by limiting reimbursement and recruitment of even fewer trainees.
