Docking and binding analyses demonstrated selective interaction between EMPA and JNK3 over JNK1/2. EMPA inhibited JNK3-dependent c-Jun/c-Fos signaling without altering pan-JNK phosphorylation, indicating selective disruption of JNK3-c-Jun coupling. In AC16 cells, EMPA or JNK3 inhibition reduced c-Jun phosphorylation and restored mitochondrial function. JNK3 overexpression impaired mitochondrial function. EMPA reversed these effects, whereas JNK3 knockdown improved mitochondrial function independently of EMPA treatment.

CONCLUSION: EMPA directly targets JNK3, selectively uncoupling it from c-Jun/c-Fos signaling and thus preserving mitochondrial function and limiting fibrosis in DCM. These findings identify JNK3 as a novel direct target of EMPA in the heart and provide a mechanistic basis to explain the cardioprotective effect of SGLT2 inhibitors.

articles.title: Fatigability after 6 Weeks of Concurrent Dryland and Sprint Swimming Training.
articles.abstract: This study examined whether the acute effects of dryland muscular endurance training on subsequent strength and swimming responses differed before (T1) and after (T2) 6 weeks of muscular endurance and sprint interval training. Sixteen male and female swimmers (16.3±3.2 y) were ranked according to their 100-m performance and divided into groups trained with muscular endurance and sprint interval training (n=8) and sprint interval training (n=8). At T1 and T2, both performed a 1-RM evaluation and completed muscular endurance and swimming and swimming conditions in counterbalanced order. At T1 and T2 between conditions %Δ of swimming performance, tethered force, hand grip, isometric shoulder strength, blood lactate, stroke rate, stroke length, stroke index, and arm-stroke efficiency were calculated: %Δ=([muscular endurance+swimming-swimming]/swimming)x100. The 1-RM and external load were increased in groups trained with muscular endurance and sprint interval training only at T2. No differences (p>0.05) between groups were found in swimming performance, tethered force, blood lactate, stroke rate, stroke length, stroke index, and arm-stroke efficiency at T1 and T2. Isometric shoulder strength in group trained with muscular endurance and sprint interval training decreased after swimming at T1 and increased at T2 (-8.1±15.8 vs. 0.68±12.68%), whereas the opposite occurred in group trained with sprint interval training (4.22±12.42 vs.-1.64±12.29%, interaction, p=0.02). Six weeks of concurrent muscular endurance and sprint interval training improved strength and maintained swimming performance despite increased external loading during the concurrent training session.

articles.title: Artificial intelligence-supported diabetic retinopathy screening in Tanzania: a randomised controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Non-attendance after referral from screening is one of the major challenges for diabetic retinopathy screening programmes in Africa. Artificial intelligence (AI) systems for the identification of diabetic retinopathy can provide point-of-screening results and therefore enable immediate counselling. We aimed to investigate whether AI-supported diabetic retinopathy screening, with a point-of-screening result and face-to-face counselling, increased the proportion of people with true referable diabetic retinopathy who attended the central ophthalmology referral clinic when compared with standard diabetic retinopathy screening with deferred human grading and telephone counselling.

METHODS: This two-arm, parallel-group, individually randomised controlled trial was conducted at non-communicable disease or diabetic clinics in 24 hospitals in the Kilimanjaro and Arusha regions of Tanzania. Eligible participants (aged ≥18 years) had diabetes and attended diabetic retinopathy screening. Participants were randomly assigned (1:1) to receive either AI-supported diabetic retinopathy screening with a point-of-screening result and face-to-face counselling (the AI-intervention group) or standard-of-care diabetic retinopathy screening with deferred human retinal image assessment and telephone counselling (the standard-of-care group). Participants had retinal photographs taken of both eyes. Images from the AI-intervention group were submitted to the AI software, and these participants were given their screening result (non-referable, referable, or ungradable) plus face-to-face counselling before leaving the photography room, with a referral to the central ophthalmology clinic if the AI output was referable or ungradable. Participants in the standard-of-care group received their screening result, along with appropriate counselling, by telephone a few weeks later. The primary outcome was attendance at the central ophthalmology clinic within 8 weeks of screening among participants classified by masked UK-certified graders as having true referable diabetic retinopathy. This trial was registered with the ISRCTN Registry, ISRCTN18317152, and is complete.

FINDINGS: Between March 8, 2023, and Aug 31, 2024, 2439 participants were assessed for eligibility and 2378 were enrolled, of whom 1192 were randomly assigned to the AI-intervention group and 1186 to the standard-of-care group. 904 participants had true referable diabetic retinopathy, comprising 437 in the AI-intervention group and 467 in the standard-of-care group. Of the participants in the AI-intervention group, 157 (35·9%) of 437 attended the central ophthalmology clinic within 8 weeks, compared with 85 (18·2%) of 467 in the standard-of-care group, an absolute difference of 17·7 percentage points (95% CI 12·0-23·4; odds ratio 2·52 [95% CI 1·86-3·42]; p<0·0001).

INTERPRETATION: AI-supported screening, with a point-of-screening result and face-to-face counselling, increased the proportion of people with true referable diabetic retinopathy that attended the central ophthalmology clinic after screening compared with the standard of care in Tanzania. Such AI-enabled screening pathways have the potential to improve diabetic retinopathy screening programmes in Africa.

FUNDING: British Council for the Prevention of Blindness, Christian Blind Mission, and the Sir Halley Stewart Trust.

articles.title: Efficacy, safety, and immunogenicity of a nine-valent vaccine (ExPEC9V) for the prevention of invasive Escherichia coli disease in older adults: a phase 3, randomised, placebo-controlled trial (E.mbrace).
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Invasive Escherichia coli disease (IED) caused by extraintestinal pathogenic Escherichia coli (ExPEC) can lead to bacteraemia and sepsis. ExPEC9V is a conjugate vaccine targeting nine E coli O-serotypes that account for most E coli bloodstream infections. We aimed to evaluate ExPEC9V for safety, immunogenicity, and prevention of IED caused by ExPEC9V O-serotypes in adults aged 60 years and older.

METHODS: In this randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 3 study conducted at 332 clinical sites in 20 countries (E.mbrace), we enrolled participants aged 60 years and older in stable health and with a history of urinary tract infection (UTI) within the previous 2 years. Participants were randomly assigned (in blocks of no set size with the use of interactive web response system, stratified by age and presence or absence of risk factors for complicated UTI) 1:1 to receive a single dose of intramuscular ExPEC9V or placebo. Participants, study-site personnel, and investigators remained masked to group allocation throughout the study. The primary endpoint was first IED in blood or sterile sites caused by ExPEC9V O-serotypes in the per-protocol efficacy analysis set (all randomly assigned, vaccinated participants without major protocol deviations); secondary endpoints included immunogenicity assessment in a subset of participants. Safety endpoints included solicited (safety subset), unsolicited (full analysis set), and serious (full analysis set) adverse events. A prespecified futility analysis conducted when at least 40% of the expected 53 IED events had occurred indicated lack of efficacy, leading to early study termination. We present final study results (data up to the date of the futility announcement), when 17 701 of the planned 19 800 participants had been vaccinated. This trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT04899336).

FINDINGS: Participants were enrolled between June 30, 2021, and Feb 13, 2025. Of 18 844 individuals assessed for eligibility, 17 701 were enrolled, randomly assigned, and vaccinated (8858 with ExPEC9V and 8843 with placebo). The per-protocol efficacy included 17 637 participants (8822 for ExPEC9V and 8815 for placebo). There were 24 IED cases (11 in vaccine and 13 in placebo groups) caused by ExPEC9V O-serotypes in blood or sterile sites, yielding a vaccine efficacy of 14·63% (95% CI -106·57 to 65·38), indicating no protective effect. ExPEC9V had an acceptable safety profile, with more frequent low-grade adverse events in the ExPEC9V versus placebo group, balanced serious adverse event distribution among both groups, and no vaccine-related deaths.

INTERPRETATION: In this large phase 3 trial of older adults, ExPEC9V did not demonstrate efficacy in preventing first IED caused by ExPEC9V O-serotypes, despite generating robust and sustained antibody responses. Development of the ExPEC9V vaccine has been discontinued.

FUNDING: Johnson & Johnson and Sanofi.

articles.title: Striatal astrocyte μ-crystallin (Crym) loss contributes to early-stage Huntington's disease pathophysiology.
articles.abstract: A striatal astrocyte subpopulation expressing μ-crystallin (gene: Crym) regulates perseverative behaviors, but its role in disease is unclear. We found that astrocytic Crym and μ-crystallin protein expression levels are reduced in human Huntington's disease (HD) tissue, cerebrospinal fluid, and HD mouse models. Selective astrocytic μ-crystallin restoration in a HD mouse model improved astrocyte and neuronal morphology, electrophysiology, gene expression, and early-stage compulsive and repetitive behaviors. Late-stage motor deficits remained mostly unchanged. Approximately 32% of the μ-crystallin rescued astrocytic genes overlapped with those dysregulated in human HD, indicating conserved molecular corrections. These results identify μ-crystallin-expressing astrocytes as modulators of HD pathophysiology and suggest that restoring μ-crystallin or targeting Crym-positive astrocytes could be beneficial in early disease stages.

articles.title: Cardiovascular effects of continued vs. discontinued anabolic-androgenic steroid use: a longitudinal follow-up study.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Anabolic-androgenic steroid (AAS) use is prevalent among men engaged in strength training and is associated with adverse structural and functional cardiac changes, but longitudinal data are lacking. This follow-up study examined myocardial effects of AAS with continued use and reversibility following discontinuation.

METHODS AND RESULTS: Participants of a previously published cohort (2017-19) of 101 AAS users and 71 non-using weightlifting controls (WLCs) were invited for a follow-up study and underwent interviews, hormonal profiling, and transthoracic echocardiography. Current AAS users at baseline were continued or discontinued users at follow-up, while former users at baseline were those with continued abstinence and those who relapsed.Among those re-enrolled, 70 were AAS users, of whom 35 continued, 15 discontinued, 14 maintained abstinence, and 6 relapsed, and 35 were WLCs. Continued AAS users had persistent indexed left ventricular mass (LVMI 119 ± 30 g/m2), reduced LV ejection fraction (LVEF 48 ± 10%), and worsened diastolic function. Continued AAS users receiving antihypertensive therapy showed improved LVEF compared with untreated users (Δ = 5 ± 8 vs. -4 ± 8%, P = 0.005). Discontinued AAS users showed reduction in LVMI (Δ = -21 g/m2, P = 0.01) and improved LVEF (Δ = 6%, P < 0.001). At follow-up, these changes were comparable with WLCs, which showed statistically but clinically insignificant differences.

CONCLUSION: Continued AAS use was associated with sustained LV hypertrophy, LV systolic dysfunction, and worsening diastolic function. Antihypertensive therapy among ongoing AAS users was associated with improved LV systolic function. Discontinuation of AAS use was associated with improvement in cardiac structure and function towards values observed in WLCs.

articles.title: Family Caregivers of People Living With Glioblastoma Report Low Palliative Care Utilization and Limited Discussions About Palliative Care With Members of the Healthcare Team: A Cross-Sectional Survey Study.
articles.journal: The American journal of hospice & palliative care
articles.abstract: BackgroundGlioblastoma is an aggressive, incurable, primary brain cancer associated with substantial symptom burden and reliance on family care partners/caregivers (CP/CG) throughout the illness trajectory. Palliative care can improve symptom management and quality of life for people with serious illness and their families. This study examined CP/CG reported palliative care utilization, understanding of palliative care, and the discussions about palliative care with members of the healthcare team.MethodsA cross-sectional survey was administered between January and February 2024 to adult CP/CG of adults living with glioblastoma recruited through online caregiver support groups. The 38-item survey collected demographic information and caregiver-reported experiences related to palliative care utilization, discussions about palliative care, and supportive care needs. Descriptive statistics and tests of association were performed.ResultsFamily CP/CG (n = 75) reported low involvement of palliative care (28%). A significant association was observed between caregiver-reported discussions about palliative care and utilization of palliative care services (χ2 = 34.31, P < .001). Fewer than 10% of CP/CG correctly identified all WHO-defined functions of palliative care. CP/CG also reported unmet supportive care needs, particularly related to physical and emotional support, symptom management, and treatment side effect management.ConclusionsFamily CP/CG of people living with glioblastoma reported low utilization of palliative care services, limited discussions about palliative care with members of the healthcare team, and persistent misconceptions regarding its role. These findings highlight opportunities to improve communication about palliative care and strengthen supportive care services for people living with glioblastoma and their caregivers.

articles.title: Immunoinformatics-based design and in silico evaluation of a multi-epitope vaccine candidate against Naegleria fowleri.
articles.abstract: Primary amoebic meningoencephalitis (PAM) is caused by Naegleria fowleri, a free-living amoeba. It is a fatal infection with more than 95% mortality rate. Even though several combinations of antimicrobial agents were used to treat the condition, the overall survival remains poor and no effective vaccine is currently available. In this study, an immunoinformatic approach was utilized for designing a multi-epitope vaccine against N. fowleri. The sequences of antigenic proteins were retrieved for epitope prediction. The computational prediction identified 400 CTL, 590 HTL, and 65 B-cell high-binding epitopes. After evaluating their antigenicity, allergenicity and toxicity, 5 CTL, 5 HTL and 3 B-cell epitopes were selected and assembled into a multi-epitope vaccine construct using linkers and a human β-defensin-3 adjuvant. The 3D structure of the vaccine was predicted using AlphaFold and refined with GalaxyRefine. Ramachandran plot analysis indicated that 96.5% of the residues of the refined vaccine are present in the most favored regions, indicating good stereochemical quality. The molecular docking analysis was performed using HADDOCK to evaluate the interaction between the vaccine and the Toll-like Receptors (TLRs), which predicted favorable binding affinities of -15.6 kcal/mol, -14.2 kcal/mol, and - 13.1 kcal/mol for TLR1 & 2, TLR3, and TLR4, respectively. The codon was optimized using JCat and cloned into the pET-28a(+) plasmid. The in silico immune simulation analysis predicted potential humoral and cellular immune responses to the vaccine construct. Overall, the proposed multi-epitope vaccine represents a promising computational candidate, however, further experimental validations have to be performed to confirm its efficacy against the pathogen.

articles.title: [Healthcare expenditure and in-hospital mortality in the Spanish National Health System (2013-2023)].
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To analyze the relationship between per capita healthcare expenditure and overall in-hospital mortality in the Spanish autonomous communities between 2013 and 2023.

METHOD: A longitudinal ecological study was conducted using official data from the Ministry of Health and regional healthcare expenditure statistics. Annual in-hospital mortality rates and per capita healthcare expenditure were calculated, and descriptive analyses, Pearson correlation, and multiple linear regression were applied. A significance level of p<0.05 was adopted.

RESULTS: The results showed a progressive increase in per capita healthcare expenditure between 2013 and 2019 and a significant increase during the pandemic (p<0.01). In-hospital mortality decreased until 2019 and increased markedly in 2020-2021 (p<0.01). A significant positive correlation was observed between per capita healthcare expenditure and in-hospital mortality (r=0.428 and p<0.001). However, in the year-adjusted regression model, expenditure ceased to be a significant predictor of mortality, showing that the bivariate association may be influenced by structural and demographic factors not included in the analysis.

CONCLUSIONS: Although per capita healthcare expenditure increased during the analyzed decade, no independent association between investment and mortality was identified. The observed positive correlation could reflect regional differences in population aging, healthcare complexity, and service structure, rather than a direct effect of expenditure.

articles.title: Pharmacological interventions for reducing the risk of cognitive decline and dementia after stroke/transient ischemic attack: A systematic review.
articles.journal: The journal of prevention of Alzheimer's disease
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Stroke is a leading cause of death and disability worldwide. Advances in stroke care have improved survival and recovery, but it remains unclear whether pharmacological treatments can prevent long-term consequences including cognitive decline and dementia. This systematic review examined whether pharmacological interventions reduce the risk of cognitive decline, mild cognitive impairment (MCI), or dementia in adults with a history of stroke or symptomatic transient ischemic attack (TIA).

METHODS: We searched Medline, EMBASE, PsychINFO, and Cochrane Central from inception to January 23, 2025, for systematic reviews and meta-analyses of randomized controlled trials (RCTs). Eligible studies included adults with prior stroke or symptomatic TIA receiving pharmacological interventions, blood pressure-lowering, antithrombotic, and lipid-lowering drugs, compared with placebo, no treatment, or usual care. Primary outcomes were incident dementia, MCI, and cognitive decline assessed at least three months post-event. Methodological quality was assessed with AMSTAR 2, and certainty of evidence using GRADE. The protocol was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251000825).

RESULTS: Of 1343 records screened, 8 systematic reviews met inclusion criteria. The most comprehensive systematic review, including all relevant RCTs, was selected for detailed data extraction. Certainty of evidence was mostly low, with a few exceptions of moderate to high certainty. Across drug classes and outcomes, pharmacological interventions generally showed no meaningful reductions in dementia, MCI, and cognitive decline over a mean follow-up of 2.0-4.9 years.

CONCLUSIONS: Current evidence does not support pharmacological interventions after a cerebrovascular event for reducing risk of cognitive decline, MCI, or dementia. Further high-quality studies with longer follow-ups are needed.

articles.title: Mitral Valve Repair in Patients With Class I Obesity: A Propensity-Matched Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Obesity may increase the technical complexity of robotic mitral valve (MV) repair, but comparative outcomes with sternotomy remain poorly defined.

OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to compare perioperative and long-term outcomes of robotic vs sternotomy MV repair in patients with class I obesity.

METHODS: A total of 880 patients with class I obesity (body mass index 30-34.9 kg/m2) underwent MV repair at our clinic between 2008 and 2025. After excluding those with mitral stenosis, active endocarditis, prior sternotomy, or concomitant procedures, 429 patients remained. Propensity score matching (1:1) yielded 132 patients in each group who underwent either robotic or conventional sternotomy MV repair.

RESULTS: Median age was 59 years (IQR: 52-66), and 81% were male. Cardiopulmonary bypass and cross-clamp times were longer in the robotic group than in the sternotomy group (86 vs 65 minutes and 60 vs 48 minutes, respectively; P < 0.001). Robotic MV repair was associated with shorter hospitalization (3.5 vs 5 days; P < 0.001) and a lower postoperative transfusion rate (1.5% vs 10.6%; P = 0.002). There were no operative deaths in either group. No sternal wound infections occurred. Thirty-day readmission was numerically higher after robotic repair (12.8% vs 4.3%; P = 0.064). Ten-year survival was 92% (95% CI: 87% to 97%) with no significant difference between groups (P = 0.83).

CONCLUSIONS: In patients with class I obesity, the robotic approach in comparison to sternotomy was associated with lower transfusion rates, shorter hospitalization, and comparable operative mortality and long-term survival relative to sternotomy. Although 30-day readmission was numerically higher among robotic patients, most events were minor and managed without intervention.

articles.title: Toxic cascade from oxidative stress to metabolic imbalance in Manila clams exposed to polyethylene terephthalate microplastics.
articles.abstract: Polyethylene terephthalate (PET) is one of the most abundant plastic pollutants in marine environments. However, compared with other polymers, research on PET microplastics (MPs)-particularly their impact on benthic organisms in sediment environments-remains relatively scarce. In this study, we exposed Manila clams (Ruditapes philippinarum) to PET MPs in fragments and fibers of five sizes at concentrations of 0.8, 8, and 80 mg/kg dry weight (dw) of sediment for 21 days using a water-sediment exposure system. Mortality in Manila clams exposed to PET MPs remained unchanged, and each MP group accumulated in the digestive glands and gills. Chronic exposure to PET MPs increased reactive oxygen species production and SOD, IL-1β, and CASP8 levels in the gill and digestive gland tissues of clams. Integrated biomarker response analysis showed stronger correlations for fragments than for fibers, and for larger than smaller sizes, in both gill and digestive gland tissues. Furthermore, omics analysis confirmed a strong response in inflammation-related factors to fragment MPs, suggesting that PET MPs induce oxidative stress, inflammation, and cellular responses that lead to digestive and secretory dysfunction, which may cause morphological and metabolic changes in clams and ultimately adversely affect their health and survival. This study contributes to our understanding of the toxic mechanisms of PET MPs, focusing on their size and shape, and ultimately raises awareness of their harmful effects in the environment.

articles.title: Biological trajectories toward universal computation: Transposons and chaperone-assisted folding as models of molecular logic.
articles.abstract: The question of whether biological systems implement computation-like processes is central to synthetic biology and theoretical biophysics. This paper proposes a formal conceptual framework in which two well-characterized molecular mechanisms-transposable elements ("jumping genes") and chaperone-mediated protein folding-are modeled as computational systems. We argue that transposons, exemplified by the ONSEN retrotransposon in Arabidopsis thaliana, implement signal-responsive genome state transitions formally analogous to probabilistic finite-state machine computation, with capacity for computational expressiveness consistent with that of a linear-bounded automaton (LBA) under explicit assumptions of bounded memory, state-dependent branching and heritable epigenetic memory (a hypothesis, not a proof). Simultaneously, molecular chaperones such as heat shock protein 70 (Hsp70) and GroEL/GroES realize an analog computation paradigm, navigating protein energy landscapes through iterative, constraint-driven optimization. Together, these systems suggest that biological macromolecular networks may intrinsically embed logical operations capable of sophisticated information processing. We develop component-level mappings, present a comparative analysis, and outline falsifiable experimental predictions and synthetic biology applications that follow from this framework. These findings carry implications for bio-computing architectures, evolutionary genomics, and the theoretical foundations of life as an information-processing substrate.

articles.title: Single-molecule resolution of post-translational modification on GRK4 with cyclodextrin/SiNx hybrid nanopore.
articles.abstract: Post-translational modifications (PTMs) on G protein-coupled receptor kinase 4 (GRK4) are implicated in hypertension pathogenesis, their label-free analysis at the single-chemical-group level remains challenging. Here, we construct a γ-cyclodextrin/silicon nitride (γ-CD/SiNx) hybrid nanopore by controlled dielectric breakdown followed by electrophoretic insertion of a single γ-CD molecule into a size-matched SiNx pore, and use it to discriminate PTMs on GRK4-derived oligopeptides. By recording ionic current blockades (ΔI/Io) and dwell times in 1 M KCl at 200 mV, the angstrom-scale hydrophobic cavity of γ-CD provides high spatial resolution: the platform resolves peptides differing by few-residue substitutions and distinguishes palmitoylation, single/multiple phosphorylation, and acetylation on identical 15-residue sequences. Palmitoylated peptides show enhanced capture rates and longer dwell times (2.2 ± 0.1 ms) than unmodified controls (1.0 ± 0.1 ms); mono-phosphorylation reduces normalized current blockade amplitude (ΔI/Io = 0.51 ± 0.02) whereas tri-phosphorylation increases it (ΔI/Io = 0.65 ± 0.02); positional phosphorylation isomers and peptide mixtures are resolved by combined amplitude and dwell-time readout. This label-free single-molecule platform offers a proof-of-concept route toward PTM profiling; validation under physiological conditions and in biological matrices is required before diagnostic application.

articles.title: Improvised cardiac function of siddha formulation Sikkanjar elixir® through CAMK2 and VEGF mechanism-in experimentally induced cardiac hypertrophy model in rats.
articles.journal: Journal of Ayurveda and integrative medicine
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sikkanjar elixir® (SE) contains 29 herbs, honey and fermented rice water. It is a modified and fortified form of Sikkanjar Manappagu (Manappagu means syrup), a Siddha traditional medicine. SE has its reference to treat vascular block, high cholesterol, varicose vein, hypertension; improved cardiac efficiency and blood circulation. However, the validation of Siddha claim of SE has not been carried out in experimentally conditions.

OBJECTIVE: The present study designed to validate the scientific claim of SE and investigate the cardio-protective prospective of SE, in a rat model of cardiac hypertrophy (CH).

MATERIALS AND METHODS: CH was induced in Sprague-Dawley rats via ligation of the descending abdominal aorta. The cardio-protective effects of SE were evaluated through behavioral assessments, biochemical parameters, antioxidant profiling, liver and kidney function tests, ATP, troponin I levels measurement. The cardiac hypertrophy markers like CAMK2, VEGF, and SIRT3 expression were measured through qRTPCR.

RESULTS: HPTLC evaluation of SE denotes 1.221 mg RUE/g and 4.604 mg GAE/g, of total flavonoid and phenolics content respectively. CH induction led to elevated heart rate, troponin I, and liver/kidney function markers, along with decreased plasma glucose, cholesterol, tissue ATP, catalase, glutathione, and VEGF levels. SE treatment significantly reversed these changes, as evidenced by reduced heart rate, normalization of biochemical markers, and improved antioxidant status. Notably, SE treatment suppressed CAMK2 expression and upregulated VEGF, suggesting enhanced myocardial contractility. Histopathological analysis further supported these findings, showing reduced myocyte fibre thickness and septal volume.

CONCLUSION: SE reversed the CH induced pathology through restoration of cardiac pumping efficiency (ejection fraction) via CAMK2 and VEGF mechanism. Normalization of cardiac output might contribute to the recovery of kidney, metabolic functions and promotion of anti-oxidant effect. These observations can also be extrapolated in CCF or MI conditions in clinical situations.

articles.title: Online chiral derivatization coupled with CE-MS for baseline separation of 16 proteinogenic amino acid enantiomers.
articles.abstract: Amino acid (AA) enantiomers influence protein function through their distinct spatial structures, making their precise separation essential for elucidating physiological and pathological pathways. In this work, a novel method for the efficient separation of AA enantiomers based on on-line chiral derivatization with (S)-N-(4-nitrophenoxycarbonyl) phenylalanine methoxyethyl ester ((S)-NIFE) coupled with CE-MS has been developed. The method utilizes the ultrafast reaction kinetics of (S)-NIFE with AA enantiomers to facilitate their efficient separation. The online strategy eliminates time-consuming offline derivatization by permitting immediate injection upon simple mixing of derivatization reagent with AA enantiomers, enabling a streamlined analytical workflow. By optimizing experimental parameters, baseline separation of 16 chiral proteinogenic AA enantiomers has been achieved with resolutions ranging from 1.5 to 11.03. The relative standard deviations of migration time and peak area for intraday and interday measurements are less than 5%, and the limits of detection (LOD) and quantification (LOQ) are as low as 40 nM and 80 nM, respectively. Furthermore, the method was further applied to comparative analyses of AA enantiomers in serum samples from healthy controls and patients with non-alcoholic fatty liver disease and atrial fibrillation. The baseline separation of three AA enantiomers was consistently achieved. The LODs and LOQs for three ᴅ-AAs in complex matrix were as low as 180 nM and 600 nM. The intraday and interday precisions were both below 11%, and the average recoveries range from 87.60% to 95.51% with low standard deviations. All these results confirm the effectiveness of the approach in separating AA enantiomers in complex matrices.

articles.title: Assessing the feasibility of reusing oral nutritional supplements in a quaternary intensive care unit.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Healthcare generates substantial carbon emissions and waste, and sustainability initiatives increasingly aim to reduce environmental impact without compromising care. In our Intensive Care Unit (ICU), unused oral nutritional supplements (ONS) are routinely discarded, contributing to financial and carbon waste. Reuse may offer benefits but must be balanced against infection prevention requirements. This study assessed microbiological contamination of ONS to inform feasibility of a safe reuse program.

METHODS: In our ICU, three ONS products were sampled using standardised surface-swabbing. Twenty "ingoing" products entering patient rooms and twenty cleaned, unconsumed "outgoing" products leaving patient rooms were cultured for both total organisms and Enterobacterales. Values were calculated as colony forming units (CFU) per centimetre-squared (CFU/cm2) and compared with food-surface contamination thresholds. Group differences were analysed using non-parametric statistical tests.

RESULTS: Forty ONS items were sampled (20 ingoing, 20 outgoing). Outgoing products had significantly lower overall bacterial counts than ingoing products (median 0.27 CFU/cm2 versus 0.00 CFU/cm2; p < 0.001). Enterobacterales were uncommon at baseline - only detected on four (20%) products - and absent on all outgoing samples. There was no significant difference observed between the three different product types.

CONCLUSIONS: Cleaning unopened ONS after ICU room exposure resulted in significantly reduced bacterial burden, with no Enterobacterales detected, supporting the feasibility of safe reuse. These findings suggest that reusing unopened ONS could deliver meaningful financial and carbon savings while upholding infection prevention measures essential for patient safety.

articles.title: Child sexual abuse in Canada: Prevalence, perpetrators, and characteristics.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Detailed information about the epidemiology of child sexual abuse (CSA) in Canada is lacking.

OBJECTIVE: To estimate the prevalence of CSA; determine if CSA prevalence differs by gender and age group; and describe CSA characteristics, including perpetrators, age of onset, age of cessation, duration, and chronicity.

PARTICIPANTS AND SETTING: Adults aged 18-49 years provided retrospective accounts of CSA in a cross-sectional survey (Childhood Adversity and Resilience-Youth and Early Adulthood Research Study [CARe-YEARS]; N = 3767; May 2024).

METHODS: CSA included non-contact CSA (looking at or exposing private parts) and three types of contact CSA (touching private parts, attempted forced sex, and completed forced sex). Descriptive statistics were conducted. Gender and age-group differences in prevalence were tested with logistic regression.

RESULTS: The prevalence of CSA was 25.8% overall, including 21.0% any contact CSA and 14.7% non-contact CSA. Women and gender-diverse individuals disproportionately experienced CSA compared to men. The overall prevalence of CSA by perpetrator type included 9.1% friend/schoolmate; 8.4% boyfriend/girlfriend; 4.8% unknown adolescent; 4.3% known adult (non-family); 4.2% unknown adult; 3.6% cousin; 2.1% parent/stepparent/parent's boyfriend or girlfriend; 2.0% grandparent, uncle, or aunt; and 1.4% sibling. Between 22 and 33% of survivors did not recall additional characteristics of the abuse. Of those who reported, the mean age of onset was 11.0 years and one in four reported that CSA occurred six or more times. Age group trends (18 to 29 years and 30 to 49 years) indicated declines in some CSA subtypes.

CONCLUSIONS: Findings from the current study provide detailed evidence of survivors' CSA experiences, addressing important knowledge gaps to inform policy and CSA prevention.

articles.title: Chinese Patients' Attitudes Toward the WHO Surgical Safety Checklist.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Strategies to reduce adverse events have mainly focused on systems of care and professional behavior despite a growing interest in involving patients in safety initiatives. Only some studies were published in developing countries. This study sought to clarify the patients' views on the surgical safety checklist in China.

METHODS: We developed a research-based patient questionnaire and delivered it through a ubiquitous social media platform. The survey was sent to patients over 12 weeks from May to July 2020. Responses were accepted up to the end of July 2020. This survey was conducted at 5 Level 3 hospitals in 4 provinces (Beijing, Shandong, Liaoning, and Henan). Descriptive statistics (frequencies and percentages) were calculated to demonstrate the overall quality of checklist use. Multivariate linear regression was utilized to assess the predictive factors for respondents' views on the risk of an adverse event. Multivariate ordinal logistic regression, with respondents' characteristics as covariates, predicted attitude toward the WHO Surgical Safety Checklist. Adjusted odds ratios with 95% confidence intervals were calculated.

RESULTS: A total of 475 patients at 5 centers responded. Previous adverse medical events occurred more (26.7%) than generally reported. For surgical patients, the estimates of adverse-event risk in the hospital were almost entirely due to the perceived risks of surgery itself. Lower risk estimates were generated by patients who had experienced more surgery before (adjusted odds ratio = -0.429, 95% confidence interval: -0.752 to 0.107, P < .01). Compared with other studies, the proportion of patients with a positive perception of the checklist was lower. However, more than half (53.3%) thought the checklist would improve communication between staff. More patients than elsewhere were anxious about hearing repetitive confirmation before surgery. In keeping with more rigid role expectations in China, more patients preferred a doctor taking charge of the checklist (37.3%). Chinese patients had a more positive view of the patient's role in surgical safety improvement.

CONCLUSIONS: Less than half of Chinese patients hold positive views on implementing the surgical safety checklist despite a higher perception of the risk of adverse surgical events than elsewhere. Patients would like to become more actively involved in surgical safety improvement. We suggest greater patient involvement during the implementation of the WHO Surgical Checklist, fostering a more supportive and collaborative environment in the future.

articles.title: Acute Effects of Impella 5.5 on Biventricular Filling and Pressure-Volume Area in Patients With Heart Failure Associated Cardiogenic Shock.
articles.journal: ASAIO journal (American Society for Artificial Internal Organs : 1992)
articles.abstract: Use of Impella 5.5 in patients with decompensated heart failure-associated cardiogenic shock (ADHF-CS) is increasing as a bridge to advanced therapies. The effects of maximal trans-valvular unloading on biventricular filling and pressure-volume area (PVA) in ADHF-CS are poorly understood. Nine patients with medically refractory ADHF-CS underwent Impella 5.5 placement with simultaneous invasive arterial, venous, and biventricular pressure-volume loop analysis. Acutely after Impella 5.5 activation, cardiac output (3.4 ± 0.5 vs. 5.0 ± 0.7 L/min, p = 0.0011), diastolic (67.2 ± 8.0 vs. 80.7 ± 9.7 mm Hg, p = 0.0044) and mean arterial pressures (77.9 ± 7.1 vs. 86.9 ± 10.4 mm Hg, p = 0.029) increased, compared to baseline. Left ventricular end-diastolic pressure (24.1 ± 6.7 vs. 16.8 ± 5.4 mm Hg, p = 0.0027), volume (262.1 ± 103.9 vs. 231.5 ± 104.3 ml, p = 0.0036), and PVA (21,913 ± 7,055 vs. 18,357 ± 7,758 mmHg·ml, p = 0.013) decreased. Right ventricular end-diastolic (12.4 ± 4.6 vs. 9.1 ± 3.8 mm Hg, p = 3.8E-5) and end-systolic pressure (42.1 ± 11.9 vs. 34.4 ± 11.1 mm Hg, p = 0.030) and PVA (6,303 ± 3,851 vs. 4,437 ± 2,473 mm Hg·ml, p = 0.027) also decreased. These findings suggest that maximal left ventricular unloading can acutely reduce biventricular filling pressures and PVA in patients with ADHF-CS.

articles.title: Impact of Thoracotomy-Based Left Ventricular Assist Device Implantation on Right Ventricular Functional Preservation.
articles.journal: ASAIO journal (American Society for Artificial Internal Organs : 1992)
articles.abstract: Right ventricular (RV) dysfunction remains a critical determinant of outcomes following left ventricular assist device (LVAD) implantation. We used a doubly robust inverse probability weighting based on propensity scores to evaluate the association between surgical approach and clinical outcomes in 187 consecutive patients (thoracotomy: n = 55; sternotomy: n = 132). The primary endpoint was RV systolic function in the early postoperative period, assessed by tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion (TAPSE). Despite comparable baseline RV performance and hemodynamics, the thoracotomy-based approach was associated with superior preservation of postoperative RV systolic function compared to median sternotomy (TAPSE: 12.0 vs. 11.0 mm, p = 0.001). In weighted regression models, median sternotomy was associated with a significant reduction in postoperative TAPSE (β = -0.085, p = 0.036) and a 35% relative increase in hospital length of stay (p = 0.015). Furthermore, accounting for heart transplantation as a competing risk, median sternotomy was associated with a significantly higher hazard of long-term mortality (subdistribution hazard ratio [sHR]: 1.78, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.07-3.00, p = 0.027). These findings suggest that the clinical benefits of sternal-sparing techniques extend beyond acute functional protection. This surgical strategy supports the use of less invasive approaches to optimize both early recovery and long-term outcomes in the LVAD population.

articles.title: Advances in photothermal therapy for antibacterial biomedical materials: Photothermal agents, near-infrared windows, and combination strategies.
articles.abstract: Bacterial infections, particularly those involving multidrug-resistant pathogens and biofilm-associated infections in wound and implant-related settings, remain difficult to treat with conventional antibiotics alone. Photothermal therapy (PTT) has emerged as a non-antibiotic antibacterial strategy owing to its localized heat generation, broad-spectrum antibacterial activity, spatial controllability, and low risk of inducing conventional drug resistance. The antibacterial efficacy of PTT is largely governed by photothermal agents (PTAs), whose light absorption capacity, photothermal conversion efficiency, structural stability, biosafety, and bacterial interfacial interactions determine therapeutic performance. This review summarizes recent advances in antibacterial PTT from the perspectives of PTA design, excitation windows, and therapeutic integration. Representative first near-infrared window (NIR-I) PTAs, including noble metal nanomaterials, carbon-based nanomaterials, metal sulfides/oxides, metal-organic frameworks, and organic PTAs, are discussed with emphasis on their structural characteristics, photothermal mechanisms, surface regulation strategies, and antibacterial performance. Recent progress in second near-infrared window (NIR-II) PTAs is then highlighted, particularly their advantages in deeper tissue penetration, biofilm treatment, imaging-guided therapy, and precise intervention in complex infections. PTT-based combination strategies involving photodynamic therapy, chemodynamic therapy, and immunotherapy are also reviewed to illustrate how localized heat can synergize with oxidative damage, catalytic radical generation, immune modulation, and infection microenvironment regulation to enhance antibacterial efficacy. Finally, challenges and future directions of antibacterial PTT are discussed, including improving PTA stability and biocompatibility, minimizing thermal damage to normal tissues, enhancing infection-site responsiveness, and promoting clinical translation. Overall, this review provides a materials and biointerface perspective on how PTA design, NIR excitation, and therapeutic integration can guide the development of effective antibacterial photothermal platforms and their clinical translation.

articles.title: Development and Validation of a Blood Test Informed Risk Prediction Model for Lung Cancer-The Copenhagen Lung Cancer Risk Model (CPH-Lung).
articles.journal: Journal of clinical oncology : official journal of the American Society of Clinical Oncology
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Lung cancer screening reduces lung cancer mortality, but identifying high-risk individuals remains difficult. We wanted to develop a blood test-based risk model (CPH-Lung) to improve risk stratification before image-based screening.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: We included individuals from two prospective general population cohorts to model 6-year lung cancer risk; the Copenhagen General Population Study (CGPS) for training and the Copenhagen City Heart Study (CCHS) for validation. We analyzed clinical and biochemical variables from ever-smokers (689 cases and 1,924 controls) nested within CGPS to train a 6-year lung cancer risk model. CPH-Lung was validated in a cohort of ever-smokers age ≥50 years in the Copenhagen City Heart Study (CCHS, 3,195 individuals) and compared with the validated PLCOm2012 model.

RESULTS: There were 689 and 68 events of 6-year lung cancer in the CGPS and the CCHS. In the CCHS validation study, the CPH-Lung versus the PLCOm2012 yielded AUCs of 0.783 (95% CI, 0.731 to 0.835) versus 0.720 (95% CI, 0.669 to 0.770) for detection of all 6-year lung cancers (P = .0059). The discrimination was similar in the CGPS. At specificity of 77.7% (as would have been achieved using currently applied screening criteria, eg, NELSON or NLST), sensitivities were 57.6% versus 39.2% in women (P < .0001) and 61.4% versus 54.7% in men (P = .004) for CPH-Lung versus PLCOm2012. The mean age at diagnosis was 68.2 years (standard deviation [SD], 7.50) in the 120 individuals with lung cancer predicted exclusively by CPH-Lung compared with 76.5 years (SD, 8.04) in the 37 individuals predicted exclusively by PLCOm2012 (P < .0001).

CONCLUSION: After inclusion of blood test information, the CPH-Lung model was more sensitive in the Danish population than PLCOm2012 for prediction of 6-year lung cancer risk particularly among women and younger individuals.

articles.title: Predicting ICU Seizures Using 1 hour of cEEG.
articles.journal: Journal of clinical neurophysiology : official publication of the American Electroencephalographic Society
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Continuous electroencephalography (cEEG) is the gold standard for detecting electrographic seizures in the intensive care unit (ICU), but limited resources limit prolonged monitoring for all patients. We developed an automated, interpretable pipeline that uses a single hour of cEEG to estimate near-term seizure risk across multiple prediction windows.

METHODS: We retrospectively studied 50 adults who underwent ICU cEEG monitoring at a single tertiary center. From a 1-hour segment, we computed automated interictal-ictal continuum (IIC) burden probabilities for lateralized periodic discharges (LPDs), generalized periodic discharges (GPDs), and lateralized rhythmic delta activity (LRDA), along with quantitative background EEG features reflecting signal organization and hemispheric asymmetry. Segments were labeled by seizure occurrence within the subsequent 1, 2, 4, 8, 12, or 24 hours. Support vector machine (SVM) and bagged-tree classifiers were trained using clinical-only, background-only, and combined feature sets with a 70/30 patient-level train-test split and cross-validation within the training set.

RESULTS: For the 4-hour horizon, the combined-feature SVM achieved 76% accuracy and the lowest Brier score (0.25), outperforming clinical-only (72%) and background-only (70%) models. Across horizons, SVM accuracy declined from 94% (1 hour) to 79% (24 hours) with increasing Brier scores, indicating reduced calibration at longer intervals. AUC-receiver operating characteristic increased with wider prediction windows, consistent with higher seizure prevalence at longer lead times.

CONCLUSIONS: Integrating automated IIC probabilities with quantitative background EEG features enables moderate, interpretable near-term seizure prediction from a single hour of ICU cEEG. Initial external validation on an independent multicenter ICU cohort supports generalizability, although broader prospective and multicenter evaluation are needed before clinical deployment.

articles.title: Updated systematic review and meta-analysis comparing Myval versus Sapien 3 transcatheter heart valves in severe aortic stenosis: focus on early and one-year mortality.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) is a guideline-recommended treatment for severe aortic stenosis (AS). While the balloon-expandable Edwards Sapien 3 valve has long been the benchmark, the newer Myval valve has emerged as a potential alternative. Comparative data on mid-term survival, specifically one-year all-cause mortality, are lacking but crucial for clinical evaluation.

METHODS: This systematic review and meta-analysis synthesised direct comparative evidence on the Myval versus Sapien 3 valves in patients undergoing TAVI, searching PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane Central up to November 2025. The primary outcomes included all-cause mortality within 30 days and 1 year. Secondary outcomes were 30-day safety events and hemodynamic parameters.

RESULTS: Five studies (n = 2771) were included. The pooled analysis indicated no statistical difference in 30-day mortality (RR: 1.05, 95% CI: 0.53-2.07; p = 0.89; I2=0%) or in one-year all-cause mortality (RR: 0.93, 95% CI: 0.64-1.35; p = 0.70; I2=0%). Rates of stroke, major bleeding, pacemaker implantation, and other 30-day complications were also comparable (all p > 0.05). Hemodynamically, the Myval valve was superior at 30 days, with a lower mean gradient (MD: -2.37, 95% CI: -3.45 to -1.30; p < 0.0001) and larger effective orifice area (MD: 0.26, 95% CI: 0.17-0.35; p < 0.00001). Available one-year data from two randomised trials indicated this hemodynamic benefit was sustained.

CONCLUSION: This updated meta-analysis demonstrates that the newer Myval valve offers comparable early safety and one-year survival to the established Sapien 3 valve, with superior and sustained hemodynamic performance. These findings support its role as a safe and effective alternative in the TAVI landscape.

articles.title: A nomogram integrating first-trimester metabolic and angiogenic markers for predicting adverse pregnancy outcomes in gestational diabetes mellitus: development and internal validation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) is associated with a significantly increased risk of adverse pregnancy outcomes. This study aimed to develop and internally validate a nomogram integrating integrating first-trimester metabolic and angiogenic markers to predict composite adverse pregnancy outcomes in GDM.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of 1,000 GDM patients (training set n=700, validation set n=300). Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify independent predictors and construct a nomogram. Model performance was assessed by discrimination (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve [AUC]), calibration (Hosmer-Lemeshow test, calibration plots), and decision curve analysis (DCA).

RESULTS: Six variables were retained as independent predictors: pre-pregnancy BMI, FPG, TG, HOMA-IR, PIGF, and sFlt-1. The full model showed excellent discrimination in internal validation, with an AUC of 0.87 (95% CI 0.84-0.90) in the training set and 0.84 (95% CI 0.80-0.88) in the validation set, significantly outperforming a metabolic-only model without PIGF/sFlt-1 (AUC 0.82, p=0.01). Calibration was good (Hosmer-Lemeshow p=0.36 and 0.42, respectively). DCA demonstrated clinical net benefit across threshold probabilities of 0.15-0.35. Subgroup analyses confirmed stable performance across age, BMI, treatment, and parity.

CONCLUSION: The nomogram incorporating first-trimester metabolic and angiogenic markers accurately predicts adverse pregnancy outcomes in GDM patients in this internal validation cohort.

articles.title: Risk of Endophthalmitis After Cataract Surgery in Immunosuppressed Patients.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: The aim of this study was to determine whether systemic immunosuppression increases postoperative endophthalmitis risk following cataract surgery and to characterize risk differences across immunosuppressant medication classes.

PATIENTS AND METHODS: Retrospective cohort study using the TriNetX federated health research network identified 422,786 immunosuppressed patients (medication exposure within 90 days pre-surgery) and 263,913 non-immunosuppressed patients undergoing cataract surgery. After 1:1 propensity score matching for age, sex, race, diabetes, ethnicity, autoimmune diagnosis, year of surgery, and prior intravitreal injections, 208,935 patients remained per cohort. Patients were identified using International Classification of Diseases, Tenth Revision (ICD-10) and Current Procedural Terminology (CPT) codes, with medications categorized as corticosteroids, classic non-biologic immunosuppressants, small molecule inhibitors, or biologic immunomodulators. Endophthalmitis outcomes were assessed at 1 to 42 days (acute), 43 to 365 days (delayed onset), and 1 to 90 days postoperatively.

RESULTS: Immunosuppressed patients showed significantly elevated 90-day endophthalmitis risk (odds ratio [OR] 1.77, 95% CI 1.42-2.21, P < .0001; risk difference 0.128%). Risk elevation persisted for acute (OR 1.86, 95% CI 1.52-2.24, P < .0001) and delayed (OR 2.07, 95% CI 1.51-2.84, P < .0001) timeframes. Classic non-biologic immunosuppressants demonstrated strongest association (OR 5.03, 95% CI 3.97-6.37, P < .0001), followed by systemic corticosteroids (OR 1.77, 95% CI 1.40-2.23, P < .0001). Small molecule inhibitors showed non-significant trends. Biologic immunomodulators demonstrated a lower observed risk for acute endophthalmitis (OR 0.58, 95% CI 0.41-0.81, P = .0015).

CONCLUSION: Systemic immunosuppression significantly increases acute and delayed-onset postoperative endophthalmitis risk following cataract surgery, with substantial variation across medication classes. Classic immunosuppressants and corticosteroids confer the highest risk, whereas biologic immunomodulators do not appear to increase risk.

articles.title: Human cytomegalovirus antagonizes SMC5/6 driven genome silencing via UL35 instituted proteasomal degradation of SLF2.
articles.abstract: Recent studies demonstrated that the structural maintenance of chromosomes complex 5/6 (SMC5/6) acts as an important antiviral restriction factor that silences episomal DNA. Consequently, viruses have evolved strategies to antagonize this defence system. Interestingly, it was shown that SMC5/6-mediated silencing of extrachromosomal DNA depends on its recruitment to PML nuclear bodies which is mediated by a protein termed SMC5/6 localization factor 2 (SLF2). Since human cytomegalovirus (HCMV) dissociates PML nuclear bodies (PML-NBs) during the first hours of infection, we asked for the fate of SMC5/6 components during the HCMV replicative cycle. We first investigated the expression levels of SMC5/6 core components at the onset of HCMV infection and found that they were not downregulated by HCMV. Instead, we observed a distinct decrease of SLF2 protein levels which correlated with a complete dispersal of the SMC5/6 complex from PML-NBs. This was also observed after infection with UV inactivated HCMV and could not be blocked by cycloheximide treatment suggesting the involvement of an imported structural component of the virion. While we could exclude a requirement of the HCMV tegument protein pp71 (UL82), a targeted screen identified the tegument protein UL35 as being required and sufficient for proteasomal degradation of SLF2. In line with these results, SLF2 levels remained stable after infection with a recombinant HCMV harbouring a stop codon within the UL35 gene region and this correlated with a defect in the onset of HCMV immediate early gene expression. Furthermore, we observed an enhanced recruitment of SMC5/6 to PML-NBs and an overall increase in the association of parental viral genomes with SMC5/6 containing PML-NBs in the absence of UL35. Congruently, siRNA mediated depletion of SLF2 resulted in a reversal of this phenotype. This strongly suggests that UL35 serves as a novel viral SLF2 antagonist to prevent the initial silencing of incoming viral genomes by SMC5/6.

articles.title: Zika virus produces two isoforms of the NS2A protein that play mutually exclusive roles in viral replication and virion assembly.
articles.abstract: Zika virus (ZIKV), dengue virus, and several other orthoflaviviruses cause disease outbreaks in human and animal populations worldwide. The orthoflaviviral nonstructural protein 2A (NS2A) is critical for both viral replication and virion assembly. However, due to its small size, hydrophobicity, and the absence of structural information or protein-specific antibodies, we lack a clear understanding of how NS2A participates in these disparate processes. Here, using endogenously tagged NS2A-containing viral RNAs, we reveal that two NS2A isoforms are present during ZIKV infection, including both full-length NS2A and a C-terminally truncated isoform, termed NS2Aα. Phylogenetic and conservation analyses combined with polyprotein cleavage assays suggest that both NS2A isoforms are generated via the viral protease and are conserved across the Orthoflavivirus genus. Finally, using assays for viral replication and infectious particle production, we demonstrate that the two distinct NS2A isoforms function at different stages of the viral life cycle, with full-length NS2A required for viral RNA replication and NS2Aα important for virion assembly. Taken together, our data helps shed light on the form(s) and function(s) of the NS2A protein and suggests that each NS2A isoform plays a mutually exclusive role in the orthoflaviviral life cycle.

articles.title: GTPase GBP7 promotes HSV-1 infection by interacting with and activating eEF1A1 to accelerate the protein translation process.
articles.abstract: Guanylate-binding proteins (GBPs) are immune GTPases induced by interferons (IFNs) and comprise GBPs1-7. In this study, GBP7, a less studied member of the GBPs, was identified to possess Herpes simplex virus I (HSV-1) promoting effects on replication both in vitro and in vivo. Knockdown of GBP7 or loss of its GTPase activity demonstrated significant antiviral effects. Consistently, GBP7-/- mice infected with HSV-1 showed higher survival and milder symptoms. Mechanistically, we discovered GBP7 directly binds to eukaryotic translation elongation factor 1α1 (eEF1A1), which was validated through immunoprecipitation mass spectrum (IP-MS) and binding affinity assays. GBP7 utilizes its GTPase activity to assist eEF1A1 in GTP hydrolysis, activating its role in promoting protein translation, thereby increasing viral replication and infection. Moreover, through high-throughput virtual screening, S-Adenosylhomocysteine (SAH) was identified as a novel GBP7 targeting inhibitor, which demonstrated potent antiviral activity against HSV-1infection and broad-spectrum potentiality. Collectively, these findings uncover the critical role of the GBP7-eEF1A1 axis in viral infection and provide theoretical basis for host-targeted antiviral therapy.

articles.title: Comparative effectiveness of amlodipine versus nifedipine prescribed at discharge in patients with ischemic stroke or transient ischemic attack: A nationwide 5-year follow-up registry study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Amlodipine and nifedipine are the most commonly prescribed calcium channel blockers (CCB) for patients suffering from ischemic stroke or transient ischemic attack (TIA). Nevertheless, there is a scarcity of direct comparative evidence on their effectiveness. This study aimed to compare the effectiveness of amlodipine and nifedipine in patients with ischemic stroke or TIA.

METHODS AND FINDINGS: This observational study was based on the Third China National Stroke Registry, which recruited consecutive adult patients with ischemic stroke or TIA from 2015 to 2018. In this study, ischemic stroke or TIA patients were prescribed either amlodipine or nifedipine at discharge. The primary outcome was the distribution of modified Rankin Scale (mRS) score, which assesses functional outcomes in patients with stroke, at 5 years. The intergroup differences were examined using ordinal logistic regression, yielding odds ratios (OR) and 95% confidence intervals (CI). Patient age, gender, body mass index, systolic blood pressure at admission, and onset date were adjusted. To improve baseline characteristic balance, inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) was implemented. A total of 2,859 eligible patients were included, and there were 1847 patients in the amlodipine group and 1,058 patients in the nifedipine group after IPTW. The amlodipine group demonstrated significantly lower 5-year mRS scores in comparison to the nifedipine group, with an OR of 0.76 (95% CI [0.65, 0.89]; p < 0.001). A total of 956 (51.76%) amlodipine users and 632 (59.74%) nifedipine users achieved a mRS score > 0 at 5 years, with an OR of 0.71 (95% CI [0.61, 0.83]; p < 0.001). The sensitivity analyses yielded consistent results. The main limitations include the inherent observational design, the exclusive reliance on registry data, and relatively high loss-to-follow-up rate at 5 years.

CONCLUSIONS: This study revealed that amlodipine, compared to nifedipine, may be associated with improved functional recovery in ischemic stroke or TIA patients. Randomized controlled trials are warranted to confirm these findings and refine CCB therapy.

articles.title: Vaccination accelerates the race of influenza virus against collective immunity.
articles.abstract: Respiratory viruses persist in a population, because their rapid evolution allows them to escape recognition by antibodies in previously-infected individuals. To optimize parameters of an effective vaccine, an epidemiological model of a population infected with an evolving virus is coupled to a model of multi-locus evolution. Model parameters are informed from influenza virus data. The cases of overlapping and non-overlapping effect of consecutive vaccinations are considered. The results predict that vaccination will accelerate viral evolution and may even increase infection incidence, unless one of two scenarios takes place: either antibodies elicited by vaccine are more broadly neutralizing than antibodies to natural infection, or the vaccine vector lies slightly ahead of the dominant virus variant in the evolutionary trajectory. These results suggest that the probabilistic prognosis of virus evolution represents a promising strategy of vaccine improvement complementing the search for broadly-neutralizing vaccines.

articles.title: Brought with the wind: A case of melioidosis acquired in the United States presenting with multiple pulmonary nodules.
articles.abstract: Burkholderia pseudomallei, the causative agent of melioidosis, is a gram-negative bacterium historically endemic to Southeast Asia and Northern Australia. However, recent environmental detection along the Gulf Coast and an increasing number of reported cases in non-travelers have raised questions regarding potential endemicity and environmental establishment in the Southern United States. We report a case of putatively locally acquired pulmonary melioidosis in a Florida resident with no recent international travel history, illustrating the diagnostic and therapeutic challenges posed by this rare pathogen. The patient presented with fever, pleuritic chest pain, and hypoxia following a period of severe weather. Computed tomography (CT) of the chest revealed multiple solid pulmonary nodules with ground-glass opacities and mediastinal lymphadenopathy. Given his underlying stage 3b chronic kidney disease (CKD), the patient was treated with an intensive course of intravenous ceftazidime followed by oral doxycycline monotherapy, achieving full clinical recovery. Follow-up imaging at 3 months demonstrated complete resolution of the pulmonary nodules. This case emphasizes the importance of considering melioidosis in the differential diagnosis for non-resolving community-acquired pneumonia or significant pulmonary nodules in the Southern United States, even in the absence of international travel. Risk factors such as diabetes mellitus and severe weather events are key clinical clues. While trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole remains the preferred eradication therapy, doxycycline may serve as a potential alternative for patients with renal impairment when first-line therapy is contraindicated.

articles.title: Thyroid Abnormalities in a Prospective Longitudinal Cohort of Pediatric Patients following SARS-CoV-2 infection.
articles.abstract: Introduction Thyroid dysfunction has been reported in adults and children following COVID-19. We evaluated thyroid function in children following SARS-CoV-2 infection compared to uninfected controls over at least one year of follow up. Methods Thyroid function tests (TSH, Free T4) were analyzed in pediatric participants enrolled in the Pediatric SARS CoV-2 Long Term Outcome Study (PECOS), a diverse, prospective, longitudinal, multicenter cohort study. Assessments were conducted at baseline, and at follow-up visits for both infected and uninfected cohorts. Results Among 505 participants with non-missing data at baseline and 12-months, no significant differences were noted in proportion of TSH or Free T4 abnormalities among the infected vs. uninfected participants. Among infected participants 5% (25/464) developed subclinical hypothyroidism (high TSH and normal free T4) following recovery from SARS-CoV-2 infection, compared with 4.9% (2/41), a similar proportion in the uninfected group (p=1). Within the infected subgroup during 36-month follow up, three were treated with levothyroxine for persistent TSH elevation or goiter and 2/3 had positive thyroid antibodies consistent with autoimmune thyroid disease. Neither the number of SARS-CoV-2 reinfections nor number of COVID-19 vaccination status predicted the occurrence of TSH abnormalities. Conclusion Children infected with COVID-19 did not have increased thyroid dysfunction compared to uninfected controls during 12 months of follow up. A small proportion (5%) developed mild subclinical hypothyroidism that was transient in both groups, and only 3 infected participants (with TSH>10mcIU/mL or thyromegaly) needed levothyroxine replacement after 36-month follow up in this subgroup. Risk of thyroid autoimmunity compared to the uninfected population needs further study.

articles.title: Neuropeptides in Immunometabolism and Neuroinflammation: Insights from Traditional Chinese Medicine.
articles.abstract: Neuropeptides are small bioactive peptides secreted by neurons and immune cells that serve as critical messengers in both central and peripheral systems. Recent studies have identified key neuropeptides-such as Substance P (SP), Vasoactive Intestinal Peptide (VIP), Neuropeptide Y (NPY), and Calcitonin Gene-Related Peptide (CGRP)-as pivotal regulators of immunometabolism and neuroinflammation. These peptides influence macrophage polarization, T cell differentiation, cytokine production, and neuroimmune crosstalk, linking chronic inflammation to conditions such as obesity, diabetes, autoimmunity, and neurodegeneration. This review synthesizes emerging evidence on Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) interventions-including herbal formulas, single herbs, bioactive compounds, and acupuncture-that modulate neuropeptide signaling via NF-κB, MAPK, and Nrf2 pathways. These mechanisms contribute to analgesia, emotional stabilization, metabolic regulation, and neuroprotection. The article further presents a modular framework connecting representative Chinese medicinal substances to specific neuropeptides and physiological functions, offering a translational foundation for neuropeptide-targeted therapies and integrative precision health strategies.

articles.title: Targeting the CEACAM6-ELANE axis to regulate the PI3K/AKT/NF-?B signaling pathway: a new strategy to improve neutrophilic airway inflammation in juvenile asthma.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Neutrophil-infiltrating inflammation is closely linked to severe asthma in teenagers, and its mechanism needs to be investigated. CEACAM6 is a critical molecule that regulates neutrophil function and is significantly expressed in the airways of asthmatic patients, but its precise role in the disease and downstream signaling mechanisms remain unknown. The goal of this study was to investigate the role and mechanism of CEACAM6 in neutrophil airway inflammation.

METHODS: The GSE188424 data set was analyzed using bioinformatics. An OVA-induced juvenile asthma mouse model was created utilizing CEACAM6 gene knockout mice. CEACAM6 was knocked down in BEAS-2B cells using siRNA, and LPS was utilized to produce inflammation. Molecular and phenotypic studies were carried out using Western blot, Co-IP, ELISA, and flow cytometry.

RESULTS: CEACAM6 expression in asthmatic lung tissue was significantly elevated. In mice, knocking down CEACAM6 drastically reduces airway neutrophil inflammation and inflammatory factor release. Cell tests demonstrated that CEACAM6 knockdown reduced LPS-induced epithelial cell damage and inflammation. CEACAM6 binds to elastase, neutrophil expressed (ELANE), activating the PI3K/AKT/NF-κB signaling cascade. ELANE supplementation reversed the anti-inflammatory effects of CEACAM6 knockdown.

CONCLUSION: CEACAM6 increases neutrophil airway inflammation by binding to ELANE and activating the PI3K/AKT/NF-κB pathway. Targeting the CEACAM6-ELANE axis could be a novel method for treating neutrophilic asthma.

articles.title: Outcomes in a cohort of preterm infants born at 22-23 weeks from a proactive center in Germany.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: We describe survival, major neonatal morbidities and neurodevelopmental outcomes of preterm infants below 24 weeks' GA in a German single- center cohort managed with an intensive care treatment approach.

METHODS: This retrospective single-center study included preterm infants born at 22+0 to 22+6 weeks' and 23+0 to 23+6 weeks' gestation (GA) between January 2008 and December 2022. Obstetric characteristics, delivery room management, short-term outcomes and neurodevelopmental outcomes at 22-28 months were described. Findings were compared with published data from other proactive centers.

RESULTS: Of 183 inborn infants, 143 received intensive care treatment, including 32 infants born at 22 weeks' GA and 111 born at 23 weeks' GA. Survival to discharge among actively treated infants was 75.0% (24/32) at 22 weeks and 84.7% (94/111) at 23 weeks. Moderate/severe Bronchopulmonary Dysplasia (BPD) occurred more frequently in 22-week than in 23-week infants (70.8% vs. 42.6%, p=0.02), and supplemental oxygen at discharge was more common (37.5% vs 16.0%, p=0.04). The rate of infants lost to follow-up was 20% in both groups. 47.4% of 22-week and 63.2% of 23-week infants had a Mental Development Index (MDI) ≥70 (no or mild impairment), whereas severe cognitive impairment (MDI <55) was present in 42.1% and 19.7%, respectively.

CONCLUSION: In this experienced center with an intensive care treatment approach, survival of infants born at 22+0 to 23+6 weeks GA was high. However, neonatal morbidity and neurodevelopmental impairment remained substantial, particularly among 22-week infants. Future efforts should focus on improving long-term outcomes in addition to survival.

articles.title: Perceived Stress, Sleep Quality, and Their Impact on Glycemic Control Among Type 2 Diabetes Patients in Riyadh: Cross-Sectional Evidence.
articles.journal: Medical principles and practice : international journal of the Kuwait University, Health Science Centre
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the relation between Perceived Stress and Sleep Quality with glycemic blood levels in T2DM patients in Riyadh.

SUBJECT AND METHODS: This cross-sectional study evaluated a total of 309 patients diagnosed with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. The study comprised an initial validation and Arabic translation phase involving 160 participants, followed by an analytical phase focusing on 149 adult patients. To investigate impact of psychosocial and metabolic factors on glycemic control (HbA1c), data were collected using the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI) and the Perceived Stress Scale (PSS-10), alongside clinical metrics such as BMI and dyslipidemia extracted from medical records. A multivariable linear regression model was utilized to identify independent factors associated with glycemic regulation within the local population.

RESULTS: The multivariable regression model demonstrated robust explanatory power (Adjusted R2 = 0.726, p < 0.001). Traditional risk factors, specifically elevated BMI (β = 0.448, p < 0.001) and dyslipidemia (β = 0.304, p < 0.001), were significantly associated with higher HbA1c levels. Notably, poor sleep quality emerged as a significant independent factor associated with elevated HbA1c (β = 0.261, p < 0.001), whereas perceived stress did not exhibit a significant correlation. Conversely, physical activity demonstrated a significant protective effect, correlating with lower HbA1c (β = -0.271, p <0.001).

CONCLUSION: Poor sleep quality, rather than perceived psychological stress, is a primary factor independently associated with hyperglycemia in this patient cohort. These findings suggest that standard diabetes care should integrate formal sleep assessments alongside patient care management.

articles.title: Best Practices in Performing CRRT during ECMO: Workgroup Statements from the Joint Acute Disease Quality Initiative (ADQI) and Extracorporeal Life Support Organization (ELSO) Consensus Conference on ECMO, AKI, Fluid Management and CRRT.
articles.abstract: Extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) is a well-established life support technology. However, among patients receiving ECMO, acute kidney injury (AKI) is common, and a substantial proportion receive concomitant support with renal replacement therapy (RRT). There are several techniques for combining RRT with ECMO in patients, including the use of in-line hemofilters in the ECMO circuit, integrated RRT machine circuits into the ECMO circuit and the use of parallel circuits where ECMO and CRRT are provided by discrete vascular access. Enclosed is a summary of work group findings from the joint Acute Disease Quality Initiative (ADQI) and Extracorporeal Life Support (ELSO) consensus meeting focused on "ECMO, AKI, Fluid Management and CRRT," which identified priorities, knowledge gaps and research opportunities, along with generating key consensus-based statements to guide best practices for performing CRRT during ECMO.

articles.title: Quantitative assessment of myocardial dysfunction in mild focal left ventricular hypertrophy using CMR feature tracking.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to investigate cardiac dysfunction in patients with mild focal left ventricular hypertrophy (MF-LVH) by analyzing the left ventricular (LV) and left atrial (LA) deformation parameters derived from cardiac magnetic resonance feature tracking (CMR-FT).

METHODS: This retrospective study included 36 patients with MF-LVH, 44 patients with HCM without late gadolinium enhancement (HCM-non-LGE), and 32 healthy controls who were examined between November 2020 and August 2025. The LA and LV strain parameters were obtained using CMR-FT. Statistical comparisons, multivariable logistic regression, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analyses were conducted.

RESULTS: While conventional parameters showed no difference, all global LV strains and most strain rate parameters were significantly impaired in both patient groups, showing a stepwise decline with advancing hypertrophy severity. In multivariable analyses, the peak diastolic radial strain rate (PD-RSR) was the primary discriminator distinguishing MF-LVH from controls, and LV global longitudinal strain (LV-GLS) was the key discriminator differentiating MF-LVH from HCM-non-LGE. LV-GLS and LA minimal volume index (LAVImin) were the key discriminators for HCM-non-LGE versus controls. ROC analysis confirmed LV-GLS as an excellent discriminator (AUC 0.85 for MF-LVH vs. HCM-non-LGE; AUC 0.96 for HCM-non-LGE vs. controls), with notably similar optimal cutoff values (-13.94% and -13.99%, respectively). PD-RSR showed good accuracy in identifying MF-LVH.

CONCLUSION: PD-RSR indicates early diastolic impairment, and LV-GLS sensitively detects systolic dysfunction in patients with MF-LVH. The overlapping LV-GLS values between patients with MF-LVH and HCM-non-LGE suggest a potential pathophysiological continuum. CMR-FT enables early detection of subclinical myocardial dysfunction in this population.

articles.title: Left Atrial Appendage Closure or Medical Therapy in Atrial Fibrillation: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The use of anticoagulation in patients with atrial fibrillation is often limited by the significant risk of bleeding, and difficulties maintaining consistent adherence over time. These challenges have led to the development of left atrial appendage closure (LAAC) as an alternative stroke prevention strategy in this patient population. Our study aimed to evaluate LAAC versus medical therapy in patients with atrial fibrillation.

METHODS: A comprehensive search was conducted using PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane Library from database inception through April 1, 2026. The predefined endpoints were composite outcome of systemic embolism, cardiovascular mortality, or stroke in addition to other endpoints including all-cause mortality, cardiovascular mortality, strokes, and major bleeding. All outcomes were pooled using a random effect Mantel-Haenszel model. The between-study variance (τ2) was estimated using the Paul Mendel method, which is the preferred method when the number of included studies is small.

RESULTS: A total of five randomized controlled trials, 5,404 patients were analyzed; 2,878 underwent LAAC and 2,526 received medical therapy. The median follow-up across studies was 4 years. LAAC met noninferiority compared with medical therapy in atrial fibrillation for major bleeding (RR 0.86; 95% CI 0.59-1.26) and all-cause mortality (RR 0.93; 95% CI 0.71-1.22). In contrast, noninferiority was not met for the composite outcome (RR 0.97; 95% CI 0.64-1.47), cardiovascular mortality (RR 0.86; 95% CI 0.51-1.42), systemic embolism (RR 1.93; 95% CI 0.21-17.5), and all stroke (RR 1.11; 95% CI 0.73-1.67).

CONCLUSION: This meta-analysis showed that LAAC was noninferior to anticoagulation for all-cause mortality and major bleeding, but it did not meet noninferiority for the other assessed outcomes, including stroke, cardiovascular mortality, and/or systemic embolism.

articles.title: A 'First-Time-Right' strategy in secondary prevention of coronary artery disease: Rationale and design of the prospective, temporally controlled observational GOLDEN study.
articles.abstract: Introduction After an acute coronary syndrome (ACS) or coronary revascularisation, the risk of recurrent vascular events remain substantial. Despite clear guideline recommendations, secondary prevention and long-term adherence to preventive treatment is often suboptimal. Current secondary prevention strategies typically involve initiating a limited number of pharmacologic therapies during hospitalisation, followed by sequential intensification after discharge to achieve individualized guideline-recommended targets.
