However, this strategy is prone to therapeutic inertia and negatively affects patient motivation and long-term adherence. We hypothesise that a 'first-time-right' strategy, where individualised, guideline-based pharmacological treatment is proactively initiated during hospitalisation, can improve risk factor control and adherence compared to current practice, and thereby reduce major cardiovascular events. Methods and analysis GOLDEN (Guided Optimisation for Long-term Disease rEduction in secoNdary Prevention of cardiovascular disease) is a prospective, temporally controlled observational cohort study aiming to include 5,586 patients hospitalised for ACS or coronary revascularisation. A guidelines-based 'first-time-right' pharmacological optimisation strategy will be compared to current practice on the 3-year incidence of cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, stroke, or ischemia-driven revascularisation (4-point MACE). This strategy targets both patients and healthcare professionals and aims to utilise the teachable moment during hospitalisation to optimise pharmacological strategies, apply key behavioural principles to improve adherence, and reframe follow-up from reactive up-titration to proactive de-escalation. A pocket card and online tool will be provided to check applicable guidelines during hospitalisation and formulate follow-up recommendations. An on-site training visit and communication aids are intended to support implementation and promote adherence. Summary This study will evaluate the effects of a 'first-time-right' strategy - focused on early in-hospital initiation and optimisation of guideline-based pharmacotherapy after acute coronary syndrome or coronary revascularisation - on the risk of recurrent MACE compared to current practice.

articles.title: Luteolin alleviates neurogenic inflammation in OVA-induced combined allergic rhinitis and asthma syndrome mice through TRPV1/ERK-related signaling.
articles.journal: International archives of allergy and immunology
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Combined Allergic Rhinitis and Asthma Syndrome (CARAS), a common chronic allergic respiratory disease, involves dysregulated neuro-immune interactions and neurogenic inflammation. Luteolin (LUT) has significant anti-inflammatory and antioxidant activities. However, its effects and underlying mechanism in CARAS remain unclear. This study aims to determine the effects of LUT administration during the airway challenge phase of CARAS and its association with TRPV1/ERK signaling.

METHODS: BALB/C mice were used to establish an ovalbumin (OVA)-induced CARAS model and LUT was administered. The nasal symptoms were evaluated by counting the number of nasal scratching and sneezing. HE and toluidine blue staining were performed to determine the histopathological changes. Total and differential cell counts in bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF) were determined. The levels of histamine, MCP-1, substance P (SP), CGRP and Th1/Th2/Th17-related cytokines were detected by ELISA kit. Besides, TRPV1 and p-ERK expression levels were measured by immunofluorescence staining and Western blotting.

RESULTS: Our study indicated that LUT administration significantly reduced sneezing frequency, nasal scratching behavior, and serum OVA-specific IgE level in CARAS mice compared to the model group. Histopathological analysis demonstrated that LUT administration reduced inflammatory cell accumulation and histological scores in the nasal mucosa and lung tissues and was associated with reduced inflammatory cell counts in BALF. In addition, LUT administration reduced mast cell density in both tissues. Serum histamine and MCP-1 levels and pulmonary levels of IL-4, IL-5, IL-13, IL-17A, and IFN-γ were also reduced following LUT administration. LUT administration also reduced serum and BALF levels of SP and CGRP. Furthermore, LUT administration reduced TRPV1 expression and p-ERK levels in the nasal mucosa and lung tissue.

CONCLUSION: LUT administration attenuates allergic and inflammatory responses in OVA-induced CARAS mice, which may be associated with TRPV1/ERK signaling.

articles.title: Diagnosis-Day Prothrombin Time and Transaminase as Exploratory Risk-Stratification Indicators for Severe Neonatal Outcomes in Acute Fatty Liver of Pregnancy.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Acute fatty liver of pregnancy (AFLP) is a life-threatening condition associated with high neonatal morbidity. This study aimed to develop a minimal, clinically feasible prediction model using diagnosis-day laboratory indicators to stratify the risk of severe adverse neonatal outcomes (SANO).

METHODS: In this single-center retrospective cohort (2004-2021), 18 pregnancies with AFLP confirmed by Swansea criteria were analyzed. Firth penalized logistic regression assessed associations between the first laboratory values on the diagnosis day and SANO (intrauterine death/severe asphyxia). A two-variable model combining prothrombin time (PT) and peak transaminase was developed. Model performance was evaluated via area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) and leave-one-out cross-validation (LOOCV).

RESULTS: The incidence of AFLP was 0.71 per 10,000 pregnancies. SANO occurred in 4 cases (17.39%). Diagnosis-day coagulopathy, especially prolonged PT, was the strongest predictor. The PT+transaminase model showed excellent discriminatory performance (AUC=0.982) and robustness upon internal validation (LOOCV AUC=0.964), with a negative predictive value of 1.000 for ruling out SANO.

CONCLUSIONS: Coagulation dysfunction at diagnosis is a key indicator for neonatal risk in AFLP. The proposed PT-based model offers a practical bedside tool for early obstetric risk stratification, aiding in urgent clinical decision-making for delivery planning and neonatal resuscitation preparedness.

articles.title: Prospective assessment of myocardial deformation in fetuses with suspected aortic coarctation.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Prenatal identification of true aortic coarctation (CoA) remains challenging as evidenced by high false-positive rates. Myocardial deformation has been proposed to improve prediction of postnatal outcome. This prospective study aimed to determine whether fetal myocardial deformation analysis can differentiate true CoA from false-positive cases throughout gestation.

METHODS: All fetuses with a prenatal suspicion of isolated CoA were prospectively recruited at our fetal cardiology services. Cases were classified as true CoA or false-positives based on their postnatal diagnosis. Speckle-tracking echocardiography was performed longitudinally to assess left and right ventricular global longitudinal strain (GLS), strain rate, and segmental strain throughout gestation. Measurements were compared between true CoA and false-positive cases.

RESULTS: Thirty-eight fetuses were included (19 true CoA, 19 false-positives). True CoA cases exhibited smaller left-sided cardiac dimensions, including the aortic valve (mean Z-score -3.2 vs. -1.6, p<0.001), aortic isthmus (-3.5 vs. -1.7, p=0.001), and mitral valve (-4.9 vs. -3.1, p<0.001), whereas right-sided cardiac dimensions were comparable (pulmonary valve Z-score 3.0 vs. 2.6, p=0.64; arterial duct Z-score 1.9 vs. 3.2, p=0.61). No clinically relevant differences in myocardial deformation parameters were observed between groups, with similar left ventricular GLS (-20.1% vs. -20.5%, p=0.57), right ventricular GLS (-20.0% vs. -19.1%, p=0.13), strain rates and segmental strain.

CONCLUSION: Fetal myocardial deformation analysis does not provide additional predictive value for postnatal outcome in prenatally suspected isolated CoA. Conventional assessment of cardiac dimensions and flow patterns remains the cornerstone of prenatal CoA diagnosis, yet current imaging modalities cannot provide sufficient diagnostic certainty to safely triage perinatal management.

articles.title: Endorsed but Undefined: Multidisciplinary Counselling for Closed Spinal Dysraphism - A National Multispecialty Survey from India.
articles.abstract: Objective To characterize current antenatal management practices for closed spinal dysraphism (CSD) among Indian specialists and determine whether practice variation is specialty-dependent or distributed within specialties. Methods A cross-sectional expert-reviewed and pilot-tested web-based survey (15 substantive items) was distributed to obstetricians, perinatologists, and radiologists across India (January-September 2023). Descriptive statistics and chi-square tests were used to evaluate the associations between respondents' characteristics and clinical practices. Response dispersion was quantified using normalized Shannon entropy (nH). Results Of the 209 respondents (104 obstetricians, 54 perinatologists, 51 radiologists), 89.5% encountered <10 CSD cases annually. Only 60.5% of the participants attempted to subtype CSD. Fetal MRI was available to 63.6% of respondents, with significantly higher access at tertiary centers (p < 0.001). While 83.3% endorsed mandatory multidisciplinary counseling, attitudes toward medical termination of pregnancy were widely divergent (normalized Shannon entropy: 0.931). No statistically significant interspecialty differences were found for the clinical decision-making domains, including subtyping, prognostication, MRI, and MTP attitudes (all p > 0.34), indicating that variation in counselling content resided within, rather than between, specialties. Conclusion Antenatal CSD management in India shows wide practice variation that is distributed uniformly within, rather than between, specialties. This pattern is consistent with an absence of condition-specific evidence and guidance rather than with specialty-specific disagreement, and supports the development of standardized prenatal reporting, defined MRI indications, and collaborative evidence-based guidelines.

articles.title: Clinical Validation of the Nursing Diagnosis "Risk for Shock" in Patients with Acute Myocardial Infarction Admitted to the ICU.
articles.abstract: ObjectiveTo clinically validate the nursing diagnosis "Risk for shock" in patients with acute myocardial infarction (AMI) admitted to an Intensive Care Unit (ICU).MethodA retrospective case-control study conducted at a high-complexity university hospital in Brazil. The sample consisted of 116 medical records of adult patients with AMI, equally distributed between the case group (with cardiogenic shock; n = 58) and the control group (without cardiogenic shock; n = 58). Diagnostic accuracy measures (sensitivity, specificity, predictive values, and likelihood ratios) were calculated, and multivariate binary logistic regression using the Stepwise Forward method was applied to identify independent predictors and control for confounders.ResultsIn the accuracy analysis, the indicator "Unstable blood pressure" showed the best clinical balance, with a sensitivity of 85.0% (95% CI: 76.2-93.8) and a specificity of 83.6% (95% CI: 74.4-92.8). "Hyperthermia" and "Inadequate fluid volume" showed the highest individual specificities (90.1% and 80.3%, respectively). After adjusting the logistic regression model (Nagelkerke R2 = 0.614; Hosmer-Lemeshow p = 0.782), only four factors remained significant as independent predictors of the outcome: unstable blood pressure (aOR = 7.80; 95% CI: 3.10-19.60; p < 0.001), hypoxia (aOR = 3.70; 95% CI: 1.50-9.20; p = 0.006), hypoxemia (aOR = 2.90; 95% CI: 1.40-6.10; p = 0.004), and inadequate fluid volume (aOR = 2.10; 95% CI: 1.00-4.50; p = 0.048). Thermal and hemorrhagic indicators lost significance after adjustment.ConclusionThe study clinically validated the diagnosis and confirmed a robust predictive model composed of four indicators. Prioritizing the monitoring of these risk factors enables critical care nurses to anticipate hemodynamic collapse, support targeted care protocols, and optimize multiprofessional decision-making at the bedside.

articles.title: Semaglutide in Heart Failure with Preserved Ejection Fraction and Obesity: The Gap Between Discussion and Use.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Semaglutide improves symptoms and physical function in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) and obesity. Whether discussion of treatment is accompanied by its use in routine care is less well understood.

METHODS: We retrospectively assessed treatment discussion, follow-up medication records and documented reasons for non-initiation in 159 patients from a prospective registry. Available follow-up information was retained when assessment dates were incompletely transcribed. Associations with registry-recorded diabetes or prediabetes were explored using Firth logistic regression.

RESULTS: Semaglutide was discussed or offered in 148/159 patients (93.1%). Among 148 baseline nonusers with subsequent medication information, it was newly recorded in 23 (15.5%). Recorded diabetes or prediabetes was associated with this outcome (adjusted odds ratio 3.76, 95% confidence interval 1.08-19.93), but a sensitivity analysis restricting the reference group by glycated haemoglobin was inconclusive. Among 125 patients without subsequently recorded semaglutide, affordability concerns were documented in 55 (44.0%), safety concerns in 48 (38.4%), and both in 38 (30.4%).

CONCLUSION: Frequent discussion of semaglutide coexisted with infrequent documentation of subsequent use. Financial and medication-related concerns commonly overlapped. These findings identify a gap in routine care without establishing its causal determinants or verifying treatment initiation.

articles.title: Failure of P-Wave Duration as a Surrogate Marker for Left Atrial Enlargement in African Americans: Insights from the Jackson Heart Study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Electrocardiographic (ECG) criteria for left atrial enlargement (LAE) serve as clinical surrogates for structural and hemodynamic left atrial (LA) overload. Their diagnostic performance compared to echocardiography remains suboptimal, and African Americans are consistently underrepresented in relevant diagnostic accuracy studies.

METHODS: We performed a cross-sectional analysis of the Jackson Heart Study (JHS), a large community-based cohort of African American adults (aged 21-94 years). P-wave duration was evaluated as the index test across continuous thresholds using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis and area under the curve (AUC) with 95% confidence intervals (95% CI). The main reference standard was echocardiographic LAE defined by American Society of Echocardiography (ASE) sex-specific left atrial (LA) two-dimensional (2D) diameter thresholds (>40 mm in men; >38 mm in women).

RESULTS: A total of 3,572 participants were included, of whom 647 (18.1%) met ASE diameter criteria for LAE. Overall discriminatory performance was poor (AUC 0.603; 95% CI 0.580-0.627). At the traditional ≥120 ms threshold, sensitivity (Sn) was 58.3% (95% CI 54.4-62.1%), specificity (Sp) was 56.8% (95% CI 55.0-58.6%), positive likelihood ratio (LR+) was 1.35 (95% CI 1.25-1.46), and negative likelihood ratio (LR-) was 0.73 (95% CI 0.67-0.81), reflecting limited capacity to rule in or out LAE.

CONCLUSION: In this cohort, P-wave duration demonstrated poor diagnostic accuracy for diameter-defined echocardiographic LAE. These findings highlight the inadequacy of this ECG criterion as a surrogate marker across a historically underrepresented population. Machine learning models may offer a path forward for higher performance of ECG as a screening tool for LAE in African Americans.

articles.title: Association of 24-Hour Anion Gap Difference with Short-Term Mortality in Critically Ill Patients with Heart Failure and Infection.
articles.abstract: Introduction High anion gap (AG) indicates poor prognosis in critical illness. However, the prognostic significance of dynamic early AG changes in patients with concurrent heart failure and infection remains unclear. We aimed to evaluate the association between the 24-hour AG difference and short-term mortality in this population. Methods This retrospective cohort study utilized the Zigong Fourth People's Hospital database. Patients with HF and infection admitted to the intensive care unit (ICU) were included. A 24-hour landmark analysis was applied. The AG difference was categorized based on the change (ΔAG) from admission to 24 hours: Decreasing (ΔAG < -2 mmol/L), Stable (-2 to 2 mmol/L), and Increasing (ΔAG > 2 mmol/L). The primary outcome was 7-day all-cause mortality. Results A total of 299 patients were included. The 7-day mortality was 24.1%. In multivariable Cox analysis adjusted for confounders including baseline lactate and renal function, the Stable difference was significantly associated with increased 7-day mortality compared to the Decreasing group (HR 2.43, 95% CI 1.27-4.63, p=0.007). The Increasing group showed a trend toward higher risk (HR 1.74, p=0.126). Subgroup analyses revealed significant interactions, where the risk of an increasing difference was amplified in patients with hyperlactatemia (>2.0 mmol/L, HR 2.65), or renal dysfunction (eGFR <60, HR 6.27). Albumin-corrected AG sensitivity analysis confirmed these findings. Conclusion Failure to decrease the anion gap within the first 24 hours of ICU admission is associated with a higher risk of short-term mortality in patients with HF and infection. The prognostic value of AG difference is particularly pronounced in high-risk subgroups with hemodynamic or metabolic instability.

articles.title: Pilot and feasibility studies in stroke rehabilitation: reporting quality, progression to trials, and barriers: a scoping review.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Pilot and feasibility studies are designed to determine whether a future trial is warranted. In stroke rehabilitation, such studies have been increasingly published over the years. To clarify how well these studies support future trials, we aimed to: (1) assess the quality of reporting of pilot and feasibility studies aimed to improve mobility (ie, walking) after stroke; (2) examine whether they progress to randomized controlled trials (RCTs); and (3) explore the barriers in following up on these studies.

DESIGN: Scoping review.

PARTICIPANTS: Adults (>18 years) after stroke.

INTERVENTION: Interventions to improve mobility (ie, walking).

RESULTS: 28 papers were included. The quality of reporting of the studies was 6.1 out of 11 points. Only 3 out of 26 studies (12%) progressed to a definitive RCT. Of those authors who replied, the main reason for not proceeding to an RCT was lack of funding.

CONCLUSION: The quality of reporting of pilot and feasibility studies still needs to improve, especially when describing the methods section. In addition, these studies should be designed a priori to provide transparency in reporting and enhance value in guiding future trials.Registration: 10.17605/OSF.IO/ENJ94.

articles.title: Morphological adaptations of cervical vertebrae in plunge-diving sulids.
articles.abstract: Foraging strategy frequently drives morphological diversification in birds. The plunge-diving behavior of certain species makes the functional and ecological trade-offs of variation in cervical vertebrae an especially intriguing question. This study compares cervical vertebrae across five plunge-diving species and two non-plunge-diving species, using morphometric analysis of micro-CT scans to test whether diving birds share specialized cervical vertebrae morphologies distinct from non-divers. Plunge-divers repeatedly experience extreme impact forces during headfirst water entry, requiring the neck to function as a shock-absorbing spring rather than a flexible manipulative system. To withstand these forces, plunge-divers exhibit reinforced cervical vertebrae-short, wide vertebrae with expanded joints and thickened arches. These features help distribute compressive and bending loads and reduce stress on the spinal column during impact. Gannets and boobies, the most extreme plunge divers, have an additional articulating surface on the dorsal arch of their anterior cervical vertebrae which limits flexion in the beginning of the neck further reinforcing against high loads. Additionally, we see that all plunge-diving sulids experience similar water impact durations and that the ratio between the radius of the head and the neck scales with impact velocity.

articles.title: Circulating Extracellular Matrix Biomarkers in the Detection of Carcinoid Heart Disease.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Carcinoid heart disease (CHD) is a severe fibrotic complication affecting cardiac valves in patients with neuroendocrine neoplasms (NEN). Early detection is crucial to improve prognosis. The value of the recommended screening biomarker, NT-proBNP, is uncertain. Biomarkers reflecting extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling may capture early fibrogenesis. We aimed to evaluate circulating ECM biomarkers for detection of CHD and to compare their performance with NT-proBNP.

DESIGN AND METHODS: In this cross-sectional study, we prospectively included patients with disseminated small intestinal NEN (siNEN). We performed transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) for CHD diagnosis, and blood samples were analyzed for 10 ECM biomarkers. Biomarker levels were compared between patients with and without CHD, and diagnostic performance was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristics (AUROC).

RESULTS: Among 98 patients, 16 (16%) had CHD. PRO-C3 levels were significantly elevated in patients with CHD compared with patients without CHD (median 19.3 ng/ml (IQR: 15.6-24.0) vs 14.3 ng/ml (IQR: 12.4-17.5), p = 0.002). The AUROC of PRO-C3 for CHD detection was 0.77 (95% CI: 0.64-0.90). At a cut-off level of 15.4 ng/ml, the sensitivity was 85 %, the specificity 56 %, the positive predictive value 27 %, and the negative predictive value 95 %. In the direct comparison between PRO-C3 and NT-proBNP, PRO-C3 did not outperform NT-proBNP (p = 0.09).

CONCLUSION: PRO-C3, reflecting collagen type III formation, demonstrated good performance in CHD detection and may represent a complementary or potentially earlier marker than NT-proBNP. However, the performance of PRO-C3 was insufficient as a stand-alone tool, and further evaluation and exploration of new biomarkers in larger cohorts is required.

articles.title: Meningeal inflammation and arachnoid barrier breakdown in a mouse model of neonatal bacterial meningitis.
articles.abstract: Newborns are especially susceptible to bacterial meningitis, primarily caused by group B Streptococcus (GBS), due to incomplete maturation of immune and barrier systems. While meningitis is well known to break down the blood-brain barrier, its effect on the meningeal arachnoid barrier remains poorly understood. Using a neonatal bacterial meningitis model, we demonstrate that GBS infection significantly increases arachnoid barrier permeability, disrupts tight junctions, and elevates meningeal production of proinflammatory cytokines. CD206+/LYVE-1+ border-associated macrophages undergo morphological and molecular activation post-infection, but their depletion prior to infection does not attenuate arachnoid barrier leakage or cytokine levels. We show that meningeal fibroblasts are a source of proinflammatory cytokines in response to GBS infection and that a systemic exposure of TNF-α alone is sufficient to induce barrier breakdown. These results support that the neonatal arachnoid barrier is vulnerable to cytokine-induced breakdown and highlight the role of non-immune meningeal cells like fibroblasts during bacterial infection.

articles.title: Nephrology Consultation Patterns and Clinical Outcomes in Hospitalized Patients with Heart Failure.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Kidney dysfunction frequently complicates heart failure hospitalization and is associated with adverse outcomes, complicating inpatient management. However, nephrology consultation practices in hospitalized patients with heart failure remain incompletely characterized.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of adults hospitalized with a primary diagnosis of heart failure at a tertiary care center in Puerto Rico between January 1, 2021, and December 31, 2023. Nephrology consultation patterns, including timing, were evaluated. Outcomes included in-hospital mortality, length of stay, and 90-day readmission. Descriptive and exploratory analyses were performed.

RESULTS: A total of 991 hospitalizations were analyzed. Mean age was 73 years, and 42% were female. Chronic kidney disease was present in 27% of patients, and acute kidney injury in 16%. Nephrology consultation occurred in 38% of hospitalizations, including 76% of patients with acute kidney injury and 73% with chronic kidney disease. Consultation rates were higher with increasing baseline serum creatinine, reaching 97% in patients with creatinine ≥3.0 mg/dL. Length of stay differed significantly across consultation groups (5.6, 8.3, and 12.2 days; P < 0.001). In-hospital mortality was 9%. Unadjusted mortality was higher among consulted patients (OR, 3.74; 95% CI, 2.48-5.90; P < 0.001). Exploratory adjusted analyses incorporating measured kidney-related variables were consistent with substantial confounding and should be interpreted cautiously because key measures of illness severity were unavailable. Ninety-day readmission occurred in 40% of hospitalizations and did not differ by consultation status.

CONCLUSIONS: Nephrology consultation occurred in fewer than half of hospitalizations and was more common in patients with advanced kidney dysfunction; however, a significant proportion of patients with acute kidney injury or chronic kidney disease did not receive consultation. These findings highlight variability in nephrology consultation practices and referral patterns in hospitalized patients with heart failure and kidney dysfunction.

articles.title: Real-World Diagnostic Coding and Biomarker Testing for CKD Across Diabetes, Hypertension, and Cancer: A Multisite OMOP Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The increasing prevalence of CKD necessitates standardized assessment of kidney function across various healthcare sites.1 Patients at risk, particularly those with diabetes, hypertension, or cancer, frequently do not receive recommended laboratory monitoring.2,3 This study assesses guideline recommended testing among various medical centers using the Observational Medical Outcomes Partnership (OMOP) common data model (CDM). The objectives are to report methodologies for extracting relevant measurements within OMOP and assess the frequency of specific biomarker evaluations and diagnosis codes in select cohorts.

METHODS: Retrospective cohort study of adult patients at 6 medical centers throughout the U.S. with a healthcare encounter to determine the frequency of diagnosis codes and biomarker measurements [eGFR, urine albumin-creatinine ratio (UACR), cystatin C, and aldosterone levels] among patients with relevant risk factors and probable CKD (sustained eGFR < 60 ml/min/1.73m2).

RESULTS: Among 9,212,799 patients with medical visits in 2024, 3% had a documented diagnosis of CKD, while 8% and 17% had a diagnosis of diabetes or hypertension, respectively. Also in 2024, only 47% of patients with probable CKD had a diagnosis code for CKD. Of the patients with diagnosed and probable CKD by eGFR, 25% had an UACR in 2024. Only 30% of patients with a diagnosis of diabetes, and 14% of patients with a diagnosis of hypertension had an UACR and eGFR in 2024. From 2021-2024, Cystatin C values were more common in patients with cancer compared to patients without cancer (1% vs 0.5%). The highest frequency of aldosterone testing (7%) was observed in patients with a diagnosis code for hypertension, serum potassium level <3 meq/L, eGFR> 60 ml/min/1.73m2, and albuminuria.

CONCLUSIONS: This study demonstrates low frequency of guideline-recommended kidney health assessments and CKD diagnosis across multiple U.S. medical centers, including albuminuria, cystatin C, and aldosterone testing.

articles.title: [Correlation between albuminuria and glycated haemoglobin in diabetic patients with an eGFR ≥ 60 mL/min/1.73 m²].
articles.abstract: Diabetic nephropathy is the leading cause of end-stage chronic kidney disease worldwide. Albuminuria, assessed by the urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio (ACR), is an independent marker of both renal prognosis and cardiovascular risk. To assess the correlation between HbA1c and ACR in diabetic patients with an eGFR ≥ 60 mL/min/1.73 m² and to determine the prevalence of pathological albuminuria in this population. A retrospective case-control study conducted from June 2023 to June 2026. Cases were diabetic patients (HbA1c ≥ 6.5%) and controls were non-diabetic subjects (HbA1c < 5.7%), all with an eGFR ≥ 60 mL/min/1.73 m² (KDIGO stages G1: ≥ 90 and G2: 60-89) and an available ACR measurement. Albuminuria was classified according to KDIGO as A1 (< 30 mg/g), A2 (30-300 mg/g) and A3 (> 300 mg/g). eGFR was calculated using the CKD-EPI 2021 equation. Statistical analysis used Spearman, Mann-Whitney and Chi² tests. Four hundred and twenty subjects were included: 232 diabetic patients and 188 non-diabetic controls. The prevalence of pathological albuminuria was significantly higher in diabetic patients than in controls (44.0% vs. 21.3%; p < 0.0001), as was the median ACR (23.5 vs. 9.0 mg/g; p < 0.0001). Within the diabetic group, no significant correlation was found between HbA1c and ACR (Spearman r = 0.016; p = 0.814). In contrast, ACR was significantly higher in stage G2 than in stage G1: 33.5 vs. 15,0 mg/g (p = 0.003), and increased with age (r = 0.169; p = 0.010). This study reveals a high prevalence of pathological albuminuria in diabetic patients with an eGFR ≥ 60 mL/min/1.73 m². Point HbA1c does not predict the degree of albuminuria, whereas eGFR stage and age are its main biological determinants. These findings support an integrated biological approach combining ACR and eGFR with HbA1c monitoring.

articles.title: Structured reporting of diagnostic hysteroscopy findings in women with reproductive disorders: an ESGE-ESHRE-IFFS international consensus†ǂ.
authors: International Hysteroscopy Working Group of ESGE, ESHRE and IFFS
articles.abstract:
STUDY QUESTION: How should the findings of diagnostic hysteroscopy in women with reproductive disorders be reported?

SUMMARY ANSWER: This collaborative document by the European Society for Gynaecological Endoscopy (ESGE), the ESHRE, and the International Federation of Fertility Societies (IFFS) provides the first detailed structured reporting template for diagnostic hysteroscopy findings in women with reproductive disorders.

WHAT IS KNOWN ALREADY: Despite its widespread use in women with reproductive disorders, no standardized framework currently exists for reporting of hysteroscopic findings. This lack of uniformity may limit the utility of the procedure and contribute to substantial heterogeneity among operators and centers. As a result, the reproducibility of hysteroscopy is limited, making it difficult to conduct robust studies that define its prognostic value in specific patient subgroups.

STUDY DESIGN, SIZE, DURATION: A dedicated working group from ESGE, ESHRE, and IFFS collaborated to develop a consensus for comprehensive structured reporting of diagnostic hysteroscopy findings in women with reproductive problems.

PARTICIPANTS/MATERIALS, SETTING, METHODS: This consensus paper focuses on grouping diagnostic hysteroscopic findings, structuring their reporting, and adopting standardized terminology for women with reproductive disorders. The virtual Nominal Group Technique, a structured consensus-building method, was adopted to ensure equal contribution from all members in the development of the final consensus.

MAIN RESULTS AND THE ROLE OF CHANCE: The document provides a structured reporting of hysteroscopic findings into five sections, each systematically capturing patient characteristics, procedural findings, and pathological observations as follows: patient's characteristics, and findings from the vagina, cervix, uterine cavity, endometrium, and tubal ostia.

LIMITATIONS, REASONS FOR CAUTION: The inclusion of a finding in this structured report is not a proof of its clinical significance, but it could be used as a validation tool for further research.

WIDER IMPLICATIONS OF THE FINDINGS: The standardized reporting of hysteroscopic findings promotes consistent data collection across centers and could help inform research and exchange of clinical experience, enhancing the value of hysteroscopy in fertility evaluation.

FUNDING: No external funding was received for the development of the consensus process or manuscript preparation.

DISCLOSURES: All authors declare that they have no competing interests.

TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: N/A.

articles.title: Characterizing sleep disturbances in developmental and epileptic encephalopathies through natural language processing: A retrospective monocentric study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Sleep disorders are frequent but undercharacterized comorbidities in developmental and epileptic encephalopathies (DEEs). We aimed to estimate the frequency, spectrum, and burden of sleep disturbances across genetic DEE subtypes using real-world data extracted from electronic health records (EHRs) through natural language processing (NLP).

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using Dr. Warehouse, an NLP-enabled clinical data warehouse, at a tertiary pediatric center. Data were extracted from January to April 2025. Patients with a group of defined DEEs were identified from narrative clinical notes and matched 1:2 with pediatric neurology patients without history of epilepsy by age, follow-up duration, and document volume. Predefined sleep-related terms were extracted from free-text reports. The proportion of patients with ≥1 documented mention during follow-up was used to estimate occurrence, alongside multivariable logistic regression analyses and a cumulative sleep burden score.

RESULTS: The final cohort included 884 patients with DEE and 1280 matched controls. At least one sleep-related disturbance was documented in 63.7% of DEE patients, significantly higher than in controls. The most frequent terms were "sleep disorder," "nocturnal seizures," and "night awakenings." Marked heterogeneity emerged across DEE subtypes; SYNGAP1-DEE showed the highest frequency of sleep disorders, Lennox-Gastaut syndrome was strongly associated with nocturnal seizures, and KCNT1- and PCDH19-DEE were more frequently associated with sleep apnea. DEE patients also exhibited a significantly higher cumulative burden of sleep disturbances compared with controls, with Lennox-Gastaut syndrome showing the greatest burden.

SIGNIFICANCE: NLP-based mining of unstructured EHR data enables large-scale characterization of sleep disorders in DEEs, revealing DEE subtype-specific sleep phenotypes. Routine and etiology-informed assessment of sleep disturbances should be integrated into the clinical management of DEEs.

articles.title: Association of BMAL1, CLOCK, and CRY1 gene polymorphisms with metabolic syndrome and glycemic phenotypes: a case-control study in a Turkish population.
articles.abstract: Metabolic syndrome (MetS) comprises cardiometabolic abnormalities that elevate the risk of type 2 diabetes and cardiovascular disease. Growing evidence links circadian rhythm disruption to obesity, diabetes, hypertension, and MetS. This study investigated functional polymorphisms in circadian rhythm-related genes and their associations with MetS and key clinical parameters. A total of 200 patients with MetS and 104 healthy controls were enrolled. Genotyping was performed using PCR-RFLP. Univariate and age-adjusted multivariable logistic regression analyses were conducted to evaluate independent genetic risk factors. The GC genotype of the CRY1 rs2287161 polymorphism was found to be significantly more frequent in the MetS group compared with healthy controls (p = 0.009). After adjusting for age in multivariable logistic regression, the CRY1 rs2287161 GC genotype remained a significant, independent factor for MetS (adjusted OR=0.381, 95%  CI: 0.175-0.831, p=0.015). No significant differences were observed between the MetS and control groups in terms of genotype distributions of BMAL1 rs7950226 and CLOCK rs1801260 (p > 0.05). Among MetS patients, individuals carrying the BMAL1 rs7950226 AA genotype exhibited significantly higher fasting plasma glucose levels compared with those carrying the GA and GG genotypes (p = 0.039). An altered distribution of the CRY1 rs2287161 polymorphism was observed in this Turkish cohort, with the GC genotype showing an age-independent statistical association with MetS risk. Additionally, BMAL1 rs7950226 variation modulates glycemic parameters within MetS patients, reinforcing the role of core circadian genes in metabolic regulation.

articles.title: The impact of chronic total occlusion percutaneous coronary intervention on the coronary physiology of the donor epicardial vessel: a case series.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In chronic total occlusion (CTO), donor vessels supplying collateral flow to the occluded artery may exhibit altered physiological indices, potentially influencing revascularization decisions. This case series evaluates the impact of successful CTO percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) on instantaneous wave-free ratio (iFR) measurements in donor vessels with moderate stenosis.

METHODS: We present a single-center case series (December 2020-September 2024) involving five patients with right coronary artery (RCA) CTO and a moderately diseased mid-left anterior descending artery (LAD) functioning as a collateral donor. All patients underwent ischemia testing and successful RCA CTO PCI. LAD iFR was measured before and after RCA revascularization.

RESULTS: Pre-PCI LAD iFR values ranged from 0.73 to 0.89, at or below the ischemic threshold. Post-RCA-PCI iFR improved in all cases (range: 0.87-0.96): in case 1, from 0.82 to 0.93; in case 2, from 0.82 to 0.89; in case 3, from 0.87 to 0.96; in case 4, from 0.73 to 0.87; and in case 5, from 0.89 to 0.96. In all cases, intervention on the LAD was deferred post-PCI, with no adverse clinical events during follow-up.

CONCLUSION: Successful RCA CTO PCI leads to immediate improvement in donor vessel iFR, suggesting that collateral demand may exaggerate ischemia. Staged physiologic assessment may improve decision-making in patients with moderate lesions in donor vessels.

articles.title: Precision Management After Childhood Acute Kidney Injury.
Plasma Phosphorylated Tau 217 Percentage by Race and Ethnicity in Preclinical Alzheimer Disease.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: In trials targeting preclinical Alzheimer disease (AD), defined as amyloid pathology without cognitive symptoms, racial and ethnic differences in plasma phosphorylated tau 217 percentage (%p-tau217) may influence screening eligibility.

OBJECTIVE: To characterize racial and ethnic differences in %p-tau217 and determine whether associations between %p-tau217, cognition, and amyloid positron emission tomography (PET) differ across groups.

DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This was a cross-sectional analysis of AHEAD 3-45 screening participants conducted from July 2020 to October 2024 at 106 sites across 4 world regions. Adults aged 55 to 80 years with %p-tau217 measured before medical and cognitive exclusions (N = 15 612) were included.

EXPOSURES: Self-reported race (Asian, Black, and White) and ethnicity (Hispanic and non-Hispanic) and apolipoprotein E ε4 (APOE ε4) carrier status.

MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: %p-tau217 levels and associations of %p-tau217 with Preclinical Alzheimer Cognitive Composite 5 (PACC5) score and amyloid PET were evaluated across racial and ethnic groups using multivariable linear regression.

RESULTS: Among 15 612 participants, the mean (SD) age was 68.4 (6.2) years; 9941 (63.7%) were female and 5755 (36.9%) were APOE ε4 carriers. %p-tau217 levels were lower among Asian, Black, and Hispanic participants than among White and non-Hispanic participants. APOE ε4 status was associated with higher %p-tau217 across all groups. The association between APOE ε4 status and %p-tau217 differed by race (APOE ε4 × race: F2,14 973 = 10.06; P < .001) and ethnicity (APOE ε4 × ethnicity: β, 0.042; 95% CI, 0.017 to 0.067; P = .005) (Asian: β, 0.05; 95% CI, 0.02 to 0.08; P = .01; Black: β, 0.05; 95% CI, 0.03 to 0.08; P = .002; Hispanic: β, 0.04; 95% CI, 0.02 to 0.07; P = .005). The %p-tau217-PACC5 association showed no pairwise differences across racial groups but differed by ethnicity (β, -0.53; 95% CI, -0.85 to -0.21; P = .008) and APOE ε4 × ethnicity (β, 0.78; 95% CI, 0.26 to 1.30; P = .02). The %p-tau217-PET association showed no significant pairwise differences across racial groups but differed by ethnicity (β, -6.30; 95% CI, -9.10 to -3.51; P < .001) and APOE ε4 × ethnicity (β, 7.12; 95% CI, 2.52 to 11.73; P = .01).

CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this cross-sectional study, plasma %p-tau217 varied across racial and ethnic groups. Consistent %p-tau217-PACC5 score and %p-tau217-PET associations across racial groups support plasma-based screening before PET confirmation, while ethnicity-related findings warrant further investigation.

articles.title: Precision Management After Childhood Acute Kidney Injury-Reply.
Heart Transplant for Advanced Heart Failure: A Review.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Heart failure affects more than 6 million US adults; approximately 4% to 5% progress to advanced disease despite optimal therapy. Heart transplant is a class I guideline-recommended therapy for select individuals with advanced heart failure.

OBSERVATIONS: Early referral for heart transplant is guided by the "I NEED HELP" mnemonic, a tool that identifies patients with advanced heart failure based on criteria such as use of inotropes, persistent symptoms (New York Heart Association class III or IV), end-organ dysfunction, left ventricular ejection fraction, defibrillator shocks, hospitalizations for heart failure, persistent edema or escalating use of diuretics, and low blood pressure. Each criterion is associated with higher risk of death or first heart failure hospitalization over a median follow-up of 260 days (adjusted hazard ratio, 1.19 [95% CI, 1.11-1.27] for each additional criterion). Typical absolute contraindications to heart transplant include active systemic infection, malignancy with limited life expectancy, severe and irreversible end-organ dysfunction (eg, cirrhosis, severe pulmonary hypertension), active substance use, major untreated psychiatric illness, inadequate social support, and severe frailty. Approximately 4600 heart transplants are performed annually in the US. The mortality rate was 8.5 deaths/100 patient-years for adults on the transplant waiting list in 2023. Leading causes of early death after transplant include primary graft dysfunction (39.5%), multiorgan failure (18.5%), and infection (13.9%). Among adults, contemporary survival rates after heart transplant are 91.5% at 1 year and 80.3% at 5 years. Lifelong maintenance immunosuppression typically combines a calcineurin inhibitor, antiproliferative agents (typically mycophenolate mofetil or azathioprine) and corticosteroids, with selective use of induction therapy (intensive immunosuppression immediately after transplant). Acute rejection requiring treatment occurs in 20% to 25% of recipients within a year, and may be treated with high-dose corticosteroids, antithymocyte globulin, and B-cell-targeted therapies (such as rituximab or bortezomib). Rejection surveillance with endomyocardial biopsies of the right ventricular septum is performed 5 to 10 times within the first year after transplant. Cardiac allograft vasculopathy (chronic rejection that causes diffuse coronary narrowing) affects 29% of heart transplant recipients within 5 years and 46.8% by 10 years and is the leading cause of late mortality. Cardiac allograft vasculopathy is treated with statins, mechanistic target of rapamycin inhibitors (such as sirolimus or everolimus), and retransplant for severe cases. Infections (62.5% are bacterial, 30.0% are viral, 6.7% are fungal, and 0.8% are parasitic) and malignancy (10.7% within 5 years after heart transplant) are other leading causes of late mortality.

CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Heart transplant is the definitive therapy for carefully selected patients with advanced heart failure despite receiving optimal, guideline-directed therapy. After heart transplant, lifelong multidisciplinary care is necessary to manage immunosuppression, prevent and treat rejection and cardiac allograft vasculopathy, and monitor for infection and malignancy.

articles.title: A Causal Inference Guided Analysis of Lung Transplant Outcomes Using Real-world Evidence from the SRTR Database.
articles.abstract: The increasing availability of real-world data (RWD) has allowed studies to use controls external to the clinical trial involving the actively treated patients. With RWD initiatives at the FDA and the recent FDA approval of several products utilizing RWD in the US, statistical methods have become an even more visible component in analyzing RWD for regulatory purposes. We reanalyzed Erdman et al. (2022) who evaluated immunosuppressive agents' performance using a retrospective cohort study to analyze transplant-related outcomes over time in adult lung transplant recipients in the Scientific Registry of Transplant Recipients (SRTR) using Cox models. We requested the data (n = 22,085) to be reanalyzed using causal inferences' potential outcome with propensity score (PS) matching, inverse probability weighting, and doubly robust estimation (DRE) for a composite endpoint of mortality or graft failure within a 3-year period from transplant. Results generally aligned with those of Erdman et al., although the magnitude of drug effects in some cohorts diminished considerably with PS matching and DRE as expected.

articles.title: Carotid stenosis reporting in Doppler ultrasound: why specifying NASCET or ECST criteria matters-an outpatient study.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Carotid artery stenosis represents a major risk factor for ischemic stroke, and Doppler ultrasound is widely used as the first-line imaging modality for its assessment. The degree of stenosis is commonly expressed as a percentage and can be calculated according to different methods, most notably the North American Symptomatic Carotid Endarterectomy Trial (NASCET) and the European Carotid Surgery Trial (ECST) criteria. However, in routine clinical practice, the classification system used to determine the percentage of stenosis is not always specified in the ultrasound report. These methods consider different reference diameters, making values non-comparable and potentially misleading for clinical decisions.

METHODS: In this study, we reviewed 1,400 patients evaluated in the Doppler ultrasound outpatient clinic of Internal Medicine at Poma Hospital, Mantova, Italy. All examinations were performed during routine clinical activity over four years by a physician tutor of the Italian Society of Medical and Biological Ultrasonology (SIUMB). The patient population included individuals aged between 18 and 97 years.

RESULTS: During follow-up evaluations, it was frequently observed that previous ultrasound reports indicated a percentage of carotid stenosis without specifying whether NASCET or ECST criteria had been used.

CONCLUSIONS: Our experience highlights the importance of clearly stating the classification system used for stenosis grading in carotid Doppler reports. Standardized reporting may improve longitudinal comparison of examinations, facilitate clinical decision-making, and enhance communication among healthcare professionals involved in the management of carotid artery disease.

articles.title: Dietary Determinants of Type 2 Diabetes Among African American Populations: A Scoping Review Through a Socio-Ecological Lens.
articles.journal: Journal of racial and ethnic health disparities
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Type 2 diabetes prevalence is 1.4-fold higher among Black/African American adults than the general U.S.

POPULATION: African Americans are also disproportionately represented among lower-income groups with reduced access to healthy food retail, factors closely tied to the dietary exposures examined here. Dietary patterns emerge from multilevel influences, including food environments, cultural practices, and structural determinants. This scoping review, organized using the socio-ecological model (SEM), synthesized dietary determinants of type 2 diabetes across five SEM levels specifically for African American populations.

METHODS: We searched PubMed/MEDLINE, CINAHL, and PsycINFO through January 2025 for studies examining diet-related exposures (sugar-sweetened beverages, ultra-processed foods, food environments, cultural practices, structural determinants) and diabetes outcomes in Black/African American populations. Given the heterogeneity of evidence types, methods followed PRISMA-ScR. Quality was assessed using adapted Johns Hopkins criteria, and narrative synthesis organized findings across SEM levels.

RESULTS: Fourteen empirical studies, supplemented by 3 reviews/meta-analyses and 3 conceptual papers, revealed a possible intervention gradient: individual-level dietary changes showed modest associations (2-10% risk reduction with SSB substitution), while community-level food environment exposures showed larger associations (34% higher diabetes incidence with unfavorable food store density; HR = 1.34, 95% CI: 1.12-1.60). Ultra-processed food consumption was linked to 17% higher diabetes risk per 10% intake increase, though not in an African American-specific sample. One qualitative study suggested cultural food practices may create management barriers. Structural racism and residential segregation were conceptually linked to "food apartheid. Evidence concentrated at individual (n = 6) and community (n = 7) levels, with no organizational-level research identified.

CONCLUSIONS: Community-level interventions may offer more immediate, near-term impact relative to structural reforms, which may support longer-term equity gains; given the limited evidence base, this apparent gradient should be considered a preliminary, hypothesis-generating pattern rather than an established comparison of intervention effectiveness, and warrants further investigation.

articles.title: Emergency physicians' knowledge and practice in reporting medically unfit drivers in Atlantic Canada.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Emergency physicians frequently encounter patients with medical conditions affecting their fitness to drive. Emergency physicians have legal and ethical duties to report medically unfit drivers. However, many report low confidence in making these decisions. This may lead to underreporting. We aimed to assess knowledge, practice, and barriers regarding reporting of unfit drivers by Atlantic Canadian emergency physicians.

METHODS: We conducted a cross-sectional survey of emergency physicians from four Atlantic Provinces. The survey contained 62 questions across four categories: 1) Demographics (seven), 2) General knowledge (five), 3) Scenarios/practice (34), 4) Barriers/needs (16). Where appropriate, participants rated answers on a five-point Likert scale.

RESULTS: Seventy-eight emergency physicians (response rate 20.6%) completed the survey: male (59.0%), age 35-44 (37.2%), formally trained in emergency medicine (74.7%). Overall, 88.5% lacked formal training to determine fitness to drive. Familiarity was low regarding provincial regulations (61.5% "slightly" or "somewhat" familiar) and the Canadian Medical Association Driver's guide (85.9% "not at all" to "somewhat" familiar) while most (80.8%) use clinical judgment to guide decisions. Half indicated they report (56.4%) and document (50.0%) unfit drivers only "sometimes" or less frequently. When presented with clinical scenarios where reporting is indicated (first seizure, recurrent seizure), most (100% and 96.2%) would advise the patients not to drive, but a third (33.4% and 37.2%) would either not report or leave it to another physician to do so. Lack of guideline knowledge was the most significant barrier to reporting, while pocket cards, an electronic app and electronic method to report were identified as enablers. Most emergency physicians (85.9%) would like formal education on this topic.

CONCLUSIONS: Atlantic Canadian emergency physicians expressed low familiarity with guidelines for determining medical fitness to drive and disclosed potential underreporting. Efforts should focus on targeted education and streamlined tools to improve reporting and enhance road safety.

articles.title: Insular involvement and atrial fibrillation first detected after ischemic stroke: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.journal: Clinical autonomic research : official journal of the Clinical Autonomic Research Society
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: The association between insular involvement identified on brain imaging and atrial fibrillation first detected after ischemic stroke remains uncertain. We evaluated this association and summarized prespecified neurocardiac outcomes.

METHODS: Seven databases were searched through April 5, 2026; six were searched from inception, and Wanfang Data was searched from January 2000. Eligible studies enrolled adults with ischemic stroke, assessed insular involvement on brain imaging, and reported atrial fibrillation or another prespecified neurocardiac outcome. Atrial fibrillation first detected after stroke was defined as atrial fibrillation identified after the index stroke in patients without previously known atrial fibrillation. Random-effects meta-analysis was performed when at least three studies were sufficiently comparable.

RESULTS: Thirty-one studies were included; only three provided comparable adjusted estimates for the primary meta-analysis, totaling 2164 participants. Insular involvement was associated with higher odds of atrial fibrillation first detected after stroke (odds ratio 3.35, 95% confidence interval 2.30-4.89; P < 0.001). An exploratory analysis of overall atrial fibrillation excluding one atrial flutter event yielded an odds ratio of 1.51 (95% confidence interval 0.99-2.32; P = 0.056). Other outcomes were summarized descriptively.

CONCLUSION: Across three observational studies, insular involvement identified on brain imaging was associated with atrial fibrillation first detected after ischemic stroke. Previously undetected paroxysmal atrial fibrillation may have preceded the stroke, leaving the temporal direction uncertain. These findings are hypothesis-generating and are insufficient to support the use of lesion location to select rhythm monitoring strategies or guide anticoagulation decisions.

articles.title: Off-label Use of U-500 Regular Insulin with a Tubeless Automated Insulin Delivery System in Type 1 Diabetes and Severe Insulin Resistance: A Case Report.
articles.journal: Diabetes therapy : research, treatment and education of diabetes and related disorders
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: U-500 regular insulin (U-500R) can overcome reservoir-capacity constraints in people with severe insulin resistance, but its delayed and prolonged action is poorly matched to automated insulin delivery (AID) algorithms developed for rapid-acting U-100 insulin analogs. Experience in type 1 diabetes (T1D) is particularly limited.

METHODS: We report the off-label transition to Omnipod 5 AID while continuing U-500R in a 46-year-old man with autoimmune T1D, obesity, severe insulin resistance, impaired hypoglycemia awareness (Gold score 6), and frequent isolated overnight work. Before transition, he was receiving approximately 245 units/day of U-500R through an Omnipod DASH patch pump. Initial adaptations included a 6-h active insulin duration, higher overnight glucose targets, semi-quantitative meal announcements, and proactive use of activity mode.

RESULTS: Before AID initiation, continuous glucose monitoring showed a mean glucose of 137 mg/dl, glucose management indicator of 6.6%, time in range of 75%, and time below range of 9%. After 12 months, time in range increased to 79.1% and time below range decreased to 5.7%, with 0.4% below 54 mg/dl. Automated mode was active for more than 95% of the time. The patient reported substantially fewer symptomatic hypoglycemic episodes, although occasional hypoglycemia persisted during overnight shifts.

CONCLUSIONS: Carefully supervised use of U-500R in an AID system may preserve patch-pump therapy and reduce hypoglycemia exposure in selected people with T1D and very high insulin requirements. This off-label approach requires explicit dose-conversion procedures, conservative individualized settings, close follow-up, and recognition that residual hypoglycemia risk remains.

articles.title: The Bidirectional Relationship Between Diabetes and Cancer: Mechanistic Insights, Epigenetic Intermediaries, and Therapeutic Approaches.
articles.journal: Diabetes therapy : research, treatment and education of diabetes and related disorders
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: The global rise in diabetes mellitus parallels an increasing cancer burden, highlighting an incompletely understood relationship between these two complex diseases. Accumulating epidemiological evidence indicates that diabetes is associated with an increased incidence and mortality of several site-specific cancers, whereas cancer and its treatment may contribute to dysglycemia and diabetes through diverse mechanisms. In addition, shared metabolic and environmental risk factors further contribute to the observed association between these conditions.

METHODOLOGY: This narrative review comprehensively examined peer-reviewed literature retrieved from PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar, focusing on the epidemiological, mechanistic, and epigenetic links between diabetes and cancer.

RESULTS: Beyond shared lifestyle risk factors, converging molecular mechanisms-including chronic hyperglycemia, insulin resistance, low-grade inflammation, oxidative stress, and metabolic reprogramming-provide a biological framework linking diabetes and cancer. Emerging evidence suggests that epigenetic dysregulation acts as a central intermediary in this relationship by integrating metabolic stress with sustained alterations in gene expression through DNA methylation, histone modifications, non-coding RNAs, chromatin remodeling, and epigenetic aging. Diabetes-related epigenetic memory, microbiome-driven epigenetic modulation, and sex-specific epigenetic signatures may further contribute to cancer susceptibility and disease heterogeneity, although the strength of evidence varies across experimental and clinical studies.

CONCLUSIONS: This review synthesizes current epidemiological, mechanistic, and epigenetic evidence linking diabetes and cancer, with particular emphasis on metabolic-epigenetic crosstalk and clinically relevant signaling pathways. It also critically evaluates the dual metabolic and oncologic effects of antidiabetic and anticancer therapies while highlighting current evidence gaps and the need for precision medicine approaches in the prevention and management of both diseases.

articles.title: Complicated Urinary Tract Infections Caused by Fluoroquinolone-Non-Susceptible/Trimethoprim-Sulfamethoxazole-Resistant Extended-Spectrum β-Lactamase-Producing Enterobacterales: Patient Characteristics, Resistance Phenotypes, Treatment Patterns, and Clinical Outcomes.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Patients with complicated urinary tract infections (cUTIs) caused by extended-spectrum β-lactamase (ESBL)-producing Enterobacterales (ESBL-E) not susceptible (NS) to fluoroquinolones (FQ-NS) or resistant (R) to trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (TMP/SMX-R) have few effective oral treatment options.

METHODS: Data from the Optum de-identified Electronic Health Record data set (Optum EHR) (January 2018-September 2023) were used. The primary objective was to describe cumulative incidence of treatment failure (TF) by care setting (hospital versus non-hospital) within 30 days of the initiation of the latest intravenous antibiotic treatment prescribed ± 7 days from the microbiology results (index).

RESULTS: Among 7388 eligible patients, mean (standard deviation) age was 65.6 (17.7) years, and 66.3% were female. Most patients (5211, 70.5%) had a cUTI with a complicating factor; 3415 (46.2%) were diagnosed in hospital. Among the 7902 ESBL-E isolates from eligible patients with cUTIs, Escherichia coli was the predominant pathogen (75.1%), followed by Klebsiella pneumoniae (13.4%). Overall, 6384 (81.7%) isolates were FQ-NS, 5323 (68.0%) TMP/SMX-R, and 170 (2.2%) carbapenem-NS. Kaplan-Meier estimates revealed that the cumulative incidence of TF by day 30 post-index was 27.5% among hospitalized patients and 25.2% among non-hospitalized, with variation by resistance profile, driven primarily by receipt of another antibiotic (both settings). Most patients (5013, 67.9%) were prescribed an intravenous antibiotic at index, often carbapenems (2157, 43.0%), but treatment sequences were heterogeneous. Recurrence occurred in 2116 patients (28.6%), hospitalization (among those not hospitalized at index) in 975 (24.5%), and readmission in 663 (19.4%).

CONCLUSIONS: These data indicate a substantial burden of cUTIs caused by ESBL-E that were FQ-NS or TMP/SMX-R, characterized by high rates of treatment failures and hospitalization for IV antibiotic treatment.

articles.title: Multi-omics analyses based identification of therapeutic targets for rapid kidney function decline and chronic kidney disease, a mendelian randomization study.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Rapid kidney function decline and chronic kidney disease (CKD) remain significant threats to global health. Currently, there are no effective therapeutic agents capable of reversing progression of CKD. A two-stage Mendelian randomization (MR) study was conducted to uncover causal therapeutic mechanisms of pQTLs during kidney function decline.

METHODS: Exposure data comprised 4,853 distinct proteins and their corresponding protein quantitative trait loci (pQTLs, p < 5×10-8) sourced from 7 large-scale proteomic datasets. Kidney function decline outcomes of 1,201,909 participants and 337,109 participants were collected as the outcome in the discovery stage and validation stage, respectively. Additionally, single cell sequencing analyses from 64,276 mice cells served as an independent cohort to explore the expression level of these potential therapeutic targets in kidney. Protein-protein and protein-drug association analysis were performed in the STITCH database, with supplementary drug-related data extracted from DrugBank database to explore potential therapeutic options.

RESULTS: A total of 37 proteins (p < 1.03×10-5) were associated with impaired kidney function, among which 7 proteins (IGFBP4, CLMP, FGF5, ANGPTL7, LRRN1, DMKN and CHST11) were validated. Lower IGFBP4 expression level was observed during the rapid kidney function decline in mice. Besides, dbcAMP and pioglitazone emerged as candidate agents with the potential to act through IGFBP4 and CLMP in rapid decline and CKD.

CONCLUSION: IGFBP4 and CLMP represent promising therapeutic targets for rapid kidney function decline and CKD. Further investigation is warranted to elucidate the underlying mechanisms and validate their functional roles through larger cohort studies.

articles.title: Molecular Detection and Genetic Characterization of Colpodella spp. DNA in Human Fecal and Tick Samples from Hebei Province, China.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Colpodella spp., a group of predatory protists closely related to the phylum Apicomplexa, are primarily known as free-living organisms associated with aquatic and terrestrial ecosystems. Although Colpodella-related DNA has increasingly been detected in vertebrate-associated samples, its distribution and ecological significance remain poorly understood. This study aimed to investigate the occurrence, molecular characteristics, and genetic diversity of Colpodella spp. DNA detected in human fecal samples and Haemaphysalis longicornis ticks from Hebei Province, China.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: A total of 2,448 human fecal samples and 215 tick samples were collected from Hebei Province, China. The presence of Colpodella spp. DNA was investigated using PCR targeting the 18S rRNA gene, followed by sequencing, phylogenetic analysis, and genetic diversity assessment based on partial Colpodella spp. 18S rRNA sequences.

RESULTS: Colpodella spp. DNA was detected in 136 human fecal samples and 11 tick samples, with detection rates of 5.56% and 5.12%, respectively. Sanger sequencing successfully detected high-quality 18S rRNA sequences from all PCR-positive samples. Because identical sequences were detected among tick-derived samples, one representative sequence derived from H. longicornis ticks and 21 representative human-derived sequence types were selected for downstream analyses. Phylogenetic analysis based on 22 representative sequences showed that the sequences obtained in this study clustered within previously reported Colpodella spp. lineages. Genetic diversity analysis identified 3 haplotypes among the analyzed sequences.

CONCLUSIONS: This study provides molecular evidence for the occurrence and genetic variation of Colpodella spp. DNA in human fecal and tick-associated samples from Hebei Province, China. However, PCR-based detection alone cannot determine active infection, colonization, pathogenicity, or biological activity of the detected organisms. Further studies using additional molecular markers, culture systems, and biological approaches are required to clarify the ecological and potential health significance of Colpodella spp.

articles.title: Pregnancy-related disorders: molecular mechanisms and management.
articles.abstract: Pregnancy-related disorders (PRDs), including preeclampsia (PE), gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM), hyperemesis gravidarum (HG), and intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy (ICP), remain major causes of maternal and perinatal morbidity. This review synthesizes their molecular, endocrine, immune, and clinical features. We propose the Placental-Maternal Adaptation Failure Continuum (PMAFC), in which gestational/fetoplacental stress load interacts with maternal adaptive reserve. This load includes placenta-derived signals, the physiological demands of gestation and fetal growth, and secondary maternal or fetal mediators. Placental drive denotes the placenta-derived component, whereas maternal adaptive reserve reflects the capacity of vascular, metabolic, hepatic, neuroendocrine, and immune systems to compensate for pregnancy-related challenges. We distinguish experimentally derived mechanistic hypotheses from findings supported by human studies and consider persistent post-pregnancy changes, termed pregnancy memory, as a potential link to later maternal cardiometabolic risk. We also separate established care from investigational biomarkers and interventions. The soluble fms-like tyrosine kinase-1/placental growth factor (sFlt-1/PlGF) ratio can support clinical assessment in selected PE pathways. Cell-free RNA, chromosome 19 microRNA cluster biomarkers, and polygenic risk scores remain investigational. Apheresis has limited human proof-of-concept evidence, whereas sFlt-1 silencing, growth differentiation factor 15 receptor blockade, and strategies to restore hepatobiliary transporter function remain under clinical or preclinical evaluation. PMAFC is an evidence-organizing framework, not a validated predictive or therapeutic algorithm.

articles.title: Occurrence of blaNDM-5 and blaNDM-29 variants and genetic diversity among Enterobacterales in hospitalized patients in northeastern Brazil : Variability of bla NDM in Enterobacterales.
articles.journal: Brazilian journal of microbiology : [publication of the Brazilian Society for Microbiology]
articles.abstract: This study investigated the genetic diversity and occurrence of blaNDM variants associated with carbapenem resistance in Enterobacterales obtained from colonization (rectal swabs) and infection sites in patients hospitalized in a public hospital in northeastern Brazil. A total of 58 multidrug-resistant clinical isolates were analyzed using ERIC-PCR to assess clonal relatedness, and PCR followed by amplicon sequencing to detect resistance genes (blaNDM, blaKPC, blaGES, blaVIM, and blaIMP). Klebsiella pneumoniae was the most frequently identified species (n = 28, 48.27%), followed by Serratia marcescens and Proteus mirabilis, among others. All seven P. mirabilis isolates were classified as XDR, as were six K. pneumoniae and three S. marcescens isolates. Amikacin (n = 46, 79.31% susceptible) and colistin (n = 37, 97.37% susceptible) exhibited the highest susceptibility rates among all antimicrobials tested against the majority of isolates. ERIC-PCR revealed multiclonal dissemination and high genetic variability among the isolates. The blaKPC gene was the most prevalent (n = 32, 55.17%), followed by blaNDM (n = 26, 44.83%). Among the blaNDM allelic variants, blaNDM-1 (n = 12, 46.15%) was the most common, followed by blaNDM-5 (n = 7, 26.92%) and blaNDM-29 (n = 1, 3.85%). This study reports the first detection in Brazil of blaNDM-5 in Klebsiella aerogenes, Citrobacter freundii, and Escherichia coli, in addition to reporting the first identification of blaNDM-29 in K. pneumoniae. Additionally, this study gives the first report in the Americas of blaNDM in Klebsiella ozaenae. These findings highlight the substantial potential for mutation and interspecies dissemination of blaNDM variants within the Enterobacterales order.

articles.title: Suppressor with morphogenetic effect on genitalia 7 (SMG7) drives hepatocellular carcinoma progression through context-dependent nonsense-mediated decay (NMD) dysregulation.
articles.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is a major risk factor for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), yet the molecular mechanisms linking metabolic stress to tumor progression remain poorly defined. RNA surveillance pathways, including nonsense-mediated decay (NMD), may represent a relevant but unexplored regulatory layer in this context. In this study, we analyzed the expression of NMD components across multiple human HCC and MASLD cohorts, identifying suppressor with morphogenetic effect on genitalia 7 (SMG7) as a key regulator of NMD associated with HCC progression. In vitro functional assays, NMD target expression, transcriptomic profiling, and weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) were used to identify downstream pathways and mediators. More than 40% of NMD components were dysregulated in HCC. Among them, SMG7 was consistently upregulated across HCC and MASLD cohorts, induced by lipotoxic stress, and identified as a hub gene in HCC transcriptional networks. SMG7 overexpression promoted proliferation, migration, and clonogenicity, whereas its silencing reduced tumor aggressiveness in a context-dependent manner inversely associated with UPF1 levels. Combined depletion of SMG7 and UPF1 suppressed aggressive traits in vitro and limited tumor growth in vivo. Transcriptomic and network analyses identified Z-DNA-binding protein 1 (ZBP1) as a downstream mediator of SMG7 dysregulation in SNU-387 HCC cells, a finding further supported by functional rescue experiments. These results identify the SMG7-ZBP1 axis as a metabolic stress-responsive pathway linking NMD dysfunction to liver tumor progression and highlight NMD modulation as a therapeutic strategy to restrain tumor aggressiveness while enhancing tumor immunogenicity.

articles.title: Prevalence of herpesvirus, polyomavirus, and respiratory viruses in saliva from a Quilombola community in the Brazilian Amazon.
articles.journal: Brazilian journal of microbiology : [publication of the Brazilian Society for Microbiology]
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Quilombola communities, composed of descendants of enslaved individuals from Brazil's colonial period, often face limited access to healthcare, which may increase their susceptibility to viral infections. Oral transmission routes, particularly through saliva, are relevant for viruses such as those in the Polyomaviridae family. Therefore, here we aimed to investigate the prevalence of HSV-1, JC (JCV), and BK polyomaviruses, and respiratory viruses (Influenza A/B, RSV, SARS-CoV-2), as well as the salivary inflammatory profile in individuals from a Quilombola community.

METHODS: A cross-sectional study was conducted in the Quilombola community of Mangabeira, Pará, Brazil. Unstimulated saliva samples were collected from 100 individuals. Oral health was assessed, and nucleic acids were analyzed using real-time PCR (JCPyV, BKPyV, HSV-1) and multiplex TaqMan PCR (RSV, Influenza A/B, SARS-CoV-2). Cytokines (IL-6, IFN-γ, TNF-α, IL-10) were quantified.

RESULTS: BKPyV was detected in 19%, while HSV-1 and SARS-CoV-2 were found in 3% each. No cases of JCPyV, RSV, or Influenza were detected. BKPyV infection was associated with elevated IFN-γ (p < 0.01). SARS-CoV-2 and HSV-1 infections were linked to pro-inflammatory cytokine profiles. No association was found between viral detection and tooth loss or the use of prosthesis.

CONCLUSION: A high prevalence of BKPyV and a salivary pro-inflammatory response were observed, highlighting potential oral health vulnerabilities in this underserved population.

articles.title: Toxic Metals and Metalloids Exposure and the Gut-Cardiometabolic Axis: A Narrative Review of Microbiome Dysbiosis, Gut Barrier Dysfunction, and Metabolic Inflammation.
articles.abstract: Toxic elements and metalloids exposure is an important environmental contributor to cardiometabolic disease, yet the gut-mediated mechanisms linking toxic elements to systemic metabolic and vascular injury remain incompletely understood. Lead, cadmium, arsenic, and mercury can enter the gastrointestinal tract through contaminated food, water, dust, smoking, seafood, and occupational sources, allowing direct interaction with the intestinal lumen, epithelial barrier, immune system, and gut microbiome. This narrative review examines the gut-cardiometabolic axis as a mechanistic framework connecting toxic metal exposure to microbiome dysbiosis, barrier dysfunction, endotoxemia, microbial metabolite imbalance, and chronic metabolic inflammation. Available evidence, derived from human, animal, and in-vitro studies of varying quality, suggests that toxic elements may alter microbial diversity and function, affect tight-junction integrity, and increase intestinal permeability; however, a consistent metal-specific signature and a complete causal chain have not been established. These changes may promote lipopolysaccharide passage through the intestinal barrier, activate innate immune pathways, and maintain systemic inflammatory signaling. At the same time, disruption of microbial metabolite profiles, including lower short-chain fatty acid production and altered trimethylamine N-oxide, bile acid and uremic toxin pathways, may promote insulin resistance, dyslipidemia, endothelial dysfunction, hypertension, atherosclerosis and overall cardiometabolic vulnerability. Viewing toxic-metal exposure through the gut-cardiometabolic axis provides a hypothesis-generating framework for integrating exposure reduction with conventional cardiometabolic risk management; the clinical value of microbiome-targeted strategies remains to be established. Longitudinal and multi-omics studies are still needed to define causal relationships and identify populations at greatest susceptibility.

articles.title: Comparative study of antibiotic resistance and virulence profiles of exoU and exoS Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolates from urinary tract infections and microbial keratitis in Bangladesh and India.
articles.abstract: Pseudomonas aeruginosa is an important opportunistic pathogen in urinary tract infections (UTIs) and microbial keratitis (MK), but differences in resistance and virulence between exoU and exoS P. aeruginosa isolates across regions and infection sites remain poorly understood. This study compared antibiotic resistance and virulence profiles of exoU and exoS P. aeruginosa isolates from Bangladeshi and Indian UTIs, and from Indian UTIs and MK collections. A total of 23 Bangladeshi UTI isolates were analyzed by broth microdilution for susceptibility to ciprofloxacin, levofloxacin, gentamicin, and tobramycin, and by whole-genome sequencing (WGS) to identify resistance-associated mutations, acquired resistance genes, and virulence factors. These WGS data were compared with 15 publicly available Indian UTI genomes, while the Indian UTI genomes were compared with 19 publicly available Indian MK genomes. In the Bangladeshi UTI cohort, exoU isolates showed greater resistance to fluoroquinolones and aminoglycosides than exoS isolates. Comparative analysis of Bangladeshi versus Indian UTI isolates and Indian UTI versus MK isolates showed that exoU isolates carried a burden of resistance mutations, including enrichment of GyrA Thr83Ile, ParE Asp533Glu, MexR Val126Glu, MexB Ser1041Glu, and MexC Ala262Glu. Aminoglycoside-associated substitutions FusA2 Gln161Leu and ParR Leu153Arg and Ser170Asn were more common in exoU UTI isolates. Acquired resistance genes showed aac(6')-II and aac(3)-Id were linked to Bangladeshi UTI, rmtF associated with Indian UTI, and crpP confined to MK exoU isolates. Virulence profiling showed exoU enrichment in pldA, pvdY, and csrA, whereas exoS was associated with pilC, pilV, pilW, pilY2, and pilA. Collectively, these results indicate that exoU and exoS isolates differ in both their resistance and virulence profiles, while also showing evidence of geographic and infection-site-specific adaptation.

articles.title: Gut microbiota dysbiosis in patients with sepsis: a meta-analysis of microbial diversity and taxonomic abundance.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Gut microbiota alterations are frequently reported in sepsis, but their magnitude, consistency, and clinical specificity remain uncertain. We evaluated microbial diversity and taxonomic abundance in patients with sepsis, distinguishing healthy/reference controls from nonseptic clinical comparators.

METHODS: PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, and Web of Science Core Collection were searched from inception to 20 September 2026, without language or geographic restrictions, supplemented by targeted retrieval of primary studies and supplementary data. Comparative human observational studies were included. Standardized mean differences (Hedges g) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were pooled using random-effects models. Healthy/reference and nonseptic clinical controls were analyzed separately. Subgroup and sensitivity analyses were performed to explore heterogeneity and assess the stability of pooled estimates. Small-study effect tests and meta-regression were restricted to outcomes with sufficient studies.

RESULTS: Twenty-three studies comprising 1201 participants were included. Compared with healthy/reference controls, patients with sepsis had lower Shannon diversity (20 studies; g = - 1.12, 95% CI - 1.38 to - 0.85; I² = 59.9%) and lower Firmicutes abundance (g = - 0.78, 95% CI - 1.32 to - 0.24), but higher Proteobacteria (g = 0.96, 95% CI 0.67 to 1.25) and Enterococcus abundance (g = 0.68, 95% CI 0.38 to 0.98).
