These associations remained statistically significant after correction for multiple comparisons. Estimates for the remaining outcomes were less consistent or imprecise. The reduction in Shannon diversity was smaller against nonseptic clinical controls (eight studies; g = - 0.29, 95% CI - 0.54 to - 0.05) and was not statistically significant after multiplicity correction.

CONCLUSIONS: Sepsis was associated with reduced gut microbial diversity and alterations in selected bacterial taxa, most consistently in comparisons with healthy/reference controls. Clinical heterogeneity and incomplete control of antibiotic exposure and illness severity limit attribution of these changes to sepsis itself. Prospective studies are needed to establish their prognostic and therapeutic relevance.

articles.title: Co-occurrence of viral respiratory pathogens: prevalence, seasonal distribution, and symptomatology in outpatients in Bavaria, Germany, from April 2025 - March 2026.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: The Bavarian Influenza Sentinel (BIS + C) monitors the circulation of respiratory viruses in outpatients in Bavaria, Germany. After the Covid-19 pandemic, the molecular surveillance program was expanded for improved insight into the rate of viral infections. Only limited information on viral co-infections is yet available, so this study provides an insight into their co-occurrence, seasonal distribution, and symptomatic outcome.

METHODS: From calendar week 15/2025 to 14/2026, general practitioners and pediatricians collected swab samples from outpatients with acute respiratory diseases, that were tested for twelve viral pathogens using qPCR multiplex systems.

RESULTS: At least one virus was found in 58.8% of the outpatients (n = 7,416/12,614) including 4.1% (n = 520) multiple viral detection, primarily in patients younger than 5 years and more frequent in males. The frequency of multiple virus detection ranges from 6.7% in influenza A (n = 118/1,761) to 43.3% in adenoviruses (n = 154/356) positive tested samples. The most common pathogens in multiple detections were entero-/rhinoviruses involved in 11.9% (n = 292/2,459). Differences in the reported symptoms between single- and co-infections have been found, including less muscle/joint pain in influenza A co-infections. The detected Ct values in co-infections compared to mono-infections were lower for SARS-CoV-2, adenoviruses, entero-/rhinoviruses, and coronaviruses.

CONCLUSION: The frequency of multi-infections follows the seasonality of the corresponding viruses. Especially children under 5 years of age are affected by co-infections. Among the studied viruses, influenza A showed the lowest relative rate of co-detection, in line with its pronounced seasonality - a pattern that warrants further investigation.

articles.title: Healthcare pathways and outpatient management prior to community-acquired sepsis hospitalization in Germany, 2016-2019.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Sepsis often presents with non-specific symptoms that delay diagnosis and treatment. This study characterized pre-hospital outpatient and emergency care among patients with community-acquired sepsis (CAS) in Germany prior to hospitalization.

METHODS: This population-based observational cohort study used de-identified health claims data from over 340,000 AOK-insured adults admitted to hospital between 2016 and 2019 with an ICD-10-GM code for sepsis plus organ dysfunction, with each patient contributing only their first qualifying hospitalization (index case). Patients without ICD-10-GM codes for and suggestive of nosocomial infection were included and their healthcare utilization in the week before admission was categorized into: hospital emergency care (HEC), outpatient care only (OC), or no healthcare utilization (no HCU) (excluding patients exclusively hospitalized in the week prior sepsis hospitalization). Treatment and patient characteristics, sepsis features, and outcomes as documented in health claims data were compared across groups using descriptive and non-parametric statistics.

RESULTS: Among 238,247 patients identified with CAS, 12.7% received HEC, 61.8% OC, and 25.5% had no HCU. HEC patients were younger, more severely ill, with higher ICU admission and mortality rates compared to the other groups. In the OC group, most patients (82.3%) had encounters with general practitioners, and 45.1% received OC on the day of admission. The last infection-related encounter occurred on average 2.0 days (SD 2.3) prior to sepsis hospitalization. Among OC patients, 48.7% underwent infection-related laboratory diagnostics, and 11.4% received anti-infective prescriptions.

CONCLUSION: Most patients with CAS had healthcare contact in the week prior to hospitalization, predominantly in outpatient care. The frequent encounters shortly before admission and low rates of anti-infective prescription may suggest opportunities for earlier recognition and better risk stratification, e.g. by strengthening sepsis awareness and diagnostic strategies in outpatient settings.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: The study was pre-registered in the German Clinical Trials Register (DRKS00031302) on 05/05/2023.

articles.title: Real-World Adherence to Dihydropyridine Calcium-Channel Blockers: A Pharmacoepidemiologic Study.
articles.journal: High blood pressure & cardiovascular prevention : the official journal of the Italian Society of Hypertension
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Low medication adherence contributes to uncontrolled cardiovascular (CV) risk.

AIMS: This study investigated 12- and 24-month adherence, all-cause mortality and CV events in subjects receiving originator or generic dihydropyridine calcium-channel blockers (CCBs) as recorded in administrative databases from Local Health Units across several Italian regions.

METHODS: We retrospectively analysed databases containing demographics and vital status, drug prescriptions, and hospital discharge diagnoses for more than 6 million individuals. Subjects receiving lercanidipine originator, generic lercanidipine, amlodipine originator, or generic amlodipine were included. Subjects with prior or occasional CCB use, inadequate follow-up time, chronic ischaemic heart disease or acute pulmonary heart disease, or switching between CCBs were excluded. Adherence was defined as a Proportion of Days Covered ≥ 80% at 12 and 24 months. Cox regression models estimated the association between treatments and a composite of all-cause mortality and CV events.

RESULTS: Adherence was assessed in 3,860 propensity-score-matched subjects (965/group), selected from 14,849 eligible subjects. Lercanidipine originator was associated with higher (p < 0.001) 12-month (43%) and 24-month (38%) adherence than generic lercanidipine (31 and 26%) and amlodipine originator (22 and 19%). The events analysis included 15,808 subjects. Compared with originator lercanidipine, originator amlodipine, generic lercanidipine and generic amlodipine were associated with 43%, 30% and 33% higher hazards of the composite outcome, respectively (corresponding 95% Confidence Intervals: 1.28-1.60, 1.10-1.55, 1.17-1.50).

CONCLUSIONS: Medium-term adherence was low across all treatments. Originator lercanidipine was associated with the highest adherence, with lower adjusted hazards of the composite outcome and all-cause mortality compared to the other treatments.

articles.title: Successful endoscopic retrieval of a plastic gallbladder stent that had completely migrated into the gallbladder.
articles.abstract: Endoscopic gallbladder stenting is a useful transpapillary drainage technique for acute cholecystitis, especially in patients who are poor candidates for cholecystectomy or percutaneous gallbladder drainage. However, long-term placement may cause late adverse events, including migration. Complete migration of a gallbladder stent into the gallbladder is rare and may make retrieval challenging. A 77-year-old woman was referred to our hospital with epigastric pain. Imaging studies suggested biliary tract inflammation with gallbladder debris and bile duct dilatation, but no gallstones or common bile duct stones. Because her condition showed insufficient improvement with antibiotics, a transpapillary biliary stent and a transpapillary gallbladder stent were placed endoscopically. Her symptoms and laboratory data improved after stenting. One year later, the distal end of the gallbladder stent had migrated from the duodenum into the common bile duct. Fifteen months after treatment, the stent had completely migrated into the gallbladder. Because symptoms of biliary infection had improved and there was no indication for cholecystectomy, endoscopic retrieval was attempted. After cystic duct cannulation, bile aspiration was performed to reduce gallbladder volume. A guidewire was placed as a safety wire, and an EndoSheather was advanced into the gallbladder. The migrated stent was grasped with biopsy forceps through the sheath and gently withdrawn into the duodenum before removal through the endoscope channel. No complications occurred. Endoscopic retrieval through the cystic duct may be feasible for a gallbladder stent that has completely migrated into the gallbladder when careful wire access, bile aspiration, safety-wire placement, and sheath-assisted forceps manipulation are used.

articles.title: Plastic-algae interactions in freshwater and marine systems: mechanisms, evidence and prospects for bioremediation.
articles.abstract: Plastic pollution is among this century's defining environmental problems, and aquatic systems carry a disproportionate share. As polymers fragment into microplastics and nanoplastics they disperse through rivers, lakes and oceans, harming organisms and entering food webs. Algae have attracted growing attention as a biological complement to physical and chemical clean-up. This review synthesises peer-reviewed studies published between 2015 and 2026 on interactions between plastics and freshwater and marine algae. We examine eukaryotic microalgae from freshwater (Chlorella, Scenedesmus, Coccomyxa, Uronema) and marine systems (Navicula, Phaeodactylum, Skeletonema, Dunaliella); cyanobacteria (Phormidium, Oscillatoria, Anabaena, Nostoc, Arthrospira), treated separately as prokaryotes; and the macroalga Sargassum. Reported outcomes range widely from a few percent of low-density polyethylene surface-altered by cyanobacteria, to roughly a quarter of mixed-polymer film attributed to Coccomyxa, and up to ~ 27% of high-density polyethylene by a freshwater epiplastic consortium, along with many studies that document surface colonisation, hetero-aggregation and physiological stress rather than complete breakdown. We explain the mechanisms involved: extracellular enzymes proposed to cleave polymer chains, the extracellular polymeric substances that anchor cells to plastic, reactive-oxygen-driven oxidation and the staged formation of the plastisphere. The supporting evidence is graded from gene prediction to demonstration by a purified enzyme. Most outcomes prove to be physical capture or surface modification, and no study reviewed demonstrates mineralisation. We assess engineered diatoms and green algae expressing bacterial PET hydrolases and identify what field application would require: synthetic consortia, omics-based enzyme mining, photobioreactor integration, machine-learning-guided enzyme design, and standardised protocols focused on mineralisation.

articles.title: Spatiotemporal variation of PM₂.₅ and its relationship with vegetation cover and meteorological factors during spring (2016-2022) in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia.
articles.abstract: Fine particulate matter (PM₂.₅) is among the most critical environmental pollutants in Saudi Arabia, especially in the capital city of Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. This study investigates the seasonal and spatial variability of PM₂.₅ concentrations and evaluates the influence of key climatic parameters (wind speed, temperature, and relative humidity) during the spring season from 2016 to 2022. Data were collected from 16 monitoring stations and analyzed using descriptive statistics, correlation analysis, and GIS-based spatial distribution mapping. The assessment also considered the role of vegetation cover (Fractional Vegetation Cover - FVC) in mitigating air pollution across the city. The results showed clear variation in PM₂.₅ levels, with the highest seasonal average in 2018 (94.6 µg/m3) and the lowest in 2020 (55.0 µg/m3). Spatial patterns showed elevated concentrations mainly in southern and central Riyadh. PM₂.₅ concentrations showed a moderate positive association with temperature and weak negative associations with relative humidity and wind speed, although these meteorological relationships were not statistically significant. The relationship between FVC and PM₂.₅ varied among years; a statistically significant inverse correlation was observed only in 2016 (Spearman's ρ = - 0.539, p = 0.031, n = 16), whereas the correlations in the remaining years were weak and statistically non-significant. These findings indicate that vegetation may contribute locally to particle interception and deposition, but its influence on PM₂.₅ was not consistent throughout the study period. Overall, the results emphasize the combined influence of meteorological conditions, dust activity, and anthropogenic sources on air quality in Riyadh and support integrated monitoring and urban air-quality management.

articles.title: Partial Splenectomy as a Definitive or Interim Solution for Young Children with Transfusion-dependent Hemolytic Anemia: Long-term Results from a 15-Year Cohort.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the long-term efficacy and safety of partial splenectomy (PS) as a definitive or interim spleen-preserving strategy in young children with transfusion-dependent congenital hemolytic anemia (HA).

METHODS: Patients with congenital HA who required frequent blood transfusions and underwent PS at the present center between 2010 and 2025 were included. The hemoglobin (Hb) level, reticulocyte count, and the need for transfusions (if any) during the follow-up period were noted. Ultrasonography of the splenic remnant was obtained at baseline, 1 mo, and 18 mo following the PS.

RESULTS: Fourteen children (median age: 23 mo; range: 7-40) underwent PS by laparotomy (n = 12) or laparoscopy (n = 2). Median follow-up after PS was 9 y (IQR: 4.8-10.5). Following PS, 8/14 (57%) patients became transfusion-free, with a median Hb of 10.3 g/dL at last follow-up. Five (36%) patients continued to require occasional transfusions and subsequently underwent total splenectomy after a median of 3 y; All of them became transfusion-free thereafter. No episode of mortality, sepsis, or thrombosis occurred.

CONCLUSIONS: PS may serve as a definitive procedure in selected young children with congenital hemolytic anemia and as a bridge to later total splenectomy in others. This approach may be particularly relevant in resource-limited settings, where blood availability, transfusion safety, and the risk of transfusion-transmitted infections are concerning.

articles.title: Artificial Intelligence in Prediction and Diagnosis of Fetal Growth Restriction: A Systematic Review.
articles.abstract: This systematic review evaluates evidence on artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) models for prediction and diagnosis of fetal growth restriction (FGR). The authors searched PubMed, Scopus, Embase, Web of Science, and Google Scholar, through June 2026 following PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Studies on AI/ML-based prediction or diagnosis techniques for FGR, Intrauterine growth restriction (IUGR) or Small for gestational age (SGA) fetuses. The prediction model risk of bias assessment Tool (PROBAST) was used to perform data extraction and risk of bias assessment. Twenty-seven studies were eligible for inclusion. AI applications were biophysical (n = 10), Doppler-based (n = 10), clinical (n = 7), ultrasound (n = 7), MRI (n = 7), radiomics imaging (n = 10), cardiotocography (n = 10), genomics (n = 10), and metabolomics-based biomarker models (n = 10). The model performance was good, with area under the receiver operating characteristic curves (AUC) of 0.71-0.91 and classification accuracies of 78.9-93.3%. Imaging and multimodal data-based models showed the highest predictive performance. The PROBAST assessment showed that the risk of bias was low for the participant, predictor and outcome domains, but the analytical domain raised methodological concerns; nine studies were low risk, 14 moderate and 4 high. The AI and ML models for FGR detection performed promisingly. Multimodal approaches that combine clinical, imaging and molecular data consistently outperform single modality models and constitute a major advance in precision obstetrics. However, there remains substantial heterogeneity, limited external validation and methodological issues. Future prospective multicenter studies, standardized reporting, and real-world implementation research are needed for routine clinical adoption.

articles.title: The effect of preload on Doppler systolic time in a large emergency department cohort with suspected sepsis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Change in the corrected flow time of the common carotid artery (ccFTΔ) during a preload challenge (PC) is a surrogate for stroke volume change (SVΔ) to infer preload responsiveness (PR).

METHODS: This is a retrospective cohort study comprising patients with suspected sepsis in a large, publicly funded, academic emergency department; no patient health information is linked to the Doppler assessments. Carotid Doppler spectrograms from a wireless, wearable critical care Doppler ultrasound system are analyzed for ccFTΔ during a PC (either infusion of 300 mL of crystalloid over 3 min or a Trendelenburg maneuver). The primary objectives of this study are to describe the proportion of PR patients by previously described ccFTΔ thresholds (i.e., both 4 and 7 ms ccFTΔ ), describe time-to-peak (TTP) ccFTΔ, and evaluate the ability of baseline ccFT to detect ccFTΔ during PC, using both the equations of Wodey and Bazett. Comparisons of related outcomes were adjusted for multiple comparisons using the Holm procedure, baseline ccFT discrimination was quantified using area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, and TTP was estimated using patient-level bootstrap resampling. Threshold-agnostic ccFTΔ trajectories were additionally explored using unsupervised k-means clustering of patient-level temporal responses for both correction equations.

RESULTS: A PC was attempted in 4367 patients and an adequate ccFTΔ was collected from 4,128 patients (95%). In total, 982,937 Doppler cardiac cycles are included. The median ccFTΔ was 7.3 milliseconds (ms). 51.9% of patients had a ccFTΔ ≥ 7 ms, while 68.6% had a ccFTΔ ≥ 4 ms by the equation of Wodey. For Bazett, these fractions were 61.2% and 73.5%, respectively. For patients identified as PR based upon either a 4 ms or 7 ms ccFTΔ threshold, the time-to-peak ccFTΔ was 27.5 s for both equations. Baseline absolute ccFT did not discriminate PR from PUR patients under both correction formulae (AUROC 0.56-0.57).

CONCLUSIONS: To our knowledge this is the largest reported dataset of ED patients with suspected sepsis receiving PR assessments by Doppler ultrasound, comprising nearly 1 million Doppler cardiac cycles obtained from over 4100 ED patients. Both 7 ms and 4 ms ccFTΔ thresholds described clinically-accepted rates of PR. The TTP was roughly 30 s into PC and baseline ccFT did not accurately detect ccFTΔ during PC. Finally, a hypothesis-generating analysis identified four distinct ccFTΔ trajectories during PC which may represent unique preload response patterns during PR testing.

articles.title: Five-Year Outcomes of Sleeve Gastrectomy with Transit Bipartition in Women with Severe Obesity and Insulin-Treated Type 2 Diabetes: A Prospective Single-Center Cohort Study of 35 Women.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Five-year data on metabolic durability, nutritional outcomes, and late morbidity after sleeve gastrectomy with transit bipartition (SG + TB) remain limited. We evaluated glycemic, weight, nutritional, and safety outcomes in women with severe obesity and insulin-treated type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM).

METHODS: This prospective single-center follow-up included 35 women who underwent laparoscopic SG + TB in 2016-2017. At 5 years, 30/35 (85.7%) retained SG + TB anatomy and had complete efficacy data; weight and HbA1c were available in one additional revised patient (31/35, 88.6%). T2DM remission was defined as HbA1c < 6.5% at least 3 months after stopping glucose-lowering pharmacotherapy. Nutritional assessment used a prespecified limited biochemical panel.

RESULTS: In the 30-patient anatomy-retained complete-case cohort, mean HbA1c decreased from 9.2 ± 1.0% to 5.5 ± 0.7%, body weight from 118.0 ± 10.6 to 75.6 ± 6.8 kg, and mean total weight loss was 35.7 ± 5.1%. Medication-free T2DM remission was 23/30 (76.7%; 95% CI, 59.1-88.2%); the conservative all-enrolled estimate was 23/35 (65.7%; 95% CI, 49.2-79.2%). At year 5, hypoalbuminemia was 20.0%, low serum iron 30.0%, vitamin B12 deficiency 13.3%, and vitamin D deficiency 73.3%; 27/30 (90.0%) had at least one predefined biochemical abnormality. Two patients required an SG + TB-related invasive intervention, including one revision; two additional patients underwent laparoscopic cholecystectomy.

CONCLUSION: SG + TB was associated with substantial 5-year weight loss and glycemic improvement, but the lower all-enrolled remission estimate highlights attrition and revision-related exclusion. Biochemical abnormalities and clinically important gastrointestinal morbidity show that preserved duodenal continuity does not eliminate potential hypoabsorptive consequences. Lifelong metabolic and nutritional surveillance is warranted.

articles.title: Postoperative acute kidney injury associated with cast nephropathy and marked renal interstitial plasma cell infiltration in multiple myeloma: a case report.
articles.abstract: Multiple myeloma (MM) is frequently associated with renal impairment, most commonly due to cast nephropathy. We report a case of severe and persistent postoperative acute kidney injury (AKI) in an 84-year-old man with smoldering MM who underwent posterior lumbar fixation for a lumbar burst fracture. Twelve hours after surgery, he developed profound hypotension and severe anemia due to surgical-site bleeding, followed by progressive renal dysfunction despite prompt transfusion and fluid resuscitation. Urinalysis revealed heavy proteinuria, and kidney biopsy demonstrated marked accumulation of eosinophilic casts within the tubules, consistent with cast nephropathy. In addition, marked renal interstitial infiltration by λ light-chain-restricted monoclonal plasma cells and focal peritubular capillary (PTC) occlusion were observed. Congo red staining was negative, and no significant glomerular immune deposits were detected. Renal function partially improved with supportive care but did not return to the preoperative baseline. This case suggests that postoperative AKI in MM may be multifactorial, with perioperative circulatory failure precipitating clinically overt cast nephropathy, while coexisting interstitial myeloma cell infiltration and focal PTC occlusion may increase susceptibility to ischemic injury and contribute to the severity and persistence of renal dysfunction. In patients with MM, latent myeloma-related kidney injury should be considered a potential contributor to perioperative AKI even when serum creatinine is preserved, particularly in those with marked proteinuria or elevated free light chain levels.

articles.title: Pituitary adenomas (PitNETs): molecular pathophysiology, targeted drug delivery strategies and clinical therapeutic outcomes.
articles.abstract: Pituitary neuroendocrine tumors (PitNETs), historically referred to as pituitary adenomas, comprise a heterogeneous group of neuroendocrine tumors with diverse hormonal phenotypes, molecular characteristics, and clinical behavior. Their management includes surgery, pharmacological therapy, radiotherapy, and, in selected refractory cases, systemic or molecularly targeted approaches. Advances in molecular endocrinology have identified recurrent alterations and dysregulated signaling networks, including GNAS, USP8, PI3K/AKT/mTOR, and MAPK-associated pathways, that contribute to the biological heterogeneity of PitNETs. This review summarizes the molecular mechanisms underlying PitNET development and examines established pharmacological therapies, including dopamine agonists, somatostatin receptor ligands, growth hormone receptor antagonists, and temozolomide, with emphasis on their mechanisms and clinical evidence. Emerging molecularly targeted approaches, including mTOR inhibition, EGFR-associated targeting, anti-angiogenic therapy, and immune checkpoint inhibition, are discussed according to their current level of experimental and clinical evidence. The review also evaluates advanced drug-delivery strategies relevant to pituitary disease, including intranasal delivery, nanoparticle-based systems, liposomal carriers, receptor-targeted platforms, and sustained-release formulations. Particular attention is given to the distinction between clinically established delivery technologies and approaches that remain experimental or are supported primarily by evidence extrapolated from other therapeutic areas. Clinical trial evidence is further summarized to contextualize the efficacy, limitations, and translational status of current and emerging therapies. Together, these perspectives highlight the opportunities and remaining challenges in developing more precise pharmacological and drug-delivery strategies for the management of PitNETs.

articles.title: A Curcumin-Based Turn-on Fluorescent Probe for Superoxide Anion in Living Cells.
articles.abstract: Superoxide (O2•-) plays a pivotal role in diverse physiological and pathological processes, a thorough understanding of its molecular mechanisms relies on dependable detection techniques. In this study, we designed and synthesized DFCD, a novel curcumin-based fluorescent probe with a switching mechanism, for the highly selective and sensitive detection of O2•-. By employing diphenylphosphinyl chloride as the reactive group, DFCD operates through a photoinduced electron transfer (PET) mechanism and exhibits significant fluorescence enhancement at 574 nm upon reaction with superoxide anion. The probe demonstrates a detection limit of 0.11 µM, excellent selectivity over competing reactive species and ions, good stability at physiological pH, and minimal cytotoxicity. Live-cell imaging confirms that DFCD is capable of monitoring endogenous superoxide anion dynamics in HeLa cells under various stimuli. Furthermore, DFCD proves highly effective for imaging macrophage inflammatory responses, providing a robust tool for studying superoxide-driven oxidative stress in inflammatory models. Collectively, these findings establish DFCD as a valuable imaging probe for studying superoxide-related oxidative stress at the cellular level.

articles.title: Cardiorenal Protective Glucose-Lowering Treatment Patterns in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus Based on a Real-World Study: A Clinical Phenotype Cluster Analysis.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Cardiorenal protective glucose-lowering treatments (CPT), consisting of sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors (SGLT2is) and glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs), are widely applied in clinical management of patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). This study aimed to identify distinct clinical phenotypes linked to CPT prescribing patterns and construct a multilevel correlation framework for standardized CPT clinical application.

METHODS: Data were extracted from the baseline dataset of an observational registry cohort study across 61 medical centers between 2023 and 2024. Based on multiple factors, clinical phenotypes of patients were identified via the Partitioning Around Medoids (PAM) clustering algorithm, CPT utilization was compared across different phenotypes.

RESULTS: A total of 9000 patients with T2DM were enrolled [median age 55 (46, 63) years, 60.8% male and 39.2% female, median diabetes duration 5.37 (0.85, 11.44) years]. Three clinically distinct phenotypes were identified: Cluster 1 [older patients with high atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) risk], Cluster 2 (metabolically stable patients without cardiorenal risk), and Cluster 3 (younger patients with obesity, high metabolic risk and short diabetes duration). The CPT utilization rates of the three clusters were 49.0%, 44.1% and 51.1%, respectively (P < 0.001), with Cluster 3 having the highest rate. Cluster 2 was dominated by SGLT2is monotherapy (73.1%). Cluster 3 showed a marked preference for GLP-1RAs-based regimens (43.6% in total), whereas Cluster 1 had an intermediate proportion of GLP-1RAs-related regimens (31.5%).

CONCLUSION: Three clinical phenotypes were identified via cluster analysis. The younger obese group with high metabolic risk had the highest CPT utilization rate and preferred GLP-1RAs, while the older group with high ASCVD risk was predominantly treated with SGLT2is alone.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: The trial was registered with https://www.chictr.org.cn/ under registration number ChiCTR230007376 on 20 July 2023.

articles.title: Economic Evaluations of Hearing Interventions in Older Adults: A Systematic Review of Evidence and Methods.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Age-related hearing loss is common among older adults and is associated with poorer quality of life, falls, cognitive and psychosocial consequences, and increased healthcare use. Hearing aids, cochlear implants and rehabilitation services may improve outcomes, but their economic value remains unclear. This systematic review assessed cost-effectiveness and cost-benefit evidence for hearing interventions in older adults and examined methods, assumptions and outcome measures used in the evaluations.

METHODS: Medline, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science and EconLit were searched from inception to August 2026 for trial- or model-based full economic evaluations of hearing interventions in adults ≥ 60 years. Eligible studies included cost-effectiveness analyses (CEAs), cost-utility analyses (CUAs), and cost-benefit analyses (CBAs). Costs were standardised to 2024 US dollars. Quality was assessed using CHEQUE for CEAs and the Drummond checklist for CBAs.

RESULTS: A total of 27 studies in 28 articles met the inclusion criteria, of which 22 studies reported CEAs, including 19 CUAs, and 6 CBAs; 1 study reported both a CUA and a CBA. CEAs generally found cochlear implants and hearing aids to be cost-effective compared with no intervention, and cochlear implants were often cost-effective compared with hearing aids in eligible populations. Post-hearing-aid counselling or rehabilitation, transcutaneous bone conduction devices and cochlear implant processor upgrades were generally cost-effective. CBAs indicated positive net monetary benefits. Health-related quality of life was most commonly measured using the Health Utilities Index Mark 3. Costs typically included device, procedure and physician-visit costs. Key drivers included utility gains, intervention costs, age at intervention and device compliance. Limitations included omission of downstream costs, limited carer and societal impacts, inconsistent preference-based outcome measurement, insufficient model validation, limited equity analysis and no evaluations in institutional and long-term care.

CONCLUSIONS: Hearing interventions, particularly hearing aids and cochlear implants, appear to offer good economic value for older adults. Future evaluations should capture broader benefits, downstream costs, carer and long-term care impacts, and use transparent, standardised methods.

articles.title: Duration-related regional patterns of gray matter alterations in hypertension and their cognitive implications.
articles.abstract: Hypertension is a major modifiable vascular risk factor for cognitive decline. However, how regional gray matter (GM) alterations differ according to hypertension duration remains incompletely understood. We hypothesized that different brain regions would exhibit heterogeneous GMV profiles across hypertension-duration groups and that regional GMV alterations would be associated with cognitive performance. Structural MRI and cognitive data were obtained from 487 participants with hypertension and 165 normotensive controls. Participants with hypertension were stratified by disease duration (≤ 4, 5-11, and ≥ 12 years). Voxel-based morphometric analysis was used to identify whole-brain GMV alterations across groups. Regional associations with hypertension duration and cognitive performance were subsequently examined, adjusting for age, sex, total intracranial volume, and, where appropriate, education. Regression models further assessed whether GMV-cognition associations differed across hypertension-duration groups. Three cross-sectional duration-related GMV patterns were identified: early and relatively stable alterations, duration-sensitive alterations, and intermediate-to-long-duration alterations. Longer hypertension duration was associated with lower GMV in the right rectus, left middle temporal, and left angular gyri, and higher GMV in the bilateral putamen and right insula after FDR correction. Only greater left thalamic GMV remained associated with higher MoCA scores after correction. Interaction analyses suggested duration-group differences in GMV-cognition associations in the right insula and right precuneus. Hypertension was associated with heterogeneous, region-specific GMV alteration across duration groups rather than a uniform cumulative atrophy pattern. The direction and cognitive relevance of these alterations varied across regions, highlighting the importance of considering hypertension duration when evaluating brain structural alterations. Longitudinal studies are needed to clarify their temporal evolution.

articles.title: Delayed eculizumab therapy guided by markedly elevated soluble C5b-9 in a child with dialysis-requiring acute poststreptococcal glomerulonephritis: a case report.
articles.abstract: Eculizumab, a monoclonal antibody targeting complement C5, has been shown to be effective when administered within 2-4 days of disease onset in children with severe acute poststreptococcal glomerulonephritis (APSGN). However, since APSGN typically follows a self-limited clinical course in most patients, the optimal timing and latest feasible time window for eculizumab initiation in APSGN remain undefined. A 9-year-old girl presented with gross haematuria, oliguria, and renal dysfunction 9 days after the onset of vomiting and abdominal pain. Laboratory tests showed a positive anti-streptolysin O titre, decreased serum complement C3 levels, massive proteinuria, and stage 3 acute kidney injury. Following high-dose methylprednisolone and continuous renal replacement therapy, her serum C3 levels recovered to normal range, yet oliguria and renal impairment persisted two weeks after disease onset. Since serum complement membrane attack complex (C5b-9) remained substantially elevated, eculizumab was initiated at a delayed time point compared with previous reports, yielding a rapid improvement in renal function. Kidney biopsy performed post-treatment with eculizumab revealed focal proliferative glomerulonephritis, accompanied by acute tubular injury. At the 6-month follow-up, except for haematuria detected by dipstick urinalysis, the patient had normal renal function, serum complement C3 levels and negative urinary protein. No severe adverse events occurred. We present a case of APSGN with persistent renal dysfunction and excessive complement activation 2 weeks after glucocorticoid therapy, who achieved substantial clinical remission upon eculizumab administration. Our observation suggests eculizumab may be an effective rescue intervention for persistent renal dysfunction in severe APSGN driven by excessive complement activation.

articles.title: Phase-adaptive automated whole-liver quantification of signal intensity-derived liver indices from gadoxetic acid-enhanced MRI.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To develop and validate a phase-adaptive pipeline for automated whole-liver, parenchyma-based quantification of signal intensity-derived liver indices from gadoxetic acid-enhanced MRI without inter-phase co-registration.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this retrospective, single-center study (2016-2025), 9,013 liver MRI examinations were screened, and 3,112 gadoxetic acid-enhanced MRI examinations were identified. The first examination per patient defined the clinical cohort (1,174 patients; mean age, 59.6 ± 14 years [range, 4-93 years]; 611 men). A phase-adaptive nnU-Net was trained on 403 and tested on 500 dynamic contrast-enhanced MRI sequences for segmentation of liver parenchyma, intrahepatic non-parenchymal structures, and spleen; paraspinal muscle reference regions were obtained using TotalSegmentator. Segmentation accuracy was assessed against manually corrected reference segmentations generated by a semi-automatic annotation workflow with Dice similarity coefficients. Automated arterial enhancement fraction (AEF), relative liver enhancement (RLE), hepatocellular uptake index (HUI), liver-to-spleen ratio (LSR), and liver-to-muscle ratio (LMR) were compared with manual region-of-interest measurements in a radiological validation cohort (50 patients) using intraclass correlation coefficients and Bland-Altman analysis. Liver indices were compared between patients with cirrhotic and non-cirrhotic livers using the Mann-Whitney U-test.

RESULTS: Liver parenchyma segmentation achieved Dice similarity coefficients of 0.998-0.999. Reader-model agreement for the liver indices ranged from 0.936 to 0.977. HUI, LSR, RLE, and LMR were lower in cirrhosis (p < 0.001), whereas AEF did not differ (p = 0.14).

CONCLUSION: Phase-adaptive segmentation enables whole-liver quantification of signal intensity-derived liver indices without inter-phase co-registration. The lower hepatobiliary uptake indices in cirrhosis support the plausibility of this approach for scalable quantitative assessment of liver MRI.

KEY POINTS: Question Can gadoxetic acid-enhanced liver MRI be quantified automatically across contrast phases without inter-phase co-registration or manual region-of-interest placement in routine clinical imaging? Findings Phase-adaptive segmentation enabled automated whole-liver quantification with liver Dice coefficients of 0.998-0.999 and excellent agreement with manual measurements for five liver indices. Relevance Statement Automated whole-liver quantification from standard gadoxetic acid-enhanced liver MRI provides reproducible, signal-intensity-derived liver indices and reduces dependence on manual region-of-interest measurements in large-scale clinical studies.

articles.title: Characteristics and correlation analysis of CDFI in contralateral healthy eye in patients with CRAO.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To investigate hemodynamic changes in the ophthalmic artery(OA) and central retinal artery(CRA) of contralateral healthy eyes in patients with central retinal artery occlusion (CRAO) and their correlation with the affected eye.

METHODS: This study included 36 patients with CRAO(affected eye group), 32 healthy contralateral eyes(healthy eye group), and 34 healthy volunteers(control group). All participants underwent comprehensive ophthalmic examinations, including best-corrected visual acuity(BCVA, converted to LogMAR for analysis), slit-lamp microscopy, indirect ophthalmoscopy, intraocular pressure measurement, and color Doppler flow imaging (CDFI). Patients with CRAO also underwent fundus fluorescein angiography(FFA) within 3 days of presentation.

RESULTS: Compared to the control group, the systolic peak velocity(Oamax) of the OA was decreased in the affected eyes but increased in the contralateral healthy eyes. The systolic peak velocity(CRAmax) of the CRA was significantly reduced in both the affected and contralateral healthy eyes compared to controls. Correlation analysis revealed significant positive correlations between various OA and CRA flow parameters(e.g.,,OAmax,OAPI,CRAmax,CRAPI,in the healthy eye and their corresponding affected eyes. Conversely, the central retinal artery pulsatility index(CRAPI) in healthy eyes was negatively correlated with the CRA minimum velocity(CRAmin) in affected eyes. Furthermore, in the contralateral healthy eye,CRAmax showed a positive correlation with the time from symptom onset to examination.

CONCLUSION: Blood flow in the contralateral healthy eyes of patients is altered and showed significant correlations with the hemodynamic parameters of the affected eyes, suggesting that these so-called "healthy" eyes may be affected by a CRAO event and could potentially have pre-existing subclinical abnormalities.

articles.title: Levels of electromagnetic radiation from telecommunication towers in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania: implications for public exposure and regulatory compliance.
articles.abstract: The rapid expansion of telecommunication infrastructure has intensified public concerns regarding exposure to radiofrequency electromagnetic fields (RF-EMFs). This study evaluates electromagnetic field (EMF) levels and power densities emitted by telecommunication towers in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania, and benchmarks them against international exposure standards. A cross-sectional design was employed involving 40 base transceiver stations. Electric field strength measurements were conducted using a calibrated Narda SRM-3006 frequency-selective radiation meter, while power density was computed using standardized propagation models. Statistical analyses were performed using SPSS (v23), including descriptive statistics, correlation analysis, and independent t-tests. The mean EMF and power density were 1.654 ± 0.457 V/m and 0.0073 W/m2, respectively. No significant correlation was observed between field-measured EMF values and regulatory data (r = 0.031, p = 0.788), suggesting methodological and temporal discrepancies. All measured values were substantially below the ICNIRP exposure limits. However, comparison with more stringent national thresholds indicates potential long-term precautionary concerns. These findings advance the understanding of RF-EMF exposure and underscore the need for future research to prioritize emerging communication technologies, network densification, and evolving urban environments, where meaningful variations in exposure are more likely to occur, rather than routinely replicating measurements under comparable conditions.

articles.title: Dietary polyphenols in atherosclerosis: a review of molecular mechanisms, endothelial dysfunction, oxidative stress, and vascular inflammation.
articles.abstract: Atherosclerosis is a chronic inflammatory disease characterized by endothelial dysfunction, oxidative stress, lipid accumulation, and vascular inflammation, leading to cardiovascular events such as myocardial infarction and stroke. Increasing evidence suggests that dietary polyphenols may offer cardioprotective benefits by targeting key molecular pathways involved in atherogenesis. This narrative review summarizes current evidence on the mechanisms and therapeutic potential of dietary polyphenols in the prevention and management of atherosclerosis. Published experimental, clinical, and epidemiological studies were evaluated to assess the effects of antioxidants and dietary polyphenols on atherosclerosis. Evidence indicates that polyphenols, including resveratrol, quercetin, catechins, curcumin, and anthocyanins, influence redox homeostasis and LDL oxidation while modulating molecular signaling pathways involved in inflammation, lipid metabolism, endothelial function, and cellular stress responses. These compounds also modulate inflammatory signaling pathways, particularly nuclear factor-kappa B (NF-κB) and MAPK, reducing the expression of adhesion molecules and pro-inflammatory cytokines. Clinical studies and meta-analyses suggest potential improvements in endothelial function, lipid profiles, blood pressure, and inflammatory biomarkers following polyphenol-rich dietary interventions, although findings remain heterogeneous and are largely based on surrogate outcomes. Emerging nano-delivery systems and gut microbiota-targeted approaches may improve polyphenol bioavailability and therapeutic potential, but their clinical efficacy remains to be established. Overall, antioxidants and dietary polyphenols may provide complementary approaches for cardiovascular risk reduction; however, their clinical efficacy in atherosclerosis management remains uncertain. Further well-designed, long-term clinical studies are needed to clarify their therapeutic relevance, optimal dosing, and safety.

articles.title: Oxidized mitochondrial DNA as a potential biomarker and mechanistic driver of autophagy-mitophagy dysregulation in pulmonary arterial hypertension: a narrative review.
articles.abstract: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) is recognized as a mitochondria-centered disease characterized by early bioenergetic and redox abnormalities that influence pulmonary vascular remodeling. Oxidized mitochondrial DNA (Ox-mtDNA), which combines mitochondrial stress with innate immune activation and dysregulated Ca2+ signaling to sustain hyperproliferation and apoptosis resistance in pulmonary arterial endothelial and smooth muscle cells, is a persistent danger signal rather than just a result of mitochondrial injury. Vasodilator therapy targeting the prostacyclin, nitric oxide, and endothelin pathways has made great strides, yet many patients still make progress. These treatments primarily enhance hemodynamics and vasomotor tone, but they do not directly reverse the cellular and molecular mechanisms that sustain pulmonary vascular remodeling. In this model, inflammatory signaling and mitochondrial redox imbalance are mutually reinforcing rather than strictly sequential: oxidative stress produces Ox-mtDNA, which mediates inflammatory activation, and cytokine and interferon signaling from the inflammatory process further weakens antioxidant defenses and mitochondrial respiration, increasing reactive oxygen species (ROS) output. Because Ox-mtDNA's synthesis, escape, sensing, and clearance all influence inflammatory tone and Ca2+ homeostasis, convergent experimental and clinical observations support Ox-mtDNA as an upstream, therapeutically actionable node. This review describes how mtDNA oxidation, reactive oxygen species amplification, and mitochondrial Ca2+ overload are all facilitated by the convergence of chronic hypoxia, inflammatory cytokines, altered shear stress, and genetic vulnerability. According to the literature, oxidative lesions increase mtDNA bioactivity and persistence when nuclease and autophagy-lysosome clearance systems are overloaded. Pathways of cytosolic and extracellular mtDNA escape, such as vesicular export, mitochondrial permeability transition pore (mPTP) or voltage-dependent anion channel (VDAC)-dependent leakage, and sublethal membrane permeabilization, are summarized in this review. It is also explained how Ox-mtDNA rewires the autophagy-mitophagy axis through reduced flux and skewed signaling, allowing injured mitochondria to continue acting as signal emitters. ER Ca2+ handling and stress-induced remodeling of ER-mitochondria contact sites (MAMs) as upstream amplifiers of mitochondrial damage are also covered. Instead of using prospective, longitudinal cohorts, the majority of these mechanistic data and the correlation between circulating Ox-mtDNA and PAH severity are now based on cross-sectional human sampling and non-PAH disease models. Therefore, until such validation is completed, the biomarker potential of Ox-mtDNA should be considered hypothesis-generating.

articles.title: From Computational Models to Clinical Decision-Making in Epilepsy: Bridging the Gap Between Theory and Practice.
articles.abstract: Epilepsy is one of the most heterogeneous and unpredictable neurological disorders, characterized by complex brain dynamics, significant interindividual variability, and a therapeutic response that is often difficult to predict. Despite major advances in neuroimaging, electrophysiology, and antiepileptic treatments, clinical decision-making still faces major challenges, including precisely localizing the epileptogenic zone, predicting seizures, identifying drug-resistant patients, and optimizing personalized therapeutic strategies. Over the past two decades, computational models have gradually emerged as promising tools for addressing these challenges. Early approaches relied primarily on mechanistic biophysical models aimed at reproducing the neural dynamics and mechanisms of hyperexcitability involved in epileptogenesis. More recently, the rise of artificial intelligence and deep learning has facilitated the development of predictive models capable of leveraging large-scale multimodal data. Finally, the emergence of digital brain twins and adaptive closed-loop systems now paves the way for personalized computational medicine integrating simulation, prediction, and real-time therapeutic intervention. This review provides a critical analysis of the major international initiatives developed between 2004 and 2026, including the EPICLUSTER/EBRAINS, EPINOSTICS, ENIGMA-Epilepsy, NeuroPace RNS, SeizeIT, EpiBioS4Rx, and NeuroVista projects, as well as several translational platforms based on artificial intelligence and biophysical modeling. We evaluate the actual contribution of these models to clinical decision-making in epilepsy, their translational contributions, their methodological limitations, and the challenges associated with their integration into hospital settings. We argue that the future of computational epileptology does not rest on the opposition between artificial intelligence and mechanistic models, but on their convergence within explainable, personalized, and clinically interpretable hybrid architectures.

articles.title: Next-generation pharmacological strategies for Parkinson's disease: a systematic literature review of symptom management and disease modification.
articles.journal: Neurological sciences : official journal of the Italian Neurological Society and of the Italian Society of Clinical Neurophysiology
articles.abstract: Parkinson disease is an ongoing neurodegenerative disorder, and both motor and non-motor symptoms are involved with the existing therapies having minimal effects on the disease but only symptom alleviation. The goal of this systematic literature review was to generalize up-to-date evidence on the next-generation pharmacological strategies to manage the symptoms and the disease in a patient with Parkinson disease. The review was based on PRISMA 2020 and included the analysis of peer-reviewed studies of human research published in 2015-2026 and retrieved in the key databases, such as PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Cochrane Library. This included 30 eligible studies consisting of randomized studies, observational studies, and early clinical trials. The results show that, although dopaminergic treatment continues to play a central role in managing motor symptoms, new methods such as gene therapy, gene editing, stem cell-based regeneration, nanomedicine delivery systems, repurposed drugs, artificial intelligence-based precision medicine approaches have a good neuroprotective and disease-modifying potential. Nonetheless, the majority of new interventions are still in preclinical or first line clinical phase, with a defined subset of emerging gene-, cell-, and nanotechnology-based approaches evaluated only in animal or in-vitro models rather than in PD patients and associated with small sample size, invasive delivery, limited follow-up and lack of long-term safety information. In general, the review concludes by stating that there has been significant advancement in diversification of therapeutic targets and mechanisms, but rigorous large-scale biomarker-directed clinical trials are needed to translate these advances to effective and sustainable treatment of the Parkinson disease.

articles.title: Impact of a dietary and exercise intervention on health-related quality of life of prostate cancer patients on active surveillance with overweight/obesity: a secondary analysis of a randomized controlled trial.
articles.journal: Supportive care in cancer : official journal of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Quality of life (QOL) is important for men on active surveillance (AS) for prostate cancer (PCa). To improve QOL, interventions such as those focused on diet and exercise have been proposed. However, their effectiveness remains unclear, especially in individuals with overweight/obesity.

METHODS: We previously conducted and published a randomized controlled trial of a lifestyle intervention for PCa patients on AS with overweight/obesity. Men were randomized to as follows: (1) 6-month diet and exercise intervention with a 7% weight loss goal vs (2) provided US Dietary and Physical Activity Guidelines. Herein, we report the secondary QOL findings from the trial. QOL was assessed at baseline and conclusion of the intervention via four validated questionnaires. Linear regression and two-sided t-tests evaluated mean differences. Subset analyses of the questionnaires were performed using cut-points correlating with clinical assessments.

RESULTS: Between 2016 and 2020, 100 men completed the trial. The intervention group had a mean weight loss of 7.1% vs 1.8% in controls. Despite this, no significant difference was observed between groups in general QOL (EQ-5D-5L), urinary QOL (IPSS), PCa-related QOL (EPIC-26), or PCa specific anxiety (MAX-PC). However, exploratory subgroup analyses demonstrated that participants with poor "bowel function," low "sexual bother," and good "sexual function" had clinically significant improvements of 12 (95% CI 0.1-24.0), 22 (95% CI 4.2-39.0), and 19 points (95% CI 4.4-34.0) on the EPIC-26.

CONCLUSION: In this secondary analysis of a previously published randomized trial, a 6-month diet and exercise intervention did not improve overall QOL among men with overweight/obesity on AS for PCa. While diet and exercise interventions may not universally improve QOL in this population, they remain important for broader health benefits and may offer targeted value for certain patients.

articles.title: Antibiotic-loaded synthetic calcium sulfate (Stimulan) in the surgical management of fracture-related complications in a low-middle income country.
articles.journal: European journal of orthopaedic surgery & traumatology : orthopedie traumatologie
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: The use of calcium sulfate antibiotic delivery systems are underreported in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), despite the high burden of fracture-related infections and complications. This study evaluates the use of Stimulan in fracture-related complications in a resource-limited setting.

METHODS: A prospective analysis was conducted of all patients treated with Stimulan (Biocomposites Ltd., Keele, UK) for fracture-related complications, between July-September 2023 at Children's Surgical Centre, Cambodia. Patients were followed up regularly at six, nine, and 12 months post-operatively and assessed on the following outcomes: radiological union, radiological/clinical infection remission and functional outcome.

RESULTS: Five out of six patients (83.3%) treated for FRI were clinically and radiologically infection-free, and six out of eight patients (75%) achieved fracture union, at 12 months follow-up. Surgical wounds had healed with no evidence of infection in seven (87.5%) patients. Five non-unions (71.4%) had radiologically healed by 12 months. All patients were fully weightbearing at one year, with two (25%) still requiring walking aids.

CONCLUSION: The use of Stimulan in LMICs appears to provide an effective adjunct for managing fracture-related complications, however more research is required to investigate its efficacy in the treatment of infected non-unions in a LMIC setting.

articles.title: Prospective results of locally delivered low-cost mesh inguinal hernia repair in a low resource setting.
articles.journal: Hernia : the journal of hernias and abdominal wall surgery
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To assess patient outcomes after locally processed ultra-low-cost hernia mesh placement became routine practice in a government hospital in one of the world's poorest countries.

METHODS: Observational study with comprehensive prospective data collection via electronic registry from June 2023 to January 2026. Interrogation of database after 2.5 years assessed demographics, hernia types and complexity, short term complications and outcomes at 2 years.

RESULTS: Between 01.06.2023 and 01.06.2025, 121 inguinal hernia repairs were repaired with mesh. 76% of inguinal hernias were primary and 24% were recurrent or re-recurrent. No Surgical Site Infection was seen after primary inguinal hernia repair. A 10% superficial wound infection rate was seen after repair of recurrent and re-recurrent inguinal hernias. No mesh infections occurred. Heavy use of prophylactic antibiotics was observed but reduced during the study period. This is a report of the first two years of an on-going service and patients are at varying time points post-surgery. 108 repairs (89%) were > one year post-surgery and one-year FU is documented for 108 repairs (100%). No hernia recurrences identified to date 0% 95% CI [0, 3.35]. 66 repairs were > 2 years post-surgery and 2-year FU is documented for 58 repairs (88%). No hernia recurrences identified to date 0% (95% CL: 0%, 6.16%).

CONCLUSION: Robust, prospective outcome monitoring is feasible in low-income-countries, even outside of the clinical trial situation. Structured training and local implementation have produced good early hernia outcomes.

articles.title: Resilience interventions for stress-related health outcomes in patients with cancer: Findings from a systematic review of randomized controlled trials.
articles.journal: Supportive care in cancer : official journal of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This systematic review aimed to synthesize evidence from randomized controlled trials evaluating the effectiveness of resilience interventions in improving stress-related health outcomes among patients with cancer and to provide a theoretical and practical foundation for advancing non-pharmacological interventions in nursing practice.

METHODS: This study adhered to the 2020 Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines. A literature search was conducted using five major databases: PubMed, EBSCO, Embase, Web of Science, and CINAHL. In addition, a manual search was performed using Google Scholar. Two independent researchers assessed the methodological quality of the included studies using the Revised Cochrane risk-of-bias tool for randomized trials (RoB 2). This study has been registered in PROSPERO (registration number: CRD420261283027).

RESULTS: The 33 included randomized controlled trials reported 70 outcome measures across 3,614 patients with cancer. The methodological quality of the included studies ranged from low risk to high risk, with most studies classified as having some concerns or a high risk of bias. Among the 19 outcomes assessing depression, 12 showed significant post-intervention reductions. Of the 21 outcomes evaluating anxiety, 16 showed significant post-intervention reductions. Of the 26 outcomes related to quality of life, 23 showed significant post-intervention improvements. Finally, among the 4 outcomes assessing perceived stress, 3 showed significant post-intervention reductions.

CONCLUSION: Overall, resilience interventions are associated with improvements in stress-related health outcomes in patients with cancer. However, substantial heterogeneity in intervention content, delivery, and outcome reporting across studies precluded quantitative synthesis. Future research should prioritize developing standardized resilience intervention programs and conducting methodologically rigorous randomized controlled trials to validate the practical benefits of resilience interventions in nursing practice.

articles.title: Anatomical variation in the cervical branch of the facial nerve: a systematic review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: There is a paucity of literature on the anatomical variations of the cervical branch of the facial nerve (CBFN). Poor awareness of its anatomy and variations risks intraoperative damage, misdiagnosis of facial nerve injury and undesirable functional and aesthetic outcomes for patients.

PURPOSE: To review anatomical studies on the CBFN and synthesise data on its course, innervations and common variations.

METHODS: A PRISMA-compliant systematic review of anatomical studies of the cervical branch of the facial nerve was conducted. PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Cochrane Library, Web of Science, and Google Scholar were searched up to July 2025. Papers were quality appraised, and data relevant to the anatomy of the CBFN were extracted.

RESULTS: Thirty-five papers with a collated sample size of 867 hemi-necks were identified: 25 with anatomical dissections and 10 case reports. The mean number of CBFN branches was 1.34 (sensitivity range 1.31-1.36). Communication with the marginal mandibular nerve, transverse cervical nerve and great auricular nerve was variable, with prevalences ranging from 22-97%. Distances between the nerve and anatomical landmarks were heterogeneous. Many individual cases of cervical branch variation in course and relationship to nearby vasculature were identified.

CONCLUSION: The cervical branch of the facial nerve displays wide variability in its course. Pre-operative mapping, careful dissection and intra-operative nerve stimulation to aid accurate identification are recommended to prevent iatrogenic damage.

articles.title: Family resilience and quality of life in breast cancer care: a correlational study of matched patient-caregiver pairs.
articles.journal: Supportive care in cancer : official journal of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Breast cancer is a "family disease" that significantly affects the well-being of both patients and their caregivers. This study aimed to determine the level of family resilience among primary caregivers of breast cancer patients, identify influencing factors, and analyze the relationship between family resilience and patient quality of life (QoL).

METHODS: This descriptive, cross-sectional, and correlational study was conducted with 208 matched patient-caregiver pairs at a university hospital in Türkiye. Data were collected using the Patient and Caregiver Information Forms, the World Health Organization Quality of Life Scale-Brief Form (WHOQOL-BREF-TR), and the Family Resilience Assessment Scale (FRAS-TR). Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, Spearman's correlation, and comparative tests (t-test, ANOVA).

RESULTS: The mean family resilience score was 3.14 ± 0.32, with the highest scores in "Making Meaning of Adversity" and the lowest in "Utilization of Social and Economic Resources." Caregivers with higher education levels reported greater family connectedness, while lower education was associated with higher spirituality scores (p < 0.05). Patients' QoL was moderate across all domains. A statistically significant positive correlation was found between caregivers' total family resilience and patients' environmental QoL domain (r = 0.264, p < 0.001). No significant correlations were found with other QoL domains.

CONCLUSION: Higher family resilience in caregivers is positively associated with better environmental QoL for breast cancer patients. Supportive care interventions should focus on strengthening the family unit's ability to mobilize social and economic resources, especially for caregivers with multi-generational responsibilities, to enhance the overall recovery environment.

articles.title: Adherence to the Nordic Nutrition Recommendations 2023 and incidence of type 2 diabetes: a Danish cohort study.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Type 2 diabetes (T2D) is one of the most burdensome chronic diseases. Unhealthy dietary patterns are associated with greater risk of T2D, whereas plant-predominant and climate-friendly diets may be associated with lower risk of T2D. This study aimed to examine the association between adherence to the Nordic Nutrition Recommendations 2023 (NNR23) and risk of T2D in Danish middle-aged adults.

METHODS: This cohort study used data from the Danish Diet, Cancer and Health cohort. The study population was defined among participants with complete baseline data and no cancer at baseline, excluding those with T2D at baseline (n = 54,313). Diet was assessed using a validated semi-quantitative 192-items food frequency questionnaire. Adherence to NNR23 was measured using the Nordic Nutrition Recommendations 2023 Food-Based Diet Score (range 0-15 points). Incident cases of T2D were identified through linkage to the National Diabetes Register. The associations were analysed using Cox proportional hazards regression.

RESULTS: During a median follow-up time of 15.3 years, 7,143 participants developed T2D. Participants with moderate-high adherence (> 10-15 points) to NNR23 had a lower risk of T2D compared to those with low adherence (0-8 points) to NNR23 (HR: 0.63, 95% CI 0.57;0.70). Restricted cubic spline analysis showed a significant non-linear inverse association between adherence to NNR23 and T2D (p-value < 0.001 for non-linearity).

CONCLUSION: Greater adherence to NNR23 was associated with lower risk of T2D, supporting the potential relevance of the NNR23 for T2D prevention.

articles.title: Innate and adaptive immunity pathways linking Mycoplasma pneumoniae to pediatric asthma phenotypes.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Mycoplasma pneumoniae (Mp) is repeatedly detected during pediatric wheeze and asthma exacerbations, but its clinical significance depends on the host-response context. This review evaluates the clinical and mechanistic evidence linking Mp to pediatric asthma phenotypes and examines approaches for distinguishing biologically meaningful infection from incidental detection. We narratively synthesized clinical, experimental, immunological, toxin, and proteomic literature addressing Mp-associated wheeze, asthma exacerbation, epithelial injury, allergic amplification, and inflammatory endotyping. Evidence was distinguished by population and experimental system. Experimental studies show that Mp adheres to airway epithelium; disrupts mucociliary function; activates TLR2/TLR4, NF-κB, autophagy, and inflammasome pathways; and promotes cytokine networks that overlap with allergic asthma. In experimental allergic-airway models, epithelial alarmins, IgE responses, mast cells, and type 2 inflammation may amplify Mp-driven signals, whereas IL-23/IL-17 pathways recruit neutrophils and suggest mixed endotypes; altered corticosteroid responsiveness has not been established in pediatric Mp-associated asthma. CARDS toxin induces eosinophilic inflammation, mucus metaplasia, airway hyperresponsiveness, functional IgE responses, and worsening allergen-driven disease in experimental models. Upper-airway PCR positivity, however, may reflect carriage or prolonged detection rather than active lower-airway infection.

CONCLUSION: Quantitative pathogen testing, paired serology, viral co-detection, age, atopy, microbiome context, and host-response biomarkers merit integrated evaluation in research. Proteomic and multi-omics signatures may support precision endotyping, improve causal attribution, and strengthen pediatric asthma trial design. Their diagnostic and treatment-predictive value remains unvalidated.

WHAT IS KNOWN: • M. pneumoniae is linked to pediatric wheeze and asthma exacerbations, but upper-airway PCR may reflect carriage rather than active lower-airway infection. • Epithelial injury, type 2/Th17 responses, and CARDS toxin can promote asthma-like inflammation in experimental systems.

WHAT IS NEW: • This review integrates diagnostic attribution, toxin biology, immune crosstalk, and proteomic endotyping in one pediatric framework. • It proposes an unvalidated combined pathogen-load and host-response assessment to investigate clinically meaningful M. pneumoniae-driven endotypes and guide trials.

articles.title: Laparoscopic and robotic management of symptomatic calyceal diverticula: a systematic review on behalf of YAU and EAU endourology.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Calyceal diverticula (CD) are outpouchings of the pelvicalyceal system into the renal parenchyma. The purpose of this systematic review is to summarize the outcomes associated with laparoscopic and robotic-assisted approaches for the management of symptomatic CD.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Our findings were structured according to the PRISMA statement. We queried three electronic databases, PubMed, Cochrane Library, and Web of Science, to systematically review the literature. Relying on the March 2009 guidelines from the Oxford Centre for Evidence-Based Medicine, two authors independently judged the quality and evidence level of the final articles.

RESULTS: Nine studies were included in final qualitative synthesis. The operative time ranged from 80 to 172 (107-197) minutes, while Estimated Blood Loss ranged from 40 (5-100) to 150 (50-300) ml. The Grade I-II complications according to Clavien-Dindo Classification System ranged from 0% to 66.7%, while no Grade III-IV complications were reported in either of the nine studies. The rate of patients reporting flank pain recurrence during the follow-up period ranged from 0% to 28.5%, while recurrence of the diverticulum ranged from 0% to 33.3%. None of the patients with flank pain or diverticulum recurrence needed a reoperation.

CONCLUSIONS: The findings of this systematic review suggest that laparoscopic and robotic approaches are feasible and have shown favorable outcomes in selected patients with symptomatic CD, particularly in cases with complex anatomy or after failed endourological treatment. However, the available evidence remains limited.

articles.title: Diagnostic and therapeutic yield of postoperative imaging after complicated appendicitis: a western pediatric surgery research consortium prospective study.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: While laparoscopic appendectomy is the standard of care for acute appendicitis, postoperative imaging practices for complicated cases remains variable, and abscesses are a frequent source of morbidity. Postoperative imaging variation may influence the timing of abscess diagnosis and intervention. This study examines the association between postoperative imaging timing and both diagnostic yield (abscess detection) and therapeutic yield (intervention rate), recognizing that detection of an abscess on imaging does not always result in intervention.

METHODS: We conducted a prospective study of children with complicated appendicitis across nine children's hospitals (2022-2024). Patients were stratified by postoperative day (POD) of first imaging (US/CT/MRI). Primary outcomes were diagnostic yield of imaging for abscess formation and therapeutic yield for drainage or reoperation. We performed multivariable logistic regression to examine the association of POD windows and yield. Pairwise comparisons of marginal predicted probabilities were obtained with post-estimation margins and delta-method standard errors.

RESULTS: Among 2,560 patients with complicated appendicitis, 578 (22.5%) underwent postoperative abdominal imaging. Of these, 327 (56.6%) occurred prior to discharge and 251 (43.4%) after discharge. Therapeutic yield varied as a continuous function of postoperative day; LOWESS analysis demonstrated increasing probability of drainage through approximately POD7-10 followed by decline, with sliding window analysis identifying peak therapeutic yield between POD6-8 (42.3% of scans resulted in drainage). Diagnostic yield was highest when imaging occurred before POD10, while imaging after POD10 identified significantly fewer abscesses (37.2% vs. 69.2%, p < 0.001) and resulted in fewer interventions (20.0% vs. 37.2%, p < 0.001). When stratified by discharge status, pre-discharge therapeutic yield peaked between POD6-10, while post-discharge yield plateaued around POD6-8. Therapeutic yield was higher among patients imaged before discharge, who represent a clinically distinct population with persistent failure to meet discharge criteria.

CONCLUSION: Postoperative imaging performed before POD10 demonstrated the highest diagnostic and therapeutic yield for detecting intra-abdominal abscess following appendectomy for complicated appendicitis. Therapeutic yield for postoperative imaging peaked between POD 6-8. Imaging performed after POD10 was significantly less likely to identify drainable collections. Among patients who re-present after discharge, imaging yield declines after POD10, which may inform the timing and modality of imaging in this population, balancing diagnostic utility against radiation exposure. Diagnosing an abscess does not always lead to intervention; clinicians should prioritize the POD6-8 window to maximize actionable yield.

articles.title: Correction to: Sacubitril/valsartan compared to equivalent/sub-equivalent dose angiotensin receptor blocker or angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction: a meta-analysis of randomized trials.
Alternative splicing acts as a strategic switch for heat shock network diversification under escalating heat stress.
articles.abstract: Alternative splicing (AS) is a pivotal post-transcriptional mechanism for plant thermal adaptation, yet its dynamics in heat-tolerant woody species remain poorly understood. Here, we map the temperature-resolved AS landscape of the highly thermotolerant woody plant Rhododendron hainanense by combining Iso-Seq with RNA-seq. Transcriptomic profiling revealed a graded regulatory architecture: moderate heat (37 °C) elicited a targeted proteostatic response, whereas severe heat (42 °C) provoked a massive transcriptome expansion. Notably, this global AS surge coincided with a widespread downregulation of core splicing factors, a correlation suggesting that a more permissive splicing environment may contribute to the rapid generation of diverse stress-responsive isoforms. The heat shock protein (HSP) family emerged as the principal hub of this AS-associated diversification; the core chaperone genes ClpB1, HSP83, and HSP70 generated the greatest transcript complexity, with HSP83 alone producing 29 distinct AS transcripts that resolved into three temperature-dependent expression groups. Within the heat shock factor network, HSFA2 showed the strongest and most sustained induction, and DAP-seq identified in vitro HSFA2 binding at the promoters of ClpB1, HSP83, and HSP70, supporting these core chaperones as putative direct DNA-binding targets. Functional complementation in Arabidopsis further showed that three structurally distinct HSFA2 splice variants each restored thermotolerance to the hsfa2 mutant and consistently induced expression of the core ATP-dependent chaperone arm, suggesting that this central chaperone-induction capacity is retained across the tested splice variants in this heterologous system. Together, these findings provide a comprehensive atlas of temperature-modulated AS in a thermotolerant woody plant and support a model in which splicing-mediated diversification of the HSP chaperone network contributes to heat adaptation, offering post-transcriptional insights for breeding climate-resilient crops.

articles.title: eIF3i inhibits nelson bay orthoreovirus replication via interaction with the σNS protein.
articles.abstract: L929 cells exhibit relatively strong resistance to infection by Nelson Bay orthoreovirus (NBV), primarily due to the unique virus-host interaction that suppresses NBV infection at multiple stages, including viral entry, genome replication, and virion assembly. This study investigates the role of host factor eIF3i in NBV replication. Co-immunoprecipitation and immunofluorescence co-localization assays were performed to verify whether eIF3i interacts with the σNS protein in vitro. The results demonstrated that eIF3i significantly inhibits NBV replication through specific binding to σNS. This finding not only provides mechanistic insights into host protein-mediated regulation of viral replication, but also offers a theoretical basis for developing novel anti-NBV therapeutic strategies.

articles.title: Inflammatory bowel disease and breast cancer: epidemiological evidence, shared biology, and clinical management.
articles.journal: Inflammation research : official journal of the European Histamine Research Society ... [et al.]
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE AND DESIGN: This narrative review examines epidemiological, genetic, mechanistic, microbial, and therapeutic evidence concerning inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) and breast cancer.

METHODS: Relevant literature was identified through targeted PubMed searches completed through May 2026 and reference-list screening. Evidence was selected for its relevance to epidemiology, candidate mechanisms, microbiome-related pathways, and treatment interactions.

RESULTS: Pooled cohort evidence does not show a significant overall increase in breast cancer risk among patients with IBD. Several inflammatory, stromal, microbial, and endocrine pathways are relevant to both diseases, although most evidence comes from separate study populations and experimental models. Studies of patients with prior malignancy have not shown a clear increase in new or recurrent cancer during commonly used IBD therapies, but few analyses have focused specifically on breast cancer. Microbiome-directed treatments have been studied in IBD and, more recently, in oncology; their value for patients with both diseases is unknown.

CONCLUSIONS: Current evidence does not support classifying IBD as a breast cancer risk state. The main clinical concern is the interaction between treatments for the two diseases, which requires individualized assessment and coordinated gastroenterology and oncology care.

articles.title: Ultrastructural insights of infection and biological control of Alternaria alternata Kl3 mediated leaf spot disease in kohlrabi.
articles.abstract: Rapid shifts in agro-climatic conditions have accelerated the emergence and severity of fungal plant diseases necessitating continuous pathogen monitoring and development of sustainable control strategies. Consequently, plant-beneficial bacteria-based biological control is one such prime and widely used strategy. Leaf spot diseases caused by Alternaria spp. pose a serious threat to Brassica cultivation, yet etiological and mechanistic insights into kohlrabi (Brassica oleracea var. gongylodes) leaf spot disease remian limited. In this comprehensive study a dominant fungal isolate Kl3, was recovered from diseased leaves of kohlrabi in Santiniketan, India. Based on combined micromorphological features and multilocus phylogeny (ITS-5.8S, gapdh, tef1, alt a1); Kl3 was identified as Alternaria alternata Kl3; which successfully produced disease symptoms in detached kohlrabi leaves ensuring its phytopathogenic potential.
