METHODS: We utilized healthy subjects and patients with SMA induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC)-derived cultures to assess phenotypes occurring intrinsically within astrocyte processes (monocultures) and at the PAP-synaptic interface (co-cultures), respectively, using cell surface capture mass spectrometry proteomics, confocal and super resolution microscopy, synaptogliosome (SG) isolation, and electrophysiology.

RESULTS: SMA astrocytes demonstrated intrinsic filopodia actin defects featuring low abundance of actin-associated cell surface N-glycoproteins, decreased filopodia density and CDC42-GTP levels after actin remodeling stimulation, and significantly reduced phosphorylated ezrin, radixin, and moesin (pERM) proteins. Within the SMA motor neuron and astrocyte co-cultures, we observed concurrent decreases in synapse number, actin-associated synapsin I expression, and PAP-associated expression of pERM proteins. Our dual treatment paradigm using SMN1 gene therapy combined with forskolin treatment to stimulate actin dynamics via increasing cyclic adenosine monophosphate levels resulted in increased branching and filopodia density of SMA astrocytes, and improved synapse formation and function of SMA motor neurons.

INTERPRETATION: We define actin-associated defects impacting astrocyte filopodia dynamics and motor neuron synaptic function in SMA. This shaped our therapeutic approach targeted to SMN-dependent and actin-related disease mechanisms, which overall demonstrated improvements in motor neuron function and disease pathology. ANN NEUROL 2026.

articles.title: Cardiovascular risk stratification using chest CT in idiopathic inflammatory myopathies.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the diagnostic and prognostic value of incidentally detected coronary artery calcification (CAC) on routine chest computed tomography (CT) for cardiovascular risk stratification in patients with idiopathic inflammatory myopathies (IIM).

METHODS: In this single-centre cross-sectional study, adult patients with IIM who underwent noncardiac, nongated high-resolution chest CT (HRCT) were included. CAC was visually categorized as absent, mild, moderate, or severe. Diagnostic performance for established coronary artery disease (CAD) and established cardiovascular (CV) events was assessed. Kaplan-Meier analyses evaluated CV death-free survival, and multivariable logistic regression identified factors associated with CAC. A matched systemic sclerosis (SSc) cohort served as validation cohort.

RESULTS: Among 234 patients with IIM (mean age 57.1±15.9 years; 70.1% female), CAC was present in 43.2%. Higher CAC thresholds showed greater specificity for established CAD and prior CV events, whereas lower thresholds were more sensitive. CAC was associated with reduced CV death-free survival (log-rank p = 0.0095), with a stepwise decline across CAC severity categories. Findings were similar in the matched SSc cohort. Increasing CAC burden was associated with older age, smoking, higher CV risk burden, interstitial lung disease, and higher disease activity. In adjusted analyses, high disease activity was independently associated with moderate CAC (OR 4.01, 95% CI 1.29-12.50), while a higher number of concomitant DMARDs was associated with severe CAC (OR 2.55, 95% CI 1.27-5.11).

CONCLUSION: Incidentally detected CAC on routine chest CT provides diagnostic and prognostic information in IIM and may represent a pragmatic approach to improve cardiovascular risk stratification in this high-risk population.

articles.title: A Miniaturized, Multilayer Structured Vertical Flow Paper Device Enabled One-Step, Multiplex, Spontaneous Detection of Biomarkers in Microliter Blood for Disease Screening.
articles.abstract: Developing a miniaturized, portable device for multiplexed detection of a library of protein biomarkers from microliter blood sample is critical for early disease screening in many scenarios, such as home healthcare and emergency care. However, major challenges remain, including multiplexed detection without cross-interference, system-level miniaturization, reliable flow manipulation, and simple user operation. Here, we present a miniaturized, multilayer structured vertical flow paper device that enables one-step, multiplexed, spontaneous detection of biomarkers in microliter blood for screening of heart disease, kidney disease, and inflammation. The device is designed with a multilayer membrane structure that integrates 3D-printed glass fiber membranes, wax-printed nitrocellulose membranes, and cellulose absorption membranes, enabling autonomous wicking of the sample through the device while concurrently distributing the sample into multiple equal parts and executing the sandwich immunoassay and washing steps. Simultaneous quantification of 12 biomarkers is achieved, and clinical performance is validated using clinical samples from patients with acute myocardial infarction (AMI), acute kidney disease (AKD), or sepsis. The device requires about 60 μL of sample, delivers results in 15 min, and is also compact (12.5 cm3). Overall, this platform provides a novel and universal strategy for miniaturized multiplexed immunoassays for rapid clinical screening.

articles.title: Assessment of accommodative function in individuals aged 40-50 years with stage 1 hypertension without hypertensive retinopathy compared with age-matched healthy controls.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To compare accommodative function between middle-aged adults with stage 1 hypertension and age-matched healthy controls and to investigate the association between blood pressure and accommodative parameters.

METHODS: This cross-sectional analytical study included 63 participants aged 40-50 years, comprising 33 patients with stage 1 hypertension without hypertensive retinopathy and 30 healthy controls. All participants underwent standardized systemic and ophthalmic examinations. Accommodative function was evaluated using accommodative amplitude (AA), monocular accommodative facility (MAF), accommodative response assessed by monocular estimation method retinoscopy (MEM), positive relative accommodation (PRA), and negative relative accommodation (NRA).

RESULTS: A total of 63 participants were included. MAF and PRA were significantly lower in the hypertension group than in the control group (both p < .05). No significant between-group differences were observed in AA, accommodative response (MEM), or NRA (all p > .05). Diastolic blood pressure was positively correlated with accommodative response (r = 0.356, p = .042). In multiple linear regression analysis, hypertension was independently associated with MAF (β =  -1.936, p = .001) and PRA (β = 0.259, p = .002).

CONCLUSIONS: Patients with stage 1 hypertension without hypertensive retinopathy showed reduced MAF and PRA despite preserved AA. These findings suggest that dynamic accommodative function may be affected early in hypertension, before clinically detectable ocular complications develop.

articles.title: Deconstructing the Modified Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (mSOFA) Score: A Decision Tree Analysis Reveals the Pathophysiological Hierarchy of Organ Dysfunction Predictors in Prehospital Critical Care.
articles.journal: QJM : monthly journal of the Association of Physicians
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Early recognition of multiple organ dysfunction syndrome (MODS) in the prehospital setting remains challenging and is critical for reducing mortality among critically ill patients. The modified Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (mSOFA) score was developed for prehospital use with point-of-care testing; however, the internal decision architecture of this score remains unexplored.

METHODS: A prospective, multicentre, observational study was conducted across three emergency medical systems (EMS) in Spain, included adults (n = 12,212) with acute illness transferred to emergency departments with high priority. A decision tree (DT) model was developed using the five components of the mSOFA score, lactate, Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS), oxygen saturation-to-fraction of inspired oxygen ratio (SaFi), mean blood pressure (MBP), and creatinine, to predict in-hospital mortality at 2 days. The study followed the STROBE and TRIPOD+AI guidelines.

RESULTS: Cohort mortality was 5.0% (n = 609). Lactate emerged as the primary decision variable, with a threshold of 3.8 mmol/L, followed by SaFi, GCS, and creatinine in patients with hyperlactataemia, and by GCS and creatinine when lactate was below the threshold.

CONCLUSIONS: The DT deconstructs the mSOFA from a static score into a dynamic, interpretable clinical decision framework. By revealing the pathophysiological hierarchy underlying the score, with lactate as the central stratification axis, this approach enables EMS clinicians to identify distinct clinical phenotypes and anticipate deterioration based on the sequential evaluation of organ dysfunction rather than a single numerical threshold.

articles.title: Pulmonary ILC2 Priming as a Link Between Severe Early-Life RSV Bronchiolitis and Asthma.
articles.journal: American journal of respiratory cell and molecular biology
articles.abstract: Severe respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) bronchiolitis in infancy is associated with increased childhood asthma risk, but the mechanisms that sustain airway vulnerability remain unresolved. Airway samples from infants with severe RSV disease and experimental models show robust IL-33 responses and pulmonary group 2 innate lymphoid cell (ILC2) activation during acute infection. Additionally, neonatal IL-33 and allergen-rechallenge studies demonstrate that ILC2s can persist and acquire memory-like properties. These observations support, but do not establish, a model in which severe lower-airway RSV disease primes ILC2s or their tissue niche for exaggerated responses to later allergens. Beyond limited interferon control and prolonged epithelial injury, which may amplify IL-33/ST2 signaling during a developmental window when long-lived lung ILC2 populations are established, we focus on additional candidate mechanisms that could sustain this priming. These include metabolic pathways governing glycolysis, lipid utilization, iron uptake, and mitochondrial function; epigenetic mechanisms involving chromatin remodeling and histone or DNA modifications; and neuroimmune signals that regulate ILC2 activation and recall. Direct evidence that RSV induces durable, cell-intrinsic metabolic, epigenetic, or neuroimmune reprogramming of infant pulmonary ILC2s is currently lacking. Longitudinal ILC2 profiling and adoptive transfer of RSV-experienced versus control ILC2s are needed to test this model. Maternal vaccination and long-acting monoclonal antibodies now provide an opportunity to determine whether preventing severe early-life RSV disease alters airway immune programming and subsequent asthma risk.

articles.title: Characterization of 24-Hour Rhythms in Vital Signs in Intensive Care Populations: A Scoping Review.
articles.abstract: Circadian rhythms in intensive care unit (ICU) patients are vulnerable to disruption, which may contribute to adverse clinical outcomes. Continuously monitored vital signs offer a unique opportunity to assess 24-hour rhythms in real-world ICU settings. The aim of this scoping review is to systematically map methodological approaches used to characterize 24-hour rhythms in vital signs in ICU populations and to summarize reported associations with patient characteristics, clinical outcomes, or interventions. A systematic literature search was conducted to identify studies that assessed 24-hour rhythms in routinely collected vital signs in adult, pediatric and neonatal ICU patients published between January 2015 and December 2025. Thirty-five studies comprising nearly 288 000 patients were included, with most studies conducted in adult ICUs (n = 32), 3 in neonatal ICUs, and none in pediatric ICUs. Substantial heterogeneity existed in preprocessing strategies, assessment windows, analytical methods, and derived rhythmicity metrics that were used to determine 24-hour variation, as well as in the level of detail with which these were reported. Cosinor analysis was the most frequently used method to characterize rhythmicity, followed by day-night comparisons, and max-min approaches. Across studies, rhythmicity analyses revealed that 24-hour rhythms in vital signs were detectable in ICU patients, although methodological heterogeneity and lack of detail on analytical decisions limit evidence synthesis. In addition, the direction and magnitude of associations between rhythmic properties (such as amplitude or acrophase) and mortality and other clinically relevant outcomes varied considerably among studies. While most, though not all, studies reported that higher amplitudes were associated with mortality, it remains unclear whether this reflects circadian physiology rather than clinical instability. Harmonization of reporting practices and the development of a core outcome set on circadian parameters derived from vital signs in critical care contexts will help to guide future research in this burgeoning field.

articles.title: Education and training interventions for healthcare workers to prevent sexual harassment.
articles.journal: The Cochrane database of systematic reviews
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE: Sexual harassment is common among healthcare workers and is associated with poor mental health, job dissatisfaction, and workforce attrition. Education and training may help prevent sexual harassment, but their effectiveness in healthcare settings has not been systematically evaluated.

OBJECTIVES: To assess the effectiveness of education and training interventions on knowledge and skills for managing sexual harassment, and to assess their impact on the incidence of sexual harassment towards healthcare workers in healthcare settings.

SEARCH METHODS: We searched CENTRAL, MEDLINE, Embase, PsycINFO, AMED, CINAHL, Scopus, ClinicalTrials.gov, and the WHO ICTRP, together with reference checking and contact with study authors, to identify eligible studies. The latest search date was March 2025.

ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA: We included randomised controlled trials (RCTs) involving healthcare workers comparing education or training interventions with control (no intervention, waiting list, placebo, or minimal intervention) or different types of education or training to prevent sexual harassment in healthcare settings.

OUTCOMES: Our critical outcomes were knowledge and skills in managing sexual harassment and the incidence of all types of sexual harassment perpetrated by patients, visitors, coworkers, and management. Important outcomes were anxiety, depression, burnout, sick leave, staff turnover, disability, and perception of the organisational climate related to harassment.

RISK OF BIAS: We used the Cochrane RoB 2 tool to assess risk of bias.

SYNTHESIS METHODS: We synthesised results for each outcome using random-effects model meta-analysis. We used GRADE to assess the certainty of evidence for each outcome.

INCLUDED STUDIES: We included two studies from Taiwan with a total of 170 nurses. Most participants were young women with little work experience. The intervention group received education to prevent sexual harassment, and the comparison group received a different type of education to prevent sexual harassment. We found no studies that had a comparison group without any active educational or training components.

SYNTHESIS OF RESULTS: Education and training interventions to prevent sexual harassment compared to control (no intervention, waiting list, placebo, or minimal intervention) in healthcare workers No studies addressed this comparison. Education and training interventions to prevent sexual harassment compared to other education and training interventions for healthcare workers We found two studies reporting on education and training interventions to prevent sexual harassment compared to other education and training interventions in healthcare workers. Educational interventions to prevent sexual harassment probably increase sexual harassment prevention knowledge slightly ('sexual harassment prevention', mean difference (MD) 4.74, 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.21 to 8.28; P = 0.71; I2 = 0%; 2 RCTs, 168 participants; moderate-certainty evidence) and may increase management skills slightly ('coping behaviour', MD 6.36, 95% CI -6.84 to 19.56; P = 0.43; I2 = 0%; 2 RCTs, 168 participants; low-certainty evidence) and ('prevention strategy', MD 11.70, 95% CI 2.56 to 20.85; P = 0.22; I2 = 33%; 2 RCTs, 168 participants; low-certainty evidence). No study evaluated the incidence of sexual harassment, anxiety, depression, burnout, sick leave, staff turnover, disability, or perception of the organisational climate related to harassment. Adverse effects were not measured or reported in the included studies. The certainty of the evidence was moderate to low. We judged the overall risk of bias as low, and we identified no inconsistency or publication bias. However, imprecision was more of a concern given the low number of participants and relatively broad CIs around the effect estimates.

AUTHORS' CONCLUSIONS: Healthcare workers may benefit from education and training compared to another type of education and training. The benefits were modest and were measured as increased knowledge ('sexual harassment prevention') and management skills ('coping behaviour' and 'prevention strategy'). The certainty of the evidence is moderate to low, and future studies could make the findings more robust. There is a need for future studies investigating other types of outcomes such as anxiety, depression, burnout, sick leave, staff turnover, disability, and perception of the organisational climate related to harassment. It would also be valuable to assess a wider range of healthcare workers, as we only found studies in nurses. No studies addressed the effects of education and training compared to control groups (no intervention, waiting list, placebo, or minimal intervention). The decision to offer sexual harassment education and training to healthcare workers is supported by the existing evidence. However, other contextual factors may also be considered, as well as healthcare workers' preferences to participate in educational activities.

FUNDING: This Cochrane review had no dedicated funding.

REGISTRATION: Registration: Cochrane Collaboration, 19th of December 2023.

TITLE: Education and training interventions for health care workers to prevent sexual harassment. Identification number: EMID:9ba735d2b5367171. Authors: Therese K Dalsbø, Rakel Aasheim Greve, Ingrid L Jørgensen, Marita S Fønhus.

PROTOCOL: Published on the 6th of February 2025 available via Cochrane Library at https://doi.org/10.1002/14651858.CD016096.

articles.title: Blood pressure targets in adults with hypertension.
articles.journal: The Cochrane database of systematic reviews
articles.abstract: This is a protocol for a Cochrane review (intervention). The objectives are as follows: Primary objective To evaluate the benefits and harms of lower targets of blood pressure (BP; i.e. BP ≤ 135/85 mmHg) versus standard targets (i.e. BP ≤ 140 to 160/90 to 100 mmHg) for total mortality and morbidity in people 18 years or older, with elevated BP. Secondary objectives To evaluate the benefits and harms of lower targets versus standard targets for achieved systolic and diastolic BP in people 18 years or older, with elevated BP. To evaluate the benefits and harms of lower targets versus standard targets for withdrawals due to adverse events in people 18 years or older with elevated BP. To assess whether the effects of lower targets versus standard targets differ according to prespecified equity-related characteristics (e.g. place of residence, race/ethnicity/culture/ancestry, sex, socioeconomic status, and social capital, plus other context-specific factors, including comorbidity burden) in people 18 years or older, with elevated BP.

articles.title: Home visits following hospital discharge for families with preterm and low-birthweight infants.
articles.journal: The Cochrane database of systematic reviews
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE: Home visiting programmes are widely used to support families of preterm and low-birthweight (LBW) infants after hospital discharge, yet evidence on their effectiveness is limited and of variable quality, particularly in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). A comprehensive, up-to-date review was needed to inform healthcare decisions.

OBJECTIVES: To assess the effectiveness of home visits following hospital discharge compared to standard of care or no home visits, for families/caregivers of preterm or LBW infants to reduce morbidity and mortality and enhance health and well-being.

SEARCH METHODS: We searched CENTRAL, MEDLINE, CINAHL, Scopus, Web of Science, ClinicalTrials.gov, and the WHO ICTRP, together with reference checking, to identify eligible studies. The latest search date was April 2026.

ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA: We included randomised controlled trials (RCTs) of preterm and LBW infants and their caregivers comparing home visits after discharge from hospital with no home visits or standard of care including home visits. There were no restrictions on language or publication status.

OUTCOMES: Our critical outcomes included all-cause mortality, neurodevelopment, morbidity, growth, breastfeeding rates, exclusive breastfeeding, and emergency hospital visits. Important outcomes were hospital readmission rates, maternal/parental emotional well-being, and maternal-infant interaction.

RISK OF BIAS: We used Cochrane's RoB 2 tool to assess the risk of bias.

SYNTHESIS METHODS: We synthesised results for each outcome in meta-analysis where possible, using random-effects models to calculate risk ratios (RRs) for dichotomous outcomes, mean differences (MDs) or standardised mean differences (SMDs) for continuous outcomes, and hazard ratios (HRs) for time-to-event outcomes, along with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). We used GRADE to assess the certainty of evidence for each outcome.

INCLUDED STUDIES: We included 35 RCTs, of which 28 (12,021 infants and 10,056 mothers/caregivers) contributed data to our prespecified outcomes. Most studies were from high-income countries; however, approximately 70% of participants were from a large study in India contributing data to comparison 2. The content, timing, duration, and frequency of home visits varied widely. Twenty-one studies contributed data to meta-analyses.

SYNTHESIS OF RESULTS: Home visits versus no home visits The effects of home visits on all-cause mortality at one year are very uncertain (RR 3.08, 95% CI 0.13 to 73.27; 1 study, 79 participants). Home visits may have little to no effect on cognitive development (SMD 0.06, 95% CI -0.17 to 0.29; 3 studies, 287 participants), and likely have little to no effect on motor development (SMD -0.02, 95% CI -0.36 to 0.33; 1 study, 127 participants). The effect on morbidity, specifically on diarrhoea at six months, is very uncertain (RR 0.71, 95% CI 0.42 to 1.19; 1 study, 179 participants). Home visits likely have little to no effect on growth, specifically weight-for-age z-scores (WAZ) at six months (MD -0.09, 95% CI -0.36 to 0.18; 1 study, 179 participants). Home visits likely increase the proportion of infants breastfeeding at six months (RR 1.26, 95% CI 1.16 to 1.37; I² = 0%; 4 studies, 1217 participants) and may result in a large increase in exclusive breastfeeding at six months (RR 2.31, 95% CI 0.85 to 6.29; 3 studies, 1129 participants). The certainty of the evidence ranged from moderate to very low due to risk of bias and imprecision. More intensive home visits versus less intensive home visits (part of standard of care) Home visits with community-initiated kangaroo mother care likely reduce all-cause mortality at 6 months (HR 0.75, 95% CI 0.60 to 0.93; 1 study, 8402 participants), likely have little to no effect on cognitive (MD 0.21, 95% CI -1.77 to 2.19; 1 study, 552 participants) or motor development (MD -0.85 95% CI -2.59 to 0.89; 1 trial, 552 participants) at 12 months, and likely reduce morbidity, specifically rates of diarrhoea slightly at 3 months (RR 0.94, 95% CI 0.85 to 1.04; 1 study, 7654 participants) and the risk of possible serious bacterial infections slightly at 28 days (RR 0.89, 95% CI 0.82 to 0.97; 1 study, 8384 participants). They likely have little to no effect on WAZ at six months (MD -0.01, 95% CI -0.06 to 0.04; 1 study, 7086 participants) and likely reduce the proportion of infants who are severely underweight at six months slightly (RR 0.95, 95% CI 0.87 to 1.04; 1 study, 6641 participants). More intensive home visits may have little to no effect on breastfeeding at six months (RR 1.18, 95% CI 0.88 to 1.59; 1 study, 308 participants), and their effect on exclusive breastfeeding at six months is very uncertain (RR 1.97, 95% CI 0.19 to 20.62; I² = 84%; 3 studies, 7091 participants). The certainty of the evidence was moderate for all outcomes except for breastfeeding and exclusive breastfeeding, for which it was low and very low, respectively. The certainty of evidence was downgraded for risk of bias, imprecision, and indirectness. No study in either comparison reported on emergency hospital visits.

AUTHORS' CONCLUSIONS: Home visits likely improve breastfeeding and may improve exclusive breastfeeding compared to no home visits. They may have little to no effect on cognitive development, and likely have little to no effect on motor development or growth. The effects on mortality or diarrhoea are very uncertain. In places where home visits are already implemented, enhancing them so that they are more intensive than the standard of care (i.e. more frequent, longer, delivered by specialised personnel, with kangaroo mother care, etc.) likely reduces mortality, morbidity, and the risk of underweight. However, they likely have little to no effect on cognitive and motor development or WAZ, and may have little to no effect on breastfeeding rates. The effects on exclusive breastfeeding are very uncertain. Better-quality studies are needed, particularly in LMICs. There is a need for studies reporting on the critical outcome of emergency hospital visits, and to standardise outcome measures reported in this area of research, particularly for mental health and neurodevelopment outcomes.

FUNDING: This review was conducted for the GELA project (africa.cochrane.org/projects/GELA) which is funded as part of the EDCTP2 programme (grant number RIA2020S-3303-GELA) supported by the European Union.

REGISTRATION: Protocol: CRD42024496298 registered on 15 January 2024 (PROSPERO), available at https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD42024496298.

articles.title: Bothersome and activity-limiting pain in community-dwelling older adults with versus without stroke: a cross-sectional analysis of the National Health and Aging Trends study (2011-2024).
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Stroke and pain are common health challenges among older adults. However, limited research has examined the burden of pain among community-dwelling older adults with a history of stroke in the United States of America (USA). This study aimed to estimate the prevalence of bothersome and activity-limiting pain and examine the association between stroke history and pain outcomes among older adults in the USA.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This cross-sectional secondary analysis used publicly available data from Rounds 1-14 of the National Health and Aging Trends Study (NHATS), conducted from 2011 to 2024. The study included adults aged ≥ 65 years and compared participants with and without a self-reported physician-diagnosed history of stroke. Pain outcomes were derived from standardized NHATS interview data and included bothersome pain and activity-limiting pain. Demographic, clinical, psychological, physical, and sleep-related variables were obtained from the NHATS dataset. Survey-weighted multivariable logistic regression was used to examine the associations between stroke history and pain outcomes after adjustment for relevant covariates.

RESULTS: Among 12,797 participants, 2,235 (15.71%) had a history of stroke, and 10,562 (84.29%) did not. The prevalence of bothersome pain was higher among participants with stroke than among those without stroke (60.77% vs. 54.66%; p = .003). Similarly, activity-limiting pain was more prevalent among participants with stroke (62.83% vs. 52.00%; p < .001). After adjustment for demographic, clinical, psychological, physical, and sleep-related factors, stroke remained independently associated with bothersome pain (OR 1.30, 95% CI 1.02-1.66; p = .034) and activity-limiting pain (OR 1.20, 95% CI 1.04-1.38; p = .013).

CONCLUSIONS: Pain represents a substantial burden among U.S. older adults with a history of stroke. Stroke was independently associated with both bothersome and activity-limiting pain, highlighting the importance of comprehensive pain assessment and management within geriatric stroke rehabilitation.

articles.title: Prenatal Cannabinoid Exposure Induces Sex-Specific Alterations in Fetal Growth and Placental Lipid Metabolism Gene Expression.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Prenatal cannabis use is becoming increasingly more commonplace. However, cannabis exposure is linked to adverse pregnancy outcomes, including gestational hypertension, preeclampsia, and preterm birth. The aim of this study was to determine the morphological and molecular effects of prenatal cannabinoid exposure on the placenta.

METHODS: Pregnant Sprague-Dawley rats were exposed daily to vaporized THC (100 mg/mL) starting at gestational day (GD)5 until GD19, when dams were sacrificed and fetuses and placentas collected. Fetuses were genotyped for genetic sex, and transcriptomic analysis was performed on male and female THC-exposed and control placentas.

RESULTS: On GD19, only the female fetuses from the THC group were significantly larger than those of the control, with no significant differences in placental weights or fetal:placental weight ratios. RNA sequencing revealed enriched biological processes related to nutrient transport and lipid catabolism, protein-lipid complex formation, and lipoprotein particle remodeling and organization. Further transcriptomic analysis determined that the differentially expressed genes and enriched biological processes related to lipid metabolism were preferentially enriched in the female THC placentas compared to the male, suggesting a sex-specific effect.

DISCUSSION: Collectively, these data present sex-specific effects of prenatal cannabinoid exposure on placental growth and global gene expression. These data also suggest that sex influences gene expression of genes related to lipid metabolism in the THC-exposed placentas.

articles.title: Provider Knowledge, Risk Perceptions, and Communication Readiness Drive Discussions about Early-Onset Colorectal Cancer: A National Survey of US Healthcare Providers.
authors: American Society of Colon and Rectal Surgeons Early- Onset Colorectal Cancer Steering Committee
articles.journal: Diseases of the colon and rectum
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The incidence of early-onset colorectal cancer continues to increase among adults younger than 50 years, yet delays in diagnosis remain common.

OBJECTIVE: As an initial step of the Early-Onset Colorectal Cancer Awareness campaign, we evaluated U.S. healthcare providers' knowledge, attitudes, diagnostic practices, and perceived barriers related to the timely recognition and evaluation of early-onset colorectal cancer.

DESIGN: This survey established baseline measures for a national early-onset colorectal cancer awareness campaign.

SETTING: We conducted a national cross-sectional survey of physicians, nurse practitioners, and physician assistants practicing family medicine, internal medicine, emergency medicine/urgent care, and obstetrics and gynecology.

MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: The survey assessed early-onset colorectal cancer awareness, screening recommendations, evaluation of symptomatic younger adults, perceived barriers to diagnosis, and educational needs. Descriptive statistics summarized responses, and multivariable regression identified factors associated with guideline-concordant screening and diagnostic evaluation.

RESULTS: A total of 277 providers completed the survey. Although 87% were concerned or very concerned about early-onset colorectal cancer and 82% reported increased concern over the preceding five years, providers identified substantial barriers to timely diagnosis. Approximately one-half reported that younger adults commonly experienced symptoms for four months or longer before seeking care. The most frequently cited barriers included patients expecting symptoms to resolve (84%), insurance and financial barriers (79%), reluctance to undergo colonoscopy (77%), and failure to recognize symptoms as serious (65%). Most providers (79%) identified additional guidance on early-onset colorectal cancer symptoms, risk factors, and diagnostic evaluation as the educational resource most likely to improve care.

CONCLUSIONS: Despite widespread awareness of the increasing incidence of early-onset colorectal cancer, patient- and system-level barriers continue to delay diagnosis in younger adults. These findings identify opportunities for targeted education, clinical decision support, and health system interventions to promote timely evaluation of symptomatic patients and improve early detection of early-onset colorectal cancer. See Video Abstract.

articles.title: Diagnosis and Management of HIV-Associated Colitis.
articles.journal: Diseases of the colon and rectum
articles.abstract: A 63-year-old male with a history of untreated HIV presented to the emergency room with acute on chronic watery diarrhea, weight loss, fatigue, fever and chills. His vital signs were within normal limits and his abdomen was soft, nondistended and tender to palpation in 4 quadrants without peritonitis. He did not have leukocytosis on presentation. CD4 count was 310. CT scan showed inflammatory changes in the rectum and sigmoid colon. Comprehensive infectious workup was negative for any pathogens including cytomegalovirus (CMV), cryptosporidium, chlamydia, gonorrhea, C. difficile, cryptococcus, tuberculosis (TB) and herpes simplex virus (HSV). Colonoscopy was performed and showed a continuous area of nonbleeding ulcerated mucosa in the rectum, sigmoid, descending and transverse colon (Fig. 1). Pancolonic biopsies revealed active colitis with focal areas of basal plasmacytosis and crypt branching in left colon, suggestive of acute on chronic colitis and possible ulcerative colitis (UC). Gastroenterology and infectious disease were consulted and patient was started on IV methylprednisolone for presumed UC flare. Over the next few weeks, the patient proceeded to develop melena as well as increased lower abdominal and pelvic pain with intermittent fevers despite IV steroid treatment. The patient was trialed on IV infliximab also without significant improvement. After several weeks of steroid and biologic treatment, he developed increased abdominal pain with tachycardia and hemodynamic instability. His examination was significant for peritonitis with abdominal distension concerning for fulminant colitis. Colorectal surgery was consulted and proceeded to do an emergent total abdominal colectomy and end ileostomy. Intraoperatively he was found to have a small anterior distal rectal perforation. The decision was made to drain this area widely with rectal drain and fecal diversion and start him on IV antibiotic therapy. His final pathology from the index operation showed ulceration and acute colitis. There was no chronic crypt architectural distortion such as crypt dropout, disarray, crypt branching or basal plasmacytosis that are often seen in inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). There was also increased apoptotic bodies and mitoses that were not consistent with IBD. After reviewing the clinical presentation, his disease progression, and final pathology, the treating team diagnosed the patient with HIV-associated colitis.

articles.title: Cardiac fibrosis and heart failure: Metabolic stress, circadian dysregulation, and extracellular matrix remodeling.
articles.abstract: Diabetes is a major risk factor for heart failure and drives a distinct cardiomyopathic phenotype characterized by oxidative stress, metabolic inflexibility, mitochondrial dysfunction, and progressive myocardial remodeling. Central to this process is cardiac fibrosis, marked by excessive extracellular matrix deposition, increased myocardial stiffness, and impaired mechanotransduction. Emerging evidence identifies circadian rhythm disruption as an under recognized modifier of diabetic cardiac fibrosis. The circadian clock regulates daily oscillations in myocardial metabolism, redox balance, inflammatory signaling, and extracellular matrix turnover, thereby maintaining cardiac homeostasis. However, modern urbanization has introduced chronic exposure to artificial light at night, particularly blue light from digital devices, which suppresses melatonin and desynchronizes central and peripheral clocks. In diabetes, loss of circadian regulation amplifies TGF-β signaling, Rho-A/ROCK-mediated mechanotransduction, oxidative stress, and myofibroblast transformation. Understanding how circadian misalignment accelerates profibrotic remodeling may reveal novel chronotherapeutic strategies to reduce cardiac fibrosis and heart failure risk.

articles.title: NHSN central line day methodology: impact on CLABSI rates, benchmarking, and quality improvement across a multi-hospital health system.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Under current National Healthcare and Safety Network (NHSN) methodology for CLABSI reporting, patients with multiple, concurrent central lines are counted as one line day, potentially underestimating true central line exposure.

OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the impact of NHSN central line reporting guidelines on CLABSI rates, benchmarking, and quality improvement outcomes across a multi-hospital health system.

DESIGN: Retrospective observational study.

METHODS: Electronic health record (EHR) data was collected for 7,645 inpatients across three adult acute care and one pediatric acute care hospital from January 2024 through December 2024. Additional data from the academic medical center's intensive care units (ICU) was collected from January 2025 to July 2025. Reported and actual central line days were compared across hospitals and care settings.

RESULTS: Actual line days totaled 113,529 compared to 90,789 reported line days with significantly different proportions across hospitals (P < .001). The reduction in CLABSI rate calculation when using actual line days was largest at higher-acuity settings, with the academic medical center ICUs demonstrating a decrease from 1.54 to 1.03 per 1,000 line days, a 33% reduction. Evaluation of a quality improvement initiative revealed significant improvement across all three ICUs when using actual line days, compared to only two ICUs under reported data alone.

CONCLUSIONS: Current NHSN reporting methodology systematically underestimates central line exposure at higher-acuity hospitals, impacting CLABSI benchmarking and obscuring quality improvement initiatives. Health systems should consider monitoring both reported and actual line days when evaluating performance or the impact of quality improvement initiatives.

articles.title: "TRACEBACK has probably saved my life": experiences of being notified about clinically significant cancer genetic information by the Australian TRACEBACK program.
articles.journal: Genetics in medicine : official journal of the American College of Medical Genetics
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: The Australian TRACEBACK program retrospectively identified women with tubo-ovarian cancer diagnosed between 2000 and 2016 who did not have genetic testing, most of whom were now deceased. Germline panel sequencing of 10 ovarian cancer-related genes was performed on tissue blocks or stored DNA. Probands or next of kin were notified of the sequencing outcome if a pathogenic variant was found. This exploratory study aimed to understand the experiences of probands and next of kin of receiving information from TRACEBACK, often unexpectedly.

METHOD: Twenty-seven TRACEBACK participants were interviewed, and the qualitative data thematically analysed.

RESULTS: Many participants described their initial shock and distress when they were notified unexpectedly about the germline information. However, these feelings were moderated by a sense of pragmatism as they gained understanding of their cancer risk management options. The majority valued TRACEBACK for enabling them to clarify their cancer risk through cascade testing, which provided opportunities for cancer prevention measures. Participants suggested germline results should be returned to biologically related relatives to minimise the risk of information not being communicated to at-risk relatives.

CONCLUSION: The benefits of unexpectedly receiving genetic information from TRACEBACK outweighed any potential harms, but consideration about to whom notification occurs is needed.

articles.title: A Two-Year Recovery Report From the Emergency Medicine Association of Türkiye (EMAT) Perspective: The 6 February Kahramanmaraş Earthquakes.
articles.journal: Disaster medicine and public health preparedness
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: On 6 February 2023, sequential Mw 7.7 and 7.6 earthquakes devastated 11 provinces in Türkiye. Two years on, the Emergency Medicine Association of Türkiye (EMAT) assessed recovery from an emergency department (ED) perspective.

METHODS: We conducted a cross-sectional survey of emergency physicians and residents in the most affected provinces (Kahramanmaraş, Adıyaman, Malatya).

RESULTS: Respondents were predominantly male (81.1%) and residents (70.3%). Family routines had partly stabilized (48.6%), yet ongoing household mental-health problems were common (54.1%). Housing remained strained: most homes were slightly damaged (59.5%); 13.5% of physicians continued to live in temporary shelters. Concerns persisted about hospital structural safety (59.4%). Equipment issues centered on delayed maintenance/repair (64.9%). ED operations suffered from crowding (70.3%), workload related to staffing gaps (67.6%), and inadequate physical space (56.8%). Academic activity was disrupted (51.4%), with perceived declines in educational standards versus non-affected provinces (40.5%).

CONCLUSIONS: Two years post-earthquake, substantial deficits persist across infrastructure, workforce, equipment maintenance, psychosocial well-being, and training. EMAT recommends coordinated actions on structural safety, supply chains, psychosocial support, durable housing, academic workforce recovery, governance/coordination, targeted financial incentives, and continuous monitoring to restore resilient, high-quality emergency care in the region.

articles.title: Transforming value-based deep vein thrombosis care through a pharmacist-led clinic.
articles.journal: American journal of health-system pharmacy : AJHP : official journal of the American Society of Health-System Pharmacists
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To address gaps in deep vein thrombosis (DVT) care, our health system implemented a pharmacist-led DVT clinic to standardize treatment, provide immediate access to pharmacy and vascular surgery services, and reduce emergency department (ED) and inpatient utilization for DVT management.

METHODS: This was a retrospective, pre-post cohort study of a DVT clinic that centralized imaging, diagnosis, anticoagulant initiation, and pharmacy services into a single outpatient location. Patients diagnosed with a DVT between January 1, 2023, and December 31, 2024, were included. The co-primary outcomes were the proportion of systemwide DVT encounters occurring in the acute care setting compared before and after the DVT clinic opened (2023 vs 2024) and compared between patients seen in the clinic or not (2024 only). A χ2 test was used to analyze the co-primary outcomes, with significance defined as a P value of less than 0.05.

RESULTS: The pharmacist saw 205 patients across 363 visits in 2024. Compared to 2023 baseline data, the proportion of systemwide DVT encounters occurring in the ED in 2024 decreased from 88.6% to 53.3% (P < 0.001), while the rate of inpatient admission for DVT decreased from 25.5% to 13.9% (P < 0.001). Stratified analysis of the 2024 data demonstrated significantly lower acute care utilization for DVT among patients managed in the DVT clinic compared to those not seen, including for ED encounters (15.2% vs 91.5%; P < 0.001) and inpatient admissions (1.8% vs 26%; P < 0.001).

CONCLUSION: The pharmacist-led DVT clinic represents a transformative advancement in pharmacy practice, redefining the role of pharmacists in ambulatory care and establishing a replicable model to optimize value-based care that shifts treatment for appropriate populations from acute to outpatient management.

articles.title: Physical activity, atrial fibrillation and the dose-response relationship: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIM: Regular physical activity (PA) may reduce atrial fibrillation (AF) risk in the general population, however, contemporary data suggests individuals engaging in the highest levels of PA may exhibit a paradoxical rise in AF risk. The point at which the dose-response curve reverses remains unclear. This meta-analysis aimed to assess the association between PA and AF across the full continuum of PA exposure.

METHODS: Four databases were searched (from January 1990 to June 2025). Eligible studies included those that reported PA exposure compared against a sedentary control group and assessed AF incidence or prevalence. PA exposures were standardised to metabolic equivalent of task hours per week (MET-hr/wk). Pooled odds ratios (ORs) were calculated using a weighted random-effects model. A weighted restricted cubic spline model of logarithmic odds was used to produce a dose-response curve.

RESULTS: 37 studies were included (n = 1,298,291 individuals). In the general population, PA was associated with a reduction in odds of AF by 22% (22 studies; OR 0.78; 95% CI 0.68, 0.89). Athlete status was associated with an increase in the odds of AF (15 studies; OR 2.74; 95% CI 1.72, 4.39). Dose-response analysis (26 studies; n = 1,022,790 individuals) showed 26 MET-hr/wk of PA was associated with the greatest reduction in odds of AF, with doses beyond 78 MET-hr/wk associated with increased odds of AF; the equivalent of 6-7 hours per week of endurance training.

CONCLUSION: PA and AF demonstrate a U-shaped relationship whereby beyond a quantitative dose threshold of 78 MET-hr/wk, the protective effect of exercise may reverse.

articles.title: Developmental toxicity screening of methylene blue in a chick embryo in ovo model.
articles.abstract: Methylene blue (MB) is a clinically important agent used for acquired methemoglobinemia and selected critical care indications, yet its effects during early embryogenesis remain poorly defined. This study evaluated developmental toxicity following in ovo MB exposure, characterized dose-dependent embryolethality, estimated the median lethal dose (LD50), and assessed developmental outcomes across a lower-dose range.An initial analytical cohort of 360 fertilized chicken eggs was allocated to two experimental phases. In the lethal-dose phase, MB was administered into the air chamber at doses 1, 2, 4, or 8 mg/kg. In the low-dose phase, MB was administered at doses of 0.067, 0.125, 0.250, or 0.500 mg/kg. Each phase included a sham-control group and a saline vehicle-control group. Embryonic mortality, developmental progression, relative embryo weight, crown-rump length, and hatch-related outcomes were recorded during incubation. Mortality data were analyzed using control-corrected probit regression. In the lethal-dose phase, mortality increased dose-dependently, reaching 23.3%, 43.3%, 90.0%, and 100.0% at 1, 2, 4, and 8 mg/kg, respectively. The estimated LD50 was 2.01 mg/kg, with a 95% confidence interval of 1.68-2.40 mg/kg. In the low-dose phase, MB concentrations from 0.067 to 0.500 mg/kg did not significantly affect mortality, relative embryo weight, or crown-rump length compared with controls. These findings indicate a steep lethal response to MB in this model, while 0.500 mg/kg may be regarded as a provisional no-observed-adverse-effect level (NOAEL) candidate under the present experimental conditions. Direct clinical extrapolation is limited because the in ovo model lacks maternal metabolism, placental transfer, and fetal clearance.

articles.title: Physically interacting immune cells in cardiometabolic disease: established platelet-immune aggregates and emerging leukocyte-leukocyte complexes.
articles.abstract: Chronic immune activation contributes to cardiometabolic disease and has most often been attributed to soluble mediators or changes in individual immune-cell subsets. A complementary dimension of immune organization is captured by direct physical interactions between immune cells, detected in blood or dissociated samples. While most dual-lineage flow-cytometric events should still be excluded as technical doublets, a validated subset represents true cell-cell conjugates (i.e., physically interacting immune cells rather than antibody-antigen complexes). The evidence base, however, is uneven as platelet-leukocyte aggregates are well-established biomarkers of platelet activation and thromboinflammation, while circulating non-platelet immune cell-cell complexes, particularly T cell-monocyte complexes, remain an emerging field supported by relatively few primary studies. Across acute infection and vaccination, these complexes appear regulated and may reflect coordinated immune activation. In chronic inflammatory states, including HIV and metabolic dysfunction, persistent complexes have been associated with inflammation and cardiometabolic risk, although mechanistic and causal data remain limited. Here, we review the current evidence for circulating immune cell complexes, distinguish established platelet-containing aggregates from the nascent literature on other immune-cell pairings, discuss candidate mechanisms that may support their formation and persistence, outline methodological requirements for their study, and consider their potential as biomarkers and therapeutic-response tools in cardiometabolic disease.

articles.title: Diagnosis-related group front-page management, coding patterns and cost structure in diabetic nephropathy.
articles.journal: Health information management : journal of the Health Information Management Association of Australia
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Accurate medical record front-page (discharge summary face sheet) documentation supports diagnosis-related group (DRG) classification and payment review. Evidence on disease-specific management for diabetic nephropathy (DN) remains limited.

OBJECTIVE: To evaluate associations of refined front-page management with complication coding patterns, length of stay, total hospitalisation cost and cost structure in adults admitted principally for DN.

METHOD: We retrospectively compared 48 index hospitalisation episodes in 2023 with 85 episodes from January 2025 to February 2026 at Peking University First Hospital Linquan Hospital. Both periods used the International Classification of Diseases, Tenth Revision, National Clinical Edition 2.0 diagnosis dictionary and China Healthcare Security Diagnosis Related Groups 1.1 framework.

RESULTS: Drug cost proportion decreased from 26.7% to 16.1% (difference, -10.6 percentage points; 95% confidence interval (CI), -15.0 to -6.2; standardised mean difference (SMD), -0.97; p < 0.001), while medical service fee proportion increased from 17.9% to 21.3% (difference, 3.4 percentage points; 95% CI, 1.5-5.3; SMD, 0.60; p = 0.001). Total costs were unchanged (median (interquartile range), 3508.56 (2940.07-4186.97) vs. 3475.42 (2902.41-4161.56) RMB; p = 0.850). Coding with E11.700 (Type 2 diabetes mellitus with multiple complications) or E11.700x033 (Type 2 diabetes mellitus with multiple complications, diabetic nephropathy) increased from 0.0% to 52.9% (risk difference, 52.9 percentage points; 95% CI, 40.1-63.2; Cramer's V = 0.54; p < 0.001), compared with E11.201 + N08.3* (Type 2 diabetes mellitus with diabetic nephropathy; N08.3*, glomerular disorders in diabetes mellitus).

CONCLUSION: Refined front-page management was associated with more service-oriented costs and more complete capture of documented complications, without higher total costs.Implications for health information management practice:Disease-specific checklists and coder-physician review may strengthen payment-related data quality under DRG reimbursement.

articles.title: Risk Factors for Postcholecystectomy Diarrhea: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.journal: Journal of laparoendoscopic & advanced surgical techniques. Part A
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To systematically evaluate potential risk-associated factors for postcholecystectomy diarrhea (PCD) and provide evidence to support clinical risk identification.

METHODS: A systematic literature search was conducted in PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, Web of Science, Scopus, CNKI, Wanfang, and VIP from inception to March 2026. Observational studies reporting PCD risk factors in adults were included. Two researchers independently screened studies, extracted data, and assessed quality using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale and Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality checklist. Meta-analyses were conducted for comparable variables, and evidence quality was assessed using GRADE.

RESULTS: A total of 17 studies including 9148 postcholecystectomy patients, of whom 1493 developed PCD, were analyzed. Alcohol consumption (odds ratio [OR] = 2.10, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.24-3.57; moderate GRADE evidence) and nonlow-fat diet (OR = 1.95, 95% CI: 1.15-3.29; moderate GRADE evidence) were associated with increased PCD risk. Postoperative food intolerance was associated with PCD, although its role as an antecedent risk factor remains uncertain because the temporal relationship with diarrhea could not be established. Age analyses showed inconsistent results: younger patients (<50 versus ≥50 years) had higher PCD risk (OR = 3.49, 95% CI: 1.56-7.80; moderate GRADE evidence), whereas continuous age analyses were nonsignificant, suggesting a potential nonlinear association. Evidence for sex, body mass index (BMI), smoking, diabetes, gallbladder function, and psychological factors was limited or inconsistent. Considerable heterogeneity and differences in outcome definitions among studies were noted.

CONCLUSION: Alcohol consumption and a nonlow-fat diet may represent clinically relevant factors associated with PCD, while postoperative food intolerance requires cautious interpretation because its temporal relationship with diarrhea remains uncertain. Age may have a nonlinear association with PCD, whereas evidence for other factors remains limited or inconsistent. These findings may assist in recognizing patients at increased risk of PCD and inform preoperative counseling and postoperative management. High-quality, multicenter studies with standardized exposure and outcome definitions are warranted to further clarify PCD risk factors.

articles.title: [Urinary biomarkers: A promising tool for modern nephrology].
articles.abstract: To avoid the need for renal biopsy, which remains an invasive procedure, numerous urinary biomarkers have been investigated for the detection, risk stratification, and prediction of disease progression in patients with acute or chronic kidney disease. Often referred to as a form of "liquid biopsy," some of these molecular candidates, particularly proteins and peptides, have shown considerable robustness and clinical potential. This review outlines the concept of a biomarker and the key stages involved in its development, drawing on practical examples such as prognostic signatures for antenatal renal developmental abnormalities and the prediction of acute kidney injury, as well as diagnostic applications in common clinical settings, including glomerular diseases using urinary soluble CD163 and acute interstitial nephritis using CXCL9. Methods used for biomarker measurement are also discussed. Despite encouraging results, even the most advanced biomarkers have struggled to progress beyond external multicenter validation because of methodological challenges related to both the underlying technologies and the heterogeneity of patient cohorts. As of 2026, these biomarkers remain primarily research tools, and a broad consensus on their routine clinical use has yet to emerge.

articles.title: Calprotectin Accelerates Pathogenic Calciprotein Particle Maturation to Promote Vascular Calcification in Chronic Kidney Disease.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Vascular calcification is a hallmark of chronic kidney disease (CKD)-mineral and bone disorder and a major determinant of cardiovascular mortality. Secondary calciprotein particles (CPP2) are key mediators of vascular calcification; however, the mechanisms regulating their maturation and pathogenic properties remain incompletely understood. CPT (Calprotectin, S100A8/A9), a myeloid-derived inflammatory mediator, is elevated in CKD and predicts cardiovascular events and mortality, particularly under high-phosphate conditions, but the underlying mechanisms remain unclear.

METHODS: We investigated the role of CPT in vascular calcification using CKD-mineral and bone disorder mice with myeloid-specific CPT deletion. Aortic calcification was assessed by ex vivo imaging, histology, and calcium quantification. Serum calciprotein particle (CPP) fractions were determined by flow cytometry. Mechanistic studies were performed in vascular smooth muscle cells exposed to CPP2 in the presence or absence of macrophage-derived CPT. Calcification propensity was evaluated using the T50 assay, and CPP2 elemental composition was analyzed by high-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy-energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy.

RESULTS: Myeloid-specific CPT deletion significantly attenuated aortic calcification and osteogenic gene expression in CKD-mineral and bone disorder mice without altering renal function or systemic mineral parameters. These changes were accompanied by an increased circulating immature CPP fraction. Macrophage-derived CPT markedly enhanced CPP2-induced vascular smooth muscle cell calcification by accelerating CPP maturation, reflected by a shortened T50, and by altering CPP2 composition to be enriched in calcium and phosphate. Although no direct interaction between CPT and CPPs was detected, CPT modified the physicochemical milieu, including ionized calcium and pH. Consistently, CPP2 from CPT-deficient serum exhibited substantially reduced calcification potency, indicating that CPT shapes CPP pathogenicity by modulating particle quality rather than quantity. Importantly, CPT-mediated CPP maturation occurred in a cell-free milieu, indicating a TLR4-independent mechanism distinct from its known receptor-mediated actions.

CONCLUSIONS: CPT is a previously unrecognized regulator of pathogenic CPP maturation and composition, thereby promoting vascular calcification in CKD-mineral and bone disorder. Targeting CPT may represent a novel therapeutic strategy to attenuate vascular calcification in CKD.

articles.title: High-Potency P2Y12 Inhibitors Among Patients With Chronic Coronary Syndrome Undergoing PCI: An Analysis From the NCDR CathPCI Registry.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Clinical practice guidelines recommend the use of clopidogrel among patients with chronic coronary syndrome undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention. The frequency of high-potency P2Y12 inhibitors, such as ticagrelor or prasugrel, in this setting is not well known.

METHODS: Using the National Cardiovascular Data Registry CathPCI registry, we analyzed patients with chronic coronary syndrome undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention from April 2018 to June 2024, excluding those discharged on oral anticoagulants. Temporal trends in high-potency P2Y12 inhibitor prescription were examined. A mixed-effects multivariable logistic regression model with a random intercept for hospital was used to identify patient-, procedural-, and institutional-level factors associated with high-potency P2Y12 inhibitor prescription while accounting for within-hospital clustering. Between-hospital variation was quantified using the median odds ratio.

RESULTS: Among 783 977 patients across 1815 hospitals, 35% were prescribed a high-potency P2Y12 inhibitor at discharge. The use of high-potency P2Y12 inhibitors declined from 35% in 2018 to 31% in 2024 (P-trend=0.019), driven by a reduction in ticagrelor (from 29% to 23%, P-trend <0.001) despite a modest increase in prasugrel use (from 6.2% to 8%, P-trend=0.10). Male sex, prior myocardial infarction, and markers of procedural complexity (high-complexity/type C lesions, left main coronary artery, proximal left anterior descending artery, or use of mechanical circulatory support) were associated with higher odds of high-potency P2Y12 inhibitor prescription. In contrast, older age (≥75 years), prior stroke/transient ischemic attack, prior coronary artery bypass graft, severe renal dysfunction, and chronic total occlusion were associated with lower odds. University hospitals had lower odds of prescribing high-potency P2Y12 inhibitors, with considerable variability in prescription patterns among institutions (median odds ratio, 2.59).

CONCLUSIONS: Nearly one-third of chronic coronary syndrome patients undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention were discharged on high-potency P2Y12 inhibitors, with decreasing trends over time. Practice patterns reflected perceived ischemic versus bleeding risk and significant institutional variation, underscoring opportunities for quality improvement and guideline alignment.

articles.title: Cadaveric Meniscal Cartilage for Ear Reconstruction.
articles.abstract: A 73-year-old man with a left-sided superior helical rim defect after basal cell carcinoma resection underwent staged auricular reconstruction using cadaveric lateral meniscal cartilage. Autologous costal cartilage harvest was avoided because of underlying pulmonary disease and elevated operative risk. At reconstruction, the meniscal allograft was shaped using the contralateral ear as a template, inset beneath a postauricular flap, and later elevated with flap division and inset; the postauricular donor site was resurfaced with a split-thickness skin graft from the anterolateral thigh. The patient healed without complications and maintained satisfactory superior helical contour at 12-month follow-up. This case suggests that cadaveric meniscal cartilage may serve as a reasonable alternative structural graft for selected auricular defects when autologous cartilage harvest is undesirable or contraindicated, although further study is needed to define long-term outcomes, including resorption risk.

articles.title: In-Stent Restenosis in Transition: Interpreting the Rise of Adjunctive Therapy.
Registered nurse prescriber role in Ontario: barriers and facilitators of role implementation.
articles.abstract:
AIM: This study explored registered nurse (RN) prescribers' perspectives on educational preparation and identified barriers and facilitators to successful role adoption.

BACKGROUND: Registered nurse (RN) prescribing was introduced in Ontario in 2023 to improve access to care and optimize the nursing scope of practice. While educational programmes were developed rapidly, little is known about RN prescribers' experiences with role implementation and workplace integration.

PURPOSE: This study explored RN prescribers' perspectives on educational preparation and identified barriers and facilitators to successful role adoption.

METHODS: A mixed-methods design was used. A cross-sectional survey of 52 RN prescribers who completed a College of Nurses of Ontario-approved prescribing programme captured demographic data and employment experiences. Quantitative analysis included descriptive statistics, bivariate tests, and hierarchical regression. Fifteen participants completed semi-structured interviews, which were analysed thematically.

RESULTS: Quantitative findings indicated generally positive employment experiences, with higher satisfaction associated with supportive colleagues and management. Unrealistic employer expectations and lack of familiarity with RN prescribing scope were identified as barriers. Qualitative analysis revealed four themes: (1) value of prior RN experience, with most participants recommending 2-5 years before prescribing; (2) mentorship as a catalyst for role transition, and physician mentorship was most common; (3) colleague support and organizational culture as critical facilitators; and (4) role clarity and system-level barriers. Participants emphasized that although education prepared them to prescribe, workplace readiness and clear role expectations were essential for building confidence and ensuring safe practice.

CONCLUSION: Successful implementation of RN prescribing requires more than education; structured mentorship, supportive organizational culture, and standardized policies are vital. These findings inform strategies to strengthen RN prescribing integration and improve access to care.

articles.title: Disaster Report: Military Helicopter Crash in a Deployed Environment - Providers' and Patient's Perspectives.
articles.abstract: The crash of a military helicopter during a 2023 United States Army deployment produced a mass-casualty incident (MASCAL) in an austere setting. One of the casualties was an Emergency Medicine (EM) physician who oversaw point-of-injury (POI) triage and early casualty evacuation with a Special Operations Forces (SOF) medic to the nearest Role II Military Treatment Facility (MTF), followed by movement of the six most severely injured patients to Role III, and subsequent transfer to Landstuhl Regional Medical Center (LRMC) via Critical Care Air Transport Team (CCATT). This disaster report explores the EM physician's actions as the initial provider, another EM physician as a receiving provider for a multi-leg fixed-wing transport, and a practicing trauma surgeon's unique perspective as one of the significantly injured patients. The viewpoints in this report highlight operational decisions including dispersion of medical assets, dynamic triage, destination/platform selection, and significant stressors of flight. Disaster care pathways should anticipate aeromedical stressors, emphasize patient positioning and communication, and align evacuation decisions with changing resources and injury patterns. These lessons are directly relevant to prehospital/disaster systems operating in contested, austere, or resource-limited environments.

articles.title: Structure-Property Engineering in Ag23 Nanoclusters for Electrocatalytic Nitrate Reduction.
articles.abstract: Electrocatalytic nitrate reduction reaction (NO3RR) provides a sustainable pathway for ambient ammonia synthesis; however, achieving concurrent high activity, high selectivity and appropriate stability of catalysts remains a substantial challenge. Here we report the synthesis and structure-property engineering of a class of atomically precise silver nanoclusters via geometric tuning and copper substitution. Compared with the parent nanocluster Ag23(PET)18(PPh3)8 (abbreviated as Ag23-1), a Cu-substituted Ag19Cu4(SCH2PhCl)18(PPh3)4 nanocluster (i.e., Ag19Cu4) modulates the electronic structure and catalytic active sites, giving rise to an improved Faradaic efficiency (FE ∼71%) upon NO3RR electrocatalysis but with irreversible alteration of the metal oxidation states. Intriguingly, a geometry-tuned [Ag23(SAdm)12]3+ cluster (Ag23-2) exhibits enhanced stability due to its superatomic eight-electron shell structure (1S2|1P6||) and delivers an NH3 yield of ∼6.5 mgNH3·h-1·mg-1 cat at -0.9 V, outperforming the parent Ag23-1 and comparable with the Ag19Cu4 NCs. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations indicate that the reaction proceeds via a stepwise hydrogenation pathway, with the *NO2-to-*NO conversion serving as the rate-determining step, where the energy barriers can be efficiently lowered by the Ag19Cu4 NCs. This work illustrates that structural engineering constitutes an effective strategy for tailoring activity, selectivity, and stability in atomically precise nanocluster catalysts.

articles.title: Clinical and Sonographic Features of Neonatal Ovarian Cysts With Autoamputation.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Autoamputation is a rare but severe complication of neonatal ovarian cysts. This case series describes the clinical, sonographic, and pathological characteristics of neonatal ovarian cysts that progressed to autoamputation, compared with those that did not, based on a retrospective review of 19 cysts. We aim to help clinicians suspect autoamputation when managing complex neonatal ovarian cysts.

METHODS: Medical records of 18 neonates (19 ovarian cysts) treated at two medical centers between January 2012 and December 2023 were reviewed. All cysts appeared complex on postnatal ultrasonography. We documented prenatal and postnatal sonographic features (cyst size, solid components, septations, fluid-debris levels, calcification), timing of examinations, intraoperative findings (adhesions, autoamputation), and pathology results. Descriptive statistics and exploratory comparisons between autoamputation (n = 9 cysts) and non-autoamputation (n = 10 cysts) groups were performed, without claims of predictive modeling.

RESULTS: Of the 19 complex ovarian cysts, 9 (47.3%) were confirmed autoamputated at surgery. The autoamputation group showed a longer median interval from first complex features to surgery (68 vs. 21.5 days) and an older age at last postnatal ultrasound (11 vs. 1 days). Intra-abdominal adhesions were observed in 66.7% of autoamputation cases versus 10% of non-autoamputation cases. Follicles were absent in all autoamputated cysts on pathology but present in 90% of non-autoamputated cysts. Sonographic findings evolved over time: fluid-debris levels became the predominant feature with increasing duration, while calcification appeared late (22.2% in the autoamputation group).

CONCLUSION: Autoamputation of neonatal ovarian cysts was associated with a longer interval from first complex features to surgery, absence of follicles on pathology, and frequent intra-abdominal adhesions. Sonographic features evolved over time, with fluid-debris levels becoming common and calcification appearing late but with poor sonographic sensitivity. These observations may help clinicians better understand the evolution of complex neonatal ovarian cysts associated with autoamputation; however, the diagnostic and predictive value of these findings requires further validation.

articles.title: Cooperative Stem Cell Homing and Photothermal Protection Driven by an Injectable Hydrogel for Bone-Vascular Regeneration.
articles.abstract: Bone defects caused by trauma or disease present significant clinical challenges, necessitating advanced biomaterials that simultaneously recruit stem cells and orchestrate a conducive microenvironment for repair. Here, we present an injectable hydrogel system designed to drive integrated bone-vascular regeneration through targeted stem cell homing and localized metabolic rescue. The composite hydrogel, crosslinked from gelatin and oxidized starch, integrates liposome-encapsulated stromal cell-derived factor-1 (SDF-1) and MXene-enabled GelMA microspheres. This minimally invasive system addresses two critical regenerative phases. First, liposomal SDF-1 undergoes controlled release to effectively recruit endogenous bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs). Concurrently, under near-infrared irradiation, the MXene-GelMA microspheres generate mild localized heat stress (40-42 °C). Crucially, this targeted photothermal therapy acts as a metabolic rescue mechanism; it upregulates heat shock protein 70 (HSP70) in BMSCs to mitigate apoptosis, stimulating endothelial cells to promote robust angiogenesis. In vitro, this cooperative environment significantly enhanced osteogenic differentiation and vascular network formation. In vivo application in a rat critical-sized calvarial defect model validated the hydrogel's therapeutic efficacy. At 8 weeks, the composite system increased the bone volume fraction (BV/TV) by 21.07% compared to a commercial bone repair material, accompanied by extensive neovascularization. This multifunctional hydrogel establishes a synchronized, translatable strategy for advanced tissue engineering.

articles.title: Effects of Antimicrobial Mouthwashes on Oral Health and Blood Pressure: A Preliminary Parallel Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Although antimicrobial mouthwashes vary in efficacy and safety for managing biofilm-induced gingivitis, concerns remain regarding their potential to reduce nitric oxide bioavailability and increase hypertension risk. Therefore, we investigated whether octenidine is more effective and causes fewer adverse events than chlorhexidine, and whether antimicrobial mouthwash use increases hypertension risk.

METHODS: In this parallel randomized controlled trial, 90 participants were randomly allocated (1:1:1) to rinse with 10 mL of 2% saline (Group I), 0.2% chlorhexidine (Group II), or 0.1% octenidine (Group III) for 21 days. Co-primary outcomes (clinical parameters and blood pressure) and secondary outcomes (salivary bacterial count, adverse events, and pulse pressure) were assessed over 42 days.

RESULTS: At day 22, antimicrobial mouthwashes significantly reduced clinical (29%-52%) and microbial (> 92%) measures (p < 0.001), whereas saline produced minimal changes (p > 0.05). Salivary nitrate levels showed the opposite trend. Groups II and III showed comparable efficacy, but octenidine was associated with fewer adverse events. Although systolic blood pressure increased slightly in all groups, the changes were clinically insignificant. Elevated pulse pressure in antimicrobial groups returned to baseline by Day 42.

CONCLUSIONS: Octenidine (0.1%) was safer and comparably effective to chlorhexidine. Short-term antimicrobial mouthwash had no clinically significant effect on blood pressure.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: CTRI/2024/08/072091 (India), date: 07/08/2024. URL: https://ctri.nic.in/Clinicaltrials/pmaindet2.php?EncHid=MTEwOTY5&Enc.

articles.title: Successful treatment of a patient with ventriculo-peritoneal shunt-associated meningitis caused by Streptococcus pyogenes.
articles.abstract: Ventriculoperitoneal shunt (VPS)-associated bacterial meningitis is a significant neurosurgical complication that can occasionally present atypical symptoms. We report a rare case of Streptococcus pyogenes meningitis in a 40-day-old infant with a history of hydrocephalus managed by VPS placement. The patient presented with vomiting, diarrhea, fever, and -abdominal distension. Microbial culture of the removed VPS valve confirmed the diagnosis, revealing Streptococcus pyogenes. Despite the strain's sensitivity to penicillin G, the patient was treated with cefotaxime and vancomycin due to negative cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) cultures and clinical improvement under this regimen. Early removal of the VPS and initiation of targeted antibiotic therapy, along with the placement of an external ventricular drain (EVD), led to a full recovery. This case highlights the importance of prompt diagnosis, tailored treatment strategies, and the critical role of infection control measures in managing VPS-related complications.

articles.title: Autoimmune Hepatitis: 2026 Update.
articles.abstract: Autoimmune hepatitis (AIH) is an autoimmune liver disease characterized by immune-mediated hepatocellular destruction. This review provides a comprehensive update on the changes in the clinical landscape of and advancements in therapy for AIH up to 2026. Recent epidemiological data indicate a significant increase in both the incidence and prevalence of AIH worldwide, emphasizing potential shifts in environmental triggers and heightened disease awareness. Diagnosing AIH remains intricate owing to atypical manifestations; however, the newly updated 2025 European Association for the Study of the Liver clinical practice guidelines introduce refined simplified diagnostic criteria that incorporate contemporary laboratory platforms and international pathology standards to enhance real-world sensitivity. Immunosuppressive therapy continues to be the cornerstone of management. Corticosteroids remain the standard first-line treatment, while the upfront combination of prednisolone and mycophenolate mofetil is increasingly recommended alongside conventional azathioprine regimens. Achieving a complete biochemical response-defined as the normalization of transaminases and immunoglobulin G within 6 to 12 months-has emerged as a powerful, universally recognized surrogate endpoint for long-term prognosis, strongly predicting lower liver-related mortality and transplantation rates across both Western and Asian cohorts. Furthermore, this review addresses complex clinical entities, including drug-induced autoimmune-like hepatitis secondary to novel immunotherapies or vaccinations, and the phenotypic continuum of the primary biliary cholangitis-AIH overlap syndrome. Finally, we highlight the clinical utility of emerging, highly specific diagnostic biomarkers, such as anti-docking protein 2 antibodies-a promising candidate for seronegative cases, pending external multicenter validation-and outline essential directions for future AIH research.

articles.title: Long-Term Outcomes According to a Device-Assisted Enteroscopy Strategy after Capsule Endoscopy in Patients with Small Bowel Bleeding: A Nationwide Population-Based Cohort Study.
authors: Small Intestine Research Group of the Korean Association for the Study of Intestinal Diseases (KASID)
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND/AIMS: Although the use of device-assisted enteroscopy (DAE) has increased, few large-scale studies have examined long-term outcomes focused on small bowel (SB) bleeding. We analyzed National Health Insurance Service data to evaluate the clinical utility of DAE in patients with SB bleeding who underwent capsule endoscopy.

METHODS: We included a cohort of 11,690 patients who underwent capsule endoscopy for SB bleeding (identified using ICD-10 codes) between 2014 and 2022. Patients were categorized into three groups: no DAE, diagnostic DAE, and therapeutic DAE. We assessed four major outcomes, including the probability and factors associated with SB rebleeding, severe SB rebleeding, rebleeding-related mortality, and all-cause mortality.

RESULTS: Of 11,690 patients, 5,211 were included in the analysis (no DAE, n=4,960; diagnostic DAE, n=173; therapeutic DAE, n=78). The probability of SB rebleeding and severe SB rebleeding was highest in the therapeutic DAE group, followed by the diagnostic DAE and no DAE groups (p<0.001), with 7-year rebleeding probabilities of 19.8%, 15.8%, and 5.0%, respectively. Rebleeding-related and all-cause mortality were also highest in the therapeutic DAE group, followed by the diagnostic DAE and no DAE groups (p<0.001 for both), with 7-year rebleeding-related mortality probabilities of 9.3%, 5.9%, and 2.7%, respectively.
