Risk factors for both rebleeding-related and all-cause mortality included age, male sex, liver cirrhosis, and malignancy.

CONCLUSIONS: Patients who require therapeutic DAE for SB bleeding remain at increased long-term risk of rebleeding and mortality. These findings likely reflect their greater underlying disease burden and highlight the need for individualized long-term surveillance and careful management of comorbidities, even after therapeutic intervention.

articles.title: Association of waist circumference trajectories with incident chronic kidney disease.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is a major public health burden. Waist circumference (WC) is associated with CKD risk, but the prognostic significance of longitudinal WC change remains uncertain. We examined the association between WC trajectories and incident CKD in Korean adults.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 5,429 adults aged 40-69 years from the Korean Genome and Epidemiology Study Ansan-Ansung cohort who were free of CKD at baseline and during the 6-year exposure period. WC trajectories were classified as stable, increasing, or decreasing using Gaussian finite mixture modeling. Incident CKD during the subsequent 12-year event accrual period was defined as new-onset reduced estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) <60 mL/min/1.73 m2 or urine dipstick albumin ≥1+ on two consecutive measurements. Multivariable Cox models estimated hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs).

RESULTS: Over a median follow-up of 11.8 years, 576 participants (10.6%) developed CKD. Compared with the stable WC trajectory, the increasing WC trajectory was associated with a higher risk of incident CKD (adjusted HR, 1.41; 95% CI, 1.17-1.71), whereas the decreasing trajectory was not (adjusted HR, 0.83; 95% CI, 0.56-1.23). Secondary analyses showed higher risks of incident reduced eGFR and new-onset dipstick albuminuria in the increasing WC group, and time-varying Cox analysis supported the primary finding. Restricted cubic spline analysis demonstrated a significant linear dose-response relationship.

CONCLUSION: Serial WC increase may serve as a simple, clinically accessible marker of cumulative metabolic burden and future CKD risk.

articles.title: Catheter-related bloodstream infections, infective endocarditis, and vertebral osteomyelitis in adults receiving home parenteral nutrition: A descriptive cohort study.
articles.journal: JPEN. Journal of parenteral and enteral nutrition
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Intestinal failure patients receiving home parenteral nutrition are at risk of catheter-related bloodstream infection. Metastatic infections include infective endocarditis and vertebral osteomyelitis. We aimed to investigate the incidences of catheter-related bloodstream infection, infective endocarditis, and vertebral osteomyelitis in type 3 intestinal failure patients.

METHODS: This was a cohort study conducted in a Danish referral intestinal failure center. All data on catheter-related bloodstream infections, infective endocarditis, and vertebral osteomyelitis were retrieved from medical records on patients receiving home parenteral nutrition through tunneled cuffed central venous access devices or peripherally inserted central catheters from 01 January 2019 to 31 December 2023.

RESULTS: A total of 323 patients (209 females) were included, totaling 913 catheters and 293,650 catheter days. The catheter-related bloodstream infection incidence was 0.93 per 1,000 catheter days (95% CI: 0.82-1.03) over the 5-year period, with a statistically significantly higher incidence for tunneled cuffed central venous access devices than for peripherally inserted central catheters (1.10 [95% CI: 0.95-1.26] vs. 0.66 [95% CI: 0.52-0.81] per 1,000 catheter days, respectively). Thirteen cases of infective endocarditis (0.04 per 1,000 catheter days [95% CI: 0.02-0.07]) and ten cases of vertebral osteomyelitis (0.03 per 1000 [95% CI: 0.01-0.06]) were identified.

CONCLUSION: The catheter-related bloodstream infection incidence is within the acceptable range recommended by current guidelines. The incidence of infective endocarditis is higher, and that of vertebral osteomyelitis is similar to those in other studies. Catheter-related bloodstream infection is a serious complication that may lead to infective endocarditis or vertebral osteomyelitis, underscoring the need for timely detection and management.

articles.title: Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonists in Multiple Sclerosis: A Topical Narrative Review.
articles.journal: Annals of clinical and translational neurology
articles.abstract: The glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonists (RAs) are a relatively new class of drugs that were initially approved by the US Food and Drug Administration to improve glycemic control in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus and, subsequently, weight reduction in patients with obesity. Multiple sclerosis (MS) is commonly associated with comorbidities for which GLP-1RAs are indicated. An increasing prevalence of comorbid chronic diseases has increased the number of people living with MS (pwMS) who are prescribed a GLP-1RA, for indications of obesity, diabetes, obstructive sleep apnea, metabolic-associated steatohepatitis, and/or chronic kidney disease. This review addresses the following key considerations: (1) the use of GLP-1RAs for weight loss in pwMS and obesity, including considerations related to drug tolerability and safety; (2) the efficacy of the GLP-1RAs for their approved non-MS indications in pwMS; and (3) the potentially pleiotropic effects of the GLP-1RAs on the MS disease course beyond their approved indications.

articles.title: Unravelling Staff's Experiences: An Exploration of Staff Attitudes Towards Parental Involvement in Residential Care.
articles.journal: Journal of intellectual disability research : JIDR
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In residential care for people with intellectual disabilities, support staff take over daily care responsibilities for residents with severe intellectual disabilities. However, parents often remain involved in their support. Yet little is known about the attitudes of support staff towards parental involvement in daily care.

METHOD: A vignette-based, qualitatively driven mixed-methods study was conducted, using structured interviews with 33 participants. A qualitative content analysis was used to analyse the data, and descriptive statistics were provided about the participants' responses.

RESULTS: The findings showed diverse cognitive, affective and behavioural responses to the vignettes. Staff were mainly sympathetic towards parental involvement but also highlighted moments of friction or uncertainty.

CONCLUSIONS: Examining staff's attitudes provided insight into how (past) experiences shaped collaboration with parents. More insight into the coping strategies towards the emotional responses of parents and the impact of negative experiences is needed to sufficiently support staff in collaboration with parents.

articles.title: Event-Weighted Desaturation Burden and Cardiovascular Mortality in Sleep Apnoea: Findings from a Large Community-Based Prospective Cohort.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Obstructive sleep apnoea's prognostic value is limited by reliance on the apnoea-hypopnoea index (AHI), which fails to capture physiological heterogeneity of respiratory events. We developed a composite metric, event-weighted desaturation burden (EWDB), integrating weighted respiratory event load, regularity of consecutive inter-event intervals, and cumulative desaturation area. We evaluated its association with cardiovascular mortality and its incremental prognostic value compared with AHI and established hypoxic metrics.

METHODS: We analysed 4,904 adults from the Sleep Heart Health Study with baseline polysomnography and adjudicated follow-up. EWDB was derived by combining a respiratory weighted index, a distribution factor based on inter-event interval regularity, and event-linked hypoxic burden (HB).

RESULTS: The primary outcome was cardiovascular mortality. Over a median follow-up of approximately 11 years, 341 cardiovascular deaths occurred. In fully adjusted multivariable Cox models, higher EWDB was independently associated with cardiovascular mortality. However, AHI and HB associations were attenuated and lost statistical significance after full adjustment. EWDB (per 1-SD increase) remained robustly associated with cardiovascular mortality, whereas AHI did not. Incorporating EWDB into a comprehensive clinical model provided incremental risk stratification. Similar robust associations were observed for fatal coronary heart disease and incident heart failure.

CONCLUSIONS: EWDB was independently associated with cardiovascular mortality and provided incremental prognostic information beyond established clinical and sleep-related factors in this cohort. By integrating respiratory event intensity, cumulative burden, and inter-event interval regularity, EWDB may better characterize cardiovascular stress related to sleep-disordered breathing.

articles.title: Human angiostrongyliasis: the past, present, and future.
articles.abstract: Human angiostrongyliasis is an emerging foodborne zoonosis caused predominantly by Angiostrongylus cantonensis and Angiostrongylus costaricensis, which produce distinct neurological and abdominal forms of disease, respectively. Human infection occurs primarily through ingestion of raw or undercooked gastropod intermediate hosts, paratenic hosts such as freshwater prawns and crabs, or fresh produce contaminated with infective third-stage larvae (L3). A. cantonensis is the principal cause of neuroangiostrongyliasis and eosinophilic meningitis, whereas A. costaricensis causes abdominal angiostrongyliasis, characterized by eosinophilic inflammation involving the intestinal wall and mesenteric vasculature. Although historically concentrated in tropical and subtropical regions, A. cantonensis has expanded its geographic range, while A. costaricensis remains predominantly distributed in Latin America. This changing epidemiology is influenced by climate and environmental change, host redistribution, globalisation, urbanisation, and dietary practices. Diagnosis remains challenging and requires integration of epidemiological exposure, clinical findings, and laboratory and imaging results. For neuroangiostrongyliasis, cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) eosinophilia, serological testing, and molecular assays, including increasingly sensitive real-time PCR approaches, provide important diagnostic evidence, whereas abdominal angiostrongyliasis frequently requires imaging, histopathology, and, where available, molecular or serological confirmation. Treatment of neuroangiostrongyliasis remains centred on corticosteroids and management of intracranial pressure, while the role of albendazole has historically been controversial but is increasingly supported as adjunctive therapy when administered with corticosteroids. In abdominal angiostrongyliasis, surgical management remains an important component of diagnosis and treatment, particularly in patients with intestinal complications. Emerging molecular diagnostics, host-directed therapies, novel anthelmintic strategies, and improved surveillance approaches offer promising opportunities for future disease control. Continued progress will require an integrated One Health approach combining epidemiological surveillance, improved diagnostic capacity, evidence-based clinical management, food-safety education, and ecological monitoring of transmission.

articles.title: Improved Visualization of Heart Valves With 4D-CT Using a Novel Motion Correction Algorithm.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Motion artifacts remain a limitation of cardiac CT when assessing both native and prosthetic heart valves, particularly during phases of rapid motion. This may lead to reduced image quality, potentially impairing the evaluation of valvular movement and pathology. The purpose of this study was to evaluate whether a novel reconstruction-based motion correction algorithm improves image quality and reduces motion artifacts of native and prosthetic heart valves compared with standard reconstructions in photon-counting detector CT (PCD-CT).

MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this retrospective single-center study, 57 patients [21 women; median age, 71 (interquartile range, 57 to 78 y)] who underwent clinically indicated 4D cardiac CT for suspected native and prosthetic valvular disease were included. Images were acquired using retrospectively electrocardiography (ECG)-gated spiral dual-source PCD-CT without ECG-pulsing. Images were reconstructed in 10% steps throughout the RR-interval using both standard (TrueStack) and an otherwise identical reconstruction using the novel motion correction algorithm (ZeeFreePlus). Subjective image quality and motion artifacts were independently assessed by 2 blinded, experienced readers using a 4-point visual analog scale for 3 categories: valve frame/annulus, valve leaflets, and valvular pathology. Objective analysis included quantification of the volume of artifacts throughout the cardiac cycle.

RESULTS: A total of 68 valves were evaluated, including 57 prosthetic valves (22 transcatheter aortic valve replacements and 19 surgical valves, 11 mitral valves, and 5 tricuspid valve interventions) and 11 native valves. Valvular pathology was present in 29 cases, with the most prevalent being hypoattenuated leaflet thickening in 14/29 (48%). Motion-corrected reconstructions significantly improved image quality and reduced motion artifacts across all cardiac phases and all categories (all, P<0.001). The largest improvements were observed during systole, particularly at 10% of the RR-interval, with significantly greater gains than during diastole (P<0.05). Improvements were consistent across aortic and atrioventricular prosthetic valves and translated into improved visualization of valvular pathology (P<0.001). Objective quantitative analysis corroborated the subjective image quality findings by demonstrating reductions in the volumes of motion-induced artifacts when using the algorithm (P<0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: A novel motion correction algorithm substantially reduced motion artifacts and improved image quality in both native and prosthetic heart valve imaging with PCD-CT, with the largest improvements in systole. These benefits resulted in enhanced visualization of valvular pathology, potentially reinforcing the growing clinical role of cardiac CT for the assessment of valve disease.

articles.title: Diagnostic Variability in the Modified Kocher Criteria for Septic Arthritis of the Hip: Implications for Aspiration Decision-Making.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study evaluates the clinical application of the modified Kocher criteria (MKC) in assessing septic arthritis of the hip (SAH) at a tertiary children's hospital.

METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was conducted on subjects presenting to the emergency department and receiving a hip ultrasound over a 1-year period. Those without a hip effusion were excluded. Patient demographics, symptoms, imaging, labs, treatment, and final diagnoses were collected. SAH was defined clinically by the treating team, supported by patient presentation, lab/imaging findings, operative intervention, and antibiotic therapy. Descriptive and bivariate statistics based on variable distribution were used during analysis.

RESULTS: A total of 326 subjects were identified, and 110 had effusion present on ultrasound. Eighteen (16.4%) underwent aspiration. Aspirated subjects had significantly higher cumulative MKC scores (P=0.001) and higher median values for all individual MKC components, including CRP, WBC, ESR, maximum temperature, and a higher prevalence of non-weight-bearing (P<0.05). SAH was diagnosed in 38.9% of the aspirated group (n=7), with MKC scores of 2 (n=2), 3 (n=3), and 5 (n=2). Aspiration rates increased across MKC scores 0 to 3, and synovial fluid inflammatory markers trended higher with increasing MKC scores. Thirteen subjects with an MKC score of 2 were not aspirated; final diagnoses included transient synovitis (n=9), hip effusion, osteomyelitis, sickle cell crisis, or limp (each n=1). Three subjects with an MKC score of 3 were not aspirated and later diagnosed with metastatic tumor, osteomyelitis, and rheumatic fever.

CONCLUSIONS: Pediatric patients undergoing hip aspiration with a concern for SAH had significantly higher cumulative MKC scores and higher levels of all individual MKC components than their nonaspirated counterparts. However, nearly 15% of patients had MKC scores of 2 or 3 that were not aspirated in the ED, and SAH was identified even in lower-score subjects. While MKC scores appear to influence clinical decision-making, diagnostic variability remains. In patients with intermediate MKC scores of 2 to 3, the criteria should prompt further evaluation, taking into consideration the overall clinical context to guide aspiration decision-making.

articles.title: Similar Presentations, Divergent Clinical Courses: Pediatric Headache Care in the Emergency Department.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pediatric emergency department (ED) headache presentations may follow heterogeneous clinical courses.

OBJECTIVE: To compare presentation characteristics, migraine order-set activation, pain-score change, treatment intensity, and health care utilization between pediatric ED headache encounters with and without a clinician-documented persistent/intractable headache.

METHODS: We conducted a multisite retrospective cross-sectional study of children aged 3 to 18 years presenting to 2 pediatric EDs with headache or migraine as a chief complaint from 2019 to 2023. Encounters were classified by clinician documentation of an intractable/refractory headache diagnosis or persistent symptoms despite initial treatment. The primary outcome was change from arrival to posttreatment/disposition pain score. Sensitivity analyses were restricted to each patient's first encounter and to clinician-documented migraine or status migrainosus.

RESULTS: Among 529 encounters, 18.5% had a documented persistent/intractable headache course. Most presentation characteristics were similar, although symptom duration and pulmonary comorbidity differed. Order-set activation did not differ significantly (76.5% vs. 68.2%; P = 0.106). Encounters with a persistent/intractable headache had less pain improvement [median: -4 (interquartile range: -6.75 to -1) vs. -5 (interquartile range: -7 to -3); P = 0.002], received more medications, radiologic imaging (39.8% vs. 26%; P = 0.006), neurology consultation (56.1% vs. 39.4%; P = 0.003), hospitalization (19.4% vs. 3.2%; P < 0.001), and 30-day return ED visits (10.2% vs. 4.6%; P = 0.049). The pain-score difference was attenuated in the first-encounter analysis (P = 0.060), but persisted in the clinician-documented migraine subgroup (P = 0.006).

CONCLUSION: Headache presentation characteristics and order-set activation did not distinguish the ED course, but pain improvement, treatment intensity, and utilization differed during ED care. Prospective studies should evaluate standardized early reassessment measures.

articles.title: Predictive Value of Preoperative Inflammatory and Nutritional Indices for Revision Surgery After Major Lower Extremity Amputation in Patients With Wagner Stage 5 Diabetic Foot.
articles.journal: Medical science monitor : international medical journal of experimental and clinical research
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND Major lower extremity amputation is a severe complication of diabetic foot disease, leading to high morbidity and repeat surgeries. Although systemic inflammatory and nutritional markers have been studied as prognostic factors in diabetic foot ulcers, their role in predicting revision surgery after major amputation is unclear. This study aims to evaluate the link between preoperative inflammatory and nutritional indices and revision surgery after major lower extremity amputation. MATERIAL AND METHODS This multicenter retrospective study reviewed medical records of patients with Wagner stage 5 diabetic foot disease who had major lower extremity amputation at 3 hospitals. Revision included stump shortening or re-amputation at a more proximal level. Patients were divided into revision and non-revision groups. Demographic characteristics, amputation side and level, and preoperative laboratory parameters were recorded. The Prognostic Nutritional Index, neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio, platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio, and monocyte-to-lymphocyte ratio were evaluated. Intergroup comparisons were performed to evaluate the association between these indices and the risk of revision surgery. RESULTS A total of 89 patients were studied; 35 (39.3%) needed revision surgery, while 54 (60.7%) healed successfully without further surgery. There were no significant differences between groups in age, sex, preoperative revascularization, amputation levels, laboratory parameters, or inflammatory and nutritional indices. No link was found between these indices and revision surgery. CONCLUSIONS Systemic inflammatory and nutritional indices before major lower extremity amputation in patients with diabetic foot were not linked to postoperative revision surgery. Risks may be more affected by local factors such as residual infection, limb perfusion, and stump viability. Future studies combining systemic biomarkers with vascular assessment could better predict revision risk.

articles.title: Invasive Bacterial Infections Other Than Escherichia coli and Streptococcus agalactiae in Febrile Infants Younger Than 90 Days: A Multicenter Emergency Department Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Invasive bacterial infections (IBIs) in febrile infants ≤90 days are mostly caused by Escherichia coli and Streptococcus agalactiae. However, data on IBIs caused by other pathogens remain limited.

METHODS: We conducted a multicenter retrospective study of febrile infants aged ≤90 days diagnosed with IBI between 2008 and 2022 at 12 Spanish pediatric emergency departments. Epidemiology, clinical features, microbiology and outcomes of cases caused by pathogens other than E. coli/S. agalactiae were analyzed. Adverse outcomes included death, inotropic or respiratory support, acute complications, or sequelae.

RESULTS: Among 375 infants with IBI, 106 (28.3%) had infections caused by pathogens other than E. coli/S. agalactiae. The most frequent pathogens were Staphylococcus aureus (n = 30, 8.0%), Streptococcus pneumoniae (n = 15, 4.0%) and Enterococcus faecalis (n = 14, 3.7%). Most cases presented as isolated bacteremia (65.1%), followed by bacteremic urinary tract infection (18.9%) and meningitis (12.3%); 46.2% of infants with meningitis had a concomitant urinary tract infection. The distribution of pathogens varied according to age, with S. aureus being more frequent among younger infants and S. pneumoniae accounting for 8.6% of IBIs in infants aged 61-90 days. Listeria monocytogenes caused 1.3% of IBIs, with only 1 case identified in the last decade. Adverse outcomes occurred in 7.5% of infants with infections caused by other pathogens and 8.6% of those with E. coli/S. agalactiae (absolute risk difference, -1.0% [95% confidence interval, -7.1 to 5.0]).

CONCLUSIONS: IBIs caused by pathogens other than E. coli/S. agalactiae accounted for a substantial proportion of cases and showed an age-dependent distribution. Most presented as isolated bacteremia, while meningitis was associated with a higher observed frequency of adverse outcomes.

articles.title: The effect of different exercise modalities on the maximal left ventricular outflow tract gradient in patients with obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Assessment of maximally provoked LVOT obstruction (LVOTO) guides treatment decisions in obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM). Guidelines recommend various maneuvers, with exercise stress echocardiography (ESE) as the preferred method if others fail. Comparative data are limited. Therefore, in this prospective study, 20 patients with obstructive HCM underwent transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) with continuous wave Doppler measuring LVOT gradients at rest, during the Valsalva maneuver, handgrip exercise at 30% and 50% of maximal hand force, squats, and bicycle ESE, with the aim of comparing commonly used maneuvers and evaluating handgrip exercise as a potential alternative for eliciting LVOTO.

RESULTS: The mean resting LVOT gradient was 38.9 ± 31.4 mmHg. Handgrip exercise caused no significant change of LVOT gradients. In contrast, gradients increased markedly during the Valsalva maneuver (98.9 ± 52.8 mmHg), squats (120.3 ± 68.8 mmHg), and bicycle ESE (83.4 ± 43.3 mmHg; p < 0.001 vs. rest). There was no significant difference between Valsalva, squats, and ESE (p = NS). Squats induced the maximal gradient in 50% of patients. Performance time was significantly shorter for the Valsalva maneuver (15 s) and squats (1 min 23 s ± 28 s) than for bicycle ESE (15 min 54 s ± 5 min 46 s; p < 0.01).

CONCLUSION: The Valsalva maneuver, squats, and bicycle ESE are equally effective in provoking LVOTO, whereas handgrip exercise is not. Given their simplicity, low cost, and shorter testing time, squats may serve as a practical adjunct to the Valsalva maneuver for LVOT gradient provocation in routine clinical assessment of obstructive HCM.

CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: German Clinical Trials Register (ID: DRKS00034473).

articles.title: Predictors of mortality and severity of hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy among neonates with birth asphyxia at Jimma University Medical Center, Southwest Ethiopia: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy is a major cause of neonatal mortality and long-term neurodevelopmental impairment, particularly in low- and middle-income countries. Evidence regarding HIE severity, survival outcomes, and predictors of mortality remains limited in Ethiopia. This study assessed the severity, survival outcomes, and predictors of mortality among neonates with HIE admitted to Jimma University Medical Center (JUMC), Southwest Ethiopia.

METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was conducted among 373 neonates diagnosed with HIE following birth asphyxia and admitted to Jimma University Medical Center(JUMC). Data were extracted from medical records using a structured checklist. Kaplan-Meier survival analysis and the log-rank test were used to estimate and compare survival experiences. Cox proportional hazards regression identified predictors of mortality, while ordinal logistic regression was employed to determine factors associated with increasing HIE severity. Statistical significance was declared at p < 0.05.

RESULTS: Among the 373 neonates, 121 (32.4%) had Stage I HIE, 169 (45.3%) had Stage II HIE, and 83 (22.3%) had Stage III HIE. The overall mortality rate was 9.1%, and the median event-free survival time was 30.6 days. Kaplan-Meier analysis showed survival probabilities of 0.99 (95% CI: 0.99-1.00) at day 1, 0.75 (95% CI: 0.65-0.86) at day 20, and 0.29 (95% CI: 0.15-0.59) at day 40. Survival differed significantly across HIE stages (log-rank χ² = 45.4, p = 0.00). Factors independently associated with increasing HIE severity included outborn status (AOR = 1.50; 95% CI: 1.00-2.26), acute kidney injury (AOR = 1.93; 95% CI: 1.21-3.08), macrosomia (AOR = 2.54; 95% CI: 1.29-5.07), and hypoglycemia (AOR = 1.59; p = 0.01). Maternal gestational diabetes showed a borderline association with severity (AOR = 1.99; 95% CI: 0.97-4.10). Predictors of mortality included Stage II HIE (AHR = 3.24; 95% CI: 2.55-4.13), acute kidney injury (AHR = 3.27; 95% CI: 2.47-4.31), Apgar score ≤ 3 (AHR = 3.71; 95% CI: 2.59-5.31), Apgar score 4-6 (AHR = 1.67; 95% CI: 1.30-2.13), outborn status (AHR = 1.62; 95% CI: 1.29-2.04), and neonatal sepsis (AHR = 2.12).

CONCLUSION: Hypoxic-Ischemic Encephalopathy remains a substantial contributor to neonatal mortality at Jimma University Medical Ceneter. Survival declined markedly with increasing disease severity. Mortality was independently associated with HIE stage, acute kidney injury, low Apgar score, outborn status, and neonatal sepsis, while HIE severity was associated with outborn status, acute kidney injury, macrosomia, and hypoglycemia. Strengthening referral systems, improving perinatal care, and ensuring early detection and management of neonatal complications are essential to improve neonatal outcomes.

articles.title: Effect of injectable platelet rich fibrin augmented with vitamin c compared to injectable platelet rich fibrin alone on healing of necrotic mature single rooted teeth with chronic periapical periodontitis following regenerative endodontic therapy (a randomized controlled trial).
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To assess the healing potential, postoperative pain and clinical normalcy associated with injectable platelet-rich fibrin combined with Vitamin C in regenerative endodontic procedure using cone-beam computed tomography and two-dimensional radiograph.

METHODS: Twenty-eight healthy patients with mature permanent single-rooted teeth diagnosed with pulp necrosis and chronic apical periodontitis were randomly allocated into two groups (n = 14). Regenerative endodontic treatment was performed using injectable platelet-rich fibrin combined with Vitamin C (intervention group) and injectable platelet-rich fibrin alone (control group). Periapical healing was assessed using CBCT and periapical radiographs over 12 months. Postoperative pain and clinical normalcy were also evaluated.

RESULTS: Both groups showed significant lesion reduction at 12 months (P = 0.001), with no significant between-group differences in postoperative lesion size (P = 0.981) or reduction magnitude (P = 0.497). CBCT-PAI scores improved in both groups without significant intergroup differences at baseline or follow-up. Two-dimensional radiographs showed a baseline difference (P = 0.007) but no postoperative differences; both groups demonstrated significant longitudinal reduction (P < 0.001). Postoperative pain scores were comparable between groups at all time points (P > 0.05), with a significant temporal decrease observed only in the intervention group (P = 0.001). All teeth remained asymptomatic during follow-up.

CONCLUSIONS: Both i-PRF combined with vitamin C and i-PRF alone appear to be effective regenerative scaffolds, demonstrating comparable clinical and radiographic outcomes in regenerative endodontic procedures.

CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: The study was registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (ID: NCT05585359), registered on 14 October 2022. Available at https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT05585359 .

articles.title: Molecular detection of biofilm-related genes and antimicrobial resistance patterns in Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolates from Northern Iran.
articles.abstract: Pseudomonas aeruginosa is widely recognized as one of the primary opportunistic pathogens responsible for a wide range of nosocomial infections, notably in immunocompromised patients. Antibiotic resistance and biofilm formation, as two major virulence factors of P. aeruginosa, are related to the persistence of prolonged infections. This study was designed to (1) evaluate the frequency of multidrug-resistant (MDR) P. aeruginosa in northern Iran and (2) analyze the frequency of biofilm-associated genes and their correlation with antimicrobial patterns. Clinical samples (n = 80) were collected from ICUs and other wards and processed for the isolation and identification of P. aeruginosa. Antimicrobial susceptibility was assessed using disk diffusion. PCR was performed to target the biofilm-associated genes. Out of 80 P. aeruginosa isolates, the prevalence of isolates was highest in the ICU (57.5%), and sputum was the most common specimen type (37%). Piperacillin/tazobactam demonstrated the highest activity (76.2% susceptible), followed by amikacin (52.5% susceptible). Notably, 45% of the isolates were MDR, 52.5% were XDR, while 2.5% were neither MDR nor XDR. The biofilm-associated genes ppyR and pslA were detected in 92.5% and 87.5% of the isolates, respectively, whereas pelA was found in 85% of the isolates. Among the 59 pelA, ppyR, and pslA-positive isolates, 47.45% were MDR, 42.37% were XDR, and 10.18% were non-MDR/XDR. Based on these outcomes, we strongly recommend strict infection prevention and control strategies to limit the transmission of MDR-PA, particularly in hospital settings. Piperacillin/tazobactam remains relatively effective; however, its administration should be guided by antimicrobial stewardship guidelines.

articles.title: Comparative perioperative outcomes of Hugo™ RAS versus laparoscopic and Da Vinci platforms for partial nephrectomy: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: Renal cell carcinoma (RCC) is a common urologic malignancy, and for localized T1 tumors, nephron-sparing surgery is now the standard of care. Laparoscopic and image-guided techniques have advanced as robotic platform procedures offer greater operator dexterity and procedural control. The da Vinci platform has dominated robot-assisted partial nephrectomy, but high costs and closed architecture limit broader use. The Hugo™ RAS system, featuring a modular design, has emerged as a promising alternative, with early studies showing feasibility and safety. However, current evidence remains preliminary, mostly single-center and small-sample. This meta-analysis aggregates data and conducts subgroup analyses to compare Hugo™ RAS with other techniques, aiming to provide more precise effect estimates and guide surgical platform selection. The four main databases (PubMed, EMBASE, Web of Science, and Cochrane Library) were thoroughly searched to identify eligible clinical studies. The selected research involved comparative evaluations of surgical metrics of partial nephrectomy performed with Hugo™ RAS vs. the da Vinci system and traditional laparoscopy. This systematic synthesis included four observational cohort studies with a total of 383 subjects. Combined metric evaluations indicated that Hugo™ RAS demonstrated no statistically significant variation relative to alternative minimally invasive approaches regarding surgery duration (MD = 2.81 min, 95% CI [- 37.42, 43.03], p = 0.89), duration of hospitalization (MD = - 0.23 days, 95% CI [- 1.59, 1.13], p = 0.74), intraoperative blood loss (MD = 18.5 ml, 95% CI [- 53.61, 90.6], p = 0.62), serum creatinine following surgery (MD = - 0.05 mg/dl, 95% CI [- 0.18, 0.08], p = 0.44), positive surgical margin incidence (OR = 0.59, 95% CI [0.19, 1.80], p = 0.35), minor-to-moderate postoperative adverse event frequency (OR = 0.98, 95% CI [0.45, 2.17], p = 0.97), major postoperative adverse event frequency (OR = 0.74, 95% CI [0.09, 6.17], p = 0.78), overall postoperative adverse event rate (OR = 1.05, 95% CI [0.39, 2.87], p = 0.92), or successful trifecta attainment (OR = 1.11, 95% CI [0.60, 2.07], p = 0.74). This meta-analysis provided some preliminary evidence: Hugo™ RAS did not demonstrate significant differences compared to other minimally invasive surgical procedures in terms of procedure time, hospital stay, intraoperative blood loss, postoperative renal function, rate of positive margins, postoperative morbidity, and composite success results. Overall, Hugo™ RAS seems to be a reasonable surgical alternative. However, large multi-site randomized clinical trials are still needed to substantiate this finding.

articles.title: Peripheral venous access in the neonate: current evidence, persistent uncertainties, and proposal of a structured insertion bundle.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Peripheral venous access devices are the most frequently inserted invasive devices in neonatal intensive care, yet fewer than half of them complete the therapy for which they were placed, and their mean dwell time is between 32 and 36 h. Despite this, they have attracted far less attention than central venous access devices: insertion and maintenance practices remain heterogeneous, rarely neonate-specific, and almost never standardized. This narrative review examines the current evidence on indications, device choice, insertion technique, securement, surveillance, and complications of peripheral venous access in the newborn. Evidence suggests that polyurethane outperforms polytetrafluoroethylene; the largest available cohort study supports 26G as the default caliber, including for transfusion; cyanoacrylate securement, structured pre-procedural vein assessment, and dedicated vascular access teams are each associated with better outcomes. Much of this evidence, however, comes from retrospective single-center studies, and important questions-such as the potential advantages of integrated devices or of long peripheral catheters, the caliber-to-vein relationship, and objective detection of infiltration-remain open.

CONCLUSION: On this basis, we propose a protocol for Safe Insertion of Peripheral Venous Catheters (SIPVeC), a seven-step insertion bundle formatted the same way as the protocols already available for umbilical and central devices in the neonate.

WHAT IS KNOWN: • Peripheral venous access devices are the most used vascular access device in neonates, yet most fail before therapy is completed. • Insertion and maintenance practices remain heterogeneous and are rarely neonate-specific.

WHAT IS NEW: • Evidence now favors polyurethane, 26G devices, structured vein assessment, and cyanoacrylate securement. • The SIPVeC protocol translates these elements into a reproducible seven-step insertion bundle for peripheral devices in neonates.

articles.title: Clinical and serological outcomes of syphilis: an 18-year retrospective cohort study on predictors of treatment response and seroreversion in Türkiye.
articles.journal: European journal of clinical microbiology & infectious diseases : official publication of the European Society of Clinical Microbiology
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Despite established protocols, the global resurgence of syphilis remains a public health challenge, with outcomes influenced by disease stage and host factors. This study described 18-year epidemiological trends and identified predictors of serological treatment response and long-term seroreversion.

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 503 adults diagnosed with syphilis between 2005 and 2022 and classified disease stages according to CDC criteria. Treatment response was defined as a ≥ 4-fold decline in rapid plasma reagin (RPR) titers within 12 months for early-stage and 24 months for late-stage syphilis, while seroreversion was defined as a non-reactive RPR. Overall, 157 patients were included in the treatment-response analysis and 159 in the seroreversion analysis, the latter including two additional patients who achieved seroreversion before treatment-response assessment. Independent predictors were identified using multivariable logistic regression.

RESULTS: Syphilis cases increased significantly after 2015, with late-stage disease accounting for 75.7% (n = 381) of diagnoses. Early syphilis rose from 10.5% (2005-2015) to 30.2% after 2015 (p < 0.001). Among patients with available HIV test results, 29.4% (134/456) of cases were in people with HIV. Early-stage syphilis was more frequent in people living with HIV (PLWH) than in HIV-negative individuals (32% vs. 20.1%). Among patients with follow-up, 75.2% (118/157) achieved a serological response. In multivariate analysis, late-stage syphilis was a negative predictor of response (OR 0.22, 95% CI 0.07-0.76; p = 0.016), while baseline RPR titers ≥ 1:8 were a strong positive predictor (OR 8.18, 95% CI 1.72-38.85; p = 0.008). HIV status was not independently associated with response (p > 0.05). Seroreversion occurred in 35.8%, with no independent predictors identified.

CONCLUSIONS: The syphilis burden has grown, driven by delayed diagnosis and late-stage predominance despite recent trends toward earlier detection. In this cohort, disease stage and baseline RPR titers were stronger predictors of serological response than HIV status. The higher frequency of early-stage diagnosis in PLWH is consistent with the potential impact of intensified screening and may reflect differences in healthcare engagement and testing practices compared with the general population.

articles.title: Papillary fibroelastoma of the coumadin ridge as an unusual cause of recurrent ischemic stroke: a case report.
articles.journal: The international journal of cardiovascular imaging
articles.abstract: Cardiac papillary fibroelastoma (PFE) is a rare benign endocardial tumor with significant embolic potential despite its non-malignant histology. We report the case of a 51-year-old woman with palpitations and a history of ischemic stroke involving the left medulla oblongata, accompanied by multiple posterior fossa infarcts. Extensive thrombophilic and autoimmune investigations were negative, and a patent foramen ovale was excluded. Multimodal cardiac imaging, including transesophageal echocardiography (TEE) and cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (CMR), identified a highly mobile pedunculated mass attached to the coumadin ridge near the left atrial appendage ostium. Differential diagnosis included thrombus, myxoma, and PFE. The lesion was successfully removed by surgical excision, and histopathological examination confirmed PFE. This case highlights the coumadin ridge as an exceptionally rare site of PFE attachment and a potential source of recurrent cardioembolism. TEE and CMR are crucial for diagnosis, while surgical resection provides definitive treatment.

articles.title: Interventricular septal thickness for cardiomyopathic phenotype enrichment in patients with established left ventricular hypertrophy.
articles.journal: The international journal of cardiovascular imaging
articles.abstract: We evaluated whether interventricular septal thickness in diastole (IVSd) ≥ 15 mm enriches cardiomyopathic phenotypes among adults with established left ventricular hypertrophy (LVH) and whether broader clinical-echocardiographic features improve triage. We studied 1,127 adults undergoing echocardiography from 2017 to 2019 who met established LVH criteria (sex-specific left ventricular mass index elevation and both IVSd and posterior wall thickness ≥ 13 mm). The primary phenotype was hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, Fabry disease, or amyloidosis. The composite phenotype occurred in 108 patients (9.6%) and was more frequent with IVSd ≥ 15 mm than 13.0-14.9 mm (16.2% vs. 3.6%, p < 0.001). After adjustment, IVSd ≥ 15 mm remained associated with the composite phenotype (odds ratio 2.38, 95% CI 1.35-4.20), with a graded association per 1-mm increase (odds ratio 1.50, 95% CI 1.33-1.70). At 15 mm, sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value, and negative predictive value were 80.6%, 55.7%, 16.2%, and 96.4%; at 18 mm, case-finding yield increased to 41.7% but 58 of 108 cases were missed. A five-variable model improved discrimination over IVSd alone (area under the curve [AUC] 0.839 vs. 0.787; ΔAUC 0.052; p = 0.007; derivation AUC 0.857, temporal validation AUC 0.788), whereas adding binary IVSd ≥ 15 mm to conventional clinical-echocardiographic variables yielded minimal incremental discrimination (ΔAUC 0.003) and minimal additional net benefit. In established LVH, IVSd ≥ 15 mm identifies cardiomyopathic enrichment, with the composite association driven predominantly by hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, but is best used as a prompt for etiologic review rather than a diagnostic rule. A compact five-variable model may support triage.

articles.title: Coronary artery imaging in Kawasaki disease: recent updates in imaging techniques and clinical indications.
articles.journal: The international journal of cardiovascular imaging
articles.abstract: Coronary artery involvement in Kawasaki disease should be evaluated throughout all disease stages. Generally, multimodality imaging is necessary for both the acute and chronic phases of coronary artery abnormalities. This review summarizes current clinical indications and recent technical advances in coronary artery imaging in Kawasaki disease with an emphasis on the roles of computed tomography and magnetic resonance imaging. Echocardiography remains the first-line modality in all disease stages for evaluating coronary artery lesions and ventricular function. Recent technical developments in coronary computed tomography angiography can provide the accurate diagnosis of coronary artery lesions including stenosis and thrombus at substantially reduced radiation dose, supporting its selective use in serial follow-up. Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging offers the comprehensive evaluation of inducible myocardial ischemia, ventricular function, inflammation, and fibrosis. Invasive catheter angiography is reserved for complex or interventional cases. This review also addresses technical considerations and potential pitfalls for each imaging modality. Continued technical developments and their optimization with standardized imaging protocols and reports are expected to enhance diagnostic precision and eventually improve clinical outcomes in children with Kawasaki disease.

articles.title: Accuracy of visual estimation of coronary artery calcifications on low-dose CT from oncologic FDG PET/CT.
articles.journal: The international journal of cardiovascular imaging
articles.abstract: To evaluate the feasibility and accuracy of visual ordinal coronary artery calcium (CAC) scoring on low-dose, non-gated CT scans acquired as part of oncologic PET/CT, using CAC scoring from ECG-gated non-contrast cardiac CT as the reference standard. 210 oncological patients who underwent both PET/CT and single-photon emission computed tomography (SPECT) myocardial perfusion imaging (MPI) with ECG-gated non-contrast cardiac CT within 6 months were retrospectively included. Four independent readers graded image quality and assessed CAC burden using a visual ordinal scoring system (scores ranging from 0 to 12) on non-gated CT images from PET/CT. CAC scores as well as information on presence of myocardial ischemia and/or scars were recorded from the dedicated cardiac diagnostic workup and were used for comparison. Image quality was considered diagnostic in 99.6% of scans. Interreader agreement of ordinal scores was excellent among all four readers (Krippendorff's alpha = 0.95). Non-gated CT demonstrated favorable diagnostic performance for detecting CAC per-patient, with a sensitivity/specificity/positive predictive value/negative predictive value of 92.2%/95%/99.3%/62.1%. Ordinal scores showed a strong correlation with quantitative reference standard CAC scores (Spearman's rho = 0.9, p < 0.001). Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis indicated that ordinal scores effectively differentiated patients based on reference standard CAC score cutoffs of 100, 400, and 1000, with AUC values of 0.96, 0.92, and 0.95, respectively. Additionally, using ordinal scores, ROC analysis yielded an AUC of 0.7 for differentiating patients with and without ischemia/scars. Visual ordinal scoring of CAC burden on low-dose non-gated CT of oncologic PET/CT scans is accurate, effective and strongly correlates with reference standard measurements. The lower negative predictive value indicates that (mild) coronary calcifications are occasionally underestimated.

articles.title: Surgical architecture and component identifiability in robot-assisted radical prostatectomy: a systematic review and network meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: Robot-assisted radical prostatectomy (RARP) combines preservation, reconstruction, and support maneuvers within named surgical packages, making component attribution difficult. To determine whether comparative evidence can identify independent surgical-component effects on strict early perfect continence while preserving oncological context. Comparative RARP studies were synthesized within a prespecified surgical-architecture framework. The primary outcome was perfect continence (0 pads/day) at 10-14 weeks. All prespecified bibliographic databases and registries were rerun through 26 September 2026. Randomized evidence underwent pairwise and network meta-analysis; component estimates were interpreted only after a prespecified structural-identifiability gate. Forty-eight reports representing 48 nonoverlapping study families, 98 arms, and 6,665 arm-level participants were included. Six randomized families provided exact strict 3-month events and formed three disconnected subnetworks; four families formed the largest connected network. In that four-family network, risk ratios versus standard RARP were 1.07 (95% confidence interval [CI] 0.65-1.78) for posterior reconstruction (PR), 2.94 (0.92-9.33) for PR plus anterior reconstruction/suspension, and 1.49 (0.63-3.52) for PR plus sling. PR was the only component meeting the prespecified structural gate; this denotes evidence structure, not a precise or validated independent causal effect. Descriptive positive surgical margin estimates were sparse (PR 0.96 [0.50-1.86]; PR plus anterior reconstruction/suspension 1.74 [0.57-5.25]). Confidence in all primary network comparisons was very low. The literature is broad at the level of named RARP techniques but insufficiently connected and replicated to isolate most component-specific effects. Package-level signals should not be reassigned to individual maneuvers unless those components vary independently across replicated comparisons. Future trials should report exact time-specific continence outcomes, explicit arm-level technical details, and replicated component contrasts.

articles.title: Clinical characteristics and associated factors of difficult-to-treat rheumatoid arthritis: a cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to describe the clinical characteristics and explore factors cross-sectionally associated with difficult-to-treat rheumatoid arthritis (D2T RA) in a Chinese population, providing evidence for characterizing the clinical phenotype and identifying current associated factors in a Chinese population.

METHODS: A cross-sectional study was conducted, enrolling RA patients treated at the Rheumatology Department of Dongfang Hospital, Beijing University of Chinese Medicine, from September 2022 to September 2024. Based on the 2020 EULAR criteria, adapted in accordance with the 2021 Chinese consensus on refractory rheumatoid arthritis, patients were categorized into a D2T RA group (n = 61) and a conventional RA group (n = 182). An exploratory subsample (n = 6 per group) underwent plasma cytokine analysis via Luminex assay. Data on demographics, disease activity measures, laboratory inflammatory parameters, comorbidities, and medication use were collected. Plasma cytokine levels were measured using Luminex technology. Statistical analysis was performed using R software, and associated factors were analyzed via univariate and multivariate logistic regression.

RESULTS: Patients in the D2T RA group were significantly younger than those in the RA group (P = 0.009) and exhibited significantly higher values in swollen joint count, VAS pain score, DAS28-ESR, CDAI, and SDAI (all P < 0.05). The prevalence of osteoporosis was significantly higher in the D2T RA group (85.25% vs. 61.54%, P = 0.001), and the usage of JAK inhibitors was also notably elevated (85.25% vs. 1.10%, P = 0.027). Regarding inflammatory markers, except for elevated plateletcrit, no significant differences were observed in CRP, ESR, IL-6, or composite inflammation indices between groups. Exploratory cytokine analysis (n = 6 per group) showed that IL-6 and IL-17A levels were significantly elevated in the D2T RA group compared to healthy volunteers, whereas no significant differences were observed between the RA and D2T RA groups. Multivariate logistic regression identified that older age was associated with lower odds of D2T RA (OR = 0.94, 95% CI: 0.91-0.98, P =  0.011), while OP remained independently associated with higher odds (OR = 4.95, 95% CI: 1.96-12.15, P < 0.001).

CONCLUSION: In this single-center Chinese cohort, D2T RA was characterized by younger age, higher disease activity, and a higher comorbidity rate of osteoporosis. Younger age and comorbid osteoporosis were cross-sectionally associated with D2T RA. These findings may assist clinicians in recognizing high-risk clinical phenotypes and inform the development of targeted intervention strategies, but require confirmation in prospective, multicenter studies.

articles.title: Post-market safety signals of energy-based surgical devices: a cross-specialty disproportionality analysis of the FDA MAUDE database with robotic-platform validation and regulatory triangulation, 2015-2025.
articles.abstract: Post-market safety evidence for energy-based surgical devices is fragmented. We characterized adverse-event signals in the FDA MAUDE database, validated them on a third (robotic) platform, and triangulated across regulatory and international sources. Medical Device Reports (2015-2025) under electrosurgical and ultrasonic product codes were analyzed with reporting odds ratios (RORs), stratified by specialty and procedure, with robustness checks. All reports under the robotic-system code were retrieved as a third-platform validation cohort. Signals were triangulated with FDA recalls, 510(k) clearances, the Health Canada and Australian TGA databases, exposure descriptors, and a retrospectively applied Poisson CUSUM feasibility analysis. Among 110,183 deduplicated reports (65.8% electrosurgical, 34.2% ultrasonic), electrosurgical devices showed an electrical-thermal fingerprint (burns ROR 3.84; electric shock ROR 15.34) and ultrasonic devices a mechanical-integrity fingerprint (foreign-body removal ROR 92.74), replicated directionally in Canada and Australia. The fingerprint localized to generator/monopolar components and varied by specialty and procedure. Within the robotic validation cohort, component-stratified analysis partly reproduced these signatures-robot-mounted monopolar instruments retained a burn signal, and robot-mounted ultrasonic instruments carried the highest injury-report share-while cross-platform, same-modality contrasts are reported strictly as report-composition (share-level) comparisons. Reporting artifacts (19.5% placeholder narratives; a 2025 robotic mass-reporting episode comprising 55.8% of the robotic cohort) left fingerprint RORs materially unchanged. A retrospectively applied CUSUM flagged the burn theme more than five years before the 2023-2024 Class I recalls, illustrating-without establishing prospective lead time-the potential of automated monitoring. Energy-modality failure-injury fingerprints were consistent across specialties, delivery platforms, three national databases, and regulatory actions. Automated, artifact-aware surveillance of vigilance databases is a promising complement to pre-market review and warrants prospective evaluation.

articles.title: Robot-assisted ileal ureter replacement for complex ureteral strictures: a systematic review and single-arm meta-analysis of surgical and functional outcomes.
articles.abstract: Complex, long-segment ureteral strictures present significant reconstructive challenges. While open ileal ureter replacement is the historical gold standard, it carries substantial perioperative morbidity. This systematic review and single-arm meta-analysis evaluate the surgical and functional outcomes of robot-assisted ileal ureter replacement (RIUR). Following Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines, a comprehensive search of four databases was conducted through September 2026 to identify studies reporting adult RIUR outcomes for complex strictures. Outcomes were pooled using random-effects models. Five retrospective cohort studies comprising 110 patients met the inclusion criteria, with radiation-induced injury representing the predominant etiology (44.5%). The pooled surgical success rate was 93.9% (95% confidence interval [CI]: 87.0-97.2%). The pooled major complication rate (Clavien-Dindo grades III-V) was 10.0% (95% CI: 4.0-24.0%), driven primarily by urinary anastomotic leaks, typically managed with prolonged stenting. Pooled rates for metabolic acidosis requiring supplementation and stricture recurrence were 7.4% and 2.6%, respectively, while renal function remained stable or improved across all evaluated cohorts. Pooled mean operative time and estimated blood loss were 339.1 min (95% CI: 310.5-367.7) and 103.7 mL (95% CI: 54.9-152.6), respectively, while length of hospital stay varied widely by regional institutional pathway (median 3.0 days in early-discharge cohorts to 14.2 days in inpatient testing protocols). Current evidence suggests that RIUR represents a feasible and promising minimally invasive option for complex ureteral defects, with observed success rates meeting historical clinical benchmarks and an acceptable perioperative safety profile.

articles.title: Stereotactic body radiotherapy versus conventional external beam radiotherapy for bone metastases: a meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: Stereotactic body radiotherapy (SBRT) and conventional external beam radiotherapy (cEBRT) are widely used treatment options for the management of painful bone metastases. Randomized phase III trials have provided direct comparative evidence for SBRT and cEBRT; however, their results vary according to treatment regimen and clinical endpoint, supporting a broader quantitative synthesis of pain response, local control, retreatment, and safety outcomes. A systematic search was conducted in PubMed, Scopus, the Cochrane Library, and Google Scholar from database inception through January 2026. Comparative clinical studies evaluating SBRT versus cEBRT for bone metastases were included. Outcomes assessed encompassed pain-related measures (change in Visual Analog Scale scores at 3 and 6 months; complete, partial, stable, and progressive pain response), opioid consumption at 3 and 6 months, radiologic local progression or treatment failure at 8 months, re-irradiation at 12 months, skeletal-related events (vertebral and non-vertebral compression fractures), spinal cord compression, treatment-related toxicity, and overall survival at 1 year. Pooled analyses were performed using random-effects models. Early pain reduction at 3 months, partial and stable pain response, and opioid consumption at 3 and 6 months were comparable between SBRT and cEBRT (all p > 0.05). However, SBRT demonstrated superior mid-term outcomes, with a significantly higher complete pain response at 6 months (RR = 1.43; p = 0.001) and a significantly lower rate of progressive pain response at 6 months (RR = 0.61; p = 0.03). SBRT was also associated with markedly improved local disease control, reflected by lower rates of radiologic local progression or treatment failure at 8 months (RR = 0.36; p < 0.001) and a substantially reduced need for re-irradiation at 12 months (RR = 0.13; p < 0.001). Rates of vertebral and non-vertebral compression fractures, spinal cord compression, treatment-related toxicity, and overall survival at 1 year did not differ significantly between treatment modalities. This meta-analysis demonstrates that both SBRT and cEBRT are safe and effective treatment options for patients with painful bone metastases. While early pain palliation and safety outcomes are comparable, SBRT provides superior durability of pain control, reduced pain progression, improved local tumor control, and a markedly lower need for re-irradiation. SBRT may be particularly advantageous for patients with longer expected survival, oligometastatic disease, or lesions at higher risk of progression, whereas cEBRT remains an effective and accessible option for rapid symptom palliation in patients with limited prognosis.

articles.title: Anesthesiological considerations and complications in robotic surgery: a retrospective analysis.
articles.abstract: Robotic-assisted surgery has become increasingly prevalent across various surgical disciplines. Understanding anesthesiological factors influencing perioperative outcome is essential for optimizing patient care. This retrospective analysis evaluated 200 patients who underwent robotic surgery across three surgical categories: gastrointestinal (GI, n=60), hepatopancreticobiliary (HPB, n=28), and colorectal (n=112) procedures. We conducted an exploratory analysis of associations between anesthesiological parameters-including fluid management, surgical duration, and blood loss-and clinical outcomes such as intensive care unit (ICU) length of stay, total hospital length of stay, complication severity (Clavien-Dindo classification) using univariable and multivariable regression models. The exploratory analyses suggested potential associations between surgical duration and outcomes across surgical specialties in multivariable analysis. For GI procedures, longer surgical duration was associated with higher odds of severe complications (Clavien-Dindo grade ≥III; OR = 1.80 (1.21, 2.66)). In colorectal surgery, surgical duration was independently associated with both development of severe complications (OR = 1.28 (1.01, 1.62)) and total hospital length of stay (log-scale, β = 0.08 (0.03, 0.12)). Fluid intake was associated with an increased hospital length of stay in colorectal surgery (log-scale, β = 0.10 (0.03, 0.17)). Anesthesiological management, particularly surgical duration and fluid management, showed associations with perioperative outcomes in robotic surgery. The estimated effects provide preliminary insights into the magnitude of these associations and may serve as a basis for hypothesis generation and the design of future prospective studies. Further studies are needed to confirm these findings and to investigate the potential clinical relevance of anesthesiological and perioperative management strategies.

articles.title: COVID-19 triggers pulmonary tumor outgrowth through hypoxia- and inflammation-induced VEGF-dependent angiogenesis.
articles.abstract: Pulmonary nodules are highly prevalent in adult human populations, with a substantial proportion representing dormant cancerous lesions. We hypothesized that these pulmonary dormant cancers debilitate in growth owing to the lack of an angiogenic switch in tumors. In this study, we comprehensively investigated the hypothesis that specific pathological triggers can activate this angiogenic switch utilizing severe acute respiratory coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) infection-induced hypoxia as a primary physiological stimulus. Our findings provide compelling experimental evidence demonstrating that SARS-CoV-2 infection induces profound pulmonary hypoxia and severe tissue inflammation in animal models. This microenvironmental disruption markedly upregulates the expression of vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) and vascular endothelial growth factor receptor 2 (VEGFR2) within lung tissues. The resulting hyperactivation of the downstream VEGF-VEGFR2 signaling pathway effectively drives robust pulmonary neovascularization, a phenomenon frequently documented in clinical observations of COVID-19 patients. Furthermore, employing an established experimental tumor model, we demonstrated that SARS-CoV-2 infection directly accelerates tumor outgrowth via this specific VEGF angiogenesis-dependent cascade. Crucially, the targeted administration of a neutralizing antibody to block VEGF significantly suppressed tumor progression and outgrowth in SARS-CoV-2-infected, tumor-bearing animals. Our data show that the COVID-19-induced hypoxia-VEGF-angiogenesis axis serves as one of the mechanisms for initiating tumor outgrowth in pulmonary tissues.

articles.title: How coronary artery disease is portrayed in images from educational websites and resources in Aotearoa New Zealand: a content analysis.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Coronary artery disease (CAD) is a leading cause of global morbidity and disproportionately affects Māori and Pacific peoples in Aotearoa New Zealand (NZ). Poor understanding of symptoms and management contributes to delayed care. Yet visual health information can enhance patient comprehension, engagement, and long-term health outcomes.

AIM: This content analysis aims to explore how CAD is portrayed in images within NZ-based online educational webpages and resources.

METHODS: A content analysis was conducted on publicly available CAD images from NZ-based health educational websites. Data were collected in January 2026 using a systematic Google search strategy. Images were coded using a pre-defined framework categorising content into themes, and descriptive frequencies and proportions were calculated.

RESULTS: Of the 279 webpages identified in the search, 105 met the inclusion criteria, yielding 257 images. Photographs (44.8%) and digital graphics (24.9%) were most common. Only 30% of images depicted people, with slightly more males with neutral expressions. Content primarily focused on prevention and healthy lifestyle choices (24.9%) and anatomical images (21.8%). Clinical aspects were significantly underrepresented, including depictions of screening and diagnoses (13.2%), consequences (9.0%), and medications (7.0%).

DISCUSSION: CAD images in NZ webpages and educational resources emphasise healthy lifestyles and diet, but are less focused on treatment and long-term management. The scarcity of images depicting CAD symptoms, screening, medications, disease pathophysiology, and long-term management represents a missed opportunity to support health literacy. Culturally appropriate and clinically balanced visual resources are needed to improve patient understanding and reduce health inequities in NZ.

articles.title: Congenital Cytomegalovirus Testing Following Pennsylvania Hearing-Targeted Screening Legislation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Congenital cytomegalovirus infection (cCMV) occurs in approximately 1/200 to 1/250 US newborns each year and can cause progressive sensorineural hearing loss. Since 2022, Pennsylvania law mandates cCMV testing for infants who fail newborn hearing screening.

OBJECTIVES: To assess changes in cCMV testing rates and diagnosis before and after Pennsylvania hearing-targeted legislation.

METHODS: Retrospective cohort study of all live births at 3 university-affiliated birth centers. We identified all infants tested for CMV at 21 days of age or younger and analyzed cCMV testing rates in pre- (January 2018-June 2022) and post- (July 2022-December 2024) legislation eras using interrupted time-series analysis. We assessed other clinical signs associated with cCMV testing using standard statistics.

RESULTS: The study cohort included 85 324 infants. Among 54 909 born prelegislation, 3168 (5.8%) had cCMV testing; among 30 415 born postlegislation, 3197 (10.5%) were tested. cCMV testing rates increased significantly among term (by 3.2%) and preterm infants (by 15.5%) at the beginning of the postlegislation era (P = .003 and .001, respectively). Among 5224 infants with hearing-based criteria for screening, CMV testing increased from 36.7% prelegislation to 74.0% postlegislation (P < .001). In the postlegislation period, testing associated with isolated microcephaly increased, but isolated small for gestational age-associated testing decreased. Among 61 infants diagnosed with cCMV, 16 (26.2%) were identified based on hearing criteria alone (2.3/1000 infants prelegislation, 6.0/1000 infants postlegislation, P = .04).

CONCLUSIONS: CMV testing and diagnosis based on hearing criteria alone increased significantly post passage of Pennsylvania hearing-targeted cCMV testing legislation, but infants tested for hearing criteria alone accounted for less than half of identified cCMV cases.

articles.title: Improving Professional Billing Practices in a Pediatric Hospital Medicine Section.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Professional billing translates clinical complexity and physician work into Current Procedural Terminology (CPT) codes and work relative value units (wRVUs), which inform reimbursement and resource planning. Pediatric hospital medicine (PHM) involves complex, cognitive, and time-intensive care, making accurate documentation and code selection essential. Baseline data in our PHM section suggested underuse of appropriate codes, contributing to undercapture of physician work. We aimed to increase wRVUs per patient-day by 25% over 12 months.

METHODS: We conducted a quality improvement initiative at an academic children's hospital from March 2024 to February 2025. Key drivers were billing knowledge, standardized documentation, workflows, and shared culture around billing. The primary outcome was wRVUs per patient-day; the secondary outcome was professional revenue. Process measures included targeted CPT code use. Balancing measures included coding, denial, or compliance concerns identified by the Revenue and Compliance team. Four Plan-Do-Study-Act cycles tested education, a billing guide, documentation tools, and billing data feedback. Statistical process control charts identified special cause variation.

RESULTS: We analyzed 23 772 CPT codes. Mean wRVUs per patient-day increased from 1.9 to 2.5, a 32% increase sustained through December 2025. Professional revenue increased 31% during intervention and 40% during sustainability. Use of level 3 initial inpatient care codes increased from 11% to 58%, level 3 subsequent inpatient care codes from 12% to 54%, and prolonged discharge codes from 13% to 42%. Neonatal intensive care and critical care code use increased. No denial or compliance concerns were identified.

CONCLUSIONS: A section-wide quality improvement approach improved capture of physician work and professional revenue without billing or compliance concerns.

articles.title: Perspectives on Gender Equity: A National Survey of Pediatric Hospital Medicine Division Leaders.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To assess pediatric hospital medicine (PHM) division leaders' perspectives on gender equity in their divisions and organizations.

METHODS: In 2025, we conducted a cross-sectional Research Electronic Data Capture survey distributed via email to 236 PHM division leaders. The survey consisted of 53 items on division and leader demographics, promotion, leadership, benefits, and gender-related experiences. Descriptive statistics summarized numeric responses, and qualitative content analysis identified emerging themes in free-text responses.

RESULTS: Responses from 125 PHM division leaders (53% response rate) were received. Leaders were predominately women (69%) and held PHM subboard certification (84%), with a median of 15 years of practice as a hospitalist. According to leaders, 76% of their faculty were women. No gender differences were reported in faculty rank or leadership roles. Compensation analysis by gender was reported by only 26% of responding institutions. Similarly, although wellness support was common, gender-stratified analyses of outcomes were rarely performed (19%). Mean paid parental leave offered to birth parents was 8 weeks. Qualitative analysis of leaders' suggestions to drive change toward gender equity revealed 6 major themes: (1) compensation transparency, (2) caregiver support, (3) career development, (4) countering gender bias through education and allyship, (5) fostering psychological safety, and (6) advancing institutional accountability.

CONCLUSIONS: Division leaders reported gaps in gender equity practices alongside systemic challenges in PHM. Identified priorities include transparent compensation practices, caregiver-inclusive benefits, career pathways, and leadership accountability. As the first national assessment of PHM leaders' perceptions, these findings highlight opportunities to strengthen structural support for gender-equitable advancement for all clinicians.

articles.title: Clinical and genetic risk factors for apolipoprotein L1-mediated chronic kidney disease in people of African ancestry with HIV.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: To summarize current understanding of the epidemiology, pathogenesis and management of HIV-Associated Nephropathy (HIVAN) and other forms of Apolipoprotein L1 (APOL1)-mediated chronic kidney disease (CKD) in people of African ancestry with HIV.

RECENT FINDINGS: The G1 and G2 variants of the APOL1 gene, which have emerged in trypanosomiasis-endemic areas of Africa, predispose to HIV-associated nephropathy (HIVAN) and other forms of CKD. The risk of APOL1-mediated CKD is attenuated with HIV control and carriage of the p.N264K genetic variant. Several treatments targeting the APOL1 gene and the transmembrane ion channel encoded by the APOL1 gene are being evaluated in clinical trials; early findings indicate they achieve rapid and marked reductions in proteinuria in those with established APOL1-mediated CKD.

SUMMARY: Genetic variants of APOL1 are causally implicated in HIVAN and other forms of severe CKD in populations of African ancestry with HIV. Genetic, epigenetic and environmental factors influence the risk of developing APOL1-mediated CKD, and emerging APOL1-directed therapies offer the prospect of clinical remission to those with established APOL1-mediated CKD.

articles.title: Screening for multidrug-resistant organism: clinical benefit or unquestioned routine.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Current strategies for multidrug-resistant organism (MDRO) screening are primarily intended to support infection prevention programs. However, accumulating evidence indicates that intestinal colonization also provides clinically relevant information for antimicrobial stewardship. This review examines the biological basis and clinical utility of mucosal screening for optimizing empirical antibiotic therapy and proposes a new conceptual framework linking intestinal pathobiont burden with endogenous bloodstream infection.

RECENT FINDINGS: Recent studies consistently show that the absence of MDRO carriage is associated with a very low risk of subsequent infection, supporting well tolerated antimicrobial de-escalation in patients with negative clinical cultures. Emerging evidence further indicates that prolonged exposure to antianaerobic antibiotics promotes expansion of intestinal pathobionts, whereas preservation or restoration of the gut microbiota limits this process. Experimental and clinical observations suggest that the abundance of pathobionts, rather than simple carriage status, determines the probability of bacterial translocation and invasive infection.

SUMMARY: We propose that physiological bacterial translocation from the intestinal microbiota is a common phenomenon and may represent one of the mechanisms of bloodstream infection in critically ill and immunocompromised patients. In this model, progression to invasive infection depends on intestinal pathobiont burden exceeding the capacity of host immune clearance. If validated, this concept would support a transition from qualitative MDRO screening to quantitative assessment of intestinal pathobiont burden to guide antimicrobial stewardship and targeted preventive strategies.

articles.title: Complications associated with thoracic endovascular aortic repair: highlighting the role of peri- and post-operative cardiac monitoring.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Thoracic endovascular aortic repair (TEVAR) is first-line therapy for most descending thoracic aortic pathologies, yet it is performed in patients with a heavy burden of coronary disease, hypertension and limited cardiac reserve, and its cardiac complications remain underemphasized relative to neurological and device-related events.

AREAS COVERED: We summarize the complication profile of TEVAR briefly and then concentrate on its cardiac dimension: myocardial injury after non-cardiac surgery, arrhythmia, acute heart failure, and the chronic ventricular consequences of stent-graft-induced aortic stiffening. We review the mechanisms linking endograft deployment to ventricular-arterial uncoupling, the echocardiographic markers of interest, blood pressure management, and a phase-based framework for peri- and post-operative cardiac monitoring, distinguishing guideline-supported recommendations from expert opinion and from evidence extrapolated from general vascular surgery. PubMed/MEDLINE were searched from database inception to August 2026.

EXPERT OPINION: Cardiac surveillance around TEVAR is inconsistent and largely informal. We argue for baseline echocardiography in all elective patients, protocolized high-sensitivity troponin and natriuretic peptide measurement, defined-duration rhythm monitoring, structured blood pressure control, and longitudinal assessment of ventricular-arterial coupling within a heart-team pathway. TEVAR-specific outcome data and Windkessel-preserving graft design are the priorities for the next phase of endovascular aortic care.

articles.title: Rapid decline in smart insulin pen decision-support use in youth with type 1 diabetes: a randomized crossover pilot trial.
articles.journal: Journal of pediatric endocrinology & metabolism : JPEM

articles.title: Indicators for Computed Tomography Angiography Following Nonfatal Strangulation: A Scoping Review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Nonfatal strangulation (NFS) is common in intimate partner violence and sexual assault and may result in blunt cervical vascular injury detectable with computed tomography angiography (CTA). Clinical indicators that reliably predict vascular injury and guide imaging decisions remain unclear.

METHODS: A scoping review following PRISMA-ScR guidelines examined studies evaluating associations between clinical presentation and CTA-confirmed vascular injury after manual NFS. Searches of PubMed, CINAHL, Web of Science, Embase, and the Cochrane Library were conducted in November 2025. Studies were eligible if they included adolescents or adults with manual NFS and reported clinical assessment findings and CTA outcomes.

RESULTS: Seven retrospective studies met the inclusion criteria. Substantial variation in assessment methods, documentation, and imaging referral practices limited comparisons across studies. Vascular injuries were rare, and inconsistent reporting prevented identification of reliable clinical predictors.

DISCUSSION: Valid predictors of vascular injury following NFS have not been established. Standardized forensic nursing assessment and documentation are essential to developing reliable CTA prediction tools.

articles.title: From Bruising to Blindness: A Practical Guide to Identifying and Managing Hyaluronic Acid Filler Complications.
articles.journal: Dermatologic surgery : official publication for American Society for Dermatologic Surgery [et al.]
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To provide a comprehensive, evidence-based review of the complications associated with hyaluronic acid (HA) dermal fillers and to offer practical guidance for their identification, prevention, and management.

DESIGN: Narrative review of the peer-reviewed literature, consensus guidelines, and postmarket surveillance data addressing the classification, pathophysiology, prevention, and treatment of HA filler complications.

FINDINGS: Hyaluronic acid fillers carry a favorable safety profile, with severe complications reported in fewer than 0.01% of injection sites. Complications are classified by onset. Early-onset events include ecchymosis, injection-site and hypersensitivity reactions, product displacement, and vascular occlusion. Late-onset events include biofilm-associated infection, delayed inflammatory nodules, granulomas, and hyperpigmentation.
