The 10-year absolute risk, multivariable adjusted hazard ratio (HR), and population attributable fraction for blood stream infections were determined according to impaired lung function. Outcomes were any and pathogen-specific blood stream infections.

RESULTS: In 118,565 participants, we identified 4160 blood stream infections among 3438 individuals during 950,718 person-years of follow-up. The HR was 1.5 (95% confidence interval (CI), 1.4-1.7) for individuals with obstructive spirometric pattern and 1.4 (95% confidence interval (CI), 1.2-1.5) for individuals with PRISm. The HR for blood stream infections were 1.4 (95% CI: 1.3-1.6) for forced expiratory volume 1-second (FEV1) 50-79% predicted and HR 2.5 (95% CI: 2.0-3.2) for FEV1 below 50% of predicted. A similar pattern was seen for all pathogen specific blood stream infections. The 10-year risk of blood stream infections was 5.4.3% (95% CI: 5.1-5.9) and 4.3% (95% CI: 3.9-4.7) for individuals with PRISm and obstructive spirometric pattern, respectively. The population-attributable fraction of blood stream infections attributable to abnormal spirometric pattern was 9.5% (95% CI: 6.4%-12.7%).

CONCLUSION: Impaired lung function is an important risk factor for blood stream infections and not limited to respiratory tract pathogens.

articles.title: Hepatic retromer is essential for systemic cholesterol homeostasis by regulating lysosomal cholesterol handling.
articles.abstract: Disturbed hepatic cholesterol homeostasis is associated with atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD). The endo-lysosomal system plays a central role in cholesterol uptake and intracellular trafficking, yet the molecular mechanisms governing these processes remain poorly understood. Here, we identify hepatic vacuolar protein sorting 35 (VPS35), a core component of the retromer complex, as a critical regulator of hepatocellular and systemic cholesterol homeostasis. Liver-specific VPS35 ablation in mice elevated plasma and hepatic cholesterol levels due to impaired hepatic uptake of atherogenic lipoproteins, defective cholesterol trafficking through the endo-lysosomal system, and increased de novo cholesterol biosynthesis. The decreased hepatic uptake of atherogenic lipoproteins was associated with altered subcellular distribution of the low-density lipoprotein receptor (LDLR) and reduced levels of LDLR-related protein 1 (LRP1). The increased hepatic cholesterol content was associated with altered lysosomal ultrastructure and pH and decreased levels of a wide range of lysosomal proteins, including key proteins for lysosomal cholesterol egress, such as lysosomal acid lipase (LAL), scavenger receptor class B member 2 (SCARB2), Niemann-Pick type C1 (NPC1), and NPC2. Collectively, these findings reveal a previously unrecognized function of the hepatic retromer complex in systemic cholesterol homeostasis. Beyond its established role in endosomal cargo transport, VPS35 is essential for lysosomal cholesterol handling by preserving key proteins involved in lysosomal cholesterol metabolism.

articles.title: The gene expression signature of multinucleated giant cells in the spleens of Leishmania donovani-infected mice.
articles.abstract: Multinucleated giant cells (MGCs) are associated with chronic inflammation and infectious diseases, but their biological characteristics in vivo remain poorly understood because intact cells are difficult to isolate from tissues. In visceral leishmaniasis, heavily parasitized, hemophagocytic MGCs are observed in the spleens of Leishmania donovani-infected mice, suggesting that these cells may contribute to parasite persistence and disease pathology. In this study, we established a method for isolating intact MGCs from the spleens of chronically infected BALB/c mice and performed transcriptomic analysis of manually collected single cells. Gentle enzymatic digestion of infected spleens enabled the recovery of large, multinucleated, F4/80-positive cells, indicating that size-based manual selection efficiently enriched for MGCs. Principal component analysis of single-cell RNA-seq data from 10 isolated MGCs showed that most MGCs formed a cluster distinct from those of naïve and infected bulk-spleen samples and RAW264.7 macrophage cells. Differential expression analysis identified genes that were upregulated during infection and further enriched in MGCs, including Ccl8, Cd63, Cebpb, and Fabp5, which are associated with macrophage activation and immune regulation. These findings provide a practical approach for isolating splenic MGCs and offer preliminary insight into the transcriptional features of L. donovani-induced MGCs in vivo.

articles.title: Large esophageal varices predict hepatocellular carcinoma in newly diagnosed cirrhosis: insights from machine learning and propensity score analysis.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is a major complication of chronic liver disease (CLD) requiring improved risk stratification. Esophageal varices (EVs), as manifestations of severe portal hypertension, may promote HCC development through vascular remodeling and hypoxia-related pathways. We aimed to evaluate whether variceal size independently predicts HCC risk and whether specific biomarker profiles can be identified.

PATIENTS AND METHODS: In this 12-year prospective cohort study, 545 patients with newly diagnosed compensated advanced chronic liver disease (cACLD) were enrolled at a tertiary hepatology center and followed for a median of 81 months. Baseline evaluations included endoscopy, elastography, hepatic venous pressure gradient measurement, imaging, and laboratory tests. EVs were classified as absent, small, or large according to Baveno VI nomenclature; large EVs were the primary exposure. Propensity score methods and Cox models assessed their impact on HCC risk, and random survival forests evaluated predictive value.

RESULTS: During follow-up, 92 patients (16.9%) developed HCC. Large EVs at baseline emerged as the strongest independent predictor of HCC onset, surpassing alpha-fetoprotein, hepatic venous pressure gradient, and liver stiffness. Hazard ratios ranged from 7.2 to 14.7 (all p < 0.001). After correction for multiple testing, HA, CA9, I-FABP, and TGF-β1 remained associated with large varices, suggesting extracellular matrix remodeling, hypoxia, intestinal barrier injury, and profibrogenic signaling.

CONCLUSIONS: Large esophageal varices independently predict HCC in cACLD, reflecting severe portal hypertension and a pro-tumorigenic milieu, and should inform improved surveillance and preventive strategies targeting vascular and fibrotic pathways.

articles.title: Anticoagulation in cirrhosis: Indications, drug selection, and disease-modifying potential.
articles.abstract: Anticoagulation in cirrhosis has evolved from a perceived contraindication to an integral component of modern liver disease management. Recognition of the fragile rebalanced hemostatic state has challenged the traditional concept of cirrhosis as an exclusively hemorrhagic disorder and provided the biological rationale for anticoagulation in selected patients. Beyond preventing thrombus extension and promoting portal vein recanalization, accumulating experimental and clinical evidence suggests that anticoagulants may exert disease-modifying effects by attenuating intrahepatic coagulation, hepatic fibrogenesis, sinusoidal dysfunction, and portal hypertension. The therapeutic landscape has also changed substantially. Direct oral anticoagulants have emerged as effective and generally safe alternatives to vitamin K antagonists and low-molecular-weight heparin in carefully selected patients, although important differences in pharmacokinetics, hepatic metabolism, renal elimination, and drug interactions require individualized anticoagulant selection. At the same time, management of portal vein thrombosis has shifted from a uniform treatment approach to a patient-centered strategy that considers thrombus characteristics, transplant candidacy, bleeding risk, and the increasing role of endovascular portal vein recanalization. This review summarizes current evidence regarding the indications for anticoagulation in cirrhosis, anticoagulant selection, management of portal vein thrombosis, and available clinical outcomes. It also examines the emerging concept of anticoagulation as a disease-modifying therapy and highlights key knowledge gaps that should guide future research. Together, these advances position anticoagulation as an increasingly important component of comprehensive cirrhosis care rather than a treatment reserved solely for thrombotic complications.

articles.title: Venous thromboembolism after laparotomic and laparoscopic myomectomy with large myoma burden.
articles.abstract:
STUDY OBJECTIVE: To investigate the incidence of venous thromboembolism (VTE) in patients undergoing myomectomy. To evaluate the impact of route of surgery, myoma burden, and operative time in the development of VTE in this population.

DESIGN: Retrospective cohort study (Canadian Task Force Classification II2) of targeted myomectomy data from the American College of Surgeons National Surgical Quality Improvement Program (NSQIP) SETTING: NSQIP Database PATIENTS OR PARTICIPANTS: Women aged ≥18 years undergoing laparotomic and laparoscopic myomectomy between 2011 and 2022. Patients were classified by Current Procedural Terminology (CPT) codes as having low or high myoma burden (>250 g or >4 fibroids). Patients undergoing hysterectomy, vaginal or hysteroscopic myomectomy, with malignant pathology, or missing operative time were excluded.

INTERVENTIONS: Cases were identified by CPT codes. Variables including age, ethnicity, body mass index (BMI), smoking status, diabetes, hypertension, blood transfusion, inpatient status, and American Society of Anesthesiologists classification system scores were collected. Clinical predictors of VTE were evaluated by stratifying cases according to surgical route, operative time, year of procedure, and myoma burden.

MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: A total of 38,167 myomectomies occurring between 2011-2022 were included. Of these, 20,943 (54.9%) patients underwent laparotomy, and 17,224 (45.1%) patients underwent laparoscopy. The incidence of VTE after myomectomy was 0.28%. Patients undergoing laparotomy had twice the VTE rate (0.36%) compared with those undergoing laparoscopy (0.18%). Patients undergoing laparotomy were more likely to be younger, of non-Hispanic African American ethnicity, inpatient, with higher BMI, require blood transfusion, have higher myoma burden, and have shorter operative times. After multivariable adjustment, neither myoma burden nor surgical route was independently associated with VTE. However, longer operative time (>186 min, 75 percentile) was independently associated with increased odds of VTE (aOR 2.73; CI:1.52-4.90).

CONCLUSION: The occurrence of VTE after laparoscopic and laparotomic myomectomy is uncommon. The rate of VTE is higher with longer operative times, but this outcome is not significantly associated with surgical route or myoma burden.

articles.title: Magneto-controllable cell robots for targeted myocardial infarction repair.
articles.abstract: Myocardial infarction (MI) triggers irreversible cardiomyocyte loss, maladaptive remodeling, and heart failure processes exacerbated by insufficient endogenous angiogenesis and unresolved inflammation. While pro-angiogenic therapies hold promise, their clinical translation is hindered by poor lesion targeting, subtherapeutic drug accumulation, and transient bioactivity. To overcome these barriers, we engineered "magnetically guided cellular robots", M2a-polarized macrophages intracellularly loaded with superparamagnetic Fe3O4 nanoparticles and genetically programmed for sustained VEGF secretion (Mag-M2). Mag-M2 exhibits dual responsiveness: chemotactic homing to ischemic myocardiumandprecise magnetic navigation under a 0.5-T field, enabling enhanced transendothelial migration and deep infarct-zone penetration. In MI models, intravenous Mag-M2 administration followed by magnetic guidance significantly preserved left ventricular ejection fraction (67.8 % vs. 40.7 %), reduced infarct size (25.96 % vs. 37.67 %), attenuated fibrosis, and improved survival without systemic toxicity. Mechanistically, Mag-M2 activates a novel VEGF/METRNL/KIT axis: VEGF upregulates the adipokine METRNL, which acted as a high-affinity KIT ligand, driving peri-infarct neovascularization and suppressing pro-inflammatory cytokines (IL-1β, IL-6, TNF α). This integrative platform synergizes immunomodulation, magnetic targeting, and pathway-specific regenerative signaling, offering a rationally designed, translatable strategy for precision myocardial repair.

articles.title: An integrated prediction model using machine learning and dynamics simulation for the selection of transdermal penetration enhancers.
articles.journal: Journal of controlled release : official journal of the Controlled Release Society
articles.abstract: Penetration enhancers (PEs) are widely used in transdermal drug delivery systems (TDDS) due to their cost-effectiveness and excellent biocompatibility. However, the rapid selection of PEs for TDDS is hindered by two critical challenges: first, in vitro permeation tests (IVPT) are costly and time consumption; second, the datasets for drug-PE matching are relatively limited. To address these issues, this study established a rapid screening platform for PEs in transdermal formulations using machine learning (ML) approaches based on a self-constructed database and further explored the permeation process of "drug-PE" systems via molecular dynamics simulation (MD). Systematic evaluation of five ML algorithms showed that the Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LightGBM) model achieved the optimal predictive performance using 5-fold cross-validation based on random selection and unseen drug-excipient combination splitting, with R2 values of 0.78 ± 0.03 (random split), 0.73 ± 0.01 (unseen PE split), and 0.72 ± 0.06 (unseen drug-PE combination split) on the test sets, respectively. In contrast, performance decreased substantially for the unseen-drug split (R2 = -0.40), indicating that the model performs well primarily for interpolation within the chemical space represented in the dataset but does not reliably extrapolate to entirely unseen drugs. Feature importance analysis revealed a dose-dependent relationship between PE concentration and transdermal efficiency, while the log S of drugs exerted a non-singular effect on transdermal flux. Moreover, transdermal database analysis indicated that drugs with log P values of 2-3, when paired with PEs possessing log P values of 4-6, tended to achieve higher transdermal permeation efficiency. The accuracy of the prediction model was verified by IVPT using two model drugs, berberine and ferulic acid. Furthermore, MD simulations were employed to elucidate the penetration mechanism of the model drugs in "drug-PE" combinations at the atomic level. Finally, a rapid screening platform (https://permapp-online.streamlit.app) was developed, which enabled transdermal flux prediction through the input of molecular descriptors. This platform can provide valuable support for the future design of transdermal formulations.

articles.title: Factors affecting serum neurofilament light chain in transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: While serum neurofilament light chain (sNfL) has shown promise as a biomarker for the development of peripheral neuropathy (PN) in hereditary transthyretin (TTR) amyloidosis (vATTR), its role in all-comers with ATTR cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM) is less well defined, and it is unknown how CM severity and TTR stabilizer therapy affect sNfL.

METHODS: Study participants included those with ATTR-CM not on gene-silencer therapy referred to Oregon Health & Science University. The association between sNfL and baseline patient characteristics, including age, sex, body mass index (BMI), presence of PN, ATTR subtype, N-terminal pro b-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP), estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) and tafamidis treatment, were evaluated utilizing linear regression.

RESULTS: 66 patients (age: 78.5 ± 6.9 years, 6.1% female, 16.7% with diabetes mellitus, 10.6% vATTR-CM, 43.9% with PN symptoms, 30.3% receiving tafamidis at baseline) were included. There was no difference in sNfL levels when stratified by ATTR subtype (p = 0.168), PN symptoms (p = 0.881), or tafamidis treatment measured categorically (p = 0.418). In 17 patients (17.6% vATTR-CM) with available paired pre-tafamidis and on-tafamidis samples, there was no difference in sNfL level. In our univariable and multivariable analysis, NT-proBNP and eGFR were associated with sNfL.

CONCLUSIONS: In ATTR-CM, cardiomyopathy severity and renal dysfunction impact sNfL more than presence of PN or other clinical factors.

articles.title: Isoform differentiation studies of arginase: From structural function to design strategies for specific ligands and their application prospects.
articles.abstract: Arginase (ARG), a binuclear manganese metalloenzyme, hydrolyzes L-arginine to L-ornithine and urea, competitively regulating NO bioavailability with NOS. Mammals express two isoforms, ARG1 (cytosolic) and ARG2 (mitochondrial), that share a conserved catalytic core yet exert distinct physiological and pathological effects. ARG1 is essential for hepatic urea detoxification, as systemic Arg1 knockout mice develop hyperammonemia within 10-12 days after birth; in contrast, Arg2 knockout mice show only slightly elevated plasma arginine levels with no overt phenotypic abnormalities, this significant difference highlights the importance of a thorough analysis of the functional divergence between ARG1 and ARG2. Pathologically, ARG1 drives immunosuppression in the tumor microenvironment, promotes vascular dysfunction in hypertension and atherosclerosis, and contributes to fibrotic remodeling; ARG2 fuels M1 macrophage inflammatory responses, modulates mitochondrial metabolism, and participates in neurodegeneration. This review systematically examines isoform differences across four dimensions: structural-functional divergence, localization-driven functional segregation, differential pathological contributions, and the current landscape of isoform-selective inhibitors. We further discuss rational design strategies for specific ligands and highlight the translational prospects of isoform-targeted therapies. Exploiting ARG1/ARG2 differentiation represents a promising avenue for precision intervention in cancer, cardiovascular disease, inflammation, and neurodegenerative disorders.

articles.title: The dual immunomodulatory roles and signaling mechanisms of toll-like receptor 2 in different diseases.
articles.abstract: Toll-like receptors are important components of the pattern recognition receptor (PRR) family, and Toll-like receptor 2 (TLR2) is one of the most important Toll-like receptors involved in defending against infection and injury. TLR2 senses a wide array of pathogen- and damage-associated molecular patterns and has very broad functions in infectious diseases and other diseases. On one hand, TLR2 drives pro-inflammatory responses through the classical MyD88/NF-κB pathway, which is crucial for pathogen clearance; on the other hand, TLR2 can also limit excessive inflammation by activating the PI3K/Akt pathway, inducing IL-10, and promoting the expansion of regulatory T cells (Tregs), thereby maintaining immune tolerance. Such functional plasticity is regulated by ligand milieu, cell types and disease stages, which underpin the dual roles of TLR2 under diverse pathological conditions including infection, inflammation, autoimmunity and organ transplantation. This review systematically summarizes advances in TLR2 signaling transduction and its immunological functions across various diseases and enables a more cautious evaluation of its pleiotropic effects in distinct disease contexts.

articles.title: A dual-bioeffect nanoengineered piezoelectric-photothermal hydrogel induces endochondral ossification and promotes critical-sized bone regeneration.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Critical-sized bone defects remain a major clinical challenge in orthopedics. Current strategies including inert implants and autologous bone grafts suffer from complications like loosening, infection, and donor site morbidity. Piezoelectric and photothermal stimuli synergistically regulate bone regeneration, and black phosphorus nanosheets (BPNSs) possess both effects and biodegradability, but are prone to oxidation and aggregation.

OBJECTIVES: This study aims to develop an injectable biomimetic hydrogel with dual piezoelectric-photothermal bioeffects for minimally invasive and efficient repair of irregular critical-sized bone defects.

METHODS: BPNS@rhCOL1MA composite system was constructed by embedding BPNSs into recombinant human methacrylated type I collagen hydrogel. Physicochemical characterization, in vitro cell assays, transcriptomic analysis, and in vivo validation in a rabbit rib defect model were performed.

RESULTS: The material exhibited stable network, injectability, and controllable dual-responsive properties. It significantly enhanced osteogenic differentiation of BMSCs in vitro. Transcriptomics revealed activation of electrical/thermal signal transduction and angiogenesis pathways. In vivo, it markedly improved new bone formation, bone mineral density, and mechanical properties.

CONCLUSION: This work first integrates the dual bioeffects of BPNSs with injectable human-derived collagen hydrogel, providing a novel strategy for minimally invasive repair of irregular bone defects.

articles.title: Association of protein signature of fine particulate matter with MASLD: the underlying pathways and Mendelian randomization analysis.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: MASLD is a common chronic liver disease worldwide; identifying modifiable risk factors is crucial. Although fine particulate matter (PM2.5) has been epidemiologically linked to MASLD, its mechanism remains unclear.

OBJECTIVES: To explore the mediating role of protein signature on the association between PM2.5 and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), and the underlying biological pathways.

METHODS: We included 52,190 participants free of MASLD at baseline of a large cohort. Annual average PM2.5 exposure was estimated by bilinear interpolation, and time-weighted method. PM2.5-related protein signature was constructed by elastic net regression, and KEGG/GO enrichment analysis was performed to identify potential pathways. Cox models were used to evaluate the associations of PM2.5 and the protein signature with incident MASLD. Mendelian randomization (MR) analysis was applied to examine potential causality between proteins and MASLD. Structural equation modeling (SEM) was employed to the evaluate statistical mediation involving the protein and metabolic signatures.

RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 11.8 years, 624 incident MASLD cases were identified. The PM2.5-related protein signature comprised 700 proteins, which were mainly enriched in pathways including NF-κB signaling pathway, and cytokine-cytokine receptor interaction. Both PM2.5 exposure, and protein signature were significantly associated with incident MASLD, with hazard ratios (95 % confidence intervals) of 1.19 (1.10, 1.30), and 1.19 (1.08, 1.31). MR analysis provided genetic evidence supporting that CD28, CSF3 and HAVCR2 were associated with MASLD. Mediation analysis indicated that PM2.5-related protein signature mediated 15 % (95 % CI: 2.7 %, 37.7 %) of the PM2.5-MASLD association. SEM further suggested that PM2.5-related protein signature might mediate the PM2.5-MASLD association by regulating metabolic signatures.

CONCLUSIONS: The PM2.5-related protein signature was associated with MASLD, and showed statistical mediation of PM2.5-MASLD association potentially involving inflammatory and metabolic pathways.

articles.title: Patient-Reported Benefits of Acoramidis Across Genotypes in Transthyretin Amyloid Cardiomyopathy: KCCQ and EQ-5D-5L Outcomes From ATTRibute-CM.
Left Ventricular Functional Improvement is Associated With Lower Morbidity and Mortality During Long-Term Mechanical Circulatory Support: An STS Intermacs Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: A subset of patients with advanced heart failure (HF) supported with durable left ventricular assist devices (LVADs) demonstrate significant improvement in left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), but the impact of such functional improvement on clinical outcomes is unclear.

METHODS: We analyzed adults in the STS-Intermacs registry who underwent continuous-flow LVAD implantation (2006-2017) and had echocardiographic data ≥6 months post-implant. Post-LVAD myocardial function was defined by the maximum LVEF after ≥6 months of support and categorized as <40% vs ≥40% and into finer strata. Outcomes included all-cause mortality, clinically significant sustained cardiac arrhythmia, hepatic and renal dysfunction, CVA/TIA, right HF during follow-up, and HF hospitalization. Incidence rates and incidence rate ratios were calculated during 6-month landmarked follow-up through 5 years, and associations were assessed using landmarked multivariable Cox models.

RESULTS: Among 9,518 eligible patients (age 56.6±13.2 years, 21.4% female), 1,131 (12%) achieved LVEF ≥40% over a median 27.0 months of follow-up. Compared with LVEF <40%, LVEF ≥40% was associated with lower adjusted incidence rates of death (adjusted IRR 0.85, 95% CI 0.73-0.98), arrhythmia (0.59, 0.48-0.72), hepatic dysfunction (0.58, 0.35-0.97), and HF hospitalization (0.65, 0.51-0.82), whereas adjusted differences in right HF and renal dysfunction were not significant. In adjusted time-to-event analyses, LVEF ≥40% was independently associated with lower hazards of all-cause mortality (aHR 0.82, 95% CI 0.71-0.96), HF hospitalization (0.63, 0.50-0.80), cardiac arrhythmia (0.69, 0.58-0.83), and hepatic dysfunction (0.57, 0.37-0.88). Across ordered LVEF strata, higher LVEF was associated with progressively lower risks of death and HF-related events.

CONCLUSIONS: In a large multicenter LVAD cohort, LV functional response to durable support spanned a spectrum, with ∼1 in 8 (12%) durable LVAD recipients achieving a maximum post-implant LVEF ≥40% after ≥6 months of support. Higher post-implant LVEF was independently associated with improved survival and fewer HF-related events. These findings support viewing myocardial improvement during LVAD support as a clinically meaningful target that affects positively the outcomes of patients while being on mechanical support.

articles.title: Cardiac resynchronization therapy outcomes by sex and QRS duration: insights from AdaptResponse and a Real-world registry.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sex-related differences in cardiac resynchronization therapy (CRT) outcomes in heart failure (HF) patients, particularly at shorter QRS durations, remain incompletely defined. We evaluated outcomes by sex and QRS duration in AdaptResponse trial and, pooled with Medtronic product surveillance registry (PSR) data, evaluated mortality comparing CRT and no CRT.

METHODS AND RESULTS: AdaptResponse patients (symptomatic HF, LVEF≤35%, Strauss-LBBB, and normal atrioventricular conduction; 43% women) were analyzed by sex and baseline QRS (150ms cut-off), and pooled with PSR CRT and No CRT groups meeting CRT indications. Average treatment effect on treated (ATT) propensity weighting was used to standardize the PSR groups to AdaptResponse baseline characteristics. All-cause mortality was compared between the pooled CRT patients and No CRT controls with weighted Cox models. In AdaptResponse, adjusted mortality rates did not differ significantly between women and men (HR 0.91, 95% CI: 0.72-1.15; p=0.45), and no interaction was observed between sex and QRS (p=0.31). Adjusted mortality in women with QRS<150ms was not statistically different from men with QRS≥150ms (HR 1.02, CI: 0.75-1.38). After ATT-weighting and adjustment, CRT was observed to be associated with lower mortality versus No CRT across sex and QRS subgroups (QRS 120-149ms: HR 0.50, CI: 0.31-0.82 for women and HR 0.51, CI: 0.31-0.86 for men; QRS≥150ms: HR 0.46, CI: 0.28-0.74 for women and HR 0.46, CI: 0.29-0.72 for men; all p<0.05).

CONCLUSION: In this exploratory analysis, among patients with QRS 120-149ms, CRT was associated with a 49% and 50% relative mortality reduction in men and women, respectively, through five years of follow-up compared to No CRT controls. In AdaptResponse, mortality in women with these shorter QRS durations was similar to men with QRS≥150ms. These observational findings are hypothesis-generating and suggest a potential benefit of CRT in this patient population, particularly for women, but have not been confirmed in a randomized trial.

articles.title: Continuous Vutrisiran Reduces Cardiovascular Events and Hospitalizations in Patients With Transthyretin Amyloidosis With Cardiomyopathy in the HELIOS-B One-Year Open Label Extension.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Vutrisiran significantly reduced the risk of all-cause mortality and recurrent cardiovascular (CV) events vs placebo in patients with transthyretin amyloidosis with cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM) in the phase 3 HELIOS-B study (NCT04153149). Here, we report the long-term impact of vutrisiran on hospitalizations and urgent heart failure (HF) visits from the ongoing HELIOS-B open-label extension (OLE).

METHODS: In HELIOS-B, patients received vutrisiran 25 mg or placebo every 3 months over a 33-36-month double-blind period, followed by a 24-month OLE continuing with vutrisiran (continuous treatment), or if previously receiving placebo, initiating vutrisiran (delayed treatment). Hospitalizations and urgent HF visits were analyzed through 48 months (12 months of the OLE) in the overall and monotherapy (not receiving tafamidis at baseline) populations, and the baseline tafamidis subgroup.

RESULTS: Of 654 participants, 466 entered the OLE. Continuous vutrisiran reduced the risk of all-cause hospitalizations vs delayed treatment in the overall population (relative rate ratio [RRR] 0.71, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.62-0.82, P<0.001) and the monotherapy population (RRR 0.60, 95% CI 0.50-0.72, P<0.001). Continuous vutrisiran also significantly reduced the risk of CV hospitalizations, HF hospitalizations, and non-CV hospitalizations vs delayed vutrisiran in the overall and monotherapy populations, and urgent HF visits in the overall population and baseline tafamidis subgroup.

CONCLUSIONS: Continuous vutrisiran reduced the risk of CV events and hospitalizations relative to patients originally randomized to placebo in HELIOS-B. Many treatment effects were of greater magnitude at 48 months vs 36 months with continuous vutrisiran, highlighting the benefits of earlier diagnosis and treatment.

articles.title: Ultra-processed food consumption in people with chronic kidney disease.
articles.journal: Journal of renal nutrition : the official journal of the Council on Renal Nutrition of the National Kidney Foundation

articles.title: High Infection Rate in Open Anterior Talofibular Ligament Repair with Internal Brace Augmentation and Immediate Permissive Weight Bearing.
articles.journal: The Journal of foot and ankle surgery : official publication of the American College of Foot and Ankle Surgeons
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Modified Broström repair is the gold standard for chronic lateral ankle instability. Internal brace augmentation was introduced to increase ligament strength and allow earlier rehabilitation, but concerns exist regarding surgical site infection (SSI).

PURPOSE: To compare the incidence of SSI following anterior talofibular ligament (ATFL) repair with internal brace augmentation and immediate permissive weight bearing versus ATFL repair without augmentation and restricted rehabilitation.

STUDY DESIGN: Retrospective cohort study.

METHODS: Patients undergoing open ATFL repair with internal brace augmentation and immediate permissive weight bearing (ATFL-IB group) between January 2022 and February 2024 (n = 34) were compared with patients undergoing open ATFL repair without augmentation and restricted rehabilitation (ATFL group) between January 2016 and March 2019 (n = 31). The primary outcome was SSI, defined as infection within 90 days requiring antibiotic therapy or surgical intervention. Secondary outcomes included other complications. Baseline characteristics and SSI-related risk factors were assessed.

RESULTS: SSI occurred in 5 patients (15%) in the ATFL-IB group and none in the ATFL group (0%) (p = .034). Other complications included persistent ankle instability (3%) and malposition (3%) in the ATFL-IB group and knot pain (3%) in the ATFL group. Baseline characteristics and operative time were comparable, only smoking prevalence was higher in the ATFL group.

CONCLUSIONS: ATFL repair with internal brace augmentation and immediate permissive weight bearing was associated with a higher SSI rate compared with ATFL repair without augmentation and restricted rehabilitation. Because augmentation and rehabilitation differed concurrently, their relative contributions could not be determined.

articles.title: A temporal framework of redox dysregulation in autoimmunity: interplay between oxidative deficiency and oxidative stress.
articles.abstract: Reactive oxygen species (ROS) occupy a paradoxical position in autoimmune disease: excessive or dysregulated ROS contribute to oxidative injury and inflammatory amplification, whereas physiological ROS function as spatially and temporally regulated signals required for immune homeostasis. This duality suggests that redox dysregulation may involve not only excessive ROS but also failure of physiologically required ROS signaling. We define this latter state as oxidative deficiency: a functionally defined state in which an inadequate physiological ROS signal impairs a specific redox-dependent biological process, rather than simply reflecting low total ROS or increased antioxidant capacity. Genetic and experimental studies of NADPH oxidase (NOX) pathways demonstrate that impaired NOX-dependent ROS generation can modify immune regulation and autoimmune susceptibility in selected contexts, with particularly strong support in systemic lupus erythematosus and experimental arthritis. However, divergent findings in experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis and protection from autoimmune diabetes following reduced NOX2 activity demonstrate substantial disease- and function-specific effects. We therefore propose that oxidative deficiency and pathological oxidative stress represent distinct, independently testable dimensions of autoimmune-associated redox dysregulation whose relationship may be sequential, concurrent, or absent depending on disease context. In selected settings, oxidative deficiency may precede and later coexist with pathological oxidative stress, although direct temporal evidence for this trajectory in human autoimmune disease remains limited. The framework is experimentally falsifiable: evidence for oxidative deficiency requires demonstration of an inadequate physiological ROS signal, impairment of the corresponding biological function, and, where feasible, functional rescue following selective restoration of the deficient signal. This framework extends established redox concepts by distinguishing failure of physiological ROS signaling from pathological oxidant excess and provides testable criteria for defining their roles in autoimmune disease.

articles.title: Usp3 negatively regulates Mda5-mediated antiviral response by attenuating its K63-linked ubiquitination in black carp.
articles.abstract: Melanoma differentiation-associated gene 5 (MDA5) is a critical cytosolic RNA sensor that initiates type I interferon (IFN) signaling upon viral infection, and its activity must be tightly regulated to maintain immune homeostasis. Ubiquitin-specific protease 3 (USP3) has been identified as a negative regulator of RLR-mediated IFN signaling in mammals, yet its role in teleost antiviral immunity remains unknown. In this study, we cloned and characterized usp3 (bcusp3) from black carp (Mylopharyngodon piceus). The full-length coding sequence of bcusp3 encodes a protein of 524 amino acids containing conserved ZnF-UBP and UCH domains. Overexpression of bcUsp3 significantly suppressed bcMda5-induced ifn promoter activation in a dose-dependent manner, whereas knockdown of bcUsp3 in MPF cells markedly enhanced ifn and interferon-stimulated gene (isg) expression and inhibited SVCV replication. Mechanistically, co-immunoprecipitation (Co-IP) assays revealed that bcUsp3 directly interacts with bcMda5. Furthermore, bcUsp3 over-expression reduced both total and K63-linked ubiquitination of bcMda5, indicating that bcUsp3 attenuates the K63-linked ubiquitination of bcMda5. Collectively, our findings demonstrate that bcUsp3 functions as a negative regulator of bcMda5-mediated Ifn signaling by attenuating its K63-linked ubiquitination, providing the first evidence for the regulatory role of Usp3 in teleost antiviral innate immunity.

articles.title: Veratric acid ameliorates metabolic-dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease via targeting PPARG.
articles.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease (MAFLD) is one of the most common metabolic syndromes worldwide. Its pathogenesis is multifactorial, involving disruptions in lipid metabolism, insulin resistance, chronic inflammation, and mitochondrial dysfunction. Veratric acid (VA), a naturally occurring phenolic compound, is known for its antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties; however, its therapeutic potential and underlying mechanisms in the context of MAFLD remain largely uncharacterized. This study aimed to investigate the protective effects and underlying mechanisms of VA in a high-fat diet induced mouse model of MAFLD. In this study, C57BL/6J mice were fed an HFD with or without VA supplementation. Metabolic phenotypes, hepatic steatosis, and serum biochemical parameters were evaluated. In vitro experiments were conducted in HepG2 cells to assess lipid accumulation, mitochondrial function, oxidative stress, and gene expression. Network pharmacology, molecular docking, CETSA, and DARTS assays were employed to identify potential targets. The results demonstrated that VA significantly alleviated HFD-induced weight gain, adipose tissue accumulation, and hepatic steatosis. VA also improved glucose homeostasis, reduced serum lipid levels, and ameliorated liver injury. Mechanistically, VA modulated lipid metabolism by enhancing fatty acid β-oxidation and lipolysis. Network pharmacology, molecular docking, and biochemical validation further identified peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma (PPARG) as a key target of VA. VA stabilized the PPARG protein, thereby promoting lipid metabolic reprogramming. These findings provide new insights into the bioactivity of VA and suggest its potential as a natural therapeutic agent for MAFLD.

articles.title: Precision medicine in MASLD: Integrating genetics, multi-omics, and artificial intelligence for risk stratification and targeted therapy.
articles.journal: Clinica chimica acta; international journal of clinical chemistry
articles.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), formerly termed nonalcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD), encompasses a heterogeneous clinical spectrum ranging from isolated hepatic steatosis to metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH), fibrosis, cirrhosis, and hepatocellular carcinoma. Differences in susceptibility to disease, progression and extrahepatic complications between individuals are due to many different variables, such as genetic, metabolic and environmental factors, sex, reproductive status and gut microbiota. Precision medicine offers a framework to navigate this complexity by combining clinical phenotyping with inherited genetic variation and large-scale multi-omics data including transcriptomics, epigenomics, proteomics, metabolomics, lipidomics, glycomics and microbiome analysis. Here we review the current evidence on important susceptibility genes, novel multi-omics biomarkers and polygenic risk scores, and discuss how these tools can improve risk prediction and sub-phenotyping. We also discuss artificial intelligence and machine learning algorithms that integrate clinical, imaging and molecular information to allow for non-invasive diagnosis and staging. Finally, we highlight precision-based therapeutic approaches such as oligonucleotide-based agents, genotype-stratified lifestyle and pharmacological interventions, and digitally supported personalized lifestyle programs. We outline the remaining challenges and research priorities needed to integrate precision hepatology into routine care, highlighting the identification of clinically actionable MASLD subtypes and the equitable translation of findings into improved long-term outcomes.

articles.title: Pulsed field ablation with Renal denervation for persistent Atrial fibrIllation: Rationale and design of the PRAISE-AF randomized trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is the most common sustained cardiac arrhythmia worldwide and is associated with increased risks of stroke, heart failure, hospitalization, disability, and mortality. Catheter ablation has become an established rhythm-control strategy for symptomatic AF; however, the recurrence rate after ablation remains substantial, especially in patients with persistent AF. Pulsed field ablation (PFA) is an emerging nonthermal ablation technology with myocardial tissue selectivity and a potentially improved safety profile compared with conventional thermal ablation. Renal denervation (RDN) reduces sympathetic nervous system activity and has shown promising effects in reducing AF recurrence when combined with catheter ablation, mainly in patients with paroxysmal AF and hypertension. Whether RDN combined with PFA improves rhythm outcomes in patients with persistent AF remains unknown.

TRIAL DESIGN: This is a single center, prospective, randomized, patient-blinded, sham-controlled pilot exploratory trial. A total of 86 patients with symptomatic persistent AF undergoing first-time catheter ablation will be enrolled and randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive either PFA combined with RDN or PFA combined with a sham RDN procedure. Antiarrhythmic drugs (AADs) will be discontinued after the index procedure in both groups. The primary endpoint is freedom from documented atrial tachyarrhythmia recurrence, including AF, atrial flutter, or atrial tachycardia lasting more than 30 seconds, within 12 months after a single ablation procedure without AADs. Secondary endpoints include freedom from atrial tachycardia recurrence within 3 months, AF burden, blood pressure changes, and major adverse cardiovascular events. Safety endpoints include cardiac, vascular, renal, and other procedure-related adverse events.

CONCLUSIONS: This trial will assess the safety and efficacy of PFA with RDN in a postablation contemporary persistent AF patient population.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov:NCT07320768.

articles.title: Chitosan nanoparticles enhance the anti-inflammatory and anti-adipogenic effects of tart cherry anthocyanin in 3T3-L1 adipocytes.
articles.abstract: Obesity-associated adipose inflammation and gut dysfunction represent critical targets for dietary intervention. Tart cherry juice (TCJ)-derived anthocyanins (ACNs) exhibit potent anti-inflammatory and gut-protective bioactivity, but their poor stability and low oral bioavailability limit efficacy. Although nanotechnology can improve ACN delivery, conventional nanocarriers contain surfactants or emulsifiers that may impair gut health with chronic use. To overcome these challenges, we developed a surfactant-free nanoparticle platform using polysaccharides. Void nanoparticles (Vnano) were fabricated by ionic gelation of chitosan and carboxymethyl chitosan, followed by ACN adsorption through hydrogen bonding and electrostatic interactions to generate ACN-loaded nanoparticles (Tnano). Optimized Tnano achieved 80% ACN adsorption efficiency with spherical morphology (about 200 nm), narrow size distribution, and positive zeta potential (23 mV). Compared to free TCJ, Tnano demonstrated sustained ACN release, and fluorescence imaging showed dose- and temperature-dependent binding of the chitosan nanoparticles to 3T3-L1 preadipocytes. Tnano more effectively suppressed lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced inflammation, reducing interleukin-6 and monocyte chemoattractant protein-1 secretion by 39% (p < 0.0001) and 35% (p = 0.0316) in preadipocytes, and by 56.8% (p = 0.05) and 20% (p < 0.0001) in mature adipocytes, respectively, compared to LPS groups. Compared to control, Tnano reduced adipogenic lipid accumulation by 35%, versus only 14.2% for TCJ (p = 0.0003). As a proof of concept for future oral delivery applications, Tnano was encapsulated within an alginate hydrogel shell by electrospray to form a nano-in-micro format. This fully natural polysaccharide-based nanoplatform offers a strategy to enhance anthocyanin bioavailability and combat obesity-associated inflammation and metabolic disease.

articles.title: Subclinical Leaflet Thrombosis, Transcatheter Heart Valve Characteristics and Structural Valve Deterioration: Rationale and Design of the POPular PET TAVI Study.
articles.journal: Journal of nuclear cardiology : official publication of the American Society of Nuclear Cardiology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Subclinical leaflet thrombosis is common after transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) and may contribute to structural valve deterioration over time, this may be influenced by transcatheter heart valve (THV) design and other valve-related factors.

METHODS: The 'Effect of Subclinical Leaflet Thrombosis and Prosthesis Type on Transcatheter Aortic Valve Degeneration (POPular PET TAVI)' study is an international, multicenter, cross-sectional cohort study. Patients (n=180) are enrolled at five years after TAVI for a detailed assessment of THV structure and function using a multi-modality imaging approach. High-resolution four-dimensional cardiac computed tomography (4D-CT) is used to assess subclinical leaflet thrombosis and THV characteristics (e.g. neosinus volume, prosthesis deformation index, valve expansion and commissural alignment). 18F-sodium fluoride (18F-NaF) positron emission tomography (PET) is used to measure micro-calcification activity in the THV leaflets as a marker of structural valve deterioration. Transthoracic echocardiography is performed to evaluate THV and cardiac function. Obtained images are analyzed by dedicated Core Laboratories for PET and 4D-CT. To facilitate comparisons between balloon-expandable, intra-annular and self-expanding, supra-annular prostheses, enrollment is stratified for valve size and type. As of September 2026, 159 patients have been enrolled successfully, completion is anticipated in December 2026.

CONCLUSION: The POPular PET TAVI study evaluates the interplay between subclinical leaflet thrombosis, THV characteristics and structural valve deterioration at five years after TAVI. Improved understanding of these mechanisms may inform individualized antithrombotic strategies and optimized valve design aiming to enhance long-term valve durability.

articles.title: Emerging novel therapies for the treatment of hereditary haemorrhagic telangiectasia.
articles.abstract: Hereditary haemorrhagic telangiectasia is the second most common heritable bleeding disorder worldwide, with a prevalence more than twice that of haemophilia, and is the most morbid inherited bleeding disorder of women. As an autosomal dominant vasculopathy due to dysregulated angiogenic signalling, patients with hereditary haemorrhagic telangiectasia develop telangiectasias and arteriovenous malformations which cause numerous complications. These complications include moderate-to-severe chronic epistaxis, gastrointestinal bleeding, iron deficiency anemia, and requirement for intravenous iron or red cell transfusion. Additionally, incidence of intracranial haemorrhage is high and morbid non-bleeding complications, such as venous thromboembolism, stroke, and liver disease, are common. Despite this serious disease burden, hereditary haemorrhagic telangiectasia remains without licensed therapies worldwide. However, many novel, investigational agents targeting vascular and haemostatic systems are now rapidly undergoing formal development specifically in hereditary haemorrhagic telangiectasia. These agents include the selective AKT1/AKT2 inhibitor engasertib, AKT1-selective inhibitors ATV-1601 and TER-4480, plasminogen siRNA agent ALN-6400, activin receptor-like kinase 1-bone morphogenetic protein receptor type II (ALK1-BMPRII) bispecific clustering antibody DIAG723, and apelin receptor antagonist antibody TX2100. This comprehensive Review provides essential background information and illustrations summarising relevant hereditary haemorrhagic telangiectasia pathophysiology, followed by focused, detailed discussions of each of the novel agents in development, including the mechanisms, therapeutic rationale, clinical trial programmes, and potential therapeutic effects.

articles.title: Statement of Retraction: Predictors of futile recanalization following mechanical thrombectomy in acute ischemic stroke: a single-center retrospective cohort study.
Prominent V Waves Augment Right Ventricular Afterload Independent of the Lung Vessels in Heart Failure: Implications for Clinical Assessment of Pulmonary Vascular Disease.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Left atrial (LA) stiffening augments the LA V wave, pressurizing the pulmonary artery (PA) out of proportion to left ventricular end-diastolic pressure. We characterized the pathophysiologic, diagnostic, and clinical implications of LA stiffening, as defined by prominent V waves, in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction.

METHODS: In this retrospective cohort study, patients with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction and less than moderate mitral regurgitation at rest underwent invasive hemodynamic exercise testing. Patients with heightened operant LA stiffening were defined by the PA wedge pressure (PAWP) V wave exceeding mean PAWP by ≥10 mm Hg. A previously used formula for V wave-corrected PAWP was validated against the PAWP waveform pressure-time-area to explore impact of the V wave on transpulmonary pressure gradients. Clinical, echocardiographic, hemodynamic, and outcome data were compared for patients with and without prominent V waves.

RESULTS: Compared with patients without prominent V waves (n=844, 79%), those with prominent V waves (n=225, 21%) were older and more likely to be women, with more severe LA myopathy, evidenced by greater LA volume index (42.2±15.0 versus 32.5±13.0 mL/m2, P<0.001), lower LA reservoir strain (16.4±7.5% versus 23.2±8.3%, P<0.001), more atrial fibrillation (61.3% versus 22.9%, P<0.001), and increased operant LA reservoir stiffness (0.59±0.25 versus 0.23±0.24 mm Hg/mL, P<0.001). Patients with prominent V waves had markedly higher PA systolic pressure than those without (54±16 versus 38±12 mm Hg, P<0.001) despite no difference in end-diastolic PAWP-PA pressure gradient (3±5 versus 3±4 mm Hg, P=0.950). Incorporating the V wave into PAWP improved correlation between directly measured PAWP pressure-time integral compared with mid-A wave PAWP (R2=0.96 versus R2=0.86, P<0.001 for comparison). In patients with prominent V waves, the prevalence of combined pre- and postcapillary pulmonary hypertension decreased from 60.2% to 29.3% after V wave correction for the transpulmonary pressure gradients. Despite similar corrected pulmonary vascular resistances in patients with and without prominent V waves, apparent PA compliance was much lower in patients with prominent V waves (3.03±1.56 versus 4.90±2.27 mL/mm Hg, P<0.001), augmenting right ventricular afterload, and these changes were coupled with more severe right ventricular dysfunction, tricuspid regurgitation, blunted cardiopulmonary exercise reserve, and increased risk of hospitalization for heart failure or death in patients with versus without prominent V waves (adjusted hazard ratio, 2.09 [95% CI, 1.53-2.86]; P<0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: More than 1 in 5 patients with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction display prominent V waves in excess of end-diastolic PAWP. This augments right ventricular afterload due to backward transmission of the V wave, contributing to right heart failure that is independent of the pulmonary vasculature. Failure to account for the V wave during hemodynamic assessment overestimates the severity of pulmonary vascular disease present.

articles.title: Clarifying the Clinical Relevance of V Waves.
Cardiometabolic disease burden and first health-related cessation of work among middle-aged Chinese adults: a longitudinal competing-exit study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To examine whether a time-updated count of physician-diagnosed cardiometabolic conditions is associated with first survey-reported health-related cessation of work among adults in China.

METHODS: We analyzed 4,404 participants aged 45-60 years working and neither formally retired nor reporting baseline health-related work disruption in the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study. Across three intervals from 2011 to 2018, the exposure was the lagged, time-updated count of physician-diagnosed hypertension, diabetes, heart disease, stroke, and kidney disease. The outcome was first health-related work exit, with retirement, other exit, and death as competing states. The primary association was estimated with discrete-time cause-specific pooled logistic regression, participant-clustered standard errors, and 50 longitudinal imputations.

RESULTS: The cohort contributed 10,852 observed person-periods and 346 health-related work exits. Each additional diagnosed cardiometabolic condition was associated with higher odds of health-related work exit after adjustment for interval, age, sex, education, work type, smoking, alcohol, and body mass index (odds ratio 1.73, 95% confidence interval 1.51-1.97). Estimates were similar across clustering, weighting, and other sensitivity analyses. By Wave 4, standardized cumulative incidence was 6.4%, 10.5%, and 16.6% for condition counts 0, 1, and 2.

CONCLUSIONS: A higher count of physician-diagnosed cardiometabolic conditions was prospectively associated with first survey-reported health-related cessation of work, although residual confounding by unmeasured socioeconomic and job-demand factors cannot be excluded. Replication with adjudicated employment outcomes and cross-cohort validation is needed before policy or causal interpretation.

articles.title: Perfusion quality does not necessarily predict ultrastructural preservation after hyperosmotic brain perfusion.
articles.abstract: Perfusion fixation is widely used in neuroscience to prepare mammalian brain tissue for histological and ultrastructural analysis. Perfusion protocols are commonly assessed using macroscopic indicators such as gross appearance and neuroimaging, which assess the extent to which perfusate has been distributed throughout the brain. There is a critical need to determine to what extent these metrics can accurately predict high-quality ultrastructural preservation, particularly as new perfusion protocols are developed for connectomics. In this technical report, we describe evidence that these two measures can be decoupled by the addition of dehydrating agents to the perfusate solution. In three human brain donors and one canine brain donor perfused with a fixative solution containing 10% mannitol and 10% polyethylene glycol 35 kDa, macroscopic and radiological indicators of perfusion quality appeared adequate or favorable. However, electron microscopy revealed expanded extracellular space, shrunken cellular processes, and distorted cell membranes, consistent with an osmotic shock artifact resulting from severe hyperosmotic dehydration. Similar ultrastructural artifacts were observed in a canine brain donor perfused with 20% mannitol in 20% neutral buffered formalin without PEG. We compare these ultrastructural findings with findings from previously reported cases perfused with standard neutral buffered formalin without osmotic additives. These findings illustrate a risk of optimizing brain perfusion protocols designed to preserve neural circuitry based on macroscopic or radiological perfusion quality metrics alone, since these metrics can be satisfied while the ultrastructure is severely compromised.

articles.title: Development and Validation of a Novel Contact Force-Integrated Pulsed Field Quantization Index for Pulmonary Vein Isolation in a Porcine Model.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: There is no bipolar-specific quantitative ablation index currently available to guide pulsed field ablation (PFA). We aimed to develop and validate a novel contact force (CF)-integrated pulsed field quantization index (PFQI) for real-time lesion depth prediction during bipolar PFA.

METHODS AND RESULTS: In total, 27 healthy Yorkshire swine were included in a two-phase preclinical study. In Phase I, a nonlinear multivariable model was developed to derive a novel PFQI incorporating real-time CF, pulse train number, delivery voltage, and impedance variation. In Phase II, the PFQI was prospectively validated by comparing predicted with actual lesion depth, followed by PFQI-guided circumferential pulmonary vein isolation (PVI). Acute procedural success, 30-day PVI durability, and extracardiac safety were evaluated using serial electroanatomic mapping and blinded histopathological examination. Lesion depth was strongly associated with CF, pulse train number, voltage, and impedance change. The PFQI predicted actual depth with high accuracy (R = 0.94, R2 = 0.88; validation R2 = 0.82, slope = 1.014). In the validation cohort, 92% of predicted depths fell within ±0.75 mm of measured values. PFQI-guided PVI achieved 100% (6/6) acute isolation and 100% 30-day durable electrical isolation, with contiguous transmural fibrosis on histology. No collateral phrenic nerve, esophageal, or pulmonary vein injury occurred, and phrenic capture thresholds remained unchanged.

CONCLUSION: The PFQI is the first bipolar-specific, CF-integrated quantitative metric for PFA, enabling accurate, real-time lesion depth prediction. PFQI-guided PVI achieved consistent, durable, and safe PVI in a porcine model, providing a promising operator-independent quantitative strategy to optimize clinical bipolar PFA for atrial fibrillation.

articles.title: Left Atrial Appendage Closure Versus Oral Anticoagulation for Prevention of Stroke or Systemic Embolism in Patients With Atrial Fibrillation: An Updated Meta-Analysis of 7004 Patients Across Six Randomized Trials.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Left atrial appendage closure (LAAC) is an emerging alternative for stroke prevention in patients with atrial fibrillation (AF) who are unsuitable for long-term oral anticoagulants (OACs). However, its efficacy and safety relative to OACs remain uncertain.

METHODS: Three databases were searched up to April 7, 2026, for randomized controlled trials comparing LAAC with OAC in patients with AF. Risk ratios with 95% confidence intervals were pooled using a random-effects model.

RESULTS: Six RCTs (n = 7004 patients) were analyzed. The risk of stroke or systemic embolism (SSE) did not differ significantly between the LAAC and OAC groups (RR: 1.10 [0.87-1.39]; p = 0.42). The risk of ischemic SSE was significantly increased with LAAC (RR: 1.41 [1.07-1.85]; p = 0.02) compared with OAC. No significant differences were observed in all-cause mortality (RR: 0.94 [0.81-1.09]), cardiovascular mortality (RR: 0.91 [0.69-1.21]), non-cardiovascular mortality (RR: 0.91 [0.75-1.12]), or hemorrhagic stroke (RR: 0.58 [0.29-1.17]). LAAC was associated with a similar risk of overall major bleeding (RR: 0.92 [0.77-1.09]) and low risk of non-procedural bleeding (RR: 0.61 [0.52-0.73]; p < 0.001) compared with OAC. Upon sensitivity analysis comparing LAAC with DOACs, the findings remained consistent across most clinical outcomes.

CONCLUSION: LAAC demonstrates comparable risks of SSE and major bleeding to OACs, but is associated with a higher risk of ischemic SSE and reduced non-procedural bleeding, supporting its use in selected patients at high risk for long-term bleeding while emphasizing individualized shared decision-making.

articles.title: Social Engagement Programs of Area Agencies on Aging: Understanding Efforts to Reduce Social Isolation and Loneliness Among Older Adults.
articles.journal: Journal of applied gerontology : the official journal of the Southern Gerontological Society
articles.abstract: BackgroundSocial isolation and loneliness in later life are major public health concerns associated with increased morbidity and premature mortality. Area Agencies on Aging (AAAs) constitute the primary local infrastructure for aging services in the US.ObjectiveTo describe social engagement program types and partnership structures among AAAs and to examine rural-non-rural differences.MethodsWe analyzed data from the 2025 National Survey of AAAs (n = 449). Descriptive statistics summarized program and partnership prevalence; item-level Pearson chi-square tests with Bonferroni adjustments compared rural and non-rural agencies.ResultsMost AAAs offered multiple social engagement programs; volunteer engagement (66.0%), arts and creative activities (62.2%), visiting/calling programs (57.7%), and technology engagement (55.5%) were common. Non-rural AAAs were more likely to offer visiting/calling, technology-based activities, and memory cafes, while rural AAAs were more likely to partner with public health units. Rural-non-rural differences suggest context-specific influences of resources and infrastructure on program availability.

articles.title: Electrical Alternans With Alternating Left Ventricular Apical Ballooning Mimicking Takotsubo Cardiomyopathy in a Patient With Extreme QT Prolongation.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: We report unique and rare findings of coupled electrical and mechanical alternans in a patient with extreme QT prolongation.

METHODS: A 5-year-old girl with congenital long QT syndrome type 3 developed alternate left ventricular apical ballooning precipitated by mycoplasma pneumonia and azithromycin exposure.

RESULTS: During atrial pacing, electrocardiography showed beat-to-beat alternation not only in T-wave morphology but also in QRS configuration, ST segment, and QT interval. These electrical changes were tightly associated with mechanical alternans: beats with markedly prolonged QT intervals showed normal left ventricular (LV) contraction, whereas beats with shorter QT intervals and ST elevation exhibited LV apical ballooning. Treatment with mexiletine shortened the QT interval, abolished both electrical and mechanical alternans, and restored normal LV function.

CONCLUSIONS: Alternate LV apical ballooning mimicking Takosubo cardiomyopathy can be seen in a patient with extreme QT prolongation. These findings probably reflected a functional intraventricular conduction block due to marked spatial heterogeneity of repolarization between the LV base and apex.

articles.title: Changes in Lead Parameters of Cardiac Implantable Electronic Devices After VT/VF Ablation Using a Dual-Energy Lattice-Tip Catheter.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Interactions between cardiac implantable electronic devices (CIEDs) and pulsed field ablation (PFA) have been studied mainly in the context of atrial ablation, whereas the effects of ventricular ablation using a dual-energy lattice-tip catheter on ventricular leads remain unclear.

METHODS: This retrospective study involved 79 patients (mean age 60.9 ± 13.6 years) with an implantable cardioverter-defibrillator or cardiac resynchronization therapy defibrillator who underwent ventricular ablation using a lattice-tip catheter between February 2024 and November 2025. Pacing thresholds were assessed before, immediately after, and 3 months after ablation and standardized to a pulse width of 0.4 ms using the Lapicque-Weiss model. Marked acute threshold elevation was defined as an increase in pacing threshold of ≥ 1.0 V immediately after ablation. The anatomical relationship between ablation sites and ventricular lead locations was assessed based on the American Heart Association 17-segment model of the left ventricle and classified as corresponding when ablation involved the same or opposing ventricular region as the lead location, adjacent when ablation involved a directly adjacent region, and remote otherwise.

RESULTS: Marked acute pacing-threshold elevation occurred in 5 of 79 right ventricular (RV) leads (6.3%) and 2 of 22 evaluable left ventricular (LV) leads (9.1%). For RV leads, marked threshold elevation occurred in 4 of 14 patients (28.6%) in the corresponding group, 1 of 19 (5.3%) in the adjacent group, and none of 46 (0%) in the remote group. When threshold change was analyzed as a continuous variable, the acute increase was significantly greater in the corresponding group (+ 0.74 V; 95%CI 0.465-1.018) than in the adjacent (+ 0.31 V; 95%CI 0.076-0.550) and remote (+ 0.007 V; 95%CI - 0.145-0.160) groups. For LV leads, the pacing threshold increased significantly after ablation involving the corresponding segment (+ 0.71 V; 95%CI 0.167-1.245), although the overall association between anatomical relationship and threshold change was not significant. At 3 months, pacing thresholds in the corresponding groups were not significantly different from baseline for either RV or LV leads.

CONCLUSION: Marked acute pacing-threshold elevation was observed in both RV and LV leads after ventricular arrhythmia ablation using a dual-energy lattice-tip catheter. However, both RV and LV thresholds were no longer significantly different from baseline at 3 months. These findings suggest the importance of considering the anatomical relationship between ablation sites and CIED leads and of careful peri-procedural assessment of lead function during ventricular ablation.

articles.title: Borrowing-dependent estimands in external-control trials: Identification, efficiency, and sensitivity in survival analysis.
articles.abstract: Augmenting randomised trials with external controls is increasingly common in oncology and rare diseases. This paper reviews the methodology of externally controlled trials - estimands, identification assumptions, estimation, efficiency and sensitivity analysis - for right-censored survival outcomes, and organises it around a single question: what quantity does a borrowing analysis actually deliver? We distinguish the intended estimand, fixed in advance by the clinical question and the target population, from the borrowing-dependent estimand, the quantity to which a given borrowing rule is consistent. The two coincide under source-conditional exchangeability and separate otherwise, so that the borrowing-dependent estimand names, and makes estimable, a discrepancy that is otherwise reported only as unquantified bias. Within a nonparametric potential-outcomes framework we (i) define borrowing-weighted causal contrasts indexed by a weighting kernel and set out when such a contrast is, and is not, a scientifically meaningful target in its own right; (ii) establish nonparametric identification and derive the efficient influence function; (iii) construct a doubly robust, locally efficient estimator with n-consistency; (iv) introduce a sensitivity-analysis framework yielding closed-form bias bounds, E-values, and tipping points; and (v) characterise the sensitivity of the delivered estimand to the pre-specified borrowing rule via Fréchet differentiability. Simulations across 12 factorial scenarios confirm up to 49% RMSE reduction under compatibility, show that the estimators remain unbiased for the borrowing-dependent estimand when compatibility fails, and validate the sensitivity bounds. A worked example in metastatic colorectal cancer illustrates the complete analytical workflow.

articles.title: [Principles of treating patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease].
articles.abstract: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is a heterogeneous condition characterized by inflammation of the airways and lung parenchyma, manifested by persistent respiratory symptoms such as dyspnoe and cough. As a global pandemic, it affects approximately 10.3% of the population over the age of 40 and remains among the leading causes of death with an increasing mortality trend. In Hungary, the estimated actual prevalence is approximately three times higher than the number of officially registered cases. COPD imposes a significant economic burden, primarily driven by the hospital care required for acute exacerbations. The systemic consequences of chronic inflammation contribute to the development of frequent comorbidities, such as atherosclerosis and heart failure. The primary objectives in managing stable COPD are symptom reduction, improvement of quality of life, and the prevention of disease progression. The cornerstones of therapy include smoking cessation, maintenance inhalation pharmacotherapy, and various non-pharmacological interventions. The latter encompasses appropriately indicated pulmonary rehabilitation, long-term oxygen therapy, and non-invasive ventilation, as well as lung volume reduction interventions and lung transplantation in selected cases. The selection of optimal, individualized therapy combined with high patient adherence significantly improves survival rates. Orv Hetil. 2026; 167(41): 1639-1645.

articles.title: [Successful treatment of hypokalemic cardiac arrest with massive potassium replacement in a patient with Bricker urinary diversion].
articles.abstract: Severe hypokalemia is a rare but potentially reversible cause of malignant arrhythmias and cardiac arrest. Early recognition of significant fluid, electrolyte, and acid-base disturbances in patients with intestinal urinary diversion may be life-saving. We present the clinical course of a 55-year-old woman who developed severe hyperchloremic metabolic acidosis and extreme hypokalemia following prolonged vomiting and high-output fluid loss through a Bricker ureteroileocutaneostomy. The patient was admitted to the intensive care unit in a peri-arrest condition, where cardiac arrest occurred shortly thereafter. The monitored rhythm was ventricular fibrillation alternating with "torsade de pointes" ventricular fibrillation. During advanced life support, targeted high-dose intravenous potassium replacement, magnesium sulfate administration, and bicarbonate substitution were performed. A total of 120 mL of 7.4% potassium chloride was administered during resuscitation, resulting in return of spontaneous circulation after approximately 18 minutes. During the first 24 hours, a total of 460 mmol potassium chloride replacement was required. Following the return of spontaneous circulation, intermittent hemodialysis was performed to correct severe metabolic acidosis. During subsequent intensive care treatment, sepsis and bilateral pneumonia developed; however, with targeted antimicrobial therapy, organ support, and continuous electrolyte correction, the patient's condition gradually improved. Successful extubation was performed on day 7, and the patient was transferred back to the nephrology ward with favourable neurological outcome. This case highlights that rapidly developing severe hypokalaemia and metabolic acidosis in patients with Bricker urinary diversion may lead to malignant arrhythmias and cardiac arrest; however, prompt recognition of reversible metabolic abnormalities and aggressive targeted potassium replacement can be life-saving. Orv Hetil. 2026; 167(41): 1664-1668.

articles.title: [Atypical cutaneous manifestations of B19 parvovirus infection in children].
articles.abstract: The most well-known skin manifestation of human parvovirus B19 infection is erythema infectiosum, also known as fifth disease. In atypical cases, particularly among young adults, purpuric-petechial glove-and-sock syndrome (PPGSS) is observed, which is a condition characterized by a symmetrical distribution in the acral areas. Its onset is attributed to the active viremia phase; therefore, patients exhibiting symptoms are contagious, which is of particular importance in the case of immunocompromised individuals and pregnant women. In our report, we present three cases: in two patients, the skin manifestations appeared as an atypical petechial-purpuric exanthem, while in the third child, they manifested as pityriasis rosea; to our knowledge, the parvovirus-associated form of this condition has not been described in the literature to date. During laboratory testing, in addition to typical abnormalities, we observed monocytosis in the blood counts of all three patients. Detecting the virus or the virus-specific antibody response is a highly challenging, comprehensive microbiological task in which molecular tests play a key role alongside serological tests. With our cases, we wish to draw attention to the rising prevalence of diseases caused by parvovirus B19, the periodic clusters and small outbreaks, the appearance of unusual skin symptoms, and the difficulties in detecting the virus. Orv Hetil. 2026; 167(41): 1669-1675.

articles.title: Pulmonary Artery Approach for Radiofrequency Catheter Ablation of Atrial Tachycardia Originating From Left Atrial Post Wall: A Case Report.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Due to limitations in ablation energy delivery and myocardial wall thickness, endocardial ablation of atrial tachycardia can sometimes be challenging.

METHODS AND RESULTS: In this case, ablation of the left atrial posterior wall shifted the earliest endocardial breakthrough site from the posterior wall to the roof, suggesting a potential epicardial origin near left atrial roof. The atrial arrhythmia was successfully eliminated via a right pulmonary artery approach.

CONCLUSION: The right pulmonary artery approach may be an effective strategy for ablating epicardial atrial arrhythmias, particularly those originating from the left atrial posterior roof.

articles.title: The Curse of Black Sigatoka: A Backward Bifurcation Perspective.
articles.abstract: Black Sigatoka disease (BSD), also known as black leaf streak disease, is an airborne fungal infection caused by Pseudocercospora fijiensis that severely impacts global banana and plantain production. Its persistence and resistance to eradication make it one of the most challenging plant diseases to manage. In this paper, we propose a deterministic pathogen-host model to describe BSD dynamics. Due to dual transmission pathways (ascospores and conidia) and mate limitation in sexual reproduction, the model exhibits a backward bifurcation: a stable endemic equilibrium coexists with the disease-free equilibrium for certain parameter values in which the basic reproduction number, R 0  , is less than 1. This phenomenon explains why control strategies that solely reduce R 0  below one may fail. For the backward bifurcation regime, we perform sensitivity analysis of the endemic equilibrium using normalized forward sensitivity indices, Latin Hypercube Sampling, and Partial Rank Correlation Coefficients. Results indicate that effective control must extend beyond R 0  reduction and prioritize (1) limiting production of new susceptible leaves during high-risk periods and (2) developing and deploying disease-resistant plant varieties. To incorporate transmission variability, we also formulate a stochastic version of the model using the Stochastic Simulation Algorithm (SSA). Extensive numerical simulations compare stochastic realizations with deterministic predictions and quantify variability in disease dynamics. To identify the principal drivers of persistence and variability, we analyze the endemic equilibrium using Sobol's variance-based sensitivity method, which highlights the role of nonlinear parameter interactions in shaping variability.

articles.title: Sustainable iodine contrast media for a healthy future (SUSTAINED): a global survey of practice.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To investigate healthcare professionals' knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAPs) of the environmental impact and sustainability of iodinated contrast media (ICM).

MATERIALS AND METHODS: A cross-sectional web-based survey was distributed to members of professional societies and advertised via social media between June and December 2024. The questionnaire covered themes including sustainability attitudes, reduction strategies, waste management, patient awareness, and institutional policies. Data were analysed using descriptive statistics, chi-square tests, and analysis of variance (ANOVA).

RESULTS: 231 respondents from 44 countries completed the survey, primarily diagnostic radiographers (59%) and radiologists (38%). Most respondents (60%) reported that their institutions had sustainable ICM policies, and there was a significant association between institutional size and alignment with sustainability goals    X 2  = 14.2 , p = 0.003   . Adoption of reduction strategies such as protocol optimisation, saline chasers, and multi-patient systems varied significantly across institutions    X 2  = 18.5 , p = 0.001   , with younger professionals (25-44 years) more engaged  A N O V A , F = 5.62 , p = 0.001   . Respondents reported waste management practices being inconsistently applied, with 26% of respondents reporting "never engaging"    X 2  = 19.6 , p  <  0.001   . Patient awareness was perceived as low, 47% "strongly disagreeing" that patients understood the environmental impact of ICM use    X 2  = 16.9 , p = 0.002   . Variability in KAPs across European countries was minimal    s 2  = 0.0068   .

CONCLUSIONS: This survey highlights widespread professional awareness of ICM sustainability issues but reveals variability in institutional practices, limited patient awareness, and inconsistent waste management. Findings emphasise the importance of stronger institutional policies, targeted education, and international collaboration to promote sustainable ICM use.

KEY POINTS: Question How do healthcare professionals perceive and implement sustainable practices in the use of iodinated contrast media (ICM) within clinical practice? Findings While many institutions endorse sustainability, notable gaps exist in waste management, patient and practitioner education, and consistency of reduction strategies. Critical relevance statement Strengthening institutional frameworks and professional and patient engagement can enhance sustainable ICM use, safeguard resources, and mitigate environmental impact.

articles.title: Time-Dependent Prognostic Value of the sCD25-to-Ferritin Ratio in Chronic Active Epstein-Barr Virus-Associated Hemophagocytic Lymphohistiocytosis.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Chronic active Epstein-Barr virus infection (CAEBV) is an EBV-positive T/NK-cell lymphoproliferative disease characterized by persistent EBV infection in T or NK cells. CAEBV-HLH refers to hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis secondary to CAEBV.
