METHODS: Twenty-one patients who underwent surgery for ipsilateral femoral and tibial fractures were retrospectively reviewed. Fractures were classified using the Fraser and Gustilo-Anderson systems. Functional outcomes were assessed using the Karlström-Olerud criteria.

RESULTS: The mean age was 31 ± 12.1 years; 85% of patients were male. The mean follow-up was 66.6 months. The most common injury mechanism was motorcycle accident (71.4%). According to Karlström criteria, 76.1% of patients achieved excellent or good functional outcomes. External fixation was associated with significantly longer total hospital stay (p = 0.003) and higher superficial infection rates (60.0% vs. 6.3%, p = 0.028) however, this likely reflects greater initial injury severity in patients selected for this approach rather than a direct effect of the device. Patients requiring postoperative ICU admission had significantly higher complication rates (75% vs. 23.1%, p = 0.032). The Injury Severity Score (ISS) correlated significantly with operative time (rs = 0.549, p = 0.010). Delayed definitive surgery was associated with longer total hospital stay (rs = 0.492, p = 0.024) but had no effect on functional outcomes or complication rates. Fraser classification and Gustilo-Anderson grade did not significantly influence functional outcomes.

CONCLUSION: Floating knee injuries carry significant morbidity despite favourable functional outcomes in the majority of patients. External fixation prolongs hospitalisation and increases infection risk, highlighting the importance of early conversion to definitive fixation in eligible patients. Postoperative ICU admission may serve as a useful indicator for heightened complication risk.

articles.title: Multimorbidity patterns and outcomes among adults (non-maternity) with community-onset sepsis in Ireland: a retrospective national analysis of acute hospital data, 2020-2025.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Community-onset sepsis accounts for most sepsis cases and frequently occurs in individuals with underlying comorbidity. While national analyses in Ireland have described its epidemiology, impact of multimorbidity and how comorbidities co-exist to form patterns remain poorly characterised.

OBJECTIVES: To identify multimorbidity patterns among adult (non-maternity) episodes with community-onset sepsis and examine their association with critical care admission and in-hospital mortality.

METHODS: We conducted a secondary analysis of Hospital In-Patient Enquiry data from all acute public hospitals in Ireland from January 2020 to December 2025. Community-onset sepsis was defined using the present-on-admission flag. The sample comprised adult episodes aged ≥ 16 years excluding maternal admissions from conception to 6 weeks postpartum. K-means clustering identified patterns of co-occurring diseases. Multivariable logistic and negative binomial regression examined associations between patterns and outcomes.

RESULTS: Of 80,628 sepsis admissions, 58,101 (72.0%) were community-onset. Of these, 53,812 (93.0%) were adult (non-maternity); of these, 35,316 (65.6%) had at least one Charlson comorbidity. Five data-derived multimorbidity patterns were identified: metabolic-multimorbid (31%), oncological-dominant (29%), renal-metabolic (15%), progressive metabolic (13%) and cardiopulmonary (12%). Outcomes varied across patterns, with differences in critical care admission and in-hospital mortality. Cardiopulmonary pattern had the highest odds of in-hospital mortality (adjusted-OR 2.01, 95% CI 1.86-2.17).

CONCLUSIONS: Charlson comorbidity was recorded in approximately two-thirds of adult community-onset sepsis episodes and formed data-derived patterns associated with differences in critical care admission and in-hospital mortality. Multimorbidity clustering may support future risk stratification research and targeted clinical vigilance for episodes at highest risk of adverse outcomes.

articles.title: Cerebral cavernous malformations: epidemiology, molecular pathogenesis, diagnosis and therapy.
articles.abstract: Cerebral cavernous malformations (CCMs) are cerebrovascular diseases characterized by vascular lesions of the central nervous system (CNS) that can result in epileptic seizures, headaches, focal neurologic deficits (FNDs), and hemorrhagic stroke. Germline and somatic loss-of-function (LOF) mutations in one of the three established CCM-associated genes, namely CCM1 (or krev interaction trapped protein 1, KRIT1), CCM2, and CCM3 (or programmed cell death 10, PDCD10), which have been validated as core drivers of CCM pathogenesis and progression. Over the past few decades, a substantially improved understanding of the hallmarks and molecular basis of CCMs has been achieved. Key pathological hallmarks include but are not limited to excessive angiogenesis, vascular leakage, endothelial-mesenchymal transition (EndMT), defective autophagy, inflammation and immune response, oxidative stress, influenced gut microbiome and altered brain vascular microenvironment. These hallmarks are orchestrated by dysregulated signaling cascades, notably MEKK3-KLF2/4, PI3K-mTOR, and RhoA-ROCK, which integrate genetic, inflammatory, and hemodynamic cues. Concurrently, sophisticated neuroimaging (MRI with SWI/QSM) and genetic testing now enable precise diagnosis and risk stratification. Although surgical resection remains the mainstay for accessible symptomatic lesions, a wave of mechanism‑based pharmacological candidates has shown promising efficacy in preclinical models, and several have advanced to early‑phase clinical trials. This review summarizes the current understanding of CCM epidemiology, molecular pathogenesis, diagnosis and therapy, highlighting how the evolving multi‑hit concept and the dissection of downstream signaling are paving the way towards personalized management of this complicated vascular disease.

articles.title: Bone marrow adipose tissue in cardiometabolic disease: marrow niche remodeling, inflammatory hematopoiesis, and vascular pathology.
articles.abstract: Bone marrow adipose tissue (BMAT) is increasingly recognized as a metabolically active, endocrine, and immunomodulatory component of the marrow niche rather than a passive fat depot. This narrative review synthesizes biological, imaging, epidemiological, and therapeutic evidence linking BMAT and marrow metabolic activation with cardiometabolic disease. BMAT arises from marrow stromal progenitors and exhibits depot-specific heterogeneity, endocrine activity, insulin responsiveness, and context-dependent expansion during aging, diabetes, obesity, menopause, osteoporosis, and chronic kidney disease. Mechanistically, experimental studies indicate that marrow adipocytes and adipocyte-lineage niche cells can influence hematopoiesis through metabolic and local signaling, whereas trained immunity is established primarily in HSPCs, myeloid progenitors, and monocyte/macrophage populations. Human MRI/MRS studies characterize BMAT quantity and composition, whereas 18F-FDG PET reflects non-BMAT-specific marrow activation associated with vascular inflammation and early atherosclerosis; direct BMAT-cardiovascular evidence remains limited. Emerging population imaging and genetic analyses support BMAT as a disease-associated phenotype, particularly for osteoporosis and fractures. Interventions affecting metabolic, inflammatory, skeletal, or marrow pathways have differing degrees of BMAT-related evidence, and none has established that modifying BMAT improves cardiovascular outcomes. This review identifies BMAT as an emerging research phenotype while emphasizing that its causal, prognostic, and therapeutic relevance to cardiovascular disease remains unresolved.

articles.title: Chronic kidney disease as a potential risk factor for pituitary hormone dysregulation: a review of the underlying mechanisms.
articles.abstract: Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD) is a condition of abnormal kidney structure or function, pathologically characterized by chronic inflammation, tubular atrophy, vascular rarefaction, glomerulosclerosis, and interstitial fibrosis. CKD potentially represents a risk factor for several disease conditions, such as cardiovascular disease, mineral bone disorder, and electrolyte imbalance. Hormone dysregulation within the pituitary axis is yet another condition that CKD influences. Notably, CKD dysregulates several anterior pituitary hormones, either by directly influencing hypothalamic-pituitary secretion or by altering downstream hormones, which then dysregulate pituitary secretion via negative feedback. In the context of CKD-influenced hormone dysregulation, several contributors, including high uremic toxins, inflammatory cytokines, mineral imbalance, and dysregulated molecular mediators related to fibroblast growth factor 23-Klotho signaling, circulating microRNAs, the kidney-gut-brain axis, and glial and endothelial modulation, play integral roles. In conclusion, this review highlights the potential participation of CKD in pituitary dysregulation and provides insights into its potential contributors.

articles.title: Post-dexamethasone cortisol levels in non-functioning adrenal incidentalomas: a pooled individual participant data analysis.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Non-functioning adrenal incidentalomas (NFAI) are defined by 1 mg-dexamethasone suppression test (F-1mgDST) cortisol levels < 1.8 µg/dL. However, many individuals with NFAI may exhibit subtle hypercortisolism associated with increased cardiometabolic and skeletal risk. The aims of the present study are to compare F-1mgDST distributions between individuals with NFAI and population-based controls and to explore whether alternative F-1mgDST thresholds would meaningfully modify patient classification.

METHODS: This is a pooled individual participant data analysis of 7 studies evaluating cortisol secretion in patients with type 2 diabetes, osteoporosis and/or fragility fractures, hypertension, or adrenal incidentalomas. The study included 1681 participants (915 NFAI, 766 controls) with F-1mgDST < 1.8 µg/dL. Data included age, sex, body mass index (BMI), F-1mgDST, and adrenocorticotroph hormone (ACTH). We assessed the between-group differences in F-1mgDST and ACTH and the accuracy of different F-1mgDST thresholds for identifying NFAI.

RESULTS: Compared to controls, patients with NFAI had lower age and ACTH levels (62.1 ± 9.8 and 59.8 ± 12.0 years, 25.1 ± 14.1 pg/mL and 16.3 ± 10.4, respectively, p < 0.001 for all comparisons), but higher BMI and F-1mgDST values (28.1 ± 4.9 and 29.0 ± 5.0 kg/m2, 1.04 ± 0.37 µg/dL and 1.13 ± 0.39 µg/dL, respectively, p < 0.001 for all comparisons) and were more less frequently females (48.0% and 38.6%, respectively, p < 0.001). A propensity score analysis performed on 730 patients and 730 age-, BMI- and gender-matched controls confirmed these findings. We did not identify any F-1mgDST threshold with an accuracy exceeding 60% for distinguishing controls from patients with NFAI. The F-1mgDST threshold the best balance between sensitivity (54.8%) and specificity (57.2%) was set at 1.1 µg/dL (30 nmol/L), although with a low accuracy of 55.8%.

CONCLUSIONS: Individuals with NFAI have higher F-1mgDST levels than controls. More than 40% overlap exists in F-1mgDST values between NFAI and controls.

articles.title: The Role of Point-of-Care Lung Ultrasound in Diagnosing Ventilator-Associated Pneumonia in Pediatric Patients.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to assess the diagnostic accuracy of LUS for diagnosing VAP and to develop a new score based on Clinical Pulmonary Infection Score (CPIS) incorporating LUS to assess its accuracy for pediatric VAP diagnosis.

METHODS: A prospective observational study was conducted over one year (Nov 2022-Nov 2023) in the PICU of a tertiary care hospital in North India. A total of 112 mechanically ventilated children, aged 1-12 y with new respiratory deterioration and CPIS > 6 were enrolled. LUS, CXR, and endotracheal aspirate cultures were performed. LUS characteristics were analysed, and a composite score, the Lung Ultrasound Pulmonary Assessment Score (LUPAS), was developed.

RESULTS: Among 94 culture-confirmed VAP cases, LUS demonstrated high diagnostic performance. Coalescent B-lines (55.3%) and subpleural consolidations with air bronchograms (17%) had sensitivities and specificities of 75%/90% and 70%/95%, respectively. Integration of LUS into CPIS improved diagnostic accuracy, with the combined score yielding 90% sensitivity and 95% specificity, PPV of 85% and NPV of 95%, AUC 0.925.

CONCLUSIONS: LUS appears to be a promising adjunctive imaging modality for evaluating VAP in mechanically ventilated paediatric patients.

articles.title: Effect of Hepatitis B virus X T118N mutant protein in HepG2 cell cycle and apoptosis regulation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) belongs to Hepadnaviridae family and caused liver infection. HBV infection can develop into hepatocellular carcinoma, one of which is due to presence of HBV X protein (HBx). Some mutations are known to be associated with development of liver carcinoma, for instance HBx K130M/V131I (HBx_KV). In Indonesia, HBx T118N (HBx_T) has been found at similar frequency as the HBx_KV. This study aims to examine the effect of HBx T118N mutant on cell cycle and apoptosis regulation.

METHODS AND RESULTS: In this study, analysis of CyclinE, p21, Bax, and Bcl-2 gene expression was performed using RT-qPCR. Cell cycle and apoptosis analysis was done using flowcytometry with PI and Annexin V-PI staining, respectively. Caspase 3 activity assay was performed using CaspACE™ Colorimetric Assay Kit. The presence of HBx_T mutant increased CyclinE expression at 72 h post transfection, similarly to HBx_KV. Both Bax and Bcl-2 mRNA level were also increased HepG2 cells expressing HBx_T in comparison to HBx_KV expression at 72 h post transfection. HBx_T expression in HepG2 cells at 48 h post transfection caused increase of AnnexinV+/PI- and AnnexinV+/PI+ cell populations, as compared to HBx_wt expression.

CONCLUSIONS: Our data suggests that HBx_T influences cell cycle and apoptosis regulation in slightly different mechanism to HBx_KV. Further investigations are still required to understand HBx_T mutant involvement in development of chronic liver disease and liver cirrhosis.

articles.title: Cardiovascular events in aging Japanese people with hemophilia: a 3-year interim analysis of the ADVANCE Japan cohort.
articles.abstract: As life expectancy increases in people with hemophilia (PWH), cardiovascular disease (CVD) has emerged as an important comorbidity. However, prospective data on CVD occurrence and its clinical management remain limited. We performed a prespecified 3-year interim analysis of ADVANCE Japan, an ongoing 10-year multicenter prospective cohort study of PWH aged ≥ 40 years, to describe CVD occurrence, clinical management, bleeding outcomes, and associated changes in hemostatic treatment. We also explored factors associated with CVD occurrence using Cox proportional hazards models. Among 588 participants, 24 developed CVD, yielding 26 events over 3 years (cumulative incidence, 4.1%). Ischemic heart disease was the most frequent event. Exploratory analyses suggested that older age, dyslipidemia, and current smoking were associated with CVD occurrence, although estimates were imprecise because of the limited number of events. Antiplatelet or anticoagulant therapy was administered to selected patients, and hemostatic management was frequently modified following CVD events. One major bleeding event was observed among patients receiving antithrombotic therapy. This prespecified interim analysis provides prospective real-world data on the occurrence and clinical management of CVD in aging Japanese PWH. Risk factor analyses should be considered exploratory, and continued follow-up is required to define long-term cardiovascular risk and outcomes in this population.

articles.title: Metabolic basis of post-infectious sequelae after Ebola virus disease.
articles.journal: Metabolomics : Official journal of the Metabolomic Society
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Ebola virus disease (EVD) survivors often present with clinical sequelae after acute disease resolution, called post-Ebola syndrome (PES). Why some survivors develop these sequelae and others do not is poorly defined. Altered metabolism has been noted in acute EVD but has not been studied in PES. Here, we identified distinct metabolic pathways in EVD survivors with PES compared to asymptomatic survivors and potential biomarkers of PES.

OBJECTIVES: The purpose of this study was to determine if EVD survivors with PES demonstrated differential metabolism compared to asymptomatic EVD survivors.

METHODS: Plasma was collected from EVD survivors in Sierra Leone as part of an ongoing cohort study. Untargeted metabolomics (LC-MS/MS) was performed on survivors with and without sequelae as well as household contacts. Univariate, multivariate, biomarker and pathway analyses were performed in MetaboAnalyst. Spearman's R correlation was performed using JMP.

RESULTS: We identified differential expression of metabolites involved in multiple metabolic pathways in EVD survivors with PES compared to asymptomatic survivors. These pathways include the tricarboxylic acid cycle as well as amino acid, nucleotide, and short chain fatty acid metabolism. Several of these pathways are associated with immune dysfunction. The identified metabolites have potential use as biomarkers of PES.

CONCLUSION: EVD survivors with PES exhibit differing metabolism compared to asymptomatic EVD survivors in several pathways. Other studies have linked these pathways to immune dysfunction and chronic viral infection, however further immunometabolic studies of EVD survivors with PES are needed.

articles.title: Hemostatic dysfunction and thrombotic risk in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease.
articles.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is increasingly recognized as a systemic disorder with clinically relevant vascular and thrombotic consequences. Beyond hepatic steatosis, inflammation, and fibrosis, MASLD is associated with disturbances in hemostatic regulation that may shift the overall balance toward thrombosis. The prothrombotic phenotype of MASLD arises from the interaction of metabolic dysfunction, chronic inflammation, endothelial injury, platelet hyperreactivity, increased procoagulant activity, reduced natural anticoagulant capacity, and impaired fibrinolysis. These abnormalities may be detectable at early disease stages and appear to evolve with progression to steatohepatitis, advanced fibrosis, and cirrhosis. Epidemiological and clinical studies associate MASLD with venous thromboembolism, portal vein thrombosis, myocardial infarction, and ischemic stroke, with population-based data indicating approximately 1.8-fold higher venous thromboembolism risk and 3.4-fold higher PVT risk. However, conventional coagulation tests do not adequately reflect the net hemostatic balance, while candidate biomarkers and global hemostatic assays remain insufficiently validated for routine risk stratification. Hemostatic dysfunction in MASLD, particularly hypercoagulability, impaired fibrinolysis, endothelial dysfunction, and platelet activation, represents a clinically relevant but still underrecognized component of the disease. Clinical management should integrate liver disease stage, cardiometabolic burden, conventional thrombotic risk factors, and bleeding or procedural risk. Routine antiplatelet or anticoagulant therapy cannot currently be recommended solely on the basis of MASLD-related laboratory abnormalities.

articles.title: Admission serum mitochondrial DNA relative abundance is associated with angiographic no-reflow or slow-flow after primary percutaneous coronary intervention in STEMI.
articles.abstract: This study aimed to evaluate the independent association of admission serum mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) relative abundance with no‑reflow or slow‑flow (NR/SF) after primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PPCI) in patients with acute ST‑segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI), and to quantify its incremental predictive value along the clinical timeline. We prospectively enrolled 892 consecutive STEMI patients undergoing PPCI and measured pre‑procedural serum mtDNA relative abundance using quantitative real‑time polymerase chain reaction (qPCR). After overlap weighting adjustment for 17 baseline covariates, high mtDNA abundance was independently associated with an increased risk of NR/SF (OR = 2.461, 95% CI 1.535-3.948, P < 0.001), with an absolute risk difference of 11.73%, and the exposure-response relationship exhibited a significant non‑linear threshold pattern (non‑linear P = 0.006). This association remained significant for both the NR component (OR = 2.689, 95% CI 1.377-5.250, P = 0.004) and the SF component (OR = 1.940, 95% CI 1.044-3.604, P = 0.036), and high mtDNA levels were also associated with higher in‑hospital risks of cardiogenic shock, acute heart failure, and severe arrhythmias. In predictive modeling, adding mtDNA to the early admission baseline model significantly improved the area under the curve (AUC) from 0.616 to 0.680 (ΔAUC = 0.064, DeLong P = 0.001), with a net reclassification improvement index of 0.453 and an integrated discrimination improvement index of 0.035. However, once angiographic or periprocedural characteristics were introduced, the incremental predictive value no longer reached statistical significance (ΔAUC = 0.023, P = 0.056-0.068). In conclusion, elevated admission serum mtDNA relative abundance is independently associated with post‑PPCI angiographic NR/SF in STEMI patients, showing a threshold‑like exposure-response relationship; its incremental predictive value is confined to the pre‑angiographic phase, suggesting that it may serve as an auxiliary biomarker for pre‑procedural risk stratification rather than an independent predictive tool.

articles.title: Severity-associated endothelial dysfunction in post-COVID-19 patients: flow-mediated dilation and vasoactive biomarkers.
articles.abstract: COVID-19 is frequently associated with endothelial dysfunction, characterized by an imbalance between vasodilatory and vasoconstrictive mediators. This study evaluated endothelial function in the early post-COVID-19 period across groups of acute disease severity using flow-mediated dilation (FMD), circulating vasoactive biomarkers, and echocardiography. Serum endothelin-1 (ET-1), arginase-1 (Arg1), thromboxane A₂ (TxA₂)-related immunoreactivity, and prostacyclin (PGI₂)-related immunoreactivity were measured by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay. An impaired FMD response was defined as < 10% brachial artery dilation from baseline. Overall, 502 post-COVID-19 patients were classified by acute COVID-19 severity as mild (n = 262), moderate (n = 183), severe (n = 41), or critical (n = 16); 27 healthy individuals served as a reference group. Impaired FMD responses were more frequent after severe (90.24%) and critical (100.00%) disease than in the reference group (18.52%). Greater acute disease severity was associated with progressively lower FMD values, smaller absolute brachial artery diameter changes, higher ET-1, Arg1, and TxA₂-related immunoreactivity, and lower PGI₂-related immunoreactivity. After adjustment for age, sex, body mass index, systolic blood pressure, smoking, diabetes mellitus, pre-existing cardiovascular disease, and post-COVID-19 interval, acute disease severity remained associated with impaired FMD (adjusted odds ratio 3.32, 95% confidence interval 2.29-4.82; p < 0.001 per one-category increase). Biomarker-FMD correlations were generally weak. Among patients assessed during the early post-COVID-19 period, greater acute COVID-19 severity was associated with greater impairment of endothelium-dependent vasodilation and an altered profile of circulating vasoactive biomarkers. These findings indicate associated functional and biochemical vascular abnormalities without establishing causality or a mechanistic relationship. Prospective longitudinal studies are needed to clarify their temporal evolution and clinical significance.

articles.title: Discussion of mechanism behind "bamboo blind" sign observed in fatty liver parenchyma.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To elucidate the mechanism behind the so-called "bamboo blind" sign frequently observed on B-mode images as multiple low-echoic lines in nonalcoholic steatohepatitis and highly fatty liver cases.

METHODS: Six types of acoustic shadowing artifacts that might be the cause of the bamboo blind sign were defined. B-mode images were acquired for 21 fatty liver cases (inc. 9 highly fatty liver cases). The cases were then pathologically diagnosed. A phantom experiment was also performed to investigate whether refraction occurs due to the gap of sound velocity between two different media.

RESULTS AND DISCUSSION: The mechanism of the bamboo blind sign corresponded well to the acoustic shadowing from small vessels in the liver. The phantom experiment validated the same phenomenon at a larger gap in sound velocity, which can be regarded as the same level as that in highly fatty liver cases.

CONCLUSION: The refraction between blood vessels and highly fatty liver parenchyma with decreased sound velocity is the dominant reason for the bamboo blind sign.

articles.title: Effect of web-based education on NIV-related side effects and insomnia severity in COPD patients using home NIV: a randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: This study aimed to evaluate the effect of web-based education on NIV-related side effects and insomnia severity in COPD patients using home noninvasive ventilation (NIV).

METHODS: This randomized controlled trial was conducted with 75 patients between October 2023 and May 2024. Data were collected using the S³-NIV Questionnaire and the Insomnia Severity Index (ISI). The intervention group received web-based education regarding NIV-related side effects and insomnia management. Independent samples t-tests were used to compare numerical descriptive characteristics between groups, while Pearson chi-square and Fisher's exact tests were used for categorical variables. Repeated-measures ANOVA was performed to evaluate changes over time and between groups.

RESULTS: Compared with the control group, the intervention group demonstrated significantly higher total S³-NIV Questionnaire scores and higher respiration, sleep, and side-effect subscale scores at weeks 4 and 8. Significant group × time interaction effects were observed for total S³-NIV scores (p < 0.001, η²p = 0.753) and ISI scores (p < 0.001, η²p = 0.352). For insomnia severity, no significant between-group difference in ISI scores was observed at Week 4, whereas ISI scores were significantly lower in the intervention group at Week 8.

CONCLUSION: Web-based education may help improve patient-reported NIV-related symptoms and reduce insomnia severity in patients with COPD using home NIV. These findings suggest that web-based educational interventions may support symptom management and patient adaptation in clinical practice.

articles.title: Body Mass Index Variability and Cardiovascular Risk: Contemporary Evidence and Clinical Implications for Diabetes Care.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: To synthesize contemporary evidence on body mass index (BMI) variability as a determinant of cardiovascular risk, integrate mechanistic insights, and clarify its clinical relevance in individuals with and without diabetes.

RECENT FINDINGS: Large cohort studies demonstrate that greater BMI or weight variability is associated with increased risks of all-cause mortality, atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, heart failure and atrial fibrillation, independent of mean BMI. Mechanistic evidence to explain the observed association implicates adipose tissue dysfunction, ectopic fat deposition, metabolic instability, systemic inflammation, and autonomic imbalance. Diabetes may amplify these pathways through impaired metabolic flexibility and treatment-related weight fluctuations. Evidence from diabetes-specific cohorts suggests that structured, intentional weight loss may attenuate the adverse associations seen with unstructured weight cycling. BMI variability is an emerging marker of cardiometabolic instability with implications for cardiovascular risk, particularly in diabetes. Defining actionable thresholds and determining whether stabilizing weight improves outcomes are key future research priorities.

articles.title: EORTC QLQ-C30 symptom components and their functional correlates during adjuvant chemotherapy for early breast cancer: a multivariate analysis. Data from GEICAM/2003-02 study.
articles.journal: Quality of life research : an international journal of quality of life aspects of treatment, care and rehabilitation
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Understanding how multiple symptoms jointly impact functioning is essential for interpreting patient-reported outcomes (PROs) in oncology. We aimed to characterize the main dimensions underlying change-from-baseline (CFB) in symptom scores during adjuvant chemotherapy for early breast cancer, and to examine their associations with functional outcomes.

PATIENTS AND METHODS: We analyzed EORTC QLQ-C30 CFB scores from 820 patients enrolled in the GEICAM/2003-02 trial. Principal component analysis (PCA) was used to summarize correlated symptom changes into a smaller number of components, and graphical LASSO network modelling was applied to explore relationships among Health-Related Quality of Life (HRQoL) domains. Associations between components and functional scales and global health status were assessed using Spearman correlations.

RESULTS: Three components were identified in the pooled sample, explaining 53.6% of the variance: a dominant general symptom burden component, a gastrointestinal component, and a diarrhea-specific component. The general component, primarily defined by fatigue, pain, appetite loss, insomnia, nausea/vomiting and dyspnea, showed consistent negative correlations with all functional scales and global health status. Similar patterns were observed across treatment arms, although gastrointestinal-related components differed. Graphical LASSO identified fatigue as the symptom most strongly connected to functional impairment.

CONCLUSION: Symptom changes during chemotherapy are not independent, but follow a multivariate structured pattern in which a general symptom burden, anchored by fatigue, plays a central role in functional decline. These findings suggest that multivariate approaches may provide a complementary exploratory framework for summarizing correlated patterns of treatment-related burden and generating hypotheses regarding PROs. Trial registration number ClinTrials.gov: GEICAM/2003-02: NCT00129389.

articles.title: Dynamic transitions from prediabetes to diabetes and incident cardiovascular events in middle-aged and older chinese adults: a nationwide longitudinal study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Prediabetes is a heterogeneous metabolic state that may revert to normoglycemia, persist, or progress to type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). However, the cardiovascular implications of different prediabetes transition patterns and the ability to predict diabetes progression among middle-aged and older Chinese adults remain unclear. We aimed to characterize glycemic transitions, examine their associations with incident cardiovascular events, and develop prediction models for progression from prediabetes to T2DM.

METHODS: This longitudinal cohort study used data from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study. Glycemic status was defined according to American Diabetes Association criteria using fasting plasma glucose, HbA1c, self-reported diabetes, and medication use. Four-year glycemic transitions from Wave 1 to Wave 3 were assessed among 7,927 participants. Among participants with baseline prediabetes, multinomial logistic regression was used to identify factors associated with reversion to normal glucose tolerance or progression to T2DM. A Wave 3 landmark design was applied to examine subsequent incident heart disease and stroke in separate outcome-specific cohorts. Prediction models for 4-year T2DM progression were developed and internally validated using a stratified 70:30 training-test split; no external validation was performed.

RESULTS: Among 3,313 participants with baseline prediabetes, 696 (21.01%) reverted to normal glucose tolerance, 2,007 (60.58%) remained in prediabetes, and 610 (18.41%) progressed to T2DM over 4 years. Higher BMI, fasting glucose, HbA1c, dyslipidemia, smoking, and C-reactive protein, together with lower grip strength, were associated with higher odds of progression. Older age, male sex, higher fasting glucose, and higher HbA1c were associated with lower odds of reversion. Compared with stable normal glucose tolerance, prediabetes progression was associated with higher odds of incident heart disease (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 1.53; 95% CI, 1.13-2.09), whereas the association with incident stroke was not statistically significant (aOR, 1.29; 95% CI, 0.90-1.87). Stable T2DM was associated with higher odds of both incident heart disease (aOR, 1.36; 95% CI, 1.04-1.79) and stroke (aOR, 1.44; 95% CI, 1.05-1.97). The full-variable logistic regression model achieved the highest discrimination for T2DM progression (AUC, 0.715; 95% CI, 0.674-0.754), modestly outperforming the clinical baseline model (AUC, 0.699; 95% CI, 0.656-0.739) and the evaluated tree-based models.

CONCLUSIONS: Prediabetes showed dynamic 4-year transitions within the analytic cohort. Progression from prediabetes to T2DM was associated with higher subsequent odds of incident heart disease, whereas its adjusted association with incident stroke was not statistically significant. The full-variable logistic regression model showed moderate discrimination and only limited incremental improvement over the clinical baseline model; it should therefore be considered an exploratory risk-stratification tool requiring external validation rather than a clinically deployable prediction model.

articles.title: The impact of ventilation mode on systemic inflammation and organ dysfunction in a porcine model of abdominal sepsis-associated acute respiratory distress syndrome.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Sepsis commonly causes acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), and immune hyperactivation may be a causal link. Ventilator-induced lung injury (VILI) is common in ARDS, and VILI may potentiate organ dysfunction in severe sepsis. We used a porcine model of abdominal sepsis-associated ARDS to test whether ventilation strategy could impact systemic inflammation and organ dysfunction.

METHODS: Female Yorkshire pigs (6-8 months) underwent ischemia-reperfusion (I/R) injury of the small bowel and fecal clot implantation or sham laparotomy. The abdominal sepsis animals were ventilated with a volume-controlled (VC) mode using the ARDS-Net low tidal volume (LVt) method to set and adjust the mode, and applied at two time points. Late LVt, was applied once PaO2/FiO2 was ≤300, and Early LVt was applied immediately following injury. The third lung protective group used the airway pressure release ventilation (APRV) mode set and adjusted with the time-controlled adaptive ventilation (TCAV) method, also applied immediately after injury. Animals were supported for 48 h using standardized resuscitation protocols and euthanized. Physiologic variables, clinical lab data, lung histology, and plasma proteome were assessed.

RESULTS: Sham animals showed no evidence of sepsis or ARDS, whereas all experimental animals developed septic shock, requiring fluid resuscitation and vasopressors. Both LVt groups developed ARDS as measured by PaO2/FiO2 ratio by the study end (Late LVt: 129.9±16.0; Early LVt: 205.2±24.2), while the Early APRV group did not (429.4±59.4). The Sham and experimental groups all had similar proteomes at baseline. The proteomes diverged over time and ended in three distinct groups: Sham, Late LVt/Early LVt, and Early APRV. The most significantly differentially expressed proteins distinguishing the groups were involved in the immune and inflammatory response, with APRV having the lowest inflammatory signature.

CONCLUSION: In a porcine model of abdominal septic shock we found that animals ventilated with a higher mean airway pressure strategy (APRV) had decreased plasma proteomic signatures of inflammation compared to those ventilated with a conventional low tidal volume strategy. Our findings are hypothesis generating and not directly translatable to the clinical setting. Future studies should focus on further elucidating a link between VILI and its effect on systemic inflammation and organ dysfunction.

articles.title: Quality of life in patients with epilepsy in the context of socioeconomic challenges in Lebanon.
articles.journal: Quality of life research : an international journal of quality of life aspects of treatment, care and rehabilitation
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Epilepsy significantly impairs health-related quality of life (HRQoL), yet evidence from Lebanon; a country experiencing one of the most severe economic crises since the mid-nineteenth century, remains limited. This study examined multidimensional quality of life (QoL) among adults with epilepsy in Lebanon and identified its clinical, socioeconomic, and crisis-related determinants.

METHODS: A multicenter cross-sectional study was conducted between June and October 2025, recruiting 578 adults with confirmed epilepsy from community pharmacies and neurology outpatient clinics across all Lebanese governorates. Three validated instruments were administered: the Quality of Life in Epilepsy Inventory-10 (QOLIE-10), the EuroQol Five-Dimension Five-Level (EQ-5D-5 L), and the ICEpop CAPability measure for Adults (ICECAP-A). Bivariate analyses and multivariable linear regression models (Enter method) identified independent determinants of each QoL outcome.

RESULTS: Mean scores indicated meaningful impairment across all domains (QOLIE-10: 2.39 ± 0.78; EQ-5D-5 L utility index: 0.79 ± 0.24; ICECAP-A: 0.81 ± 0.21). Nearly half of participants were unemployed (48.3%) and faced antiseizure medication (ASM) shortages (50.5%). Adverse ASM effects had the largest independent effect on QoL across all three instruments (standardized β = 0.25-0.42), representing a small-to-moderate effect and exceeding all other predictors. Poorer medication adherence showed smaller but consistent independent effects on worse outcomes in the QOLIE-10 and ICECAP-A models (β = 0.08-0.12, negligible-to-small), while greater household crowding was independently associated with worse QOLIE-10 scores only (β = 0.08, negligible). Higher health literacy showed small independent effects on better QoL across all three instruments (β = 0.16-0.19).

CONCLUSION: Adults with epilepsy in Lebanon experience substantial QoL impairment across epilepsy-specific, generic, and capability-based domains, associated with treatment burden, socioeconomic vulnerability, and crisis-related barriers to care. Integrated strategies addressing medication tolerability, adherence, health literacy, and structural determinants of health are needed to improve outcomes in this population.

articles.title: Terpenes and terpenoids modulating TRPV channels in diabetes: role in fibrosis and inflammatory signaling.
articles.abstract: Transient receptor potential vanilloid (TRPV) channels are non-selective cation channels that mediate thermosensation, nociception, osmotic balance, and metabolic regulation. In diabetes, altered TRPV channel expression and decreased calcium influx key pathways modulates, include NF-κB, AMPK, and TGF-β, promoting extracellular matrix accumulation and fibrotic remodelling. The limited availability of pathway specific interventions highlights TRPV channels as potential therapeutic target in diabetes. Recently, natural phytoconstituents have shown to exhibit TRPV channel modulating properties. Studies also highlights the potential of terpenes and terpenoids to inhibit NF-κB mediated inflammation, and activate AMPK-promoted metabolic homeostasis, mitigating diabetes-associated tissue damage. Preclinical studies have explored major terpenoids such as d-limonene, p-cymene and carvacrol in diabetic models. These compounds have been reported to improve glucose tolerance and alter the blood glucose levels via different molecular mechanisms. Clinically, there are limited evidences reporting terpenoids in the metabolic syndrome and TRPV modulation. Example, Astaxanthin, a tetraterpenoid has multiple human trials in type 2 diabetes, reducing diabetic biomarkers like SIRT1, HbA1c, and fasting glucose. This review summarizes current evidence on terpenes and terpenoids in diabetes with their reported and proposed interactions with TRPV1, TRPV4 with particular emphasis on their potential links to oxidative stress, NF-κB-mediated inflammation, TGF-β-associated fibrosis, and metabolic signaling. By distinguishing experimentally supported TRPV modulation with mechanistic associations and which require further validation, this review provides an integrated framework for understanding potential contribution of terpenoid-TRPV interactions to diabetes progression and its inflammatory and fibrotic complications, while highlighting key gaps for future experimental and translational investigation.

articles.title: Worsening heart failure is not a single endpoint: a severity-gradient perspective from digoxin in rheumatic heart disease.
articles.abstract: The composite of cardiovascular or all-cause death and worsening heart failure (WHF) has become the principal efficacy endpoint of heart failure trials. Yet WHF is not one event: it spans outpatient oral-diuretic escalation, urgent intravenous-diuretic visits, hospitalisation, and HF-related death-tiers that differ markedly in frequency, ascertainment, and prognostic weight. A composite WHF benefit therefore cannot be properly interpreted without knowing which tier carries the signal, and we argue that this tier is both phenotype- and setting-dependent. Two trials published on the same day in 2026 make the point with unusual clarity. In the Dig-RHD trial of digoxin in rheumatic heart disease, the benefit concentrated in outpatient diuretic events, with neutral results at hospitalisation and death; in a contemporaneous meta-analysis of digitalis glycosides in reduced or mildly reduced ejection fraction, the same drug class reduced worsening heart failure mainly through hospitalisation, again without a mortality benefit. We use this contrast to propose a severity-gradient framework for reporting and interpreting worsening heart failure, and discuss its implications for trial design, for the translation of guideline-based evidence across health systems, and for the use of inexpensive therapies such as digoxin in low- and middle-income settings.

articles.title: Effect of vasopressin and its analogues on microcirculatory perfusion: a systematic review.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Arginine vasopressin (AVP) is a non-adrenergic vasopressor increasingly used in the management of shock. While it restores arterial pressure, its effects on the microcirculation remain uncertain, with potential for reduced regional perfusion and tissue oxygenation. The aim of this systematic review is to evaluate the effects of intravenous AVP and its analogues on microcirculatory perfusion across different haemodynamic conditions and vascular beds.

METHODS: A systematic search of MEDLINE, EMBASE, and Web of Science was conducted. Animal and human publications evaluating the effects of intravenous AVP or analogues on microcirculatory perfusion assessed with in vivo microcirculatory imaging or flowmetry techniques were included. Publications were grouped by haemodynamic condition and vascular bed.

RESULTS: Of 1693 records, 39 publications (31 animal, 7 human, 1 combined) were included, comprising 43 study-units and 152 individual measurements. Overall perfusion was decreased in 33%, unchanged in 48%, and increased in 19% of measurements, compared with baseline, saline, or other vasopressors. By haemodynamic condition, perfusion was decreased/unchanged/increased (n=study-units; % of measurements) in physiological conditions (n = 14: 57/38/4), vasodilatory or septic shock (n = 23: 24/55/21; versus baseline, fluid resuscitation or noradrenaline), haemorrhagic shock (n = 3: 17/17/67; versus baseline, saline or noradrenaline), cardiac dysfunction or arrest (n = 2: 0/67/33; versus adrenaline or noradrenaline) and cirrhosis-related portal hypertension (n = 1: 0/0/100). Across vascular beds: gastrointestinal tract (n = 18: 30/42/27), kidney (n = 9: medulla 77/23/0, cortex 27/64/9), sublingual bed (n = 7: 19/68/13), cerebral cortex (n = 2: 0/67/33), cutaneous bed (n = 6: 42/42/17), and conjunctiva (n = 1, 100/0/0).

CONCLUSION: AVP and its analogues reduced microcirculatory perfusion most consistently under physiological conditions, whereas effects in vasodilatory or septic shock were more heterogeneous. Across vascular beds, the highest proportion of measurements showing reduced perfusion was in the renal medulla. These results highlight the divergent effects of vasopressin across vascular beds and clinical conditions.

articles.title: The critical role of NFAT transcription factors in pulmonary arterial remodeling and pulmonary hypertension: from PASMC proliferation to therapeutic targeting.
articles.abstract: Pulmonary vascular remodeling is the primary driver of pulmonary hypertension (PH) progression and represents a major therapeutic challenge. Excessive proliferation of pulmonary artery smooth muscle cells (PASMCs) is a key contributor to pulmonary vascular remodeling. Accumulating evidence indicates that activation of nuclear factor of activated T cells (NFAT) transcription factors plays a critical role in the phenotypic switching of PASMCs. This review outlines the involvement of the NFAT transcription factor family in PH pathogenesis. It details the regulatory pathways of NFAT1-5 in this process, particularly their functions in PASMC proliferation, synthesizes current findings on PH therapy by modulating NFAT activity, and discusses limitations of existing research to enhance understanding of the critical role of NFAT in PH. Collectively, current evidence suggests that activation of NFAT1-4 constitutes a fundamental molecular mechanism underlying aberrant PASMC proliferation, whereas the role of NFAT5 in PH remains to be further elucidated.

articles.title: Subcutaneous furosemide in an ambulatory heart failure clinic: a single center reflection on implementation.
articles.abstract: Subcutaneous (SC) furosemide offers an outpatient option for decongestion in chronic heart failure (HF) patients who remain symptomatic on oral diuretics or who would otherwise require recurrent intravenous (IV) therapy. Furoscix, the only FDA-approved SC furosemide, delivers 80 mg over 5 hours via an on-body infusor with pharmacokinetics and diuretic effects comparable to IV dosing. In this primer, we summarize the evidence supporting SC furosemide and share our institutional experience implementing it in a multidisciplinary ambulatory HF clinic, where it has now been prescribed to more than 75 patients. We argue that successful adoption depends less on the drug itself than on the workflows-patient selection, prescribing logistics, education, and post-administration monitoring-built around it, and we outline emerging opportunities to extend SC furosemide to advanced HF, hospital discharge, and emergency department transitions.

articles.title: Primary care and idiopathic scoliosis: an evaluation of family physicians' roles.
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Idiopathic scoliosis (IS) can progress silently during growth. Early primary care detection prevents curve progression and reduces treatment burden. This study aimed to assess the role of family physicians in screening, diagnosis, counseling, and follow-up of adolescents with IS, and to evaluate primary care attributes using the Primary Care Assessment Survey (PCAS). This cross-sectional study included 150 patients with IS followed at a university orthopedics clinic in Türkiye. Data were collected via structured telephone interviews using a custom 13-item questionnaire and the validated Turkish PCAS. Descriptive statistics and bivariate parametric and non-parametric tests were used for the analysis (p < 0.05). Only 11% of participants were first diagnosed by family physicians, whereas 68% were diagnosed by orthopedic surgeons. Primary care involvement was low: scoliosis-focused examination (15%), counseling (15%), referral (15%), and exercise recommendations (19%) were infrequent. PCAS scores were highest for longitudinal continuity (79 ± 20) and trust (63 ± 12), and lowest for preventive services and counseling (44 ± 35). Late-onset scoliosis was associated with significantly higher scores in comprehensive knowledge, physical care, personal approach, accessibility, and communication (p < 0.05).

CONCLUSION: Most patients with IS are diagnosed outside primary care, highlighting a substantial underutilization of opportunistic screening and early clinical evaluation in primary care settings. Standardizing scoliosis screening during routine adolescent well-visits, enhancing primary care awareness and guidance, and strengthening referral pathways are crucial for enabling earlier detection, modifying disease progression, and mitigating long-term clinical burdens.

WHAT IS KNOWN: • Early detection of idiopathic scoliosis (IS) through opportunistic screening prevents curve progression, avoids invasive surgeries, and reduces long-term healthcare burdens..

WHAT IS NEW: • Only 11% of IS patients are diagnosed in primary care, revealing critical gaps in screening, posture examination, and counseling despite high longitudinal trust in family physicians..

articles.title: Effects of anti-inflammatory dietary education on sleep disturbances among patients with breast cancer undergoing chemotherapy: A randomized controlled trial.
articles.journal: Supportive care in cancer : official journal of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: This randomized controlled trial evaluated the effects of anti-inflammatory dietary education on sleep disturbances and inflammatory biomarkers in patients with breast cancer undergoing chemotherapy.

METHODS: A total of 132 patients with sleep disturbances were randomized to receive either a 12-week anti-inflammatory dietary education program based on the energy-adjusted dietary inflammatory index (E-DII) or usual care. Sleep disturbances were assessed using the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI) at baseline and at 12 weeks. Additional outcomes included inflammatory biomarkers, E-DII scores, and quality of life (QoL). Treatment effects on continuous outcomes were evaluated using linear mixed-effects models (LMMs) under the intention-to-treat principle. The proportions of participants with sleep disturbance (PSQI ≥ 8) at 12 weeks were compared between groups using a completer analysis.

RESULTS: Of the 132 participants, 116 (87.9%) completed the 12-week assessment. In the completer analysis, the proportion of participants with sleep disturbance at 12 weeks was significantly lower in the intervention group than in the control group (49.2% vs. 78.9%, P < 0.001). The intervention group demonstrated greater reductions in PSQI (β =  - 2.10; 95% CI: - 3.01, - 1.18; P < 0.001) and E-DII scores (β =  - 1.23; 95% CI: - 1.98, - 0.47; P = 0.002) and improved overall QoL (β = 14.07; 95% CI: 8.61, 19.52; P < 0.001). Furthermore, levels of interleukin-1β, interleukin-6, and C-reactive protein were significantly reduced, whereas interleukin-10 increased (all P < 0.05).

CONCLUSION: Anti-inflammatory dietary education reduced sleep disturbances and improved QoL in patients with breast cancer undergoing chemotherapy and was accompanied by favorable changes in inflammatory biomarkers.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: ChiCTR2500097053. Registered on 11 February 2025.

articles.title: Anti-inflammatory effects of JI-017 in cellular and an LPS-induced endotoxemia model.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Sepsis is a life-threatening condition characterized by dysregulated inflammatory responses and excessive cytokine production, leading to multi-organ dysfunction. Despite advances in supportive care, effective pharmacological strategies to directly modulate sepsis-associated inflammation remain limited. JI-017 is a multi-herbal formulation composed of Angelica gigas, Aconitum carmichaeli Debeaux, and Zingiber officinale Roscoe (2:1:1), previously studied for its anticancer properties.

METHODS: The anti-inflammatory effects of JI-017 were evaluated using an integrative approach combining in silico analysis, in vitro macrophage assays, and an in vivo lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced endotoxemia model. RAW 264.7 macrophages were used to assess nitric oxide production, cytokine expression, and inflammatory signaling pathways. In vivo effects were evaluated through survival analysis, serum cytokine measurement, and histopathological examination.

RESULTS: JI-017 significantly reduced nitric oxide production and suppressed inflammatory cytokine and chemokine expression in LPS-stimulated RAW 264.7 macrophages. In vivo, JI-017 was associated with improved survival and attenuated systemic and hepatic inflammatory responses in an LPS-induced endotoxemia model. Under the experimental conditions examined, JI-017 did not reduce LPS-induced phosphorylation of the selected MAPK and NF-κB signaling proteins.

CONCLUSION: Under the experimental conditions examined, JI-017 reduced inflammatory responses and was associated with improved survival in an acute LPS-induced endotoxemia model. These findings support further preclinical investigation of JI-017.

articles.title: The effect of a stress ball on pain, anxiety, satisfaction, and treatment continuation during extracorporeal shock wave lithotripsy: a randomized controlled trial.
articles.abstract: This study aimed to evaluate the effect of a stress ball on pain, anxiety, satisfaction, and treatment continuation among patients undergoing extracorporeal shock wave lithotripsy (ESWL). This prospective, two-arm, randomized controlled trial was conducted at the urology outpatient clinic of a university hospital between May 2025 and May 2026. A total of 50 patients undergoing ESWL for the first time were randomly assigned to the stress ball group (n=25) and the control group (n=25). Patients in the stress ball group were provided with a stress ball during the procedure in addition to routine care, whereas the control group received routine care only. Patients' pain intensity during and after the procedure, as well as satisfaction levels following the procedure, were assessed using a visual analog scale. Anxiety levels before and after the procedure were measured using the State-Trait Anxiety Inventory-State. Patients' continuation to ESWL sessions was recorded. Pain scores during (p=0.001) and after (p<0.001) ESWL were lower in the stress ball group than in the control group. Post-procedure anxiety scores were lower in the stress ball group (p=0.035), whereas satisfaction scores were higher (p=0.011). The rate of continuation to the third ESWL session was higher in the stress ball group (92% vs. 68%, p=0.034). This study found that the use of a stress ball during ESWL reduced patients' pain and anxiety levels while increasing satisfaction and continuation to subsequent ESWL sessions. As a simple, low-cost, and non-pharmacological intervention, stress ball use may improve patient comfort, tolerance of ESWL, and adherence to repeated treatment sessions.Trial Registration: ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT06846723, registered January 28, 2025.

articles.title: Metabolic stress remodels the Golgi-sphingolipid-lipid droplet axis in INS-1E β-cells: an integrated molecular signature of early β-cell vulnerability.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Glucotoxicity, lipotoxicity, and glucolipotoxicity contribute to pancreatic β-cell dysfunction in type 2 diabetes. Although endoplasmic reticulum stress has been widely studied, the response of the Golgi apparatus to metabolic stress and its relationship with sphingolipid metabolism, lipid droplets, and insulin granule-associated pathways remain poorly understood. We examined these processes together in INS-1E β-cells exposed to different forms of metabolic stress.

METHODS AND RESULTS: INS-1E cells were exposed to high glucose (33 mM), palmitic acid (0.5 mM), or both for 24 h. Cellular metabolic activity was measured by MTT assay. The expression of CREB3, ARF4, SMPD1, SMPD2, perilipin-3, ATGL, PC1/3, Syntaxin 6, and Syntaxin 12/13 was assessed by Western blotting, while NBD-ceramide fluorescence was examined by fluorescence microscopy. Metabolic stress affected Golgi stress-associated proteins and increased SMPD1 and SMPD2 expression. Increased NBD-ceramide fluorescence was consistent with changes in ceramide handling. Perilipin-3 increased without a corresponding change in ATGL, suggesting a shift toward lipid sequestration. High glucose alone largely preserved metabolic activity, whereas palmitate and combined glucose-palmitate exposure reduced both metabolic activity and PC1/3 expression. Syntaxin 6 and Syntaxin 12/13 remained unchanged.

CONCLUSIONS: Metabolic stress was associated with concurrent changes in Golgi stress-associated proteins, sphingolipid metabolism, lipid droplet regulation, and PC1/3 expression in INS-1E β-cells. These findings demonstrate coordinated molecular alterations involving Golgi stress-associated proteins, sphingolipid metabolism, lipid droplet regulation, and PC1/3 expression during metabolic stress. Functional and lipidomic studies are now needed to determine how these molecular changes contribute to β-cell dysfunction.

articles.title: Adropin signaling pathways in metabolic and non-metabolic disorders.
articles.abstract: Adropin is a secreted 76-amino-acid peptide encoded by the energy homeostasis-associated gene ENHO. First identified in 2008 as a nutrient-responsive signal linking macronutrient intake with energy balance and lipid metabolism, it is now recognized as a pleiotropic hormone with actions extending well beyond classical metabolic tissues. Circulating adropin is typically reduced in obesity, type 2 diabetes, metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease, atherosclerosis, heart failure, cognitive aging, and several fibrotic and reproductive disorders. However, diabetic kidney disease and some acute stress states show the opposite pattern. Two cell-surface partners, the orphan G-protein-coupled receptor GPR19 and the GPI-anchored neuronal protein NB-3/CNTN6, initiate overlapping but tissue-specific cascades: AMPK/ACC, PI3K/Akt/eNOS, GPR19/MAPK/PDK4, Notch1/Hes1, and TGF-β/GLI1. Through these pathways, adropin improves insulin action and mitochondrial fuel selection, increases endothelial nitric oxide bioavailability, restrains vascular remodeling, preserves blood-brain barrier integrity, and represses fibroblast activation. This review (i) separates metabolic from non-metabolic disease evidence, (ii) introduces an explicit evidence map distinguishing direct evidence, indirect evidence, and genuine controversy for every receptor and pathway, (iii) adds dedicated coverage of central feeding control, calcium-handling dysregulation in coronary disease, TGF-β/GLI1 signaling, biomarker interpretation, and translational pharmacology, and (iv) argues that progress now depends on receptor definition, assay harmonization, and delivery chemistry rather than on further disease associations. Remaining barriers include peptide instability, blood-brain-barrier delivery, non-standardized immunoassays, incomplete receptor pharmacology, and a narrow or bidirectional therapeutic window in kidney injury and tumor immunity.

articles.title: Exercise modality and planned weekly exercise exposure for motor outcomes in Parkinson's disease: a systematic review, Bayesian network meta-analysis, and meta-regression.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Exercise modality and planned weekly structured-exercise exposure may provide complementary information for Parkinson's disease motor outcomes, but their outcome-specific effects and evidential confidence remain uncertain.

METHODS: We synthesized 173 randomized trials using covariance-aware Bayesian random-effects network meta-analysis for motor symptoms, balance, walking speed, and Timed Up and Go (TUG). A key secondary analysis estimated exercise-class-adjusted associations per 250 metabolic equivalent task minutes/week, with pre-specified sensitivity analyses.

RESULTS: The category NMA networks included 110, 106, 89, and 96 trials for Unified Parkinson's Disease Rating Scale part III (UPDRS III), balance, walking speed, and TUG, respectively. Mind-body exercise had the largest posterior median versus non-exercise control for UPDRS III (g = 0.65, 95% credible interval [CrI] 0.42-0.87). In the reconstructed, exercise-category-adjusted dose models, planned weekly structured-exercise exposure was positively associated at the trial level with UPDRS III (0.121 SMD per + 250 MET-min/week, 95% CrI 0.055-0.194), balance (0.111, 0.047-0.184), and TUG (0.124, 0.058-0.190), but not walking speed (0.008, - 0.063 to 0.076). The TUG estimate attenuated after P95 dose truncation. All active-versus-control prediction intervals crossed zero; CINeMA confidence was low or very low. The evidence did not establish a universally best modality, an optimal dose, or an individual causal target. Higher planned weekly exposure was associated at the trial level with greater average improvement in UPDRS III, balance, and TUG, whereas walking speed showed no clear association. However, within-class randomized dose-contrast estimates were imprecise for all four outcomes, and the TUG association was sensitive to the high-dose tail.

articles.title: Bridging evidence gaps in opioid-sparing postoperative pain control for percutaneous nephrolithotomy: a network meta-analysis identifying optimal strategies.
articles.abstract: Percutaneous nephrolithotomy (PCNL) is the gold standard for large renal calculi, yet postoperative pain from tract dilation, capsule injury, and inflammation often delays recovery, prolongs hospital stays, and reduces patient satisfaction. Amid the opioid crisis, reliance on opioids for pain control raises concerns over adverse effects like respiratory depression, nausea, and dependence. This has spurred interest in opioid-sparing multimodal strategies, with recent studies suggesting feasibility of opioid-free discharge and comparable relief from NSAIDs with fewer side effects. However, robust comparative evidence remains scarce. This systematic review and network meta-analysis (NMA) evaluates and ranks postoperative analgesic strategies in PCNL, aiming to highlight approaches that may reduce opioid use while improving clinical outcomes in endourology. We searched PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and Cochrane Library up to March 11, 2025 for RCTs assessing VAS pain in adults undergoing PCNL. Interventions grouped: local anesthesia/nerve blocks, intravenous analgesics, local instillation, intrathecal anesthesia, aromatherapy. Bayesian NMA used ADDIS v1.16.8/R v4.0.5, with MCMC simulations, node-splitting for consistency, SMAA for benefit-risk of VAS (<24h, ≥24h) and complications. 45 RCTs (2,626 patients) formed consistent network without significant inconsistency/heterogeneity. Levobupivacaine outperformed bupivacaine/ropivacaine in VAS reduction (<24h, ≥24h) via erector spinae plane block/local infiltration. Non-opioid analgesics (NSAIDs/paracetamol) showed superior efficacy; opioids excelled short-term but not long-term. IV paracetamol plus LI-levobupivacaine ranked highest in the multicriteria analysis, although the benefit-risk ranking should be interpreted cautiously because the safety component was based on sparse and imprecise data. Limitations: RCT protocol variability (e.g., pain assessment), moderate bias in 21 studies, limited data for high-risk subgroups (e.g., renal impairment, obesity). Comparative safety could not be established because complication data were sparse and estimates were highly imprecise. This NMA supports levobupivacaine and NSAID-based IV analgesics for PCNL pain management, positioning IV-Paracetamol+LI-Levobupivacaine as a leading opioid-sparing multimodal option to address complex pain profiles. These findings encourage safer practices amid opioid concerns, potentially accelerating recovery, shortening stays, and enhancing endourology patient outcomes.Trial registration: PROSPERO CRD42024600872.

articles.title: Aridity Threshold Alters Trait-mediated Regulation of Grassland Productivity at a Global Scale.
articles.abstract: Understanding how grassland productivity responds to increasing aridity is critical under climate change, yet whether consistent thresholds exist and how underlying mechanisms shift remain unclear. Here, we conducted a global meta-analysis to examine the response of aboveground net primary productivity (ANPP) to the aridity index (AI) and the role of plant functional traits. ANPP showed a significant nonlinear relationship with AI, with a threshold at AI ≈ 0.51. Below this threshold, ANPP increased strongly with AI, whereas this relationship weakened above it. This threshold coincided with a shift in trait-productivity relationships. Before the threshold, ANPP was positively associated with traits linked to resource acquisition and conservation (LCN and SLA). After the threshold, key traits (LCN and SRL) showed reduced or reversed effects, indicating a reorganization of functional controls. Structural equation modeling further showed that the relative importance of direct climatic and trait-mediated pathways differed across the threshold. These results identify a distinct aridity threshold associated with changes in grassland productivity responses and their functional controls, emphasizing the importance of incorporating nonlinear climatic responses and trait-mediated pathways into predictions under future climate change.

articles.title: Association of virulence genes with biofilm formation in clinical Enterococcus faecalis isolates: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: This systematic review and meta-analysis examined association between virulence gene carriage and phenotypic biofilm formation in human clinical Enterococcus faecalis isolates. PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science databases were searched on April 9, 2026, and the protocol was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261405485). Eligible studies used microplate-based biofilm assessment, detected virulence genes, and provided extractable 2 × 2 data. Random-effects meta-analyses were performed using odds ratios (OR). Twenty-six studies comprising 1848 isolates were included. For strong versus non-strong biofilm formation, esp (OR 2.34, 95% CI 1.32-4.13), efaA (OR 26.28, 95% CI 1.12-614.84), and sprE (OR 3.06, 95% CI 1.18-7.92) showed significant associations, although efaA and sprE estimates were based on few studies and were imprecise. For any biofilm versus no biofilm formation, asa1 (OR 2.55, 95% CI 1.39-4.67), esp (OR 2.71, 95% CI 1.82-4.04), agg (OR 1.87, 95% CI 1.25-2.78), and cylA (OR 2.17, 95% CI 1.20-3.91) were significant. Sensitivity analyses identified esp as the most consistent association, although heterogeneity remained for strong biofilm formation. Gene-biofilm associations were gene-specific and phenotype-dependent. esp positivity alone is insufficient to predict biofilm phenotype because biofilm formation is multifactorial and context dependent.

articles.title: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease is associated with higher bone mineral density: results from NHANES.
articles.journal: Osteoporosis international : a journal established as result of cooperation between the European Foundation for Osteoporosis and the National Osteoporosis Foundation of the USA
articles.abstract:
UNLABELLED: We used data from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) to investigate the association between metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) and bone mineral density (BMD) among U.S. adults. Our findings indicated that participants with MASLD had higher BMD than those without MASLD.

INTRODUCTION: Given the stigma associated with the term "NAFLD," experts participating in a Delphi consensus proposed renaming the condition "MASLD". Nevertheless, the association between MASLD and BMD remains unclear. This study aimed to investigate the relationship between MASLD and BMD.

METHODS: A cross-sectional study was conducted among 6470 participants aged 18 years or older using data from the 2005 to 2010, 2013 to 2014, and 2017 to 2018 cycles of the NHANES. MASLD was defined according to diagnostic criteria established through a Delphi consensus. Multivariable linear regression analyses were performed to evaluate the associations of MASLD with femoral neck and total femur BMD, while logistic regression analysis was used to investigate the association between MASLD and osteoporosis.

RESULTS: Among the 6470 participants, the mean age was 53.16 ± 17.27 years, 49.54% were male, and 23.52% met the criteria for MASLD. After multivariable adjustment, participants with MASLD had higher femoral neck BMD (β = 0.0238; 95% CI, 0.0154-0.0321) and total femur BMD (β = 0.0332; 95% CI, 0.0244-0.0419) than those without MASLD. In subgroup analyses, participants with individual cardiometabolic components of MASLD, including BMI ≥ 25 kg/m², diabetes, hypertension, and hyperlipidemia, also exhibited higher femoral BMD after multivariable adjustment. Moreover, multivariable logistic regression analysis indicated that MASLD was significantly associated with lower odds of osteoporosis.

CONCLUSIONS: Our findings suggest that participants with MASLD have higher BMD compared to those without MASLD.

articles.title: Viral subversion of B-cell tolerance: mechanisms linking infection to autoimmunity.
articles.abstract: Viral infections are increasingly recognized as triggers of autoimmunity, yet the mechanisms linking viral infection to breakdown of B-cell tolerance remain incompletely understood. B-cell tolerance is maintained through sequential central and peripheral checkpoints that normally eliminate or silence self-reactive clones. Viral infections converge on shared mechanisms, including inflammatory cytokines, innate immune activation, molecular mimicry, and persistent antigen exposure, while also promoting polyreactivity, thereby enhancing the survival, activation, and expansion of autoreactive B cells. In this review, we propose that autoimmune outcomes are determined less by viral identity than by the immunological and anatomical context in which tolerance fails. We integrate mechanistic and clinical evidence across systemic, localized, and neurotropic viral infections to present a unifying framework for virus-induced B-cell tolerance breakdown. This framework identifies conserved principles underlying post-viral autoimmunity and provides a foundation for developing therapeutic strategies to preserve B-cell tolerance.

articles.title: Physical Activity Counselling for Children with Congenital Heart Disease: A Pilot Study.
articles.abstract: It is still not known how to best help children with congenital heart disease (CHD) be more active despite many previous interventions. This study aimed to determine the feasibility and acceptability of a theoretically-based physical activity (PA) counselling intervention. This is a mixed-methods pilot study of children ages 9-12 with moderate-to-complex CHD. A 12-week intervention based on behaviour change theory was designed. Participants who did not meet the World Health Organization PA guidelines (measured via accelerometers) and expressed readiness to change (measured via questionnaires) at baseline qualified. The intervention consisted of six virtual sessions with a PA counsellor, during which participants engaged in workbook activities to learn strategies to engage in PA. Intervention feasibility (recruitment, retention, completion of measures, remote implementation, session and intervention length) and acceptability (compliance, interview feedback) were assessed. PA was measured post-intervention and one year later. Thirty-three children were recruited (recruitment success: 51%). Nine out of 12 eligible participants completed the intervention (retention: 75%) with few technical difficulties (14.5%). Completion rates of PA metrics declined over the study. It took the PA counsellor 15.5 h on average per participant to conduct the intervention. Compliance was high (attendance: 100%, workbook activity completion: 64.4%). During feedback interviews, participants denoted the importance of engaging the whole family, promoting participant autonomy and empowerment, and identified lessons learned. Although this intervention was acceptable to children with CHD, the feasibility remains uncertain given recruitment challenges and time commitment required. Successful components should be considered when designing future interventions.

articles.title: Tirofiban after intravenous thrombolysis in acute ischemic stroke patients: An updated systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
articles.abstract: Early antiplatelet therapy after intravenous thrombolysis (IVT) for acute ischemic stroke remains controversial because of concerns regarding hemorrhagic complications. Tirofiban, a reversible glycoprotein IIb/IIIa receptor antagonist, may reduce platelet-mediated rethrombosis and improve reperfusion after thrombolysis. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) evaluating the efficacy and safety of early intravenous tirofiban following IVT. PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library were searched from inception through May 2026. RCTs comparing early intravenous tirofiban versus standard care or placebo after IVT were included. Outcomes included functional independence (modified Rankin Scale [mRS] 0-2), excellent outcome (mRS 0-1), symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage (sICH), any intracranial hemorrhage (ICH), and 90-day mortality. Risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were pooled using random-effects models. Six randomized controlled trials (RCTs) involving 1787 patients were included. Tirofiban significantly increased the likelihood of achieving functional independence at 90 days (RR, 1.14; 95% CI, 1.03-1.25; P = 0.019). Although tirofiban showed a trend toward improving excellent functional outcome, the difference was not statistically significant (RR, 1.21; 95% CI, 0.95-1.56; P = 0.080). No significant differences were observed in symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage (RR, 1.72; 95% CI, 0.57-5.19; P = 0.265), any intracranial hemorrhage (RR, 1.17; 95% CI, 0.72-1.90; P = 0.453), or 90-day mortality (RR, 0.92; 95% CI, 0.59-1.45; P = 0.668). Sensitivity analyses demonstrated robust findings across all outcomes. Early intravenous tirofiban following thrombolysis was associated with improved functional recovery without a significant increase in mortality or intracranial hemorrhage on a relative scale. Although a 1% absolute increase in symptomatic ICH was observed, the difference was not statistically significant. These findings support further investigation of tirofiban as an adjunct to thrombolysis in selected patients with acute ischemic stroke.

articles.title: Distinct arterial and cardiac remodelling patterns in hypertensive heart failure with a preserved ejection fraction.
articles.abstract: Hypertension (HTN) affects 30% of Africans, a driver of heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF), particularly in older adults with arterial stiffness. Studies in sub-Saharan Africa report HFpEF in younger black South Africans. Black, older, and obese patients with HTN often show left ventricular hypertrophy (LVH), raising whether HFpEF presents distinct clinical and cardiac characteristics compared to HTN alone. This study used a matched case-control design with cross-sectional data from a South African community-based sample to examine HTN in Black participants with and without HFpEF. A total of 125 HFpEF cases and 510 controls were initially identified, including 95 hypertensive HFpEF cases and 256 hypertensive controls without HFpEF for final analysis. Clinically stable consenting adults (>18 years) were enrolled, and echocardiographic, anthropometric, haemodynamic, and pulse wave velocity (PWV) measurements were obtained. The mean age was ~58 years in both groups, and 80% were overweight or obese. Central diastolic blood pressure (DBPc) (p = 0.0295) and pulse pressure (PPc) (p = 0.0352) were lower in HFpEF, while PWV was higher (10.9 ± 4.8 vs 6.9 ± 3.9 m/s, p < 0.0001). Most HFpEF participants had concentric LVH (73%). Normal LV geometry was the most prevalent pattern among controls (45%); however, among controls with LVH, eccentric LVH was more prevalent than concentric LVH. Peripheral BP (BPp) was associated with the early to late ventricular filling velocities (E/A), while DBPp, PPp, and E/A correlated with HTN treatment. Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction was associated with greater arterial stiffness, concentric LVH, reduced renal function, higher heart rate, and elevated C-reactive protein and galectin-3, supporting adverse arterial-ventricular coupling and inflammatory-driven concentric remodelling in hypertensive HFpEF.

articles.title: Continuous efficacy and safety of fluocinolone acetonide implant: long-term insights in diabetic macular edema patients from a portuguese hospital.
articles.journal: Graefe's archive for clinical and experimental ophthalmology = Albrecht von Graefes Archiv fur klinische und experimentelle Ophthalmologie
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: To assess the efficacy and safety of the 0.19 mg intravitreal fluocinolone acetonide (FAc) implant over a 36-month period in patients with refractory diabetic macular edema (DME).

METHODS: Retrospective, single-center study including patients with refractory DME treated with the FAc implant, with outcomes assessed over 36 months. The primary endpoint was the proportion of eyes with CRT ≤ 280 μm at month 36.

RESULTS: Ninety-one eyes from 62 patients were included, with a mean baseline BCVA of 44.7 ± 18.1 ETDRS letters, CRT of 508.6 ± 176.2 μm, and DME duration of 3.6 ± 1.9 years. Eyes had received a median of 6 anti-VEGF injections (IQR, 3-13) and 2 corticosteroid injections (IQR, 1-3), and 23 (25.3%) were phakic. At month 36, 44 of 87 evaluable eyes (50.6%) had a CRT ≤ 280 μm (p < 0.0001). Mean BCVA increased by 9.4 ETDRS letters from baseline to month 36 (p < 0.0001), while mean macular volume decreased by 1.76 mm³ (p < 0.0001). Adjunctive intravitreal treatment was required in 52 eyes (57.1%), and 11 eyes (12.1%) received a second FAc implant. IOP-lowering treatment was initiated or intensified in 45 eyes (49.5%), 33 eyes (36.3%) met event-based criteria for ocular hypertension, and 8 eyes (8.8%) required glaucoma surgery. All phakic eyes at baseline (n = 23) subsequently underwent cataract surgery.
