Effective long-term management is essential to prevent or delay progression to CKD and ESKD, with particular emphasis on individualized follow-up, lifestyle modification, blood pressure control, reduction of proteinuria, and avoidance of additional nephrotoxic insults. Previous publications have often addressed pediatric congenital solitary functioning kidney (CSFK), living kidney donors, and disease-related nephrectomy cohorts separately, limiting the translation of heterogeneous evidence into a common clinical approach. This review integrates congenital and acquired SFK across the life course, distinguishes shared markers of established kidney injury from etiology-specific determinants of renal reserve, and proposes an evidence-informed framework for dynamic risk stratification and risk-adapted follow-up and management. This framework is conceptual and requires prospective validation.

articles.title: Application of antibiotic-loaded bone cement in unicompartmental knee arthroplasty: inhibiting IL-6 levels and reducing postoperative infection rate.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: We aim to clarify the inhibitory effect of antibiotic-loaded bone cement (ALBC) on inflammatory factors, and its preventive effect on postoperative infections in unicompartmental knee arthroplasty (UKA).

METHODS: This prospective randomized controlled trial enrolled 104 osteoarthritis patients undergoing UKA, randomly assigned to the non-ALBC group (n = 52, bone cement without antibiotics) and ALBC group (ALBC with 1.0 g vancomycin hydrochloride, n = 52). Primary outcomes were postoperative inflammatory markers (CRP, ESR, TNF-α, IL-6); secondary outcomes included infection rate and HSS score. Independent-samples t-tests were used for continuous variables, χ2 test for categorical variables (infection rate, efficacy), and repeated measures analysis of variance for intra-group longitudinal comparisons.

RESULTS: The ALBC group demonstrated lower inflammatory markers at postoperative day 7 and at 3 months [CRP (3.52 ± 0.81 vs 6.92 ± 1.17, Cohen's d = 3.379), ESR (16.29 ± 2.31 vs 20.19 ± 4.05, Cohen's d = 1.183), TNF-α (29.71 ± 4.03 vs 36.25 ± 5.17, Cohen's d = 1.411), and IL-6 (17.05 ± 3.72 vs 22.05 ± 4.38, Cohen's d = 1.230)] (all p < 0.001), and also showed superior clinical outcomes, with lower postoperative infection rate (p = 0.016), higher HSS score (p < 0.001), and better overall clinical efficacy (p = 0.010) than the non-ALBC group.

CONCLUSION: The application of ALBC in UKA was associated with reduced postoperative inflammatory markers such as IL-6 and a lower incidence of postoperative infection. These findings suggest that ALBC may play a beneficial role in postoperative recovery and joint function rehabilitation.

articles.title: Effect of a single high-concentration sodium bicarbonate bolus on contrast-induced nephropathy in STEMI patients undergoing Primary PCI: a prospective randomized study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Contrast-induced nephropathy (CIN) remains an important complication following primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PPCI) in patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI). In emergency settings, preventive strategies must be rapid and compatible with timely reperfusion. This study evaluated whether a single preprocedural bolus of high-concentration sodium bicarbonate was associated with a lower incidence of CIN.

METHODS: In this prospective randomised study, 110 STEMI patients undergoing PPCI at two tertiary centres were enrolled. All patients received standard care, including isotonic saline hydration. Participants were assigned to saline hydration alone or saline plus a single intravenous bolus of 20 mEq of 8.4% sodium bicarbonate administered 5-10 min before contrast exposure. The primary endpoint was CIN within 48 ± 12 h, defined as an increase in serum creatinine ≥0.5 mg/dL or ≥25% from baseline.

RESULTS: Baseline characteristics were generally comparable, although baseline blood urea nitrogen was higher and estimated glomerular filtration rate lower in the control group. CIN occurred more frequently in controls than in the sodium bicarbonate group (16.4% vs. 1.8%; p = 0.008). Renal function trajectories also favoured sodium bicarbonate. However, sodium bicarbonate did not remain an independent predictor of CIN after multivariable adjustment (OR 0.061, 95% CI 0.003-1.205; p = 0.066).

CONCLUSIONS: Sodium bicarbonate administration was associated with a lower unadjusted incidence of CIN. These findings should be considered hypothesis-generating and require confirmation in larger multicentre studies.

articles.title: Surgery and/or biologics in chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps: EUFOREA/EPOS consensus paper.
articles.abstract: The therapeutic landscape of chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps (CRSwNP) has rapidly evolved over the past 6 years with the arrival of biologics, prompting a re-evaluation of the traditional stepwise management centred on corticosteroids and endoscopic sinus surgery (ESS). Although both ESS and biologics have proven efficacy, the optimal sequence, extent and timing of ESS relative to biologics remains a matter of debate. The international multidisciplinary panel of experts of EUFOREA/EPOS reached consensus on the aims, indications, timing, and therapeutic positioning of ESS, and biologics in CRSwNP. Evidence from pivotal RCTs, real-life studies and recent guidelines was critically reviewed. Consensus statements were drafted and refined through multiple rounds of discussion and voting. This EUFOREA/EPOS report provides key definitions and clinical criteria for ESS and biologics particiin CRSwNP, offering a unified framework for personalized, evidence-based care with the aim to achieve the best outcomes for patients. The expert group agreed that patients with diffuse disease should have at least a primary complete ESS, that concurrent initiation of sinus surgery and biologic therapy is not recommended with current evidence, and the indication for biologic therapy as established by earlier guidelines were enforced. It was emphasized that with the current knowledge on side effects of systemic corticosteroids, their long-term use is no longer accepted especially where biologics are available. By emphasizing complementary and disease-modifying effects of novel care strategies, this initiative aims at optimizing outcomes across the entire airway continuum in line with EPOS/EUFOREA's mission.

articles.title: Sestrin2 mitigates obesity-associated HFpEF via adaptive IRE1α-XBP1 signaling and redox regulation.
articles.abstract: Obesity-associated heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) is a metabolic cardiac disorder characterized by diastolic dysfunction. Sestrin2 is a stress-inducible regulator of metabolic and redox homeostasis, but its role in HFpEF remains incompletely defined. This study demonstrates that Sestrin2 has cardioprotective effects on obesity-associated HFpEF. In an obesity-associated HFpEF mouse model, cardiac Sestrin2 overexpression attenuates diastolic dysfunction, myocardial lipid accumulation, fibrosis, hypertrophy, and mitochondrial dysfunction without significantly affecting adiposity, circulating lipid levels, or whole-body substrate utilization. Mechanistically, Sestrin2 overexpression increases IRE1α phosphorylation and XBP1 splicing, indicating enhanced adaptive unfolded protein response signaling. Sestrin2 overexpression is also associated with increased Sigma-1 receptor (Sigmar1) expression, whereas Sigmar1 knockdown attenuates Sestrin2-associated IRE1α-XBP1 activation in vitro, suggesting the involvement of Sigmar1 in endoplasmic reticulum-mitochondrial stress adaptation. In addition, Sestrin2 overexpression enhances AMPK activation, increases acetyl-CoA carboxylase (AAC) and eNOS phosphorylation, suppresses mTOR signaling, enhances Nrf2-HO-1 antioxidant responses, and reduces inflammatory marker expression and mitochondrial ROS production. Metabolomic analysis further reveals partial alterations in metabolites associated with endoplasmic reticulum stress and redox homeostasis. Collectively, these findings suggest that Sestrin2 alleviates obesity-associated HFpEF and is associated with the activation of adaptive IRE1α-XBP1 signaling involving Sigmar1, together with improved metabolic and redox homeostasis.

articles.title: PKP2 orchestrates OXPHOS expression in cardiomyocytes via a PGC1α-dependent mechanism.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy (ACM) is an inherited cardiac disease in which most patients carry (likely) pathogenic variants in desmosomal genes, most commonly in plakophilin-2 (PKP2). While the genetic causes are well described, the molecular mechanisms driving disease progression-particularly in response to exercise-remain poorly understood.

METHODS AND RESULTS: To investigate disease-driving pathways in ACM, we used PKP2 mutant human-induced pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes (hiPSC-CMs) and myocardial tissue from ACM patients. Transcriptomic profiling revealed consistent downregulation of oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS) genes in PKP2 mutant hiPSC-CMs, which was confirmed in explanted ACM hearts carrying PKP2 variants. Reduced expression of OXPHOS-related genes was associated with lower PPARGC1A expression and decreased mitochondrial spare capacity in PKP2 mutant hiPSC-CMs. The reduction in PPARGC1A expression appeared to result, at least in part, from decreased AMPKα protein levels, a known activator of PPARGC1A previously shown to localize at the intercalated disc, as PKP2 mutant cells failed to increase PPARGC1A expression following treatment with AICAR, an AMPK activator. To directly assess whether increasing PPARGC1A expression could compensate for this defect, we overexpressed PPARGC1A, which partially restored OXPHOS gene expression and improved contractility in PKP2 mutant cells.

CONCLUSION: Our study identifies a novel transcriptional mechanism linking PKP2 loss to reduced mitochondrial function via decreased PGC1α signaling, partially through reduced AMPKα levels. Disruption of this axis reduces OXPHOS gene expression and mitochondrial function in PKP2 mutant hiPSC-CMs, potentially impairing the heart's ability to meet increased energy demands during stress, and offering a mechanistic explanation for the detrimental effects of exercise in ACM. Furthermore, these findings highlight PGC1α induction as a potential therapeutic strategy to restore OXPHOS gene expression and mitochondrial adaptability in ACM.

articles.title: Iron oxide nanoparticles for hepatocellular carcinoma theranostics: From nanoplatform design to clinical translation.
articles.abstract: The challenges in early diagnosis and effective treatment of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) are largely attributable to the underlying cirrhosis, impaired hepatic reserve, and the added complexity of heterogeneous tumor vascularity in many patients. Iron oxide nanoparticles (IONPs) are promising platforms for HCC diagnosis and treatment because of their magnetic properties, tunable magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) contrast, magnetothermal conversion capability, and modifiable surface chemistry. These features enable IONPs to be used for image-guided diagnosis, liver-directed locoregional therapy, systemic drug delivery, and treatment monitoring. In this review, we summarize the composition, crystal structure, size-dependent magnetic properties, surface modification, and in vivo fate of IONPs, along with how these characteristics influence their performance in HCC imaging and therapy. For diagnostic applications, we focus on passive accumulation, particularly mononuclear phagocyte system (MPS)-mediated hepatic contrast, ligand-mediated active targeting, and multimodal imaging. We then review therapeutic strategies, including magnetic hyperthermia (MHT), stimuli-responsive drug delivery, and combination therapy. Major barriers to clinical translation are also addressed, encompassing the heterogeneous enhanced permeability and retention (EPR) effect, high background uptake by non-tumoral liver tissue, liver function-related safety concerns, limitations of alternating magnetic fields, and manufacturing reproducibility.

articles.title: Correction to: The Role of Echocardiography in the Assessment of Epicardial Adipose Tissue: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
Robotic systems in cranial surgery: a systematic review of accuracy, clinical outcomes, and adverse events.
articles.abstract: Robotic-assisted surgery is becoming more prevalent in neurosurgery. Many studies have classified the advantages and disadvantages, particularly in spinal robotic surgeries. However, the use of robotics in cranial procedures has been limited to individual studies without large-scale review of the different modalities. This study is a comprehensive systematic review of the major robotics utilized in cranial neurosurgical procedures and their respective outcomes. Following Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines, a systematic review was conducted over PubMed, Cochrane, and Embase for articles published between January 2000 to February 2025. EndNote and Rayyan were utilized to organize the 1,409 identified studies and conduct a blinded multiphase process for including and excluding studies. Originally, studies were intended to be run as a meta-analysis to compare robotic modalities, but the existing data was too heterogeneous to statistically contrast outcomes. Overall, 51 studies were included, with six robots being discussed in more than one study. The use of robotics in cranial neurosurgery stretches mostly across functional neurosurgery, with different applications in brain tumor biopsies and resection, hemorrhage drainage, and endoscopic surgeries. Cranial neurosurgical procedures primarily apply robotics in the world of functional neurosurgery. Outside of this subspecialty, robotic-assisted cranial surgery remains sparse in the literature. As technology evolves, more use cases may be realized.

articles.title: Online vs. In Person Gambling: Does Exposure to Brick-and-Mortar Gambling Shops Lead to Increased Online Gambling?
articles.abstract: The rise of online gambling in Great Britain in the past two decades has caused increased public health concerns. This study adds to existing evidence on physical gambling environment as a driver of gambling participation, using a 2022 national survey. With respect to gambling-related risks, existing evidence suggests a relationship, albeit complex, between gambling opportunities and increased levels of related problems. The study cuts into this complexity by factorising the risk of online gambling, and leveraging a double negative control design to estimate the causal effect of exposure to physical gambling shops on individuals' online gambling participation. Our findings show that, for the survey sample, an increase in shop exposure predicts an increased average risk of online gambling. Measuring shop exposure by distance to nearest shops, we find that for all-type gambling (i.e gaming and betting), being in the highest versus lowest exposure decile raises the risk of online gambling by around 1.49 fold for the general population, and around 1.69 fold for the rural-suburban residents. These observations are in line with existing research reporting gambling risk differentials across exposure levels. Besides contributing causal estimates of these risk differences on average and for urban, rural residents, the study provides novel insights on the interpretations of the main findings in terms of partial substitution between online vs. land-based gambling. The results and methods from this study are relevant for theoretical as well as policy debates on possible interventions to prevent and mitigate online gambling harms.

articles.title: Treadmill exercise impedes cognitive decline in type 2 diabetic rats by improving mitochondrial function and modulating the TGF-β/Smad-3 pathway.
articles.journal: Pflugers Archiv : European journal of physiology
articles.abstract: Chronic hyperglycemia and cerebral insulin resistance are the major contributors to cognitive impairment in the ageing population. Due to the increased number of the worldwide type - 2 diabetic mellitus (T2DM) population, the prevalence of cognitive decline and dementia has also increased. It is well documented that moderate aerobic exercise dramatically improves cognitive function in individuals with diabetes. However, the impact of exercise on T2DM-associated cognitive decline modulating TGF-β/Smad-3 signalling is yet to be explored. In this study, we assessed the impact of treadmill exercise on cognitive health in a preclinical model of T2DM, focusing on neuroinflammation, mitochondrial function, and the TGF-β/Smad-3 signalling pathway. To develop an experimental type - 2 diabetic model, rats were fed a high-fat diet (HFD), followed by an intraperitoneal injection of a single low dose of streptozotocin (STZ, 35 mg/kg). After confirmation of diabetes, rats underwent moderate-intensity treadmill exercise for 14 weeks. We observed a significant alternation in behavioural patterns in diabetic rats compared to controls, which reversed on exercise treatment. Moreover, chronic Type - 2 diabetes compromises mitochondrial function and increases inflammation in the hippocampal region of the brain. An increase in pro-inflammatory cytokines, such as IL-1β and TNF-α, was observed in the hippocampus of T2DM animals and was reduced by exercise. Oxidative stress is markedly increased in the type - 2 diabetic brain, resulting in compromised mitochondrial function with elevated hippocampal MDA and decreased GSH and ATP levels, which are reversed in the exercise group. Furthermore, we evaluated the role of exercise on TGF-β/Smad-3 signalling in the type - 2 diabetic brain. Exercise suppresses the overexpression of this signalling cascade in the diabetic brain. In summary, moderate-intensity treadmill exercise ameliorated type - 2 diabetes-associated cognitive impairment by decreasing oxidative stress, neuroinflammation, mitochondrial dysfunction and downregulating the TGF-β/Smad-3 signalling pathway.

articles.title: Outcomes of total temporomandibular joint replacement: a systematic review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Temporomandibular joint replacement (TMJR) is a reconstructive surgical modality that is available to patients with end-stage temporomandibular disorders (TMDs) that fail conservative treatment. Alloplastic prostheses are either custom-made or stock devices used to restore mandibular function and reduce pain; however, comparative data and long-term outcomes are limited. This systematic review aimed to assess post-surgical functional, pain, and quality-of-life outcomes following alloplastic total TMJR.

METHODS: We searched PubMed, Google Scholar, Scopus, and institutional databases through March 2025, following PRISMA guidelines, to identify outcomes of alloplastic TMJR. Three reviewers independently screened and extracted the data, and a fourth reviewer resolved discrepancies. Results were summarised narratively because of variability in clinical and methodological approaches. We used ROBINS-I to evaluate study quality and the GRADE system to rate evidence certainty.

RESULTS: Eleven studies (569 patients, follow-up 12-62 months) fulfilled the inclusion criteria. Alloplastic TMJR was consistently associated with improved MMO, reduced pain, and better patient-reported QoL, although lateral excursion and protrusion were often lower than in healthy controls. Custom-made prostheses were more prevalent than stock devices, and no evidence supported one type over the other. Transient facial nerve paresis was a rare complication, and the 5-year survival rate of prostheses was > 90%. Nine out of eleven studies were at serious or critical risk of bias; however, across all outcomes, GRADE certainty was rated very low.

CONCLUSIONS: Although alloplastic TMJR holds promise of functional, pain, and quality-of-life improvements in carefully selected patients with end-stage TMD, current evidence is of very low certainty. Future multicentre trials with agreed-upon outcome measures and direct comparisons between custom and stock systems are required to reach definitive conclusions.

articles.title: Association between gestational diabetes mellitus and periodontal inflammation in a South African cohort.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To investigate the association between gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM), periodontal status, and systemic inflammatory gene expression among pregnant women in South Africa.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This case-control study included 105 pregnant women, comprising 52 women with GDM and 53 normoglycaemic controls. Participants were classified into four groups according to GDM and periodontal status. Periodontal assessment included probing depth (PD), clinical attachment level (CAL), and bleeding on probing (BOP). Peripheral blood expression of CRP, IL-6, TNF-α, MMP-8, and MMP-9 was assessed using quantitative real-time PCR and expressed as relative gene expression. Multivariable logistic regression was adjusted for maternal age, BMI, gestational age, parity, smoking status, ethnicity, and toothbrushing frequency.

RESULTS: PD, CAL, and BOP differed significantly across the four groups (all p < 0.001), with the highest BOP observed in women with both GDM and periodontitis. By GDM status, BOP was significantly higher in women with GDM [median 32.5% (range 8-70) vs. 13.0% (range 1-38); p < 0.001], whereas PD and CAL did not differ significantly in unadjusted analyses. After adjustment, BOP, PD, and CAL were significantly associated with GDM. MMP-9 relative expression differed overall across the four groups (p = 0.047), although adjusted post-hoc pairwise comparisons were not significant. IL-6 differed by GDM status in unadjusted analysis (p = 0.039) but not after adjustment.

CONCLUSION: GDM was associated with greater periodontal inflammatory burden, particularly BOP. Systemic inflammatory gene-expression differences were less consistent and showed no independent associations with GDM after adjustment.

articles.title: Sex-specific skeletal muscle fiber atrophy and reduced macrophage inflammation in a rodent transverse aortic constriction model.
articles.journal: Pflugers Archiv : European journal of physiology
articles.abstract: Heart failure is associated with systemic skeletal muscle remodeling, where sex-specific differences suggest differential peripheral involvement in disease progression. Skeletal muscle macrophages regulate angiogenesis and tissue remodeling and may contribute to early alterations in muscle structure and function during cardiac pressure overload. We tested whether chronic pressure-overload induces sex-specific skeletal muscle remodeling and alters macrophage abundance and paracrine signaling in male and female Sprague Dawley rats that underwent transverse aortic constriction (TAC) or sham surgery at 4 weeks of age and were studied after 40 wk. TAC induced 12% greater heart mass (p = 0.049) and 17% greater heart-to-body mass ratio (p = 0.018) in males, while females showed minimal cardiac remodeling. In extensor digitorum longus (EDL) muscle, TAC males exhibited ~ 10% smaller fiber perimeter corresponding with higher capillary-to-fiber perimeter exchange (p < 0.05 for both), while female TAC rats had no difference in fiber size and 17% lower capillary-to-fiber ratio than female sham (p = 0.033). In soleus muscle, TAC rats had higher capillarization indices (p < 0.05) regardless of sex. Muscle macrophage abundance was 19% lower in TAC males than sham males (p = 0.005). TAC macrophages secreted less MCP-1 (- 35%, p = 0.0058), IL-1β (- 16%, p = 0.0167), TNF-α (- 16%, p = 0.0337), and VEGF-A (- 16%, p = 0.0120) and produced less complex endothelial networks (18% larger mesh size, p = 0.001). These findings indicate that TAC is associated with skeletal muscle remodeling and macrophage immunosuppression, with some changes occurring in a sex-specific manner. This suggests the potential for immune-microvascular coupling in peripheral adaptations to cardiac pressure overload.

articles.title: Longitudinal Functional Magnetic Resonance Imaging to Assess Lung Disease in Cystic Fibrosis.
articles.journal: Annals of the American Thoracic Society
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE: Matrix pencil decomposition magnetic resonance imaging (MP-MRI) enables quantitative assessment of lung ventilation and perfusion and was shown to correlate with contrast-enhanced (CE) perfusion MRI.

OBJECTIVES: To determine the longitudinal course of MP-MRI parameters in people with cystic fibrosis (pwCF).

METHODS: Morpho-functional MRI including CE perfusion MRI and MP-MRI were performed twice in 136 pwCF with a median (range) baseline age of 14.5 (0.1-56.0) years to obtain the morpho-functional MRI score. Perfusion defect percentage (QDP) and ventilation defect percentage (VDP) were calculated by automated software. Additionally, lung clearance index (LCI) and forced expiratory volume in one second (FEV1) z-score were assessed. The participants were divided in subgroups depending on the clinical course according to cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator modulator therapy, pulmonary exacerbation status and Pseudomonas aeruginosa infection status.

RESULTS: In the total cohort, VDP improved at follow up. Change in VDP correlated with change in MRI global score, MRI CE perfusion score and FEV1 z-score. Additionally, change in QDP correlated with change in MRI global score, MRI morphology score, MRI CE perfusion score and FEV1 z-score. QDP and VDP remained stable in clinically stable pwCF (n = 55) and improved in clinically improved pwCF (n = 67). In the stable and improved group, change in QDP correlated moderately with change in MRI CE perfusion score.

CONCLUSIONS: MP-MRI assesses stability and improvement of lung perfusion and ventilation in pwCF. Changes correlate with those of established MRI scores. Therefore, QDP and VDP are sensitive longitudinal outcome parameters for future clinical studies.

articles.title: Rare Coding Variants in FOXF1 are Associated with Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension.
articles.journal: American journal of respiratory and critical care medicine
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE: Most patients with nonheritable forms of pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) lack identifiable pathogenic variants. Increasing evidence suggests that, in addition to high-impact predicted loss-of-function variants, rare missense coding variants may also contribute to disease pathogenesis.

OBJECTIVES: We identified ultra-rare missense variants in FOXF1 in two index cases with PAH. FOXF1 encodes a highly conserved transcription factor essential for lung vascular development. We sought to define the frequency of FOXF1 variants, characterize FOXF1 expression, and assess the functional relevance of FOXF1 alterations in PAH.

METHODS: Three independent international PAH cohorts were analyzed for predicted deleterious FOXF1 variants. FOXF1 expression was evaluated using bulk and single-cell RNA sequencing and immunofluorescence. Bioinformatic and chromatin-profiling approaches were used to identify potential downstream transcriptional targets, followed by promoter-reporter assays in vitro.

MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: Nine novel and one rare missense variants, one start-site variant, and one in-frame deletion in FOXF1 were identified across the three cohorts. FOXF1 expression was reduced in PAH lungs and localized predominantly to the endothelial cell compartment. Histopathological analysis revealed heterogeneous FOXF1 expression, with the lowest levels in phenotypically abnormal endothelial cells within complex vascular lesions. Single-cell analyses confirmed reduced endothelial FOXF1 expression in PAH, whereas broad FOXF1 downregulation across endothelial populations was not observed in other chronic lung diseases. Integration of CUT&Tag and ATAC-seq identified a canonical FOXF1-binding motif within the BMPR2 promoter. Promoter-reporter assays further supported FOXF1-dependent transcriptional regulation of BMPR2 and demonstrated reduced transcriptional activity of PAH-associated FOXF1 variants.

CONCLUSIONS: Large-scale genomic and transcriptomic analyses support an association between FOXF1 dysregulation and PAH and identify BMPR2 as a potential downstream transcriptional target.

articles.title: A Birth, a Death: The Grief Experiences of Mothers Who Lose One of Their Twins after Birth.
articles.abstract: This study explores the unique grief experiences of mothers who have lost one of their babies after a twin pregnancy. It aims to provide an in-depth understanding of their emotions, the challenges they faced, and their coping strategies. The data were analyzed using six-phase thematic analysis. Data were collected through semi-structured, in-depth interviews with seven mothers in Türkiye who experienced this loss. The analysis revealed that mothers experienced an intense emotional duality characterized by simultaneous grief and attachment to the surviving infant. Mothers described feelings of shock, guilt, emotional conflict, overprotective parenting, and disenfranchised grief shaped by societal minimization of their loss. Interactions with healthcare systems, funeral practices, spouses, and social environments significantly influenced the process. The study highlights the need for trauma-informed psychosocial interventions for bereaved families and emphasizes the importance of legitimizing the grief of mothers who lose one of their twins.

articles.title: Claustrophobia Symptoms in Individuals Undergoing FDG-PET Imaging: Evidence-Based Implications for Nursing Management.
articles.journal: International journal of psychiatry in medicine
articles.abstract: BackgroundFluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography (FDG-PET) is an indispensable imaging modality within precision medical practice. Nevertheless, the enclosed scanner space often triggers claustrophobic distress in scanned patients. This cross-sectional research aimed to quantify the prevalence of claustrophobia among individuals receiving FDG-PET scans and clarify relevant predictive factors linked to this adverse emotional response.MethodsA single-center cross-sectional investigation enrolled a total of 542 participants who completed FDG-PET imaging from March 2025 to November 2025. Study data were gathered via a self-designed questionnaire named Survey of Claustrophobic Severity and Nursing Demands for Patients Undergoing FDG-PET Scans.ResultsModerate to severe claustrophobic symptoms occurred in 37.27% of all subjects (202 out of 542). Multivariate Logistic regression revealed 5 statistically significant independent predictors of moderate-to-severe claustrophobia (all P < 0.05): aged 75 years or older (OR = 2.27, 95%CI: 1.15-4.51), female gender (OR = 1.92, 95%CI: 1.25-2.96), education attainment at junior high school level or below (OR = 2.53, 95%CI: 1.61-3.98), first FDG-PET scan experience (OR = 2.86, 95%CI: 1.89-4.32), and insufficient pre-scan relevant knowledge (OR = 3.46, 95%CI: 2.16-5.54). A risk scoring system built upon these 5 predictors allocated 1 point to each risk indicator, the model demonstrated satisfactory discriminative capacity.ConclusionA considerable proportion of FDG-PET scan patients suffer from moderate or severe claustrophobia, which is simultaneously influenced by personal demographic attributes and procedure-associated variables. The newly developed risk scoring tool enables efficient identification of patients at high risk of severe claustrophobic reactions.

articles.title: Community views of factors influencing participation in dengue research: Fuzzy cognitive mapping in Dhaka, Bangladesh.
articles.abstract: BackgroundBangladesh is among the countries most affected by dengue, the fastest spreading vector-borne disease worldwide. Engaging communities in designing and implementing solutions is a promising strategy for dengue control. However, collaborating with communities in urban settings like Dhaka presents challenges. As part of a pilot study for a cluster randomized controlled trial testing participatory interventions, we aimed to understand factors influencing community participation in dengue research in Dhaka.MethodsWe used fuzzy cognitive mapping to explore perceived barriers and enablers of participation. We engaged 97 participants (community members and leaders, community health workers, personnel from NGOs, public health actors, and local researchers) in 28 participatory mapping sessions. We analyzed maps using tools from graph theory, fuzzy logic, and thematic and social network analysis. Composite maps compared community and non-community perspectives.ResultsParticipants identified 223 factors influencing participation, grouped into 22 categories. Composite maps highlighted the five most influential. Both community and non-community participants emphasized positive community perceptions of dengue, involvement of community leaders, and logistical challenges as important determinants of participation. Community participants also stressed receiving benefits and innovative information sharing, while non-community participants focused on Dhaka's sociopolitical context.DiscussionAddressing barriers and leveraging enablers to community participation before beginning research is essential. Fuzzy cognitive mapping not only identified key factors, but also revealed which were most important, to whom, and why. This approach can guide researchers and others in building more equitable partnerships with communities - a step towards inclusive and decolonizing global health research.

articles.title: [Psychotic Depression: A Systematic Review of its Clinical Aspects, Diagnosis and Treatment].
articles.abstract: Psychotic depression (PD) is a severe manifestation of major depressive disorder characterized by the presence of psychotic symptoms, such as hallucinations and delusions, alongside the typical signs and symptoms of depression. This condition poses significant challenges in both diagnosis and treatment due to the complexity of its clinical presentation. A systematic review was conducted with the aim of outlining the fundamental aspects of PD, including its definition, clinical features, differential diagnosis, and therapeutic strategies. The goal is to provide healthcare professionals with a comprehensive and up-to-date overview of PD, contributing to a better understanding and clinical management of this serious psychiatric disorder.

articles.title: Integrated Multimodal Fusion Network and Multispectral Sensing Photoelectrochemical Platform for Sweat Glucose Monitoring.
articles.abstract: Sweat glucose detection offers the advantages of being painless, noninvasive, and suitable for continuous monitoring, showing broad application prospects in diabetes management. However, a single sweat glucose detection method cannot meet the requirements of multiscenario applications. To address this challenge, we developed a multimodal sweat glucose sensing platform integrating a type-II heterojunction with rare-earth nanoparticles (RENPs), which achieves an ultralow limit of detection (LOD) and a wide linear range while enabling robust adaptation to diverse scenarios. First, a photoelectrochemical sensing strategy was developed based on a Co(OH)2/Co3O4@Ag (CCA) type-II heterojunction, in which the surface plasmon resonance (SPR) effect of Ag nanoparticles lowered the LOD from 1.85 μM to 0.312 μM while maintaining a broad linear detection range of 0.001-13.776 mM. Second, a portable fluorescence quenching-recovery system was constructed based on the inner filter effect between RENPs and CCA, overcoming the corrosion and safety limitations inherent to alkaline electrolytes. To resolve spectral overlap issues at low concentrations, a dual-branch deep learning model was further designed to jointly process dual-modal fluorescence and absorption spectra, achieving 99.25% accuracy within the range of 10 μM-2 mM. Collectively, the integrated "RENPs-CCA-AI" strategy systematically addresses key challenges in sensitivity, detection range, wearable compatibility, and analytical accuracy, offering a systematic pathway toward noninvasive, continuous, and precise health monitoring.

articles.title: Association of dexmedetomidine use with stroke-heart syndrome in critically ill patients with ischemic stroke: a MIMIC-IV study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Stroke-heart syndrome (SHS) is associated with poor outcomes after ischemic stroke (IS), but the relationship between dexmedetomidine (DEX) use and SHS remains unclear.

OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the association between DEX use and SHS in critically ill patients with IS.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study used MIMIC-IV v2.2. Patients with IS receiving mechanical ventilation were included. DEX exposure was defined as use within 72 hours after ICU admission. Multivariate logistic regression, inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW), restricted cubic splines, and subgroup analyses were performed.

RESULTS: Among 953 patients, 146 (15.3%) received DEX. In the fully adjusted model, DEX use was associated with lower odds of SHS (OR = 0.611, 95% CI: 0.398-0.929, p = 0.023). The associations of cumulative DEX dose (p-nonlinearity = 0.018) and treatment duration (p-anonlinearity = 0.011) with SHS were nonlinear. Antiplatelet therapy significantly modified the DEX-SHS association (p-interaction = 0.042).

CONCLUSION: DEX use was associated with lower odds of SHS in critically ill patients with IS. Antiplatelet therapy may modify this association. Prospective studies are needed to confirm these findings.

articles.title: Exploring rehabilitation therapists' knowledge and perspectives on the use of artificial intelligence and machine learning for persons post-stroke.
articles.abstract: BackgroundThe integration of artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) within the clinical work of rehabilitation therapists in post stroke rehabilitation has the potential to transform their work performance, habits, and routines. The impact could potentially enhance integration of assessment/data analysis, personalizing therapies, documentation, and promoting home program adherence.ObjectiveThis study assesses occupational and physical therapists' current perspectives on AI/ML in post-stroke clinical rehabilitation and examines perceived barriers to potential application of AI/ML in their clinical work.MethodsThis mixed methods study includes quantitative survey data collected pre/post an AI/ML educational webinar, as well as qualitative focus group analysis that includes therapist attitudes and experiences with AI/ML, practical applications to using AI/ML, as well as the difficulties associated. The recruited therapists include occupational and physical therapy practitioners from the United States and Asia. Individuals included in the study had to have a caseload of 30% persons with stroke.ResultsFour key themes emerged from qualitative analysis: 1) current clinical work practice and identified gaps, 2) current therapists' perceptions of AI/ML, 3) perceived future of AI/ML in clinical work practices and 4) steps needed for implementation. Survey data reporting frequencies of technology use and AI/ML perceptions are integrated into qualitative findings.ConclusionsTherapists can articulate potential future uses for AI/ML technology in post-stroke rehabilitation, however, remain uncertain about when, how, and at what cost utilization will be supported in clinical work environments. Therapists desire education and support to utilize the evolving technologies in practice.

articles.title: Effects of Intrinsic Feedback-Based Gait Training Under Visual Deprivation on Balance and Gait in Stroke Survivors: A Randomized Controlled Study.
articles.abstract: Feedback is an essential component of motor learning and rehabilitation. Although extrinsic feedback is widely used in stroke rehabilitation, excessive dependence on external cues may limit opportunities for independent movement regulation. Training that emphasizes intrinsic feedback during visual deprivation (VD) may provide individuals with greater opportunities to perceive and regulate their movements using internally available sensory information. This study investigated the effects of gait training with intrinsic feedback on balance and gait abilities in individuals with stroke compared with extrinsic feedback training and conventional physical therapy. Thirty-six individuals with stroke were randomly assigned to the gait training with intrinsic feedback (GIF) group, gait training with extrinsic feedback (GEF) group, or control group (CG). The GIF performed forward and backward linear and curvilinear gait tasks on stable and unstable surfaces during VD without continuous verbal guidance. The GEF performed the same gait tasks during VD while receiving continuous verbal guidance, whereas the CG received conventional physical therapy. All interventions were conducted for 30 min, five times per week, for 8 weeks. Outcome measures included the Four Square Step Test (FSST), weight distribution, spatiotemporal gait variables, center of pressure (COP) variables, and the 10-Meter Walk Test (10 MWT). Significant group × time interactions were observed for the FSST, weight distribution, gait velocity, cadence, paretic stance phase, paretic swing phase, paretic step time, stride time, and the 10 MWT (p < 0.05). The GIF demonstrated significantly greater improvements than both the GEF and CG in the FSST, gait velocity, cadence, paretic step time, stride time, and the 10 MWT (p < 0.05). The GIF also showed greater improvement than the CG in weight distribution (p < 0.05). These findings suggest that gait training emphasizing intrinsic feedback during VD may provide additional benefits for selected aspects of balance and gait performance in individuals with stroke.

articles.title: Persistent Hypoperfusion on Post-Recanalization Digital Subtraction Angiography Perfusion Maps in Anterior Circulation Large Vessel Occlusion.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite high recanalization rates with endovascular thrombectomy for large vessel occlusion stroke, a large proportion of patients remain disabled. This study aims to investigate the clinical impact of persistent hypoperfusion that was detected immediately after recanalization.

METHODS: In this multicenter retrospective study of patients with large vessel occlusion with near-complete or complete recanalization, perfusion maps were generated from post-recanalization digital subtraction angiography. Focal hypoperfusion within the ischemic territory was detected and categorized as regional or cortical according to spatial distribution. The primary outcome was 90-day functional independence (modified Rankin Scale 0 to 2). The associations of no-reflow and outcomes were examined by multivariable logistic regression.

RESULTS: Among 375 patients (median age 69 [interquartile range 57-77] years; 67.5% men), persistent hypoperfusion was detected in 29.6% of patients. Patients with hypoperfusion had higher baseline National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (median 14 versus 12, P=0.076) and more thrombectomy passes (P=0.021). The presence of persistent hypoperfusion was strongly associated with reduced functional independence (adjusted odds ratio [aOR]=0.23, 95% CI 0.13-0.39, P<0.001), higher rates of hemorrhagic transformation (aOR=1.88, 95% CI 1.14-3.11; P=0.013) and symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage (aOR=2.95, 95% CI 1.20-7.23; P=0.018). Quantitative analysis revealed minimum regional cerebral blood flow as a key factor of functional outcome (aOR=1.67, 95% CI 1.07-2.60; P=0.023). There is no significant agreement with 24-hour computed tomography perfusion-defined hypoperfusion (κ=0.106, P=0.524).

CONCLUSIONS: Persistent hypoperfusion could be detected immediately post-recanalization in one-third of successfully treated large vessel occlusion strokes. The adverse impact to functional outcome highlights its potential as an intraprocedural biomarker for future adjunctive therapies.

articles.title: Association between multimorbidity and discordance between creatinine- and cystatin C-based eGFR.
articles.journal: Nephrology, dialysis, transplantation : official publication of the European Dialysis and Transplant Association - European Renal Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND HYPOTHESIS: Large differences between glomerular filtration rate estimated with creatinine and cystatin C-termed eGFR discordance-have important implications for health. Several demographic factors and individual long-term conditions (LTCs) are associated with eGFR discordance. We hypothesise that the presence of multiple LTCs i.e. multimorbidity is likely to be associated with eGFR discordance.

METHODS: Differences between creatinine-based and cystatin C-based eGFR (eGFRcr and eGFRcys, respectively) using European Kidney Function Consortium equations were calculated in over 400 000 UK Biobank participants. Large negative eGFR difference was defined as an eGFRcys more than 30% lower than eGFRcr i.e. ([eGFRcys - eGFRcr]/eGFRcr) <-30%. Self-reported LTCs were counted and analysed overall and by type of multimorbidity (cardiometabolic, non-cardiometabolic, mixed mental and physical). Proportions of participants with large negative eGFR differences were cross-tabulated at different chronic kidney disease (CKD) stages and according to number of LTCs. The association between number of LTCs and eGFR discordance was assessed in logistic regression models adjusted for age, sex, body mass index, smoking status and thyroid disease.

RESULTS: Multimorbidity (two or more LTCs of any type) was observed in 33% of the overall cohort and 63% of those with large negative eGFR differences. When CKD stage was assigned based on eGFRcr and then reassigned using eGFRcys, 15% of the cohort were reclassified to a more advanced CKD stage with frequency of reclassification increasing progressively with increasing counts of LTCs. Individuals with four or more LTCs of any type were more than four-fold more likely to have a large negative eGFR difference (adjusted odds ratio 4.64, 95% confidence interval 4.13-5.21) compared to individuals with no LTCs.

CONCLUSION: Discordance between creatinine-based and cystatin C-based eGFR increased substantially with multimorbidity. Cystatin C testing should be considered (alongside creatinine) in individuals with multimorbidity to refine estimation of kidney function and risk stratification.

articles.title: Child Health Challenges, Ecosystem Mismatches, and the Case for State-Level Policy Innovation.
articles.abstract: Policy Points From 2011-2023, US children's health deteriorated across >170 indicators. Chronic conditions rose from 25.8% to 31%, risk of anxiety tripled, and autism and learning disability more than doubled. Policies based on biomedical models have failed to address these trends. Life course models regard health as a developmental process, with mismatches between children's physical, nutritional, and relational environments and the ones they are evolutionarily calibrated to expect as likely drivers of declining health. State policies can help to overcome mismatches and optimize developmental ecosystems. New Mexico is pioneering and testing an approach linking early childhood policy innovation with population-level developmental measurement. The health of US children has deteriorated significantly across multiple indicators with trends accelerating since 2007. From 2011-2023, the prevalence of chronic conditions among 3-19-year-olds rose from 25.8 to 31%, obesity rose from 17 to 20%, and autism and learning disabilities more than doubled. Rates of anxiety, loneliness, depression, early onset of menstruation and trouble sleeping all increased. Biomedically driven policy and practice have improved treatment of certain established medical conditions (e.g., childhood cancers and congenital heart disease), but failed to stem increasing mental health challenges, and neurodevelopmental disorders. Life course models point to fundamental changes in the early developmental ecosystem resulting in profound mismatches between the conditions children are evolutionarily primed and historically calibrated to expect and those they currently experience as primary drivers of these changes. The Industrial Revolution accelerated changes in children's physical, relational, and nutritional environments; temporal rhythms; and cognitive demands. The Digital Revolution further accelerated the speed and degree of change, potentially outpacing children's capacity for adaptive developmental responses. These multiple environmental changes do not act in isolation but interact in multilevel, dynamic, and complex ways to form the developmental ecosystems shaping children's developmental trajectories. In this paper we suggest a reorientation of child health policy and resulting interventions-expanding the focus beyond isolated social risks and behavioral deficits to address ecosystem-level influences and shift population outcomes by altering health development trajectories. We also suggest a suite of actionable state-level policy solutions geared to improve the configuration of these developmental ecosystems. We highlight state policy innovations such as New Mexico's comprehensive portfolio of early childhood policy changes and infrastructure upgrades along with ongoing population-level measurement of children's health development to monitor policy impact.

articles.title: Effects of environmental estrogen on the development of pulmonary inflammatory response in a murine model of older adults.
articles.journal: Journal of environmental science and health. Part C, Toxicology and carcinogenesis
articles.abstract: Allergic diseases are the most common chronic disorders in developed countries. Asthma in older adults is a significant cause of morbidity and mortality, and is increasingly important as life expectancy rises. We investigated the effects of environmental estrogen (EE) exposure on pulmonary inflammatory response in a murine model of older adults. We used our exposure model in old (>18 months) and young (6-8 wk) mice. Bisphenol S (BPS), the most widely used bisphenol A substitute, was administered in drinking water. Cat dander extract (CDE) allergen was given every other day for two weeks. Twenty-four hours after the last nasal application of CDE, the airway hyperresponsiveness (AHR) was analyzed, and bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF), serum, and lung samples were collected. Our model demonstrated that EE exposure promotes AHR in older mice but not in young mice. Baseline numbers of total leukocytes and neutrophils in old mice were significantly higher than those of young mice. Lung histology shows increased cellular infiltration in EE-exposed/allergen-sensitized mice, with higher percentages of severity scores in older mice than in young mice. These findings indicate increased sensitivity to EE exposure and allergen sensitization in older adults. Further investigation into the mechanisms underlying these differential responses is necessary.

articles.title: USP11 Drives Cerebral Ischemia-Reperfusion Injury Via Promoting Ferroptosis by Deubiquitinating and Stabilizing ASK1.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury (CIRI) represents a pivotal pathological mechanism underlying ischemic cerebrovascular disorders including cerebral stroke. Currently, there are lack of effective preventive or therapeutic methods. Ubiquitin-specific protease 11 (USP11) is a member of the most prevalent ubiquitination-specific protease (USP) family. It has been shown that USP11 plays diverse and significant roles in a variety of diseases, such as hepatocellular carcinoma, prostate cancer, and intervertebral disc degeneration. However, its precise function and molecular mechanisms involvement in CIRI remain unknown.

METHODS: USP11 knockout (USP11-KO) and adeno-associated virus 9-mediated USP11 over-expression (USP11-OE) mice were established as a mouse model of CIRI, and USP11 knockdown and overexpression adenovirus were used to establish a cell model, to investigate the effect of USP11 on CIRI in vivo and in vitro. Molecular biological studies were used to clarify the mechanism of USP11 mediated ferroptosis during CIRI.

RESULTS: The expression of USP11 is increased during CIRI. Functionally, USP11 deficiency attenuated neurological deficits, cerebral infarction, neuroinflammation, and ferroptosis during CIRI, whereas specific overexpression of USP11 exacerbated these pathological processes. Furthermore, USP11 knockdown inhibited neuronal injury, inflammatory response and ferroptosis, while USP11 overexpression promoted these processes. Mechanistically, USP11 bind to ASK1 and inhibit its K48-linked ubiquitination, thereby enhancing the activity of the ASK1-JNK/p38 signaling pathway. More importantly, the regulation of USP11 on neuronal ferroptosis and CIRI relied on its regulation of the ASK1-JNK/p38 signaling axis.

CONCLUSIONS: Our study clarified the new functions and mechanisms of USP11 during CIRI. Targeting USP11-ASK1-JNK/p38-ferroptosis may be a new promising strategy for the prevention and treatment of CIRI.

articles.title: Anthocyanin and Blueberry Intake, Lipids, C-Reactive Protein, and the Risk of Cardiovascular Disease in Women.
articles.journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Anthocyanins and anthocyanin-rich berries have demonstrated lipid-lowering and anti-inflammatory effects; however, associations with cardiovascular disease remain mixed. We therefore examined anthocyanin and blueberry intake for prospective associations with cardiovascular disease risk and cross-sectional associations with lipids and hs-CRP (high-sensitivity C-reactive protein) in the WHS (Women's Health Study).

METHODS: Among 38 088 women who completed a baseline semiquantitative food frequency questionnaire in 1992 to 1995, we estimated intake of total anthocyanins, 6 anthocyanin subclasses, and blueberries. Multivariable hazard ratios (HRs) were calculated for confirmed major adverse cardiovascular events, including nonfatal myocardial infarction, nonfatal stroke, and cardiovascular disease death. In a subset of 26 912 women with baseline blood samples, multivariable odds ratios were calculated for adverse lipid and hs-CRP levels.

RESULTS: During a median 28.0-year follow-up, 2752 major adverse cardiovascular event cases occurred. Age-, energy-, and WHS treatment-adjusted HRs across quintiles of total anthocyanin intake were 1.00 (reference), 0.87 (95% CI, 0.78-0.98), 0.79 (95% CI, 0.70-0.89), 0.81 (95% CI, 0.72-0.91), and 0.88 (95% CI, 0.79-0.99) (P-trend=0.23). Further adjustment for clinical, lifestyle, and dietary factors showed no significant associations with major adverse cardiovascular events or their components, with similar null findings observed for anthocyanin subclasses and blueberries. In cross-sectional analyses, higher total anthocyanins and anthocyanin subclasses, except pelargonidin, were significantly associated with lower multivariable-adjusted odds of adverse high-density lipoprotein cholesterol and triglycerides (all other P-trend<0.05).

CONCLUSIONS: In the WHS, anthocyanin and blueberry intake were not significantly associated with cardiovascular disease risk. However, higher anthocyanin intake was cross-sectionally associated with lower odds of adverse high-density lipoprotein cholesterol and triglycerides.

articles.title: Managing growth and puberty concerns in individuals with Duchenne muscular dystrophy: Updated guidance and future directions.
articles.abstract: Long-term glucocorticoid therapy is standard of care for individuals with Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) but often results in impaired growth and delayed or incomplete puberty, impacting their physical and psychosocial health. Although DMD endocrine care has evolved, leading to inclusion in the 2018 Care Considerations, these issues remain prevalent and concerning, and gaps in care persist. The Growth and Puberty Working Group of the OPTIMIZE DMD Consortium, an international multidisciplinary group including endocrinology and neuromuscular specialists with DMD expertise, conducted a literature review and surveyed clinicians to inform updated clinical guidance on growth and puberty. This report is based on evidence where available, plus expert consensus, and thereby provides revised guidance on the investigation and management of growth and pubertal delay, as well as hypogonadism beyond the pubertal years, among individuals with DMD. It also addresses new topics subsequent to the 2018 Care Considerations, including: 1) the dissociative glucocorticoid vamorolone and its impact on growth, and 2) gonadal function in older adolescents and young adults. With the current lack of long-term data on growth and puberty outcomes, prevailing themes underscore the importance of person- and family-centered care with informed shared decision-making aligned with individualized goals plus interdisciplinary team communication. This report also highlights specific areas in these domains in need of research. Through ongoing collaborations within the OPTIMIZE DMD Consortium, growth and puberty care continues to evolve and will inform and advance research to improve the health and quality of life of individuals with DMD.

articles.title: Neuroprotective effects of lithium and caffeic acid co-loaded liposomes in diabetes-induced Alzheimer's disease: association with GSK-3β and β-catenin.
articles.abstract:
AIM: To investigate the therapeutic effects of co-loaded lithium (Li) and caffeic acid (CA) liposomes in diabetes-induced Alzheimer's disease rats by improving cognitive dysfunction and attenuating neurodegeneration through the modulation of β-catenin/GSK-3β signaling.

METHODS: Li- and CA-co-loaded liposomes were prepared by the ethanol injection method and characterized. A diabetes-induced Alzheimer's disease model was established in male Wistar rats using a high-fat diet followed by low-dose streptozotocin (35 mg/kg) administered intraperitoneally. Li- and CA-co-loaded liposomes were given via the same route every day for 4 weeks. At the end of the experiment, the animals were sacrificed, and various biochemical and oxidative stress parameters, histopathological assessments, and ELISA analyses were performed.

RESULTS: Dual-drug-loaded Li and CA liposomal treatment significantly improved cognitive function, ameliorated metabolic dysfunction, and reduced oxidative stress by restoring antioxidant enzyme levels. Additionally, liposomes attenuated nitrite, acetylcholinesterase, and amyloid-β levels in diabetes-induced Alzheimer's rats. Histopathological assessment confirmed marked neuroprotective and pancreatic protective effects. Further, at a molecular level, Li and CA liposomal treatment reduced the expression of GSK-3β and increased the expression of β-catenin levels in rats.

CONCLUSION: This study provides the first evidence demonstrating the therapeutic potential of Li- and CA-co-loaded liposomes in attenuating diabetes‑associated cognitive dysfunction.

articles.title: Preconception incretin therapy reduces pregnancy and cardiometabolic outcomes in polycystic ovary syndrome.
articles.journal: The Journal of clinical endocrinology and metabolism
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS), now polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS), is associated with reproductive and cardiometabolic complications. Glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) and glucose-dependent insulinotropic peptide (GIP) receptor agonists (RAs) improve obesity-related outcomes, but their impact on pregnancy outcomes in PMOS remains unclear.

METHODS: We conducted a target trial emulation using the TriNetX global federated health research network. Women ≥18 years with PCOS/PMOS receiving pre-conception GLP-1/dual GLP-1/GIP RA therapy (liraglutide, semaglutide or tirzepatide) were compared with metformin. Propensity score matching (1:1) accounted for demographics, anthropometrics, comorbidities and medications. The primary outcome was a composite of adverse pregnancy outcomes (hypertensive, glycaemic, placental, delivery, labour, foetal growth, preterm and early pregnancy complications) over two years. Individual pregnancy endpoints, major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) and type 2 diabetes (T2D) were exploratory secondary outcomes. Cox regression generated hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs).

RESULTS: After matching, 48,126 patients were included per group. Pre-conception GLP-1/GIP RA use was associated with lower risk of the composite pregnancy outcome (HR 0.38; 95% CI 0.34-0.41). Exploratory analyses also demonstrated lower risks of individual pregnancy endpoints, MACE (HR 0.88; 95% CI 0.81-0.95) and T2D (HR 0.31; 95% CI 0.30-0.33). Associations varied across some sensitivity analyses.

CONCLUSION: Pre-conception GLP-1/GIP RA use in women with PCOS/PMOS was associated with lower risks of adverse pregnancy outcomes and cardiometabolic disease compared with metformin, consistent with potential benefits of pre-conception metabolic optimisation. This study cannot evaluate in-pregnancy safety or efficacy, and these findings do not support GLP-1/GIP RA use during gestation.

articles.title: Clinical and non-invasive assessment of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease and glycogenic hepatopathy in individuals with type 1 diabetes.
articles.journal: The Journal of clinical endocrinology and metabolism
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To deepen understanding of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) and presumptive glycogenic hepatopathy (GH) in adults with type 1 diabetes (T1D), and to evaluate non-invasive indices and novel biomarkers for their differentiation.

METHODS: We conducted a cross-sectional study including 202 adults with T1D. Hepatic steatosis was assessed using a stepwise imaging approach: all participants underwent ultrasound (US); liver magnetic resonance imaging-proton density fat fraction (MRI-PDFF) was performed when US was abnormal. Based on imaging, participants were categorized into three hepatic phenotypes: normal liver (NL), MASLD (steatosis on both US and MRI), and presumptive GH (hyperechogenicity on US but <5% fat on MRI). MRI-derived fat correlations and the performance of non-invasive indices and biomarkers were assessed.

RESULTS: Hepatic steatosis was identified by US in 39 participants, yielding a MASLD prevalence of 19.3%. Among the 32 participants with abnormal US who underwent MRI-PDFF, only 50% had liver fat ≥5%, indicating limited specificity of US and enabling identification of a presumptive GH phenotype (8.2%). MASLD was associated with a worse metabolic profile than presumptive GH or NL. The Fatty Liver Index (FLI) correlated strongly with MRI liver fat (ρ = 0.726, p < 0.0001) and showed promising exploratory performance (AUC = 0.842, 95% CI 0.687-0.998).

CONCLUSIONS: US may overestimate hepatic steatosis in adults with T1D, partly due to presumptive GH. Among participants undergoing MRI-PDFF, FLI showed promising exploratory performance for identifying steatosis, but requires further validation in cohorts undergoing systematic MRI-PDFF assessment.

articles.title: Tirzepatide-induced pneumatosis intestinalis: a rare but clinically significant gastrointestinal adverse effect.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Glucagon-like peptide 1 receptor agonists such as tirzepatide are increasingly prescribed to treat type 2 diabetes mellitus and obesity because they improve glycemic control and promote weight loss. Although gastrointestinal adverse effects such as nausea, vomiting, constipation, and delayed gastric emptying are well recognized, very rare cases of pneumatosis intestinalis have also been reported in association with this class of medications. We report the first documented histologic diagnosis of a possible tirzepatide-associated pneumatosis intestinalis.

METHODS: A 55-year-old man with obesity, type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension, and obstructive sleep apnea underwent colonoscopy for evaluation of abdominal pain, constipation, and anal fissures. He had been receiving tirzepatide therapy for approximately 1 year and experienced a 49-pound weight loss. Colonoscopy demonstrated mucosal edema of the cecum and ascending colon.

RESULTS: Biopsy specimens of the colon revealed mucosal and submucosal air-filled spaces associated with foreign body-type giant cell reactions and mixed inflammatory infiltrates, including eosinophils and neutrophils, consistent with pneumatosis intestinalis. The patient lacked other recognized risk factors for pneumatosis intestinalis, and his symptoms improved following discontinuation of tirzepatide.

CONCLUSIONS: As the use of tirzepatide and related glucagon-like peptide 1 receptor agonists continues to increase, awareness of this rare side effect and its characteristic histologic features should facilitate prompt recognition and accurate diagnosis. Reporting these rare events remains essential to refine the safety profile of these increasingly used medications and improve our understanding of their long-term gastrointestinal effects in broader patient populations.

articles.title: From Resection to Transplantation: Rethinking Training and Certification for the Modern HPB Surgeon.
articles.abstract: Hepatopancreatobiliary (HPB) surgery has evolved beyond the confines of traditional liver and pancreatic resection. Contemporary practice increasingly encompasses advanced vascular reconstruction, extended hepatectomy in compromised livers, transplantation for malignancy, and complex operations following multimodality therapy. These developments have fundamentally altered the technical and cognitive demands placed upon HPB surgeons, raising an important question: which training pathway best prepares surgeons for the future of the specialty? Dedicated HPB, surgical oncology, and integrated transplant-HPB fellowships each provide valuable but distinct expertise. Surgical oncology emphasizes tumor biology, multidisciplinary cancer care, and clinical investigation. Dedicated HPB fellowships focus on advanced liver and pancreatic resection. In contrast, integrated transplant-HPB training uniquely combines these competencies with mastery of hepatic physiology, complex vascular reconstruction, management of portal hypertension and liver failure, transplantation, and operative rescue under extreme physiologic conditions. We contend that integrated transplant-HPB training now represents the most comprehensive preparation for modern HPB surgery. This argument is not intended to promote territorial ownership of the specialty but rather to advocate for competency-based training that reflects the realities of current practice. As transplant oncology, living donor liver transplantation, machine perfusion, and increasingly aggressive surgical strategies continue to redefine operability, developments now supported by randomized and large-registry data rather than qualitative impression alone, certification pathways should evolve accordingly. Rather than existing outside mainstream HPB training, integrated transplant-HPB fellowships should be fully embraced within HPB certification frameworks, ensuring that future surgeons are equipped to offer the complete spectrum of operative strategies available to patients with complex HPB disease.

articles.title: Malnutrition defined by three global leadership initiative on malnutrition-based models and the risk of all-cause mortality in adults with common cancers: A retrospective cohort study.
articles.journal: JPEN. Journal of parenteral and enteral nutrition
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Our study compared the diagnostic agreement and prognostic value for overall survival of three nutritional screening tools integrated with the Global Leadership Initiative on Malnutrition framework in patients with cancer.

METHODS: The nutritional screening tools evaluated were the Malnutrition Universal Screening Tool, Malnutrition Screening Tool, and Nutritional Risk Screening 2002. Prognostic assessment was conducted using Kaplan-Meier survival analysis and Cox proportional hazards regression, with sensitivity analyses to ensure robustness. Logistic regression analysis was employed to assess the predictive value of each Global Leadership Initiative on Malnutrition-based model for malnutrition. Harrell's concordance index compared the discriminatory power of the models for overall survival outcomes, while kappa statistics evaluated diagnostic consistency for malnutrition across the models.

RESULTS: Each of the three models combining the Global Leadership Initiative on Malnutrition criteria with the Malnutrition Universal Screening Tool, the Malnutrition Screening Tool, or Nutritional Risk Screening 2002 was independently associated with an increased risk of all-cause mortality. The corresponding hazard ratios were 1.494, 1.517, and 1.530, respectively, with all P values less than 0.001. Across all three models, mortality risk increased progressively with the severity of malnutrition, while their discriminatory performance for overall survival was comparable. Among the three models, the model incorporating the Malnutrition Screening Tool demonstrated the strongest agreement with the Patient-Generated Subjective Global Assessment (kappa = 0.481, P < 0.001) and the greatest ability to identify malnutrition.

CONCLUSIONS: All three models provided meaningful prognostic information. The model incorporating the Malnutrition Screening Tool showed the closest diagnostic agreement and the strongest identification of clinically significant malnutrition.

articles.title: Jue Tone Music Therapy for Post-stroke Depression in China: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.journal: International journal of psychiatry in medicine
articles.abstract: ObjectiveTo evaluate the effects of Jue tone music therapy on depressive symptoms, sleep quality, activities of daily living, and selected serum biomarkers in patients with post-stroke depression (PSD).MethodsIn this randomized controlled trial, patients with PSD were randomly assigned to a control group or an intervention group. The control group received usual care, including sertraline hydrochloride and comprehensive rehabilitation training. The intervention group received additional Jue tone music therapy based on Five Element Music Therapy for 6 weeks. Depressive symptoms were assessed using the 24-item Hamilton Depression Scale (HAMD-24) and the depression subscale of the Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale (HADS-D). Sleep quality and activities of daily living were evaluated using the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI) and the Barthel Index (BI). Serum interleukin-6 (IL-6), brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF), and 5-hydroxytryptamine (5-HT) levels were measured before and after the intervention.ResultsA total of 91 patients completed the study (control group, n = 46; intervention group, n = 45). After 6 weeks, the intervention group showed significantly lower HAMD-24, HADS-D, and PSQI scores and higher BI scores compared with the control group (all P < 0.01). Serum IL-6 levels were significantly reduced, while BDNF and 5-HT levels were significantly increased in the intervention group (all P < 0.05). No significant differences in adverse events were observed between groups.ConclusionJue tone music therapy is a safe and effective adjunct to usual care, improving depressive symptoms, sleep quality, and functional outcomes in patients with PSD.

articles.title: Looking for Something Nobody Is Counting.
articles.journal: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America

articles.title: Conception methods and perinatal outcomes among women with kidney disorders: an Australian population-based cohort study.
articles.abstract:
STUDY QUESTION: Do conception methods and related pregnancy outcomes differ between women with and without kidney disease?

SUMMARY ANSWER: In this cohort, 3.3% of births among women with kidney disorders were conceived using ART, 1.9% were conceived following IUI and ovulation induction (OI), and 94.8% were conceived spontaneously; however, women with kidney disorders consistently experienced higher risks of adverse pregnancy outcomes than those without, regardless of conception method.

WHAT IS KNOWN ALREADY: Kidney disorders can impair fertility and pregnancy outcomes, but population‑level data on the use of medically assisted reproduction (MAR), including ART, IUI, and OI, in this group are limited.

STUDY DESIGN, SIZE, DURATION: This retrospective cohort study included all live births and stillbirths in New South Wales (NSW) and the Australian Capital Territory (ACT), Australia, between 2009 and 2017.

PARTICIPANTS/MATERIALS, SETTING, METHODS: We used linked state perinatal records to identify births. Kidney disorder diagnoses before delivery were identified using hospital dataset diagnostic coding. Conception mode was classified as (i) spontaneous conception, (ii) IUI/OI, or (iii) ART (including IVF or ICSI or other procedures [e.g. gamete intra-fallopian transfer, surrogacy]) using the Australia and New Zealand Assisted Reproduction Database and the national claims databases for medical services and pharmaceutical dispensing.

MAIN RESULTS AND THE ROLE OF CHANCE: During the study period, 911 229 babies were born from 898 084 pregnancies among 606 488 mothers in NSW/ACT. Among these, 10 858 babies (1.2%) were born to 7634 mothers with kidney disorders. Of the babies born to mothers with kidney disorders, 563 babies (5.2%), born to 470 mothers, were MAR-conceived. Women who conceived via MAR were older than those who conceived spontaneously in both groups (kidney disorders: MAR median age 33 (IQR: 30-37) years vs spontaneous median age 29 (24-33), standardized difference (sdiff) = 0.80; non-kidney disorders: MAR median age 34 (31-38) years vs spontaneous median age 31 (27-35), sdiff = 0.71). The most common kidney disorders were renal tubulo-interstitial diseases (MAR: 62.1% vs spontaneous: 72.7%) and urolithiasis (MAR: 36.8% vs spontaneous: 27.2%). The proportion of births conceived using ART was 3.3% among births to women with kidney disorders. The most common MAR treatments were fresh embryo transfers (33.6% kidney disorders vs 37.4% non-kidney disorders), frozen embryo transfers (28.7% vs 29.5%), any OI/IUI (36.0% vs 31.8%), and OI using clomiphene citrate alone (27.0% vs 23.5%). After adjusting for maternal age, parity, Index of Relative Socio-economic Disadvantage, multiple births and pre-existing diabetes, hypertension, and cardiovascular disease, women with kidney disorders had higher odds of caesarean section (MAR: OR 1.49, 95% CI 1.22-1.81; spontaneous: 1.36, 1.29-1.44), preterm birth (MAR: 2.09, 1.62-2.70; spontaneous: 1.76, 1.64-1.89), low birthweight (MAR: 1.69, 1.27-2.27; spontaneous 1.54, 1.41-1.67), and low Apgar scores (MAR 1.37, 1.06-1.79; spontaneous 1.17, 1.09-1.26) than women without kidney disorders, regardless of conception method.

LIMITATIONS, REASONS FOR CAUTION: As our study included only women who achieved a birth, it did not include those who underwent MAR but did not conceive or those who experienced miscarriage; therefore, MAR success rates could not be assessed. The association between kidney disorders and adverse pregnancy outcomes should not be interpreted as causal.

WIDER IMPLICATIONS OF THE FINDINGS: Although most births among women with kidney disorders were spontaneously conceived, MAR was utilized by a substantial proportion of women with and without kidney disorders, particularly among older women. Women with kidney disorders experienced higher risks of adverse pregnancy outcomes regardless of conception method, emphasizing the importance of early identification and specialized multidisciplinary care throughout the reproductive journey.

FUNDING: This study is funded by the Australian National Health and Medical Research Council (APP1127437).

DISCLOSURES: The National Perinatal Epidemiology and Statistics Unit (NPESU) at University of New South Wales (UNSW) received funding from the Fertility Society of Australia and New Zealand (FSANZ) to prepare annual and benchmarking reports using data from the Australian and New Zealand Assisted Reproductive Technology Database (ANZARD). G.M.C is the Director of the NPESU and an employee of UNSW. W.L. is a deputy editor for Human Reproduction. The remaining authors have no relevant disclosures for this study.

TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: N/A.

articles.title: Type 2 diabetes remission following a comprehensive metabolic program including surgery in adults with BMI ≥50 kg/m2 versus BMI <50 kg/m2.
articles.journal: Diabetic medicine : a journal of the British Diabetic Association
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Previous reports have suggested that higher baseline BMI (bBMI) or %excess weight loss (EWL) are independent predictors of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) remission after metabolic bariatric surgery (MBS). However, %EWL appears lower in individuals with bBMI ≥50 kg/m2 than those with lower bBMI. Thus, this cohort study aimed to examine T2DM remission after MBS in adults with bBMI <50 kg/m2 versus bBMI ≥50 kg/m2.

METHODS: This cohort study included adults with obesity and T2DM who underwent MBS between 01/06/2018 and 31/05/2024 at an Australian tertiary hospital. The primary outcome was complete diabetes remission (HbA1c < 6.0%) at 12 months following MBS.

RESULTS: At 12 months following MBS, when compared to those with bBMI <50 kg/m2, a higher proportion of patients with bBMI ≥50 kg/m2 experienced complete diabetes remission (37.8% vs. 66.7%, 95% CI for the difference -48.5% to -6.3%, p = 0.014); this was no longer significant after adjustment for variables such as baseline T2DM duration and HbA1c. The bBMI ≥50 kg/m2 group had greater total weight loss (kg) but lower %EWL, though neither was an independent predictor of remission.

CONCLUSIONS: In our cohort, neither bBMI ≥50 kg/m2 nor %EWL appeared as an independent predictor of T2DM remission. The higher proportion with remission (on unadjusted analyses) in those with bBMI ≥50 kg/m2 potentially reflects less advanced diabetes despite greater obesity. Early consideration of MBS may be beneficial given that markers of diabetes duration/severity appeared as potentially important variables associated with T2DM remission.

articles.title: Fibrosis burden and spatial pattern affect left atrial appendage stasis in multi-beat multi-physics simulations.
articles.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
articles.abstract: Purpose: Atrial fibrosis is associated with thromboembolic risk in atrial fibrillation, but it remains unclear how fibrosis-related contractile impairment alters blood transport in the left atrium (LA) and left atrial appendage (LAA). Prior multi-physics simulations coupling electromechanical (EM) and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) models showed that fibrosis impairs LA function and flow, but were limited to booster-only contraction and could not separate the effects of fibrosis burden from its spatial distribution.
