Active MM and related malignancy were diagnosed 1 year earlier in the intervention arms with fewer symptomatic presentations and hospitalizations at diagnosis. MGUS notification was not associated with adverse psychological outcomes. These findings demonstrate that population-based screening facilitates earlier detection of MM and expands access to early intervention without detectable psychological harm. Longer follow-up is required to determine the effects on survival and cost-effectiveness.

articles.title: Temozolomide Versus Radiotherapy as First-Line Therapy for Low-Grade Glioma: Mature Results of a Randomized Phase III Trial (EORTC 22033-26033/NCIC-CTG/TROG/MRC-CTU).
articles.journal: Journal of clinical oncology : official journal of the American Society of Clinical Oncology
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Prognosis in low-grade gliomas (LGGs) remains highly variable, and treatment-related late toxicity is a concern. This trial was comparing single-modality therapies in patients who often survive for years or decades and investigating differential responses according to molecular markers.

METHODS: Four hundred seventy-eight patients with clinical high-risk LGG (WHO grade 2) were randomly assigned to standard radiotherapy (RT; 28 × 1.8 Gy) or dose-dense temozolomide (TMZ; 75 mg/m2 once daily × 21/28 days, up to 12 cycles).

RESULTS: There was no significant difference in progression-free survival or overall survival (OS) between study arms. Analyzable tumor tissue in 73% (351/478) of patients allowed for post hoc reclassification according to the 2021 WHO pathologic criteria. In astrocytoma, IDHmt/1p/19q noncodeleted (n = 178), median OS was similar, 6.6-6.7 years irrespective of arm (0.67-1.44, P = .93). In oligodendroglioma, IDHmt/1p/19q codeleted (n = 109), median OS was 12.9 years (9.4-not reached) with RT and 14.9 years (10.1-number of events not reached) with TMZ (hazard ratio [HR], 0.88 [0.52-1.49], P = .63). In 64 tumors without isocitrate dehydrogenase (IDH) mutations, survival favored the TMZ arm: OS 2.5 (1.8-3.3) versus 4.7 (2.2-7.2) years (HR, 0.47 [0.27-0.82], P = .0068). Patients age 40 years and older fared better than patients younger than 40 years, challenging the current notion of age alone as a negative prognostic factor.

CONCLUSION: The assigned initial treatment modality did not affect progression-free survival or OS, regardless of the molecular subtype. Combined-modality therapy was not tested in this trial but has since become a standard of care for IDH-mutant astrocytoma. With emerging novel therapeutic options, rational treatment strategies tailored at the individual clinical and pathologic recurrence risk profiles will be needed. The validity of an age cutoff as prognostic factor is challenged when tumors are molecularly classified.

articles.title: Modulating sentence comprehension in people with aphasia through anodal tDCS: A double-blind randomized cross-over study.
articles.abstract: This double-blind randomized cross-over study investigated the effects of perilesional anodal transcranial direct current stimulation (AtDCS) combined with speech-language therapy on sentence comprehension in eight individuals with chronic nonfluent agrammatic aphasia. The behavioral therapy consisted of an intensive comprehension treatment including drilling in sentence-to-picture matching and Mapping Therapy. Each participant underwent both the anodal tDCS and sham stimulation conditions (five received sham first followed by real stimulation, and the remaining three the reverse sequence), with each condition paired with the same behavioral treatment and separated by a four-month washout period. Stimulation was applied over the perilesional area (left BA6) for 20 min during daily 40-min therapy sessions over four consecutive weeks. Sentence comprehension was assessed with the RiComprendo battery and functional communication with the Communicative Effectiveness Index (CETI). Data were analyzed using paired t-tests, Bayesian analyses, and linear mixed-effects models to control for baseline performance and individual variability. Both stimulation conditions produced significant pre-to-post improvements in sentence comprehension, particularly for syntactically complex structures such as passives and center-embedded object relatives. However, gains were overall greater following AtDCS, as reflected in larger effect sizes, stronger Bayes factors, and a significant treatment effect in the mixed-effects models. Only the AtDCS condition yielded significant improvements in self-perceived comprehension abilities on the CETI. These findings suggest that AtDCS over perilesional cortical areas may boost the effects of traditional language therapy on sentence comprehension, supporting its feasibility and potential as an adjuvant intervention in post-stroke aphasia rehabilitation.

articles.title: Deficient processing of regularity violations during visuospatial neglect: a visual mismatch negativity study.
articles.abstract: Visuospatial neglect (VSN) after right-hemisphere stroke causes reduced engagement with left-sided stimuli, but how VSN affects automatic processes, i.e. the registration of regularities and regularity violations is still equivocal. This study investigated these processes using event-related potential components C1, C2/N1, and the visual mismatch negativity (vMMN), and how they differ in VSN compared to stroke and healthy controls, and their changes with time and rehabilitation. We applied a passive oddball paradigm, where diamond patterns periodically disappeared (OFF events) and reappeared (ON events) on the lower left and right sides, creating two simultaneous but independent sequences with standard and deviant events. The study included a VSN group (N = 17, M = 53.88 ± 0.28 yrs); stroke patients (N = 16, M = 56.81 ± 13.26 yrs); and healthy participants (N = 17, M = 53.89 ± 10.79 yrs). The VSN group underwent measurements three times: pre- and post-rehabilitation, and at a 4-month follow-up. Our results show that the C1 component emerged reliably in healthy participants and as a tendency in stroke controls, but not in VSN at any measurement point. The C2/N1 component emerged for all events without group differences. VSN patients showed no reliable vMMN, while it emerged in stroke patients for left-sided OFF events. Healthy controls showed vMMN in every condition. Our results suggest that both stroke and VSN impair the automatic detection of regularity violations, but VSN does so in a more substantial way, and this deficit does not improve with time or rehabilitation. Furthermore, the missing C1 component in VSN may indicate an early-stage deficiency even in visual processing.

articles.title: Effects of gliflozins on bone health of patients with chronic kidney disease: a systematic review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sodium-glucose co-transporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) are a crucial therapy for chronic kidney disease (CKD), yet concerns persist regarding their impact on bone metabolism. This systematic review evaluates the skeletal safety and metabolic effects of SGLT2i in patients with CKD.

METHODS: A systematic review of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and observational cohort studies was conducted. Data on study design, population characteristics, baseline kidney function, bone-related comorbidities, and outcomes (osteoporosis, fractures, falls, amputations, and bone mineral markers) were summarized. Risk of bias was evaluated according to the included category.

RESULTS: The analysis revealed that while one RCT and a cohort study reported a significantly increased risk of bone fracture and amputation, this finding was not replicated in other subsequent cohort studies and other RCTs, which generally showed non-significant differences. Of note, the reporting of bone-related outcomes was inconsistent throughout the literature, and a substantial proportion of the evidence derives from studies primarily designed for patients with type 2 diabetes, largely involving early-stage CKD subgroups. One study suggests that SGLT2i may favorably modulate markers of CKD-mineral bone disease (MBD), reporting reduced risk of hyperphosphatemia, hypocalcemia, high parathyroid hormone, and low vitamin D levels. The reviewed literature primarily included data on empagliflozin, canagliflozin, dapagliflozin, and ertugliflozin.

CONCLUSIONS: Mostly, SGLT2i demonstrated a possible reassuring skeletal safety profile in CKD. Initial safety concerns regarding fractures have not been consistently supported, although evidence in moderate-to-advanced CKD remains limited. Long-term, prospectively defined skeletal outcomes are needed to confirm these findings and clarify class effects.

articles.title: Hidden glyoxylic acid in hair straightening products: a forensic lesson for the nephrologist.
Clonal hematopoiesis and circulating biomarkers in cardiovascular diseases.
articles.abstract: Clonal hematopoiesis, characterized by the age-related expansion of hematopoietic stem cell clones harboring somatic mutations, has emerged as an essential contributor to cardiovascular disease. Accumulating evidence indicates that clonal hematopoiesis driven by myeloproliferative neoplasm-associated driver mutations, particularly JAK2, is associated with an increased risk of vascular and cardiac complications, even at low variant allele frequencies. Experimental models and clinical studies demonstrate that mutant hematopoietic cells promote inflammation and pathological remodeling, thereby contributing to cardiovascular disorders such as pulmonary hypertension and aortic aneurysm. In addition, advances in circulating biomarker research have enabled less invasive assessment of cardiovascular diseases. Biomarkers, including cell-free DNA, reflect ongoing cardiac damage, while the extracellular matrix protein of collagen triple helix repeat-containing protein 1 (CTHRC1) provides insights into cardiac fibrosis. Clonal hematopoiesis and circulating biomarkers may enhance risk stratification and improve mechanistic understanding of cardiovascular pathology. This review summarizes current evidence of clonal hematopoiesis and circulating biomarkers in cardiovascular diseases.

articles.title: Inflammation meets calcium in iCMP.
Addition of Metastasis-Directed Therapy to Standard of Care for Oligometastatic Disease: Primary Aggregated Analysis of All Baskets from the Phase II Randomized EXTEND Trial.
articles.journal: Journal of clinical oncology : official journal of the American Society of Clinical Oncology
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: We tested the hypothesis that adding metastasis-directed therapy (MDT) to standard-of-care (SOC) systemic therapy improves progression-free survival (PFS) among patients with oligometastatic disease.

METHODS: EXTEND was a multicenter randomized phase II trial. Patients with 1-5 metastases were randomly assigned to MDT + SOC versus SOC in one of the six baskets (breast, pancreas, kidney, two prostate baskets, and an other basket) with basket-specific stratification and powering. PFS, the primary end point, was prespecified in the per-protocol set within each basket, across all baskets, and across all baskets excluding the prostate baskets. Exploratory end points included circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) and immune profiling.

RESULTS: From 2018 through 2023, 521 patients were screened, 350 were randomly assigned, and 334 were analyzed per protocol (MDT + SOC, n = 166; SOC, n = 168). Radiotherapy was used as MDT for 98% of metastases (370/379). Overall, after a median follow-up of 53 months, PFS was improved with MDT + SOC (hazard ratio [HR], 0.54 [95% CI, 0.41 to 0.72], P < .001). Similarly, PFS was improved when excluding the prostate baskets (HR, 0.60 [95% CI, 0.40 to 0.89]). Within each basket, PFS superiority was identified for the pancreas, prostate, and other baskets, whereas the breast and kidney baskets were inconclusive. At enrollment, detectable ctDNA correlated with shorter PFS and survival; by contrast, ctDNA clearance 3 months postenrollment correlated with improved survival. MDT + SOC-induced systemic immune activation was most pronounced among baskets demonstrating PFS superiority.

CONCLUSION: The phase II EXTEND trial supports the addition of MDT to SOC for oligometastatic disease. Histology-specific efficacy signals were identified for phase III testing. Translational insights suggest the potential for optimizing the definition of oligometastasis using ctDNA and point to systemic immune responses as a possible mechanism of benefit from MDT.

articles.title: The Lancet Commission on Sepsis: transforming sepsis care and outcomes.
A case of circumferential caval penetration caused by an inferior vena cava filter with asymptomatic duodenal perforation.
articles.abstract: We report a case of asymptomatic duodenal perforation caused by an inferior vena cava (IVC) filter. A 43-year-old man presented with multiple filter struts projecting through the IVC wall and penetrating the duodenum, identified on esophagogastroduodenoscopy. The patient had undergone retrievable IVC filter placement one year earlier for left iliac vein thrombosis and was being followed up with computed tomography. Open surgical removal of the IVC filter and primary repair of the duodenum were performed to prevent potential hemorrhagic and infectious complications. The postoperative course was uneventful, and the patient was discharged on postoperative day 10 after resuming anticoagulation therapy.

articles.title: Pathogenic Variants in NKX2-5 Associated With Familial Atrial Septal Defect and Conduction System Disease.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Most atrial septal defects (ASDs) occur sporadically, but familial cases can occur and carry a 10% risk of transmission to offspring.

CASE SUMMARY: We describe a 3-generation family with autosomal dominant secundum ASD and conduction system disease related to a novel NKX2-5 variant (c.300del; p.Asp101Thrfs∗75). The index patient, a 58-year-old woman with prior ASD repair and mitral valve replacement, presented with chronotropic incompetence, atrial fibrillation, left bundle branch block, and prolonged pauses, leading to pacemaker implantation. Her mother had an ASD, atrial fibrillation, left bundle branch block, and pulmonary arterial hypertension. The proband's daughter also had an ASD. Genetic testing revealed a novel NKX2-5 pathogenic variant in all 3 patients.

REVIEW SUMMARY: The combination of an ASD and conduction system disease represents the most common phenotype in patients with pathogenic NKX2-5 variants.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: A thorough family history and genetic testing are needed when evaluating patients with ASD and concurrent conduction system abnormalities.

articles.title: Clinical practice guidance for imaging selection in pulsatile tinnitus: an evidence-based expert consensus.
articles.abstract: Pulsatile tinnitus (PT) is a rhythmic sound synchronized with the patient's heartbeat that represents a complex diagnostic challenge with a broad spectrum of vascular and non-vascular etiologies. Persistent symptoms can severely impact mental health, yet a specific causative abnormality can be identified via targeted radiological imaging in more than 75% of cases. Improper imaging selection frequently leads to misdiagnosis, reduced therapeutic efficacy, and increased healthcare costs. The choice of imaging protocol must be guided by a thorough initial clinical evaluation, including detailed medical history, physical maneuvers, and otoscopic examinations. Commissioned by the Medical Imaging Center Branch of the Chinese Hospital Association, this evidence-based expert consensus guidance aims to provide structured recommendations for the strategic selection of imaging modalities in PT patients. The guidance explicitly distinguishes recommendations grounded in comparative diagnostic literature from those derived from formal expert consensus where high-level comparative evidence is limited.

articles.title: Sonographic findings in fontan-associated liver disease across pediatric and adult patients: A cross-sectional imaging study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study aimed to characterize sonographic hepatic findings across pediatric, adolescent, and adult Fontan patients and to examine their cross-sectional relationships with time since Fontan completion and chronological age. As a secondary objective, we explored a composite score integrating complementary sonographic findings.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this retrospective cross-sectional analysis of a prospectively established single-center Fontan cohort, hepatic ultrasound findings from 153 patients were evaluated, including gray-scale imaging, Doppler assessment, and shear-wave elastography performed according to institutional acquisition protocols. Individual sonographic findings were analyzed as the primary imaging outcomes. Cross-sectional associations with time since Fontan completion were assessed using sex-adjusted regression models; additional models simultaneously included chronological age, time since Fontan completion, and sex to examine their closely related contributions. A secondary exploratory 5-point composite score integrating five complementary sonographic domains was evaluated descriptively.

RESULTS: Longer time since Fontan completion was associated cross-sectionally with greater IVC diameter, liver size, shear-wave velocity, structural abnormality, and hepatic nodularity in sex-adjusted analyses. Chronological age and time since Fontan completion were nearly collinear (r = 0.970). When both variables and sex were included simultaneously, associations with IVC diameter, liver size, shear-wave velocity, and structural classification were attenuated and no longer statistically significant, whereas hepatic nodularity remained associated with time since Fontan completion (OR = 1.22/year; 95% CI 1.03-1.45; p = 0.024). Complete composite-score data were available in 101 patients; mean scores were 0.81 ± 0.88, 2.15 ± 1.26, 3.18 ± 0.80, and 4.27 ± 0.80 across < 5-, 5-<10-, 10-<20-, and ≥ 20-year post-Fontan categories, respectively. In 15 patients with serial examinations, scores were higher at the later examination in 10 and unchanged in five (p = 0.004). In a stratified subset of 40 independently reread examinations, interobserver agreement was high for liver size (ICC = 0.922) and IVC diameter (ICC = 0.947), whereas agreement for qualitative sonographic findings was lower (κ = 0.202-0.369).

CONCLUSION: Sonographic vascular, morphologic, structural, elastographic, and nodular abnormalities differed across patients examined at increasing intervals after Fontan completion. However, because chronological age and Fontan duration were nearly collinear, this cross-sectional study cannot determine whether these imaging gradients reflect duration of Fontan physiology, chronological maturation, or both. Hepatic nodularity showed the most robust association with time since Fontan completion in simultaneous models. The composite score provides a secondary exploratory framework for integrating complementary sonographic findings but requires prospective longitudinal and external validation. The limited interobserver agreement for qualitative findings further emphasizes the need for standardized image interpretation and supports the exploratory status of the composite score.

articles.title: Dynamic edge-event-based consensus of nonlinear multi-agent systems with sampled-data measurement.
articles.abstract: This paper investigates the leader-following consensus problem for a class of nonlinear multi-agent systems (MASs) by developing a novel edge-event-triggered control framework. To alleviate communication burdens, an edge-based triggering strategy is employed, wherein both the control protocols and triggering conditions depend exclusively on local relative information, eliminating the reliance on global network knowledge. Recognizing the constraints of practical communication scenarios, asynchronous information interactions across different edges are explicitly considered. As a core contribution, we seamlessly integrate sampled-data measurements with the edge-triggering paradigm, proposing a sampled-data edge-event triggered mechanism. This framework fundamentally circumvents the stringent requirement of continuous state monitoring and intrinsically excludes Zeno behavior, thereby significantly saving computational and communication resources. Furthermore, the framework is extended to a dynamic sampled-data-based edge-event-triggered mechanism, which introduces an auxiliary variable to provide greater flexibility in communication scheduling. Finally, the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed methods are demonstrated through an application example and comparative simulations.

articles.title: Association of beta-blocker therapy with outcomes after ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction stratified by GRACE risk score: A nationwide registry analysis.
authors: Korea Acute Myocardial Infarction Registry (KAMIR) Investigators
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Associations between beta-blocker use following ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) and clinical outcomes remain uncertain in the contemporary era of near-universal early revascularization and drug-eluting stent (DES) implantation, particularly for patients with preserved left ventricular function. We sought to determine whether associations between beta-blocker use at discharge and outcomes varied across Global Registry of Acute Coronary Events (GRACE) risk strata.

METHODS: We performed a post-hoc analysis of 11,866 STEMI survivors from two prospective nationwide Korean registries who underwent successful percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) with second-generation DES. Patients were categorized by beta-blocker prescription at discharge. The primary endpoint was all-cause mortality at one year; secondary outcomes included major adverse cardiac events (MACE). Propensity-score matching and inverse-probability treatment weighting were employed to mitigate confounding. Variation in associations was examined across the continuous GRACE risk spectrum, categorized into low-risk (GRACE <85), intermediate-risk (GRACE 85-179), and high-risk (GRACE ≥180) strata.

RESULTS: Beta-blockers were prescribed to 83.8% of the cohort. After propensity matching, beta-blocker use was associated with lower one-year all-cause mortality (2.7% vs. 4.2%; hazard ratio [HR] 0.63; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.44-0.91) and MACE (6.0% vs. 8.3%; HR 0.71; 95% CI 0.55-0.92). These associations attenuated by three years. The GRACE 2.0 score exhibited robust discrimination for mortality (AUC = 0.79; 95% CI: 0.76-0.82). Continuous interaction analyses showed small model-estimated absolute risk differences in low-risk patients (GRACE <85), whereas the largest model-estimated absolute risk difference was observed in intermediate-risk individuals (GRACE 85-179).

CONCLUSIONS: Among STEMI survivors treated with contemporary PCI, associations between beta-blocker use at discharge and outcomes varied according to baseline GRACE risk. No statistically significant association was observed in low-risk individuals (GRACE <85), whereas the association with lower mortality was most evident in the intermediate-risk group (GRACE 85-179). These hypothesis-generating findings warrant evaluation in randomized trials before being used to guide treatment decisions.

articles.title: Impact of atrial fibrillation catheter ablation o'n tricuspid regurgitation severity: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Atrial fibrillation (AF) and tricuspid regurgitation (TR) commonly coexist and are associated with adverse clinical outcomes. Whether restoration of sinus rhythm through catheter ablation improves TR severity has not been systematically quantified. We evaluated the association between AF catheter ablation and changes in moderate or greater TR.

METHODS: We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis of studies evaluating patients with AF undergoing catheter ablation and reporting paired preablation and postablation assessments of TR severity. MEDLINE, Embase, CENTRAL and Web of Science were searched from inception to 22 April 2026. The primary outcome was change in the prevalence of moderate or greater TR following ablation. Random-effects meta-analysis was performed using restricted maximum likelihood estimation. Meta-regression evaluated prespecified study-level modifiers, including sex proportion, mean age and baseline AF type.

RESULTS: 17 studies comprising 2747 patients were included. AF catheter ablation was associated with a lower prevalence of moderate or greater TR (risk difference −0.21, 95% CI −0.33 to −0.09; pooled risk ratio 0.49, 95% CI 0.40 to 0.60), although heterogeneity was substantial (I²=98.3%) and the 95% prediction interval was wide (−0.74 to 0.31). Patients who maintained sinus rhythm had greater TR reduction than those with recurrent AF (risk difference −0.28, 95% CI −0.55 to −0.01). In meta-regression, higher proportions of female participants and persistent AF were associated with greater TR improvement, whereas mean left ventricular ejection fraction was not. Findings were consistent in sensitivity analyses restricted to studies at low-to-moderate risk of bias, observational studies and leave-one-out analyses.

CONCLUSIONS: AF catheter ablation was associated with a significant reduction in moderate or greater TR, with greater improvement among patients maintaining sinus rhythm. These findings support prospective evaluation of rhythm control as a potential strategy for patients with moderate or greater TR and AF.

PROSPERO REGISTRATION NUMBER: CRD420251154277.

articles.title: Identifying the High-Risk Arrhythmic Mitral Valve Prolapse Phenotype by Imaging.
articles.abstract: Within arrhythmogenic mitral valve prolapse (AMVP), a distinct subset of mitral valve prolapse (MVP), there is a small group that carries a higher risk of malignant ventricular arrhythmias and sudden cardiac death called malignant MVP. The malignant MVP phenotype is over-represented in young women with unexplained sudden cardiac death on autopsy. AMVP is defined by myxomatous, often bileaflet MVP with mitral annular disjunction, abnormal valvular-myocardial mechanics, complex ventricular ectopy, and nonsustained ventricular tachycardia. Excessive mechanical force from systolic annular expansion, papillary muscle traction, and basal inferolateral "curling" promotes focal replacement and diffuse interstitial fibrosis, creating an arrhythmogenic substrate. Premature ventricular contractions act as triggers, whereas autonomic modulation influences the timing of ventricular arrhythmia initiation and progression to ventricular fibrillation or sustained monomorphic ventricular tachycardia. Baseline evaluation with an electrocardiogram and transthoracic echocardiography is necessary to identify AMVP, exclude severe mitral regurgitation, and identify high-risk markers. If no premature ventricular contractions are found on a resting electrocardiogram, exercise stress testing and extended rhythm monitoring can help bring out ventricular premature contractions, which are triggers of ventricular arrhythmias. Cardiac magnetic resonance provides incremental prognostic value with late gadolinium enhancement reflecting replacement fibrosis and T1 mapping identifying diffuse fibrosis, even in those with no late gadolinium enhancement. Machine-learning analysis may further refine risk stratification by integrating high-risk features such as mitral annular disjunction, fibrosis extent, and location that outperform symptom-based assessment. As transcatheter and surgical mitral interventions expand, accurate phenotyping of AMVP is increasingly important, as hemodynamic correction of mitral regurgitation alone does not eliminate the underlying arrhythmogenic substrate. Comprehensive multimodality imaging and integrated rhythm assessment are therefore central to individualized risk stratification and management in this vulnerable population.

articles.title: Comparison of the Efficacy of Appiani and Zuma Maneuvers in Patients with Apogeotropic Horizontal Canal Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo.
articles.journal: The journal of international advanced otology
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Apogeotropic horizontal canal benign paroxysmal positional vertigo (HC-BPPV) is a challenging variant of BPPV with lower treatment success rates compared to the geotropic form. The Appiani maneuver (ApM) and the Zuma maneuver (ZmM) represent 2 repositioning strategies targeting this condition, but head-to-head comparative data remain limited.

METHODS: A prospective randomized comparative study was conducted between December 2024 and November 2025. Patients with unilateral apogeotropic HC-BPPV confirmed by videonystagmography (VNG)-assisted supine roll testing were assigned to either the ApM (n = 38) or the ZmM (n = 39). The primary outcome was resolution of positional nystagmus; the secondary outcome was the number of maneuver sessions required (maximum 4). Patients who developed canal conversion to another semicircular canal during follow-up were excluded from efficacy analysis.

RESULTS: Among 77 patients (63.6% female; 59.7% aged ≥ 60 years), the overall single-session resolution rate was 63.6%. Resolution after 1 session was achieved in 68.4% (ApM) and 59.0% (ZmM) of patients, with no significant between-group difference (P = .389). Older age (≥60 years) was the only factor significantly associated with requiring ≥2 sessions (82.1% vs. 46.9%; P = .002).

CONCLUSION: Both the ApM and ZmM are effective and comparable treatments for apogeotropic HC-BPPV. Advanced age (≥60 years) was identified as an exploratory factor associated with requiring multiple treatment sessions.

articles.title: Etrasimod reduces circulating and mucosal inflammatory lymphocyte populations and alters innate immune and non-immune cell signatures in intestinal mucosa: ELEVATE UC phase 3 clinical data.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Innate and adaptive immune cell dysregulation contributes to ulcerative colitis pathogenesis. The sphingosine 1-phosphate receptor modulator etrasimod showed efficacy in ulcerative colitis treatment in Phase 3 ELEVATE UC studies. Changes in circulating immune cells and mucosal cell types were characterized in etrasimod-treated patients with ulcerative colitis.

METHODS: Blood (etrasimod n = 525, placebo n = 257 patients) and mucosal biopsies (etrasimod n = 411, placebo n = 200 patients) from patients in the ELEVATE UC trials were used to assess cellular and molecular changes for etrasimod versus placebo in clinical remitters and non-remitters using immunophenotyping, transcriptomic and proteomic techniques.

RESULTS: Selective and partial reduction in circulating T- and B-cell subsets was observed for etrasimod versus placebo (Week 12), with greater effects on CD4+ T cells, including Treg and Th17 cells, than CD8+ T cells, and on naive T cells and T central memory cells than T effector memory cells, without difference between remitters and non-remitters. No significant effects on monocytes nor NK cell numbers were observed. Mucosal biopsies showed corresponding reductions in T- and B-cell subsets, myeloid cells and neutrophils accompanied by downregulation of interleukin-17 and interleukin-8 signaling in both tissue and blood, most prominently in remitters, where non-immune cell changes were consistent with tissue repair.

CONCLUSIONS: Etrasimod treatment of patients with ulcerative colitis drives T- and B-lymphocyte subset reductions in blood and intestinal mucosa, neutrophil reductions in tissue and mucosal downregulation of inflammatory pathways associated with ulcerative colitis pathogenesis.

CLINICAL TRIALS REGISTRATION NUMBER: ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT03945188; NCT03996369).

articles.title: Effect of pre-visit computer-assisted history-taking with a structured copy-ready summary on documentation completeness in screening for inflammatory rheumatic diseases: a randomized pilot study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Clinical encounters in outpatient care are constrained by high demand, limited consultation time, and documentation requirements. Computer-assisted history-taking (CAHT) may improve the structured collection of patient information before consultations and disease screening, but evidence is limited. This randomized pilot study evaluated whether pre-visit CAHT combined with a copy-ready summary increased documentation completeness and assessed patient and physician acceptance.

METHODS: MAESTRI was a multicenter, parallel-group, randomized pilot study conducted across rheumatology, dermatology, and orthopedics outpatient services. Adults at increased risk of an underlying inflammatory rheumatic disease (IRD) were randomized to pre-visit CAHT or usual care. Specialty-specific questionnaires generated structured narrative summaries covering predefined screening-relevant items. The primary outcome was documentation completeness, assessed by a blinded reviewer as the percentage of these predefined items present in the final clinical documentation. Secondary and exploratory outcomes included patient and physician acceptance, usability ratings, and free-text feedback.

RESULTS: Of 45 screened patients, 43 were randomized and analyzed. The mean age was 54.2 years (SD 14.3), and 29 participants (67.4%) were female. All intervention-group clinical notes contained the generated summary. Overall median documentation completeness was 100.0% (IQR 100.0-100.0) in the intervention group compared with 46.9% (IQR 10.0-68.8) in the control group (p < 0.001), with consistent differences across rheumatology, dermatology, and orthopedics. CAHT acceptance was high among both patients and physicians, with 41 of 43 patients (95.3%) willing to complete and the six responding physicians (100%) willing to offer digital pre-visit questionnaires before future appointments. Qualitative feedback was predominantly positive, with patients reporting that pre-visit questionnaires could improve consultation preparation, support recall of symptoms, and help physicians focus the visit on relevant issues. Some participants emphasized that digital questionnaires should complement, rather than replace, direct physician interaction.

CONCLUSIONS: Pre-visit CAHT combined with a structured, copy-ready summary substantially increased the completeness with which predefined screening-relevant information was transferred into clinical documentation while also suggesting high acceptance among both patients and physicians. These findings support further evaluation in a larger trial assessing workflow impact and clinical impact.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: The study was registered at German Clinical Trials Register (DRKS; ID: DRKS00036519). Date of Registration: 2025-03-31.

articles.title: cGMP production of radiometal solutions from solid targets at a university-scale facility.
articles.abstract: Radiometals have emerged as a critical tool for positron emission tomography. These radionuclides provide the opportunity for theranostic pairs, using the same compound with different radionuclides complexed at the same position. Additionally, radiometals span a range of half-lives, from minutes to days, providing excellent flexibility in matching radioactive half-lives with the biological half-lives of targeting vectors. However, cyclotron production of these radiometals is not yet standardized. Some radiometals have common purification and production methods, but there is still a need for widespread, easily adoptable current Good Manufacturing Practices (cGMP) methods. Such methods would minimize the use of custom, in-house methods and rely on widely available instrumentation. In this work, [89Zr]ZrCl4 was produced under cGMP methods to provide a framework for simple, rapid production and purification with commonly available instrumentation. [89Zr]ZrCl4 was produced at 40.02 MBq/μA-h and underwent standard quality control analyses to determine appearance, pH (1-2), radioactive concentration (185-1850 MBq/mL), specific activity (>370 MBq/μg), radionuclidic and radiochemical purity (both >99%), chemical purity (from oxalate, <1% and metallic impurities, <75 μg/mL total), endotoxins (<17 EU/mL), and sterility (no growth). All specifications for release of a cGMP batch of [89Zr]ZrCl4 across the validation runs were passed. This work highlights the need for standardized methods for production, purification, and quality control for radiometal solutions and provides an example of such methods for [89Zr]ZrCl4.

articles.title: Stakeholder Perspectives on Digital Health Technologies in Poststroke Self-Management and Rehabilitation: Systematic Review Based on the NASSS Framework.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Digital health technologies (DHTs) offer opportunities to support poststroke self-management and rehabilitation, but their implementation may be hindered by mismatches between technological design, stakeholder needs, and care contexts. Synthesizing stakeholder perspectives can clarify implementation priorities and gaps in the evidence.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to synthesize stakeholders' perceptions, experiences, and recommendations regarding DHT implementation in poststroke self-management and rehabilitation and to map the findings to the NASSS (Nonadoption, Abandonment, Scale-Up, Spread, and Sustainability) framework.

METHODS: Six databases (PubMed, MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, CINAHL, and Web of Science) were searched from inception through October 2025. Eligible studies were English-language, peer-reviewed primary studies using qualitative, quantitative, or mixed methods designs to report stakeholder perspectives on DHTs in poststroke care. Two reviewers independently screened studies, extracted data, and assessed methodological quality using the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool (MMAT). A convergent integrated synthesis was conducted: quantitative findings were transformed into textual descriptors, combined with qualitative findings, coded inductively, and subsequently mapped deductively to NASSS domains and subdomains. Disagreements were resolved through consensus or by third-reviewer adjudication.

RESULTS: Of 15,262 records identified, 42 studies published between 2019 and 2025 were included: 24 qualitative, 8 quantitative, and 10 mixed methods studies. Patients, health care professionals, caregivers, and members of the public were represented in 32, 19, 8, and 3 studies, respectively, with some studies including multiple groups. Evidence concentrated on the condition, technology, value proposition, and adopter-system domains. Stakeholders valued personalized functions, intuitive interfaces, timely feedback, and digital support that complemented human care. Barriers included stroke-related motor, cognitive, communication, and sensory impairments; unequal digital access and literacy; caregiver demands; staff workload and training needs; and poor integration with clinical routines. Data privacy and unclear payment arrangements also raised concerns. Evidence on organizational readiness and wider-system determinants was limited, and no eligible study directly examined interaction and adaptation over time. Methodological concerns included nonresponse bias and insufficient interpretation of integrated findings in mixed methods studies.

CONCLUSIONS: Stakeholder perspectives indicate that DHT implementation in poststroke care should combine accessible, personalized design with support for patients, caregivers, and health care professionals, alongside integration into clinical workflows and clear data governance and financing arrangements. The NASSS mapping identified priorities beyond usability, but current evidence does not establish sustained adoption, scale-up, or spread. Longitudinal studies in routine care are needed to evaluate adaptation and sustainability.

articles.title: Managing the Hospital Capacity Challenges of Medetomidine Withdrawal: A Retrospective Report of Dexmedetomidine Use in Intermediate Care Units.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Medetomidine, a veterinary alpha-2-adrenergic agonist, has emerged as a dominant adulterant in the Philadelphia illicit opioid supply, producing a severe withdrawal syndrome requiring significant inpatient support. We developed an intravenous dexmedetomidine protocol for intermediate care units (IMCU) and describe the safety and feasibility of delivering this care outside the intensive care unit (ICU).

METHODS: A retrospective descriptive analysis of patients who received dexmedetomidine under an IMCU orderset for alpha-2 withdrawal was conducted at two urban medical centers in Philadelphia, PA, from April 2024 to February 2026. Encounters were classified as protocol-concordant or protocol-discordant by dosing and level of support; the concordant cohort was primary. Variables included demographics and addiction consult status. Outcomes included length of stay (hospital and IMCU), ICU admission, rapid response team activation, intubation, and discharge disposition.

RESULTS: Of 487 encounters, 449 (92.2%) were protocol-concordant and 38 (7.8%) protocol-discordant. All subsequent results describe the protocol-concordant cohort (n=449) unless otherwise noted. The cohort was predominantly male (58.1%) with a mean age of 41.8 years. Median hospital stay was 6.0 days and median IMCU stay was 2.2 days. ICU admission was not required in 50.1% of encounters. Rapid response team activation occurred in 38 encounters (8.5%), the majority for escalating withdrawal management. Patient-directed discharge occurred in 41.4% of encounters.

CONCLUSIONS: An IMCU dexmedetomidine protocol deployed across seven monitored units at 2 hospitals offers a replicable framework for managing medetomidine withdrawal while potentially mitigating critical care capacity challenges. Identified opportunities include modification of titration and dosing strategies and further investment in addiction consult infrastructure.

articles.title: Severe strongyloidiasis and Gram-negative bacterial superinfections: epidemiology, clinical implications, and therapeutic strategies.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Strongyloidiasis is a neglected tropical disease affecting over 600 million people worldwide. Its severe forms carry a fatality rate exceeding 60%, yet death is rarely attributable to the parasite alone: the terminal event is often bacterial sepsis or meningitis of enteric origin. We review recent evidence on Gram-negative and other bacterial superinfections in severe strongyloidiasis, and their diagnostic and therapeutic implications.

RECENT FINDINGS: Cohort studies show that bacteraemia is the commonest complication of severe disease, affecting 38.3% of cases against 4.1% of uncomplicated infections, and is predominantly Gram-negative, with Klebsiella pneumoniae and Escherichia coli most often isolated; Gram-positive and polymicrobial infections also occur. Beyond corticosteroids, targeted immunosuppressants and transplantation are increasingly implicated. Recognition is difficult, as eosinophilia is frequently absent and serological tests, including recent rapid assays, perform poorly in immunocompromised patients. Diagnostic delay is associated with higher risk of sepsis and mortality. Emodepside and moxidectin show promise in chronic infection but remain untested in severe disease.

SUMMARY: Enteric Gram-negative bacteraemia or meningitis in an at-risk patient, particularly if recurrent or polymicrobial, should prompt parasitological investigation. As treatment of established disease is unproven, detecting and treating chronic infection before immunosuppression, including transplant donors and recipients, remains the intervention most likely to reduce mortality.

articles.title: Extensive metallosis following reverse shoulder arthroplasty managed with custom glenoid reconstruction: A case report.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Metallosis is a rare but serious complication following reverse shoulder arthroplasty (RSA) that can lead to progressive bone loss and implant failure. Although revision strategies have been described planned two-stage revision with custom implants has not previously been reported.

CASE PRESENTATION: A 55-year-old female presented with pain and dysfunction following RSA. Examination demonstrated severe motion limitation, while imaging revealed loosening and progressive bone loss. Intraoperatively, we identified extensive metallosis with micromotion at the modular humeral junction, and a large glenoid defect. The initial glenoid baseplate was also positioned relatively high, resulting in impingement and subsequent scapular notching, which may have contributed to the metallosis. Owing to extensive metallosis, severe osteolysis, poor bone stock, and uncertain infection status, a staged revision was performed. An antibiotic spacer was placed and glenoid was bone grafted. Eventually definitive reconstruction was performed using a custom glenoid baseplate and humeral component because standard revision implants could not achieve stable fixation. At 1 year, the patient had improved shoulder function with forward elevation of 130° and was able to perform activities of daily living.

CONCLUSION: Catastrophic metallosis secondary to modular junction failure may require staged revision and patient-specific reconstruction when extensive bone loss precludes standard revision implants.

articles.title: Neuromonitoring of perioperative microembolization and its association with postoperative stroke after carotid endarterectomy.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: This study aims to assess whether perioperative microembolization can identify patients at risk for postoperative stroke.

METHODS: A total of 257 carotid endarterectomy procedures in 254 patients were analyzed (154 symptomatic, 103 asymptomatic). Neuromonitoring, combining transcranial Doppler ultrasonography and continuous electroencephalography, was utilized to evaluate cerebral perfusion and detect microembolic signals (MES). Monitoring covered the entire intraoperative phase and a standardized 20-minute postoperative observation window.

RESULTS: Postoperative stroke occurred in seven patients, six of whom were symptomatic prior to the procedure. In exploratory penalized regression analyses, higher postoperative MES counts (OR 1.02 per MES, 95% CI 1.01-1.04; p < 0.001) and an intraoperative burden of ≥ 10 MES (OR 6.06, 95% CI 1.40-34.78; p = 0.016) were associated with postoperative stroke. Symptomatic patients exhibited a significantly higher embolic burden (6.7 ± 13.3 vs. 2.2 ± 5.0, p = 0.004).

CONCLUSION: Beyond its role in guiding selective shunting, transcranial Doppler monitors the occurrence of microembolization, which could serve as a potential indicator of perioperative stroke. In this exploratory analysis, both an intraoperative burden of 10 or more MES and sustained postoperative microembolization were associated with postoperative stroke. Given the low number of events, these findings are hypothesis-generating and require prospective validation before they can guide perioperative management.

articles.title: Morpho-molecular assessment of nanomaterials in teleost fish wound healing: a systematic review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Teleost fish skin is a vital barrier for regulating osmoregulation, immune defense, and respiration. Cutaneous wounds in farmed fish cause significant economic loss and welfare concerns, as standard treatments, like antibiotics and chemical baths, are often ineffective, toxic, and fail to adhere to mucus-covered surfaces. While nanomaterials show great promise for wound healing, current data on how they work in fish remain incomplete. This systematic review evaluates the performance of these nanomaterials, explains their healing mechanisms, and highlights the key research gaps to guide future aquaculture treatments.

RESULTS: Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, we included twelve in vivo studies (2017-2026). A clear shift was observed over time: research before 2020 focused only on metallic nanoparticles (silver and zinc oxide), whereas recent studies have mostly used biopolymeric nano-delivery systems. Nanoparticle treatments consistently led to faster wound closure, with several formulas healing over 90% of the wound within two weeks; however, these quantitative outcomes are strictly descriptive due to high methodological heterogeneity across studies. Under the microscope, nanomaterials accelerated re-epithelialization, improved collagen organization, and reduced inflammation. At the molecular level, they decreased pro-inflammatory cytokines (IL1β, TNFα) and matrix metalloproteinases (MMPS), while increasing anti-inflammatory markers (IL10, TGF-β) and antioxidant enzymes (SOD, CAT). Transcriptomics data also showed the activation of fibroblast growth factor 7 (FGF7) and the Jak-STAT pathways. Finally, zebrafish (Danio rerio) constituted 75% of the study models, showing a major gap in research on farmed fish like Nile tilapia (Oreochromis niloticus).

CONCLUSIONS: This systematic review shows that nanomaterials significantly accelerate teleost wound healing by promoting tissue regeneration and regulating the immune response. The shift toward biopolymeric systems, especially chitosan, indicates a clear trend toward safe and sustainable aquaculture medicine. Notably, testing hybrid nano-hyaluronic acid and nano-chitosan systems remains completely unexplored in farmed fish. This gap is important due to the complementary biological properties of these materials and the high global value of Nile tilapia. Testing this hybrid biomaterial under real farming conditions will help improve skin healing, support the immune system, and provide a safe wound treatment for global aquaculture.

articles.title: Early integration of palliative care in outpatient nephrology: exploring healthcare professionals' knowledge, attitudes, and communication practices - an exploratory multi-methods study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with advanced kidney disease often experience high symptom burden and complex illness trajectories, highlighting the importance of integrating palliative care into nephrology. However, palliative care remains insufficiently integrated into routine care within nephrology outpatient centers. This study explored healthcare professionals' (HCPs) perspectives on palliative care integration, including knowledge and confidence in identifying patients with palliative care needs as well as perceived barriers and facilitators to implementation.

METHODS: An explorative multi-methods study was conducted as part of a project aiming to implement a minimally invasive intervention in nephrology outpatient centers in Germany (MINI-Neph). HCPs from participating centers received a one-hour training introducing palliative care in nephrology, communication strategies for emotionally challenging situations, and using two validated tools for identifying patients with palliative care needs: the Surprise Question (SQ) and the Supportive and Palliative Care Indicators Tool (SPICT-DE). Data were collected through an online survey, free-text responses and semi-structured interviews with HCPs and analyzed using descriptive statistics and qualitative content analysis, respectively.

RESULTS: Five nephrology outpatient centers located in different regions across Germany were involved in the MINI-Neph-Study. A total of 52 HCPs participated; most were female (82.7%), with the largest age groups being 31-40 years (30.8%) and 51-60 years (28.8%). Roles included nurses (57.7%), medical assistants (25.0%), and nephrologists (15.4%). While most participants recognized the relevance of integrating palliative care into nephrology, only about half reported confidence in identifying patients with palliative care needs in their presumed last year of life. Communication about patients' preferences regarding care, treatment decisions, and advance directives occurred inconsistently, while discussions about preferred place of care or death were reported less frequently. Knowledge of legal aspects of end-of-life care and confidence in organizing referrals to palliative care services were limited. Additionally, 13 qualitative interviews were conducted with HCPs from three nephrology outpatient centers (2 nephrologists, 2 medical assistants, and 8 nurses). The interviews highlighted the complex and dynamic trajectories of patients with advanced kidney disease. Conversations about serious illness and care goals were mostly reactive, while interprofessional communication and collaboration with external providers remained limited. Training increased awareness of palliative care needs, but structural barriers such as time pressure and a treatment-focused culture hindered consistent implementation.

CONCLUSIONS: Early integration of palliative care in outpatient nephrology is valued by HCPs, while confidence in identifying palliative care needs and communicating about end-of-life issues was inconsistent, and palliative care remains predominantly reactive in routine care. The MINI approach may support more systematic and proactive care. More proactive care may require protected time, structured communication, clear responsibilities, and established communication pathways.

articles.title: Association of obstructive sleep apnea with pancreatic cancer in high-risk patients under surveillance in CAPS and PCYST cohorts.
articles.journal: Pancreatology : official journal of the International Association of Pancreatology (IAP) ... [et al.]
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) has been linked with increased cancer incidence and mortality. We hypothesized that OSA may be a risk factor for neoplastic progression among patients undergoing pancreatic cancer surveillance.

METHODS: Retrospective medical record review of two Johns Hopkins Hospital cohorts undergoing pancreas surveillance; patients with familial/genetic risk enrolled in the Cancer of the Pancreas Screening (CAPS) study and patients with incidentally detected pancreatic cysts, enrolled in the PCYST study. Time-to-progression to pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) and neoplastic progression (either PDAC, high-grade dysplasia or pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor) were compared by OSA status, adjusting for covariates.

RESULTS: OSA was diagnosed prior to or during surveillance in 174 (19.5%) of 893 patients in CAPS and 376 (23.7%) of 1585 patients in the PCYST cohort. In the combined cohorts, OSA was associated with increased risk of progression to PDAC (unadjusted HR: 3.12, 95% CI: [1.82, 5.34], p < 0.001). OSA was also associated with male sex, higher BMI, fatty liver, fatty pancreas, diabetes, and history of smoking (all p < 0.01). After covariate adjustment, OSA remained associated with PDAC risk (adjusted HR: 2.56 [1.44, 4.55], p = 0.001). Factors associated with neoplastic progression included OSA (adjusted HR: 1.93 [1.25, 2.97], p = 0.003), increasing age (age-per 5-years adjusted HR: 1.14 [1.05, 1.24], p = 0.003), fatty liver (adjusted HR: 1.76 [1.19, 2.60], p = 0.005), and diabetes (adjusted HR: 1.77 [1.16, 2.71], p = 0.008).

CONCLUSIONS: Patients undergoing pancreatic surveillance for their familial/genetic risk and/or incidentally detected pancreatic cysts have a greater likelihood of developing pancreatic cancer if they've been diagnosed with OSA.

articles.title: Parental fear of progression in juvenile idiopathic arthritis and type 1 diabetes.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This cross-sectional study examined the relevance and impact of fear of disease progression (FoP) to parents of youth with two common childhood chronic conditions—juvenile idiopathic arthritis (JIA) and type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM).

METHODS: 124 parents (57 JIA, 67 T1DM; 107 mothers, 17 fathers) of youth aged 2–18 years (M=11.36, SD=3.90) were recruited through social media and patient organisation groups. Parents completed online questionnaires assessing fear of their child’s disease progression (FoP), responses to their children's symptoms and their own psychopathology. In addition, we measured parent reports of their child’s pain, health-related quality of life (HRQoL), anxiety and depressive symptoms. Bivariate correlations were used to assess the associations between parental FoP and parent and parent-reported youth psychosocial outcomes. A hierarchical regression was conducted to identify the unique contribution of parental FoP to youth HRQoL. Secondary exploratory analyses estimated the proportion of parents with elevated levels of FoP.

RESULTS: Parental FoP was associated with poorer parent and parent-reported youth psychosocial outcomes. After controlling for covariates, parental FoP explained a small amount of additional variance (1.6%) in parent-reported youth HRQoL. Secondary analyses revealed that 76% of parents had elevated levels of FoP.

CONCLUSIONS: As FoP appears to be a common concern among parents of youth with JIA and T1DM, which is consistently associated with poorer psychosocial outcomes, future research should be directed towards understanding and treating FoP in parents of children with a chronic condition.

articles.title: Late-Night Eating is Associated with MASLD and Cirrhosis: The Nurses' Health Study and Health Professionals' Follow-Up Study.
articles.journal: Clinical gastroenterology and hepatology : the official clinical practice journal of the American Gastroenterological Association

articles.title: Dietary Patterns and Their Association with Postpartum Glucose Metabolism Disorders after Gestational Diabetes Mellitus.
articles.abstract:
AIM: To identify dietary patterns and evaluate their association with postpartum glucose metabolism disorders after gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM).

METHODS: A nested case-control study was conducted in women aged 18-40 with GDM (n = 233) who participated in an educational intervention program. Clinical, biochemical, and anthropometrical parameters were evaluated at the end of pregnancy and three months postpartum. An oral glucose tolerance test (OGTT) with 75 g glucose was performed three months after giving birth. Women were classified as follows: i) Those with glucose metabolism disorders (n = 100), fasting plasma glucose (FPG) ≥100 mg/dL and/or ≥140 mg/dL at 2 h; ii) Those with normal glycemia (n = 133), FPG <100 mg/dL and <140 mg/dL at 2 h. For this study, we defined postpartum glucose metabolism disorders as having impaired fasting glucose and/or impaired glucose tolerance, or type 2 diabetes. Dietary patterns were analyzed using factor analysis and multivariate logistic regression to identify associations with postpartum glucose metabolism disorders, after adjusting for confounders.

RESULTS: Three dietary patterns were identified. The highest compared to the lowest adherence to a healthy postpartum dietary pattern was associated with lower odds (OR 0.445; 95% CI 0.209-0.951; p = 0.037) of postpartum glucose metabolism disorders; no association was found for the Western dietary pattern or the Sweets and Dairy-Rich in Fat and Sugar dietary pattern.

CONCLUSION: In women with previous GDM, the highest compared to the lowest adherence to the Healthy postpartum dietary pattern was associated with lower odds of postpartum glucose metabolism disorders.

articles.title: Stage-wise far-UVC/chlorine process curbs antimicrobial resistance in hospital wastewater: Short-burst inactivation and sustained suppression of recovery and resistance transfer.
articles.abstract: Conventional UV254/chlorine can leave incomplete genetic damage and create a low-dose window that promotes horizontal gene transfer (HGT), limiting reliable antimicrobial-resistance (AMR) control. Here, UV222/chlorine (1 mg/L free chlorine) was evaluated in 0.22-μm-filtered hospital wastewater inoculated with E. coli DH5α-RP4 and compared with UV222, UV254, and UV254/chlorine. During UV222/chlorine treatment in hospital wastewater, free available chlorine (FAC) declined rapidly and approached the detection limit at approximately 35 mJ/cm2, whereas UV254/chlorine retained measurable FAC at 100 mJ/cm2. Chloride promoted conversion of Cl· to selective Cl2·-, whereas tert-butanol quenching indicated a smaller contribution from ·OH. Accordingly, the process comprised an initial chlorine-enhanced phase (0-35 mJ/cm2), which delivered ∼2.5-log greater ARB inactivation than UV222 alone, followed by a UV222-dominated phase after FAC depletion. Membrane permeabilization largely saturated during Stage 1, supporting an acute rather than dose-proportional envelope attack. At 100 mJ/cm2, UV222/chlorine prevented regrowth, reduced intracellular antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) by 76.6-88.3%, and drove RP4 conjugation toward zero. In contrast, UV254/chlorine transiently increased conjugation to ∼150% of the control at low doses. Transcriptomics showed concurrent suppression of envelope maintenance, DNA repair, protein homeostasis, and metabolism. Thus, UV222/chlorine combines a short RCS shock with sustained multi-target damage to control ARB, ARG persistence, and plasmid-mediated HGT in complex wastewater.

articles.title: Stage-dependent expression of CB1 and CB2 receptors and their vascular effects during the progression of diet-induced atherosclerosis.
articles.abstract: Cardiovascular diseases (CVDs) remain the leading cause of global mortality, with ischemic heart disease and stroke representing the most common clinical manifestations. Atherosclerosis, a chronic inflammatory disorder of the arterial wall, constitutes the primary pathological basis of these conditions. Recent studies have implicated the endocannabinoid system (ECS), which includes cannabinoid receptors CB1 and CB2, their endogenous ligands, and metabolic enzymes, in the pathophysiology of atherosclerosis. In the present study, we explored the molecular and functional interactions between the ECS and diet-induced atherosclerosis in Wistar rats. Our results show distinct expression patterns of CB1 and CB2 receptors in the aortic wall, with significant downregulation observed in the advanced stages of atherosclerosis. Functional assays demonstrated stage-dependent vascular responses to selective CB1 and CB2 agonists, indicating that modulation of the ECS influences vascular tone and blood pressure. Additionally, biochemical analysis of endocannabinoids and their catabolic enzymes, including 2-arachidonoylglycerol (2-AG)/monoacylglycerol lipase (MAGL) and anandamide (AEA)/fatty acid amide hydrolase (FAAH), revealed dynamic alterations throughout the course of disease progression. These findings underscore the critical role of the ECS in vascular homeostasis and suggest that cannabinoid-based therapeutic strategies may hold potential for the management of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease.

articles.title: Convergent molecular evidence identifies a robust seven-gene signature in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma.
articles.abstract: Esophageal Squamous Cell Carcinoma (ESCC) is an aggressive gastrointestinal malignancy with unfavorable clinical outcomes, and current molecular biomarkers offer limited clinical utility for early detection and precise risk stratification. In this study, we integrated multi-cohort transcriptomic profiling with systems-level network analysis and causal inference to identify robust candidate biomarkers. Differential expression analysis across four independent datasets revealed consistent transcriptional alterations in ESCC. Several co-expression modules derived from the core dataset remained stable across independent cohorts and demonstrated significant correlations with tumor status. Mendelian Randomization (MR) analysis of module-derived genes prioritized 18 candidates with genetically supported associations with ESCC risk. These candidates were further refined using Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator (LASSO) regression, yielding a seven-gene diagnostic signature comprising LMBRD1, ZNF365, NPEPPS, CCNB1, TFRC, COL4A1, and TIMELESS. The resulting signature demonstrated strong discriminatory performance in both training and independent validation cohorts. To strengthen biological relevance, MR-prioritized genes were additionally supported by protein-level evidence from four independent ESCC proteomic studies. Collectively, this integrative analytic framework highlights convergent molecular features of ESCC and identifies a seven-gene signature with strong diagnostic performance. Ultimately, experimental validation in cellular and clinical cohorts will be essential to translate these computational findings into clinically actionable strategies for ESCC.

articles.title: Cardiovascular Risk in SELECT-Eligible MI Patients With Overweight or Obesity: The Western Denmark Heart Registry.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In the SELECT (Semaglutide Effects on Cardiovascular Outcomes in People with Overweight or Obesity) trial, treatment with semaglutide reduced the risk of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) in patients with cardiovascular disease, overweight or obesity, and no diabetes.

OBJECTIVES: The purpose of this study was to estimate cardiovascular risk in first-time myocardial infarction (MI) patients meeting the SELECT-eligibility criteria and the preventive potential for treatment with semaglutide.

METHODS: We conducted an observational cohort study applying the SELECT trial's inclusion and exclusion criteria to patients with first-time MI recorded between 2010 and 2021 in the Western Denmark Heart Registry. Five-year incidence of second MI, MACE, and all-cause death was estimated for SELECT-eligible patients with a body mass index (BMI) ≥27 kg/m2. In an assumption-dependent scenario analysis the preventive potential for semaglutide was estimated as the postponement of MACE incidence.

RESULTS: In 21,777 first-time MI patients without diabetes, 10,768 patients were SELECT-eligible with BMI ≥27 kg/m2. Median age at first-time MI was 65 years for the SELECT-eligible MI patients and 69 years for normal-weight (BMI 20-26 kg/m2) comparisons. Five-year incidence of second MI (n = 544), MACE (n = 975), and all-cause death (n = 914) was 5.9% (95% CI: 5.4%-6.4%), 10.7% (95% CI: 10.1%-11.4%), and 10.3% (95% CI: 9.7%-11.0%) in SELECT-eligible MI patients, respectively. Among these, treatment with semaglutide was estimated to postpone a 5% MACE incidence by 12 months.

CONCLUSIONS: In SELECT-eligible first-time MI patients with overweight or obesity and no diabetes, the cardiovascular risk was substantial with 1 in 10 having a MACE event within 5 years after first-time MI. Based on the SELECT trial results, semaglutide may markedly postpone MACE incidence in these patients.

articles.title: Benchmarking of growth hormone therapy in Hong Kong: ten-year data from the multi-centre GROWTH study.
articles.journal: Growth hormone & IGF research : official journal of the Growth Hormone Research Society and the International IGF Research Society
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the local practice and short-term efficacy of recombinant human growth hormone (rhGH) therapy in children and adolescents in Hong Kong.

METHODS: A retrospective analysis of rhGH therapy in children and adolescents between 2013 and 2022 who attended six Hong Kong centres that had enrolled in GloBE-Reg.

RESULTS: The cohort comprised 161 males and 190 females with a range of clinical indications that consisted mainly of growth hormone deficiency (GHD) (n = 147, 41%). The median age at rhGH initiation was 10.1 years (range, 0.3, 18.1). Median one-year change in height standard deviation score (HtSDS) was available in 319 children (90.8%) and was 0.41 (range, -0.98, 3.4). The median starting dose of rhGH for GHD was 0.028 mg/kg/day (range, 0.008, 0.051).

CONCLUSIONS: This multicentre study shows the utility of GloBE-Reg for understanding the use of rhGH therapy at a regional level. Findings demonstrate a variation in clinical practice as well as in short-term growth outcomes. These results support the need for continued optimisation of rhGH therapy through local benchmarking and care quality improvement activities.

articles.title: Mitochondria Beyond Bioenergetics: Canonical and Non-Canonical Functions in Ischemic Stroke and Aging.
articles.abstract: Ischemic stroke remains a leading cause of death and long-term disability worldwide, yet effective neuroprotective therapies beyond reperfusion strategies are still lacking. Emerging evidence highlights mitochondria as central regulators of neuronal fate, expanding their traditional role in cellular energy homeostasis through ATP production by oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS). Together with calcium buffering and redox regulation, these represent canonical mitochondrial functions. Mitochondria also regulate cellular adaptation to stress through mitochondrial quality control (MQC), mitochondrial ferritin-dependent iron buffering, signaling mediated by mitochondrial metabolites and mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA), and intercellular organelle transfer. These non-canonical functions link mitochondrial state to ferroptotic cell death, innate immune activation, and epigenetic regulation of nuclear responses. During cerebral ischemia, mitochondrial dysfunction involves impaired OXPHOS, the generation of reactive oxygen species (ROS), opening of the permeability transition pore, disruption of organelle dynamics, and dysregulation of non-canonical functions, collectively promoting neuronal injury, inflammation, and impaired recovery. These disturbances are further exacerbated by aging, which compromises MQC mechanisms, including fusion/fission balance, mitophagy, and biogenesis, and increases neuronal vulnerability. Mitochondrial signals, including mtDNA, cardiolipin, and ROS, also contribute to inflammasome activation and glial metabolic reprogramming, linking mitochondrial injury to neuroinflammation. Moreover, mitochondrial ferritin and iron buffering may influence oxidative damage and ferroptosis. Therefore, integrating canonical and non-canonical mitochondrial functions provide a broader framework for understanding ischemic injury and underscore the potential of MQC, redox regulation, iron homeostasis, and mitochondrial transfer as therapeutic targets and strategies for stroke recovery.

articles.title: Pectin alleviates alcohol-associated liver disease partly through cell-type-specific aryl hydrocarbon receptor signaling in female mice.
articles.abstract: The aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AhR) plays a critical role in alcohol-associated liver disease (ALD). Pectin improves ALD partially through the AhR pathway. However, AhR is expressed across different organs and cell types, and the specific cellular targets mediating AhR's effects in ALD remain unclear. We generated conditional AhR knockout mice in intestinal epithelial cells, hepatocytes, dendritic cells, and Rorγt-positive cells, in which AhR may play a critical role in regulating the gut-liver axis and pectin protection against ALD. ALD was induced using the Lieber-DeCarli model, and mice received pectin supplementation. AhR deficiency in intestinal epithelial cells and hepatocytes in mice leads to increased hepatic inflammation and serum ALT following alcohol administration compared with their littermate controls. However, pectin exerted strong protective effects against ALD in all the models. Our results suggest that AhR activation across multiple cell types, rather than a single cell type, mediates the protective role of pectin.

articles.title: Early infiltration of ischemia-conditioned Tregs attenuates BBB damage via suppressing neutrophil extracellular traps in ischemic stroke.
articles.abstract: Regulatory T cells (Tregs) modulate myeloid cells but are absent early after ischemic stroke when neutrophil infiltration peaks. Whether promoting their early infiltration into the brain as an introduced niche could modulate the cerebral immune micromilieu remains unknown. Here, we show that splenic Tregs at day 5 post-MCAO (ischemia-conditioned Tregs, ICTregs) exhibit enhanced adhesion. Transferred ICTregs infiltrate the infarcted area early, alter brain cellular composition, reduce neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) and preserve blood-brain barrier (BBB) integrity during the acute phase. Mechanistically, integrin α4 anchors ICTregs to cerebral venous endothelium, and ICTreg Annexin A1 interacts with neutrophil Dectin-1 to suppress NETs. The transcription factor Ikzf2 is critical for ICTreg induction, and modulating Ikzf2 enables Sham Tregs to acquire early brain-homing capacity. These findings offer valuable insights into the neuroprotective function of ICTregs in the early stage of ischemic stroke and identify engineered-Tregs target for optimizing the brain-immune ecosystem for neural protection.

articles.title: Diagnostic and Surgical Challenges in Atypical Right Coronary Sinus-Right Atrial Rupture With Concurrent VSD.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sinus of Valsalva aneurysm is a rare anomaly that, when ruptured, causes high-flow shunts and rapid-onset heart failure. We report a rare anatomical variant of right coronary sinus aneurysm rupturing into the right atrium with a concurrent perimembranous ventricular septal defect (pmVSD).

CASE SUMMARY: A 16-year-old male with known pmVSD presented with progressive NYHA functional class III dyspnea for 15 days. Volume overload was initially misattributed to ventricular septal defect progression. However, transthoracic echocardiography demonstrated a restrictive pmVSD (3.4 mm opening, peak gradient 60 mm Hg), elevated right ventricular systolic pressure (76 mm Hg) as a flow-mediated surrogate for pulmonary artery systolic pressure, and a ruptured sinus of Valsalva aneurysm with a high-velocity jet into the right atrium. Because of "washout" artifacts, coronary computed tomography angiography failed to visualize the fistulous tract. Single-stage surgical repair of both lesions achieved complete recovery.

DISCUSSION: This case emphasizes color Doppler echocardiography's value in dual-shunt physiology when coronary computed tomography angiography is inconclusive, supporting single-stage surgical repair for multilesion presentations.

articles.title: Beyond the Newborn Screen: An Infant With Hypoxic Respiratory Failure.
articles.journal: Journal of pediatric health care : official publication of National Association of Pediatric Nurse Associates & Practitioners
articles.abstract: Anchoring bias can narrow diagnostic reasoning in infants with nonspecific but severe presentations. We describe a 4-month-old full-term female who presented with acute hypoxic respiratory failure and significant recent weight loss. Initial evaluation revealed profound CD4 lymphopenia and hypogammaglobulinemia, prompting early concern for severe combined immunodeficiency (SCID). A normal newborn T-cell receptor excision circle screen and preserved IgA and IgM levels later reduced the likelihood of classic SCID, but the diagnostic focus remained anchored on primary immunodeficiency as the child worsened. Human immunodeficiency virus-1 (HIV-1) RNA PCR testing confirmed a markedly elevated viral load, and bronchoalveolar lavage identified Pneumocystis jirovecii. Maternal testing revealed previously undiagnosed HIV, suggesting late-term seroconversion. This case demonstrates how anchoring on SCID delayed consideration of HIV despite evolving clinical and immunologic findings and highlights the role of HIV testing at delivery in identifying perinatal HIV exposure and preventing delayed diagnosis.

articles.title: Single-Channel Electrophysiology Using a Miniaturized Montal-Mueller Planar Lipid Bilayer System for Recording a Synthetic K2P Channel.
articles.abstract: The functional reconstitution of ion channels into planar lipid bilayers provides a strategy to investigate channel activity at the single-molecule level. However, conventional Montal-Mueller bilayer systems typically require bulky experimental setups, manual chamber assembly, and relatively large recording volumes, which increase reagent consumption and may introduce additional sources of electrical noise due to extended wiring and external headstages. Here, we present a miniaturized, ready-to-use bilayer platform (BLMchipMM) integrated with a compact amplifier that enables stable single-channel recordings with reduced reagent consumption and simplified operation. This protocol describes the use of this system for performing single-channel electrophysiology measurements. Using this system, we reconstituted a synthetic K2P channel (ancTREK1) and used it as a proof-of-principle test protein to validate reconstitution and single-channel recording. Single-channel recordings show a current-voltage relationship in Mg2+-free symmetric K+ solutions, with conductance values consistent with those reported for TREK1 channels. The successful reconstitution of this K2P-like channel demonstrates the utility of this system for single-channel analysis in artificial membranes.

articles.title: Gua Sha (Scraping Therapy) for Spasticity After Stroke: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of RCTs with Integrated Preclinical Mechanistic Synthesis.
articles.abstract: ​Emerging clinical data from Chinese randomized controlled trials (RCTs) suggest Gua Sha (scraping therapy) may deliver adjunct antispastic benefits for spasticity after stroke (SAS) when combined with standard rehabilitation. This study aimed to synthesize clinical efficacy evidence and explore treatment parameters for this intervention. We searched eight electronic databases from database inception to January 1, 2026; two independent reviewers completed study screening, risk-of-bias assessment using Cochrane Risk of Bias 2.0 tool, and data extraction. Meta-analytic effect sizes were calculated using mean difference (MD), and the review protocol was preregistered on PROSPERO. Sixteen eligible RCTs enrolling 1227 stroke survivors were included, all conducted in China, which may limit the external transferability of our results. Pooled random-effects estimates indicated that add-on scraping therapy was associated with reduced Modified Ashworth Scale and Visual Analog Scale for Pain (VAS-P) scores, lower serum hs-CRP and Hcy, as well as improved motor function and activities of daily living. Grading of Recommendations Assessment (GRADE) rated the certainty of evidence for all outcomes as very low due to high heterogeneity, methodological limitations, suspected publication bias and limited cross-regional data. Exploratory subgroup analyses identified numerically larger spasticity relief in regimens with 5-day treatment intervals, 1.5-month treatment duration and intensive scraping stimulation. These cross-study comparisons generate preliminary hypotheses awaiting verification through dedicated head-to-head dosing trials. Proposed mechanistic pathways linking scraping therapy to symptom relief rely largely on preclinical evidence, including enhanced local microcirculation and modulation of inflammatory and neural signaling. Current evidence supports scraping therapy as an investigational adjunctive strategy for SAS. Given the low-certainty evidence base and lack of inclusion in international rehabilitation guidelines, this therapy should be evaluated only in clinical settings with certified practitioners and standardized adverse event monitoring. Further well-designed RCTs are required to clarify its long-term therapeutic benefits and complete safety profile.

articles.title: Evaluating the Role of miR-93-5p in Children Infected by Mycoplasma pneumoniae with Digestive System Injury.
