articles.title: Perceptions of Climate Change, Health Impacts, and Climate Resilience, among Urban Residents Living with Asthma: An Exploratory Qualitative Study.
articles.journal: Journal of urban health : bulletin of the New York Academy of Medicine
articles.abstract: In the US, rates of asthma, and in particular, uncontrolled asthma, are disproportionately high among historically marginalized racial/ethnic groups and among urban residents. Against the backdrop of climate change and its known consequences, which can exacerbate the environmental triggers of asthma, these inequities are further magnified. This qualitative study explored perceptions of climate change, health impacts, and climate resilience among historically marginalized urban adults with asthma. Black/African-American, Hispanic/Latino, and/or multiracial adults ( ≥ 18 years) diagnosed with asthma, and residing in the Chicagoland area, were recruited. Semistructured interviews informed by the capability, opportunity, motivation, and behavior (COM-B) model were conducted, and data were transcribed for thematic coding. Data from 20 interviews revealed four primary themes: (1) climate change awareness, (2) perceived harms of climate change, (3) climate resiliency: barriers and strategies, and (4) perceived outlook on climate change. Participants consistently associated extreme weather with adverse asthma management consequences and highlighted the negative impacts of climate-related events on their outdoor time, physical activity, and social life. Virtually all participants emphasized significant financial burden resulting from their daily living adaptations for managing their condition in the context of climate change. Participants showed variable levels of climate preparedness and reported limited community-level engagement in climate action activities. This study supports enhancing climate resilience as a potentially effective strategy for improving asthma management among historically marginalized urban residents, warranting future research. Findings emphasize the need to strengthen both individual- and societal/environmental-level climate resilience to optimize health and well-being for all.

articles.title: Higher Myocardial miR-1-3p, miR-30a-5p, miR-34a-5p, and Lower miR208a-3p Levels are Associated with Lower Age at the Time of Heart Transplantation.
articles.abstract: Expression of microRNAs (miR-1-3p, miR-21-3p, miR-30a-5p, miR-34a-5p, miR-133a-3p, miR-208a-3p, and miR-423-5p) and mitochondrial unfolded protein response (UPRmt) genes (HSPA9, HSPD1, LONP1, OMA1, and YME1L) was investigated by qRT-PCR in six controls and 65 failing human hearts (33 ischemic cardiomyopathy (ICM), 28 dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM), 2 hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, and 1 non-compaction and restrictive cardiomyopathy each). Failing hearts had higher expression of miR-208a-3p, HSPA9, HSPD1, OMA1, YME1L and lower miR-1-3p expression compared to controls. Patients with higher miR-1-3p, miR-30a-5p, miR-34a-5p, (miR-423-5p exhibited a trend) and lower miR-208a-3p expression underwent heart transplantation or LVAD implantation earlier in life. DCM group had higher expression of miR-1-3p, miR-30a-5p, HSPD1, and LONP1 compared to the ICM group. Thus, myocardial expression of miR-1-3p, miR-30a-5p, miR-34a-5p, and miR-208a-3p could be associated with the HF progression; miR-208a-3p, HSPA9, HSPD1, OMA1, YME1L, and miR-1-3p could discriminate HF form control; and miR-1-3p, miR-30a-5p, HSPD1, and LONP1 could discriminate DCM from ICM.

articles.title: YAP and WWTR1/TAZ Connect Mechanotransduction and Mitochondrial Metabolism in Cardiac Hypertrophy and Ventricular Remodeling.
articles.abstract: Cardiac hypertrophy is a mechanometabolic remodeling process shaped by mechanical load, matrix stiffness and mitochondrial adaptation. YAP and TAZ, encoded by YAP1 and WWTR1, are paralogous, non-DNA-binding transcriptional co-activators that link cytoskeletal tension to TEAD-dependent transcription. This review organizes current evidence along a mechanical stress-YAP/TAZ activation-mitochondrial remodeling-ventricular remodeling axis and distinguishes direct human myocardial data, animal cardiac mechanisms, related cardiovascular or in vitro evidence, and cross-disease extrapolation. Experimental studies suggest that TEAD1 supports mitochondrial gene programs, transient YAP activation promotes glycolytic compensation during early pressure overload, whereas sustained Yap1 activation may impair mitochondrial biogenesis. Cell-specific studies further implicate fibroblast, endothelial, immune and epicardial programs, although many data derive from non-hypertrophic contexts. Thus, the adaptive-to-maladaptive YAP/TAZ model remains provisional. Human lineage-resolved data are limited, and no YAP/TAZ-targeted therapy is established for cardiac hypertrophy.

articles.title: Problematic Pornography Use Among Swedish Adolescents: Characteristics and Clinical Implications.
articles.abstract: Problematic pornography use (PPU) is the most common manifestation of compulsive sexual behavior disorder (CSBD). Many adults seeking help for CSBD report onset during adolescence, yet there is limited knowledge of PPU in adolescents and its predisposing factors. This study investigated the prevalence of self-perceived PPU among Swedish adolescents and explored associated factors as well as pornography use patterns. In this cross-sectional study, data were collected from a representative sample of 3106 Swedish third-year senior high school students. Information on sociodemographic background, pornography use, sexual behaviors, health, and experiences of abuse was collected. PPU was based on self-reported difficulties in refraining from or stopping pornography use. Gender-stratified descriptive statistics and logistic regression analyses were used to examine relationships between groups and variables. PPU was reported by 10.4% of respondents, with a higher prevalence among boys (18.8%) compared to girls (3.9%). It was associated with increased time spent on pornography and higher exposure to violent or other concerning sexual content. Compared to the reference group, adolescents with PPU exhibited higher rates of abusive experiences, mental health issues, risky behaviors, and nonsuicidal self-injury. Gender-specific patterns emerged. PPU is a significant issue among Swedish adolescents, particularly boys. Addressing concerns related to pornography use, underlying vulnerabilities and gender-specific factors is crucial to prevent the progression of PPU into adulthood and in treatment efforts.

articles.title: Development and validation of prediction models for any and severe acute kidney injury in children with sepsis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sepsis-associated acute kidney injury (SA-AKI) is a serious complication in children. We developed and validated models to predict any AKI and severe AKI in pediatric sepsis.

METHODS: This retrospective study included 375 children who met the Phoenix sepsis criteria between January 2019 and December 2025. Patients who developed AKI during the first 24 h were excluded. Outcomes were any AKI (KDIGO stages 1-3) and severe AKI (stages 2-3) occurring from 24 h through day 7. Patients were randomly divided into training and validation cohorts (7:3). Predictors were selected using LASSO followed by multivariable logistic regression. Model performance was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), calibration curves, and decision curve analysis.

RESULTS: New-onset AKI occurred in 111 patients (29.6%), including 90 (24.0%) with severe AKI. The any AKI model included age, mechanical ventilation, activated partial thromboplastin time, uric acid, and cystatin C. Its AUCs were 0.911 (95% CI, 0.874-0.948) and 0.911 (95% CI, 0.854-0.968) in the training and validation cohorts. The severe AKI model included lactate, activated partial thromboplastin time, blood urea nitrogen, and uric acid, with corresponding AUCs of 0.864 (95% CI, 0.809-0.919) and 0.897 (95% CI, 0.817-0.977). Both models showed acceptable calibration and positive net benefit. Sensitivity analyses using an alternative baseline serum creatinine definition yielded similar results.

CONCLUSIONS: Two models based on routinely available early variables showed good internal performance for predicting any AKI and severe AKI in pediatric sepsis. External validation is required before clinical implementation.

articles.title: Severe alkalemia in the emergency department : Acid-base patterns, clinical presentation and short-term outcomes in hospitalized patients.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Alkalemia is the most common acid-base disorder in hospitalized patients; however, data on patients with severe alkalemia admitted to the emergency department are limited. This study aimed to characterize the acid-base patterns of patients with severe alkalemia presenting to the emergency department and to describe the clinical presentation and short-term clinical outcomes of those requiring hospitalization.

PATIENTS, MATERIAL AND METHODS: We conducted a retrospective analysis of arterial and venous blood gas measurements and medical records of all adult nontrauma patients admitted to the emergency department of a tertiary university hospital in Austria with a pH> 7.55, between 1 June 2022, and 31 December 2023.

RESULTS: Among 215 patients with severe alkalemia, 84 (39%) required hospitalization. Acute respiratory alkalosis was the predominant acid-base disorder (57%), followed by mixed respiratory and metabolic alkalosis (35%), whereas isolated metabolic alkalosis was not observed. Detailed clinical data were available for 80 hospitalized patients. Pain (67%) and emesis (49%) were the most common presenting symptoms, while psychiatric disease was the most prevalent comorbidity (38%). Despite severe alkalemia, the disorder was documented as a diagnosis in only 4% of hospitalized patients. No in-hospital deaths occurred. Application of a published venous-to-arterial correction algorithm resulted in only minor changes in the classification of acid-base disorders.

CONCLUSION: In contrast to previous reports from intensive care populations, patients with severe alkalemia requiring hospitalization had a clinically distinct phenotype and favorable short-term outcomes. Despite marked alkalemia, the condition was very rarely documented as a diagnosis, suggesting that severe alkalemia might be underrecognized in the emergency department.

articles.title: Comparative Efficacy and Safety of Nitrofurantoin Versus Fosfomycin for Acute Uncomplicated Lower Urinary Tract Infection: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION AND HYPOTHESIS: Nitrofurantoin and fosfomycin are first-line oral agents for acute uncomplicated lower urinary tract infection (u-UTI) in women, yet direct comparative evidence remains limited. This study compared clinical and microbiological outcomes of multi-day nitrofurantoin versus single-dose fosfomycin trometamol for u-UTI, including pregnant and nonpregnant women.

METHODS: Databases were searched from inception through 9 May 2025, for RCTs comparing oral nitrofurantoin with single-dose fosfomycin trometamol (3g) for u-UTI. Primary outcomes were clinical and microbiological cure; secondary outcomes were 14-day relapse and adverse drug reactions (ADRs). Pooled risk ratios (RRs) with 95% CIs were calculated. Risk of bias was assessed using Cochrane RoB 2.0, and evidence certainty was graded using GRADE.

RESULTS: Six RCTs (n = 1762; mean age 36.49±15.29) were included. Clinical cure at ≤7, 7-10, 14, and ≥28 days was comparable (RR 0.98, 0.99, 1.05, 1.02). Nitrofurantoin 300 mg/day was associated with higher clinical cure at 14 and ≥28 days (RR 1.14 and 1.22), whereas no significant difference was observed with 200 mg/day. In pregnant women, fosfomycin was associated with higher clinical cure at ≤7 days (RR 0.87; 95% CI 0.76-0.98). Microbiological cure showed no significant overall difference between treatments (RR 0.99; 95% CI 0.92-1.08), including at 14 and ≥28 days. Nitrofurantoin was associated with higher 14-day relapse (RR 1.71; 95% CI 1.13-2.59). Overall ADR rates were not significantly different (RR 1.27; 95% CI 0.95-1.70), although ADRs were higher with nitrofurantoin 300 mg/day (RR 1.63; 95% CI 1.07-2.49).

CONCLUSIONS: Nitrofurantoin and single-dose fosfomycin are both effective treatment options for uncomplicated cystitis. Treatment choice may be influenced by pregnancy, dosing regimen, and adherence considerations. Further well-designed trials are needed to clarify differences between treatment regimens.

articles.title: Identifying Intracranial Atherosclerotic Disease in Emergent Large Vessel Occlusion.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Intracranial atherosclerotic disease (ICAD) represents a substantial proportion of large vessel occlusion (LVO) strokes refractory to mechanical thrombectomy, yet its diagnosis in the hyperacute setting remains challenging without direct vessel-wall imaging.

METHODS: This narrative review is intended as a narrative and conceptual roadmap, acknowledging the inherent limitations of current methodologies for assessing ICAD in LVO patients. We evaluate clinical, pre-procedural imaging, angiographic, and intraprocedural features supporting a diagnosis of ICAD-related LVO, drawing on own experience and evidence from the literature. Articles were selected by authors for relevance to the conceptual framework. Randomized controlled trials, systematic reviews, and mechanistic pre-clinical studies were prioritized where available.

RESULTS: Truncal occlusion morphology, fixed residual stenosis after thrombectomy, and early reocclusion emerge as the most reproducible high-specificity markers, while clinical risk-factor profile, absence of the susceptibility vessel sign, and collateral or perfusion patterns provide corroborating rather than standalone evidence.

DISCUSSION: We propose a tiered diagnostic framework combining these markers to guide real-time decisions on bailout angioplasty or stenting, alongside a differential diagnosis of non-atherosclerotic mimics. Existing prediction scores show promising discriminative performance but remain largely unvalidated outside their Asian derivation cohorts. We propose illustrative enrollment criteria for future randomized trials, informed by recent studies.

CONCLUSION: Systematic, reproducible recognition of ICAD is essential to guide bailout treatment decisions and to enable rigorous evaluation of endovascular strategies tailored to this distinct stroke subtype.

articles.title: Varicella zoster virus meningitis with a dermatomal rash in immunocompetent hosts: a systematic review and novel case report.
articles.abstract: Varicella zoster virus (VZV) reactivation with central nervous system (CNS) involvement is an uncommon but important cause of lymphocytic meningitis in both immunocompromised and immunocompetent individuals. While cranial presentations, especially V1 involvement, are well documented, spinal-dermatomal VZV meningitis is rarely reported. We conducted a systematic review of PubMed, Scopus, and Embase using PRISMA guidelines to identify all cases of laboratory-confirmed VZV meningitis or encephalitis with a dermatomal rash in immunocompetent adults affecting spinal levels C1 and below. Data extracted included demographics, dermatome distribution, CSF findings, treatment, and outcomes. We also report a novel case from our institution involving isolated C4-C5 involvement. Seventeen total cases met inclusion, including our 44-year-old male patient who presented with fever, severe headache, and a right-sided vesicular rash in the C4-C5 dermatomes. He was initially misdiagnosed with a tick-borne illness. Mean CSF values across all cases were WBC count 382/µL (SD ± 270), protein 177 mg/dL (SD ± 106), and glucose 52.7 mg/dL (SD ± 15.8). IV acyclovir was used in 15 of 17 cases, with oral acyclovir (41%) or valacyclovir (29%) as the most common step-down therapies. Mean treatment duration was 14 days, and average length of hospital stay was 6.4 days. All patients survived and made a full recovery. Spinal-dermatomal VZV meningitis can occur in immunocompetent adults, including cases with cervical involvement. Early recognition of the rash pattern and timely PCR testing are essential for accurate diagnosis and prompt antiviral therapy, which is associated with favorable outcomes.

articles.title: Parental reactions to and preferences for genomic newborn screening in Germany: findings from a scenario-based survey experiment.
articles.journal: European journal of human genetics : EJHG
articles.abstract: Parental perspectives are central in ongoing debates about genomic newborn screening (gNBS). This study examined (expecting) parents' interest in gNBS in Germany. We hypothesized that condition characteristics (actionability, genetic penetrance) and personal factors (e.g., attitudes towards gNBS, anticipated coping, risk perception) predict parental interest in gNBS for their child. We also investigated determinants of risk perception. In an online survey (N = 556; 60% women; M age=35 years), participants evaluated nine hypothetical case-scenarios that systematically varied penetrance and actionability. Data were analyzed using multilevel models, latent profile analysis and descriptive statistics. Overall, (expecting) parents showed a strong demand for information, driven more by perceived benefits than concerns. Two profiles emerged: one highly open and one seeking information more selectively. Across scenarios, higher interest in potential gNBS findings was associated with high actionability and moderate penetrance (50-74%) of possible target conditions, prior experience with chronic conditions, greater anticipated coping with test results, higher perceived probability of condition development, and more positive than negative attitudes toward gNBS. Perceived probability (subjective risk) predicted interest better than objective risk (penetrance), but was itself well explained by penetrance. Diagnostic concern (worry about disease manifestation) was consistently higher than perceived probability across penetrance levels and more pronounced in women. Implications include avoiding the reporting of low-penetrance findings due to disproportionate diagnostic concern and providing decision aids to support informed parental decision-making.

articles.title: α7-nAChR Activation is Associated with Attenuation of Cardiac Fibrosis in Ischemic Cardiomyopathy via SIRT3-Dependent Modulation of EndMT.
articles.abstract: To investigate whether α7-nicotinic acetylcholine receptor (α7-nAChR) activation attenuates ischemic cardiomyopathy (ICM) through regulation of endothelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EndMT), and to explore the involvement of Sirtuin-3 (SIRT3) in this process. ICM was induced in rats by coronary ligation for 4 weeks, followed by treatment with PNU-282,987, a selective α7-nAChR agonist, or cardiac-specific SIRT3 knockdown using serotype 9 adeno-associated virus (AAV9). Human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVECs) were treated with transforming growth factor-β (TGF-β) and/or PNU-282,987 (10 µM). α7-nAChR activation improved cardiac function, reversed ICM-induced TGF-β upregulation and SIRT3 downregulation, and inhibited EndMT-related changes. These effects were weakened by SIRT3 knockdown. The findings suggest that α7-nAChR activation alleviates ICM and myocardial fibrosis through a SIRT3-dependent mechanism, although direct receptor-level specificity requires further validation.

articles.title: Insulin resistance is potentially associated with 24-h blood pressure variability related to blunted sympathetic reactivity in older adults with hypertension.
articles.journal: Clinical autonomic research : official journal of the Clinical Autonomic Research Society
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Blood pressure variability (BPV) increases with aging and hypertension; however, the underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. Aging-related insulin resistance is known to contribute to abnormalities in autonomic circulatory regulation. Although hypertension and autonomic dysfunction are closely linked, it remains unclear whether hypertension modifies the effects of insulin resistance on autonomic cardiovascular control and BPV. Since daily life is mostly spent upright, sympathetic responses to postural change may determine BPV. Therefore, we aimed to determine whether insulin resistance is associated with muscle sympathetic nerve activity (MSNA) responses to orthostatic stress in older adults with and without hypertension.

METHODS: We studied 37 older adults without hypertension (normotension [NTN]) and 30 older patients with hypertension (HTN) without diabetes mellitus. Participants underwent 30° and 60° head-up tilt (HUT), whereby MSNA responses were assessed. In addition to 24-h BPV, fasting glucose, insulin, and homeostasis-model-assessment-estimated insulin resistance (HOMA-IR) were measured.

RESULTS: HTN exhibited higher 24-h BPV. There were no significant group differences in MSNA responses to HUT or in fasting glucose, insulin, or HOMA-IR. Importantly, however, only in the HTN group, MSNA responses to HUT were negatively correlated with fasting glucose and HOMA-IR. In multivariable models adjusting for age, sex, and body mass index (BMI), fasting glucose remained an independent predictor of MSNA responsiveness. Furthermore, mediation analysis revealed indirect associations of fasting glucose and HOMA-IR with 24-h BPV in relation to attenuated MSNA responses to HUT.

CONCLUSIONS: In older adults with hypertension, insulin resistance may be associated with elevated BPV through blunted sympathetic responses to orthostatic stress.

articles.title: Beyond diagnosing acute kidney injury: defining what we need from kidney biomarkers.
Modulation of the noradrenergic system using transcranial ultrasonic stimulation targeted to the brainstem locus coeruleus in awake mice.
articles.journal: Neuropsychopharmacology : official publication of the American College of Neuropsychopharmacology
articles.abstract: Transcranial ultrasound stimulation (TUS) is a novel neuromodulation technique that can be used to non-invasively target the locus coeruleus (LC). The LC provides the majority of noradrenergic input to the brain and has been implicated in several neurological and psychiatric disorders. Before translation to human studies, establishing a dose-response relationship requires systematic characterization of two distinct effects: (1) the influence of stimulation protocol variations on norepinephrine (NE) release in LC target structures, and (2) the broader brain and bodily effects of LC-targeted TUS. We used fiber photometry to measure TUS-induced activation of LC neurons and release of NE in one of its major projection areas, the hippocampus. To evaluate widespread functional effects, we investigated changes in [18F]FDG uptake in the brain and body in response to LC-targeted TUS using small-animal PET imaging. Five-second trains of TUS resulted in intracellular calcium level increases in the LC, accompanied by a biphasic change in NE levels in the hippocampus and LC, i.e., an initial rise followed by a transient decrease. The same TUS protocol showed a decrease in [18F]FDG uptake across the brain and a strong increase in [18F]FDG uptake in brown adipose tissue. If TUS was prolonged to 30 s the initial biphasic change in hippocampal NE levels was followed by a secondary increase that persisted throughout the remainder of the stimulation period. This study provides the first demonstration that TUS can modulate the LC-NE system in awake mice. Adjusting the stimulation protocol resulted in distinct patterns of hippocampal NE release, highlighting the therapeutic potential of LC-targeted TUS as distinct stimulation protocols may differentially restore disrupted NE levels across disorders. PET imaging further revealed engagement of both central and peripheral systems, emphasizing the broad physiological reach of this approach.

articles.title: The bacteriophage transcription factor Gp53 suppresses cell division and regulates Pseudomonas aeruginosa physiology.
articles.abstract: Pseudomonas aeruginosa is a highly drug-resistant pathogen that poses a major challenge to clinical treatment. Bacteriophages encode diverse regulatory proteins that can alter host cellular processes during infection. Here we show that the ΦPA1019-encoded transcription factor Gp53 regulates bacterial physiology by targeting key host pathways. Gp53 expression reduces bacterial growth, motility, and biofilm formation, and causes filamentous cell morphology. Transcriptomic analysis reveals that Gp53 alters the expression of 3,342 genes, including genes involved in cell division and virulence-associated processes. DNA-binding assays demonstrate that Gp53 directly represses promoters of key host genes, including ftsZ, fleQ, pslA, and amrZ. Gp53-mediated repression of ftsZ disrupts Z-ring formation and inhibits cell division, while ftsZ expression restores these defects. Structural and mutational analyses identify residues important for Gp53-DNA interaction. Together, these findings reveal a phage-encoded mechanism that coordinately interferes with bacterial cell division and virulence-associated pathways, providing mechanistic insights into host transcriptional regulation during phage infection and expanding our understanding of phage-host interactions.

articles.title: Sickle cell haemoglobin status shapes malaria parasite genotype in asymptomatic infections.
articles.abstract: Sickle cell haemoglobin (HbS) confers protection against symptomatic malaria caused by Plasmodium falciparum. HbS carriers with symptomatic malaria harbour parasites enriched for P. falciparum sickle-associated alleles (Pfsa+), which appear to partially overcome HbS-mediated protection, but their role in asymptomatic infections is unclear. Here we conducted a cross-sectional survey of 2,246 healthy schoolchildren in a region of high malaria transmission in Cameroon. Analysing the parasite Pfsa and the human HbS genotypes for 1,701 asymptomatic P. falciparum infections confirmed that heterozygous HbS (HbAS) and homozygous non-HbS (HbAA) genotypes have similar rates of asymptomatic infection. However, the HbS genotype is strongly associated with parasites carrying the Pfsa+ alleles at the Pfsa1 and Pfsa3 loci, indicating a selective advantage for these alleles in HbS carriers. Our findings reveal that the protective effect of HbS is complex: HbS has a protective effect before symptoms appear against Pfsa- parasites and Pfsa+ alleles may contribute to the lower rates of symptomatic disease observed in HbS carriers. In HbS-mediated protection against malaria, both resistance and tolerance and ongoing co-evolution with parasites should be considered.

articles.title: DNMT1 function in cortical PV interneurons modulates cortical network activity, mood disorder‑related behavior, and perineuronal nets.
articles.abstract: Parvalbuminergic (PV) interneurons are central to cortical network stability and psychiatric vulnerability. Here, we identify DNA methyltransferase 1 (DNMT1) as a key epigenetic regulator linking PV interneuron function to glial and extracellular matrix remodeling. Conditional PV-specific Dnmt1 deletion, combined with single-nucleus RNA-seq (snRNA-seq), snATAC-seq, in vivo electrophysiology, histology, and behavioral analyses, revealed that DNMT1 loss increases PV spiking but reduces inhibitory efficacy, driving network desynchronization and depression- and anxiety-like behavior in mice. These physiological changes were accompanied by non-cell-autonomous transcriptional and chromatin alterations, affecting perineuronal net (PNN) organization and neuron-glia communication. Cell-cell communication analyses predicted reorganized perisomatic signaling, and compartmental modeling of oligodendrocyte lineage dynamics further revealed impaired formation of PNN-supporting perineuronal oligodendrocytes, consistent with a tissue-level reduction in PNN integrity. Together, our findings demonstrate that DNMT1 maintains inhibitory circuit stability through PV interneuron function, secondarily shaping glial states and extracellular scaffolds to support cortical network synchronization and affective behavior.

articles.title: Primary defect closure in minimally invasive direct inguinal hernia repair: a propensity-weighted analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The benefit of defect closure during minimally invasive repair of direct inguinal hernias remains uncertain. Prior studies have reported conflicting findings and often lacked adequate control for confounding.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included adult patients undergoing elective, unilateral, laparoscopic or robotic repair of direct inguinal hernias with complete 30-day follow-up in the Abdominal Core Health Quality Collaborative registry. Inverse probability of treatment weighting adjusted for age, BMI, ASA class, smoking, anticoagulation, diabetes, hypertension, immunosuppressant use, prior pelvic operation, recurrent hernia, direct hernia size, and prior mesh. The primary outcome was 30-day surgical site occurrence (SSO). Secondary outcomes included 30-day readmission, reoperation, and recurrence. A prespecified robotic subgroup analysis was performed.

RESULTS: A total of 4,209 patients were included. Closure was associated with lower SSO rate (3.6% vs 6.2%, p = 0.034) but higher 30-day cardiac readmissions (2.2% vs 0.3%, p < 0.001), driven by 3 versus 1 events, while other causes were infrequent and similar between groups. In the robotic subgroup (n = 2,171), the wound benefit lost statistical significance (SSO 3.9% vs 5.1%, p = 0.330), whereas cardiac readmissions remained elevated (2.1% vs 0.3%, p = 0.001). Closure clustered with distinct operative practices, including more frequent use of self-fixating mesh (60% vs 38%, p < 0.001), TAP blocks under direct visualization (46% vs 9.9%, p < 0.001), and shorter operative times (62% vs 51% completed in < 60 min, p = 0.001).

CONCLUSION: Direct defect closure was associated with a reduction in early wound complications and higher 30-day cardiac readmissions. Given the very small absolute number of cardiac readmissions (3 vs 1) that are likely unrelated to defect closure, these findings support selective use of direct defect closure, particularly in patients with larger medial defects or higher wound complication risk. Randomized trials with standardized operative protocols are still needed to confirm our findings.

articles.title: Do structural ICU requirements reflect critical care demand in elective metabolic and bariatric surgery? A retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Metabolic and bariatric surgery (MBS) is increasingly delivered in lower-acuity settings, yet on-site intensive care unit (ICU) capability remains a structural requirement for the highest center-designation tier. Direct data on critical-care utilization after elective MBS without an on-site ICU are limited. We describe 30-day outcomes at such a center, using contemporaneous elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy (LC) in the same environment as a reference.

METHODS: Retrospective cohort study of consecutive adults undergoing elective MBS (sleeve gastrectomy or Roux-en-Y gastric bypass) or LC (2022-2025) at a single center without an on-site ICU but with a pre-defined escalation and transfer protocol. The primary outcome was the 30-day complication rate (Clavien-Dindo); ICU utilization was grade ≥IV. Outcomes are reported descriptively with 95% confidence intervals (CIs); regression and propensity-score-matched analyses are exploratory (Supplementary Material).

RESULTS: Of 1,065 patients (MBS n=351, LC n=714), 30-day complication rates were 4.27% (95% CI 2.39-6.94%) versus 3.64% (95% CI 2.37-5.27%). No MBS patient was admitted to intensive care (0/351), compatible with a true rate up to 1.05% (upper 95% CI); two LC patients required ICU admission (0.28%), both for retained-stone acute pancreatitis. All five MBS reoperations were for postoperative hemorrhage; none developed organ dysfunction or met ICU-transfer criteria, and none died. Because events were rare, this study cannot exclude clinically meaningful ICU demand, and absence of a detected difference does not establish equivalence.

CONCLUSIONS: In this single-center experience, elective MBS without an on-site ICU under a structured escalation protocol showed no observed ICU admissions over 30 days, though the confidence interval remains compatible with infrequent critical-care need. These hypothesis-generating findings demonstrate feasibility in one environment and should not be generalized to accreditation policy; prospective multicenter data are required.

STUDY REGISTRATION: Research Registry (UIN: researchregistry11829); retrospectively registered; https://www.researchregistry.com.

articles.title: Genotype-phenotype variability in TRMT10A deficiency: divergent developmental outcomes associated with biallelic loss-of-function variants.
articles.abstract: Loss-of-function variants in TRMT10A are known to cause a rare autosomal recessive disorder primarily characterized by microcephaly, short stature, and impaired glucose metabolism. However, the extent of phenotypic variability and the factors influencing clinical heterogeneity remain poorly understood. Here, we describe two individuals harboring distinct biallelic loss-of-function variants in TRMT10A who exhibited divergent developmental phenotypes. The first patient, a 34-year-old man with a homozygous early frameshift variant, presented with preserved cognitive function and previously unreported multisystem features, including male infertility, high-grade myopia, bilateral sensorineural hearing loss, and tetralogy of Fallot. In contrast, the second patient, a 3-year-old boy with a homozygous deletion involving exons 6-7, demonstrated early-onset developmental delay, epilepsy, congenital heart disease, and neonatal hypoglycemia. Transcript-level analyses supported the predicted effects of both variants on TRMT10A transcripts. These findings suggest phenotypic variability associated with TRMT10A loss-of-function variants. Notably, the frameshift variant identified in the adult patient has previously been reported in association with a more typical neurodevelopmental phenotype, whereas our patient exhibited preserved cognitive function. This observation supports variable expressivity and suggests that additional factors may contribute to clinical heterogeneity.

articles.title: Visuospatial working memory performance under emotional face distraction in non-athletes, team-sport athletes, and individual-sport athletes.
articles.abstract: Sports expertise and emotional face distractors have both been examined in working memory (WM) research; however, little is known about whether visuospatial WM performance under emotional face distraction differs among non-athletes, team-sport athletes, and individual-sport athletes, or whether such effects vary across processing stages. This study addressed these questions in 71 young adults using a delayed-matching task. Angry and happy face distractors were presented during encoding, retrieval, or both stages. Accuracy and reaction time (RT) were analysed with mixed-design ANOVAs and Bayesian statistics. For accuracy, the overall distraction analysis showed no significant effects of distraction presence, participant type, or their interaction. Under distractor-present conditions, no significant main effect of distraction stage or participant type was found, whereas accuracy was slightly higher in happy-face than angry-face parts; interactions were non-significant. For RT, the overall distraction analysis showed slower responses in distractor than no-distractor conditions and a participant-type effect, although pairwise comparisons were non-significant. Under distractor-present conditions, only the distraction stage × distraction type interaction was significant, with longer RTs for happy than angry faces during retrieval. Supplementary analyses yielded a similar pattern. Collectively, the hypothesised group differences were not supported, and emotional face distractor effects were limited and stage- and index-dependent.

articles.title: Real-world analytical and diagnostic evaluation of the Abbott i-STAT Alinity point-of-care high-sensitivity troponin I assay in a UK emergency department.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: High-sensitivity cardiac troponin (hs-cTn) testing is central to emergency department assessment of suspected acute coronary syndrome. Point-of-care hs-cTn testing may reduce turnaround time, but local analytical and clinical evaluation is required before implementation.

METHODS: In a single-centre real-world evaluation, paired whole-blood and plasma samples from patients with suspected acute coronary syndrome were analysed using the Abbott i-STAT Alinity point-of-care hs-cTnI assay and the Alinity laboratory hs-cTnI assay. Imprecision, method comparison, threshold concordance, diagnostic discrimination for adjudicated Type 1 myocardial infarction (MI), and potential effects of haemolysis, icterus, lipaemia and haematocrit were assessed.

RESULTS: Low-level imprecision was below 10% CV. Concordance at the <5 ng/L rule-out threshold was high (84.1%); all discordant classifications reflected higher POCT values, with no false-negative rule-outs. Both assays showed similar discrimination for adjudicated Type 1 MI and 100% observed sensitivity and negative predictive value at the 5 ng/L threshold, although confidence intervals were wide. POCT specificity was lower than laboratory specificity. Method comparison showed a modest positive POCT bias, and regression analyses did not identify clinically meaningful effects of haemolysis, icterus, lipaemia or haematocrit.

CONCLUSION: The Abbott i-STAT Alinity POCT hs-cTnI assay demonstrated analytical performance and clinical concordance supportive of local implementation, with similar diagnostic discrimination to the Alinity laboratory hs-cTnI assay in a small cohort. Larger prospective studies are needed to confirm clinical safety and workflow impact.

articles.title: Dietary Flavonoid Hyperoside Ameliorates High-Fat Diet-Induced Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus by Enhancing Brown Adipose Tissue Thermogenesis, White Adipose Tissue Browning, and Gut Microbiota Remodeling.
articles.abstract: Hyperoside, a natural dietary flavonoid widely found in a variety of fruits, vegetables, and medicinal plants, exhibits hypoglycemic as well as hepatorenal protective activities. However, its effects on type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and the underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. In this study, T2DM mice were established after 8 weeks of high-fat diet (HFD) feeding and were subsequently treated with hyperoside for 6 weeks. Then, indices of glucose and lipid metabolism, energy expenditure, hepatic histopathology, brown adipose tissue (BAT) thermogenesis, inguinal white adipose tissue (iWAT) browning, macrophage polarization in iWAT, and gut microbiota composition were evaluated. Hyperoside significantly reduced HFD-induced body weight gain in T2DM mice without suppressing appetite. HFD-induced insulin resistance, dyslipidemia, hepatic steatosis, and fibrosis were markedly ameliorated by hyperoside. Hyperoside also increased oxygen consumption, carbon dioxide production, and energy expenditure, and decreased the respiratory exchange ratio. In addition, hyperoside treatment was accompanied by increased UCP1 and PGC-1α protein expression and upregulated mRNA expression of PGC-1α, UCP1, PRDM16, and Cidea in BAT and iWAT, consistent with enhanced BAT thermogenic activity and an iWAT browning-related phenotype. Flow cytometry analysis further revealed that hyperoside inhibited M1 macrophage polarization and reduced the M1/M2 ratio in iWAT. Moreover, hyperoside partially modulated gut microbial diversity and taxonomic composition in T2DM mice, increased the relative abundance of Bacteroidetes and the Bacteroidetes/Firmicutes ratio, and partially restored the relative abundance of Muribaculaceae and Lachnospiraceae_NK4A136_group. In conclusion, hyperoside ameliorated metabolic dysfunction in HFD-induced T2DM mice, accompanied by enhanced BAT thermogenic activity, iWAT browning-related changes, modulation of macrophage polarization in iWAT, and remodeling of the gut microbiota. These findings suggest that hyperoside may represent a potential natural product candidate with metabolic benefits, although further pharmacokinetic, safety, long-term, and clinical validation is required.

articles.title: Reducing Dietary Sodium Exposure in Chronic Kidney Disease: Challenges and Opportunities.
articles.abstract: Over 750 million individuals worldwide experience chronic kidney disease (CKD), which is a major contributor to cardiovascular disease and kidney failure as well as increased morbidity and mortality. Diet is a key lifestyle factor in CKD risk prevention and management. Overall public dietary quality and sodium intake have shown limited improvement despite decades of public health efforts. Excessive sodium consumption is a challenging dietary risk factor because exposure is largely passively embedded within the modern food environment. Furthermore, the consequences of overconsumption of dietary sodium are often delayed, invisible, or difficult for patients to recognize. The complexity of dietary behavior approaches coupled with conventional education approaches also contributes to persistently high sodium intake across the CKD spectrum. In this review, we discuss three major overarching challenges to sodium reduction, which comprise the invisible nature of sodium-related risk, the ubiquity of sodium within commercially prepared and processed foods, and the limitations of knowledge-based interventions alone. We also highlight subsequent opportunities to improve implementation. These include practical, patient-centered, and personalized nutrition strategies; food environment and food supply improvements that make lower-sodium choices the default; and expansion of Food Is Medicine and culinary medicine approaches. Reducing dietary sodium exposure and its consequences requires coordinated efforts that extend beyond individual patients and health care providers to include multidisciplinary collaboration across health care systems, public health, industry, community organizations, professional societies, and policymakers. Such multilevel approaches offer important opportunities to improve kidney health trajectories as well as cardiovascular health. Semin Nephrol 36:x-xx © 20XX Elsevier Inc. All rights reserved.

articles.title: Searching for Hidden Sources of Potassium and Phosphorus Additives in Adults Living With Chronic Kidney Disease.
articles.abstract: Reducing dietary potassium (K) and phosphorus (P) intake is considered a cornerstone for managing hyperkalemia and hyperphosphatemia in adults with chronic kidney disease (CKD). K and P additives in processed foods are a growing concern as hidden sources of these minerals, yet their prevalence is unknown. The objective of this study was to investigate the characteristics of foods purchased by individuals with CKD, including the prevalence and types of K and P additives and the food categories most associated with these additives. This observational cohort study involved adults with CKD who collected grocery receipts over 4 weeks. Receipts were used to identify foods that may contain K or P additives. Ingredient lists of processed and ultra-processed foods were reviewed to identify items containing these additives. Statistical analysis was performed using IBM SPSS Statistics 31.0. Thirteen adults with CKD aged 54-80 (53.8% female, 84.6% of European descent) participated. A total of 889 food items were identified from 115 receipts, including 429 (48.3%) processed foods. Among these, 51 (11.9%) contained K additives only, 120 (28.0%) contained P additives only, and 34 (7.9%) contained both K and P additives. The most common K additive was K sorbate (57.3%), whereas the most common P additive was lecithin (42.6%). K additives were predominantly found in beverages (28.2%), sauces/salad dressings (20.0%), and ready-to-eat foods (20.0%). P additives were common in snacks (34.4%) and ready-to-eat foods (22.1%). Of 108 excluded foods, 65 items (60.2%) lacked food labels, with 25 (38.5%) being deli items and 23 (35.4%) being bakery items. Adults with CKD frequently purchased foods containing K and P additives. Educating patients about how to avoid these additives may help manage hyperkalemia and hyperphosphatemia. Future research is needed to validate the observed levels of additive exposure.

articles.title: Prevalence of cardiovascular risk factors among Nepalese adults who work at higher altitudes.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Non-communicable diseases such as diabetes mellitus, obesity, and hypertension are major global health concerns, with 80% occurring in low-middle income countries. High-altitude exposure can influence cardiovascular health, affecting disease prevalence and life expectancy. In Nepal, a significant portion of the population lives and works at high altitudes, facing unique environmental and physiological stresses. This study aimed to determine the prevalence of cardiovascular disease risk factors among adults working at high altitudes in Nepal.

METHODS: A descriptive medical camp-based study was conducted in Kathmandu in February and May 2023. The sample included 239 participants, predominantly Sherpa trekking guides, porters, and trekkers working above 4000 m. Data collection involved a structured questionnaire covering socio-demographic variables, health profiles, and lifestyle habits. Blood pressure and echocardiogram were performed, and data were analyzed using SPSS version 25.

RESULTS: Among the participants, 75% were male, with 35.6% aged 31-40. Diabetes was reported by 19.1%, followed by hypertension in 9.2%. Additionally, 53.8% engaged in regular physical activity, 67% were non-smokers, and 59.1% consumed alcohol. Echocardiogram results showed normal left ventricular ejection fraction for all participants. Notably, 32.5% experienced acute mountain sickness, and 3.8% reported syncope.

CONCLUSION: The prevalence of diabetes, hypertension, dyslipidemia are there among the participants who work in high altitudes. Addressing cardiovascular risk factors among high-altitude workers in Nepal is urgent. So, further research on cardiovascular diseases should be carried out at high altitudes.

articles.title: IgG4-related disease is not associated with an increased incidence of malignancy in a large, single-centre cohort.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Immunoglobulin G4-related disease (IgG4-RD) is a systemic, immune-mediated disease-causing inflammation and fibrosis in multiple organs, often associated with elevated serum IgG4 concentrations. Whether IgG4-RD is associated with malignancy remains unclear. We investigated whether there is an association between IgG4-RD and incident malignancy.

METHODS: We performed a single-centre, retrospective cohort study of patients who fulfilled the American College of Rheumatology/European Alliance of Associations for Rheumatology IgG4-RD Classification Criteria. Malignancy history was collected by survey and medical record review. Age- and sex-stratified malignancy incidence rates in the cohort were compared with rates in the general US population. Cox proportional hazards were used to identify disease characteristics associated with incident malignancy.

RESULTS: Of the 348 patients with IgG4-RD in our cohort, 34 (10%) developed incident malignancies over a median follow-up of 8.04 years (IQR, 1.35-14.72 years). The most common malignancies were lymphoma (n = 6, 16% of malignancies), prostate cancer (n = 6, 16%), and lung cancer (n = 5, 13%). Compared with the general US population, there was no increased incidence of malignancy in patients with IgG4-RD (standardised incidence ratio, 0.88 [0.61-1.23]). Among patients with IgG4-RD, those who ever smoked (adjusted hazard ratio [HR], 2.46 [1.16-5.24]) or were older (HR, 1.35 [1.00-1.83] per decade) had increased risk of malignancy, whereas female patients (HR, 0.37 [0.14-0.96]) and those with submandibular gland involvement (HR, 0.25 [0.10-0.61]) had decreased risk.

CONCLUSIONS: IgG4-RD was not associated with an increased incidence of malignancy following IgG4-RD onset. Among patients with IgG4-RD, smoking and older age at IgG4-RD onset were associated with higher malignancy risk. Female sex and submandibular gland involvement were associated with lower malignancy risk.

articles.title: Context-dependent roles of ketone metabolism in intestinal inflammation.
articles.abstract: Ketone metabolism is traditionally viewed as an alternative metabolic pathway providing energy during carbohydrate deprivation through the production and utilization of ketone bodies. Ketone bodies also function as signaling molecules regulating immune and metabolic processes. Accumulating evidence shows that ketone metabolism influences diverse diseases and immune responses, including inflammation, autoimmunity, and infection. Recently, ketone metabolism has been associated with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), a chronic inflammatory disorder of the intestine, although reported effects are heterogeneous and context-dependent. In this review, we synthesize current evidence on ketone metabolism in IBD and intestinal inflammation, highlighting its roles in barrier integrity, immune regulation, and microbiota interactions. We also discuss potential mechanisms underlying divergent outcomes and outline key questions for future research.

articles.title: Phenotypes of diabetic kidney disease and cardiovascular outcomes.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To quantify the association between diabetic kidney disease (DKD) phenotypes and cardiovascular disease (CVD) mortality and incident major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), atrial fibrillation (AF), and peripheral artery disease (PAD).

METHODS: In this longitudinal analysis of adults with diabetes from NHANES (N = 5035) and the UK Biobank (UKBB, N = 26,968), participants were categorized by estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR, ml/min per 1.73m[2]) and urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio (UACR, mg/g) into four phenotypes: no DKD (eGFR≥60, UACR<30), albuminuria-only (eGFR≥60, UACR≥30), low eGFR only (eGFR<60, UACR<30), and albuminuria+low eGFR (eGFR<60, UACR≥30). We estimated absolute and relative risk of CVD mortality (both cohorts) and incident non-fatal CVD (UKBB), adjusting for demographics, anthropometric and laboratory values, and medications.

RESULTS: In both cohorts, the albuminuria+low eGFR phenotype was associated with the highest cardiovascular risk versus no DKD (reference). In NHANES, albuminuria-only was more strongly associated with CVD mortality than low eGFR only: albuminuria-only HR 2.56 (95%CI 1.86-3.53), low eGFR only HR 1.92 (1.35-2.73), albuminuria+low eGFR HR 3.16 (2.27-4.41). In UKBB, the low eGFR only phenotype was associated with higher risk of CVD mortality than the albuminuria-only phenotype: albuminuria-only HR 1.88 (1.66-2.13), low eGFR only HR 2.42 (1.99-2.95), albuminuria+low eGFR HR 4.65 (3.78-5.71). In UKBB, the albuminuria+low eGFR phenotype exhibited the strongest association with MACE, AF, and PAD. Similar patterns were observed with absolute risk calculations.

CONCLUSIONS: Across two large cohorts, DKD phenotypes conferred distinct cardiovascular risk profiles. Consistent measurement of both eGFR and UACR in clinical practice may facilitate targeted, preventative cardiovascular care in diabetes.

articles.title: Receptivity and susceptibility to care models for Metabolic dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease (MASLD) in Europe: a mixed-methods, landscaping study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The healthcare landscape for metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is evolving rapidly, and further introduction of care innovations is anticipated. We aimed to map current approaches to MASLD care and to gain health system insights supporting the implementation of novel, MASLD-related initiatives.

METHODS: We conducted a cross-sectional, mixed-methods comparative analysis, assessing receptivity and susceptibility to adopting new care models, defined as the extent to which a healthcare system can accommodate the implementation of an innovation. We distributed an in-depth survey amongst healthcare providers (May-October 2025), and performed document analyses.

RESULTS: A total of 36 health professionals from ten European countries were surveyed (36% primary care, 19% non-academic hospital, 39% university hospital), and 56 documents were analyzed. Alignment was observed across countries and care levels regarding standard practices of care. Patients still predominantly entered MASLD care upon incidental findings. Referral structures were largely absent, with MASLD rarely embedded in diabetes care. Accessibility and availability of care was suboptimal, relating to care organization, allocation of diagnostics, and reimbursement policies. MASLD guidelines were available in eight countries, but specific primary care guidance remained scarce. Available guidelines primarily differed in non-invasive tests utilization, follow-up, and pharmacotherapy recommendations.

CONCLUSION: The European healthcare landscape for MASLD is largely comparable across countries. Care for MASLD is not structurally embedded in national healthcare systems. All examined healthcare systems offered opportunities to strengthen receptivity and susceptibility to care innovations. Any MASLD-related innovations introduced in future must be tailored to local healthcare contexts to facilitate effective implementation.

Maternal knowledge and practices regarding complementary and alternative medicine in the management of childhood asthma: A cross-sectional study of Jordanian mothers.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Complementary and alternative medicine (CAM) is widely used in childhood asthma, particularly where traditional healing practices are deeply rooted, but evidence on Jordanian mothers' knowledge and practices is limited.

PURPOSE: This study examined Jordanian mothers' knowledge and practices regarding CAM in the management of childhood asthma and identified the sociodemographic factors associated with them.

METHODS: A descriptive correlational, cross-sectional design was used. A convenience sample of 264 Jordanian mothers of children with physician-confirmed asthma was recruited from seven governmental and teaching hospitals across northern, central, and southern Jordan. A researcher-developed questionnaire measured CAM knowledge (28 items) and CAM practices (20 items). Descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation, and multiple linear regression were computed in SPSS version 29.

RESULTS: Fair knowledge was reported by 51.9% of mothers, poor knowledge by 26.1%, and good knowledge by 22.0%. Practice was mainly moderate to high (M = 3.54, SD = 0.66). Knowledge and practice were weakly correlated (r = 0.143, p = .020). Higher maternal education, higher household income, and more frequent asthma symptoms predicted knowledge (p < .05), and knowledge was the only significant predictor of practice (p = .022). Food-based remedies and herbal therapies were the most commonly reported modalities.

CONCLUSIONS: CAM use is common among Jordanian mothers of children with asthma, yet only one in five had good knowledge of CAM and knowledge explained little of the variation in practice. Pediatric nurses should assess CAM use routinely and nonjudgmentally and provide culturally congruent education on safe use and potential herb-drug interactions.

articles.title: Voice-Related Outcomes Among Patients With Temporomandibular Disorders: A Systematic Review and Narrative Synthesis.
articles.journal: Journal of voice : official journal of the Voice Foundation
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Temporomandibular disorders (TMD) may influence voice through effects on mandibular movement and vocal tract configuration. This review synthesized subjective and objective voice-related outcomes among patients with TMD.

METHODS: A systematic search of MEDLINE via Ovid, PubMed, EMBASE, Scopus, Cochrane Library, and Google Scholar was completed, with no date restrictions. Observational studies were eligible if they included patients with TMD and reported at least one voice-related outcome. Methodological quality was assessed using Joanna Briggs Institute critical appraisal tools. Data were synthesized narratively.

RESULTS: The search identified 440 records; after duplicate removal, screening, and review, 10 studies comprising 3,467 TMD participants were included. Study designs, TMD definitions, comparator groups, and voice outcome measures varied substantially. Voice outcomes included symptom-based reporting of dysphonia or voice disorder, Voice Handicap Index, voice-related quality of life questionnaires, auditory-perceptual assessment, acoustic and cepstral analyses, spectrography, and the Dysphonia Severity Index. Symptom-based studies reported dysphonia or voice disorder in 12.6% of a 1,000-patient TMD cohort and in 73.1% of older adults with TMD compared with 29.7% without TMD in the same sample. Patient-reported outcomes were variable, but several studies showed greater voice handicap or poorer voice-related quality of life with increasing TMD severity. Auditory-perceptual assessment showed reduced loudness among patients with severe TMD. Objective measures showed reduced loudness, increased antiresonance, lower cepstral peak prominence values, and lower Dysphonia Severity Index scores in patients with TMD or greater TMD severity. Overall methodological quality was high in three studies, moderate in six, and low in one.

CONCLUSION: Voice symptoms and abnormal voice findings are frequently reported among patients with TMD and may worsen with increasing TMD severity. However, methodological heterogeneity and predominantly cross-sectional designs limit causal inference. Future studies should use standardized TMD definitions, matched controls, and integrated voice assessment methods.

Perfusion imaging predicts therapeutic cooling response and tracks cis-p-tau pathology in porcine brain injuries.
articles.journal: Neurotherapeutics : the journal of the American Society for Experimental NeuroTherapeutics
articles.abstract: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) and ischemic stroke cause substantial morbidity and mortality, yet effective neuroprotective therapies remain elusive. Although therapeutic hypothermia shows strong neuroprotection in lissencephalic rodent models, adult clinical trials have repeatedly failed, largely due to poor preclinical translatability and uniform cooling protocols that overlook patient heterogeneity. Using a large cohort of gyrencephalic porcine models (n = 89) of TBI and stroke, subjects were allocated to sham, injury, or therapeutic cooling groups administered via a custom-designed, non-invasive intranasal selective brain cooling device for pre-hospital and hospital settings. We combined clinical CT perfusion and neuropathology to identify biomarkers that predict cooling efficacy. Brain cooling significantly reduced mortality in TBI and stroke compared to untreated controls. We showed that concurrent hyperemia (elevated cerebral blood flow) and blood-brain barrier (BBB) leakage during cooling predicted intracranial hypertension, which may facilitate identification of high-risk subjects that require intervention. Sustained hyperemia was pathological. Neuropathological assessment revealed that cis-phosphorylated-tau (cis-p-tau), a major early driver of both TBI and stroke, is correlated with injury severity, treatment response, and BBB permeability. In TBI, mild selective brain cooling (∼1.3 °C reduction) was associated with reduced secondary brain damage, whereas deeper cooling (≥3 °C) offered no added benefit in this cohort. These findings suggest that integrating perfusion imaging and the early molecular driver cis P-tau can guide personalized hypothermia, advancing the field toward precision medicine in acute brain injury neuroprotection.

articles.title: Regional Expansion of Transplant Oncology: The First Case of Liver Transplantation for Unresectable Colorectal Liver Metastasis in the Gulf Region.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Liver transplantation for colorectal liver metastases (CRLM) has emerged as a potential curative option for highly selected patients with unresectable liver-only disease, with recent trials demonstrating 5-year overall survival rates of 55% to 83%. Surgical resection remains the only curative treatment for colorectal liver metastases (CRLM), but its applicability is limited, with only 25% of patients eligible. However, this approach remains investigational with limited global experience and has never been implemented in the Middle East region. Recently, liver transplantation (LT) has emerged as a potential curative option for select patients with unresectable liver-only metastases. This report highlights the potential for liver transplantation to serve as a curative modality in highly selected patients with CRLM and demonstrates its feasibility in a new geographic region.

CASE REPORT: We report the first case in the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) region of a 41-year-old male with unresectable CRLM who underwent LT following an aggressive multimodal pretransplant protocol. The patient was initially treated at an outside facility for synchronous left-sided colorectal cancer with liver metastases, achieving complete remission after FOLFOX chemotherapy. He subsequently developed 2 liver recurrences: the first in July 2023, with 17 metastases managed at the outside facility by surgical resection and chemotherapy; and the second in October 2023, with 40 metastases, treated with systemic chemotherapy and trans arterial radioembolization (TARE-Y90). He received additional treatment with ablative liver-directed therapies consistent with the "Cleveland Protocol." The patient subsequently underwent orthotopic liver transplantation. His postoperative course was complicated with moderate acute cellular rejection, which was successfully treated, and he was discharged on post-operative day 16.

CONCLUSION: This case demonstrates the successful implementation of liver transplantation for CRLM in the Gulf region, achieving disease-free survival at 4-month follow-up despite high-risk biological features typically associated with poor prognosis. It illustrates the feasibility and potential benefit of LT for unresectable CRLM in carefully selected patients, following an aggressive pretransplant locoregional therapy protocol modeled after the Cleveland Clinic approach. Key success factors included rigorous patient selection using established criteria (Oslo score 0, low Fong score, low PET-MTV), intensive pretransplant optimization with multimodal therapy, and experienced multidisciplinary management of post-transplant complications. With careful patient selection and integration of systemic and liver-directed therapies to achieve maximal disease control, this strategy may help expand transplant eligibility, possibly offering a curative approach. This case provides valuable regional data for the evolving role of transplant oncology in colorectal cancer management in a resource-limited setting.

Cost-effectiveness of anti-inflammatory reliever (AIR) or maintenance and reliever therapy (MART) for mild to moderate asthma: a systematic review.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The Global Initiative for Asthma recommends inhaled corticosteroid (ICS)-formoterol as anti-inflammatory reliever (AIR) or as maintenance and reliever therapy (MART) for the management of all asthma severities based on evidence of superior clinical effectiveness. This systematic review aimed to collate available evidence of the cost-effectiveness of ICS-formoterol for mild to moderate asthma compared with bronchodilator and ICS, used separately or in combination, in adolescents and adults.

METHODS: Systematic literature searches were conducted on MEDLINE/PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, Cochrane and the first 150 records from Google Scholar. Studies comparing the cost-effectiveness of ICS-formoterol AIR/MART to short-acting beta-2 agonist (SABA), ICS and ICS-long-acting beta-2 agonist (LABA) (other than formoterol) inhalers in people with asthma aged 12 years and older were included. Reporting was done using the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) model.

RESULTS: Six studies evaluated as moderate to high quality involving 8901 patients were included in the analysis. Three studies were from low- and middle-income countries and three from high-income countries. ICS-formoterol AIR/MART was cost-effective when compared with SABA, ICS plus SABA and ICS-LABA plus SABA. The cost difference of ICS-formoterol ranged from an additional cost of US$56 to a cost-saving of US$9900, with small quality-adjusted life-year (QALY) gains (0.001 to 0.0077) and exacerbation reductions (up to 2.33 fewer events).

CONCLUSIONS: The data suggest that ICS-formoterol AIR/MART is cost-effective for mild to moderate asthma. Due to cost-effectiveness thresholds being based on each country’s gross domestic product (GDP), more country-specific data, particularly from countries in Africa, is needed.
